AC ENG 20A.title: Academic Writing
AC ENG 20A.description: Grammar, sentence structure, paragraph and essay organization of formal written English.

AC ENG 20B.title: Academic Writing
AC ENG 20B.description: Grammar, sentence structure, paragraph and essay organization of formal written English.
AC ENG 20B.prereq_text: AC ENG 20A. Placement into AC ENG 20B is also accepted.

AC ENG 20C.title: Essentials of Academic Writing
AC ENG 20C.description: Grammar, sentence structure, paragraph and essay organization of formal written English.
AC ENG 20C.prereq_text: AC ENG 20B. Placement into AC ENG 20C is also accepted.

AC ENG 22A.title: Academic English Reading and Vocabulary
AC ENG 22A.description: Intensive reading exercises with occasional practice in extensive reading, focusing on comprehension, development of vocabulary, syntax, rhetorical features, reading strategies, and study skills.
AC ENG 22A.prereq_text: Placement into AC ENG 22A is required.

AC ENG 22B.title: ESL Reading and Vocabulary
AC ENG 22B.description: Extensive reading and discussion with emphasis on journal articles, textbook chapters, notetaking, and the interpretation of charts, diagrams, tables, and figures.

AC ENG 29.title: Special Topics in ESL
AC ENG 29.description: Directed and individualized work in English as a second language not covered in the AC ENG 20, 21, 22 sequence.

AC ENG 139W.title: Advanced Academic Writing Across the Curriculum
AC ENG 139W.description: Designed for transfer students who speak English as a second language. Focuses on developing academic reading and writing skills including essay content, organization, vocabulary, and grammar. Academic content also covered.
AC ENG 139W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
AC ENG 139W.restriction: Restricted to students whose first language is not English.

AC ENG 200.title: Oral English Communication I
AC ENG 200.description: Designed to help students hear and produce the sounds of English as an International Language with greater accuracy and confidence. Focuses on pronunciation features (e.g., consonant sounds, consonant clusters, vowels, thought groups, and nuclear stress).

AC ENG 201.title: Oral English Communication II
AC ENG 201.description: Designed to help students develop conversational fluency in English as an International Language. Focuses on applying knowledge of linguistic features and communicative skills during conversational exchange in a variety of social, academic, and professional contexts.

AC ENG 202.title: Oral English Communication III
AC ENG 202.description: Designed to help students hone their public speaking skills in English as an International Language. Focuses on preparing, organizing, and delivering speeches and presentations and interacting with the audience, emphasizing skills needed in academic settings.
AC ENG 202.prereq_text: AC ENG 200 with a minimum grade of B- or AC ENG 201 with a minimum grade of B-.

AC ENG 210.title: Introduction to Graduate Research Writing
AC ENG 210.description: Designed to introduce key components and skills for successful graduate-level academic writing. Topics cover summarizing and synthesizing sources, understanding appropriate source use conventions, developing and organizing ideas for research writing, revising, and editing.

AC ENG 211.title: Graduate Writing for Scholarly Publication
AC ENG 211.description: Designed to help graduate students in the preparation of a conference paper or journal manuscript for publication. Topics cover writing for academic publication in their fields and understanding disciplinary source use conventions.

AC ENG 212.title: Thesis/Dissertation Writing for Graduate Students
AC ENG 212.description: Designed to help graduate students in the preparation of a thesis/dissertation (or proposal). Topics cover planning a thesis/dissertation project, understanding the focuses and goals of different chapters, and practicing different ways of integrating sources to avoid plagiarism.

AFAM 40A.title: African American Studies I
AFAM 40A.description: Discusses main contours of African American experience from the forced importation of Africans into the Americas in the late fifteenth century to the development of social movements in post-emancipation societies of the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

AFAM 40B.title: African American Studies II
AFAM 40B.description: Introduction to the history of modern racial thinking in Western society and its relationship to the material contexts of racial oppression, with emphasis on its development in British colonies and in the U.S.

AFAM 40C.title: African American Studies III
AFAM 40C.description: Introduction to theories of racial blackness in the modern world, with emphasis on developments in British colonies and U.S. Traces emergence of blackness as term of collective identity, social organization, and political mobilization.

AFAM 50.title: Introductory Topics in African American Studies
AFAM 50.description: Introduction to a broad range of topics in African American studies, exploring history, literature, art, culture, politics, and contemporary social issues. Topical organization of courses addresses issues that have been of importance historically and are reshaping the African diaspora today.

AFAM 111A.title: Modern African American Art
AFAM 111A.description: Investigates the history of modern African American art; emphasis on the politics of representation. Examines art in a variety of media from material culture and textiles to painting and photography. Issues of migration, nationalism, gender, sexuality, and hybridity are discussed.

AFAM 111B.title: Contemporary African American Art
AFAM 111B.description: Investigates the history of contemporary African American art; emphasis on the politics of representation. Explores art in a variety of media: painting, sculpture, photography, installation, and new media. Cultural politics, appropriation, identity, gender, sexuality, hybridity and civil rights issues discussed.

AFAM 112A.title: Early African American Literature
AFAM 112A.description: Examines the earliest forms of black literary practices, including the jeremiad, the slave narrative, the pamphlet, poetry, the short story, and how these literary forms are related to the historical experiences of enslavement and emancipation.

AFAM 112B.title: African American Literature 1900-Present
AFAM 112B.description: Examines individual literary forms and/or authors, as well as movements such as the Harlem Renaissance and the Black Arts Movement. Explores how black literary practices represent the conditions of modern subjectivities and environments.

AFAM 113.title: African American Cinema and Media
AFAM 113.description: Explores the diversity of Black creative production and the historical, social, and economic forces that shaped their emergence. May include Black film, hip-hop culture, fine art, photography, and others.

AFAM 114.title: International Cultures
AFAM 114.description: Explores the various cultures of the African diaspora and their impacts on a global scale. Examines a diverse range of media, including music (reggae, hip-hop), literature, film, and others and the links between culture and social movements throughout the diaspora.

AFAM 115.title: Race and Visual Representation
AFAM 115.description: Examines film, documentary, fine art, photography, and other visual media to explore the multiple ways in which ideas about race are projected and woven through the visual landscape and the impacts this has on perpetuating social inequalities.

AFAM 118.title: Topics in African American Humanities
AFAM 118.description: Provides students with an opportunity to pursue advanced work in African American studies from one or more humanities approaches (literature, film and media studies, art history, and others).

AFAM 119.title: Black Latinidades
AFAM 119.description: Questions the parameters of Latinidad by centering the origins and development of African descent communities in the Americas through a multidisciplinary, transnational, and diasporic approach to the study of Afro-Latinidad.

AFAM 125.title: African American Women in Art
AFAM 125.description: Examines depictions of and by African American women in art and popular culture through a variety of media including textiles, painting, sculpture, photography, and installation. Focuses on African American women's experiences, perspectives, and strategies for contemporary representation.

AFAM 128.title: Topics in Gender/Sexuality
AFAM 128.description: Expressions of genders and sexualities across the spectrum of African American experience and creativity.

AFAM 134A.title: Caribbean History: Colonization to Emancipation
AFAM 134A.description: Exploration of the history of the archipelago from pre-Columbian times to the end of slavery; examining the impact of European colonization, decimation of the indigenous populations, African slavery, resistance, and emancipation; the unity and diversity of experience in region.

AFAM 134B.title: Caribbean History: Emancipation to Independence
AFAM 134B.description: Post-emancipation and anti-colonial struggles ending with political independence for most of the region. Examines social, political, economic, cultural dimensions of post-emancipation period, including large-scale migration to Central America, the U.S., and Britain; the region's global cultural and political contribution.

AFAM 137.title: History of the African Diaspora
AFAM 137.description: Examines the causes and consequences of the multiple diasporas of African peoples since the sixteenth century in the Atlantic world, especially the Americas and Europe.

AFAM 138.title: Topics in African American History
AFAM 138.description: Studies in selected areas of African American history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

AFAM 143.title: Topics in African American Music
AFAM 143.description: Examines African American musical forms and traditions, such as blues, jazz, and reggae, in performance and/or critical and theoretical contexts.

AFAM 144.title: Topics in Expressive Forms
AFAM 144.description: Examines various forms of aesthetic expression in the African diaspora, including dance, music, and the plastic arts, as well as artistic visions of black cyberspace, digital activism, film, video, and aesthetic conceptions of the future.

AFAM 145.title: African Americans and Photography
AFAM 145.description: Explores depictions of and by African Americans through photography. Examines the history of photography in relationship to African American culture through a variety of media from early daguerreotype processes to digital imagery.

AFAM 146.title: Afro-Latin American Music
AFAM 146.description: Musical culture of Afro-Latin American peoples, emphasizing Spanish-speaking Caribbean. Topics include background in West Africa, the persistence of traditions in the Caribbean, the commercial music of the 20th century, the connections between musical culture, religion, and the economy.

AFAM 151.title: Comparative Minority Politics
AFAM 151.description: Examines the political experiences of Blacks, Latinos, and Asian Americans in the United States from roughly 1950 to the present. Focuses on how each group has pursued political empowerment via both conventional political channels and social movements.

AFAM 152.title: African American Politics
AFAM 152.description: Examines politics of African Americans in order to gain a broader perspective of the American political process. Major developments in African American politics (including the civil rights movement, Black presidential bids), continuing problem of racism, responsiveness of key governing institutions.

AFAM 153.title: African American Psychology
AFAM 153.description: Historical overview of the development of black psychology and the African American frame of reference. Topics include personality development, psychological assessment, issues in education, black mental health, and the role of the African American psychologist in the community.

AFAM 154.title: African American Social Formations
AFAM 154.description: Topics which promote critical investigation into the historical, political, and social formations associated with the Black Diaspora.

AFAM 155.title: Intercultural Studies
AFAM 155.description: Studies relationships between various cultural formations within the Black Diaspora and the exchange, amalgamations, and tensions between Black Diasporic formations and non-Black formations. Examines expressions of racialization as representation, adaption, and resistance.

AFAM 156.title: African Societies and Politics
AFAM 156.description: Examines the violent incorporation of Africa within European modernity. Places the discourse of Pan-Africanism, African Nationalisms, Negritude, African Marxism, and/or African Socialism in juxtaposition to the forces of capitalism, colonialism, and imperialism that restructure African history.

AFAM 157.title: Critical Race Theory
AFAM 157.description: Introduction to Critical Race Theory and key American cases on racial inequality. Using this literature, examines the possibilities and pitfalls of legal claims of race, gender, and sexuality discrimination in the age of colorblindness.
AFAM 157.restriction: African-American Studies majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

AFAM 159.title: Prisons and Public Education
AFAM 159.description: Looks at the connections between schools and prisons in the United States. Students learn about ideas that push beyond common trope of the “school to prison pipeline.”

AFAM 162W.title: The Black Protest Tradition
AFAM 162W.description: History and discourses of the black protest tradition. Traces emergence of black protest against racial slavery and white supremacy from the early colonial period to present and the complex elaboration of identity politics within black communities in the twentieth century.
AFAM 162W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

AFAM 198.title: Directed Group Study
AFAM 198.description: Special topics through directed reading. Paper required.

AFAM 199.title: Independent Study
AFAM 199.description: Investigation of special topics through directed reading. Paper required.

AI SCI 210.title: Introduction to Python Programming and Artificial Intelligence
AI SCI 210.description: Introduction to Python programming and artificial intelligence. Programming emphasis on techniques used in artificial intelligence. Jupyter Notebooks, NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib.

AI SCI 220.title: Methods in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
AI SCI 220.description: Fundamental concepts, algorithms, and techniques in machine learning, along with an overview of the necessary mathematics. Basic principles underlying regression, classification, and unsupervised learning.

AI SCI 230.title: Software Engineering and Data Visualization for Artificial Intelligence
AI SCI 230.description: Best practices of software engineering for machine learning and artificial intelligence. Effective data visualization and exploratory data analysis.

AI SCI 240.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
AI SCI 240.description: Key concepts of neural networks and deep learning. Selecting appropriate architecture, training, evaluation of neural networks. Convolutional neural networks, transformers.

AI SCI 285.title: Special Topics in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
AI SCI 285.description: Special topics in machine learning and artificial intelligence of particular relevance to applications in industry, including use of large-language models.

AI SCI 286.title: Research Topics in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
AI SCI 286.description: Research topics in machine learning and artificial intelligence. Emphasis on recent developments and applications in the physical sciences.

AI SCI 290A.title: Project Course A
AI SCI 290A.description: Fundamental concepts of artificial intelligence through programming projects. Data preprocessing, model evaluation, interpretation of results, managing large datasets, cloud-based resources.

AI SCI 290B.title: Project Course B
AI SCI 290B.description: Fundamental concepts of artificial intelligence through programming projects. Emphasis on adapting and applying state-of-the-art neural networks.

AI SCI 290C.title: Project Course C: Artificial Intelligence for Science Capstone
AI SCI 290C.description: Capstone project applying techniques from artificial intelligence to a problem related to the physical sciences.

AI SCI 294.title: Ethics in Data Science
AI SCI 294.description: Seminar on ethical issues related to machine learning and artificial intelligence.

AI SCI 295.title: Professional Development
AI SCI 295.description: Seminar preparing students for careers in artificial intelligence. CV/resume, portfolio, interview skills, the AI/ML job landscape.

ANATOMY 200.title: Research in Anatomy
ANATOMY 200.description: Individual research supervised by a particular faculty member.

ANATOMY 200R.title: Research in Anatomy and Neurobiology for First-Year Students
ANATOMY 200R.description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Anatomy and Neurobiology for first-year Ph.D. students.

ANATOMY 201.title: Human Gross Anatomy
ANATOMY 201.description: Study and dissection of the human body, including muscular, skeletal, nervous, and cardiovascular systems. Emphasis on both normal and abnormal structure and function.

ANATOMY 202B.title: Human Neuroscience
ANATOMY 202B.description: Study of the human nervous system at the systems level including the physiology and anatomy of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.
ANATOMY 202B.prereq_text: ANATOMY 202A with a minimum grade of B-.

ANATOMY 203A.title: Human Microscopoic Anatomy
ANATOMY 203A.description: Lecture and laboratory course on human microscopic anatomy. Emphasis is on functional implications of structure of cells and tissues.

ANATOMY 203B.title: Human Microscopoic Anatomy
ANATOMY 203B.description: Lecture and laboratory course on human microscopic anatomy. Emphasis is on functional implications of structure of cells and tissues.
ANATOMY 203B.prereq_text: ANATOMY 203A with a minimum grade of B-.

ANATOMY 206.title: Tutorial in Anatomy
ANATOMY 206.description: Series of tutorials on advanced topics in anatomy.

ANATOMY 206B.title: Neuroanatomy from a Systems Perspective: Humans to Rodents
ANATOMY 206B.description: Covers structures and pathways of the functional systems of the human brain (motor, sensory, visual, auditory, and limbic) and how these are represented in rodents, emphasizing circuitry involved in learning and memory, neurodegenerative disorders, and neurotrauma.

ANATOMY 206C.title: Tutorial in Microanatomy
ANATOMY 206C.description: Special topics in microanatomy. Primarily library work, but study of prepared histological slides and photographs included.

ANATOMY 210A.title: Systems Neuroscience
ANATOMY 210A.description: Study of the mammalian nervous system at the systems level. Anatomy and physiology of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.

ANATOMY 215.title: Epilepsy as a Window to Mechanisms of Neuronal Plasticity
ANATOMY 215.description: Understanding the mechanisms of brain disorders provides novel insights into the normal function of neurons and circuits. Discusses approaches to studying mechanisms of brain function ranging from imaging, the use of models and others to study epilepsy.

ANATOMY 227A.title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
ANATOMY 227A.description: Focuses on critical reading, presentation, and discussion of current literature in neuroscience research.

ANATOMY 227B.title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
ANATOMY 227B.description: Focuses on critical reading, presentation, and discussion of current literature in neuroscience research.

ANATOMY 227C.title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
ANATOMY 227C.description: Focuses on critical reading, presentation, and discussion of current literature in neuroscience research.

ANATOMY 230.title: Topics in Translational Neuroscience
ANATOMY 230.description: One-hour seminar presentation by participating faculty or guest lecturer and open to the science community, followed by one-hour student discussion of the lecture topic or related topic. Students are responsible for presentations and readings.
ANATOMY 230.restriction: Interdepartmental Neuroscience majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANATOMY 230A.title: Molecular, Cellular, & Developmental Neurobiology
ANATOMY 230A.description: Molecular aspects of the structure and function of neurons and glia including neurotransmission, synaptic modulation, and channels. Neural development at the cellular and molecular level including neurogenesis, pattern formation, trophic factors, axonal growth, and synaptic rearrangement.

ANATOMY 292A.title: Topics in Neural Circuit Mapping
ANATOMY 292A.description: Presentations/lectures by invited faculty and student discussion.

ANATOMY 292B.title: Scientific Communication
ANATOMY 292B.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

ANATOMY 292C.title: Scientific Communication
ANATOMY 292C.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

ANTHRO 2A.title: Introduction to Sociocultural Anthropology
ANTHRO 2A.description: Introduction to cultural diversity and the methods used by anthropologists to account for it. Family relations, economic activities, politics, gender, and religion in a wide range of societies. Stresses the application of anthropological methods to research problems.

ANTHRO 2B.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
ANTHRO 2B.description: Evolutionary theory and processes, comparative primate fossil record, human variation, and the adequacy of theory, and empirical data.

ANTHRO 2C.title: Introduction to Archaeology
ANTHRO 2C.description: Archaeological theory and cultural processes with emphasis on North American Indigenous and contemporary cultures in a global context.

ANTHRO 2D.title: Introduction to Language and Culture
ANTHRO 2D.description: Explores what the study of language can reveal about ourselves as bearers of culture. After introducing some basic concepts, examines how cultural knowledge is linguistically organized and how language might shape our perception of the world.

ANTHRO 10A.title: Probability and Statistics
ANTHRO 10A.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.
ANTHRO 10A.prereq_text: NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = F OR BETTER
ANTHRO 10A.restriction: Anthropology majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 10B.title: Probability and Statistics
ANTHRO 10B.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.
ANTHRO 10B.restriction: Anthropology majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 10C.title: Probability and Statistics
ANTHRO 10C.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.
ANTHRO 10C.restriction: Anthropology majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 20A.title: People, Cultures, and Environmental Sustainability
ANTHRO 20A.description: Anthropological consideration of global environmental sustainability from the perspective of human cultures and communities. Causes and consequences of population growth, natural resource management, environmental law, environmental ethics. Case studies emphasize tropical rain forests, arid lands of Africa and North America.

ANTHRO 25A.title: Environmental Injustice
ANTHRO 25A.description: Explores how pollution, climate change, and other environmental problems impact people around the world, often worsening social inequality. Students use social science frameworks to understand environmental problems, different interpretations of these problems, and how people have organized for political change.

ANTHRO 30A.title: Global Issues in Anthropological Perspective
ANTHRO 30A.description: Explores anthropological perspectives on issues of importance in an increasingly global society. Topics include emphases on ethnic conflict; identity; immigration and citizenship; religion and religious diversity; medical anthropology; legal anthropology; development and economic change; gender.
ANTHRO 30A.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 30C.title: Visual Anthropology
ANTHRO 30C.description: Focusing on the construction of culture through visuality, this course engages traditional ethnographic films, popular media and anthropological texts to analyze ethics, “reality” and fiction; propaganda and documentary, construction of a frame, the responsibility of the filmmaker, photographer, and anthropologist.

ANTHRO 41A.title: Global Cultures and Society
ANTHRO 41A.description: Offers a general overview of the rise of global interdependence in political, economic, demographic, and cultural terms. Considers what drove people from relative isolation into intensified intercourse with one another, and investigates the consequences of this shift.
ANTHRO 41A.restriction: Anthropology majors and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 45A.title: Science, Culture, Power
ANTHRO 45A.description: Examines science in historical and cultural context (Scientific and Darwinian Revolutions, Manhattan Project, contemporary biosciences) to understand scientific truths and their limits, scientists as social actors, and vital intersections of sciences with religion, politics, gender, and other forms of culture.

ANTHRO 48.title: Archaeology or Aliens?: Conspiracy, Pseudoscience, and the Emergence of Civilizations
ANTHRO 48.description: Archaeology has inspired (and sometimes actively encouraged) various theories about aliens, lost civilizations, dark conspiracies, and mysterious technologies. Does such an intimate relationship with these fantastic notions undermine archaeology and its claims of authoritative knowledge about past cultures?

ANTHRO 60.title: Global Themes in Sikh Studies
ANTHRO 60.description: Serves as an introduction to Sikhism and the field of Sikh Studies. Examines the development of the religious tradition and the formation of the scholarly field of Sikh Studies in the contemporary Western university.

ANTHRO 100A.title: Ethnography and Anthropological Methods
ANTHRO 100A.description: Anthropological research, learning ethnographic methods, and how to choose a research topic, construct research questions, explore library resources, collect data, and write an analytical paper on research findings.
ANTHRO 100A.restriction: Anthropology majors, Anthropology minors, and Medical Anthropology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 100B.title: Anthropology Careers
ANTHRO 100B.description: Gives students the skills and perspective needed to leverage undergraduate anthropology education in diverse career domains. Students explore different career domains (health care, tech development, environmental governance, etc.) and learn to represent themselves professionally.
ANTHRO 100B.restriction: Anthropology majors, Anthropology minors, and Medical Anthropology minors only.

ANTHRO 101.title: Anthropology at UCI
ANTHRO 101.description: Students learn the breadth of research by UCI’s Anthropology faculty and graduate students. Weekly meetings showcase a professor or graduate student’s work. Students have opportunities to read professor’s research, engage them in conversation, and learn their visions of anthropology’s future.

ANTHRO 121AW.title: Kinship and Social Organization
ANTHRO 121AW.description: Organization of social life primarily in preindustrial societies. Theories of kinship, marriage regulations, sexual behavior, and social roles. Comparisons of biological, psychological, sociological, and economic explanations of social organization.
ANTHRO 121AW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ANTHRO 121D.title: Sex, Gender, and Culture
ANTHRO 121D.description: The social construction of sex and gender. Themes include how race, class, and global inequities shape gender experiences; how power informs cultural understandings of sex/gender; and how gender structures politics and institutions in the U.S. and across the world.

ANTHRO 121J.title: Urban Anthropology
ANTHRO 121J.description: Cultural roles of cities and the processes of urbanization in a comparative perspective. Focus includes nonwestern, nonindustrial societies of past and present; the relationship between modern urban centers across different world regions. Themes covered include: inequality, race, migration, poverty, capitalism.

ANTHRO 122.title: Anthropology of Work
ANTHRO 122.description: Focuses on different kinds of labor that range from domestic and gardening work to transnational surrogacy and mothering work, even covering the entangled worlds of human, animal, and ecological workers to understand theories of life, exploitation, and resistance.

ANTHRO 124.title: Gold: The Alchemy of Socio-Economic Practice
ANTHRO 124.description: Before bitcoin, before derivatives and mortgage-backed securities, before even writing itself, there was gold. Explore gold’s role in the development of culture, politics, and power. From Pharaohs to modern financial wizards, gold has impacted and mediated social life.
ANTHRO 124.restriction: Anthropology majors, Economics majors, Anthropology minors, Archaeology minors, and Economics minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 125.title: Anthropology of Debt
ANTHRO 125.description: Explores how debt has shaped culture across varied contexts geographically and historically. In what ways have societies naturalized indebtedness, taken it for granted as a fact of life, and used it for organizing social relations.
ANTHRO 125.restriction: Anthropology majors, Economics majors, Anthropology minors, Archaeology minors, and Economics minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 125A.title: Economic Anthropology
ANTHRO 125A.description: Economic systems in comparative perspective: production, distribution, and consumption in market and non-market societies; agricultural development in the third world.
ANTHRO 125A.prereq_text: One course in general science, anthropology, economics, geography, or sociology.
ANTHRO 125A.restriction: Anthropology majors, Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors only.

ANTHRO 125F.title: Humans and Other Animals
ANTHRO 125F.description: Explores peoples' relationships with other animals, a topic that continues to shape anthropological understandings of humanness, culture, and the social. Subthemes: symbol and matter, nature/culture, ontologies, relations, moralities, ecologies, futures.

ANTHRO 125X.title: Transnational Migration
ANTHRO 125X.description: Examines the movement of people across national borders, governmentality and the role of state practices to control populations, and issues of citizenship, belonging, and identity. Examples are drawn from the United States, Europe, Latin America, Asia, and Africa.

ANTHRO 125Z.title: Arabs and Muslims in the US
ANTHRO 125Z.description: Offers a critical academic study of Islam in America, focusing on the core tenets of belief, the diversity of practices, and historical transformations that have taken place since the arrival of Muslims in the United States.

ANTHRO 126.title: Cultures of the Middle East
ANTHRO 126.description: The diversity of cultures and peoples who constitute the Middle East demonstrates the failure of much contemporary media and discourse to understand this region. Students learn about the broad scope of the contemporary Middle East through an ethnographic lens.
ANTHRO 126.restriction: Anthropology majors and Anthropology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 126A.title: Elite Cultures
ANTHRO 126A.description: The distinctive contribution that ethnographic studies have made to the understanding of elites past and present, in particular societies and globally.
ANTHRO 126A.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 127.title: Controversies, Courts, Cultures: The Anthropology of Law
ANTHRO 127.description: Assesses the contributions anthropology has made to legal scholarship, reviewing historical and contemporary themes. Considers both comparative questions of law’s norms, structures, and practices around the globe, and the specific insights anthropology offers about contemporary U.S. law.

ANTHRO 127C.title: Language and the Law
ANTHRO 127C.description: Considers the role of language in legal practice and power. Particular attention is paid to linguistic and discourse analytic research that cover topics such as: trial talk, language crimes, law talk in cross-cultural perspectives, and linguistic evidence.
ANTHRO 127C.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 127D.title: Anthropology of Law
ANTHRO 127D.description: Introduces the anthropological study of law through a focus on the foundations of this subfield, its primary methodologies, and several important topics of inquiry, including policing, immigration, and structural inequalities. Provides an international perspective on law and society.
ANTHRO 127D.restriction: Anthropology majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 127E.title: Law and Violence
ANTHRO 127E.description: Interrogates the historical and ongoing relationship between law and violence. How is the law employed to justify violence? Is the law itself a form of violence? Does the language used to describe violence matter for how it's addressed?

ANTHRO 128A.title: Science, Technology, Controversy
ANTHRO 128A.description: Explores ways in which the social sciences conceive of science as a sociocultural practice. Emphasis on literature in Science and Technology Studies (STS), especially writings that concern the relationship of science to space and place, power, and politics.

ANTHRO 128B.title: Race, Gender, and Science
ANTHRO 128B.description: Perfect for pre-health, science, and social science majors wanting to appreciate how science and society interact. Race and gender as biological and socio-cultural constructs are examined. Questions explored: What is disease? What is science? What are social and biological differences?

ANTHRO 128C.title: Digital Cultures
ANTHRO 128C.description: Explores cultural and political implications of the infotech revolution and the ways new media are used around the world, new cultural practices and spaces (e.g., cybercafes), debates surrounding the meanings of these new technologies, and their implications for transforming society.
ANTHRO 128C.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 128D.title: Science and Myth
ANTHRO 128D.description: Examines how science and myth may conflict but also reinforce, with complex ethical and political implications. Analyzes contemporary media representations of science, the cultural power of myths and narratives, and their devolution into conspiracy theories and disinformation.

ANTHRO 129.title: Special Topics: Social and Economic Anthropology
ANTHRO 129.description: Studies in selected areas of Social and Economic Anthropology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ANTHRO 129.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 132A.title: Psychological Anthropology
ANTHRO 132A.description: Cultural differences and similarities in personality and behavior. Child-rearing practices and consequent adult personality characteristics, biocultural aspects of child development and attachment, culture and behavior evolutionary models, politically linked personality, cognitive anthropology, psychology of narrative forms, comparative national character studies.
ANTHRO 132A.prereq_text: ANTHRO 2A or COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B).
ANTHRO 132A.restriction: Anthropology majors, Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychology majors, Anthropology minors, and Medical Anthropology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 134A.title: Medical Anthropology
ANTHRO 134A.description: Introduces students to cross-cultural perspectives and critical theories in anthropological studies of medicine. Special attention is given to diverse ways of understanding bodies, illnesses, and therapeutic practices in our changing world.

ANTHRO 134B.title: Cultures of Biomedicine
ANTHRO 134B.description: An introduction to the anthropolobical study of biomedicine and biotechnology. Topics include medicalization, experimentation and discovery, diagnosis, expertise, health activism, and biotechnology.

ANTHRO 134C.title: Medicine, Food, and Health
ANTHRO 134C.description: With anthropological studies of edible things as its foundation, this course explores topics related to the relationship between medical knowledge, eating, and health from a medical anthropological perspective.

ANTHRO 134F.title: Anthropology of the Body
ANTHRO 134F.description: Examines human bodies as both biological and sociocultural entities and explores the relationship among mind, body, and society cross-culturally. Topics include embodiment; race, sex, gender, and the body; somatization; control of the body; commodified bodies; and hybrid/cyborg bodies.

ANTHRO 134H.title: Anthropology of Food
ANTHRO 134H.description: Examines how food communicates ideas about ethnocentrism, disgust, privilege, gender, race, labor, social identities and hierarchies, globalization, power, and the "Western diet" and its health consequences.

ANTHRO 134I.title: Comics and Medicine
ANTHRO 134I.description: Patients, caregivers, and healers have increasingly described their illness experiences in comics format, offering therapeutic value for both producers and readers. Read and analyze comics about disability, chronic and mental illness, epidemics, caregiving, dementia, cancer, and health justice.

ANTHRO 134N.title: Disease, Health, and Inequality
ANTHRO 134N.description: Examines the relationships among disease, health, and social inequality in the U.S. and globally. Topics include infectious and chronic disease case studies, health policy, and strategies for promoting health equity.

ANTHRO 136A.title: Nationalism and Ethnicity in the Contemporary World
ANTHRO 136A.description: An exploration of the concepts of identity, culture, ethnicity, race, and nation through ethnographic cases, with a view to asking larger questions: how do people create nativeness and foreignness? How does "culture" get worked into contemporary racisms and nationalisms?

ANTHRO 136B.title: History of Anthropological Theory
ANTHRO 136B.description: Provides foundational knowledge in the discipline of anthropology by reviewing competing approaches in anthropological theory, from the 19th century to the present. Covers historically fundamental approaches—social evolutionism, functionalism—and recent movements such as feminism, cultural studies, poststructuralism, and postmodernism.
ANTHRO 136B.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 136D.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
ANTHRO 136D.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

ANTHRO 136G.title: Colonialism and Gender
ANTHRO 136G.description: An anthropological enquiry into the ways colonial relations of power have been structured and gendered throughout the world, and to what effect. Examines the social locations of men and women in the everyday exercise of colonial and imperial power.
ANTHRO 136G.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 136K.title: The Woman and the Body
ANTHRO 136K.description: Probes culture and politics of the female body in contemporary American life. Focusing on "feminine beauty," examines diverse notions of beauty, bodily practices, and body politics embraced by American women of different classes, ethnicities, and sexualities.

ANTHRO 138.title: Prisons and Public Education
ANTHRO 138.description: Looks at the connections between schools and prisons in the United States. Students learn about ideas that push beyond common trope of the “school to prison pipeline.”

ANTHRO 139.title: Special Topics in Cultural and Psychological Anthropology
ANTHRO 139.description: Studies in selected areas of Cultural and Psychological Anthropology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ANTHRO 139.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 140.title: Sex and Conquest in Latin America
ANTHRO 140.description: Competing ideas of masculinity and femininity, sexual violence, sexual identities, and gendered hierarchies informed how the Spanish engaged in military and religious domination of Mexican and Andean communities, as well as the forms of native resistance throughout colonial Latin America.

ANTHRO 141A.title: Ancient Civilization of Mexico and the Southwest
ANTHRO 141A.description: The prehistory and cultural evolution of the civilization which originated in Mexico, including the Olmecs, Aztecs, Toltecs, Maya, and Zapotec, as well as the Pueblos of the Southwestern U.S. Topics include the origins of food production and of the state.

ANTHRO 144.title: Archaeology of California
ANTHRO 144.description: Explores the archaeology of California, including evidence of human migration, the ancient environment and its management by Native Californians, European colonialism, the Gold Rush, global immigration, college campuses, Japanese incarceration camps, hippie communes, and the U.S.-Mexico border.

ANTHRO 145.title: Museums and Heritage
ANTHRO 145.description: Focuses on understanding the history of museums, practices of collecting and displaying material culture, the role of anthropology and museums in perpetuating or addressing colonialism, digital collections research, and museums as community-collaborative spaces.

ANTHRO 146.title: Consumption and Culture
ANTHRO 146.description: Our modern "society of the spectacle" often equates your consumption to your very humanity. Explores the ways in which our desire for things expresses our identity, politics, place within society, and how what we consume dominates social life.
ANTHRO 146.restriction: Anthropology majors and Anthropology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 147.title: Egyptomania
ANTHRO 147.description: An exploration into the archaeological heritage and cultures of ancient Egypt. Also examines how ancient Egypt became appropriated as a popular cultural phenomenon and site of scholarship in the centuries after the Pharaohs.
ANTHRO 147.restriction: Anthropology majors, Anthropology minors, and Archaeology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 147A.title: Archaeology of the Islamic World
ANTHRO 147A.description: The archaeological record connected with the Islamic tradition spans nearly 1,500 years and stretches from Spain to South East Asia. Working with artifacts and other materials, students learn about the sites and historical transformations associated with Islam and Muslim societies.
ANTHRO 147A.restriction: Anthropology majors, Anthropology minors, and Archaeology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 147B.title: Archaeology, Politics, and Identity
ANTHRO 147B.description: Archaeologists don’t excavate in a political vacuum. Their research has profound consequences for the ways in which people identify with and claim their cultural heritage. Examines archaeology’s role in constructing such identities through the traces of the past.
ANTHRO 147B.restriction: Anthropology majors, Anthropology minors, and Archaeology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 148.title: I Dig UCI
ANTHRO 148.description: An introduction to archaeological fieldwork through participation in an active excavation on campus. Students engage with research design and learn the foundational methods of archaeological recovery: survey, mapping, sampling strategies, documentation, excavation, artifact identification, and interpretation.

ANTHRO 149.title: Special Topics in Archaeology
ANTHRO 149.description: Studies in selected areas of Archaeology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ANTHRO 149.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 150A.title: Language and Social Cognition
ANTHRO 150A.description: Explores the relationship between language and cognition in social and cultural contexts. The overall goal is to think through how language structure and use impact how individuals perceive, think about, and understand the world around them.
ANTHRO 150A.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 151A.title: Improvisation, Language, and Culture
ANTHRO 151A.description: Addresses improvisation, both in performance and in everyday life. Examines improvisation as the "flexible regulation" of everyday behavior by exploring different scholarly treatments of language and interaction, and working on developing actual theatrical improvisation skills.

ANTHRO 152A.title: Language Origins: Evolution, Genetics, and the Brain
ANTHRO 152A.description: Examines how human language(s) may have originated. Studies pertinent techniques (reconstruction) and addresses related questions, including is our language faculty inborn (i.e., genetically encoded)? Can brain imaging and population genetics research help to unlock this mystery of human evolution?

ANTHRO 162A.title: Peoples and Cultures of Latin America
ANTHRO 162A.description: Surveys the prehistory of Latin America and its indigenous cultures, emphasizing the impact of colonial rule, capitalism, and 20th-century transformations. Emphasis on communities from several countries. In some years, emphasis on comparisons between the Latin American and Caribbean experiences.

ANTHRO 162B.title: Indian North America
ANTHRO 162B.description: A survey of indigenous peoples in North America: American Indians, Alaska Natives, First Nations, Native Americans. Tribal populations and geographic distributions, political and social organization, sovereignty, self-determination, intergovernmental relations; cultural continuity and change; management, preservation, development of environments/resources.

ANTHRO 162D.title: Anthropology of the United States
ANTHRO 162D.description: Examines anthropological research in and of the United States. Topics include race, class, identity, politics, law, and media.

ANTHRO 162E.title: Revolution and Memory in Latin America
ANTHRO 162E.description: Comparison of how Andeans resurrected the leaders of the Inca, a defeated indigenous empire, to contest the Spanish empire with how enslaved Africans, with their descendants and others, defeated Spanish colonial rule in what would become the Cuban nation.

ANTHRO 163A.title: Peoples of the Pacific
ANTHRO 163A.description: The cultural history and recent developments among the Pacific peoples of Polynesia, Micronesia, Melanesia, New Guinea, and Australia.

ANTHRO 164P.title: Peoples and Cultures of Post-Soviet Eurasia
ANTHRO 164P.description: Examines the cultures and political conflicts of the more than 130 indigenous ethnic groups in the European and Asian territories of the former U.S.S.R. Emphasis is on the theoretical issues of ethnicity, nationalism, and conflict management.

ANTHRO 165A.title: Modern Iran: Cinema and the City
ANTHRO 165A.description: Exploring modern Iran through film, literature, photography, travel writing, and philosophy and social science texts that introduce students to important concepts in post-colonial studies, social thought, war culture, religion, and media as experienced through the paradigm of a non-Western modernity.

ANTHRO 167.title: United States Material Culture
ANTHRO 167.description: Considers the recent history of the United States through material culture as a lens to understand power, race, colonialism, gender, religion, and other aspects of identity. Weekly themes include ceramics, glass, and metals, stone, food, bodies, and toys.

ANTHRO 169.title: Special Topics in Area Studies
ANTHRO 169.description: Studies in selected areas of Anthropology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ANTHRO 169.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 180AW.title: Anthropology Majors Writing Seminar
ANTHRO 180AW.description: Anthropological theory designed especially for majors in Anthropology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ANTHRO 180AW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ANTHRO H190A.title: Honors Research Design
ANTHRO H190A.description: Students design a research project and articulate its goals and significance. Written work consists of a research proposal describing the research questions, the relevant literature, methods of data collection and analysis, and ethical considerations.

ANTHRO H190B.title: Honors Field Research
ANTHRO H190B.description: Students begin or continue ethnographic field research and gain experience with a variety of data collection methods, including participant-observation, interviews, surveys, and the study of archival and documentary materials.

ANTHRO H190C.title: Honors Research Analysis
ANTHRO H190C.description: Students apply qualitative data analysis techniques to ethnographic data collected as part of their Honors research.
ANTHRO H190C.prereq_text: ANTHRO H190B and ANTHRO 199. Anthropology Honors ONLY.

ANTHRO H190W.title: Honors Thesis Writing
ANTHRO H190W.description: Students draft a senior honors thesis (typically) with the following sections: problem statement, literature review, ethnographic background, and descriptions of the methods, results, and conclusions.
ANTHRO H190W.prereq_text: ANTHRO H190C and ANTHRO 199. Anthropology Honors ONLY. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ANTHRO 202A.title: Proseminar in Anthropology
ANTHRO 202A.description: Year-long intensive introduction to the history of anthropological thought and reading in classical and contemporary ethnography for first-year graduate students.

ANTHRO 202B.title: Proseminar in Anthropology
ANTHRO 202B.description: Year-long intensive introduction to the history of anthropological thought and reading in classical and contemporary ethnography for first-year graduate students.
ANTHRO 202B.prereq_text: ANTHRO 202A with a minimum grade of B-.

ANTHRO 202C.title: Proseminar in Anthropology
ANTHRO 202C.description: Year-long intensive introduction to the history of anthropological thought and reading in classical and contemporary ethnography for first-year graduate students.
ANTHRO 202C.prereq_text: ANTHRO 202B with a minimum grade of B-.

ANTHRO 204A.title: Proseminar in Medicine, Science, and Technology
ANTHRO 204A.description: Explores the phenomena studied by "medical anthropology" and "science and technology studies" are inextricably linked, and how understanding formations requires moving between disparate fields of inquiry. Required for students pursuing a Graduate Certificate in Anthropoligies of Medicine, Science, and Technology.
ANTHRO 204A.restriction: Students pursuing a Graduate Certification in Anthropoligies of Medicine, Science, and Technology have first consideration for enrollment.

ANTHRO 215A.title: Ethnographic Methods
ANTHRO 215A.description: Exposes students to diverse methods, both traditional and experimental, used in anthropological ethnographic research. Students gain experience practicing diverse methods, and learn to select methods appropriate to particular study designs and contexts.

ANTHRO 215B.title: Research Design
ANTHRO 215B.description: Introduces research design for anthropology, including concept work and mapping, research topic and aims development, research question construction, and fieldwork planning.
ANTHRO 215B.prereq_text: ANTHRO 215A with a minimum grade of B-.

ANTHRO 215C.title: Grant and Proposal Writing
ANTHRO 215C.description: Focuses on production, critique, and revision of student research proposals. A practical seminar designed to improve student proposals, help students through the application processes, and increase students' chances of obtaining support for their research.
ANTHRO 215C.prereq_text: ANTHRO 215B with a minimum grade of B-.

ANTHRO 220.title: Pedagogy and Professionalization in Anthropology
ANTHRO 220.description: Introduces students to pedagogical approaches in anthropology, fostering professional development in and beyond academia, and providing general advice about teaching and mentorship. Periodically invites authors of the reviewed texts to participate in classroom conversation.

ANTHRO 230F.title: Ethnography
ANTHRO 230F.description: Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies.

ANTHRO 235A.title: Transnational Migration
ANTHRO 235A.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

ANTHRO 236.title: Black Ethnography in the Anthropological Imagination
ANTHRO 236.description: What is ethnography? Rather than an existential question, students cull through the history of the field and understand the very oft-problematic stance of ethnography to construction of particular types of blackness.

ANTHRO 245A.title: Seminar in Political Anthropology
ANTHRO 245A.description: Explores anthropological approaches to politics. Covers a range of issues and topics, including: theories of culture, power, and hegemony; approaches to colonial and post-colonial relations of global inequality; and ethnographic approaches to the modern state.

ANTHRO 246.title: Feminist Anthropology
ANTHRO 246.description: Examines feminist anthropology’s rise as an interdisciplinary field. Paying special attention to issues of power, subjectivity, and authority in the research encounter, feminist anthropologists’ major contributions to ethnography, gender studies, queer studies, and cultural anthropology are surveyed.

ANTHRO 247A.title: Structuralism and Post-Structuralism
ANTHRO 247A.description: Traces recent theoretical discussions and arguments over the philosophical and historical "subject" from structuralist decenterings toward the characteristically "post-structuralist" contemporary concern with the historical and political constitution of subjectivities and subject positions.

ANTHRO 248.title: Archival Violence
ANTHRO 248.description: Synthesizes the multifaceted nature of the archive as both an object/tool of western ontological warcraft and as a driver/accelerator of difference making.

ANTHRO 249A.title: Humanism and Posthumanism
ANTHRO 249A.description: Examines alternative forms of human, humanisms, and posthumanisms to explore the inherent ambiguities and shifting boundaries of knowing and being human, and to venture into modes of analysis that problematize the universality and globality of liberal humanism.

ANTHRO 252A.title: Queer Anthropology
ANTHRO 252A.description: Explores historical and contemporary scholarship that employs ethnographic approaches to address the discursive construction of sexuality. Also examines how the discipline of anthropology has been shaped by the study of sexuality.

ANTHRO 253A.title: Design, Aesthetics, and Social Life
ANTHRO 253A.description: Anthropology has only recently recognized that design demands consideration as a cultural form linked to, yet nonetheless distinct from, other aesthetic endeavors. Largely oriented toward collaboratively working out a conceptual basis for a distinctly anthropological approach to design.

ANTHRO 254.title: Digital Anthropology
ANTHRO 254.description: Examines “the digital” from an anthropological perspective by exploring ethnographic research on digital culture and using anthropological frameworks to approach the digital and the human. Readings are interdisciplinary, including work from history and communications.

ANTHRO 255A.title: Disability Worlds
ANTHRO 255A.description: Explores disability from a range of methodological and theoretical perspectives. Examines the genealogy of disability in anthropology and related disciplines, with an emphasis on ethnographic work. Topics addressed include access, embodiment, politics, selfhood, and sexuality.

ANTHRO 256A.title: Ethnographies of Technology
ANTHRO 256A.description: Surveys current ethnographic research pertaining to technologies, technical systems, and infrastructures.

ANTHRO 256B.title: Secrecy, Security, and Surveillance
ANTHRO 256B.description: Explores secrecy and security as fundamental to constructions of public and private domains, relations of citizenship and sovereignty, the militarization of everyday life, and the ways that the fabrics of societies are woven of both trust and deceit.

ANTHRO 259A.title: Dissertation Writing Seminar
ANTHRO 259A.description: Intended for advanced, post-fieldwork Anthropology graduate students. Emphasis on the presentation of research design and results, problems of ethnographic writing, and qualitative and quantitative data and analysis. Prerequisites: post-fieldwork; graduate standing in Anthropology or consent of instructor.

ANTHRO 260.title: Critical Medical Anthropology
ANTHRO 260.description: Reading-intensive graduate seminar offers an overview of theoretical and ethnographic approaches to illness and healing in different settings, while also studying the political economic distribution of risks that contribute to disease. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.

ANTHRO 261.title: Anthropology of the Mind
ANTHRO 261.description: Reading-intensive graduate seminar looks at emergence of mind/soul in modern age and similar concepts across cultural and historical contexts; studies psychiatric anthropological approaches to trauma, the subconscious, dreaming, madness. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.

ANTHRO 263.title: Black Political Theory in the United States
ANTHRO 263.description: Black Political Theory analyzes the development of Black political ideologies and the strategic processes by which Black people in the United States have attained freedom.

ANTHRO 263A.title: Prisons in the United States
ANTHRO 263A.description: Analyzes, deconstructs social relations and posits new realities with respect to interlocking violence that is levied against Black people in the form of prisons in the United States of America.

ANTHRO 264.title: Literary Anthropology
ANTHRO 264.description: Looks at genre-blending between creative nonfiction, ethnography, fiction, memoir and other forms of expression, interrogating the boundary between literature and ethnography.

ANTHRO 270.title: Transformative Teaching in Higher Education
ANTHRO 270.description: Introduces graduate students to the theoretical and practical aspects of teaching and learning in higher education. Topics include critical and liberatory pedagogies; theories of learning; course design and instructional strategies; inclusive teaching; and teaching in academic careers.

ANTHRO 289.title: Special Topics in Anthropology
ANTHRO 289.description: Studies in selected areas of Anthropology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ARABIC 1A.title: Fundamentals of Arabic
ARABIC 1A.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Arabic. Using real world texts, provides a firm foundation in the orthography, grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of Modern Standard Arabic. Introduces students to Arab world cultures.
ARABIC 1A.restriction: ARABIC 1A and ARABIC S1AB may not be taken for full credit.

ARABIC 1B.title: Fundamentals of Arabic
ARABIC 1B.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Arabic. Using real world texts, provides a firm foundation in the orthography, grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of Modern Standard Arabic. Introduces students to Arab world cultures.
ARABIC 1B.prereq_text: ARABIC 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARABIC 1B is also accepted.
ARABIC 1B.restriction: ARABIC 1B and ARABIC S1AB and ARABIC S1BC may not be taken for full credit.

ARABIC 1C.title: Fundamentals of Arabic
ARABIC 1C.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Arabic. Using real world texts, provides a firm foundation in the orthography, grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of Modern Standard Arabic. Introduces students to Arab world cultures.
ARABIC 1C.prereq_text: ARABIC 1B with a minimum grade of C or ARABIC S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement is also accepted.

ARABIC 2A.title: Intermediate Arabic Language and Culture
ARABIC 2A.description: Designed for students to advance their Arabic language skills to intermediate level. Students will develop their understanding of grammar and syntax to a more sophisticated level. Facilitates intermediate-level reading, writing, and speaking skills. Fosters college-level cultural literacy.
ARABIC 2A.prereq_text: ARABIC 1C with a minimum grade of C or ARABIC S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARABIC 2A is also accepted.
ARABIC 2A.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ARABIC 2B.title: Intermediate Arabic Language and Culture
ARABIC 2B.description: Designed for students to advance their Arabic language skills to intermediate level. Students will develop their understanding of grammar and syntax to a more sophisticated level. Facilitates intermediate-level reading, writing, and speaking skills. Fosters college-level cultural literacy.
ARABIC 2B.prereq_text: ARABIC 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARABIC 2B is also accepted.
ARABIC 2B.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ARABIC 2C.title: Intermediate Arabic Language and Culture
ARABIC 2C.description: Designed for students to advance their Arabic language skills to intermediate level. Students will develop their understanding of grammar and syntax to a more sophisticated level. Facilitates intermediate-level reading, writing, and speaking skills. Fosters college-level cultural literacy.
ARABIC 2C.prereq_text: ARABIC 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARABIC 2C is also accepted.
ARABIC 2C.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ARABIC 10A.title: Arabic Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
ARABIC 10A.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. ARABIC 10A is for language mentors.

ARABIC 10B.title: Arabic Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
ARABIC 10B.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. ARABIC 10B is for language mentees.

ARABIC 15A.title: Conversational Arabic
ARABIC 15A.description: Introductory colloquial Arabic course for students with little or no prior experience. Develops basic spoken communication, pronunciation, alphabet recognition, essential vocabulary, and grammar with exposure to common dialects and cultural practices.

ARABIC 15B.title: Conversational Arabic
ARABIC 15B.description: Low-intermediate colloquial Arabic course for students with limited prior experience. Strengthens spoken communication, expands vocabulary and grammar control, and builds the ability to sustain conversations across commonly used dialects.
ARABIC 15B.prereq_text: ARABIC 15A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARABIC 15B is also accepted.

ARABIC 15C.title: Conversational Arabic
ARABIC 15C.description: Intermediate colloquial Arabic course for students with prior foundational experience. Advances conversational fluency through more complex dialogues while refining pronunciation, vocabulary range, and grammatical accuracy across commonly used dialects.
ARABIC 15C.prereq_text: ARABIC 15B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARABIC 15C is also accepted.

ARABIC 51.title: Introduction to the Koran
ARABIC 51.description: An introduction to understanding the Koran and its significance to Muslim life, culture, and history. An overview of scholarly traditions related to the Koran, and its critics. Close readings of the Koran in English translation.

ARMN 1A.title: Elementary Armenian
ARMN 1A.description: Written and conversational Armenian for students with no knowledge of the language. Students learn the Armenian alphabet, read and comprehend simple texts, and carry basic conversation. Emphasis on reading and comprehension, grammar rules, and basic composition.

ARMN 1B.title: Elementary Armenian
ARMN 1B.description: Continues development of the fundamentals of Armenian, including comprehension, reading of simple texts, basic conversation, and writing with a fair degree of grammatical correctness. Students learn basic reading, writing, and sentence structure through lectures, games, and assignments.
ARMN 1B.prereq_text: ARMN 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARMN 1B is also accepted.

ARMN 1C.title: Elementary Armenian
ARMN 1C.description: Focus on building grammatical knowledge of the Armenian language and developing skills in reading, writing, listening, and speaking. Includes a strong emphasis on expanding vocabulary and developing oral proficiency in higher/formal registers.
ARMN 1C.prereq_text: ARMN 1B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARMN 1C is also accepted.

ARMN 2A.title: Intermediate Armenian
ARMN 2A.description: Designed to develop students’ ability to communicate further orally and in writing in Armenian (Western or Eastern) by consolidating knowledge of grammar, increasing vocabulary, and developing reading, comprehension, and writing.
ARMN 2A.prereq_text: ARMN 1C with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARMN 2A is also accepted.

ARMN 2B.title: Intermediate Armenian
ARMN 2B.description: Designed to develop students’ ability to communicate further orally and in writing in Armenian (Western or Eastern) by consolidating knowledge of grammar, increasing vocabulary, and developing reading, comprehension, and writing.
ARMN 2B.prereq_text: ARMN 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARMN 2B is also accepted.

ARMN 2C.title: Intermediate Armenian
ARMN 2C.description: Designed to develop students’ ability to communicate further orally and in writing in Armenian (Western or Eastern) by consolidating knowledge of grammar, increasing vocabulary, and developing reading, comprehension, and writing.
ARMN 2C.prereq_text: ARMN 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into ARMN 2C is also accepted.

ARMN 197.title: Armenian Studies Internship
ARMN 197.description: Students learn to translate their knowledge about Armenian history and culture and their interest in Armenian Studies into practical applications by working closely with the Center for Armenian Studies and through community engagement.

ARMN 199.title: Independent Study
ARMN 199.description: Investigation of special topics through directed reading. Paper required.

ART 1A.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
ART 1A.description: First in a three-quarter foundation sequence introducing students to a broad range of contemporary art, media, and practices in relation to their 20th-century cultural and historical antecedents. ART 1A deals specifically with contemporary painting and photography.
ART 1A.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 1B.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
ART 1B.description: Deals with film/video/performance. Concerned with the development of modern/contemporary film, video, and performance, with a focus on experimental and avant-garde production from the early 20th century to today.
ART 1B.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 1C.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
ART 1C.description: Third in a three-quarter foundation sequence introducing students to a broad range of contemporary art, media, and practice in relation to their 20th-century cultural and historical antecedents. Deals specifically with space and cyberspace.
ART 1C.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 8.title: Changing Creativity
ART 8.description: Explores creativity as a changing concept in historical and contemporary terms from the perspectives of producers, consumers, and institutions. Encompasses international perspectives and the role of new technologies in considering creativity as a resource for innovation and social change.

ART 9A.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology
ART 9A.description: Examines creative activities in all spheres of life, including the "artistic" impulses that dwell in the individual. Culture is addressed in broad terms of the many institutions and cultural forces that shape everyday activities of listening, seeing, doing.
ART 9A.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 9B.title: Visual Culture: A Culture Divided
ART 9B.description: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, controversies flourished in the mainstream media over purportedly obscene art, anti-American writing, and moral decay, among other issues. Examines these new conflicts as they manifest themselves in public life and everyday experience.
ART 9B.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 9C.title: Visual Culture: Thematic Investigations
ART 9C.description: Considers a broad range of concerns and questions raised by various acts of appropriation in contemporary art and visual culture, such as originality, authenticity, authorship, translation, audience and aesthetics, temporal dimensions of a work, and context.
ART 9C.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 9D.title: Visual Culture: Graffiti as Art and Language
ART 9D.description: Examines how graffiti art transforms urban landscapes and serves as a powerful means of global communication and cultural expression.

ART 11A.title: Topics in History of Contemporary Art
ART 11A.description: Surveys mid-19th and 20th-century art production, from modernity through post-modernity, in a historical and cultural context.

ART 12A.title: Art, Design, and Electronic Culture
ART 12A.description: Introduction to historical and theoretical foundations of digital media art, tracing how information technologies seeded growth of new expressive medium. Considers how today's pervasive digital culture evolved through interdisciplinary collaborations between artists, engineers, scientists, scholars.

ART 12B.title: Cultural History of the Anthropocene
ART 12B.description: A survey of the ongoing interactions between technological and social change through the 19th century and 20th century, with special attention to the history of computing, changing arts and cultural practices, and the idea of the Anthropocene.

ART 12C.title: Intelligences of Arts
ART 12C.description: Introduces contemporary neuroscience and new approaches to cognition – embodied, enactive, extended, situated, distributed. Reviews the history of related ethological, biological, psychological, technological, and philosophical traditions. Considers arts and cultural practices from these and other perspectives, and considers case studies.

ART 20A.title: Basic Drawing I
ART 20A.description: Encourages an investigation of the premises and limits of drawing, primarily, but not inevitably, as a two-dimensional medium. Includes slide presentations and discussions of the historical uses of a wide range of drawing. Materials Fee
ART 20A.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 30A.title: Basic Painting I
ART 30A.description: Examination of the fundamental components of painting: color, form, space, surface, scale, and content. Studio work, slide presentations, and critiques of student work. Materials Fee
ART 30A.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 30B.title: Basic Painting II
ART 30B.description: Further examinations of the essential qualities of painting: color, form, space, surface, scale, and content. Studio work, slide presentations, and critiques of student work. Materials Fee
ART 30B.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 40.title: Beginning Sculpture
ART 40.description: The practice of sculpture in the contemporary arts; inclusion of spatial interventions, site-specific and environmental design, appropriation of found materials; techniques in cutting joining, and assembly of wood, metals, and plastics. May include casting, welding, and ceramics. Materials Fee
ART 40.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 50A.title: Matter and Media
ART 50A.description: A project-based introduction to tools and approaches for creating and sharing digital media content within internet-mediated social environments, with a particular emphasis on art-making and personal expression. Includes an overview of basic user experience and interaction design principles.

ART 50B.title: Interaction and Experience
ART 50B.description: An overview of digital video and audio production for the Web, emphasizing art-making and personal expression. Includes digital media aesthetics and conceptual design, basic audio and video recording, and fundamentals of desktop video, audio, and Web authoring software applications.

ART 51.title: Basic Ceramic Sculpture
ART 51.description: Exploration of use of clay as sculptural basis with an emphasis on development of an idea and its relation to contemporary and experimental art practice. Hand-building, glazing, finishing processes, and use of other structural materials. Materials Fee
ART 51.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 65A.title: Foundations in Media Design
ART 65A.description: Provides an overview of media design in the digital age, covering principles of design for different media (2D, time-based, interactive); history of relationship between art and design; and practice in working with different design approaches. Materials Fee
ART 65A.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 65B.title: Foundations in Internet Art and Design
ART 65B.description: Introduction to creating art for the Internet, covering history and structure of networks; key types of net-based interactivity; basics of Web design and scripting. Materials Fee
ART 65B.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 65C.title: Gizmology and Kinetics
ART 65C.description: Provides students with basic skills in materials, construction and design applicable to making machines, musical instruments and things with moving parts enabling work in kinetic sculpture, custom interactive systems, Mechatronics, Robotics, and Maker/DIY culture. Materials Fee

ART 71A.title: Introduction to Photography I
ART 71A.description: Introduction to technical underpinnings emphasizing photography as a contemporary art practice. Topics include 35mm non-automatic camera operation, exposure and lighting, black and white printing, introduction to digital photography, discussion of critical and historical issues. Materials Fee
ART 71A.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 71B.title: Introduction to Photography II
ART 71B.description: Techniques covered include medium and large format cameras, digital photography, studio lighting, digital and analog color printing, mural room. Conceptual direction is developed through critiques, critical readings, discussions, slide lectures. Materials Fee
ART 71B.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 81.title: Beginning Video
ART 81.description: Offers an introduction to the experimental histories and contemporary practices of video art with training in video, audio, lighting equipment, and editing software. Screenings, readings, and discussions engage issues of installation, representation, technology, and critical media literacy. Materials Fee
ART 81.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 91.title: Basic Performance Art
ART 91.description: Exploration of objects, gesture, action, text, image, and media to create narrative or non-narrative works. Elements of theory and history of performance art are discussed to illustrate techniques and styles to understand, identify, and articulate artistic vision and voice.
ART 91.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 95.title: Special Topics in Basic Media
ART 95.description: Basic instruction in media or disciplines not otherwise represented in the regular curriculum. Topics vary according to the instructor.
ART 95.restriction: Art majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ART 101W.title: Artists as Writers
ART 101W.description: Contemporary art practice involves text, as final form or an integral element. Many contemporary artists consider writing as essential to their practice. Covers historical and contemporary uses of text and image as well as artists' writing.
ART 101W.prereq_text: ART 9A and ART 11A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ART 101W.restriction: Art majors only. No Campuswide Honors Collegium students.

ART 106A.title: Programming for Artists
ART 106A.description: Programming as a means to create interactive artworks with an emphasis on the integration of video, sound, text, and stills. Topics include basic concepts in programming, understanding the limits of code, working with video and audio files, and interface design. Materials Fee

ART 108.title: Advanced Video
ART 108.description: Students learn to conceive, develop, and produce original video works building directly upon previously learned skills. Use of video stage and post-production editing facilities. Lectures on video/film subjects, production strategies, readings, screening, field trips, and group critiques. Materials Fee

ART 109.title: Performance and the Camera
