BIO SCI D111L.description: Covers the division of cells, isolate cellular organelles (chloroplasts, mitochondria, nuclei), and follows changes in cells undergoing programmed cell death. Development is demonstrated in experiments showing cooperation of individual cells in forming a multicellular organism. Materials Fee
BIO SCI D111L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and (BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104).
BIO SCI D111L.restriction: Seniors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, Genetics majors, Developmental and Cell Biology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E112L.title: Physiology Laboratory
BIO SCI E112L.description: Laboratory with a focus on the whole organism and its organ systems. Examples of structure-function relationships are drawn from both animal and human physiology. Cellular and molecular aspects are introduced as required. Materials Fee
BIO SCI E112L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and (BIO SCI E109 or (BME 120 and BME 121)).
BIO SCI E112L.restriction: Seniors, Exercise Sciences majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI M112.title: Microbiology and Immunology Seminar
BIO SCI M112.description: Microbiology and Immunology majors attend weekly seminar on current microbiology and immunology research at UCI, career pathways, post-graduate programs, and other select topics.

BIO SCI D113.title: Genetics Majors Seminar
BIO SCI D113.description: Genetics majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.
BIO SCI D113.prereq_text: NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = C OR BETTER (see SOC comments for repeat policy)

BIO SCI N113L.title: Neurobiology Laboratory
BIO SCI N113L.description: An in-depth exploration into biology and physiology of the nervous system. Labs include neuroanatomy, electrophysiology, pharmacology, behavior, experimental design, EEG, and scientific writing. Materials Fee
BIO SCI N113L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and (BIO SCI N110 (may be taken concurrently) or BIO SCI N115A (may be taken concurrently)).
BIO SCI N113L.restriction: Seniors, Neurobiology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI D114.title: Developmental and Cell Biology Majors Seminar
BIO SCI D114.description: Developmental and Cell Biology majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.
BIO SCI D114.restriction: Developmental and Cell Biology majors only.

BIO SCI M114.title: Advanced Biochemistry
BIO SCI M114.description: Physical-chemical properties of macromolecules. Structure-function relationships in nucleic acids, protein, carbohydrates, and lipids. Integration and regulation of metabolism. Biochemistry of organs and biochemistry of diseases.

BIO SCI M114L.title: Biochemistry Laboratory
BIO SCI M114L.description: Properties of enzymes and the culture and isolation of mutants of microorganisms. Materials Fee
BIO SCI M114L.prereq_text: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108).
BIO SCI M114L.restriction: Seniors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology majors, Microbiology and Immunology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E115L.title: Evolution Laboratory
BIO SCI E115L.description: Students perform experiments which illustrate important concepts in evolutionary biology such as natural selection, random genetic drift, inbreeding, age-specific selection, sexual selection, and phylogenetic reconstruction. Materials Fee
BIO SCI E115L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
BIO SCI E115L.restriction: Seniors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI M115.title: Allied Health Microbiology
BIO SCI M115.description: Introductory microbiology lecture and laboratory with an emphasis on microbial growth control and the relationship between microbes and human health.
BIO SCI M115.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93) and CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C-.
BIO SCI M115.restriction: School of Nursing students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N115A.title: Advanced Neurobiology I
BIO SCI N115A.description: In-depth coverage of neurobiology, ranging from molecular neurobiology to functional brain imaging. Discussion of molecular, cellular, and developmental neurobiology.

BIO SCI N115B.title: Advanced Neurobiology II
BIO SCI N115B.description: In-depth coverage of neurobiology, ranging from molecular neurobiology to functional brain imaging. Discussion of systems and behavioral neurobiology.

BIO SCI M116.title: Advanced Molecular Biology
BIO SCI M116.description: Mechanisms of gene expression; special emphasis on regulatory events that occur in Eukaryotic organisms other than initiation of transcription. Chromatin structure and rearrangement, RNA polymerases, cis- and trans-acting elements, RNA processing, transport and stability, protein synthesis, trafficking, and turnover.

BIO SCI M116L.title: Molecular Biology Laboratory
BIO SCI M116L.description: Students perform experiments which illustrate the chemical and biological properties of nucleic acids. Emphasis is placed on recent techniques in recombinant DNA technology including gene isolation and characterization. Materials Fee
BIO SCI M116L.prereq_text: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108).
BIO SCI M116L.restriction: Seniors, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology majors, Microbiology and Immunology majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E117A.title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
BIO SCI E117A.description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
BIO SCI E117A.prereq_text: (BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120) and BIO SCI E183 and BIO SCI E112L.

BIO SCI E117B.title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
BIO SCI E117B.description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.

BIO SCI E117C.title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
BIO SCI E117C.description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.

BIO SCI N117.title: Introduction to Neuroscience Clinical Trials
BIO SCI N117.description: Provides an overview of the science of clinical development of treatments for neurological disease and injury.

BIO SCI E118.title: Ecosystem Ecology
BIO SCI E118.description: A mechanistic perspective on ecosystem processes. Covers ecosystem development, element cycling, and interactions with plants and microbes. The role of ecosystems in environmental change is also addressed.
BIO SCI E118.prereq_text: BIO SCI E106 or EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 60A or CHEM 51C.
BIO SCI E118.restriction: Earth System Science majors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and Environmental Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI M118L.title: Experimental Microbiology Laboratory
BIO SCI M118L.description: Introductory general microbiology designed for preprofessional biology majors. Includes microscopy, cultivation of bacteria, morphological and biochemical characterization of bacteria, microbial metabolism, growth and genetics, microorganisms and human disease, and interactions of microorganisms with the environment. Materials Fee
BIO SCI M118L.prereq_text: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108).
BIO SCI M118L.restriction: Seniors, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology majors, Microbiology and Immunology majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E119.title: Selfish DNA
BIO SCI E119.description: Focuses on the genetics and evolution of selfish DNA, and introduces necessary background knowledge from molecular biology, cytogenetics, and bioinformatics.
BIO SCI E119.prereq_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H94 or BIO SCI H97.

BIO SCI M119.title: Advanced Topics in Immunology
BIO SCI M119.description: Literature-based, interactive discussions focused on review of seminal historic and recent immunology literature. Student responsibilities include reading, critical evaluation, and discussion of manuscripts.
BIO SCI M119.restriction: Microbiology and Immunology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N119.title: History of Neuroscience
BIO SCI N119.description: An overview of the conceptual and technical foundations of contemporary neuroscience from ancient times to the present. The subjects include synapses, neurons, brain organization, sensory, motor and regulatory systems, learning and memory, human brain function and dysfunction.
BIO SCI N119.prereq_text: BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or PSCI 115D or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 9C).
BIO SCI N119.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI D120.title: Bioimaging and Spatial Biotechnology
BIO SCI D120.description: Covers the theory, history, and application of light microscopy, electron microscopy, and spatial biotechniques in a non-mathematical way. Starts with principles of various microscopes, and discusses recent innovations in imaging techniques such as super-resolution microscopy.
BIO SCI D120.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E120.title: Marine Biology
BIO SCI E120.description: Examines the biotic and abiotic factors influencing the physiology, distribution, abundances, interactions, and evolution of marine organisms and the roles of those organisms in mediating ecosystem services and functions. A field trip is required. Materials Fee
BIO SCI E120.prereq_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94.

BIO SCI N120A.title: Human Biology I
BIO SCI N120A.description: Provides an in-depth look at cutting-edge topics in physiology and epidemiology as they relate to global issues of ethics, anthropology, and socioeconomics, providing the student with an understanding of human health beyond basic biological function.

BIO SCI N120B.title: Human Biology II
BIO SCI N120B.description: Provides an in-depth look at cutting-edge topics in physiology and epidemiology as they relate to global issues of ethics, anthropology, and socioeconomics, providing the student with an understanding of human health beyond basic biological function.

BIO SCI N120C.title: Human Biology III
BIO SCI N120C.description: Provides an in-depth look at cutting-edge topics in physiology and epidemiology as they relate to global issues of ethics, anthropology, and socioeconomics, providing the student with an understanding of human health beyond basic biological function.

BIO SCI M121.title: Immunology with Hematology
BIO SCI M121.description: Antibodies, antigens, antigen-antibody reactions, cells and tissues of lymphoreticular and hematopoietic systems, and individual and collective components of cell-mediated and humoral immune response.

BIO SCI M121L.title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory
BIO SCI M121L.description: Emphasis is placed on learning modern techniques in immunology such as ELISAs, western blotting, and immunofluorescent staining assays. Materials Fee
BIO SCI M121L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI M121.
BIO SCI M121L.restriction: Seniors, Microbiology and Immunology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N121.title: Drug Addiction
BIO SCI N121.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of topics in the addiction field, including drug pharmacology, models/approaches to investigate addiction, brain circuits, genetics, epigenetics, and the cellular and molecular biology of drug addiction.

BIO SCI M122.title: General Microbiology
BIO SCI M122.description: Comparative metabolism of small molecules and cell structure and relationship to microbial classification. Macromolecule synthesis and regulation, sporulation, cell division, growth, and effect of antibiotics.
BIO SCI M122.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N122.title: Scientific Argumentation and Critical Thinking
BIO SCI N122.description: Explicitly teaches argument structure, deductive logic, inductive logic, and common fallacies in the biology context. Students identify assumptions and fallacies in faulty arguments and data figures and learn to compose sound arguments.
BIO SCI N122.prereq_text: BIO SCI 93. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

BIO SCI M123.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
BIO SCI M123.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
BIO SCI M123.prereq_text: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8.

BIO SCI N123L.title: Human Neuroimaging Lab
BIO SCI N123L.description: Hands-on laboratory course in human neuroimaging, with particular emphasis on using MRI to understand brain function and how it changes over the course of the lifespan and with disease.
BIO SCI N123L.prereq_text: BIO SCI 93 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108).
BIO SCI N123L.restriction: Seniors and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI D124.title: Biology of Integrative Medecine
BIO SCI D124.description: Presentation of biological principles and the latest clinical and basic research on complementary and alternative therapies (e.g., mind-body medicine, energy medicine, herbal medicine, acupuncture, manipulative therapies) and their integration with Western medicine. Lectures supplemented by demonstrations and hands-on learning sessions.
BIO SCI D124.prereq_text: NO BIO SCI 9J AND NO BIO SCI 9N AND NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = C OR BETTER (see SOC comments for repeat policy)

BIO SCI M124A.title: Virology
BIO SCI M124A.description: Replication of viruses in populations, animals, and the host cell. The effects of viral infection on populations, individuals, and specific molecular effects on the target cell. Role of viral infections in cancer and degenerative diseases.
BIO SCI M124A.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students only.

BIO SCI M124B.title: Viral Pathogenesis and Immunity
BIO SCI M124B.description: The mechanisms of viral pathogenesis and of host resistance to viruses are explored in detail. HIV-1 and Influenza-A are used as examples. In each case, viral replication, cytopathic effects, immune response, and viral evasion are discussed.
BIO SCI M124B.prereq_text: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M124A. Recommended: BIO SCI M122.

BIO SCI N124.title: Model Systems in Biology
BIO SCI N124.description: On the use of animal and in vitro models in biomedical research, focusing on assumptions, promises, limitations, and compromises.

BIO SCI M125.title: Molecular Biology of Cancer
BIO SCI M125.description: Covers topics in basic molecular and cellular cancer biology with focus on oncogenes and tumor suppressors, cancer signaling pathways, mechanisms of cancer initiation and progression, metastasis, tumor microenvironment, and modern cancer therapeutics.
BIO SCI M125.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N125.title: Advanced Data Science with R
BIO SCI N125.description: Equips biology students with vital skills in R programming, statistical analysis, and genomic data analysis. Gain a competitive edge in research and industry by mastering these interdisciplinary techniques essential for modern biological research.
BIO SCI N125.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E126.title: Parasitology
BIO SCI E126.description: Parasitism is the most common animal lifestyle. Yet, because parasites are invisible, they are often overlooked. Explore parasite diversity, disease dynamics, and more with an emphasis on the influential roles that parasites play on ecosystem structure and function.
BIO SCI E126.prereq_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94.
BIO SCI E126.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E127.title: Physiological Plant Ecology
BIO SCI E127.description: An examination of the interactions between plants and their environment. Emphasis on the underlying physiological mechanisms of plant function, adaptations and responses to stress, and the basis of the distribution of plants and plant assemblages across the landscape.
BIO SCI E127.prereq_text: EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 40B or BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94.
BIO SCI E127.restriction: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, Earth System Science majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N127.title: Foundations in Neuroimmunology
BIO SCI N127.description: The immune system supports normal brain development as well as controls central nervous system (CNS) infections and augments neurodegenerative and neurological diseases. Assesses how the immune system contributes to both host defense and disease.

BIO SCI E128.title: Chemical Ecology
BIO SCI E128.description: An introduction to the unspoken chemical language of nature. Emphasis on interactions between insects, plants, and microbes including plant defense, pollination, and microbial warfare.
BIO SCI E128.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94) and CHEM 51A with a minimum grade of C-.

BIO SCI M128L.title: Introductory Bioinformatics Lab
BIO SCI M128L.description: An introduction to modern methods of analyzing genomic, transcriptomic, and protein structure data. Students design experiments, extract information from a variety of different public databases and synthesize information to gain a deeper understanding of biological systems.
BIO SCI M128L.prereq_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108).
BIO SCI M128L.restriction: Seniors, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology majors, Microbiology and Immunology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N128.title: Into the Human Brain
BIO SCI N128.description: Explores different methods for studying the human brain in vivo (EEG, MRI, TMS, and others). Discusses ways to measure and manipulate brain activity directly and indirectly and how these different approaches complement each other.

BIO SCI D130.title: Photomedicine
BIO SCI D130.description: Studies the use of optical and engineering-based systems (laser-based) for diagnosis, treating diseases, manipulation of cells and cell function. Physical, optical, and electro-optical principles are explored regarding molecular, cellular, organ, and organism applications.
BIO SCI D130.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E131L.title: Image Analysis in Biological Research
BIO SCI E131L.description: Introduction to scientific image analysis including techniques such as high-speed, time-lapse, thermal imaging, and flow visualization. Students make movies using cameras, edit and analyze images using computers, and do a writing project.
BIO SCI E131L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI E106 or PHRMSCI 120 or BIO SCI E109) and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108).
BIO SCI E131L.restriction: Seniors and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI M131.title: Innate Immunity, Infection, and Pathogenesis
BIO SCI M131.description: Role of the innate immune system in health and disease. Molecular pathways of innate immune recognition, expression, and regulation of immune receptors, signal transduction, pathogen sensors, and detection of microbial ligands. Lecture and discussion of primary research articles.
BIO SCI M131.prereq_text: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M122 or BIO SCI M124A or BIO SCI M124B or BIO SCI M143.

BIO SCI N131.title: Human Neurodegenerative Diseases
BIO SCI N131.description: Clinical and epidemiological aspects of neurodegenerative diseases causing dementia are reviewed, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Seminar format includes student presentation and group discussion.

BIO SCI D132.title: Introduction to Precision Medicine
BIO SCI D132.description: Introduction to the use of genomic techniques for the study of individual genomes and transcriptomes in healthy and diseased samples. Covers GWAS, current sequencing techniques, cancer genomics, and biomarker discovery.

BIO SCI E132.title: Diversity of Fishes
BIO SCI E132.description: A survey of the many dimensions of diversity existing across fishes, the largest group of vertebrate organisms (over 30,000 species). Covers systematics, functional anatomy, development, physiology, biogeography, behavior, and more.
BIO SCI E132.prereq_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94.

BIO SCI D133.title: Advances in Regenerative Medicine
BIO SCI D133.description: Introduces the rapidly growing field of regenerative medicine. New developments in stem cell research are discussed. Cellular, molecular, and engineering aspects of stem cell-based organ replacement strategies are examined, with emphasis on specific regenerative therapies.
BIO SCI D133.prereq_text: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104.

BIO SCI E133.title: Environmental Microbiology
BIO SCI E133.description: Focuses on non-pathogenic microbes within all habitats (soils, oceans, associated with animals and plants) and their essential functions for ecosystems. Their applied importance for agriculture, bioremediation, energy and food production are also discussed.

BIO SCI M133.title: Structural Biology
BIO SCI M133.description: Basic principles of magnetic resonance, X-ray crystallography, and CryoEM toward the determination of high-resolution biomolecular structures.
BIO SCI M133.prereq_text: MATH 2B or MATH 5B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4.
BIO SCI M133.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E134.title: Microbiomes
BIO SCI E134.description: Students develop an understanding of microbiomes in the context of both their environment and their impact on host physiology. Discussions on how microbiomes interact with the human body.

BIO SCI D135.title: Cell Biology of Human Disease
BIO SCI D135.description: Builds on prior biology courses about the underlying cell biological mechanisms and recent treatment advances of several model diseases. Emphasizes literature searches, reading primary literature, and student group work.

BIO SCI E136.title: The Physiology of Human Nutrition
BIO SCI E136.description: Examines the biochemical basis of energy metabolism, physiological processes in digestion and uptake, and the biochemical transformation of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins in the human body. The emphasis is on expanding the students' understanding of physiology.
BIO SCI E136.prereq_text: BIO SCI 98 and (BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120).

BIO SCI D137.title: Eukaryotic and Human Genetics
BIO SCI D137.description: Structure and function of genes in eukaryotes with emphasis on special problems of genetic studies in humans. Molecular methods of genetic analysis and gene transfer are discussed. Practical applications and ethical and social issues raised by genetic studies are addressed.
BIO SCI D137.prereq_text: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97.

BIO SCI E137.title: Genetics of Complex Traits
BIO SCI E137.description: Many ecologically important traits (e.g., size, age at sexual maturity) and clinical conditions are rooted in the interaction of multiple genetic loci with the environment. Theoretical and practical approaches to dissecting the genetic architecture of complex traits are explored.
BIO SCI E137.prereq_text: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97.

BIO SCI M137.title: Microbial Genetics
BIO SCI M137.description: Basic principles of microbial genetics are presented as lectures for the first half of the course. The second half is devoted to applications of these principles and requires reading review and original research papers and interactions with guest lecturers.

BIO SCI E138.title: Comparative Animal Physiology
BIO SCI E138.description: Maintenance aspects of physiology: water balance; feeding and digestion; metabolism; respiration and circulation.
BIO SCI E138.restriction: Exercise Sciences majors and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N138.title: Sex Differences in the Brain
BIO SCI N138.description: Explores the neural bases of sex influences on brain function.

BIO SCI D139.title: Intercellular Signaling and Disease
BIO SCI D139.description: Introduces cell-to-cell communication mechanisms, which are fundamentally essential but still not well understood. From well-established to cutting-edge, researches of intercellular communication and how its malfunction leads to diseases are discussed.
BIO SCI D139.prereq_text: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104.

BIO SCI E139.title: Animal Locomotion
BIO SCI E139.description: The physiology, biomechanics, and neuroscience that determines how animals propel themselves and navigate through the world. Considers the principles that govern the walking, running, flying, and swimming of animals, including exercising humans.

BIO SCI E140L.title: Evolution and the Environment Laboratory
BIO SCI E140L.description: Explores basic topics in ecology and evolutionary biology and applications to agriculture, conservation, environmental issues, and public health. Format involves lab activities and discussion of scientific journal articles, with focus on learning to evaluate scientific evidence.
BIO SCI E140L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106.
BIO SCI E140L.restriction: Seniors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI D142.title: Advanced Cell Biology
BIO SCI D142.description: An in-depth view on general regulatory processes within the cell, with emphasis on research design, techniques, and review of primary literature describing current cell biology research.
BIO SCI D142.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI M143.title: Human Parasitology
BIO SCI M143.description: Introduction to human animal-parasitic diseases including worms and protozoan infections.

BIO SCI M144.title: Cell Organelles and Membranes
BIO SCI M144.description: Structure, function, and biogenesis of biological membranes and membrane-bound organelles.

BIO SCI D145.title: Genomics, Development, and Medicine
BIO SCI D145.description: Focuses on the applications of genomics and proteomics to problems in genetics, cell, and developmental biology. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the techniques currently used for genomics analysis and how best to apply these tools to solve problems.

BIO SCI E145.title: Animal Coloration and Vision
BIO SCI E145.description: Physiological and behavioral mechanisms of color production and vision including crypsis, mimicry, aposematism, masquerade, sexual dimorphism, and predator-prey interactions through the lens of signals, receivers, and receptors; color and polarization vision in mate choice and visual adaptations to aquatic environments.
BIO SCI E145.prereq_text: BIO SCI E106 (may be taken concurrently).

BIO SCI E147.title: Behavioral Endocrinology
BIO SCI E147.description: Comparative examination of the major hormone systems that regulate behavior across animals. Emphasizes the reciprocating nature of hormone-behavior interactions and seeks to understand how natural selection drives the evolution of hormone structure and function.

BIO SCI N147.title: Hearing and the Brain
BIO SCI N147.description: An overview of brain mechanisms of hearing, including perception of simple sounds, speech, and music. Begins with sound itself, and looks at processing by the ear, auditory pathways, auditory cortex, and beyond. Also auditory development, learning, and clinical issues.
BIO SCI N147.prereq_text: COGS 160A or BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93.
BIO SCI N147.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E150.title: Conservation Biology
BIO SCI E150.description: Genetic and ecological issues in conservation biology, including effects of human population growth, the value of biodiversity, conservation genetics, demography, metapopulation dynamics, community and ecosystem processes, species invasions, global climate change, and reserve design and management.

BIO SCI E152.title: Biochemistry of Animals in their Environments
BIO SCI E152.description: Interactions between organisms and their environments. Topics include the effects of environmental variables on biochemical functions: membrane stability, protein kinetics, energy metabolism, heat-shock-responses, energetics, gene-expression, and circadian rhythms. These topics are integrated with physiological-ecology in context of global climate change.

BIO SCI N152.title: Developmental Neurobiology
BIO SCI N152.description: The development of the nervous system is discussed with emphasis on the processes that underlie the appearance of complex and highly ordered neural circuits. Topics include neural induction, specification, migration and death; axon growth, and neural circuit formation.
BIO SCI N152.prereq_text: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93.

BIO SCI E153.title: Functional and Structural Evolutionary Genomics
BIO SCI E153.description: Function and organization of genomes analyzed from an evolutionary perspective. Review of some of the most recent experimental approaches in genome analysis and comparative genomics. Relevant software to analyze DNA and expression data is used.
BIO SCI E153.prereq_text: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97.

BIO SCI M153.title: Vascular Biology: Blood Vessels in Health and Disease
BIO SCI M153.description: Every cell in the body is within a half hair’s width of a blood vessel. As such, we cannot understand the body, in health or disease, without understanding the vasculature. Mixes lectures and primary literature reviews.

BIO SCI N153.title: Neuropharmacology
BIO SCI N153.description: Survey of neurotransmitter systems, focusing on how transmitters are made, how they interact with their receptors, and how drugs can influence these processes to alter neural function and behavior.
BIO SCI N153.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.

BIO SCI E154.title: Genetics and Human History
BIO SCI E154.description: Explores topics in human health/history from an evolutionary perspective, with emphasis on genetics. Topics include the relationship between genetics and human disease as an evolutionary question, and how modern genetic techniques are used to study the history of human populations.
BIO SCI E154.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E155.title: Physiology in Extreme Environments
BIO SCI E155.description: An in-depth look at the physiological mechanisms that allow animals, including humans, to be physically active and survive in extreme environments. Physiological responses to high altitude, diving, microgravity, deserts, and extreme cold are examined.
BIO SCI E155.prereq_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94.

BIO SCI M155.title: Advanced Cryogenic Electron Microscopy
BIO SCI M155.description: Electron microscopy for biological applications. Practical aspects of cryo-EM, including sample preparation, instrumentation, data collection, and processing methods. Electron crystallography, tomography, and microED. Applications of cryo-EM, current issues and future avenues are discussed along with computational protein design.
BIO SCI M155.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N158.title: Neurobiology of Learning and Memory
BIO SCI N158.description: How the brain and behavior change as a result of experience, with an emphasis on identifying the neurochemical processes through which memory is stored and the parts of the brain that are involved.
BIO SCI N158.prereq_text: BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.

BIO SCI E160L.title: Biology of Birds Lab
BIO SCI E160L.description: A thorough introduction to the biology of birds, covering topics ranging from avian anatomy and physiology to behavior, natural history, ecology, genetics, evolution, systematics, and conservation. Requires field trips to identify local birds and study avian natural history.
BIO SCI E160L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI 94.
BIO SCI E160L.restriction: Seniors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N160.title: Language and the Brain
BIO SCI N160.description: Research analysis on biological bases of human linguistic capacity. Development, focusing on hemispheric specialization, plasticity; localization of specific linguistic functions in adults, with emphasis on study of aphasias; relation of linguistic capacity to general cognitive capacity, considering research on retardation.
BIO SCI N160.prereq_text: (COGS 7A or PSCI 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or (COGS 9A or PSCI 11A) and (COGS 9B or PSCI 11B) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.
BIO SCI N160.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Biological Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and Language Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N164.title: Functional Neuroanatomy
BIO SCI N164.description: How neuroscience uses tools of many disciplines, from imaging to behavior, to develop and test hypotheses about functions of specific parts of the brain. Basic organization of nerve cells/vertebrate nervous system; methods of visualizing nerve cells; neural connections/activity patterns.

BIO SCI N165.title: Brain Disorders and Behavior
BIO SCI N165.description: Examines the localization of human brain functions and the effects of neurological disorders on psychological functions such as perception, motor control, language, memory, and decision-making.
BIO SCI N165.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.
BIO SCI N165.restriction: Biological Sciences majors, Cognitive Sciences majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E166L.title: Field Biology
BIO SCI E166L.description: Conducting group and independent studies in Southern California ecosystems, this course covers the fundamentals of experimental design, statistical analysis, communicating scientific findings (orally, visually, in writing), and other skills necessary for the scientific investigation of biological processes in the field. Materials Fee
BIO SCI E166L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
BIO SCI E166L.restriction: Seniors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E168.title: Evolution
BIO SCI E168.description: An integrative treatment of evolutionary biology that covers evolutionary processes, basic research methods, and the history of life.

BIO SCI D170.title: Applied Human Anatomy
BIO SCI D170.description: Systems approach to analyze the form and function of the human body with an emphasis on applying anatomical concepts to evaluate clinical cases. The laboratory uses human models and a simulated cadaver dissection for structure. Materials Fee
BIO SCI D170.prereq_text: BIO SCI E109 with a minimum grade of C or PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C or (BME 120 with a minimum grade of C and BME 121 with a minimum grade of C).
BIO SCI D170.restriction: Nursing Science majors and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N170.title: Clinical Neuroscience
BIO SCI N170.description: An introduction to the neuroclinical bases of human behavior, including neuropsychological approaches to mental disorders. Also includes case formulations, research articles, therapeutic approaches, and other discussions related to select psychopathology and other neurobehavioral topics.
BIO SCI N170.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or PSY 21 or COGS 9A or BIO SCI 99.
BIO SCI N170.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, Social Ecology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N172.title: Regenerative Neurobiology
BIO SCI N172.description: Explores the field of regenerative neurobiology. Both basic stem cell discoveries and their potential clinical application to brain disorders examined. Opportunities, challenges, and implications of this research also discussed.
BIO SCI N172.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.

BIO SCI N173.title: Human Neuropsychology
BIO SCI N173.description: A survey of human brain disorders using a clinical case study approach to illustrate fundamental issues in studying brain and behavior. Topics include sensory deficits, attentional neglect, amnesia, cortical organization, clinical psychopathology, and more.
BIO SCI N173.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or COGS 9A.
BIO SCI N173.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI N174.title: Principles of Neural Computation
BIO SCI N174.description: Introduction to the theoretical principles and biological mechanisms underlying how brains acquire, assimilate, store, and retrieve information, and how they compute adaptive responses to external inputs.
BIO SCI N174.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.

BIO SCI N176.title: Cerebral Cortex: Structure, Function, and Plasticity
BIO SCI N176.description: The cerebral cortex is highly developed in mammals and is responsible for higher perceptual and cognitive functions. Explores some amazing aspects of cortical structure, function, and plasticity emphasizing primary literature.
BIO SCI N176.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.

BIO SCI E179.title: Limnology and Freshwater Biology
BIO SCI E179.description: Biology of freshwater environments: lakes, ponds, rivers, their biota, and the factors which influence distribution of organisms.
BIO SCI E179.prereq_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94.

BIO SCI E179L.title: Field Freshwater Ecology
BIO SCI E179L.description: Analytical techniques for common water-quality variables of lakes, streams, and rivers. Benthic fauna, vertebrates and invertebrates, algae, and aquatic plants. Emphasis on field methods with an experimental approach; laboratory exercises. Field trips to marshes, vernal pools, rivers, and streams. Materials Fee
BIO SCI E179L.prereq_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E179.
BIO SCI E179L.restriction: Seniors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI M180.title: Biotechnological Applications of Energy and Environmental Research
BIO SCI M180.description: Covers microbiological and biochemical background related to current biotechnological applications, case studies of biotech-companies, and basic information related to patents and start-up companies. Topics include biofuel, bioremediation, agricultural, and environmental applications.

BIO SCI N182.title: Vision
BIO SCI N182.description: Visual perception and the anatomy and physiology of the visual system. Topics include the retina and the visual pathway; visual sensitivity; color vision; spatial vision; motion perception; and the development of the visual system.
BIO SCI N182.prereq_text: NO PSYCH 130A AND NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = C OR BETTER (see SOC comments for repeat policy)
BIO SCI N182.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E183.title: Exercise Physiology
BIO SCI E183.description: Focus upon critical topics in the area of exercise biology using the comparative physiological approach. Specifically examine the physiological factors that limit the capacity of an organism to sustain high levels of aerobic metabolism.

BIO SCI E184.title: Ecology and Diversity of Insects
BIO SCI E184.description: Insects—representing two-thirds of all species—play fundamental roles in human health, agriculture, and natural ecosystems. Topics include insect morphology, development, physiology, taxonomy, ecology, and insects in human affairs. Lecture includes interactive demonstrations and an optional weekend trip. Materials Fee

BIO SCI E186L.title: Population and Community Ecology Lab
BIO SCI E186L.description: Covers processes specific to groups of the same species (populations) and multiple species (communities). Includes growth, regulation, dynamics, and persistence of populations and community interactions, development, diversity, and macroecology. Lab activities focus on application of population prediction and biodiversity assessment.
BIO SCI E186L.prereq_text: BIO SCI E106 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108).
BIO SCI E186L.restriction: Seniors, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI E187.title: Exercise as Medicine
BIO SCI E187.description: Explores the link between regular physical activity and health, focusing on mechanistic insights into how regular exercise improves overall health and alters disease trajectories of cancer, type-II diabetes, depression, and other chronic illnesses.

BIO SCI E189.title: Environmental Ethics
BIO SCI E189.description: History of evolution of environmental ethics in America. Management problems in national parks, wilderness areas, wild and scenic rivers, national forests. Contemporary and historical aspects/contributors to the field. Mitigation, endangered species, habitat restoration, biodiversity, and environmental activism. Field trips required.
BIO SCI E189.prereq_text: UPPER DIVISION STANDING ONLY AND NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = C OR BETTER (see SOC comments for repeat policy)

BIO SCI 190.title: Transfer Student Seminar
BIO SCI 190.description: Weekly meetings consisting of presentations by faculty, professional staff, and New Student Peer Academic Advisors provide information about the School of Biological Sciences, campus resources, and special programs/opportunities.
BIO SCI 190.prereq_text: NEW TRANSFERS ONLY AND NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = C OR BETTER (see SOC comments for repeat policy)

BIO SCI D190.title: Topics in Developmental and Cell Biology
BIO SCI D190.description: Studies in selected areas of developmental and cell biology.
BIO SCI D190.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students only.

BIO SCI E190.title: Topics in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
BIO SCI E190.description: Studies in selected areas of ecology and evolutionary biology.

BIO SCI M190.title: Topics in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
BIO SCI M190.description: Studies in selected areas of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.

BIO SCI N190.title: Topics in Neurobiology and Behavior
BIO SCI N190.description: Studies in selected areas of neurobiology and behavior.
BIO SCI N190.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.

BIO SCI 191A.title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability I
BIO SCI 191A.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare bibliography.
BIO SCI 191A.restriction: Seniors and Global Sustainability minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BIO SCI 191B.title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability II
BIO SCI 191B.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare research proposal.
BIO SCI 191B.prereq_text: BIO SCI 191A or SOCECOL 186A or EARTHSS 190A.

BIO SCI 191CW.title: Writing/Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability III
BIO SCI 191CW.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum also is required. Seminar utilized to analyze Forum presentations and to prepare senior research paper. Prepare/write research paper under direction of faculty member.
BIO SCI 191CW.prereq_text: BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B. BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

BIO SCI 192.title: Topics in Biological Sciences Tutoring
BIO SCI 192.description: Tutoring programs with biological sciences student peers.
BIO SCI 192.prereq_text: NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = C OR BETTER (see SOC comments for repeat policy)
BIO SCI 192.restriction: Students tutoring under School of Biological Sciences programs only.

BIO SCI 192A.title: Biological Sciences Learning Assistant Mentoring
BIO SCI 192A.description: Oversight of trained learning assistants by the course instructor, including training in the discipline and responsibilities associated with supporting active group work. Instructor mentors LAs in how assisting small groups supports their career goals.

BIO SCI 193.title: Center for Environmental Biology Internship
BIO SCI 193.description: Focuses on the theory and practice of ecological research and education and outreach, especially related to the management of natural resources.

BIO SCI 193A.title: Campus as a Living Lab I
BIO SCI 193A.description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.

BIO SCI 193B.title: Campus as a Living Lab II
BIO SCI 193B.description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.

BIO SCI 193C.title: Campus as a Living Lab III
BIO SCI 193C.description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.

BIO SCI H195.title: Honors Topics in Biological Sciences
BIO SCI H195.description: Varied course topics in Biological Sciences designed for students in Honors in Biological Sciences.
BIO SCI H195.restriction: School of Biological Sciences Honors students only.

BIO SCI 197.title: Special Study in Biological Sciences
BIO SCI 197.description: Individualized instruction dealing with conceptual or theoretical problems in the biological sciences, rather than technical problems.
BIO SCI 197.restriction: Maximum of 5 units (per quarter) between BIO SCI 197, BIO SCI 198, and BIO SCI 199.

BIO SCI 199.title: Independent Study in Biological Sciences Research
BIO SCI 199.description: Individual experimental laboratory or field research under a professor's direction. Required for participation in the Excellence in Research Program.

and.other: Bio 199 Packet must be submitted to Bio Sci Student Affairs prior to enrollment.

BIO SCI 199W.title: Research Writing
BIO SCI 199W.description: Development of research skills such as learning how to plan and conduct research experiments, read and analyze scientific journal articles, and practice presenting the data experiments and journal articles with an emphasis on scientific writing.

BIO SCI 285.title: Topics in Allied Health Microbiology
BIO SCI 285.description: Basic microbiology with emphasis for allied health professions such as nursing. Emphasis is on micro-organisms involved in human health, disease and food safety.
BIO SCI 285.restriction: Nursing Science majors, Community and Population Health majors, School of Nursing students, and Master of Science only.

BIOCHEM 200A.title: Research in Biological Chemistry
BIOCHEM 200A.description: Individual research under the supervision of a professor.

BIOCHEM 200B.title: Research in Biological Chemistry
BIOCHEM 200B.description: Individual research under the supervision of a professor.

BIOCHEM 200C.title: Research in Biological Chemistry
BIOCHEM 200C.description: Individual research under the supervision of a professor.

BIOCHEM 200R.title: Research in Biological Chemistry for First-Year Students
BIOCHEM 200R.description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Biological Chemistry for first-year Ph.D. students.

BIOCHEM 202A.title: Laboratory Seminar Series
BIOCHEM 202A.description: Study within a laboratory group including research and journal presentations.

BIOCHEM 202B.title: Laboratory Seminar Series
BIOCHEM 202B.description: Study within a laboratory group including research and journal presentations.

BIOCHEM 202C.title: Laboratory Seminar Series
BIOCHEM 202C.description: Study within a laboratory group including research and journal presentations.

BIOCHEM 207.title: Current Topics in Cancer Genomics
BIOCHEM 207.description: Literature-based discussion of molecular principles in genetics and functional genomics, with focus on cancer and stem cell biology.

BIOCHEM 210A.title: Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
BIOCHEM 210A.description: Covers the following topics from a biomedical perspective: protein and nucleic acid biochemistry, carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, purines and pyrimidines, genome structure, molecular mechanisms of development, and signal transduction.

BIOCHEM 225.title: Epigenetics in Health and Disease
BIOCHEM 225.description: Focuses on the role of chromatin/nuclear structure organization (histone and DNA modification, chromatin remodeling, higher order chromatin structure and nuclear organization) on gene regulation, DNA replication and repair, relevant to development, metabolism, learning and memory, and human disease.
BIOCHEM 225.prereq_text: MOL BIO 203 with a minimum grade of B- or MOL BIO 204 with a minimum grade of B- or NEURBIO 206 with a minimum grade of B-.

BIOCHEM 228.title: Neuromuscular Biology and Disease
BIOCHEM 228.description: Covers fundamental knowledge and cutting-edge research of muscle biology and muscle diseases. Topics include development and stem cell biology of muscle, immune and inflammatory responses, epigenetics and gene regulation, and diagnostic marker discovery and therapy development.

BIOCHEM 237.title: Muscle Journal Club and Research in Progress
BIOCHEM 237.description: Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of current research and advancements in the field of skeletal muscle biology and disease.
BIOCHEM 237.restriction: School of Medicine students, Master of Science, and Doctor of Philosophy only.

BIOCHEM 242.title: Applications and Current Topics in Bioinformatics
BIOCHEM 242.description: Provides an introduction to bioinformatics with a focus on performing core analyses using coding techniques. Students learn essential concepts in bioinformatics, gain proficiency in programming languages such as R and bash, and apply these skills.

BIOCHEM 281.title: Fundamentals of Informatics for Biologists
BIOCHEM 281.description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics and the unix operating system.

BIOCHEM 291.title: Research Seminar
BIOCHEM 291.description: Student research-based colloquium covering current topics in gene organization and expression, cell cycle and differentiation, DNA repair, checkpoint control, and the physical, chemical, and biological properties of macromolecules. Students are encouraged to read critically and analyze recent literature.

BIOCHEM 292A.title: Scientific Communication
BIOCHEM 292A.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

BIOCHEM 292B.title: Scientific Communication
BIOCHEM 292B.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

BIOCHEM 292C.title: Scientific Communication
BIOCHEM 292C.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

BME 1.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
BME 1.description: Introduction to the central topics of biomedical engineering. Offers a perspective on bioengineering as a discipline in a seminar format. Principles of problem solving, design, engineering inventiveness, entrepreneurship, information access, communication, ethics, teamwork, and social responsibility are emphasized.
BME 1.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 3.title: Engineering Innovations in Treating Diabetes
BME 3.description: Innovations in diabetes treatment from the 1800s until the present: purification of insulin, measuring and control of blood glucose, recombinant DNA, clinical trials, and ethics. Solving optimization problems in engineering with Excel.

BME 50A.title: Cell and Molecular Engineering
BME 50A.description: Molecular, structural, genetic, biophysical, and cellular principles of life and bioengineering. Introduction to molecular bioengineering, genetic engineering, synthetic biology, and cell biology. Applications to genetic and biomolecular design.
BME 50A.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 50B.title: Cell and Molecular Engineering
BME 50B.description: Physiological function from a cellular, molecular, and biophysical perspective. Introduction to genetics, structure and function of cells and tissues, cell cycle control, cancer, and immunology.
BME 50B.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Chemical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 60A.title: Engineering Analysis/Design: Data Acquisition
BME 60A.description: Fundamentals of data acquisition programming, basics of computer-based experimentation, establishing interface between computer and data acquisition instrumentation, signal conditioning basics. Materials Fee
BME 60A.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 60B.title: Engineering Analysis/Design: Data Analysis
BME 60B.description: Overview of MATLAB; numeric, cell, and structure arrays; file management; plotting and model building; solving linear algebraic equations; signal and image processing. Materials Fee
BME 60B.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 60C.title: Engineering Analysis/Design: Computer-Aided Design
BME 60C.description: Introduction to SolidWorks and Computer-Aided Design software; design; analysis; rapid prototyping; visualization and presentation; manufacturing planning. Materials Fee
BME 60C.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 98.title: The Heart of MedTech: Innovation and Career Discovery
BME 98.description: Offers a real-world look at how medical devices are developed, from concept to market. Topics include manufacturing, regulatory, marketing, supply chain, and intellectual property.
BME 98.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors only.

BME 110A.title: Biomechanics I
BME 110A.description: Introduction to statics and dynamics. Topics include rigid bodies, analysis of structures, forces in beams, moments of inertia, friction, kinetics, work, and energy.
BME 110A.prereq_text: PHYSICS 7C and MATH 3A and MATH 3D and BME 60B.
BME 110A.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 110B.title: Biomechanics II
BME 110B.description: Introduction to biomechanics from subcellular to tissue levels. Introduction to stress, strain, and constitutive laws of cells and tissues. Emphasis is placed on biosolids. Introduction to elastic and viscoelastic behaviors with emphasis on the standard linear model of viscoelasticity.
BME 110B.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 110C.title: Biomechanics III
BME 110C.description: Introduction to human biomechanics with emphasis on cardiovascular biomechanics and biofluid mechanics.
BME 110C.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 111.title: Design of Biomaterials
BME 111.description: Natural and synthetic polymeric materials. Metal and ceramics implant materials. Mechanical properties, degradation, surface characterization, and design of materials. Wound repair, blood clotting, foreign body response, biocompatibility of material. Artificial organs and medical devices. Government regulations.
BME 111.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 112.title: Finite Element Modeling for Bioengineers
BME 112.description: Introduction to finite-element simulation; fundamentals of Multiphysics simulation; essential skills in performing simulations with COMSOL®.
BME 112.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 114.title: Genetic Engineering and Synthetic Biology
BME 114.description: Exploring how biological function can be engineered and "synthesized" from the DNA level up.
BME 114.prereq_text: (CHEM 1C or CHEM H2C) and MATH 3D and BME 50A and BME 50B.
BME 114.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 120.title: Sensory Motor Systems
BME 120.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the nervous and musculoskeletal systems.
BME 120.prereq_text: (BME 60B or EECS 10 or EECS 12 or ENGRCEE 20 or ENGRMAE 10) and MATH 3D and PHYSICS 7D.
BME 120.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 121.title: Quantitative Physiology: Organ Transport Systems
BME 121.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the cardiopulmonary, circulatory, and renal systems.
BME 121.prereq_text: (BME 60B or EECS 10 or EECS 12 or ENGRCEE 20 or ENGRMAE 10) and MATH 3D and BME 150 and BME 110A.
BME 121.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and Chemical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 126.title: Astronaut Physiology: Biomedical Engineering for Space
BME 126.description: Applies engineering principles to physiological microgravity adaptation. Qualitative symptoms are analyzed, producing quantitative measurements for assessing countermeasures. Students (voluntarily) experience simulated microgravity (parabolic flight) or hypergravity (high angle turns) in single engine aircraft. Materials Fee
BME 126.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 130.title: Biomedical Signals and Systems
BME 130.description: Analysis of analog and digital biomedical signals; Fourier Series expansions; difference and differential equations; convolutions. System models: discrete-time and continuous-time linear time-invariant systems; Laplace and Fourier transforms. Analysis of signals and systems using computer programs.
BME 130.prereq_text: BME 60B and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N) and MATH 3D. Recommended: STATS 8.
BME 130.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 132.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
BME 132.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
BME 132.prereq_text: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8.

BME 135.title: Photomedicine
BME 135.description: Studies the use of optical and engineering-based systems (laser-based) for diagnosis, treating diseases, manipulation of cells and cell function. Physical, optical, and electro-optical principles are explored regarding molecular, cellular, organ, and organism applications.
BME 135.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 136.title: Engineering Medical Optics
BME 136.description: Principles of optics and photonics, integration of optical components into systems and devices, and analysis of physiological signals obtained from Biophotonics measurements.
BME 136.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 137.title: Introduction to Biomedical Imaging
BME 137.description: Introduction to imaging modalities widely used in medicine and biology, including X-ray, computed tomography (CT), nuclear medicine (PET and SPET), ultrasonic imaging, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), optical tomography, imaging contrast, imaging processing, and complementary nature of the imaging modalities.
BME 137.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 138.title: Spectroscopy and Imaging of Biological Systems
BME 138.description: Principles of spectroscopy; absorption; molecular orbitals; multiphoton transitions; Jablonski diagram; fluorescence anisotropy; fluorescence decay; quenching; FRET; excited state reactions; solvent relaxations; instruments; microscopy: wide field, LSM, TPE; fluorescent probes, fluctuations spectroscopy; optical resolution and super-resolution; CARS and SHG microscopy.
BME 138.prereq_text: (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N) and MATH 3D. Recommended: STATS 8.
BME 138.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 140.title: Design of Biomedical Electronics
BME 140.description: Analog and digital circuits in bioinstrumentation. AC and DC circuit analysis, design and construction of filter and amplifiers using operational amplifier, digitization of signals and data acquisition, bioelectrical signals, design and construction of ECG instrument, bioelectrical signal measurement and analysis. Materials Fee
BME 140.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 142.title: Microfabrication
BME 142.description: Essentials of photolithography, soft-lithography, microfabrication, Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS), BioMEMS; applications in biomedical engineering.
BME 142.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 147.title: Microfluidics and Lab-on-a-Chip
BME 147.description: Introduction to principles of microfluidics and state-of-the-art micro Total Analysis Systems (uTAS). Lab-on-a-Chip for bimolecular assays with device design principles for microscale sample preparation, flow transport, bimolecular manipulation, separation and detection, and the technologies for integrating these devices into microsystems.
BME 147.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 148.title: Microimplants
BME 148.description: Essential concepts of biomedical implants at the micro scale. Design, fabrication, and applications of several microimplantable devices including cochlear, retinal, neural, and muscular implants.
BME 148.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 150.title: Biotransport Phenomena
BME 150.description: Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer, similarities in the respective rate equations. Emphasis on practical application of fundamental principles.
BME 150.prereq_text: (BME 60B or ENGRCEE 20) and MATH 3D and CHEM 1C and PHYSICS 7E and MATH 2D.
BME 150.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 160.title: Tissue Engineering
BME 160.description: Quantitative analysis of cell and tissue functions. Emerging developments in stem cell technology, biodegradable scaffolds, growth factors, and others important in developing clinical products. Applications of bioengineering.
BME 160.prereq_text: (BME 50B or BIO SCI 99) and BME 111 and BME 121 and BME 150.
BME 160.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and Chemical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 161.title: Introduction to Modern Bioengineering Tools
BME 161.description: A broad picture of diverse modern bioengineering tools, including genetic engineering and its risks to society, how to sequence DNA/RNA molecules with single base resolution, how to manipulate small biomolecules one at a time.
BME 161.prereq_text: (BME 50A and BME 50B) or (BIO SCI 97 and BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99).
BME 161.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors and Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 170.title: Biomedical Engineering Laboratory
BME 170.description: Measurement and analysis of biological systems using engineering tools and techniques. Laboratory experiments involve living systems with the emphasis on measuring physiological parameters. Materials Fee
BME 170.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 179.title: Biomedical Engineering Design: Addressing Unmet Clinical Needs
BME 179.description: Introduction to unmet clinical needs identification and evaluation in biomedical engineering design.
BME 179.restriction: Biomedical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering: Premedical majors, and School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 180A.title: Biomedical Engineering Design
BME 180A.description: Design strategies, techniques, tools, and protocols commonly encountered in biomedical engineering; industrial design experience in group projects; ethics, economic analysis, and FDA product approval. Materials Fee
BME 180A.prereq_text: (BME 60B or ENGRMAE 10 or EECS 10) and (BME 60C or ENGRMAE 52 or EECS 31L) and (BME 140 or ENGRMAE 106 or EECS 170B) and BME 179. BME 180A, BME 180B, and BME 180C must be taken in the same academic year.
BME 180A.restriction: Seniors and Biomedical Engineering majors only.

BME 180B.title: Biomedical Engineering Design
BME 180B.description: Design strategies, techniques, tools, and protocols commonly encountered in biomedical engineering; industrial design experience in group projects; ethics, economic analysis, and FDA product approval. Materials Fee
BME 180B.prereq_text: BME 180A. BME 180A, BME 180B, and BME 180C must be taken in the same academic year.
BME 180B.restriction: Seniors and Biomedical Engineering majors only.

BME 180C.title: Biomedical Engineering Design
BME 180C.description: Design strategies, techniques, tools, and protocols commonly encountered in biomedical engineering; industrial design experience in group projects; ethics, economic analysis, and FDA product approval. Materials Fee
BME 180C.prereq_text: BME 180B. BME 180A, BME 180B, and BME 180C must be taken in the same academic year.
BME 180C.restriction: Seniors and Biomedical Engineering majors only.

BME 195.title: Special Topics in Biomedical Engineering
BME 195.description: Studies in selected areas of Biomedical Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

BME 197.title: Seminars in Biomedical Engineering
BME 197.description: Presentation of advanced topics and reports of current research efforts in Biomedical Engineering.
BME 197.restriction: Seniors and Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

BME 198.title: Biomedical Engineering Internship
BME 198.description: Students majoring in BME may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.

BME 199.title: Individual Study
BME 199.description: Independent research conducted in the lab of a biomedical engineering core faculty member. A formal written report of the research conducted is required at the conclusion of the quarter.

BME 199P.title: Individual Study
BME 199P.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

BME 201P.title: Biomedical Big Data
BME 201P.description: Analysis and visualization of large biomedical datasets. Topics covered include cloud computing, learning Structured Query Language (SQL), database normalization and joins, using Google’s BigQuery, using the statistical analysis package R, machine learning algorithms, application of machine learning for classification problems.

BME 202P.title: Biomedical Imaging and Biophotonics
BME 202P.description: Designed as a subfield of optical imaging and biophotonics as it applies to their applications to basic lifesciences and in vivo imaging to diagnose disease. Topics span all of of the areas of biophotonics and techniques.

BME 203P.title: Digital Health
BME 203P.description: Digital health is the convergence of genomics and technology to radically change the way health and medicine is practiced. Explores the history of healthcare in the U.S., its current status, and the future of digital health.

BME 210.title: Molecular and Cellular Engineering
BME 210.description: Engineering of physiological function at the genetic, cellular, and tissue scales. Topics include cloning and genetic engineering, extracellular matrix biomaterials, principles of regenerative medicine and tissue engineering, and experimental design.

BME 210P.title: Molecular and Cellular Engineering
BME 210P.description: Engineering of physiological function at the genetic, cellular, and tissue scales. Topics include cloning and genetic engineering, extracellular matrix biomaterials, principles of regenerative medicine and tissue engineering, and experimental design.

BME 211.title: Microscale Tissue Engineering
BME 211.description: Engineering of physiological function at the scale of individual cells. Topics include cell micropatterning, microfluidic tissue culture, engineering the cellular microenvironment, and microphysiological systems.

BME 211P.title: Microscale Tissue Engineering
BME 211P.description: Engineering of physiological function at the scale of individual cells. Topics include cell micropatterning, microfluidic tissue culture, engineering the cellular microenvironment, and microphysiological systems.

BME 212.title: Cardiovascular Mechanobiology
BME 212.description: Advanced topics in cellular engineering and mechanobiology, with focus on the cardiovascular system. Tools and techniques used to manipulate and measure mechanical forces at the molecular, cellular, tissue, and organ levels, and their applications in cardiovascular devices and tissue engineering.

BME 212P.title: Cardiovascular Mechanobiology
BME 212P.description: Advanced topics in cellular engineering and mechanobiology, with focus on the cardiovascular system. Tools and techniques used to manipulate and measure mechanical forces at the molecular, cellular, tissue, and organ levels, and their applications in cardiovascular devices and tissue engineering.

BME 213.title: Systems Cell and Developmental Biology
BME 213.description: Introduces concepts needed to understand cell and developmental biology at the systems level, i.e., how the parts (molecules) work together to create a complex output. Emphasis on using mathematical/computational modeling to expand/modify insights provided by intuition.

BME 215.title: Linking Modeling and Experiments in Bioengineering
BME 215.description: Overview of modeling based on experimental techniques in bioengineering. Construct and evaluate models of varying complexity and to relate them to experimental data.
BME 215.prereq_text: BME 220 with a minimum grade of B- and BME 221 with a minimum grade of B-.

BME 220.title: Sensory Motor Systems
BME 220.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the nervous and musculoskeletal systems.

BME 220P.title: Sensory Motor Systems
BME 220P.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the nervous and musculoskeletal systems.

BME 221.title: Organ Transport Systems
BME 221.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the cardiopulmonary, circulatory, and renal systems.

BME 221P.title: Organ Transport Systems
BME 221P.description: Applies engineering models and mathematics to understand human physiology in order to understand the physiology. Covers the pulmonary, cardiac, and cardiovascular systems focusing on transport phenomena.

BME 226.title: Astronaut Physiology: Biomedical Engineering for Space
BME 226.description: Applies engineering principles to physiological microgravity adaptation. Qualitative symptoms are analyzed, producing quantitative measurements for assessing countermeasures. Students experience simulated microgravity (parabolic flight) or hypergravity (high angle turns) in single engine aircraft. Materials Fee
BME 226.restriction: Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy only.

BME 230A.title: Applied Engineering Mathematics I
BME 230A.description: Analytical techniques applied to engineering problems in transport phenomena, process dynamics and control, and thermodynamics.

BME 230B.title: Applied Engineering Mathematics II
BME 230B.description: Focuses on biomedical system identification. Includes fundamental techniques of model building and testing such as formulation, solution of governing equations, sensitivity theory, identifiability theory, and uncertainty analysis.

BME 232.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
BME 232.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.

BME 233.title: Dynamic Systems in Biology and Medicine
BME 233.description: Introduces principles of system theory to analyze biological, biochemical, physiological, and bioengineering systems. Analytical and computational tools are used to model and analyze dynamic systems such as population, neuronal and heart dynamics, biochemical and physiological systems, oxygen diffusion and similar.

BME 233P.title: Dynamic Systems in Biology and Medicine
BME 233P.description: Introduces the elements of system theory, and applies these principles to analyze biomedical, chemical, social, and engineering systems. Using analytical and computational tools to model and analyze various dynamic systems.

BME 234.title: Neuroimaging Data Analysis
BME 234.description: Knowledge and understanding of recent techniques for the analysis of healthy and pathological structure and function in neuroimaging data.

BME 234P.title: Neuroimaging Data Analysis
BME 234P.description: Knowledge and understanding of recent techniques for the analysis of healthy and pathological structure and function in neuroimaging data.

BME 235.title: Analysis of Neural Time Series
BME 235.description: Hands-on introduction to techniques for the analysis of neural time series data, with a primary focus on the electroencephalogram (EEG). Topics may include the physiological basis of EEG, time-frequency analysis, spatial filtering, and methods of assessing connectivity.

BME 238.title: Spectroscopy and Imaging of Biological Systems
BME 238.description: Principles of spectroscopy; absorption; molecular orbitals; multiphoton transitions; Jablonski diagram; fluorescence anisotropy; fluorescence decay; quenching; FRET; excited state reactions; solvent relaxations; instruments; microscopy: wide field, LSM, TPE; fluorescent probes, fluctuations spectroscopy; optical resolution and super-resolution; CARS and SHG microscopy.

BME 238P.title: Spectroscopy and Imaging of Biological Systems
BME 238P.description: Principles of spectroscopy; absorption; molecular orbitals; multiphoton transitions; Jablonski diagram; fluorescence anisotropy; fluorescence decay; quenching; FRET; excited state reactions; solvent relaxations; instruments; microscopy: wide field, LSM, TPE; fluorescent probes, fluctuations spectroscopy; optical resolution and super-resolution; CARS and SHG microscopy.

BME 240.title: Introduction to Clinical Medicine for Biomedical Engineering
BME 240.description: An introduction to clinical medicine for graduate students in biomedical engineering. Lectures and rotations through nephology, gastroenterology, pulmonary, and critical care cardiology.

BME 240P.title: Introduction to Clinical Medicine for Biomedical Engineering
