CHEM 203.title: Organic Spectroscopy
CHEM 203.description: Modern methods used in structure determination of organic molecules. Topics include mass spectrometry; ultraviolet, chiroptical, infrared, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
CHEM 203.prereq_text: (CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C) or (CHEM H52A and CHEM H52B and CHEM H52C).

CHEM 204.title: Organic Synthesis I
CHEM 204.description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry is developed. Major emphasis is on carbon-carbon bond forming methodology. Topics include carbonyl annelations, cycloadditions, sigmatropic rearrangements, and organometallic methods.

CHEM 205.title: Organic Synthesis II
CHEM 205.description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry will be developed. Major emphasis this quarter is on natural product total synthesis and retrosynthetic (antithetic) analysis.
CHEM 205.prereq_text: CHEM 204 with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 206.title: Advanced Data Acquisition and Analysis
CHEM 206.description: Introduces students to a variety of practical laboratory techniques, including lock-in, boxcar, coincidence counting, noise filtering, PID control, properties of common transducers, computer interfacing to instruments, vacuum technology, laboratory safety, basic mechanical design, and shop skills. Materials Fee

CHEM 207.title: Applied Physical Chemistry
CHEM 207.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts in molecular structure and reactivity: theory of bonding, valence and molecular orbitals; structure and reactivity in inorganic chemistry; elements in molecular group theory; nomenclature in organic chemistry; and survey of macromolecules.

CHEM 208.title: Math Methods
CHEM 208.description: Applications of mathematics to physical and chemical problems. Calculus of special functions, complex variables and vectors; linear vector spaces and eigenvalue problems. Differential equations.

CHEM 213.title: Chemical Kinetics
CHEM 213.description: Surveys gas phase and organic reaction mechanisms and their relationship to kinetic rate laws; treats the basic theory of elementary reaction rates. A brief presentation of modern cross-sectional kinetics is included.

CHEM 215.title: Inorganic Chemistry I
CHEM 215.description: Principles of modern inorganic chemistry with applications to chemical systems of current interest. Inorganic phenomena are organized into general patterns which rationalize observed structures, stabilities, and physical properties.
CHEM 215.prereq_text: CHEM 107 and CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C.

CHEM 216.title: Organometallic Chemistry
CHEM 216.description: Synthesis and reactivity of organometallic complexes with an emphasis on mechanisms. Topics include bonding and fluxional properties; metal-carbon single and multiple bonds; metal š-complexes. Applications to homogenous catalysis and organic synthesis are incorporated throughout the course.
CHEM 216.prereq_text: CHEM 107 or CHEM 215 with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 217.title: Physical Inorganic Chemistry
CHEM 217.description: General principles of the spectroscopy and magnetism of inorganic compounds. Characterization of inorganic complexes by infrared, near-infrared, visible, ultraviolet, NMR, EPR, EXAFS, and Mossbauer spectroscopies. Some necessary group theory developed.
CHEM 217.prereq_text: CHEM 215 with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 218.title: Metallobiochemistry
CHEM 218.description: A review of the biochemistry of metallic elements emphasizing: methods for studying metals in biological systems; the chemical basis for nature's exploitation of specific elements; structures of active sites; mechanisms; solid-state structures and devices; metals in medicine.
CHEM 218.prereq_text: CHEM 131C (may be taken concurrently) or CHEM 132C (may be taken concurrently).

CHEM 219.title: Chemical and Structural Biology
CHEM 219.description: A survey of the organic chemistry underlying biological function. Introduction to chemical genetics, receptor-ligand interactions, small molecule agonists and antagonists, combinatorial synthesis, high throughput assays, molecular evolution, protein and small molecule design.

CHEM 220.title: Advanced Chemical Biology
CHEM 220.description: Modern topics in chemical biology, with an emphasis on application of principles from organic chemistry to biological research and biotechnology. Topics include methods to generate, identify, and manipulate major classes of biomolecules including nucleic acids, carbohydrates, lipids, and secondary metabolites.
CHEM 220.prereq_text: CHEM 219 with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 221A.title: Fundamentals of Molecular Biophysics
CHEM 221A.description: An overview of the principles and concepts in molecular biophysics. Topics covered include energy and entropy in biology, non-equilibrium reaction kinetics, random walks and molecular diffusion, molecular forces in biology.
CHEM 221A.prereq_text: Undergraduate courses in physical chemistry and biochemistry.

CHEM 223.title: Biological Macromolecules
CHEM 223.description: Introduction to nucleic acid and protein structure, dynamics, and function. Topics include analytical methods, molecular evolution, folding, and catalysis.

CHEM 225.title: Polymer Chemistry: Synthesis and Characterization of Polymers
CHEM 225.description: Structure of synthetic and natural polymers. Survey of modern polymer synthetic methods. Molecular weight and molecular weight distribution. Chain conformation and stereochemistry. Introduction to polymer characterization, chain models, and solution behavior.
CHEM 225.prereq_text: Undergraduate courses in organic and physical chemistry.

CHEM 228.title: Electromagnetism
CHEM 228.description: Maxwell’s equations, electrodynamics, electromagnetic waves and radiation, wave propagation in media, interference and quantum optics, coherent and incoherent radiation, with practical applications in interferometry, lasers, waveguides, and optical instrumentation.

CHEM 229A.title: Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences
CHEM 229A.description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.

CHEM 230.title: Classical Mechanics and Electromagnetic Theory
CHEM 230.description: Fundamentals of classical mechanics and electromagnetic theory are developed with specific application to molecular systems. Newtonian, Lagrangian, and Hamiltonian mechanics are developed. Boundary value problems in electrostatics are investigated. Multipole expansion and macroscopic media are discussed from a molecular viewpoint.

CHEM 231A.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Mechanics
CHEM 231A.description: The postulates of quantum mechanics are discussed and applied to a variety of model problems.

CHEM 231B.title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics
CHEM 231B.description: Approximate methods for solving atomic and molecular structure problems are developed, and the application of quantum mechanics to spectroscopy is introduced.
CHEM 231B.prereq_text: CHEM 231A with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 231C.title: Molecular Spectroscopy
CHEM 231C.description: Theory and techniques of spectroscopy as used for the study of molecular and condensed phase properties. Coherent time domain spectroscopies are covered.
CHEM 231C.prereq_text: CHEM 231B with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 232A.title: Thermodynamics and Introduction to Statistical Mechanics
CHEM 232A.description: A detailed discussion from an advanced point of view of the principles of classical thermodynamics. The fundamentals of statistical mechanics. Topics include an introduction to ensemble theory, Boltzmann statistics, classical statistical mechanics, and the statistical mechanics of ideal gas systems.

CHEM 232B.title: Advanced Topics in Statistical Mechanics
CHEM 232B.description: Continued discussion of the principles of statistical mechanics. Applications to topics of chemical interest including imperfect gases, liquids, solutions, and crystals. Modern techniques such as the use of autocorrelation function methods.
CHEM 232B.prereq_text: CHEM 232A with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 232C.title: Non-Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics
CHEM 232C.description: Phenomenology of material processes, including: kinetic theories of transport and continuum, linear response theory, critical phenomena of phase transition, self-assembly, and nucleation.

CHEM 233.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
CHEM 233.description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.

CHEM 237.title: Mathematical Methods in Chemistry
CHEM 237.description: Survey of essential math methods in chemistry. Topics may include series and limits, complex analysis, Fourier and Laplace transforms, linear algebra and operators (theory and algorithms), differential equations, and probability concepts for stochastic processes.

CHEM 238.title: Special Topics in Density Functional Theory
CHEM 238.description: Advanced topics in density functional theory.
CHEM 238.prereq_text: One year of graduate quantum mechanics, or the equivalent.

CHEM 239.title: Machine Learning in Chemistry
CHEM 239.description: Introductory course in machine learning, accessible to any graduate student in chemistry. Covers the basics of theory and practice of machine learning in modern chemistry. No coding or previous experience required.
CHEM 239.prereq_text: Must be familiar with standard computer operation.

CHEM 241.title: Current Issues Related to Air Quality, Climate, and Energy
CHEM 241.description: Current issues related to the atmosphere, climate, and air quality in the context of energy conversion and sustainability. Topics include transportation systems; building design; impacts on humans and ecosystems; modeling and meteorology; economics; and application to public policies.
CHEM 241.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 261 with a minimum grade of B- or CHEM 245 with a minimum grade of B- or EARTHSS 240 with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 243.title: Advanced Instrumental Analysis
CHEM 243.description: Theory and applications of modern advanced instrumental methods of analysis. Includes data acquisition, storage, retrieval, and analysis; Fourier transform methods; vacuum technologies; magnetic sector; quadrupole and ion trap mass spectrometry; surface science spectroscopic methods; lasers and optics.
CHEM 243.prereq_text: CHEM 152 with a minimum grade of B and CHEM 132C with a minimum grade of B.

CHEM 244.title: Detection and Measurement of Radiation
CHEM 244.description: Basic principles of detection and measurement of ionizing radiation; both theory and practical aspects of measurement techniques for alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron radiation, properties of different detector materials, electronics and data treatments, and analysis.
CHEM 244.prereq_text: CHEM 233 with a minimum grade of B- or CBE 276 with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 245A.title: Gas-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
CHEM 245A.description: Sources, chemistry, sinks, and measurements of key atmospheric gaseous species. Chemistry of photochemical oxidant formation, transformation of key inorganic and organic trace gases, and stratospheric ozone cycling. Applications of atmospheric chemistry models to control strategies.

CHEM 245B.title: Multi-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
CHEM 245B.description: Chemical and physical processes leading to the production, aging, and removal of atmospheric particles. Multi-phase processes involving gases, particles, water droplets, and environmental surfaces. Approaches for modeling these processes with applications to control strategies.
CHEM 245B.prereq_text: CHEM 245A with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 245C.title: Special Topics in Atmospheric Chemistry
CHEM 245C.description: The subjects covered vary from year to year.
CHEM 245C.prereq_text: CHEM 245B with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 246.title: Separations and Chromatography
CHEM 246.description: Introduction to modern separation techniques such as gas chromatography, high-performance liquid chromatography, supercritical fluid chromatography, capillary electrophoresis, and field flow fractionation. Applications of these separation strategies are discussed.

CHEM 248.title: Electrochemistry
CHEM 248.description: Fundamentals of electrochemistry including thermodynamics and the electrochemical potential, charge transfer kinetics, and mass transfer. Methods based on controlled potential and controlled current are described; the effects of slow heterogeneous kinetics and the perturbation caused by homogeneous chemistry are discussed.

CHEM 249.title: Analytical Spectroscopy
CHEM 249.description: Advanced treatment of spectroscopic techniques and instrumentation. Atomic and molecular absorption, emission, and scattering processes and their application to quantitative chemical analysis are outlined. Puts different spectroscopic techniques in perspective and demonstrates most appropriate applications to analytical problems.

CHEM 249A.title: Optics I - Physical Optics and Electromagnetic Theory
CHEM 249A.description: Treatment of optical phenomena and interactions between electromagnetic radiation and matter using fundamental electromagnetic laws, with applications to modern spectroscopic methods.

CHEM 249B.title: Optics II – Light-Matter Interaction and Advanced Spectroscopy
CHEM 249B.description: Advanced treatment of interactions between electromagnetic radiation and matter, with applications to linear spectroscopy, time-resolved nonlinear methods, high-power light-matter interactions, and optical parametric processes.
CHEM 249B.prereq_text: CHEM 249A with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 250.title: Computational Chemistry
CHEM 250.description: Basic concepts, methods, and techniques in computational chemistry: density functional and wavefunction theory, molecular property calculations, analysis tools, potential energy surfaces, vibrational effects, molecular dynamics simulations.

CHEM 250L.title: Computational Chemistry Laboratory
CHEM 250L.description: Introduction to the practice of modern computational chemistry through a series of advanced computational experiments.
CHEM 250L.prereq_text: CHEM 250 with a minimum grade of B-.

CHEM 252.title: Special Topics in Physical Chemistry
CHEM 252.description: Advanced topics in physical chemistry. Materials Fee

CHEM 254.title: Special Topics in Computational and Theoretical Chemistry
CHEM 254.description: Subjects covered vary from year to year.

CHEM 263.title: Materials Chemistry
CHEM 263.description: An introduction to crystalline solids, descriptive crystal chemistry, solid-state synthesis and characterization techniques, x-ray and electron diffraction, phase diagrams, electronic band structure of extended solids, semi conductors, and nanoscale inorganic materials.

CHEM 264.title: Analytical Methods for Organic Nanomaterials
CHEM 264.description: Fundamentals of analytical techniques related to measuring the structure and dynamics of organic nanomaterials. Topics include transmission electron microscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, liquid phase electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, light scattering, small angle X-ray, and neutron scattering.

CHEM 266.title: Current Topics in Chemical, Applied, and Materials Physics
CHEM 266.description: The subjects covered vary from year to year. Connection between fundamental principles and implementations in practice in science, industry, and technology.

CHEM 267.title: Photochemistry
CHEM 267.description: Photochemical and photovoltaic processes in molecules and semiconductors; quantum mechanics; statistical thermodynamics; kinetics; and experimental techniques relevant to photon absorption and emission; photochemical charge separation, recombination, and transport of electrons and ions; and interfacial redox chemistry.

CHEM 273.title: Technical Communication Skills
CHEM 273.description: Development of effective communication skills, oral and written presentations, through examples and practice.

CHEM 280.title: Research
CHEM 280.description: Supervised original research toward the preparation of a Ph.D dissertation or M.S. thesis.

CHEM 290.title: Seminar
CHEM 290.description: Weekly seminars and discussions on general and varied topics of current interest in chemistry.

CHEM 291.title: Research Seminar
CHEM 291.description: Detailed discussion of research problems of current interest in the Department. Format, content, and frequency of the course are variable.

CHEM 292.title: Graduate Symposium
CHEM 292.description: Students present public seminars on literature-based research topics in contemporary chemistry. Topics to be chosen by student and approved by instructor.

CHEM 399.title: University Teaching
CHEM 399.description: Required of and limited to Teaching Assistants.

CHINESE 1A.title: Fundamental Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 1A.description: Natural approach emphasizing four fundamental skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Specifically designed for students with no previous experience in any dialect of Chinese. Conducted in Mandarin Chinese using the Pinyin system of Romanization, traditional and simplified Chinese characters.
CHINESE 1A.prereq_text: Placement into CHINESE 1A is also accepted.

CHINESE 1B.title: Fundamental Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 1B.description: Natural approach emphasizing four fundamental skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Specifically designed for students with no previous experience in any dialect of Chinese. Conducted in Mandarin Chinese using the Pinyin system of Romanization, traditional and simplified Chinese characters.
CHINESE 1B.prereq_text: CHINESE 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 1B is also accepted.

CHINESE 1C.title: Fundamental Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 1C.description: Natural approach emphasizing four fundamental skills: listening, speaking, reading and writing. Specifically designed for students with no previous experience in any dialect of Chinese. Conducted in Mandarin Chinese using the Pinyin system of Romanization, traditional and simplified Chinese characters.
CHINESE 1C.prereq_text: CHINESE 1B with a minimum grade of C or CHINESE S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 1C is also accepted.

CHINESE 1MA.title: Fundamentals of Mandarin Chinese - Mandarin Background Track
CHINESE 1MA.description: Natural approach emphasizing four fundamental skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Specifically designed for students with previous background in Mandarin Chinese. Conducted in Mandarin Chinese using the Pinyin system of Romanization, traditional, and simplified Chinese characters.

CHINESE 1MB.title: Fundamentals of Mandarin Chinese - Mandarin Background Track
CHINESE 1MB.description: Natural approach emphasizing four fundamental skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Specifically designed for students with previous background in Mandarin Chinese. Conducted in Mandarin Chinese using the Pinyin system of Romanization, traditional, and simplified Chinese characters.
CHINESE 1MB.prereq_text: CHINESE 1MA with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 1MB is also accepted.

CHINESE 1MC.title: Fundamentals of Mandarin Chinese - Mandarin Background Track
CHINESE 1MC.description: Natural approach emphasizing four fundamental skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Specifically designed for students with previous background in Mandarin Chinese. Conducted in Mandarin Chinese using the Pinyin system of Romanization, traditional, and simplified Chinese characters.
CHINESE 1MC.prereq_text: CHINESE 1MB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 1MC is also accepted.

CHINESE 2A.title: Intermediate Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 2A.description: Both authentic and pedagogically-prepared materials are used to further develop students' ability to communicate in culturally, socially, and linguistically appropriate manners. Taught in Chinese using Pinyin romanization system and both traditional and simplified forms of Chinese.
CHINESE 2A.prereq_text: CHINESE 1C with a minimum grade of C or CHINESE S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 2A is also accepted.

CHINESE 2B.title: Intermediate Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 2B.description: Both authentic and pedagogically-prepared materials are used to further develop students' ability to communicate in culturally, socially, and linguistically appropriate manners. Taught in Chinese using Pinyin romanization system and both traditional and simplified forms of Chinese.
CHINESE 2B.prereq_text: CHINESE 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 2B is also accepted.

CHINESE 2C.title: Intermediate Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 2C.description: Both authentic and pedagogically-prepared materials are used to further develop students' ability to communicate in culturally, socially, and linguistically appropriate manners. Taught in Chinese using Pinyin romanization system and both traditional and simplified forms of Chinese.
CHINESE 2C.prereq_text: CHINESE 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 2C is also accepted.

CHINESE 10.title: Learning Assistant Program
CHINESE 10.description: Learning Assistant Program in which advanced Chinese students provide assistance to students at a lower level. One hour of learning assistance per week.

CHINESE 100A.title: Classical Chinese
CHINESE 100A.description: Introduction to classical Chinese grammar and vocabulary with emphasis on reading basic texts.

CHINESE 100B.title: Classical Chinese
CHINESE 100B.description: Introduction to classical Chinese grammar and vocabulary with emphasis on reading basic texts.

CHINESE 100C.title: Classical Chinese
CHINESE 100C.description: Introduction to classical Chinese grammar and vocabulary with emphasis on reading basic texts.

CHINESE 103A.title: Advanced Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 103A.description: A continuation of CHINESE 2A-CHINESE 2B-CHINESE 2C. Emphasizes conceptualization, self-expression, and academic skills in Chinese. Authentic texts from modern Chinese prose and newspapers are used. Taught in Mandarin Chinese using both traditional and simplified forms of Chinese characters.
CHINESE 103A.prereq_text: CHINESE 2C with a minimum grade of C or CHINESE 2DC with a minimum grade of C or CHINESE 2MC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 103A is also accepted.

CHINESE 103B.title: Advanced Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 103B.description: A continuation of CHINESE 103A. Emphasizes conceptualization, self-expression, and academic skills in Chinese. Authentic texts from modern Chinese prose and newspapers are used. Taught in Mandarin Chinese using both traditional and simplified forms of Chinese characters.
CHINESE 103B.prereq_text: CHINESE 103A with a minimum grade of C.

CHINESE 103C.title: Advanced Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 103C.description: A continuation of CHINESE 103B. Emphasizes conceptualization, self-expression, and academic skills in Chinese. Authentic texts from modern Chinese prose and newspapers are used. Taught in Mandarin Chinese using both traditional and simplified forms of Chinese characters.
CHINESE 103C.prereq_text: CHINESE 103B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 103C is also accepted.

CHINESE 104A.title: Fourth-Year Mandarin Chinese
CHINESE 104A.description: Continued emphasis on comprehension, grammar, and proficiency in reading, composition, and conversation through intensive study and analysis of specific literary texts.
CHINESE 104A.prereq_text: CHINESE 103C with a minimum grade of C.

CHINESE 105.title: Topics in Professional Chinese
CHINESE 105.description: Designed for students with advanced fluency in Chinese. Develops students’ language learning to professional levels with cultural and contextual knowledge and with formal communication and presentation skills.
CHINESE 105.prereq_text: CHINESE 103C with a minimum grade of C. Placement into CHINESE 104A or higher is also accepted.

CHINESE 115.title: Topics in Chinese Literature: Advanced Texts
CHINESE 115.description: Designed for students with near-fluency in reading Chinese. Readings may include both literary and philosophical work by important writers, but the emphasis is on literary texts and writings that interpret those texts.

CHINESE 199.title: Independent Study
CHINESE 199.description: Investigation of special topics through directed reading in Chinese. Paper required.

CHINESE 202.title: Readings in Traditional Chinese Poetry
CHINESE 202.description: Close readings of selected premodern poetic texts.
CHINESE 202.prereq_text: CHINESE 100C with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 203.title: Readings in Modern Chinese Literature
CHINESE 203.description: Close readings of selected modern literary texts.
CHINESE 203.prereq_text: CHINESE 101C with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 204.title: Readings in Chinese Literary and Cultural Theory
CHINESE 204.description: Close readings of selected texts in premodern criticism and theory.
CHINESE 204.prereq_text: CHINESE 100C with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 211A.title: Studies in Traditional Chinese Narrative and Prose
CHINESE 211A.description: Two-quarter seminar in traditional Chinese narrative and prose, with topics varying from year to year.
CHINESE 211A.prereq_text: CHINESE 100C with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 211B.title: Studies in Traditional Chinese Narrative and Prose
CHINESE 211B.description: Two-quarter seminar in traditional Chinese narrative and prose, with topics varying from year to year.
CHINESE 211B.prereq_text: CHINESE 211A with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 212A.title: Studies in Traditional Chinese Poetry
CHINESE 212A.description: Two-quarter seminar in traditional Chinese poetry, with topics varying from year to year.
CHINESE 212A.prereq_text: CHINESE 100C with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 212B.title: Studies in Traditional Chinese Poetry
CHINESE 212B.description: Two-quarter seminar in traditional Chinese poetry, with topics varying from year to year.
CHINESE 212B.prereq_text: CHINESE 212A with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 213A.title: Studies in Modern Chinese Literature
CHINESE 213A.description: Two-quarter seminar in modern Chinese literature, with topics varying from year to year. Research paper required.

CHINESE 214.title: Studies in Chinese Literature and Cultural Theory
CHINESE 214.description: Seminar in Chinese literature and cultural theory, with topics varying from year to year. Research paper required.
CHINESE 214.prereq_text: CHINESE 100C with a minimum grade of B- or CHINESE 101C with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 230.title: Topics in Chinese Literature and Culture
CHINESE 230.description: Seminar in Chinese literature and culture, with topics varying from year to year. Research paper required.
CHINESE 230.prereq_text: CHINESE 100C with a minimum grade of B- or CHINESE 101A with a minimum grade of B-.

CHINESE 290.title: Independent Study
CHINESE 290.description: Directed research on topic determined in consultation with faculty member. A term paper or project is required.

CLASSIC 10.title: Medical Terminology
CLASSIC 10.description: A study of English terms derived from Greek and Latin that are important to contemporary medicine, science, and other professions. Emphasis on development of word-building skills. No prior knowledge of Greek or Latin required.

CLASSIC 36A.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Early Greece
CLASSIC 36A.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from its origins in the Bronze Age to the mid-Archaic period. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, religion, and archaeological remains.

CLASSIC 36B.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Late Archaic and Classical Greece
CLASSIC 36B.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the Late Archaic period to the Classical period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

CLASSIC 36C.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Fourth-Century and Hellenistic Greece
CLASSIC 36C.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the fourth century BCE through to the Hellenistic period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

CLASSIC 37A.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Origins to Roman Republic
CLASSIC 37A.description: A survey of the development of Roman civilization from its eighth century BCE beginnings to the civil wars of the first century BCE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

CLASSIC 37B.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Roman Empire
CLASSIC 37B.description: A survey of Roman civilization from Augustus’s consolidation of power following the civil wars of the first century BCE to the crisis of the third century CE. Includes social history, literature, art, architecture, and religion.

CLASSIC 37C.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: The Fall of Rome
CLASSIC 37C.description: A survey of Roman civilization from the crisis of the third century CE to the so-called “fall of Rome” in 476 CE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

CLASSIC 45A.title: Classical Mythology: The Gods
CLASSIC 45A.description: An overview of the main myths of the gods of the ancient Greeks and Romans and their influence in contemporary and later literature and art. Includes readings from both ancient and modern sources.

CLASSIC 45B.title: Classical Mythology: The Heroes
CLASSIC 45B.description: An overview of the main myths of the heroes of the ancient Greeks and Romans and their influence in contemporary and later literature and art. Includes readings from both ancient and modern sources.

CLASSIC 45C.title: Classical Mythology: Ancient and Modern Perspectives of Classical Mythology
CLASSIC 45C.description: Detailed examination of key Greek and Roman myths, their interpretations, and the influence they have exerted on literature, art, and popular culture in subsequent periods.

CLASSIC 99.title: Special Studies in Classics
CLASSIC 99.description: Lower-division level independent research with Classics faculty.

CLASSIC 131B.title: Ancient Persia
CLASSIC 131B.description: Survey of the history of Persia in antiquity.

CLASSIC 140.title: Classics and History: The Ancient World
CLASSIC 140.description: Selected topics in society and culture of the Graeco-Roman world. Readings in translation.

CLASSIC 150.title: Classical Mythology
CLASSIC 150.description: Selected myths and legends as used in Classical literature, and their modern interpretations.

CLASSIC 160.title: Topics in Classical Literature in English Translation
CLASSIC 160.description: Studies in selected areas of Classical literature. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

CLASSIC 160W.title: Topics in Classical Literature in English Translation
CLASSIC 160W.description: Studies in selected areas of Classical literature. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
CLASSIC 160W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

CLASSIC 166.title: Topics in Classical Reception
CLASSIC 166.description: Studies in selected areas of Classical reception. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

CLASSIC 170.title: Topics in Classical Civilization
CLASSIC 170.description: Studies in selected areas of Classical civilization. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

CLASSIC 176.title: International Studies and the Classics
CLASSIC 176.description: Develops a broader understanding of the formation of different cultures and countries of Classical times and their impact on the modern world.

CLASSIC 192A.title: Senior Capstone
CLASSIC 192A.description: Under the guidance of a faculty mentor, majors design and execute a senior project. This project may be a research paper, dramatic production, school curriculum, etc. All projects must be approved by the faculty mentor.
CLASSIC 192A.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

CLASSIC 192B.title: Senior Capstone
CLASSIC 192B.description: Under the guidance of a faculty mentor, majors design and execute a senior project. This project may be a research paper, dramatic production, school curriculum, etc. All projects must be approved by the faculty mentor.
CLASSIC 192B.prereq_text: CLASSIC 192A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

CLASSIC 197.title: Colloquium
CLASSIC 197.description: Students meet faculty members and explore the depth and breadth of a classical education inclusive of and beyond the Greco-Roman antiquity. They are also introduced to ideas and methods of reception of ancient worlds to the present day.

CLASSIC 198.title: Directed Group Study
CLASSIC 198.description: Special topics in Classical studies through directed reading and research.

CLT&THY 200A.title: Political Economy: Methods and Critique
CLT&THY 200A.description: Introduction to canonical texts in Marxism coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken after CLT&THY 200B.

CLT&THY 200B.title: Libidinal Economy: Methods and Critique
CLT&THY 200B.description: Introduction to canonical texts in psychoanalysis coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken before CLT&THY 200A.

CLT&THY 200C.title: Theory from Below
CLT&THY 200C.description: Introduction to systems of thought understudied or undervalued in academic canons; for instance, systems constituted in communities' practices or theories that do not seek permanence or generality.

CLT&THY 280.title: Independent Study
CLT&THY 280.description: Limited to students who have not yet received the M.A. degree.

CLT&THY 289.title: Topics in Culture and Theory
CLT&THY 289.description: Seminars on various topics in Culture and Theory.

CLT&THY 298.title: Directed Reading
CLT&THY 298.description: Directed readings on a specific topic agreed upon by students and their instructors. Limited to students who have completed their M.A. degree and are preparing for their qualifying exam.

CLT&THY 299.title: Dissertation Research
CLT&THY 299.description: Dissertation research in Culture and Theory.

COGS 7A.title: Introduction to Psychology
COGS 7A.description: Introduction to field of psychology, addressing the application of scientific methods to the study of human development, learning, memory, problem solving, perception, biological mechanisms, emotions and motivation, personality, psychopathology, and effects of diverse social and cultural contexts on human behavior.

and.not: AP PSYCHOLOGY score of 4 or greater

COGS 7A.prereq_text: NO AP PSYCHOLOGY score of 4 or greater AND NO PSYCHOLOGY MAJORS ONLY AND NO COGNITIVE SCIENCES MAJORS ONLY AND NO PSYCH & SOC BEHAVIOR MAJORS ONLY AND NO PSYCHOLOGICAL SCI MAJORS ONLY AND NO PSYCH 7A AND NO PSCI 9

COGS 9A.title: Psychology Fundamentals
COGS 9A.description: Part of a two-course series that provides a comprehensive introduction to psychology. Required for students majoring in Cognitive Sciences or Psychology. Topics include the science of psychology, research methods, biology and behavior, consciousness, sensation, and perception.

COGS 9B.title: Psychology Fundamentals
COGS 9B.description: Part of a two-course series that provides a comprehensive introduction to psychology. Required for students majoring in Cognitive Sciences or Psychology. Topics include learning and memory, thinking, language and intelligence, human development, emotion, and motivation.

COGS 10A.title: Exploratory Data Analysis
COGS 10A.description: Learn multiple ways of visualizing data, of transforming data, looking for consistencies and patterns in data, and interpreting these patterns to reach conclusions. Serves as first introduction to computer programming using the R language.
COGS 10A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 10B.title: Probability and Inference
COGS 10B.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on thorough understanding of the probabilistic and logical basis of formal statistical inference, and the concept of statistical evidence. Applications in R.
COGS 10B.prereq_text: COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 10B.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 10C.title: Statistical Models
COGS 10C.description: Students learn about standard procedures in statistics for the social sciences, with a focus on linear models for discovering the underlying structure in data. Applications in R.
COGS 10C.prereq_text: COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 10C.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 14M.title: MATLAB Programming
COGS 14M.description: MATLAB is a mathematical software package for solving quantitative problems often encountered in experimental psychology. Topics include rudiments of programming, statistical analysis of data, matrix algebra, signal processing, graphic visualization, and simulated models of cognitive and perceptual processes.
COGS 14M.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 14P.title: Scientific Python for Research
COGS 14P.description: Introduces Python for data analysis and modeling encountered in cognitive science and neuroscience. Topics include data structures, execution control, graphic visualization, and interaction with sound and display interfaces. Application in statistical analysis, model simulation, and stimulus presentation and experimental control.
COGS 14P.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 21A.title: Adolescent Psychology
COGS 21A.description: Focuses on psychosocial dynamics of today's adolescents in America emphasizing the quest for identity, independence, values, and sexual orientation. The influence of society, family, school, and peers is analyzed. Strategies for helping troubled adolescents are discussed.
COGS 21A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 56L.title: Acquisition of Language
COGS 56L.description: What children say, what they mean, and what they understand. Theories about the learning of language by one-, two-, and three-year-olds. Comparison of kinds of data on which these theories are based.

COGS 60N.title: Neurobiology of Cognition
COGS 60N.description: Introduces the neurobiological components of human cognition. Topics include discussion of the cortical structures and functions that underlie these behaviors. Emphasis placed on the development and organization of the healthy brain.
COGS 60N.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 78A.title: Self-Identity and Society
COGS 78A.description: Studies sociological contributions to theory and research in social psychology, with focus on the social influences on personality, attitudes, beliefs, and behavior; socialization, human groups, and social interaction.

COGS 89.title: Special Topics in Lower-Division Cognitive Sciences
COGS 89.description: Studies in selected areas of cognitive science at the lower-division level. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
COGS 89.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS H101A.title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences I
COGS H101A.description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.
COGS H101A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors only.

COGS H101B.title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences II
COGS H101B.description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.
COGS H101B.prereq_text: COGS H101A with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS H101B.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors only.

COGS H101C.title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences III
COGS H101C.description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.
COGS H101C.prereq_text: COGS H101B with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS H101C.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors only.

COGS 105.title: Introduction to Statistical Learning
COGS 105.description: Introduction to statistical learning as a tool for scientific research. Topics include linear regression, logistic regression, model selection, cross-validation, ridge and Lasso regularization, classification trees, ensemble methods, random forests, unsupervised learning, PCA, k-means clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and PLS regression.
COGS 105.prereq_text: COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 or MATH 9 and ((COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110) and MATH 2B.

COGS 106.title: Computational Lab Skills
COGS 106.description: Teaches programming tools, skills, and conventions for collaborative work in computational cognitive science. Topics covered include program structure, version control, random number generation, plotting, basic model fitting, and numerical optimization methods.
COGS 106.prereq_text: COGS 14M or COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 and ((COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110).

COGS 107.title: Cognitive Modeling
COGS 107.description: Cognitive process models analyzed using computational Bayesian methods. Formal statistical specification of models, parameter estimation, model evaluation, and research applications. Covers multinomial process trees, signal detection theory, Thurstone ranking models, item-response theory, decision models, and reaction time models.
COGS 107.prereq_text: COGS 14M or COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 and ((COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110).
COGS 107.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 108.title: Neural Analytics
COGS 108.description: Introduces the theoretical foundations and practical applications of neural data analysis. Topics include models of neural signals, neural time series analysis, and machine learning applications in cognitive neuroscience.
COGS 108.prereq_text: COGS 14M or COGS 14P or I&C SCI 31 and ((COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-) or STATS 110).
COGS 108.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 109W.title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
COGS 109W.description: Read and discuss examples of the primary research leading to the concepts covered in Psychology Fundamentals. Focuses on how this research is conducted and how inferences from it are drawn.
COGS 109W.prereq_text: COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C-. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

COGS 112A.title: Experimental Psychology
COGS 112A.description: Emphasis on design of experiments and analysis of results. Experiments are conducted in laboratory sections.
COGS 112A.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 112A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112BW.title: Advanced Experimental Psychology
COGS 112BW.description: Design and analysis of multivalent, factorial, and correlational studies. Students prepare proposals for independent research.
COGS 112BW.prereq_text: COGS 112A and COGS 112LA. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
COGS 112BW.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112C.title: Research in Experimental Psychology
COGS 112C.description: Each student conducts a research project in experimental psychology. The projects are discussed in a seminar format. Written reports on each project are submitted at the end of the quarter.
COGS 112C.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112D.title: Research Design
COGS 112D.description: An examination of design of studies through the lens of validity of scientific claims. You already know how to perform statistical inference. Here we ask a different, broader question: When is an inference worth believing?
COGS 112D.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C- and (COGS 14P with a minimum grade of C- or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C-).
COGS 112D.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112E.title: Learning and Memory
COGS 112E.description: Theories in learning and memory research and the methodological tools used to test them. Experimental design, statistical data analysis, and interpretation using hands-on lab exercises and the R programming language.
COGS 112E.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 112E.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LA.title: Experimental Psychology Laboratory
COGS 112LA.description: Required laboratory section and co-requisite for COGS 112A.
COGS 112LA.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LB.title: Advanced Experimental Psychology Laboratory
COGS 112LB.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LC.title: Research in Experimental Psychology
COGS 112LC.description: Required laboratory section and co-requisite for COGS 112C.
COGS 112LC.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LE.title: Learning and Memory Lab
COGS 112LE.description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112E.
COGS 112LE.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LM.title: Research Methods in Psychology Laboratory
COGS 112LM.description: Required laboratory section and co-requisite for COGS 112M.
COGS 112LM.restriction: Psychology majors and Cognitive Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LN.title: fMRI Research Laboratory
COGS 112LN.description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112N.
COGS 112LN.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LP.title: Research in Perception and Psychophysics Laboratory
COGS 112LP.description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112P.
COGS 112LP.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112LR.title: Cognitive Robotics Laboratory
COGS 112LR.description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for COGS 112R.
COGS 112LR.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112M.title: Research Methods in Psychology
COGS 112M.description: Research methods in psychology for majors who wish to fulfill this requirement separately from upper-division writing. Covers both experimental and descriptive research methods, analysis of results, and reading the psychological literature. Research experience is provided in laboratory sections.
COGS 112M.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 112M.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112N.title: Introduction to fMRI Research
COGS 112N.description: Introduction to functional magnetic resonance imaging as a tool in cognitive neuroscience. Covers inferences about brain activity using MRI, evaluates experimental design considerations, and univariate and multivariate statistical analysis approaches.
COGS 112N.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 112N.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112O.title: Computational Modeling of Behavior
COGS 112O.description: Learn how computational models can be used as theoretical tools to predict, evaluate, and interpret psychological data in a number of domains in psychology, such as perception, learning, decision-making, and problem-solving. Focuses on skill development through coding.
COGS 112O.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C- and (COGS 14P with a minimum grade of C- or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C-).
COGS 112O.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112P.title: Research in Perception and Psychophysics
COGS 112P.description: Introduction to design and practice of experiments: students perform auditory, visual, tactile, or other experiments. Emphasis on methodology, finding and reading previous research, generating research ideas, statistical analysis.
COGS 112P.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 112P.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 112R.title: Cognitive Robotics
COGS 112R.description: Introduces concepts on experimental design, embodiment, robot construction, and computer programming. Concepts of embodied intelligence and case studies of cognitive robotics are covered in lecture. Simple robots are constructed and programmed to carry out different behavioral experiments in lab.
COGS 112R.prereq_text: COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 10B with a minimum grade of C- and COGS 10C with a minimum grade of C-.
COGS 112R.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 119.title: Special Topics in Research Methodologies
COGS 119.description: Studies in selected areas of research methodologies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
COGS 119.restriction: Psychology majors and Cognitive Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 120A.title: Abnormal Psychology
COGS 120A.description: Introduction to psychopathology and behavioral deviations, and the concepts of theories regarding these conditions.
COGS 120A.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 120A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 120D.title: Developmental Psychology
COGS 120D.description: A general introduction to the study of the physical, intellectual, social, and emotional development of the child from birth to adulthood.
COGS 120D.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 120D.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 120H.title: History of Psychology
COGS 120H.description: A history of the development of various schools and systems of psychological thought.
COGS 120H.prereq_text: (COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B).
COGS 120H.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 120P.title: Personality Theories
COGS 120P.description: A survey of the evolution of personality theory during this century. An overview of major perspectives in the field, with special attention to Freud, Jung, and Adler.
COGS 120P.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 120P.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 121S.title: Psychology of Sleep and Consciousness
COGS 121S.description: Covers the physiology, neurochemistry, and neuroanatomy associated with sleep, contemporary sleep theory, REM and NREM, phenomenology, sleep disorders, examination of differences between conscious and unconscious cognitive function, the history of sleep and dream theories from ancient time to present day.
COGS 121S.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 121S.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 122C.title: Clinical Psychology
COGS 122C.description: Provides overview of the clinical psychology field including theories and techniques used in counseling and testing.
COGS 122C.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 122C.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 122I.title: Organizational/Industrial Psychology
COGS 122I.description: Introduction to applied psychology in organizations, including personnel testing, selection, training and evaluation, job and classification analysis, job satisfaction and motivation, organizational development, leadership, market research, and consumer psychology. Potential ethical problems are discussed.
COGS 122I.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A or COGS 9B.
COGS 122I.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 122J.title: Advanced Industrial-Organizational Psychology
COGS 122J.description: Covers advanced topics in industrial-organizational psychology focused on organizational behavior and development; integrates cognitive psychology and business; emphasizes culture, personality, leadership, and motivation in optimizing systems and managing change and conflict.
COGS 122J.prereq_text: (COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or COGS 9A or COGS 9B.
COGS 122J.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 123C.title: Creativity
COGS 123C.description: Introduction to creativity, addressing creativity with respect to cognition, development, neuroscience, education, personality, motivation, and social aspects of creativity.
COGS 123C.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B).
COGS 123C.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 123M.title: Psychology of Music
COGS 123M.description: Introduction to the psychology of music, addressing music with respect to the workings of the ear and brain, the perception and cognition of musical elements like rhythm and melody, and the development of musical skills.
COGS 123M.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B).
COGS 123M.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 124S.title: Sports Psychology
COGS 124S.description: Discusses the field of sports psychology with an emphasis on clinical practice including motivation, goal setting, performance skills, and mental skills. Discusses and utilizes a wide range of techniques designed to enhance performance and manage problems among athletes.
COGS 124S.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 124S.restriction: Psychology majors and Cognitive Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 124V.title: Psychology of Violence
COGS 124V.description: Discusses the psychology of violence and aggression with an emphasis on understanding the psychological, social, and physiological roots of violent and aggressive behavior. Psychological treatment techniques and strategies for prevention of aggressive and violent behavior are also discussed.
COGS 124V.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 124V.restriction: Psychology majors and Cognitive Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 126M.title: Moral Psychology
COGS 126M.description: Survey course studying moral psychology and philosophy. Empirical research from psychology is supplemented with texts from philosophy for better grounding in philosophical theory.
COGS 126M.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9B.
COGS 126M.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 127P.title: Personality Disorders
COGS 127P.description: The history of personality disorder classification; defining characteristics of each disorder; the causes, courses, and outcomes of personality disorders; and information regarding assessment, prevention, and treatments of these disorders.

COGS 130A.title: Perception and Sensory Processes
COGS 130A.description: A general introduction to the scientific study of sensory processes and perceptual phonomena, with special emphasis in the visual systems.
COGS 130A.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 130A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 130N.title: Neuroscience of Perception
COGS 130N.description: Introduces the principles that human perception is determined by the properties of brain circuitry and that these brain circuits evolved to interpret the properties of the physical environment to explore human perception from peripheral sensory organs to cortical processing.
COGS 130N.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 130N.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 131A.title: Vision
COGS 131A.description: Visual perception and the anatomy and physiology of the visual system. Topics include the retina and the visual pathway; visual sensitivity; color vision; spatial vision; motion perception; and the development of the visual system.
COGS 131A.prereq_text: NO PSYCH 131A AND NO BIO SCI N182
COGS 131A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 131B.title: Hearing
COGS 131B.description: Auditory perception, the anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, and the physics of sound. Topics include neural transduction of sound, sensitivity, sound localization, complex sound perception, and hearing loss.
COGS 131B.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 140J.title: Judgment and Decision Making
COGS 140J.description: The psychology of human decision making. Theories, models, experiments, and data that inform how people make choices, judgments, and other decisions. Topics include optimality and bias, mental simulation, learning and feedback, expertise, emotional effects, and group decision making.
COGS 140J.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 140L.title: Learning and Decision Making
COGS 140L.description: The psychological and neural bases of learning about and interacting with the world. Topics include shaping of behavior by rewards and punishments, abstraction of relational information, goal-directed versus habitual decision strategies, social knowledge transmission, and behavioral and substance addictions.
COGS 140L.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9A.
COGS 140L.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 140M.title: Human Memory
COGS 140M.description: Developments in the area of memory; history of memory research; theories of the nature of memory. Visual memory, recognition memory, high-speed scanning, free recall, short-term memory, mnemonics, retrieval, relationship of memory to thinking. Selected theoretical formulations for memory.
COGS 140M.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9B.
COGS 140M.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 143P.title: Human Problem Solving
COGS 143P.description: Modern developments in the psychology of human problem solving. Topics include concept identification, arithmetic, sets, logic puzzles, story problems, group problem solving, and theorem proving.
COGS 143P.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or COGS 9B.
COGS 143P.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 150.title: Psychology of Language
COGS 150.description: Examines language using the tools of experimental psychology. From sounds to words to spoken and written sentences, explores how language is used in real time, and how its use reveals how it is represented in the mind.

COGS 153.title: African American Psychology
COGS 153.description: Historical overview of the development of black psychology and the African American frame of reference. Topics include personality development, psychological assessment, issues in education, black mental health, and the role of the African American psychologist in the community.

COGS 157M.title: Computational Methods for Language Research
COGS 157M.description: Focuses on computational methods useful for language research. Students become familiar with software and programming languages used for extracting information from electronic datasets and for creating basic simulations of linguistic cognition. No prior programming experience assumed.
COGS 157M.prereq_text: COGS 150 or LSCI 155 or COGS 156A or LSCI 151.

COGS 160A.title: Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience
COGS 160A.description: Introduction to the neural basis of human perceptual, motor, and cognitive abilities. Topics include sensory perception, motor control, memory, language, attention, emotion, frontal lobe function, functional brain imaging, and neuropsychological disorders.
COGS 160A.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B).
COGS 160A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 160D.title: Brain Disorders and Behavior
COGS 160D.description: Examines the localization of human brain functions and the effects of neurological disorders on psychological functions such as perception, motor control, language, memory, and decision-making.
COGS 160D.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.
COGS 160D.restriction: Biological Sciences majors, Cognitive Sciences majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 161.title: Language and the Brain
COGS 161.description: Research analysis on biological bases of human linguistic capacity. Development, focusing on hemispheric specialization, plasticity; localization of specific linguistic functions in adults, with emphasis on study of aphasias; relation of linguistic capacity to general cognitive capacity, considering research on retardation.
COGS 161.prereq_text: (COGS 7A or PSCI 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or (COGS 9A or PSCI 11A) and (COGS 9B or PSCI 11B) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A.

COGS 161H.title: Hearing and the Brain
COGS 161H.description: An overview of brain mechanisms of hearing, including perception of simple sounds, speech, and music. Begins with sound itself, and looks at processing by the ear, auditory pathways, auditory cortex, and beyond. Also auditory development, learning, and clinical issues.
COGS 161H.prereq_text: COGS 160A or BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93.
COGS 161H.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 161M.title: Evolution of Language and Music
COGS 161M.description: Focuses on the biological evolution of two rather unique human traits: language and music. No other species is capable of “doing” language or music with the complexity that humans can.
COGS 161M.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B) or LSCI 3.
COGS 161M.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and Language Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 162N.title: Human Neuropsychology
COGS 162N.description: A survey of human brain disorders using a clinical case study approach to illustrate fundamental issues in studying brain and behavior. Topics include sensory deficits, attentional neglect, amnesia, cortical organization, clinical psychopathology, and more.
COGS 162N.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or COGS 9A.

COGS 163A.title: Metacognition
COGS 163A.description: Critical analysis of primary literature targeting metacognition in perception and memory, including neural correlates. Coverage includes behavioral experimental design, computational models, psychophysics, noninvasive neuroimaging, and neural stimulation approaches.
COGS 163A.prereq_text: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B).
COGS 163A.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 173A.title: Psychological Anthropology
COGS 173A.description: Cultural differences and similarities in personality and behavior. Child-rearing practices and consequent adult personality characteristics, biocultural aspects of child development and attachment, culture and behavior evolutionary models, politically linked personality, cognitive anthropology, psychology of narrative forms, comparative national character studies.
COGS 173A.prereq_text: ANTHRO 2A or COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or (COGS 9A and COGS 9B).
COGS 173A.restriction: Anthropology majors, Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychology majors, Anthropology minors, and Medical Anthropology minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 174H.title: Chicano/Latino Families
COGS 174H.description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

COGS 176A.title: Political Psychology
COGS 176A.description: Examination of how psychological theory and research may be used to better understand political thought and behavior. Drawing on theories of learning, cognition, and personality, discusses such topics as the formation of political attitudes, and the process of political decision-making.
COGS 176A.prereq_text: NO PSYCH 176A AND NO POL SCI 128C

COGS 177D.title: Deviance
COGS 177D.description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.
COGS 177D.prereq_text: NO PSYCH 177D AND NO CRM/LAW C107 AND NO SOCIOL 156
COGS 177D.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology majors, Sociology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 177F.title: Forensic Psychology: Advanced Seminar
COGS 177F.description: Focuses on the psychology of criminal offending, particularly violent behavior. Examines violence, sexual offending, and mental disorder related to crime with regard to clinical assessment and treatment; mental health services within forensic institutions.
COGS 177F.prereq_text: (PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C) and PSY 102C and (PSY 161C or CRM/LAW C160). Interview required

COGS 178N.title: Social Psychology of Networks
COGS 178N.description: Review of network methods used in small group and organizational research. Discussion of social psychological literature relevant to the network of study of cognitive social structure, exchange/communication, identity negotiation, and social control. Case study of network datasets exemplifies research issues.

COGS 189.title: Special Topics in Upper-Division Cognitive Sciences
COGS 189.description: Studies in selected areas of cognitive science at the upper-division level. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
COGS 189.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COGS 198.title: Directed Group Study
COGS 198.description: Directed study with Cognitive Sciences faculty.

COGS 199.title: Individual Study
COGS 199.description: Independent research with Cognitive Sciences faculty.

COGS 201A.title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
COGS 201A.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.
COGS 201A.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors and Cognitive Sciences majors only.

COGS 201B.title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
COGS 201B.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.
COGS 201B.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors and Cognitive Sciences majors only.

COGS 201C.title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
COGS 201C.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.
COGS 201C.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors and Cognitive Sciences majors only.

COGS 202A.title: Proseminar in the Cognitive Sciences
COGS 202A.description: Introduction to the conceptual foundations and basic research results in the cognitive sciences for first-year graduate students.
COGS 202A.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors and Cognitive Sciences majors only.

COGS 203A.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences I
COGS 203A.description: Logic and set theory are covered during the first three weeks, using an interactive computer system. The remaining seven weeks are devoted to probability theory and cover elementary concepts from samples spaces to Chebychev's Inequality and the moment generating function.

COGS 203B.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences II
COGS 203B.description: An introduction to statistical estimation and statistical inference. Topics include sufficiency and the Rao-Blackwell Theorem, completeness and the Lehmann-Scheffe Theorem. The method of maximum likelihood is explored in some detail. Inference in linear models covers regression and analysis of variance.

COGS 203C.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences III
COGS 203C.description: Discussion of the fundamentals of statistical inference and computational implementations of common statistical models.

COGS 204A.title: Seminar in Professional Development
COGS 204A.description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on grant writing and submission process, responsible conduct of research, and ethics training.
COGS 204A.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors, Cognitive Sciences majors, and Psychology majors only.

COGS 204B.title: Seminar in Professional Development
COGS 204B.description: Development of professional skills. Focus on scientific presentations and preparation.
COGS 204B.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors, Cognitive Sciences majors, and Psychology majors only.

COGS 204C.title: Seminar in Professional Development
COGS 204C.description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on career opportunities, interests and information, and community outreach.
COGS 204C.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors, Cognitive Sciences majors, and Psychology majors only.

COGS 205B.title: Computational Lab Skills for Cognitive Scientists I
COGS 205B.description: Provides an in-depth introduction to writing MATLAB programs to run auditory and visual experiments. Topics covered include program structure, stimulus generation, presentation, and data collection.
COGS 205B.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors and Cognitive Neuroscience majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Doctor of Philosophy only.

COGS 205C.title: Introduction to Statistical Learning
COGS 205C.description: Introduction to statistical learning for scientific research. Topics include linear regression, logistic regression, model selection, cross-validation, ridge and Lasso regularization, classification trees, ensemble methods, random forests, unsupervised learning, PCA, k-means clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and PLS regression.
COGS 205C.prereq_text: Required: Knowledge of calculus, computer programming, and undergraduate-level statistics.
COGS 205C.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors and Cognitive Sciences majors only.

COGS 205D.title: Neural Networks and Machine Learning
COGS 205D.description: An introduction and review of the current state of the art in neural networks and machine learning with specific emphasis of applications to behavioral and neuroscience data analysis and modeling.

COGS 210A.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences I: Topics in Perception
COGS 210A.description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on visual, auditory, and somatic perception and bottom-up mechanisms of attention.

COGS 210B.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences II: Topics in Cognition
COGS 210B.description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on emotion, top-down attention, goal-directed behavior, categorization, judgment, and decision-making.

COGS 210C.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences III: Topics in Learning and Development
COGS 210C.description: Discusses experimental data, formal models of learning, and evidence linking learning and development to its neural substrates. Topics include Pavlovian and instrumental conditioning, language acquisition, causal reasoning, perceptual learning, category formation, and structure learning.

COGS 213.title: The Mind/Body Problem
COGS 213.description: Multidisciplinary, drawing on information from the fields of quantum physics, computer vision, artificial intelligence, cognition, neurophysiology, philosophy, and psychophysics.

COGS 214.title: Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
COGS 214.description: Considers a range of statistical methods of data analysis and simple cognitive models using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.

COGS 218.title: Hearing
COGS 218.description: Examines auditory sensation and perception using psychophysical and neuroscientific perspectives. Covers physical aspects of sound; subcortical auditory processing; aspects of sensation and perception such as sensitivity, sound localization, and complex-sound recognition; neuroscientific studies of cortical function; and abnormal auditory processing.

COGS 229.title: Special Topics in Human Cognition
COGS 229.description: Current research in brain/ behavior relationships, human memory, and learning theory is presented.

COGS 235.title: Analysis of Neural Time Series
COGS 235.description: Hands-on introduction to techniques for the analysis of neural time series data, with a primary focus on the electroencephalogram (EEG). Topics may include the physiological basis of EEG, time-frequency analysis, spatial filtering, and methods of assessing connectivity.

COGS 237.title: Advanced Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
COGS 237.description: Considers a range of advanced cognitive process models including models of signal detection, memory retention, category learning, stimulus representation, and reasoning using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.
COGS 237.prereq_text: COGS 214 with a minimum grade of B-.

COGS 239.title: Special Topics in Methodology and Models
COGS 239.description: Current research in cognitive sciences methodologies, concepts, and models is presented.

COGS 259.title: Special Topics in Human Performance
COGS 259.description: Current research in the human issues involved with sensation, perception, and cognition.

COGS 261N.title: Cortical Neuroscience
COGS 261N.description: Physiology of the cerebral cortex, theoretical neuroscience, and the neural basis of perception.

COGS 262.title: Functional Neuroanatomy
COGS 262.description: It is impossible to truly understand human behavior without some understanding of the physical structure that enables behavior. Examines recent findings in functional neuroantomy through lectures and papers discussing links between particular behaviors and specific brain structures.

COGS 265.title: Introduction to Functional MRI
COGS 265.description: Describes the fundamentals of imaging the human brain function using functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI). Topics include basic fMRI physics, experimental design, and data acquisition and analysis.

COGS 268A.title: Computational Neuroscience
COGS 268A.description: Introduction to computational neuroscience. Mathematical models of single neurons, neural circuits, thalamocortical systems, and cortical mass action can stimulate single-unit, local field potential, and EEG dynamics. These models are used to investigate mechanisms of sensation, motor control, attention, and consciousness.

COGS 268R.title: Cognitive Robotics
COGS 268R.description: Introduces concepts for studying cognitive function by embedding brain models on robotic platforms. Topics include robot construction, computer programming, and the notion of embodiment. Students construct simple robots and program these robots to perform different behaviors.

COGS 289.title: Special Topics in Sensation and Perception
COGS 289.description: Current research in the reception and processing of visual and auditory stimuli presented.

COGS 290.title: Dissertation Research
COGS 290.description: Dissertation research with Cognitive Science faculty.
COGS 290.restriction: Cognitive Neuroscience majors and Cognitive Sciences majors only.

COGS 299.title: Individual Study
COGS 299.description: Individual research with Cognitive Science faculty.

COM LIT 3.title: Just Reading: Developing the Reading Experience
