COM LIT 3.description: Develops the reading experience apart from writing. Develops tools for sustained attention in reading practice across a wide range of genres and media from across the globe. Students learn to appreciate elements of reading experience such as attention and perplexity.

COM LIT 6.title: Topics in Native American and Indigenous Literatures
COM LIT 6.description: Reading literature by Native American/Indigenous writers from the U.S. and beyond. Texts may include an array of genres including, fiction and non-fiction, poetry and prose, film, and video games.

COM LIT 8.title: Travels in Comparative Literature
COM LIT 8.description: Readings in English and in English translation on such topics as love, war, cities, travel writing, politics, fantasy and science fiction, violence.

COM LIT 9.title: Introduction to Multiculturalism
COM LIT 9.description: Various themes and forms of literary and cultural production within a multicultural framework, including African American, Asian American, Chicano/Latino, and Native American literatures and cultures.

COM LIT 10.title: Topics in World Literature
COM LIT 10.description: Introduction to texts from across the globe and from different historical periods. Readings in English and English translation.

COM LIT 60A.title: World Literature
COM LIT 60A.description: An introduction to the comparative study of literatures and cultures in a global context. Studies literary texts and other media across the borders of various cultures, historical periods, and traditions. All texts are read in English translation.

COM LIT 60B.title: Reading with Theory
COM LIT 60B.description: Introduction to theory and methods of literary and cultural criticism in a global context. Students read theoretical approaches to literature, culture, and ideas. Marx and Freud, e.g., may be studied alongside readings in narrative poetry, film, song lyrics, novel.

COM LIT 60C.title: Cultural Studies
COM LIT 60C.description: Introduces students to a variety of cultural practices (literature, blogs, films, radio, comics) from across the globe. Focuses on the ways that context, genre, and medium (e.g., written, visual, oral) affect how these practices are produced, circulated, and received.

COM LIT 100A.title: Nations, Regions, and Beyond
COM LIT 100A.description: Intensive study of national and regional cultural and literary traditions from across the globe, among them the literary and cultural production of the Middle East, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

COM LIT 101W.title: An Introduction to Translation Studies
COM LIT 101W.description: Focuses on theories of translation and on how these theories help students understand the role of translation in the world. Students develop a critical vocabulary for discussing translation in multiple linguistic traditions and complete a final translation project.
COM LIT 101W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Working knowledge of at least one foreign language.

COM LIT 102W.title: Comparative Studies in Literature and Theory
COM LIT 102W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

COM LIT 105.title: Topics in Comparative Multiculturalism
COM LIT 105.description: Treats the literatures and cultures of one or more minority groups in California and the United States, including African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicano/Latinos, and Native Americans, and their relations to other national literatures.
COM LIT 105.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement.

COM LIT 107.title: Colonialisms and Postcolonialisms
COM LIT 107.description: Explores topics such as colonialism and race, decolonization, pre- and postcoloniality, globalization, and the cultural dynamics of colonization and subjectivity.

COM LIT 110.title: Topics in Critical Theory
COM LIT 110.description: In-depth discussion of one or more theoretical paradigms, debates, or writers (Marxism, Foucault, Queer Theory, Psychoanalysis) with a special focus on what it means to read and think with theoretical texts.

COM LIT 121.title: Narrative, Pattern, and Text
COM LIT 121.description: Explores textual patterns, structures, and effects. May include topics such as novel, hypertext, genre, reader responses, intertextuality.

COM LIT 123.title: Literatures in Dialogue
COM LIT 123.description: Studies how texts interact across time and space in a global context. Uses concepts of influence, imitation, and parody, to ask, for example, how the Homeric epics can help us understand Caribbean novels and U.S. movies such as Troy.

COM LIT 130.title: Gender, Sexuality, Race, Class
COM LIT 130.description: Discusses the roles of differences such as race, class, gender, and sexuality in society, culture, and literature across the globe, covering topics such as theoretical and literary representations of queer sexuality, gender performance, critical race theory.

COM LIT 131.title: Psychoanalysis and Culture
COM LIT 131.description: Discusses major psychoanalytic writings of Freud and others in connection with questions of culture.

COM LIT 132.title: Discourse, Ideologies, and Politics
COM LIT 132.description: Compares ideologies and systems, e.g., nationalism and fundamentalism, as they affect literature and culture in a global context.

COM LIT 140.title: Critical Cultural Studies
COM LIT 140.description: Introduces a variety of ways of understanding cultural phenomena in relation to different power structures. These cultural phenomena may include comics, film, literature, sports, music, festivals, telling stories, or eating out.

COM LIT 142.title: The Metropolis and Other Cultural Geographies
COM LIT 142.description: Examines the relationship between space and culture; cultural production in the city, suburb, and/or countryside; spaces in texts and artifacts (film, literature, comics, photographs) in a global context.

COM LIT 143.title: Literature, Arts, and Media
COM LIT 143.description: Explores literature and other arts and media in a global context. May include film and electronic media, fine arts, oral cultures, architecture, in an international framework.

COM LIT 144.title: Literature, History, and Society
COM LIT 144.description: Explores the relationship between literary texts and their historical and social contexts in an international framework. Courses may address, for example, literary and cultural expressions in social revolutions or the way literary texts talk back to medicine, religion, and anthropology.

COM LIT 150.title: Literature in Translation
COM LIT 150.description: The study of literary works in one or more genres in English translation. May be a comparative study of works from several different original languages or a concentration on works from a single cultural/linguistic tradition.

COM LIT 160.title: World Cinema
COM LIT 160.description: Comparative analysis of contemporary film in languages other than English.

COM LIT 190W.title: Advanced Seminar in Comparative Literature and Theory
COM LIT 190W.description: Capstone seminar for the Comparative Literature major. Deepens understanding of the field through investigation of a special topic and a substantial research and writing project.
COM LIT 190W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Recommended: COM LIT 60A, COM LIT 60B, and COM LIT 60C.
COM LIT 190W.restriction: Comparative Literature majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Humanities students only.

COM LIT 199.title: Independent Study in Comparative Literature
COM LIT 199.description: To be taken only when the materials to be studied lie outside the normal run of departmental offerings.

COM LIT 200A.title: History of Comparative Literature and Introduction to Methods and Theories of CL
COM LIT 200A.description: Seminar designed to introduce graduate students in Comparative Literature to the discipline of Comparative Literature. Issues and theories of comparative literary and cultural study are covered. Strongly recommended for first and second year students before the M.A. exam and review.

COM LIT 200B.title: Topics in Theories of Translation
COM LIT 200B.description: The reproduction, translation, and transfer of literary and cultural, ideological and political, and symbolic codes and texts have long been the object of study in Comparative Literature. Addresses the diverse ways in which expressive systems interact and intersect.

COM LIT 210.title: Comparative Studies
COM LIT 210.description: Studies in selected areas of Comparative Literature. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

COM LIT 280A.title: Professionalization Seminar
COM LIT 280A.description: The first of two required professionalization seminars in Comparative Literature. Intended for first and second year students and covers preparation for the M.A. and Ph.D. exams, conference presentations, teaching and classroom management, and publishing journals.

COM LIT 280B.title: Professionalization Seminar
COM LIT 280B.description: The second of two required professionalization seminars in Comparative Literature. Intended for fourth and fifth year students and covers course design, applying for grants, dissertation prospectus and support, and the job application process.
COM LIT 280B.prereq_text: COM LIT 280A with a minimum grade of B.

COM LIT 290.title: Reading and Conference
COM LIT 290.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

COM LIT 291.title: Guided Reading Course
COM LIT 291.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

COM LIT 292.title: Teaching Practicum
COM LIT 292.description: Graduate students develop their pedagogical practices by accompanying a professor teaching a UCI undergraduate class. Meets individually with the professor to discuss relevant pedagogical practices, syllabus design, lecturing, assessment, classroom management, etc. Actively participates in one teaching component.

COM LIT 298.title: Pre-Dissertation Research
COM LIT 298.description: Taken under the direction of the graduate advisor or committee member in preparation for the Ph.D. exam. It can be taken after students have completed the M.A. review and program coursework requirements.

COM LIT 299.title: Dissertation Research
COM LIT 299.description: A units-only course for students in the dissertation phase.

COMPSCI 103.title: Advanced Programming and Problem Solving with C++
COMPSCI 103.description: Advanced programming language concepts for more complex, higher performance software design. Builds depth of programming skills in C++ as a foundation for upper-division courses and projects. Focuses on strengthening programming, debugging, and problem solving skills.
COMPSCI 103.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 111.title: Digital Image Processing
COMPSCI 111.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts of digital signal and image processing as applicable in areas such as multimedia, graphics, AI, data mining, databases, vision, or video games. Topics include image representation, space- and frequency-domain transformations, filters, segmentation, and compression.
COMPSCI 111.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C and I&C SCI 6D with a minimum grade of C and (MATH 3A with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 6N with a minimum grade of C).
COMPSCI 111.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 112.title: Computer Graphics
COMPSCI 112.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of 3D computer graphics including polygonal modeling, geometric transformations, visibility algorithms, illumination models, texturing, and rasterization. Use of an independently-learned 3D graphics API to implement these techniques.
COMPSCI 112.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C and (MATH 3A with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 6N with a minimum grade of C).
COMPSCI 112.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 114.title: Projects in Advanced 3D Computer Graphics
COMPSCI 114.description: Projects in advanced 3D graphics such as illumination, geometric modeling, visualization, and animation. Topics include physically based and global illumination, solid modeling, curved surfaces, multiresolution modeling, image-based rendering, basic concepts of animation, and scientific visualization.
COMPSCI 114.prereq_text: COMPSCI 112 and I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C. Recommended: COMPSCI 161 or COMPSCI 164 or COMPSCI 165.
COMPSCI 114.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 115.title: Computer Simulation
COMPSCI 115.description: Discrete event-driven simulation; continuous system simulation; basic probability as pertaining to input distributions and output analysis; stochastic and deterministic simulation; static and dynamic system simulation.
COMPSCI 115.prereq_text: I&C SCI 6B with a minimum grade of C and (I&C SCI 6N with a minimum grade of C or MATH 3A with a minimum grade of C) and (STATS 67 with a minimum grade of C or (STATS 7 with a minimum grade of C or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3) and STATS 120A with a minimum grade of C) and I&C SCI 51 with a minimum grade of C and (SWE 43 with a minimum grade of C or IN4MATX 43 with a minimum grade of C).
COMPSCI 115.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 116.title: Computational Photography and Vision
COMPSCI 116.description: Introduces the problems of computer vision through the application of computational photography. Specific topics include photo-editing (image warping, compositing, hole filling), panoramic image stitching, and face detection for digital photographs.
COMPSCI 116.prereq_text: I&C SCI 6D with a minimum grade of C and (MATH 3A with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 6N with a minimum grade of C) and (MATH 2B with a minimum grade of C or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4 or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 4) and I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C.
COMPSCI 116.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 117.title: Project in Computer Vision
COMPSCI 117.description: Students undertake construction of a computer vision system. Topics include automatically building 3D models from photographs, searching photo collections, robot navigation, and human motion tracking.
COMPSCI 117.prereq_text: I&C SCI 6D with a minimum grade of C and (MATH 3A with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 6N with a minimum grade of C) and (MATH 2B with a minimum grade of C or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C and (COMPSCI 112 or COMPSCI 116 or COMPSCI 171 or COMPSCI 178).
COMPSCI 117.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 118.title: Introduction to Virtual Reality
COMPSCI 118.description: Introduces virtual reality systems and software. Topics include computer graphics pipeline, human visual system and perception, head mounted displays, image formation, sensors and tracking, and 3D sound. Students use a popular cross-platform game engine to create VR environments.
COMPSCI 118.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A) and I&C SCI 33.
COMPSCI 118.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 121.title: Information Retrieval
COMPSCI 121.description: An introduction to information retrieval including indexing, retrieval, classifying, and clustering text and multimedia documents.
COMPSCI 121.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C) and (STATS 7 or STATS 67 or MGMT 7 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3).
COMPSCI 121.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 122A.title: Introduction to Data Management
COMPSCI 122A.description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for applications. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational design theory, and Structured Query Language (SQL) programming.
COMPSCI 122A.prereq_text: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C or EECS 114.
COMPSCI 122A.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 122B.title: Project in Databases and Web Applications
COMPSCI 122B.description: Introduces students to advanced database technologies and web applications. Topics include database connectivity (ODBC/JDBC), extending databases using stored procedures, database administration, web servers, web programming languages (Java servlets, XML, Ajax, and mobile platforms).
COMPSCI 122B.prereq_text: (COMPSCI 122A or EECS 116) and (I&C SCI 45J or AP Computer Science A with a minimum score of 4).
COMPSCI 122B.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 122C.title: Principles of Data Management
COMPSCI 122C.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying data management systems. Content includes key techniques including storage management, buffer management, record-oriented file system, access methods, query optimization, and query processing.
COMPSCI 122C.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 122D.title: Beyond SQL Data Management
COMPSCI 122D.description: Survey of modern data management and analysis technologies beyond relational (SQL) database management. Topics include semistructured data, NoSQL databases, big data analysis, and text search/query engines. Additional topics vary and may include data frames, streaming data, and/or time-series data.
COMPSCI 122D.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 and (I&C SCI 51 or EECS 31) and (COMPSCI 122A or EECS 116).
COMPSCI 122D.restriction: Computer Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science and Engineering and all School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.

COMPSCI 125.title: Next Generation Search Systems
COMPSCI 125.description: Discusses concepts and techniques related to all aspects of search systems. After considering basic search technology and the state-of-art systems, rapidly developing techniques for multimedia search, local search, event-search, and video-on-demand are explored.
COMPSCI 125.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C) and (STATS 7 or STATS 67 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3).
COMPSCI 125.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 130.title: Introduction to Security and Privacy
COMPSCI 130.description: Introductory course on security mindset and basic principles/practices of software and systems security. Covers the foundations of building, using, and managing secure systems. Topics include standard security principles, threats, and defenses for real-world systems, including web, mobile, and IoT security.
COMPSCI 130.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C.
COMPSCI 130.restriction: Computer Science majors, Computer Science and Engineering majors, and School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

COMPSCI 131.title: Parallel and Distributed Computing
COMPSCI 131.description: Parallel and distributed computer systems. Parallel programming models. Common parallel and distributed programming issues. Specific topics include parallel programming, performance models, coordination and synchronization, consistency and replication, transactions, fault tolerance.
COMPSCI 131.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 132.title: Computer Networks
COMPSCI 132.description: Computer network architectures, protocols, and applications. Internet congestion control, addressing, and routing. Local area networks. Multimedia networking.
COMPSCI 132.restriction: Computer Engineering majors and Computer Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 133.title: Advanced Computer Networks
COMPSCI 133.description: Fundamental principles in computer networks are applied to obtain practical experience and skills necessary for designing and implementing computer networks, protocols, and network applications. Various network design techniques, simulation techniques, and UNIX network programming are covered.
COMPSCI 133.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 134.title: Computer and Network Security
COMPSCI 134.description: Overview of modern computer and networks security, attacks, and countermeasures. Authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Also covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.
COMPSCI 134.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 137.title: Internet Applications Engineering
COMPSCI 137.description: Concepts in Internet applications engineering with emphasis on the Web. Peer-to-Peer and Interoperability. Topics include HTTP and REST, Remote Procedure/Method Calls, Web Services, data representations, content distribution networks, identity management, relevant W3C/IETF standards, and relevant new large-scale computing styles.
COMPSCI 137.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 141.title: Concepts in Programming Languages
COMPSCI 141.description: In-depth study of several contemporary programming languages stressing variety in data structures, operations, notation, and control. Examination of different programming paradigms, such as logic programming, functional programming and object-oriented programming; implementation strategies, programming environments, and programming style.
COMPSCI 141.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 51 with a minimum grade of C or EECS 31 with a minimum grade of C) and I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C.
COMPSCI 141.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

COMPSCI 142A.title: Compilers and Interpreters
COMPSCI 142A.description: Introduction to the theory of programming language processors covering lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, code generation, optimization, interpretation, and run-time support.
COMPSCI 142A.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 46 or EECS 114) and (I&C SCI 51 or EECS 31). Recommended: COMPSCI 141 or IN4MATX 101 or I&C SCI 45J or EECS 40
COMPSCI 142A.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

COMPSCI 142B.title: Project in Compilers and Interpreters
COMPSCI 142B.description: Project course which provides working laboratory experience in construction and behavior of compilers and interpreters. Students build actual language processors and perform experiments which reveal their behaviors.
COMPSCI 142B.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 143A.title: Principles of Operating Systems
COMPSCI 143A.description: Principles and concepts of process and resource management, especially as seen in operating systems. Processes, memory management, protection, scheduling, file systems, and I/O systems are covered. Concepts illustrated in the context of several well-known systems.
COMPSCI 143A.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 46 or CSE 46) and (I&C SCI 51 or EECS 31 or CSE 31).
COMPSCI 143A.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 143B.title: Project in Operating System Organization
COMPSCI 143B.description: Detailed specification and design of critical components of an actual operating system including a memory manager, a process server, and a file/IO subsystem. Hardware/software tradeoffs. Emphasis on logical organization of system and communication.
COMPSCI 143B.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 145.title: Embedded Software
COMPSCI 145.description: Principles of embedded computing systems: embedded systems architecture, hardware/software components, system software and interfacing, real-time operating systems, hardware/software co-development, and communication issues. Examples of embedded computing in real-world application domains. Simple programming using an embedded systems development environment.
COMPSCI 145.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 and (I&C SCI 51 or EECS 31).
COMPSCI 145.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 146.title: Programming in Multitasking Operating Systems
COMPSCI 146.description: User- and systems-level programming of modern Internet-connected, multi-user, multitasking operating systems. Shells, scripting, filters, pipelines, programmability, extensibility, concurrency, inter-process communication. Concrete examples of a modern operating system (such as, but not necessarily, Unix programmed in C) are used.
COMPSCI 146.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C and I&C SCI 51 with a minimum grade of C. Recommended: COMPSCI 143A.
COMPSCI 146.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 147.title: Internet of Things (IoT) Software and Systems
COMPSCI 147.description: Introduction to the Internet of Things (IoT) from a systems and software perspective. IoT ecosystem including sensors, embedded CPUs, networking protocols, software, cloud services, and security and privacy requirements. IoT use cases, system design, and programming project.
COMPSCI 147.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 151.title: Digital Logic Design
COMPSCI 151.description: Boolean algebra. Design/analysis of combinational and sequential systems using SSI/MSI/LSI modules. Number systems. Error detecting and correction codes. Arithmetic algorithms. Hardware/firmware implementation of algorithms.
COMPSCI 151.prereq_text: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C and I&C SCI 51 with a minimum grade of C and I&C SCI 6B and I&C SCI 6D.
COMPSCI 151.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 152.title: Computer Architecture
COMPSCI 152.description: Design of computer elements; ALU, control unit, and arithmetic circuits. Memory hierarchy and organization. Caches. Function unit sharing and pipelining. I/O and interrupt processing. RTL and behavioral modeling using hardware description languages. Microprocessor organization and implementation techniques.
COMPSCI 152.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 154.title: Computer Design Laboratory
COMPSCI 154.description: Underlying primitives of computer instruction sets. Principles of microprogramming. Microprogramming. Microprograms written for one or more systems. Typical microprogramming applications discussed and implemented or simulated.
COMPSCI 154.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 161.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
COMPSCI 161.description: Techniques for efficient algorithm design, including divide-and-conquer and dynamic programming, and time/space analysis. Fast algorithms for problems applicable to networks, computer games, and scientific computing, such as sorting, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, network flow, and pattern matching.
COMPSCI 161.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C and I&C SCI 6B and I&C SCI 6D and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4).
COMPSCI 161.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors, Computer Science majors, Data Science majors, Software Engineering majors, and School of Information and Computer Sciences students only. Business Information Management, Computer Game Science, and Informatics majors have second right of consideration.

COMPSCI 162.title: Formal Languages and Automata
COMPSCI 162.description: Formal aspects of describing and recognizing languages by grammars and automata. Parsing regular and context-free languages. Ambiguity, nondeterminism. Elements of computability; Turning machines, random access machines, undecidable problems, NP-completeness.
COMPSCI 162.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and I&C SCI 6B and I&C SCI 6D.
COMPSCI 162.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Computer Science and Engineering majors, Language Science majors, and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 163.title: Graph Algorithms
COMPSCI 163.description: Algorithms for solving fundamental problems in graph theory. Graph representations, graph traversal, network flow, connectivity, graph layout, matching problems.
COMPSCI 163.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 164.title: Computational Geometry
COMPSCI 164.description: Algorithms and data structures for computational geometry and geometric modeling, with applications to computer vision and graphics. Topics: convex hulls, Voronoi diagrams, algorithms for triangulation, motion planning, and data structures for geometric searching and modeling of 2D and 3D
COMPSCI 164.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 165.title: Project in Algorithms and Data Structures
COMPSCI 165.description: Design, implementation, execution, and analysis of algorithms for problems such as sorting, searching, data compression, and data encryption. Time-space-structure trade-offs.
COMPSCI 165.restriction: Computer Science majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science and Engineering majors and all School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.

COMPSCI 166.title: Quantum Computation and Information
COMPSCI 166.description: Basic models for quantum computation and their foundations in quantum mechanics. Quantum complexity classes and quantum algorithms, including algorithms for factoring and quantum simulation. Introduction to quantum information theory and quantum entanglement.
COMPSCI 166.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 6N with a minimum grade of C+ or MATH 3A with a minimum grade of C+) and (COMPSCI 161 or PHYSICS 113A).
COMPSCI 166.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 167.title: Introduction to Applied Cryptography
COMPSCI 167.description: An introduction to the essential aspects of applied cryptography, as it is used in practice. Topics include classical cryptography, block ciphers, stream ciphers, public-key cryptography, digital signatures, one-way hash functions, basic cryptographic protocols, and digital certificates and credentials.
COMPSCI 167.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 169.title: Introduction to Optimization
COMPSCI 169.description: A broad introduction to optimization. Unconstrained and constrained optimization. Linear and integer programming. Combinatorial and geometric optimization. AI-assisted optimization and optimization applications to AI.
COMPSCI 169.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A) and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and COMPSCI 161.
COMPSCI 169.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 171.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
COMPSCI 171.description: Different means of representing knowledge and uses of representations in heuristic problem solving. Representations considered include predicate logic, semantic nets, procedural representations, natural language grammars, and search trees.
COMPSCI 171.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and STATS 67 or ((STATS 7 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3) and STATS 120A).
COMPSCI 171.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 172B.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
COMPSCI 172B.description: Neural network and deep learning from multiple perspectives. Theory of parallel distributed processing systems, algorithmic approaches for learning from data in various manners, applications to difficult problems in AI from computer vision, to natural language understanding, to bioinformatics and chemoinformatics.
COMPSCI 172B.prereq_text: (STATS 120A and STATS 120B) or MATH 121A or COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A.
COMPSCI 172B.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 172C.title: Artificial Intelligence Frontiers: Technical, Ethical, and Societal
COMPSCI 172C.description: Explores the frontiers of artificial intelligence and related technologies with a focus on the underlying ethical, legal, and societal challenges and opportunities they create. Encourages critical thinking about these issues.
COMPSCI 172C.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 175.title: Project in Artificial Intelligence
COMPSCI 175.description: Construction of a working artificial intelligence system. Evaluation of capabilities of the system including impact of knowledge representation.
COMPSCI 175.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 177.title: Applications of Probability in Computer Science
COMPSCI 177.description: Application of probability to real-world problems in computer science. Typical topics include analysis of algorithms and graphs, probabilistic language models, network traffic modeling, data compression, and reliability modeling.
COMPSCI 177.prereq_text: (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and I&C SCI 6B and I&C SCI 6D and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N) and STATS 67.
COMPSCI 177.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 178.title: Machine Learning and Data-Mining
COMPSCI 178.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and data-mining applied to real-world datasets. Typical applications include spam filtering, object recognition, and credit scoring.
COMPSCI 178.prereq_text: I&C SCI 6B and I&C SCI 6D and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A) and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and STATS 67 or ((STATS 7 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3) and STATS 120A).
COMPSCI 178.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 179.title: Algorithms for Probabilistic and Deterministic Graphical Models
COMPSCI 179.description: Graphical model techniques dealing with probabilistic and deterministic knowledge representations. Focuses on graphical models such as constraint networks, Bayesian networks, and Markov networks that have become a central paradigm for knowledge representation and reasoning in AI and general computer science.
COMPSCI 179.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 180A.title: Project in Computer Science
COMPSCI 180A.description: Students to solve a substantial real-world problem with knowledge gained from many areas in computer science. Project has a focus on computer science but can overlap with neighbor disciplines.
COMPSCI 180A.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 180B.title: Project in Computer Science
COMPSCI 180B.description: Students to solve a substantial real-world problem with knowledge gained from many areas in computer science. Project has a focus on computer science but can overlap with neighbor disciplines.
COMPSCI 180B.prereq_text: COMPSCI 180A. In Progress (IP) grade for COMPSCI 180A is also accepted.
COMPSCI 180B.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 183.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
COMPSCI 183.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
COMPSCI 183.prereq_text: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8.

COMPSCI 184A.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine
COMPSCI 184A.description: Introduction to computational methods in molecular biology, aimed at those interested in learning about this interdisciplinary area. Covers computational approaches to understanding and predicting the structure, function, interactions, and evolution of DNA, RNA, proteins, and related molecules and processes.
COMPSCI 184A.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 184C.title: Computational Systems Biology
COMPSCI 184C.description: Computational inference and modeling of gene regulation networks, signal transduction pathways, and the effects of regulatory networks in cellular processes, development, and disease. Introduction of required mathematical, computational, and data handling tools.
COMPSCI 184C.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 189.title: Project in Bioinformatics
COMPSCI 189.description: Teaches problem definition and analysis, data representation, algorithm design, component integration, solution validation, and testability with teams specifying, designing, building, and testing a solution to a bioinformatics problem. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of biomedical computing issues.
COMPSCI 189.prereq_text: COMPSCI 184A with a minimum grade of C.
COMPSCI 189.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 190.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
COMPSCI 190.description: Studies in selected areas of Information and Computer Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
COMPSCI 190.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI H198.title: Honors Research
COMPSCI H198.description: Directed independent research in computer science for honors students.
COMPSCI H198.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium only. School of Information and Computer Sciences Honors students only.

COMPSCI 199.title: Individual Study
COMPSCI 199.description: Individual research or investigation with Computer Science faculty.

COMPSCI 200S.title: Seminar in Computer Science Research
COMPSCI 200S.description: Graduate colloquium series. Includes weekly talks by notable computer scientists.

COMPSCI 201.title: Foundations of Cryptographic Protocols
COMPSCI 201.description: Explores fundamental cryptographic tools, including encryption, signatures, and identification schemes. Students are introduced to the provable security paradigm of modern cryptography, focusing on understanding of security properties provided by cryptographic tools, and on proving security (or insecurity) of cryptographic constructions.
COMPSCI 201.prereq_text: COMPSCI 260 with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 263 with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 201P.title: Computer Security
COMPSCI 201P.description: Introduction to computer security, including systems, technology, and management. Topics include authorization, authentication, data integrity, malware, operating systems security, network security, web security, and basic cryptography.
COMPSCI 201P.prereq_text: Knowledge of Python or C++ programming is required.
COMPSCI 201P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 202.title: Applied Cryptography
COMPSCI 202.description: Design and analysis of algorithms for applied cryptography. Topics include symmetric and asymmetric key encryption, digital signatures, one-way hash functions, digital certificates and credentials, and techniques for authorization, non-repudiation, authentication, identification, data integrity, proofs of knowledge, and access control.
COMPSCI 202.prereq_text: COMPSCI 260 with a minimum grade of B- and COMPSCI 263 with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 203.title: Network and Distributed Systems Security
COMPSCI 203.description: Modern computer and networks security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Group communication and multicast security techniques. Covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.

COMPSCI 203P.title: Network Security
COMPSCI 203P.description: Introduction to network security, including network threats and attacks, as well as defenses against such attacks. Topics include network infrastructure security, mobile and Wi-Fi security, spam, phishing, firewalls, anonymity, secure email, secure and private cloud computing, and web security.
COMPSCI 203P.prereq_text: COMPSCI 201P with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 202P with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 204.title: Usable Security and Privacy
COMPSCI 204.description: Examines how to design for security and privacy from a user-centered perspective by combining insights from computer systems and human-centered computing. Explores several challenges in integrating usability into core security and privacy systems design.
COMPSCI 204.restriction: Undergraduate degree in Computer Science is strongly recommended.

COMPSCI 205.title: Computer and Systems Security
COMPSCI 205.description: Lecture and discuss latest security research in software, OS, protocols, mobile devices, machine learning, sensors, and emerging IoT/CPS systems such as smart home and smart transportation. Students perform research projects and gain hands-on experience evaluating and designing secure systems.
COMPSCI 205.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 206.title: Principles of Scientific Computing
COMPSCI 206.description: Overview of widely used principles and methods of numerical and scientific computing, including basic concepts and computational methods in linear algebra, optimization, and probability.
COMPSCI 206.prereq_text: Basic courses in multivariate calculus, linear algebra, and probability.

COMPSCI 211A.title: Visual Computing
COMPSCI 211A.description: Fundamentals of image processing (convolution, linear filters, spectral analysis), vision geometry (projective geometry, camera models and calibration, stereo reconstruction), radiometry (color, shading, illumination, BRDF), and visual content synthesis (graphics pipeline, texture- bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing).

COMPSCI 211B.title: Computer Graphics and Visualization
COMPSCI 211B.description: Interactive 3D graphics rendering pipeline, illumination and shading, ray tracing, texture-, bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing, multiresolution representations, volume rendering techniques, iso-surface extraction.
COMPSCI 211B.prereq_text: COMPSCI 211A with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 216.title: Image Understanding
COMPSCI 216.description: The goal of image understanding is to extract useful semantic information from image data. Course covers low-level image and video processing techniques, feature descriptors, segmentation, objection recognition, and tracking.
COMPSCI 216.prereq_text: I&C SCI 6D and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 6G or MATH 3A) and MATH 2B and I&C SCI 46.

COMPSCI 217.title: Light and Geometry in Computer Vision
COMPSCI 217.description: Examines the issues of light transport and multiview geometry in computer vision. Applications include camera calibration, 3D understanding, stereo reconstruction, and illumination estimation.
COMPSCI 217.prereq_text: I&C SCI 6D and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 6G or MATH 3A) and MATH 2B and I&C SCI 46 and COMPSCI 211A with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 219S.title: Seminar in Graphics and Visualization
COMPSCI 219S.description: Current research and research trends in computer graphics, visualization, virtual/augmented reality, and other visual computing topics.
COMPSCI 219S.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

COMPSCI 220P.title: Databases and Data Management
COMPSCI 220P.description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for managing and utilizing data. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational schema design, and use of SQL (Structured Query Language).

COMPSCI 221.title: Information Retrieval, Filtering, and Classification
COMPSCI 221.description: Algorithms for the storage, retrieval, filtering, and classification of textual and multimedia data. The vector space model, Boolean and probabilistic queries, and relevance feedback. Latent semantic indexing; collaborative filtering; and relationship to machine learning methods.
COMPSCI 221.prereq_text: COMPSCI 161 and COMPSCI 171 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G).

COMPSCI 222.title: Principles of Data Management
COMPSCI 222.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying data management systems. Content includes key techniques including storage management, buffer management, record-oriented file system, access methods, query optimization, and query processing.

COMPSCI 222P.title: Principles of Data Management
COMPSCI 222P.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying data management systems. Understanding and implementation of key techniques including storage management, buffer management, record-oriented file system, access methods, query optimization, and query processing.
COMPSCI 222P.prereq_text: Required: C++ programming skills, understanding of data structures and algorithms.
COMPSCI 222P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 223.title: Transaction Processing and Distributed Data Management
COMPSCI 223.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying transaction processing including database consistency, concurrency control, database recovery, and fault-tolerance. Includes transaction processing in centralized, distributed, parallel, and client-server environments.

COMPSCI 223P.title: Transaction Processing and Distributed Data Management
COMPSCI 223P.description: Introduction to fundamental principles underlying transaction processing systems including database consistency, atomicity, concurrency control, database recovery, replication, commit protocols, and fault-tolerance. Includes transaction processing in centralized, distributed, parallel, and client-server environments.
COMPSCI 223P.prereq_text: Recommended: Knowledge of basic concepts of databases such as entity-relation diagram, relational model, relational algebra, and SQL, record storage, and indexing.
COMPSCI 223P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 224P.title: Big Data Systems
COMPSCI 224P.description: Focuses on Big Data management frameworks such as Hadoop and Spark. Also covers relational and non-relational database technologies, including document (“NoSQL”) databases as well as emerging cloud data management solutions.
COMPSCI 224P.prereq_text: Knowledge of fundamental database concepts and data management techniques.
COMPSCI 224P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 230.title: Distributed Computer Systems
COMPSCI 230.description: Principles of distributed computing systems. Topics covered include message-passing, remote procedure calls, distributed shared memory synchronization, resource and process/thread management, distributed file systems, naming and security.

COMPSCI 231P.title: Parallel and Distributed Computing for Professionals
COMPSCI 231P.description: Covers a wide variety of concepts related to the design and application of high-performance concurrent computing systems, including architectural features, communications networks and models, parallel program development for numerical and non-numerical applications, programming models, and more.

COMPSCI 232.title: Computer and Communication Networks
COMPSCI 232.description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.

COMPSCI 232P.title: Computer and Communication Networks
COMPSCI 232P.description: Internet architecture, protocols, and services. Advanced concepts of IP and TCP, including addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, and implementations of flow and congestion control. Internet services such as Network Address Translation and Domain Name Servers. Overview of Local Area Networks.

COMPSCI 233.title: Networking Laboratory
COMPSCI 233.description: A laboratory-based introduction to basic networking concepts such as addressing, sub-netting, bridging, ARP, and routing. Network simulation and design. Structured around weekly readings and laboratory assignments.

COMPSCI 234.title: Advanced Networks
COMPSCI 234.description: Design principles of networked systems, advanced routing and congestion control algorithms, network algorithms, network measurement, management, security, Internet economics, and emerging networks.
COMPSCI 234.prereq_text: NET SYS 201 with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 232 with a minimum grade of B- or EECS 248A with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 236.title: Wireless and Mobile Networking
COMPSCI 236.description: Introduction to wireless networking. The focus is on layers 2 and 3 of the OSI reference model, design, performance analysis, and protocols. Topics covered include: an introduction to wireless networking, digital cellular, next generation cellular, wireless LANs, and mobile IP.

COMPSCI 237.title: Middleware for Networked and Distributed Systems
COMPSCI 237.description: Discusses concepts, techniques, and issues in developing distributed systems middleware that provides high performance and Quality of Service for emerging applications. Also covers existing standards (e.g., CORBA, DCOM, Jini, Espeak) and their relative advantages and shortcomings.
COMPSCI 237.prereq_text: An undergraduate-level course in operating systems and networks.

COMPSCI 238.title: Advanced Operating Systems
COMPSCI 238.description: Focuses on advanced and graduate-level topics in operating systems. Presents important recent developments in operating systems, topics not covered in undergraduate operating systems courses. This includes novel operating system designs and techniques to improve existing ones.

COMPSCI 238P.title: Operating Systems
COMPSCI 238P.description: In-depth organization of the core operating system abstraction and its implementation (virtual memory, kernel and user mode, system calls, threads, context switches, interrupts, inter-process communication, hardware interface, etc.) and a range of recent developments in de-facto industry standard operating systems.
COMPSCI 238P.prereq_text: Working knowledge of C and the Linux environment.

COMPSCI 241.title: Advanced Compiler Construction
COMPSCI 241.description: Advanced study of programming language implementation techniques: optimizations such as common sub-expression elimination, register allocation, and instruction scheduling. Implementation of language features such as type-directed dispatch, garbage collection, dynamic linking, and just-in-time code generation.

COMPSCI 242.title: Parallel Computing
COMPSCI 242.description: Definition of parallel processing systems. Theory and application of arrays, trees, and hypercubes. Computational models, applications: sorting, integer arithmetic, matrix operations, Fast Fourier Transform, and others. Interconnection networks: a framework for the description, analysis, and construction of hypercube-derived networks.

COMPSCI 244.title: Introduction to Embedded and Ubiquitous Systems
COMPSCI 244.description: Embedded and ubiquitous system technologies including processors, DSP, memory, and software. System interfacing basics; communication strategies; sensors and actuators, mobile and wireless technology. Using pre-designed hardware and software components. Design case studies in wireless, multimedia, and/or networking domains.
COMPSCI 244.prereq_text: I&C SCI 51 and COMPSCI 152 and COMPSCI 161 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G or I&C SCI 6D). B.S. degree in Computer Science is also accepted.

COMPSCI 244P.title: Internet of Things
COMPSCI 244P.description: Develops a comprehensive understanding of the hardware and software technology, the communication protocols, and the security and privacy requirements underlying the Internet of Things ecosystem, particularly those using computing elements (processors, DSPs/ ASIPs), sensors, and accessing cloud services.
COMPSCI 244P.prereq_text: Undergraduate-level familiarity with fundamentals of integrated circuit blocks, processors, optimization/algorithm design, and some programming experience.

COMPSCI 247.title: Complex Software Systems: Project Course
COMPSCI 247.description: Building complex systems software systems, such as Database Management Systems, Operating Systems, and Optimizing Compilers. Such systems often involve low-level programming and intricate performance optimizations. Students learn how to build such a system.
COMPSCI 247.prereq_text: COMPSCI 222 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 238 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 241 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 248A.title: Introduction to Ubiquitous Computing
COMPSCI 248A.description: The "disappearing computer" paradigm. Differences to the desktop computing model: applications, interaction in augmented environments, security, alternate media, small operating systems, sensors, and embedded systems design. Evaluation by project work and class participation.

COMPSCI 250A.title: Computer Systems Architecture
COMPSCI 250A.description: Study of architectural issues and their relation to technology and software: design of processor, interconnections, and memory hierarchies.

COMPSCI 250B.title: Modern Computer Systems
COMPSCI 250B.description: Fundamental concepts and recent advances in computer systems architecture necessary to achieve high performance and efficiency on systems available today. Topics span modern processor features, accelerators, storage and network architectures, as well as architecture-optimized software.
COMPSCI 250B.prereq_text: Required: Undergraduate-level understanding of computer architecture concepts.

COMPSCI 250P.title: Computer Systems Architecture
COMPSCI 250P.description: Study of architectural issues and their relation to technology and software: design of processor, interconnections, and memory hierarchies.
COMPSCI 250P.prereq_text: Undergraduate-level familiarity with fundamentals of integrated circuit blocks, processors, and optimization/algorithm design, and some programming experience.

COMPSCI 253.title: Analysis of Programming Languages
COMPSCI 253.description: Concepts in modern programming languages, their interaction, and the relationship between programming languages and methods for large-scale, extensible software development. Empirical analysis of programming language usage.

COMPSCI 253P.title: Advanced Programming and Problem Solving
COMPSCI 253P.description: Provides in-depth preparation for industry interviews requiring demonstration of problem solving and programming skills. Emphasis is on understanding problem statements, considering edge cases, developing effective test cases, designing correct solutions, explaining these clearly, and implementing a solution correctly.

COMPSCI 256.title: Systems and Machine Learning
COMPSCI 256.description: Course is divided into two parts. The first half covers recent research in systems for machine learning (ML) that enabled rapid progress in ML/AI. The second half revolves around application of machine learning in systems.
COMPSCI 256.prereq_text: Recommended: An undergraduate machine-learning course and an undergraduate course in one of the following areas: networking, distributed systems, or operating systems.
COMPSCI 256.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 257.title: Brain-Inspired Learning Systems
COMPSCI 257.description: Introduces the latest developments in machine learning and cognitive computing algorithms inspired by the human brain. Includes examining various neural coding approaches for data representation and developing classification and reasoning algorithms that model human cognitive behavior.

COMPSCI 259S.title: Seminar in Design Science
COMPSCI 259S.description: Current research and research trends in design science. Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress.

COMPSCI 260.title: Fundamentals of the Design and Analysis of Algorithms
COMPSCI 260.description: Covers fundamental concepts in the design and analysis of algorithms and is geared toward non-specialists in theoretical computer science. Topics include: deterministic and randomized graph algorithms, fundamental algorithmic techniques like divide-and-conquer strategies and dynamic programming, and NP-completeness.

COMPSCI 260P.title: Algorithms with Applications
COMPSCI 260P.description: Covers fundamental concepts in the design and analysis of algorithms and is geared toward practical application and implementation. Topics include greedy algorithms, deterministic and randomized graph algorithms, models of network flow, fundamental algorithmic techniques, and NP-completeness.

COMPSCI 261.title: Data Structures
COMPSCI 261.description: An in-depth treatment of data structures and their associated management algorithms including resource complexity analysis.

COMPSCI 261P.title: Data Structures with Applications
COMPSCI 261P.description: Data structures and their associated management algorithms, including their applications and analysis.
COMPSCI 261P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 262P.title: Text Processing and Information Retrieval
COMPSCI 262P.description: Techniques for text pattern matching and algorithms for the storage, retrieval, and classification of textual and multimedia data. Topics include string searching, string data structures, document and website retrieval, and search engines.

COMPSCI 263.title: Analysis of Algorithms
COMPSCI 263.description: Analysis of correctness and complexity of various efficient algorithms; discussion of problems for which no efficient solutions are known.
COMPSCI 263.prereq_text: COMPSCI 161 and COMPSCI 261 with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 265.title: Graph Algorithms
COMPSCI 265.description: Graph definitions, representation methods, graph problems, algorithms, approximation methods, and applications.

COMPSCI 266.title: Computational Geometry
COMPSCI 266.description: The design and analysis of algorithms and data structures for computational geometry, with applications to machine learning, computer vision, and graphics. Topics: convex hulls, Voronoi diagrams, Delaunay triangulations, geometric arrangements, polygon triangulation, and data structures for geometric searching and modeling.
COMPSCI 266.prereq_text: COMPSCI 161 or COMPSCI 260 with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 268.title: Introduction to Optimization
COMPSCI 268.description: A broad introduction to optimization. Unconstrained and constrained optimization. Linear and integer programming. Combinatorial and geometric optimization. AI-assisted optimization and optimization applications to AI.
COMPSCI 268.prereq_text: ( STATS 67 ( min grade = D- ) OR STATS 7 ( min grade = D- ) OR AP STATISTICS ( min score = 3 ) ) AND ( STATS 67 ( min grade = D- ) OR STATS 120A ( min grade = D- ) ) AND ( I&C SCI 6N ( min grade = D- ) OR MATH 3A ( min grade = D- ) )
COMPSCI 268.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 271.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
COMPSCI 271.description: The study of theories and computational models for systems which behave and act in an intelligent manner. Fundamental subdisciplines of artificial intelligence including knowledge representation, search, deduction, planning, probabilistic reasoning, natural language parsing and comprehension, knowledge-based systems, and learning.

COMPSCI 271P.title: Artificial Intelligence
COMPSCI 271P.description: The study of theories and computational models for systems which behave and act in an intelligent manner. Fundamental sub-disciplines of artificial intelligence, including knowledge representation, search, deduction, planning, probabilistic reasoning, natural language parsing and comprehension, knowledge-based systems, and learning.
COMPSCI 271P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 272.title: Statistical Natural Language Processing
COMPSCI 272.description: Statistical models, machine learning algorithms, and computational tasks involved in natural language processing. Focuses on approaches that learn these models from data, and covers applications such as information extraction, dialog systems, machine translation, and question answering.
COMPSCI 272.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 273A.title: Machine Learning
COMPSCI 273A.description: Computational approaches to learning algorithms for classifications, regression, and clustering. Emphasis is on discriminative classification methods such as decision trees, rules, nearest neighbor, linear models, and naive Bayes.
COMPSCI 273A.prereq_text: COMPSCI 271 with a minimum grade of B- and COMPSCI 206 with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 273P.title: Machine Learning and Data Mining
COMPSCI 273P.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and data-mining. Learning algorithms for classifications, regression, and clustering. Emphasis is on discriminative classification methods such as decision trees, rules, nearest neighbor, linear models, and naive Bayes.
COMPSCI 273P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 274A.title: Probabilistic Learning: Theory and Algorithms
COMPSCI 274A.description: An introduction to probabilistic and statistical techniques for learning from data, including parameter estimation, density estimation, regression, classification, and mixture modeling.
COMPSCI 274A.prereq_text: COMPSCI 206 with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 274B.title: Learning in Graphical Models
COMPSCI 274B.description: Models for data analysis are presented in the unifying framework of graphical models. The emphasis is on learning from data but inference is also covered. Real world examples are used to illustrate the material.
COMPSCI 274B.prereq_text: COMPSCI 274A with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 274C.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
COMPSCI 274C.description: Neural network and deep learning from multiple perspectives. Theory of parallel distributed processing systems, algorithmic approaches for learning from data in various manners, applications to difficult problems in AI from computer vision, to natural language understanding, to bioinformatics and chemoinformatics.
COMPSCI 274C.prereq_text: (STATS 120A and STATS 120B) or MATH 121A or COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A with a minimum grade of B-.

COMPSCI 274D.title: Artificial Intelligence Frontiers: Technical, Ethical, and Societal
COMPSCI 274D.description: Explores the frontiers of artificial intelligence and related technologies with a focus on the underlying ethical, legal, and societal challenges and opportunities they create. Encourages critical thinking about these issues.

COMPSCI 274E.title: Deep Generative Models
COMPSCI 274E.description: Discusses probabilistic approaches to deep learning such as generative models and their applications in computer vision, NLP, the natural sciences, and other fields. Coursework may include both homework and project components.
COMPSCI 274E.prereq_text: COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A with a minimum grade of B- or STATS 120B. Recommended: Advanced machine learning or graphical models courses such as COMPSCI 274A or COMPSCI 274B or COMPSCI 273C or COMPSCI 276.
COMPSCI 274E.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 274P.title: AI Foundations: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
COMPSCI 274P.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and neural networks. Architecture design. Feedforward and recurrent networks. Learning models and algorithms. Applications to data analysis and prediction problems in areas such as machine vision, natural language processing, biomed, and finance.
COMPSCI 274P.prereq_text: COMPSCI 271P with a minimum grade of B. Required: Knowledge of Python programming.
COMPSCI 274P.restriction: Master of Computer Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 275.title: Network-Based Reasoning/Constraint Networks
COMPSCI 275.description: Study of the theory and techniques of constraint network model. Covers techniques for solving constraint satisfaction problems: backtracking techniques, consistency algorithms, and structure-based techniques. Tractable subclasses. Extensions into applications such as temporal reasoning, diagnosis, and scheduling.
COMPSCI 275.prereq_text: Basic course in algorithm design and analysis.

COMPSCI 275P.title: Graphical Models and Statistical Learning
COMPSCI 275P.description: Introduction to principles of statistical machine learning with probabilistic graphical models. Studies efficient inference algorithms based on optimization-based variational methods, and simulation-based Monte Carlo methods. Several approaches to learning from data are covered.
COMPSCI 275P.prereq_text: COMPSCI 273P with a minimum grade of B. Required: Python programming experience.
COMPSCI 275P.restriction: Master of Conservation and Restoration Science and Master of Data Science only.

COMPSCI 276.title: Causal and Probabilistic Reasoning with Graphical Models
COMPSCI 276.description: Provides in-depth exposition of causal reasoning and probabilistic graphical models theory and algorithms within Structural Causal Models and Bayesian Networks. Covers algorithms for Bayesian networks and central concepts (e.g., identifiability, the do-calculous, counterfactuals)
COMPSCI 276.prereq_text: Recommended: A basic course in probability.

COMPSCI 277.title: Control and Reinforcement Learning
COMPSCI 277.description: Introduction to learning agents that make sequences of decisions to interact with a system and control it. The main focus is reinforcement learning from a reward signal, with emphasis on algorithms that can learn differentiable policy parametrizations (Deep Reinforcement Learning).
COMPSCI 277.prereq_text: COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A with a minimum grade of B-. Recommended: COMPSCI 274A and COMPSCI 275B and COMPSCI 275C and COMPSCI 276.

COMPSCI 278.title: Probability Models
COMPSCI 278.description: Advanced probability, discrete time Markov chains, Poisson processes, continuous time Markov chains. Queuing or simulation as time permits.

COMPSCI 279.title: Foundations of Multi-Agent Systems
COMPSCI 279.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of multi-agent systems. Techniques for centralized/decentralized planning for cooperative/competitive agents. Examples include robotic warehousing and homeland security.
COMPSCI 279.prereq_text: Recommended: (COMPSCI 161 or CSE 161) and COMPSCI 171. Knowledge of Python.

COMPSCI 280.title: Algorithmic Game Theory
COMPSCI 280.description: Cover topics at the interface of theoretical computer science and economics: zero sum games and LP duality, mechanism design, voting and impossibility theorems, "price of anarchy". Algorithms and complexity theory for learning and computing Nash equilibria.
COMPSCI 280.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

COMPSCI 284A.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine
COMPSCI 284A.description: Introduction to computational methods in molecular biology, aimed at those interested in learning about this interdisciplinary area. Covers computational approaches to understanding and predicting the structure, function, interactions, and evolution of DNA, RNA, proteins, and related molecules and processes.
COMPSCI 284A.prereq_text: A Basic course in algorithms or a basic course in molecular biology.

COMPSCI 284C.title: Computational Systems Biology
COMPSCI 284C.description: Computational inference and modeling of gene regulation networks, signal transduction pathways, and the effects of regulatory networks in cellular processes, development, and disease. Introduction of required mathematical, computational, and data handling tools.
COMPSCI 284C.prereq_text: COMPSCI 284A with a minimum grade of B- or (BIO SCI 99 and MATH 2D).

COMPSCI 287.title: Approximation Algorithms
COMPSCI 287.description: Most optimization problems arising in practice turn out to be NP-hard and therefore intractable. A pragmatic recourse is the design of polynomial time algorithms which find near-optimal solutions. This idea has led to a deep theory to address such problems.
COMPSCI 287.prereq_text: COMPSCI 161 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B-. Required: A course on Linear Programming or working knowledge of LP-duality theory and working knowledge of complexity theory and NP-completeness.

COMPSCI 288.title: Algorithms for Matching Markets
COMPSCI 288.description: Discusses algorithms underlying matching markets, drawing ideas from CS theory, economics, and game-theory. Topics include Gale-Shapley stable-matching algorithm, its incentive compatibility and LP formulation; online bipartite matching and Adwords market; one-sided matching markets; and market equilibria.
COMPSCI 288.prereq_text: Recommended: COMPSCI 263 and COMPSCI 295 (when the topic title is Game Theory), or a course on linear programming, or working knowledge of LP-duality theory.
COMPSCI 288.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 290.title: Research Seminar
COMPSCI 290.description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.

COMPSCI 290P.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
COMPSCI 290P.description: Studies in selected areas of Information and Computer Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
COMPSCI 290P.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students and Master of Computer Science have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 291P.title: Professional Development for Computer Science Careers
COMPSCI 291P.description: Prepares students for career success through workshops, coaching, experiential learning, building skills in job search, networking, interviewing, and negotiation while developing professional identity and long-term career management strategies.
COMPSCI 291P.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students and Master of Computer Science have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 295.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
COMPSCI 295.description: Studies in selected areas of Information and Computer Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

COMPSCI 295P.title: Keystone Project for Computer Science
COMPSCI 295P.description: Design and development of a software system or a hardware component of a system based on knowledge of advanced computer science principles. Students implement at least a working prototype and test this using relevant input data.

COMPSCI 297AP.title: Capstone Project I
COMPSCI 297AP.description: Design and development of a software system or a hardware component of a system based on knowledge of advanced computer science principles. Students implement at least a working prototype and test this using relevant input data.
COMPSCI 297AP.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students and Master of Computer Science have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 297BP.title: Capstone Project II
COMPSCI 297BP.description: Design and development of app, software system, or hardware component of system based on students' prior knowledge of advanced computer science principles. Implement at least a working prototype and test this using relevant use cases and/or input data.
COMPSCI 297BP.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students and Master of Computer Science have the first consideration for enrollment.

COMPSCI 297P.title: Capstone Design Project for Computer Science
COMPSCI 297P.description: Design and development of app, software system, or hardware component of system based on students' prior knowledge of advanced computer science principles. Implement at least a working prototype and test this using relevant use cases and/or input data.

COMPSCI 298.title: Thesis Supervision
COMPSCI 298.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.

COMPSCI 298P.title: Computer Science Practicum
COMPSCI 298P.description: Internship in which students work individually at an outside organization to gain experience with the challenges involved in technology-related work.

COMPSCI 299.title: Individual Study
COMPSCI 299.description: Individual research or investigation with Computer Science faculty.

COMPSCI 299P.title: Individual Study
COMPSCI 299P.description: Supervised individual study in computer science.

CRITISM 200A.title: Political Economy: Methods and Critique
CRITISM 200A.description: Introduction to canonical texts in Marxism coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken after CLT&THY 200B.

CRM/LAW C7.title: Introduction to Criminology, Law and Society
CRM/LAW C7.description: Introduces characteristics of the U.S. criminal justice system, including responses to crime, components of the system, and current challenges to the system. Examines structure and function of police and courts, criminal procedure, and sentencing and incarceration policies.
CRM/LAW C7.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology and Social Behavior majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C10.title: Fundamentals of Criminology, Law and Society
CRM/LAW C10.description: Introduces three interdisciplinary literatures: criminology, socio-legal studies, and justice studies. Focuses on theoretical and empirical work addressing law making, law breaking, and legal systems.
CRM/LAW C10.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW H80.title: The Properties of Property
CRM/LAW H80.description: Develops an understanding and critique of private property. Draws from interdisciplinary sources to explore the foundations of private property, the institutions that support it over time, and possible alternatives to it.

CRM/LAW C100.title: Special Topics in Criminology, Law and Society
CRM/LAW C100.description: Course content varies with interest of the instructor.
CRM/LAW C100.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C101.title: American Law
CRM/LAW C101.description: Introduction to substantive and procedural law governing private dispute resolution, including common law (tort, property, contracts), lawsuits (civil procedure), and alternative dispute resolution; emphasis on the socio-legal ramifications of private disputes, particularly the modern tort system and tort reform movement.
CRM/LAW C101.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C102.title: Introduction to the Comparative Study of Legal Cultures
