CRM/LAW C102.description: Traces the anthropological and comparative cultural study of law from the nineteenth century to the present; briefly surveys the diversity of recorded legal cultures and critically examines key concepts which have been used to describe and classify them.
CRM/LAW C102.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology - Urban and Regional Planning majors, and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C103.title: US Legal Thought
CRM/LAW C103.description: Evolution of legal thought in socio-historical context from 19th century to present; emphasizes the rise and fall of legal classicism and modern socio-legal critiques, including the law and society movement, critical legal studies, feminist legal theory, and critical race studies.
CRM/LAW C103.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C104.title: Sociology of Law
CRM/LAW C104.description: Examines law creation and law enforcement in their social and political context. Discusses the major theories of law and the modern state, and presents case studies in order to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of these theoretical perspectives.
CRM/LAW C104.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C105.title: Psychology and the Law
CRM/LAW C105.description: Psychological assumptions of the American legal system and mental health aspects of provision of criminal justice services. Civil commitment, insanity defense, competence to stand trial, jury selection, eyewitness identification. Use of police, courts, correctional institutions in prevention of behavior disorder.
CRM/LAW C105.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology - Urban and Regional Planning majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C106.title: Crime and Public Policy
CRM/LAW C106.description: Explores nature and dimensions of crime in America and uses and limits of various strategies to control it. Topics include growth of imprisonment, the problem of domestic violence, the death penalty, gun control, and the potential of crime prevention programs.
CRM/LAW C106.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C107.title: Deviance
CRM/LAW C107.description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.
CRM/LAW C107.prereq_text: NO SOCIOL 156 AND NO PSYCH 177D AND NO COGS 177D
CRM/LAW C107.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology majors, Sociology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C108.title: Criminological Theory
CRM/LAW C108.description: Explores the question of crime causation from a number of theoretical perspectives in the social sciences. Schools of thought examined include utilitarianism, positivism, human ecology, social structural approaches, social process (learning) theories, labeling, and radical-critical (political) perspectives.
CRM/LAW C108.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C109.title: Juvenile Delinquency
CRM/LAW C109.description: Patterns of delinquent behavior, theories that explain behavior, current research aimed at enhancing exploratory power. Attempts to prevent and control delinquency are put in historical perspective. Development of the current juvenile justice system and evolution of modern juvenile law.
CRM/LAW C109.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology - Urban and Regional Planning majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C110.title: Community Context of Crime
CRM/LAW C110.description: Examines the social context of high-crime communities, with special emphasis on the problems of poverty, joblessness, economic inequality, and racial discrimination. Assesses debates on the causes of these problems, and on the most effective policies to combat them.
CRM/LAW C110.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C111.title: Theories of Punishment
CRM/LAW C111.description: Survey of the various schools of thought regarding formal punishment theory. The purposes of legal sanctions are examined, including those of deterrence, rehabilitation, retribution, and incapacitation. Considers problems in realizing formal goals of punishment in practice.
CRM/LAW C111.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C112.title: Legal Sanctions and Social Control
CRM/LAW C112.description: Examination of criminal sanctions as mechanisms of social control. Includes the nature, function, and organization of courts as sanction generating institutions, and problems associated with punishing white-collar and corporate illegalities.
CRM/LAW C112.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C113.title: Gender and Social Control
CRM/LAW C113.description: Examines the legal system's use of sex as an organizing characteristic, focusing particularly on sameness and difference feminism, and tracing the evolution of equal treatment of men and women in the areas of constitutional rights, employment, education, and military service.
CRM/LAW C113.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C114.title: Miscarriages of Justice
CRM/LAW C114.description: Systematically describes, explains, and analyzes the causes and consequences of the wrongful accusation, prosecution, incarceration, and sometimes even execution, of the innocent in the American criminal justice system.
CRM/LAW C114.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C115.title: Prisons, Punishment, and Corrections
CRM/LAW C115.description: A review of how the U.S. punishes and rehabilitates convicted law violators. The conflicts among the major purposes of sentencing—rehabilitation, deterrence, incapacitation—are discussed, as well as the effects of different sanctions on public safety, offender rehabilitation, and justice system costs.
CRM/LAW C115.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C116.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Social Control
CRM/LAW C116.description: Provides a historical and sociological survey of racial and ethnic group relations in contexts of crime control, emphasizing the roles of racial ideology, structural racism, and social movements in shaping these dynamic relations, and their significance to American liberal democracy.
CRM/LAW C116.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C117.title: Imprisonment and Reentry
CRM/LAW C117.description: Offers an overview of imprisonment and reentry in the contemporary United States. Examines the development of the prison in the United States and explores changes in its composition, structure, and purpose over time.
CRM/LAW C117.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C118.title: Domestic Violence
CRM/LAW C118.description: General perspectives about domestic violence and theoretical accounts about what causes such behavior.
CRM/LAW C118.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C119.title: Violence in Intimate Relationships
CRM/LAW C119.description: Responses to various forms of domestic violence, such as intimate partner violence and child abuse. Covers barriers to reporting to the police, and prosecutors and courts. Human services, such as safety planning for victims, treatment programs, and restorative justice approaches.
CRM/LAW C119.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C120.title: Law and Inequality
CRM/LAW C120.description: Various aspects of the law as related to three specific areas of inequality: immigration and immigrants, race, and gender. The role of law as a tool of social reform and limitations of the legal system historically in resolving inequality issues.
CRM/LAW C120.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C121.title: Crime, Law, and Trauma
CRM/LAW C121.description: Examines trauma's role in criminal behavior and justice, exploring its impact on victims and offenders, its relationship to specific crimes, and its influence on legal proceedings. Students analyze how trauma shapes criminal justice policies.
CRM/LAW C121.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C122.title: Constitutional Law
CRM/LAW C122.description: Examines the evolution of civil liberties and individual rights in the United States, focusing on how Constitutional Amendments and U.S. Supreme Court decision-making have shaped the ongoing political and legal struggles over issues such as privacy, abortion, and free speech.
CRM/LAW C122.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C123.title: Family Law
CRM/LAW C123.description: Examines legal issues surrounding marriage, cohabitation, divorce, child custody and support, adoption, and the rights of parents and children in the family context. The findings of social science research are used to illuminate the legal issues.
CRM/LAW C123.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C126.title: Drugs, Crime, and Social Control
CRM/LAW C126.description: Implementation of drug crime policy in the U.S.; historical views of U.S. social control and crime policies. Students critically examine drugs and crime research and policy, with attention to causal rigor and how policies interact with and affect socioeconomic conditions.
CRM/LAW C126.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C127.title: Hate Crimes
CRM/LAW C127.description: Examines the causes, manifestations, and consequences of hate crimes and the larger social context within which they occur. The politics and dynamics of intergroup violence born of bigotry and manifested as discrimination; social policy designed to control bias-motivated violence.
CRM/LAW C127.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C128.title: Environmental Law and Policy
CRM/LAW C128.description: Environmental law as a combination of traditional legal principles and newly created statutes, rules, and decisions applied to environmental protection. Investigates roles of courts, legislature, executive branch and administrative agencies, and private citizens attempting to regulate environmental quality.
CRM/LAW C128.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors only.

CRM/LAW C129.title: Critical Policing Studies
CRM/LAW C129.description: Traces the historical development of policing in the United States from a critical perspective. Introduces contemporary problems and debates in policing, including issues of police use of force, disparate effects of police practices, and alternative approaches to public safety.
CRM/LAW C129.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C132.title: Forensic Science, Law, and Society
CRM/LAW C132.description: Examines use of "forensic science" to resolve issues arising in criminal cases including crime scene analysis, DNA testing, fingerprints, trace evidence comparisons, profiling, lie detectors, other forensic techniques; evaluation, statistical characterization, and legal admissibility of evidence; regulation of forensic laboratories.
CRM/LAW C132.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C135.title: Mass Incarceration and Social Inequality in America
CRM/LAW C135.description: Explores the origins and consequences of mass incarceration; extraordinarily high incarceration rates within particular demographic groups above and beyond historical levels in the U.S. Theoretical explanations for, and current policy debates around, mass incarceration are covered.
CRM/LAW C135.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C136.title: Forensic Psychology: Advanced Seminar
CRM/LAW C136.description: Focuses on the psychology of criminal offending, particularly violent behavior. Examines violence, sexual offending, and mental disorder related to crime with regard to clinical assessment and treatment; mental health services within forensic institutions.
CRM/LAW C136.prereq_text: (PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C) and PSY 102C and (PSY 161C or CRM/LAW C160). Interview required
CRM/LAW C136.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C138.title: Media Effects on Law and Justice
CRM/LAW C138.description: Examines theoretical and methodological frameworks necessary for understanding mass media effects. Trains students to analyze and create media content that cover a wide array of law and justice topics, such as criminal trial procedures, coerced confessions, and mass incarceration.
CRM/LAW C138.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C139.title: Police and Change
CRM/LAW C139.description: Organizational efforts to modify police conduct are addressed by focusing on the history of policing in the United States including training, education, and the contributions of women.
CRM/LAW C139.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C140.title: Surveillance and Society
CRM/LAW C140.description: Explores the development and deployment of surveillance technologies in contemporary society. The social and legal impact of surveillance technologies, in such areas as crime control, privacy, trust, community, democracy, and the war on terror.
CRM/LAW C140.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors only.

CRM/LAW C141.title: Anthropology of Law
CRM/LAW C141.description: Introduces the anthropological study of law through a focus on the foundations of this subfield, its primary methodologies, and several important topics of inquiry, including policing, immigration, and structural inequalities. Provides an international perspective on law and society.
CRM/LAW C141.restriction: Anthropology majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C142.title: White-Collar Crime
CRM/LAW C142.description: Examines criminal activity in business and corporate enterprise, organizations, and the professions. Theories regarding the causes and control of white-collar and corporate crime are covered as well as the numerous definitions of these terms.
CRM/LAW C142.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology majors, and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C144.title: Criminal Law
CRM/LAW C144.description: Deals specifically with the substantive nature of criminal law and its historical development. Focuses on understanding the development of fundamental doctrinal principles upon which criminal law is based, including mens rea, actus reus, homicide, causation, group criminality, and exculpation.
CRM/LAW C144.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C146.title: Crimes of the State
CRM/LAW C146.description: Examines the origins, operations, and outcomes of historical and contemporary international justice measures used to address—and potentially adjudicate—crimes of the state including torture, disappearances, genocide, etc.
CRM/LAW C146.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C147.title: Criminal Justice and Public Health
CRM/LAW C147.description: Examines intersections between criminal justice systems and public health. Through critical analysis of research and policy, students explore how health challenges drive criminal justice involvement, challenges in healthcare delivery within correctional settings, and the health consequences of criminal justice contact.

CRM/LAW C149.title: Violence in Society
CRM/LAW C149.description: Current theory and research on aggression; anger and violence as problems in individual and social functioning. Process and functions of anger examined with regard to normal behavior and psychopathology. The determinants, prevalence, and implications of violence in society are analyzed.
CRM/LAW C149.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C.
CRM/LAW C149.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW 151.title: Language and the Law
CRM/LAW 151.description: Considers the role of language in legal practice and power. Particular attention is paid to linguistic and discourse analytic research that cover topics such as: trial talk, language crimes, law talk in cross-cultural perspectives, and linguistic evidence.
CRM/LAW 151.restriction: Anthropology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C160.title: Forensic Psychology
CRM/LAW C160.description: Forensic psychology is the interface between clinical psychology and the law. Emphasizes clinically relevant legal topics (insanity defense; competency to stand trial) and includes critical thinking about issues that arise when psychologists are involved in legal proceedings.
CRM/LAW C160.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 21 or PSY 22.
CRM/LAW C160.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C162.title: Crime Hotspots
CRM/LAW C162.description: Criminological theories of local public safety hazards or hotspots are introduced. Spatial statistics are developed for different types of hotspots. Hotspot policing theories are introduced and research on the effectiveness of policing strategies is reviewed.
CRM/LAW C162.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C163.title: Ethics and Politics of Justice
CRM/LAW C163.description: Theoretical perspective on how ethics and politics relate to criminal justice through an introduction to moral philosophy; consideration of specific theories of punishment and justice; and consideration of practical and empirical illustrations of the intersection of ethics, politics, and justice.
CRM/LAW C163.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C164.title: Social Control of Delinquency
CRM/LAW C164.description: Assumes familiarity with theories of delinquency, the juvenile justice system, and elements of juvenile law. Explores socio-historical origins and evolution of juvenile justice, current research and policy on delinquency prevention and treatment, and future directions of law, policy, and practice.
CRM/LAW C164.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C165.title: The Death Penalty
CRM/LAW C165.description: Examines why the U.S. continues to have a death penalty when so many other countries have abandoned it. Arguments for and against the death penalty are covered.
CRM/LAW C165.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C166.title: Spatial Criminology
CRM/LAW C166.description: Scholars have long noted crime events exhibit a spatial patterning. The principal theoretical perspectives that attempt to explain such a spatial patterning, as well as the research methods used to study crime in spatial context are considered.
CRM/LAW C166.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C167.title: Crime Measurement
CRM/LAW C167.description: The strengths and weaknesses of three crime measures (police reports, victim surveys, and offender self-reports) are illustrated through analyses of research articles. Common measurement problems are analyzed with a focus on reliability and validity.
CRM/LAW C167.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C168.title: Extreme Punishment
CRM/LAW C168.description: Explores the history and law of America’s Eighth Amendment prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment, examining the death penalty, long prison sentences, harsh confinement conditions, and other punishments. Students debate practical, legal, and moral arguments for and against these punishments.
CRM/LAW C168.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C169.title: Crime, Violence, and Social Conflict in the Global South
CRM/LAW C169.description: Crime, violence, and social conflict in the Global South; historical, political, and institutional contexts; state and non-state responses; criminological theory across Latin America, Africa, and Asia; implications for state-building, punishment, and reconciliation.
CRM/LAW C169.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C169W.title: Advanced Research Methods
CRM/LAW C169W.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
CRM/LAW C169W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

CRM/LAW C174.title: Immigration and Crime
CRM/LAW C174.description: Examines immigration and crime in the global context, highlighting immigrants as criminals and victims; immigration and crime control; immigrants’ perceptions of the criminal justice system; public discourse and public perception on immigration and crime; and human rights issues.
CRM/LAW C174.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C175.title: Issues in Policing
CRM/LAW C175.description: Lectures and readings focus on the history and strategies of policing, measuring the quality of policing, and police misconduct. Strategies for enhancing the quality of policing for controlling misconduct are covered.
CRM/LAW C175.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C176.title: Classics in Crime Cinema
CRM/LAW C176.description: A multidimensional understanding of crime films and how they shape public thinking about crime and criminals.
CRM/LAW C176.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C177.title: Eyewitness Testimony
CRM/LAW C177.description: Faulty eyewitness testimony is a major cause of wrongful convictions. Covers the fast-growing topic of eyewitness testimony and memory for real-world events, both how psychologists study eyewitness capacity, and how the legal system has dealt with eyewitness issues.
CRM/LAW C177.restriction: Seniors, Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C178.title: Critical Race Theory
CRM/LAW C178.description: Introduction to Critical Race Theory and key American cases on racial inequality. Using this literature, examines the possibilities and pitfalls of legal claims of race, gender, and sexuality discrimination in the age of colorblindness.
CRM/LAW C178.restriction: African-American Studies majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C179.title: Race and Incarceration
CRM/LAW C179.description: Examines the racial politics of mass incarceration through historical, empirical, theoretical, and legal frameworks. Focuses on race, gender, and sexual differences to develop a critique on policing, incarceration, and other forms of punishment.
CRM/LAW C179.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C180.title: Power, Constructions of Deviance, and Social Control
CRM/LAW C180.description: Examines the forms and limits of power in the construction of social deviants. Theories of state power are covered to understand the prison system as a contemporary driver of social inequality. The collateral consequences of mass incarceration are discussed.
CRM/LAW C180.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C182.title: Illegal Economics
CRM/LAW C182.description: How illegal firms function in illegal markets, why individuals participate in these groups and markets, and what federal, state, and local governments do to disrupt organized illegal activity.
CRM/LAW C182.restriction: Business Economics majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C183.title: Controversies, Courts, Cultures: The Anthropology of Law
CRM/LAW C183.description: Assesses the contributions anthropology has made to legal scholarship, reviewing historical and contemporary themes. Considers both comparative questions of law’s norms, structures, and practices around the globe, and the specific insights anthropology offers about contemporary U.S. law.

CRM/LAW C184.title: Economics of Criminal Justice
CRM/LAW C184.description: Provides an introduction to the economics of crime literature.
CRM/LAW C184.restriction: Business Economics majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C186.title: Social Media and The Law
CRM/LAW C186.description: Examines legal and policy issues raised by the rise of social media. Surveys how social networking platforms and other emerging technologies impact the right to privacy, public perceptions of judicial systems, and the law generally.
CRM/LAW C186.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C189.title: Careers in Criminology, Law and Society
CRM/LAW C189.description: Gives students the skills and perspective needed to leverage undergraduate Criminology, Law and Society education in diverse career domains. Students explore different career pathways (social services, law, enforcement, nonprofits, government, graduate study, etc.) and learn to represent themselves professionally.

CRM/LAW C190.title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
CRM/LAW C190.description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.
CRM/LAW C190.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C196.title: Research Seminar in Criminology, Law and Society
CRM/LAW C196.description: Special topics research seminar. Content varies with interest of instructor. Capstone research opportunity with Criminology, Law and Society faculty members.
CRM/LAW C196.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CRM/LAW C201.title: Research Methods
CRM/LAW C201.description: An introduction to techniques of inductive methodologies, including qualitative interviewing and participant observation, and deductive methodologies, including survey research and experimental and quasi-experimental design. Provides a sound overview of research methodology with tools to pursue specific methods in greater depth.

CRM/LAW C202.title: Research Methods II
CRM/LAW C202.description: Covers qualitative approaches (interview strategies, varieties of ethnography, archival and historical methods, etc.) and quantitative approaches (survey methods, experimental designs, secondary data sets, comparative and international data, etc.), and concludes with mixed-method approaches.
CRM/LAW C202.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C201 with a minimum grade of B.

CRM/LAW C203A.title: Qualitative Methods Practicum
CRM/LAW C203A.description: Designed to deepen students’ familiarity with qualitative research strategies and to guide them through the initial stages of their Second Year Project requirement, such as the development of an original research proposal and/or a research instrument.
CRM/LAW C203A.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C202 with a minimum grade of B.

CRM/LAW C203B.title: Quantitative Methods Practicum
CRM/LAW C203B.description: Deepens familiarity with quantitative research and provides a foundation for the second-year paper, e.g., initial models for data analysis and/or a replication study. Students evaluate what assumptions are necessary for credible inference in different evaluation approaches.
CRM/LAW C203B.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C202 with a minimum grade of B.

CRM/LAW C207.title: Land-Use Law
CRM/LAW C207.description: Investigates legal and institutional frameworks for development control. Review of constitutional issues implicated in land-use regulation. Traces development control historically and analyzes contemporary approaches to land-use control which reflect environmental and economic development concerns.

CRM/LAW C210.title: Introduction to Criminology, Law and Society
CRM/LAW C210.description: Familiarizes students with the interrelated fields of criminology, law and society studies, and criminal justice studies. Organized around three well-established interdisciplinary literatures: criminology, sociolegal studies, and criminal justice studies.
CRM/LAW C210.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors only.

CRM/LAW C211.title: Legal Institutions and Society
CRM/LAW C211.description: Acquaints students with the institutions of U.S. legal system and its operations, as well as with the constitutional framework undergirding this system, and defines the relationship between U.S. citizens and government at a variety of levels.

CRM/LAW C212.title: Policing
CRM/LAW C212.description: Introduces the subject of policing. Topics include the management of police organizations, the effectiveness of police patrol strategies, the experiences of women in policing, the recruitment and retention of police officers, and other related topics.

CRM/LAW C213.title: Crime and Social Deviance
CRM/LAW C213.description: Examines the major social scientific perspectives on criminal and deviant behavior. Specific deviant and criminal activities are described and explained using established theoretical frameworks.

CRM/LAW C214.title: Research Methods
CRM/LAW C214.description: Structures research methodology, the approach to developing and evaluating knowledge of the sciences for use in criminal justice professional activities. Special emphasis on differentiating scientific approaches from pseudo-science.

CRM/LAW C215.title: Applied Statistics
CRM/LAW C215.description: Provides a basis for the use of fundamental statistical analysis techniques for solving public policy and management problems through a series of assignments, examinations, and online discussions and demonstrations.

CRM/LAW C216.title: Public Policy, Crime, and Criminal Justice
CRM/LAW C216.description: Increases understanding of crime, violence, and the criminal justice system. Assesses the state of knowledge on key policy issues of our time. Discusses the contribution of communities, schools, employment, drugs, guns, and alcohol to crime and violence.

CRM/LAW C217.title: Leadership
CRM/LAW C217.description: Introduces concepts, ideas, and theories about leadership and its operation. Explores leadership concepts through interviews with leaders from the community and fellow classmates.

CRM/LAW C218.title: Social Problems, Law, and Policy
CRM/LAW C218.description: Capstone course for M.A.S. program in Criminology, Law and Society. Students choose a social problem related to crime, criminal justice, and law; relate the problem to legal and social issues; and devise a plan of action to research the problem.
CRM/LAW C218.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors only.

CRM/LAW C219.title: Hate Crime
CRM/LAW C219.description: Examines the causes, manifestations, and consequences of hate crimes, as well as the larger social context within which they occur, are reacted to, and seem to be proliferating.

CRM/LAW C221.title: Sentencing and Corrections
CRM/LAW C221.description: Reviews U.S. attempts to punish and rehabilitate convicted law violators. Conflicts among major purposes of sentencing (rehabilitation, deterrence, incapacitation, and retribution) are discussed, as well as effects of different sanctions on public safety, offender rehabilitation, and justice system costs.

CRM/LAW C222.title: Ethnography
CRM/LAW C222.description: Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies.

CRM/LAW C228.title: Criminology: Micro Approaches
CRM/LAW C228.description: Introduces students to the dominant theories in modern criminology, their theoretical antecedents and extensions, major empirical tests and implications for programs, policy and practice, and focuses on micro-level, individual theories of crime causation. Formerly Criminology, Law and Society C233A.

CRM/LAW C229.title: Criminology: Macro Approaches
CRM/LAW C229.description: Introduces students to the dominant theories in modern criminology, their theoretical antecedents and extensions, major empirical tests and implications for programs, policy and practices, and addresses macro-level theories of crime causation. Formerly Criminology, Law and Society C233B.

CRM/LAW C231.title: Crime and Gender
CRM/LAW C231.description: Examines the legal, political, social, economic, and policy implications of making gender (primarily) and race (secondarily) the focus in the study of crime, criminal law, and the criminal justice system.

CRM/LAW C234.title: Anthropology of Law
CRM/LAW C234.description: Law has been a key site of anthropological inquiry since the discipline's nineteenth-century origins. Course introduces and critically assesses the contributions anthropology has made to sociolegal lytic trends.

CRM/LAW C238.title: White-Collar Crime
CRM/LAW C238.description: Examines the illegal behavior of individuals who commit crimes in the course of their employment. Special attention will be paid to ways in which power and organizational structure affect the behavior of the white-collar offenders.

CRM/LAW C239A.title: Law and Society I
CRM/LAW C239A.description: Provides an introduction to the law and society field from its origins in social scientific, legal, and philosophical scholarship during the eighteenth, nineteenth, and early-twentieth centuries. Formerly Criminology, Law, and Society C239.

CRM/LAW C239B.title: Law and Society II
CRM/LAW C239B.description: Building on Law and Society I, addresses contemporary issues in the field from mid-twentieth century to the present with emphasis on the degree to which the field's foundational assumptions are being challenged, refined, or confirmed through current research.
CRM/LAW C239B.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C239A with a minimum grade of B-.

CRM/LAW C240A.title: Socio-Legal Workshop
CRM/LAW C240A.description: Designed to foster intellectual discussion, encourage practice and skill-building in providing feedback, and build substantive knowledge of legal scholarship, this workshop is for both law and doctoral students across campus who are interested in interdisciplinary approaches to studying law.

CRM/LAW C240B.title: Socio-Legal Workshop
CRM/LAW C240B.description: Designed to foster intellectual discussion, encourage practice and skill-building in providing feedback, and build substantive knowledge of legal scholarship, this workshop is for both law and doctoral students across campus who are interested in interdisciplinary approaches to studying law.
CRM/LAW C240B.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C240A with a minimum grade of B-.

CRM/LAW C240C.title: Socio-Legal Workshop
CRM/LAW C240C.description: Designed to foster intellectual discussion, encourage practice and skill-building in providing feedback, and build substantive knowledge of legal scholarship, this workshop is for both law and doctoral students across campus who are interested in interdisciplinary approaches to studying law.
CRM/LAW C240C.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C240B with a minimum grade of B.

CRM/LAW C242.title: Crime Hotspots
CRM/LAW C242.description: Focuses on the criminological theory of hotspots, beginning with the “when, where, and why” questions and ending with the practical policing strategies that have been developed to mitigate hotspot public safety hazards.

CRM/LAW C250.title: Preventing Errors of Justice
CRM/LAW C250.description: Examines the types of errors that are made in the U.S. criminal justice system and how we might prevent these errors, including failures to convict guilty offenders as well as wrongful convictions of the innocent.

CRM/LAW C252.title: Issues in Environmental Law and Policy
CRM/LAW C252.description: Treatment of legal and policy strategies for promoting environmental protection and deterring environmental degradation within the context of other societal objectives. Topical approach with a focus on problems of special interest to criminologists and to environmental policy specialists.

CRM/LAW C253.title: Cybercrime, Cybersecurity, and Society
CRM/LAW C253.description: Introduces students to the world of cybercrime in the age of globally networked digital, and information and communication technologies (ICT). Presents a socio-legal approach to the study of cybercrime, cybersecurity, and how it relates to society.
CRM/LAW C253.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors only.

CRM/LAW C254.title: Immigration in the US: Economic, Fiscal, and Social Outcomes
CRM/LAW C254.description: The changing patterns of immigration in the U.S. and the role that immigrants play in our society. In particular, the economic and social outcomes of immigration, as well as the relationship between immigration, crime, and criminal justice policy.
CRM/LAW C254.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors only.

CRM/LAW C255.title: Public Policy
CRM/LAW C255.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst. Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.
CRM/LAW C255.prereq_text: NO UPPP 221 AND NO POL SCI 221A

CRM/LAW C257.title: Juvenile Justice and Gangs
CRM/LAW C257.description: Aims to understand the history and evolution of the juvenile justice system, and introduces the challenges that street and prison gangs pose to the mission and operations of juvenile justice in America.
CRM/LAW C257.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors only.

CRM/LAW C260.title: Drugs, Crime, and Drug Policy
CRM/LAW C260.description: Examines psychoactive drugs, the relationship(s) between drugs and crime, and the intended and unintended consequences of policies aimed at drug control, including racial fairness in drug control. Primary focus concerns the U.S.; however, international drug policy is explored for context.

CRM/LAW C260A.title: Race and Justice Studies Proseminar
CRM/LAW C260A.description: A year-long proseminar conducted by a team of instructors specializing in race and justice studies. Conceived as a reading and peer mentor group focusing on intellectual and professional development. Required for students pursuing the Race and Justice Studies emphasis.

CRM/LAW C260B.title: Race and Justice Studies Proseminar
CRM/LAW C260B.description: A year-long proseminar conducted by a team of instructors specializing in race and justice studies. Conceived as a reading and peer mentor group focusing on intellectual and professional development. Required for students pursuing the Race and Justice Studies emphasis.
CRM/LAW C260B.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C260A with a minimum grade of B-.

CRM/LAW C260C.title: Race and Justice Studies Proseminar
CRM/LAW C260C.description: A year-long proseminar conducted by a team of instructors specializing in race and justice studies. Conceived as a reading and peer mentor group focusing on intellectual and professional development. Required for students pursuing the Race and Justice Studies emphasis.
CRM/LAW C260C.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C260B with a minimum grade of B-.

CRM/LAW C261.title: Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
CRM/LAW C261.description: A required writing-intensive seminar conducted by an instructor affiliated with the Race and Justice Studies emphasis. Students with manuscripts on relevant topics will read and critique peer manuscripts, and revise manuscripts toward completion of articles, dissertation chapters, and other publications.
CRM/LAW C261.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C260C with a minimum grade of B-.

CRM/LAW C262.title: Special Topics in Race and Justice Studies
CRM/LAW C262.description: A seminar focused on special issues in race and justice studies.

CRM/LAW C263.title: Eyewitness Testimony
CRM/LAW C263.description: Examines the evidence that shows that faulty eyewitness memory is the major cause of wrongful convictions. Explores what the legal system thinks of eyewitness testimony and how the legal system has dealt with eyewitness issues.

CRM/LAW C265.title: Memory and the Law
CRM/LAW C265.description: Examines the controversial topic of repressed memory, or perception and memory of real-world events.

CRM/LAW C266.title: Psychology and the Law
CRM/LAW C266.description: Overview of how psychology is applied to the civil and criminal justice systems, how case law shapes this application, and how legal decisions affect the direction of psychological research. Interdisciplinary approach to research in psychology, law, and/or criminology.

CRM/LAW C268.title: Contemporary Issues in Crime and Justice
CRM/LAW C268.description: Intensive reading and discussion of several recent works that raise critical issues for criminology and criminal justice policy, with a special emphasis on issues of inequality, diversity, and social justice.

CRM/LAW C271.title: Economics of Criminal Justice
CRM/LAW C271.description: Considers empirical research from the economics literature on various topics related to the criminal justice system, such as policing, bail reform, incarceration, or recidivism.

CRM/LAW C275.title: Special Topics in Criminology, Law and Society
CRM/LAW C275.description: Topics covered vary with interests of instructor.

CRM/LAW C280A.title: Professionalization Proseminar
CRM/LAW C280A.description: Focuses on two areas that are key to scholarly and professional success in graduate school but are rarely discussed in a structured setting: 1) publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals; and 2) preparing for the academic job market.

CRM/LAW C280B.title: Professionalization Proseminar
CRM/LAW C280B.description: Focuses on two areas that are key to scholarly and professional success in graduate school but are rarely discussed in a structured setting: 1) publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals; and 2) preparing for the academic job market.
CRM/LAW C280B.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C280A with a minimum grade of B-.

CRM/LAW C280C.title: Professionalization Proseminar
CRM/LAW C280C.description: Focuses on two areas that are key to scholarly and professional success in graduate school but are rarely discussed in a structured setting: 1) publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals; and 2) preparing for the academic job market.
CRM/LAW C280C.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C280B with a minimum grade of B-.

CRM/LAW C296.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
CRM/LAW C296.description: Dissertation research with Criminology, Law and Society faculty.

CRM/LAW C298.title: Directed Study
CRM/LAW C298.description: Directed study with Criminology, Law and Society faculty.

CRM/LAW C299.title: Independent Study
CRM/LAW C299.description: Independent research with Criminology, Law and Society faculty.

CSE 90.title: Systems Engineering and Technical Communications
CSE 90.description: Introduces systems engineering concepts, including specifications and requirements, hardware and software design, integration, testing, and documentation. Emphasizes organization and writing of reports and effective presentations.
CSE 90.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CSE 112.title: Electronic Devices and Circuits
CSE 112.description: A first course in the design of Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) systems. Introduction to CMOS technology; MOS transistors and CMOS circuits. Analysis and synthesis of CMOS gates. Layout design techniques for building blocks and systems. Introduction to CAD tools.
CSE 112.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

CSE 199.title: Individual Study
CSE 199.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

DANCE 2.title: Dance Health and Injury Prevention
DANCE 2.description: An overview of factors that affect the health of dancers. Includes evaluation of general health measures and prevention and management of common dance injuries.
DANCE 2.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 3.title: Scientific Concepts of Health
DANCE 3.description: Introduction to the scientific foundations of health, emphasizing those pertaining to success in college and lifetime wellness. Includes principles of cardiorespiratory, musculoskeletal, flexibility, and nutritional fitness. A variety of learning experiences are offered to apply science to real life.

DANCE 14.title: Social Dance
DANCE 14.description: Current and historical forms that may include ballroom, disco, square dance, Latin styles, and other social dances from the early-to-mid 20th century.

DANCE 21A.title: Music for Dancers
DANCE 21A.description: Emphasis on the development of musical skills most pertinent to the dancer: vocabulary, notational literacy, rhythmic and melodic acuity, score reading, and fundamental analysis; working with live accompaniment.
DANCE 21A.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 30A.title: Studio Workshop in Ballet I
DANCE 30A.description: Beginning ballet: fundamentals and principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.

DANCE 30B.title: Studio Workshop in Ballet I
DANCE 30B.description: Beginning ballet: fundamentals and principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.

DANCE 30C.title: Studio Workshop in Ballet I
DANCE 30C.description: Beginning ballet: fundamentals and principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.

DANCE 34.title: Men's Studio Workshop in Ballet
DANCE 34.description: Emphasis on men's traditional ballet, techniques, and movements.

DANCE 40A.title: Studio Workshop in Modern/Contemporary Dance I
DANCE 40A.description: Fundamentals of modern/contemporary dance, including the use of breath, gravity, spatial awareness, and time values.

DANCE 40B.title: Studio Workshop in Modern/Contemporary Dance I
DANCE 40B.description: Fundamentals of modern/contemporary dance, including the use of breath, gravity, spatial awareness, and time values.

DANCE 40C.title: Studio Workshop in Modern/Contemporary Dance I
DANCE 40C.description: Fundamentals of modern/contemporary dance, including the use of breath, gravity, spatial awareness, and time values.

DANCE 50A.title: Studio Workshop on Jazz I
DANCE 50A.description: Fundamentals of jazz: principles of jazz dance and contemporary forms incorporating the personal point of view of the instructor.

DANCE 50B.title: Studio Workshop on Jazz I
DANCE 50B.description: Fundamentals of jazz: principles of jazz dance and contemporary forms incorporating the personal point of view of the instructor.

DANCE 50C.title: Studio Workshop on Jazz I
DANCE 50C.description: Fundamentals of jazz: principles of jazz dance and contemporary forms incorporating the personal point of view of the instructor.

DANCE 52A.title: Workshop in Tap I
DANCE 52A.description: Beginning tap: principles of rhythm and basic tap steps.

DANCE 52B.title: Workshop in Tap I
DANCE 52B.description: Beginning tap: principles of rhythm and basic tap steps.

DANCE 52C.title: Workshop in Tap I
DANCE 52C.description: Beginning tap: principles of rhythm and basic tap steps.

DANCE 53A.title: Studio Workshop in Hip Hop I
DANCE 53A.description: Designed to support non-major dance students learning outcomes in basic and foundational concepts of Hip Hop dance forms.

DANCE 53B.title: Studio Workshop in Hip Hop I
DANCE 53B.description: Designed to support non-major dance students learning outcomes in basic and foundational concepts of Hip Hop dance forms.

DANCE 53C.title: Studio Workshop in Hip Hop I
DANCE 53C.description: Designed to support non-major dance students learning outcomes in basic and foundational concepts of Hip Hop dance forms.

DANCE 60A.title: Choreography
DANCE 60A.description: Beginning-to-intermediate study of principles of dance composition. May include composition assignments for stage and video. By audition, works may be shown quarterly in public studio performances.
DANCE 60A.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 60B.title: Choreography
DANCE 60B.description: Beginning-to-intermediate study of principles of dance composition. May include composition assignments for stage and video. By audition, works may be shown quarterly in public studio performances.
DANCE 60B.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 60C.title: Choreography
DANCE 60C.description: Beginning-to-intermediate study of principles of dance composition. May include composition assignments for stage and video. By audition, works may be shown quarterly in public studio performances.
DANCE 60C.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 80.title: Introduction to Ballet and Modern Dance
DANCE 80.description: Survey of 19th- and 20th-century ballet, modern dance, and theatre dance.

DANCE 81.title: American Ballet and Modern Dance since 1900
DANCE 81.description: A survey of American ballet and modern dance in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Lectures are supplemented by video.
DANCE 81.restriction: Non-major only. Dance 81 and Dance 90C may not both be taken for credit.

DANCE 90A.title: Dance History I
DANCE 90A.description: Global perspectives. Topics and histories of dance and movement practices from various parts of the world.
DANCE 90A.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DANCE 90B.title: Dance History II
DANCE 90B.description: The history of dance in the western tradition from the Renaissance through the 19th century.
DANCE 90B.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DANCE 90C.title: Dance History III
DANCE 90C.description: The history of dance in the western tradition in the the 20th and 21st centuries.
DANCE 90C.restriction: Dance - Choreography majors, Dance - Performance majors, and Dance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DANCE 100.title: Kinesiology for Dance
DANCE 100.description: The study of the production of dance movement by the musculoskeletal system. Anatomical and dynamic analysis of dance movement.
DANCE 100.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 103.title: Pilates
DANCE 103.description: Basics of technique emphasizing alignment, breath control, correction of muscular imbalances.
DANCE 103.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 104.title: Pilates Reformer
DANCE 104.description: Utilizes the Universal Reformer apparatus, aiding the student in core stabilization, correcting muscular imbalances, increasing flexibility, and improving strength.
DANCE 104.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 110.title: World Dance
DANCE 110.description: Studio workshop of dances and movement sources of specified countries or areas.

DANCE 130A.title: Pointe Class
DANCE 130A.description: Beginning and intermediate pointe work; principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.
DANCE 130A.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 132A.title: Studio Workshop in Ballet II
DANCE 132A.description: Intermediate ballet and beginning pointe work; principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.
DANCE 132A.prereq_text: (DANCE 30A and DANCE 30B and DANCE 30C) or audition. Prerequisites are for non-Dance majors only.
DANCE 132A.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DANCE 132B.title: Studio Workshop in Ballet II
DANCE 132B.description: Intermediate ballet and beginning pointe work; principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.
DANCE 132B.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DANCE 132C.title: Studio Workshop in Ballet II
DANCE 132C.description: Intermediate ballet and beginning pointe work; principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.
DANCE 132C.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DANCE 133A.title: Advanced Studio Workshop in Ballet III
DANCE 133A.description: Advanced intermediate ballet and pointe work; principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.
DANCE 133A.prereq_text: DANCE 132C with a minimum grade of B+. Placement by audition is also accepted.
DANCE 133A.restriction: Dance - Choreography majors, Dance - Performance majors, and Dance majors only.

DANCE 133B.title: Advanced Studio Workshop in Ballet III
DANCE 133B.description: Advanced intermediate ballet and pointe work; principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.
DANCE 133B.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 133C.title: Advanced Studio Workshop in Ballet III
DANCE 133C.description: Advanced intermediate ballet and pointe work; principles of classical ballet with an emphasis on technique.
DANCE 133C.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 134A.title: Advanced Studio Workshop in Ballet IV
DANCE 134A.description: Advanced ballet, pointe work, and performance styles: principles of classical ballet.
DANCE 134A.prereq_text: DANCE 133A and DANCE 133B and DANCE 133C with a minimum grade of B+. Placement by audition is also accepted.
DANCE 134A.restriction: Dance majors, Dance - Choreography majors, and Dance - Performance majors only.

DANCE 195.title: Arts Management
DANCE 195.description: Designed for students interested in the developmental and management of nonprofit arts organizations. Examines the organizational structure and areas of operation such as marketing, fundraising, budgeting, production, and administration.

DANCE 197.title: Independent Study
DANCE 197.description: Individual independent projects in experimental laboratory, library, field, performance, under instructor's direction. Students can receive conceptual, creative, and theoretical instruction in the successful completion of a written report or performance.

DANCE 199.title: Senior Thesis

DANCE 201.title: Seminar in Kinesiology for Dance

DANCE 225.title: Seminar in the Teaching of Dance Techniques
DANCE 225.description: Principles and theories of teaching dance techniques. Supervised presentation and teaching of technique class.

DANCE 286.title: Thesis

DANCE 287.title: Graduate Lectures in Dance
DANCE 287.description: A series of lectures and discussions of announced topics in dance. Content may be from history, ethnology, notation, medicine, music, or other areas in the field.

DANCE 296.title: Proseminar in Dance History
DANCE 296.description: Discussion seminar with emphasis on reading and thinking about problems in dance history; presentation of oral and written reports.

DANCE 297.title: Directed Reading
DANCE 297.description: Topic to be approved by instructor. Paper required.

DATA 200AP.title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory I
DATA 200AP.description: Fundamental probability and distribution theory needed for statistical inference. Topics include axiomatic foundations of probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, expectation and moment generating functions, multivariate distributions, transformations, sampling distributions, and limit theorems.
DATA 200AP.prereq_text: Knowledge of basic statistics and linear algebra; Calculus I-III.

DATA 200BP.title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory II
DATA 200BP.description: Fundamental theory and methods for statistical inference. Topics include data reduction (sufficient, ancillary, and complete statistics), estimation (method of moments, maximum likelihood estimators, Bayes estimators), evaluating methods (mean squared error, best unbiased estimators, asymptotic evaluations), hypothesis testing, and confidence intervals.
DATA 200BP.prereq_text: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B.

DATA 200P.title: Data Science Career Seminar
DATA 200P.description: Covers one or more emerging topics in data science from industry professionals. The course content may vary.

DATA 210P.title: Statistical Methods I
DATA 210P.description: Statistical methods for analyzing data from multi-variable observational studies and experiments. Topics include model selection and model diagnostics for simple and multiple linear regression and generalized linear models.
DATA 210P.prereq_text: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B-. Required: Knowledge of basic statistics and linear algebra.

DATA 211P.title: Statistical Methods II
DATA 211P.description: Statistical methods for designing experiments, visualizing, and analyzing experimental and observational data using generalized regression models, multivariate analysis, and methods suitable for dependent data.
DATA 211P.prereq_text: DATA 210P with a minimum grade of B-.

DATA 220P.title: Databases and Data Management
DATA 220P.description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for managing and utilizing data. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational schema design, and use of SQL (Structured Query Language).

DATA 260P.title: Fundamentals of Algorithms in Data Science
DATA 260P.description: Covers fundamental concepts in the design and analysis of algorithms and is geared toward data science applications. Topics include greedy algorithms, deterministic and randomized graph algorithms, models of network flow, fundamental algorithmic techniques, and NP-completeness.

DATA 273P.title: Machine Learning and Data Mining
DATA 273P.description: Utilizing techniques from statistics, optimization, and computer science, machine learning and data mining algorithms empower automated systems to process and analyze large data sets swiftly, enabling them to make predictions or decisions without any need for human intervention.
DATA 273P.prereq_text: COMPSCI 271P with a minimum grade of B-. Required: Python Programming knowledge

DATA 275P.title: Machine Learning with Generative Models
DATA 275P.description: Introduction to statistical machine learning with probabilistic generative models. Studies efficient inference algorithms based on optimization-based variational methods, and simulation-based Monte Carlo methods. Several approaches to learning from data are covered, including conditional models for discriminative learning.
DATA 275P.prereq_text: COMPSCI 273P with a minimum grade of B and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B. Recommended: Python programming and advanced statistics experience.
DATA 275P.restriction: Master Of Data Science majors only.

DATA 280P.title: Data Science Career Seminar
DATA 280P.description: Covers one or more emerging topics in data science from industry professionals. Provides students with the opportunity to learn from experts in the data science industry through guest speaker presentations and Q&A sessions.

DATA 294P.title: Hypothesis and Project Development
DATA 294P.description: Supervised individual study on data science project development. Under instructor’s supervision, students either develop their own projects or undertake projects from industry which have potential to become their capstone projects for DATA 296P or DATA 297P.

DATA 295P.title: Special Topics in Data Science
DATA 295P.description: Covers one or more emerging topics in data science. Course content may vary.

DATA 296P.title: Capstone Writing and Communication
DATA 296P.description: Written and oral communication for data science careers. Production of a detailed document describing the design, methods, analytic strategy, interpretation, and conclusions as related to the concurrent capstone design and analysis class and refinement of written documents and oral communications.
DATA 296P.prereq_text: Required: Completion of at least 24 units in the Master of Data Science program.

DATA 297P.title: Capstone Design and Analysis
DATA 297P.description: Complete implementation of a data science analytic strategy for obtaining empirically-driven solutions to problems from science and industry. Focuses on the problem definition and analysis, data representation, algorithm selection, solution validation, and presentation of results.

DATA 298P.title: Curricular Practical Training
DATA 298P.description: Internship in which students work individually at an outside organization to gain experience with the challenges involved in data-related work.

DATA 299P.title: Individual Study
DATA 299P.description: Supervised individual study in data science.

DEV BIO 203A.description: Advanced study in areas not represented by formal courses. May involve individual or small group study through discussion, reading, and composition. Time and subject matter arranged individually.

DEV BIO 210.title: Developmental Genetics and Genomics
DEV BIO 210.description: Focuses on critical concepts in developmental genetics and genomics, emphasizing primary literature and new cutting edge approaches in genetic model organisms such as worms, flies, fish, and mice, with relevance for human genetics and disease.

DEV BIO 212.title: Topics in Systems Biology
DEV BIO 212.description: Studies in selected areas of Systems Biology.

DEV BIO 212A.title: Data Science Topics in Systems Biology
DEV BIO 212A.description: A journal club examining data science and machine learning applications in systems biology.

DEV BIO 214.title: Principles of Genomics
DEV BIO 214.description: A survey course of the principal subfields of genomics and their applications to biological and health sciences that covers genome assembly and annotation, genome structure, comparative genomics, population genomics, functional genomics, and medical genomics.

DEV BIO 220.title: Bioimaging and Spatial Biotechnology
DEV BIO 220.description: Theory, history, and application of light microscopy, electron microscopy, and spatial biotechniques. Principles of various microscopes, and discusses recent innovations in imaging techniques such as super-resolution microscopy, with an emphasis on practical imaging tips for research. Clinical applications also discussed.

DEV BIO 231B.title: Cell Biology
DEV BIO 231B.description: A broadly based course including topics in extracellular matrix, cytoskeleton, organelle biogenesis, receptor-mediated endocytosis, signal transduction, cell cycle, and developmental biology.

DEV BIO 232.title: Systems Cell and Developmental Biology
DEV BIO 232.description: Introduces concepts needed to understand cell and developmental biology at the systems level, i.e., how the parts (molecules) work together to create a complex output. Emphasis on using mathematical/computational modeling to expand/modify insights provided by intuition.

DEV BIO 245.title: Stem Cell Biology
DEV BIO 245.description: The basic characteristics and development roles of embryonic, adult, and cancer stem cells in the human body and in model systems and the use of experimental and genetic methods to analyze and manipulate their properties.

DEV BIO 290A.title: Colloquium in Developmental and Cell Biology
DEV BIO 290A.description: Contemporary research problems. Research students, faculty, and other invited speakers introduce research and review topics.

DRAMA 10.title: Introduction to Theatre
DRAMA 10.description: An interactive introduction to the world of theatre that serves to develop an appreciation of theatrical arts, to establish an awareness of landmarks within the performance history, and to create an understanding of the collaborative roles and departments that exist.

DRAMA 11.title: The Rock and Roll Spectacle Show
DRAMA 11.description: A thorough overview to the development and cultural significance of the Rock 'n' Roll Spectacle show. Focus on historical and recent developments of the spectacle show, trends in the aesthetics of the field, and various sub-genres.

DRAMA 12.title: Music Theatre Today
DRAMA 12.description: An interactive and thorough overview of 21st century music theatre. Develops an appreciation and awareness of the contemporary musical on stage today, current trends in the development of new music theatre work, and the art form’s global expansion.

DRAMA 13.title: Food, Film, Power
DRAMA 13.description: Food is the ambassador of cultures. The journey of food maps the history of human civilization. Examines feature films, documentaries, shorts, and writings on food, and analyzes the geopolitics, economics, migration, culture, performativity, and power of food.

DRAMA 14.title: Performing Rock 'N' Roll
DRAMA 14.description: Explores major movements in the history of rock 'n' roll in terms of performance, not virtuosity necessarily of the performers as musicians, rather as performances of aesthetics in modes of embodied ideology, iconoclastic spectacle, mixed media fashion, and subcultural formation.

DRAMA 15.title: Performance Now
DRAMA 15.description: Exposes students to what is most current in the world of performance and theatre. Begins with a series of lectures on the idea of performance, and the various theories that frame it.
DRAMA 15.restriction: Drama majors and Music Theatre majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 16.title: Performing Culture
DRAMA 16.description: Culture, aesthetics, and ideology (combined in the concept "subculture") work to fashion social identities. Using theories and methodologies of performance studies, with an emphasis on American culture, explores why and how culture is reinforced through performance.

DRAMA 20A.title: Culture in Performance
DRAMA 20A.description: A three-quarter foundation series exploring the rich depth of theatre, drama, and other genres of performance across a wide variety of worldwide forms, for performer and audience.

DRAMA 20B.title: Culture in Performance
DRAMA 20B.description: A three-quarter foundation series exploring the rich depth of theatre, drama, and other genres of performance across a wide variety of worldwide forms, for performer and audience.

DRAMA 20C.title: Culture in Performance
DRAMA 20C.description: A three-quarter foundation series exploring the rich depth of theatre, drama, and other genres of performance across a wide variety of worldwide forms, for performer and audience.

DRAMA 22.title: Applied Improvisation
DRAMA 22.description: An introduction to Applied Improvisation (AI), the improvisational mindset, the current trends and historic uses of AI, and concepts and techniques from improvised theatre that can help individuals achieve their goals beyond creating comedy.

DRAMA 30A.title: Acting
DRAMA 30A.description: Focuses on Stanislavski-based terminology and technique through theatre exercises and improvisation. The first part of a one-year series in basic acting technique and discipline.
DRAMA 30A.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 30B.title: Acting
DRAMA 30B.description: Focuses on scene work and character development. The second part of a one-year series in basic acting technique and discipline.
DRAMA 30B.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 30C.title: Acting
DRAMA 30C.description: Focuses on monologues, auditions, callbacks, and the profession of acting. The third part of a one-year series in basic acting technique and discipline.
DRAMA 30C.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 34.title: Movement for Actors
DRAMA 34.description: Fundamentals of stretch, strength, and alignment; exploring spatial awareness and physical control through mime isolations, techniques, and related improvisation.
DRAMA 34.prereq_text: ( DRAMA MAJORS ONLY OR MUSIC THEATRE MAJORS ONLY )
DRAMA 34.restriction: Drama majors and Music Theatre majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 35.title: Speech for the Theatre
DRAMA 35.description: An introductory course in voice and speech for actors, combining the body-based approach to voice developed by Fitzmaurice, and speech work of Knight and Thompson. Designed for the needs of actors and is not a public speaking course.
DRAMA 35.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors only.

DRAMA 40A.title: Development of Drama
DRAMA 40A.description: The development of Western Drama, concentrating on the drama’s intellectual, social, and artistic foundations. About 10 plays and supplementary critical material are read each quarter. Greek Drama through Shakespeare.
DRAMA 40A.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 40B.title: Development of Drama
DRAMA 40B.description: The development of Western Drama, concentrating on the drama’s intellectual, social, and artistic foundations. About 10 plays and supplementary critical material are read each quarter. Restoration Drama through Ibsen.
DRAMA 40B.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 40C.title: Development of Drama
DRAMA 40C.description: The development of Western Drama, concentrating on the drama’s intellectual, social, and artistic foundations. About 10 plays and supplementary material are read each quarter. Contemporary Drama. Post Naturalistic theatre.
DRAMA 40C.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

DRAMA 50A.title: Introduction to Costume Design
DRAMA 50A.description: Introduction to the process and procedures employed by the costume designer for the theatre. The elements of design are discussed in the context of character development, historical period, and style. Exercises extend to drawing, rendering, and investigation of human proportions.
DRAMA 50A.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors only.

DRAMA 50B.title: Introduction to Scenic Design
DRAMA 50B.description: Introduction to the principles and practice of scenic design. Weekly problems include research into various periods and styles of production with an emphasis on the conceptual idea. Perspective drawing, rendering, and model building are covered in studio exercises and assignments.
DRAMA 50B.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors only.

DRAMA 50C.title: Introduction to Lighting Design
DRAMA 50C.description: Introduction to the principles, theories, and equipment employed by the lighting designer for the stage. Areas of investigation include history, technology, and script analysis. Detailed studio attention is given to the theory and practice of design.
DRAMA 50C.restriction: Music Theatre majors, Drama majors, and Dance - Choreography majors only.

DRAMA 50D.title: Introduction to Sound Design
DRAMA 50D.description: Principles, theories, equipment use, and terminology employed by the sound designer for the stage. Areas of study include history, technology, and script analysis. Focuses on the theory and practice of design.
DRAMA 50D.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors only.

DRAMA 50E.title: Introduction to Stage Management
DRAMA 50E.description: A basic study of theatrical, dance, and opera stage management practices, forms, and methods, from first script reading to closing night. Opportunity to observe professionals at work in regional and touring situations as available.
DRAMA 50E.restriction: Music Theatre majors and Drama majors only.

DRAMA 50J.title: Introduction to Lighting and Sound Design
DRAMA 50J.description: Provides a thorough overview to the art and craft of theatrical lighting and sound design. Class time is roughly split between the two fields, and roughly split between technology and creativity.
DRAMA 50J.restriction: Drama majors and Music Theatre majors only.

DRAMA 50K.title: Introduction to Costume Design and Stage Management
DRAMA 50K.description: Provides a thorough overview to the art and craft of theatrical costume design and stage management. Class time is roughly split between the two fields, and roughly split between technology and creativity.
DRAMA 50K.restriction: Drama majors and Music Theatre majors only.

DRAMA 50L.title: Introduction to Scenic and Video Design
DRAMA 50L.description: Provides a thorough overview to the art and craft of theatrical scenic and projection design. Class time is roughly split between the two fields, and roughly split between technology and creativity.
DRAMA 50L.restriction: Drama majors and Music Theatre majors only.

DRAMA 60.title: Topics in Advanced Stage Management
DRAMA 60.description: Nurtures a greater appreciation for the stage manager and his or her process, and supports students who are interested in pursuing a career in professional stage management.

DRAMA 65.title: Music Theatre Workshop I
DRAMA 65.description: Basic vocal technique and characterization of musical theatre repertoire explored.

DRAMA 80.title: Directing I
DRAMA 80.description: Introduction to comprehensive directing process from pre-production to opening. Focus on fundamental skills: analysis, staging, action, actor coaching, and elements of design. Skills applied to scripted theatrical material. Develop a language for commenting on theatrical production. Attending and critiquing productions.

DRAMA 81.title: Laboratory for Creative Collaboration
DRAMA 81.description: Allows students to do immediate, hands-on creative work, while preparing them for a wide range of careers in arts and in arts-adjacent fields as well as in a wide variety of industries.
DRAMA 81.restriction: Drama majors and Music Theatre majors only.

DRAMA 100.title: University Theatre
DRAMA 100.description: Rehearsal and performance in a faculty-directed production.

DRAMA 101A.title: Theatre Production: Costume
DRAMA 101A.description: The production courses are offered to give students the opportunity to participate in departmental productions. Students engage in the production and construction of designed work as well as its applied execution during performance.
DRAMA 101A.restriction: May be taken for credit for a maximum of 24 units provided productions change.

DRAMA 101B.title: Theatre Production: Scenic
DRAMA 101B.description: The production courses are offered to give students the opportunity to participate in departmental productions. Students engage in the production and construction of designed work as well as its applied execution during performance.
DRAMA 101B.restriction: May be taken for credit for a maximum of 24 units provided productions change.

DRAMA 101C.title: Theatre Production: Lighting
DRAMA 101C.description: The production courses are offered to give students the opportunity to participate in departmental productions. Students engage in the production and construction of designed work as well as its applied execution during performance.
DRAMA 101C.restriction: May be taken for credit for a maximum of 24 units provided productions change.

DRAMA 101D.title: Theatre Production: Stage Management
