ECO EVO 237.description: Theory-based seminar tackles pressing issues in marine ecology, conservation, and restoration. Focuses on the science of marine ecosystems, resources and tools for their conservation, and management and the socioeconomic and policy dimensions.

ECO EVO 238.title: Chemical Ecology
ECO EVO 238.description: An introduction to the unspoken chemical language of nature. Emphasis on interactions between insects, plants, and microbes including plant defense, pollination, and microbial warfare.

ECO EVO 239.title: Animal Locomotion
ECO EVO 239.description: The physiology, biomechanics, and neuroscience that determines how animals propel themselves and navigate through the world. Considers the principles that govern the walking, running, flying, and swimming of animals, including exercising humans.
ECO EVO 239.prereq_text: Recommended: BIO SCI E109 or an introductory understanding of physiology.

ECO EVO 242.title: Comparative Animal Physiology
ECO EVO 242.description: Maintenance aspects of physiology: water balance; feeding and digestion; metabolism; respiration and circulation.

ECO EVO 246.title: Seminar in Ecology and Evolution Education
ECO EVO 246.description: Weekly discussion of teaching techniques and challenges that are specific to courses in ecology and evolutionary biology. Emphasis will be on using evidence-based pedagogy techniques. There will be a combination of readings, group discussions and speakers.

ECO EVO 247.title: Behavioral Endocrinology
ECO EVO 247.description: Comparative examination of the major hormone systems that regulate behavior across animals. Emphasizes the reciprocating nature of hormone-behavior interactions and seeks to understand how natural selection drives the evolution of hormone structure and function.

ECO EVO 253.title: Functional and Structural Evolutionary Genomics
ECO EVO 253.description: Function and organization of genomes analyzed from an evolutionary perspective. Review of some of the most recent experimental approaches in genome analysis and comparative genomics. Relevant software to analyze DNA and expression data is used.

ECO EVO 261.title: Advanced Quantitative Methods
ECO EVO 261.description: Covers advanced analytical techniques used by conservation biologists. Methods include generalized linear models, community analysis using multivariate analyses, analysis of spatial/GIS data using R, time-series analysis, and meta-analysis.

ECO EVO 262.title: Professional Workshop
ECO EVO 262.description: Identify and attend professional or technical skill workshops to gain professional knowledge and certifications related to conservation and restoration science.

ECO EVO 264.title: Conservation Biology
ECO EVO 264.description: Explores concepts in ecology with potential for conserving biological diversity. Identifies creative applications of ecological research that mitigate impacts of rapid human population growth and habitat destruction on biodiversity.

ECO EVO 265.title: Restoration Ecology
ECO EVO 265.description: Study of principles and practices that help recover degraded ecosystems including restoration in different ecological systems, restoration motives and intensities, implementation and monitoring, and scope and success of case studies.

ECO EVO 266L.title: Field Methods in Restoration
ECO EVO 266L.description: Laboratory experience performing field methods that help recover degraded ecosystems in different ecological systems. Emphasis on the plant community composition, soil, irrigation, maintenance, and monitoring of a project.

ECO EVO 267.title: Science Communication
ECO EVO 267.description: Develops students' abilities to convey information related to conservation and restoration in a way that has broad appeal and/or effective messaging for non-scientific audiences by assessing the audience, developing effective storytelling, and deploying a persuasive information campaign.

ECO EVO 268.title: Technical Writing
ECO EVO 268.description: Practice developing key documents for restoration projects including a response to a request for proposal (RFP), a restoration project plan, and a monitoring and maintenance plan.

ECO EVO 269.title: Project Management
ECO EVO 269.description: Discover the planning, design, implementation, and aftercare phases of managing a conservation or restoration project. Students will project cost, manage risk, analyze sites, evaluate and review projects, and become familiar with common permitting and consultation requirements.

ECO EVO 270.title: GIS for Environmental Science
ECO EVO 270.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of GIS. Topics include cartography, creating/editing GIS data, georeferencing, map projections, geospatial analysis, spatial statistics, and development of GIS models. Focuses on theory and practice.

ECO EVO 270B.title: Advanced GIS for Environmental Science
ECO EVO 270B.description: Introduces the advance functions of Geographic Information Systems (GIS), including hic principles, and explores database mapping, computer-assisted analysis of spatial data, computer-aided map design, and the production of computer-generated maps.

ECO EVO 271.title: Marine Research and Conservation Methods
ECO EVO 271.description: Field-based introduction to marine ecology and conservation management through the study of the ecology, resource management, and conservation of marine habitats and species, and the use of a variety of marine field research methods.

ECO EVO 275.title: Wildlife Ecology and Sampling
ECO EVO 275.description: Field-based introduction to wildlife management through the study of the ecology, physiology, population biology management, and conservation of vertebrate wildlife species, and the use of a variety of different wildlife sampling techniques.

ECO EVO 276.title: Environmental Education and Outreach
ECO EVO 276.description: Prepares students to develop tailored education programs for conservation and restoration projects. Students engage in activities that foster innovative approaches and solutions to different education and outreach needs for conservation and restoration projects.

ECO EVO 278.title: Evolution and Conservation
ECO EVO 278.description: Examines evolution applications to conservation biology in three parts: processes of evolution within populations, conservation of species, and assessing evolutionary responses to environmental change.

ECO EVO 279.title: Site Development
ECO EVO 279.description: Students learn about plan review and the permitting processes as they relate to site development. Explores how a site is developed from application to building permits, and all the steps in between.

ECO EVO 282.title: Fundamentals of Informatics for Biologists
ECO EVO 282.description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics and the unix operating system.

ECO EVO 283.title: Advanced Informatics for Biologists
ECO EVO 283.description: Students learn advanced informatics including the analysis of: Poolseq, RNAseq, ATACseq, and ChiPseq datasets using programs such as bwa, tophat, cufflinks, DEseq, Trinity, Agustus, etc., in a unix high-performance computing environment. Statistical tests carried out and publication quality.
ECO EVO 283.prereq_text: ECO EVO 282 with a minimum grade of B-.

ECO EVO 286.title: MCRS Capstone
ECO EVO 286.description: Apply knowledge and skills in a practical professional setting, working with practitioners to identify a conservation or management problem and then to plan, implement, and evaluate a solution.

ECO EVO 289.title: Evolution
ECO EVO 289.description: An integrative treatment of evolutionary biology that covers evolutionary processes basic research methods, and the history of life.

ECON 1.title: Introduction to Economics
ECON 1.description: An analysis of the problems society faces in organizing itself to provide goods and services. How decisions of government, business, and the individual relate to current economic problems such as unemployment, inflation, poverty, and environmental pollution.

and.not: AP ECONOMICS:MICRO score of 4 or greater
AP ECONOMICS:MACRO score of 4 or greater

ECON 1.prereq_text: NO AP ECONOMICS:MICRO score of 4 or greater AND NO AP ECONOMICS:MACRO score of 4 or greater
ECON 1.restriction: No Economics majors. No AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4. No AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4.

ECON 11.title: The Internet and Public Policy
ECON 11.description: How the Internet works. Current public policy issues concerning the Internet. Introductory economics. Communications law. Interactions between information technology, economics, and law. Case studies about Internet and communications policy.

ECON 12.title: Federal Reserve: Past, Present, and Future
ECON 12.description: Studies central banking in the United States from colonial times to the present. Focuses on the past, present, and future of the Federal Reserve and precursors to that system, which was established in 1913.

ECON 13.title: Global Economy
ECON 13.description: Acquaints students with the fundamental patterns of the global economy. Emphasizes the historical roots and political implications of economic choices.
ECON 13.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, International Studies majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 15.title: Probability and Statistics for Economics
ECON 15.description: Introduces basic probability and statistics for econometrics. Knowing and understanding the details of statistics, statistical test, and conclusions about the test results. Problem sets provide practical experience on actual economic data using statistical packages.
ECON 15.prereq_text: MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 3 and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4).
ECON 15.restriction: Economics majors, Business Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 15A.title: Probability and Statistics in Economics I
ECON 15A.description: An introduction to probability, statistics, and econometrics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Examples from economics.
ECON 15A.prereq_text: MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 3 and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4).
ECON 15A.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 15B.title: Probability and Statistics in Economics II
ECON 15B.description: An introduction to probability, statistics, and econometrics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Examples from economics.
ECON 15B.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 17.title: An Economic Approach to Religion
ECON 17.description: Introduction to how basic economic concepts such as demand, supply, consumption, production, competition, free-riding, innovation, regulation, and rent-seeking can be applied to understand observed religious behavior.

ECON 20A.title: Basic Economics I
ECON 20A.description: The fundamentals of microeconomics. The behavior of firms and consumers: markets, supply/demand, utility maximization, resource allocation, and efficiency.

and.not: AP ECONOMICS:MICRO score of 4 or greater

ECON 20A.prereq_text: NO AP ECONOMICS:MICRO score of 4 or greater AND NO MGMT 4A AND NO ECON 23
ECON 20A.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, Business Economics majors, Business Information Management majors, and Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4A may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20A.

ECON 20B.title: Basic Economics II
ECON 20B.description: The fundamentals of macroeconomics. Government behavior: monetary and fiscal policy, inflation, and unemployment. Effective fall 2006, the content of Economics 20B is macroeconomics. This course cannot be taken to repeat Economics 20B taken prior to fall 2006.

and.not: AP ECONOMICS:MACRO score of 4 or greater

ECON 20B.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) or ECON 13 or ECON 23.
ECON 20B.restriction: Business Information Management majors, Business Economics majors, Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, Environmental Engineering majors, International Studies majors, and Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4B may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20B.

ECON 23.title: Basic Economics for Engineers
ECON 23.description: The fundamentals of microeconomics. The behavior of firms and of consumers: markets, supply/demand, utility maximization, resource allocation, and efficiency.
ECON 23.prereq_text: ( ENGINEERING MAJORS ONLY OR CIVIL ENGINEERING MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL ENGR MAJORS ONLY OR MECHANICAL ENGR MAJORS ONLY OR AEROSPACE ENGR MAJORS ONLY ) AND NO ECON 20A
ECON 23.restriction: Engineering majors, Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors only.

ECON 25.title: The Economics of Accounting Decisions
ECON 25.description: Introduction to accounting concepts and principles, including the accounting model and accounting style, transaction analysis, and preparation of financial statements. An analysis of the similarities and differences between accounting and economic concepts (e.g., value, profits).
ECON 25.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON H80.title: Learning Economics Through Sports
ECON H80.description: Introduces students to a selection of research topics in economics and other social sciences, using sports as laboratories and as sources of exceptionally-detailed data. Topics include labor markets, psychological biases and social forces, the adoption of innovations.

ECON 100A.title: Intermediate Economics I
ECON 100A.description: Determinants of supply and demand; operation of competitive and monopolistic markets; imperfections of the market system, explanations of unemployment, inflation, recessions; public policy for macroeconomic problems.
ECON 100A.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) and (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4) and (MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 4) and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4).
ECON 100A.restriction: Business Economics majors and Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Quantitative Economics majors.

ECON 100B.title: Intermediate Economic II
ECON 100B.description: Determinants of supply and demand; operation of competitive and monopolistic markets; imperfections of the market system, explanations of unemployment, inflation, recessions; public policy for macroeconomic problems.
ECON 100B.restriction: Business Economics majors and Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Quantitative Economics majors.

ECON 100C.title: Intermediate Economics III
ECON 100C.description: Determinants of supply and demand; operation of competitive and monopolistic markets; imperfections of the market system, explanations of unemployment, inflation, recessions; public policy for macroeconomic problems.
ECON 100C.restriction: Business Economics majors and Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Quantitative Economics majors.

ECON 105A.title: Intermediate Quantitative Economics I
ECON 105A.description: An advanced and mathematical version of ECON 100A for students in the Quantitative Economics major.
ECON 105A.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) and (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4) and (MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 4) and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and MATH 3A.
ECON 105A.restriction: Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Business Economics majors and No Economics majors.

ECON 105B.title: Intermediate Quantitative Economics II
ECON 105B.description: An advanced and mathematical version of ECON 100B for students in the Quantitative Economics major.
ECON 105B.restriction: Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Business Economics majors and No Economics majors.

ECON 105C.title: Intermediate Quantitative Economics III
ECON 105C.description: An advanced and mathematical version of ECON 100C for students in the Quantitative Economics major.
ECON 105C.restriction: Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Business Economics majors and No Economics majors.

ECON 107.title: Economics of Asymmetric Information
ECON 107.description: Focuses on the effects of asymmetric information in the markets for traditional economic goods and resources, such as labor, insurance, used cars, credit, and in auctions and bargaining problems. Prerequisite:
ECON 107.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 113.title: Game Theory of Human Cooperation and Morality
ECON 113.description: Teaches how game theory is used to understand human cooperation and morality. Covers basic game-theoretic concepts and analysis, how they illuminate what it means to be moral, and how prosocial human dispositions evolved.
ECON 113.prereq_text: (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or STATS 120B or MATH 130B) and (ECON 100A or ECON 105A).
ECON 113.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors only.

ECON 115.title: Behaviorial Economics
ECON 115.description: Studies the behavioral and psychological biases in economics settings. Both individual decisions and games are discussed.
ECON 115.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) and (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4).
ECON 115.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 116.title: Game Theory
ECON 116.description: Extensive form games with perfect information and coalitional games. The key solution concepts are Nash Equilibrium, Backward Induction, and the Core. Substantive examples include public good production, oligopoly, electoral competition, auctions, holdup, market entry, and voting.
ECON 116.prereq_text: (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or STATS 120B or MATH 130B) and (ECON 100A or ECON 105A).
ECON 116.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 122A.title: Applied Econometrics I
ECON 122A.description: Introduction to econometrics emphasizing practical applications in microeconomics and macroeconomics.
ECON 122A.prereq_text: ECON 100A or ECON 105A and (ECON 15A or ECON 15B or ECON 15 or MATH 130B or MATH 133A or STATS 120C).
ECON 122A.restriction: Business Economics majors and Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Quantitative Economics majors.

ECON 122B.title: Applied Econometrics II
ECON 122B.description: Introduction to econometrics emphasizing practical applications in microeconomics and macroeconomics.
ECON 122B.restriction: Business Economics majors and Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Quantitative Economics majors.

ECON 122CW.title: Data Analysis Writing
ECON 122CW.description: Research writing course in econometrics focusing on individual research projects. Students employ econometric analysis to address an economic question in a 20-page paper and present their findings to the class in a short presentation.
ECON 122CW.prereq_text: ECON 122A and ECON 122B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ECON 122CW.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 123A.title: Econometrics I
ECON 123A.description: Specification, estimation, and testing of econometric models. Applications in various areas of microeconomics and macroeconomics.
ECON 123A.prereq_text: (MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 4 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3) and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and MATH 3A and (STATS 120C or MATH 130C) and (ECON 100A and ECON 100B and ECON 100C) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B and ECON 105C).
ECON 123A.restriction: Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Business Economics majors and No Economics majors.

ECON 123B.title: Econometrics II
ECON 123B.description: Specification, estimation, and testing of econometric models. Applications in various areas of microeconomics and macroeconomics.
ECON 123B.restriction: Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment. No Business Economics majors and No Economics majors.

ECON 123CW.title: Econometrics III
ECON 123CW.description: Seminar course in which students do an original econometric research project.
ECON 123CW.prereq_text: ECON 123B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ECON 123CW.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 125.title: Business Forecasting
ECON 125.description: Students learn how to produce forecasts of the behavior of economic (and other) variables. The techniques examined are linear regression, nonlinear regression, and nonparametric kernel regression; AR, MA, ARMA, ARIMA, and Box-Jenkins.
ECON 125.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 126.title: Computational Macroeconomics
ECON 126.description: Introduction to the computational methods for studying economic growth and the business cycle. Students learn how to write computer programs to simulate macroeconomic models, download and manage data from internet resources, and to do basic statistics.
ECON 126.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors only.

ECON 127.title: Experimental Economics
ECON 127.description: Learn what constitutes proper experimental design and what laboratory experiments teach us about human behavior and the economy. Students participate in a sample experiment, evaluate the results, and discuss experiment design and larger issues. Formerly ECON 117.

ECON 127W.title: The Economics of Opportunity
ECON 127W.description: Examines factors that allow individuals to improve their economic situation regardless of their family’s economic circumstances during childhood. Covers various topics including neighborhoods, housing, education, healthcare, labor markets, and the criminal justice system.
ECON 127W.prereq_text: (ECON 122A or ECON 123A) and (ECON 100A or ECON 105A) and (ECON 100B or ECON 105B) and (ECON 100C or ECON 105C). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ECON 128.title: Machine Learning for Economists
ECON 128.description: Develops the theory and computation of recent methods at the intersection of econometrics and machine learning as used in economics and business. Building on intermediate econometrics, it introduces causal random forests, double machine learning, and neural networks.
ECON 128.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors only.

ECON 129.title: Special Topics in Quantitative Methods
ECON 129.description: Studies in selected areas of Quantitative Methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ECON 129.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 131A.title: The Economics of Risk and Uncertainty
ECON 131A.description: The theory of insurance and joint-ownership of risky enterprises; optimal procedures for the allocation of uncertain payoffs.
ECON 131A.prereq_text: (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or MATH 130B or STATS 120B) and (ECON 100B or ECON 105B).
ECON 131A.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 132A.title: Introduction to Financial Investments
ECON 132A.description: Modern theories of investment and their application to the study of financial markets. The relation between risk and return, diversification, asset pricing, efficient markets hypothesis, and the market valuation of stocks, bonds, options, and futures.
ECON 132A.prereq_text: (ECON 122A or ECON 123A) and (ECON 100A and ECON 100B and ECON 100C) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B and ECON 105C) or (MATH 130A and STATS 120A and STATS 120B and STATS 120C) or MATH 130B or MATH 133A.
ECON 132A.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 133.title: Markets and Networks
ECON 133.description: Introduction into network effects in economic settings, such as auctions, markets, and bargaining. Networks are also important in information diffusion, aggregation, and search. Some applications refer to traffic and epidemics.
ECON 133.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 134A.title: Corporate Finance
ECON 134A.description: Provides an overview of the modern theory and practice of corporate finance and focuses on two fundamental financial decisions; investment as well as financing. Beginning with discounted cash flow analysis, basic theory will be applied to the valuation of stocks.
ECON 134A.prereq_text: (ECON 100A and ECON 100B and ECON 100C) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B and ECON 105C) and (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or MATH 130B or STATS 120B).
ECON 134A.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 134B.title: Corporate Finance II
ECON 134B.description: Advanced material in corporate finance. How to value companies, debt and equity financing, capital structure, IPOs, venture capital, private equity, and mergers and acquisitions. Applies knowledge through cases and real-life examples.
ECON 134B.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 135.title: Mathematics of Finance
ECON 135.description: After reviewing tools from probability, statistics, and elementary differential and partial differential equations, concepts such as hedging, arbitrage, Puts, Calls, the design of portfolios, the derivation and solution of the Blac-Scholes, and other equations are discussed.
ECON 135.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, Mathematics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 137W.title: Financial Markets and the Macroeconomy
ECON 137W.description: Students are required to write a paper on a research question related to financial markets and their interactions with the macroeconomic and political environment.
ECON 137W.prereq_text: ECON 122A or ECON 123A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ECON 139.title: Special Topics in Financial Economics
ECON 139.description: Studies in selected areas of Financial Economics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ECON 139.prereq_text: MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4 and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4). Prerequisites vary.
ECON 139.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 140.title: Managerial Economics
ECON 140.description: A collection of concepts and methods for effective decision making. Explores how the tools of microeconomics, including game theory and industrial organization theory, can be used to make better managerial decisions, particularly those involving allocation of resources within firms.
ECON 140.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 140E.title: Health Economics
ECON 140E.description: Builds off of economic theory to explore topics in health economics including health care demand, health insurance markets, the supply of health care, and examine health care policy.
ECON 140E.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 141D.title: Public Economics and Development
ECON 141D.description: Covers three topics of great relevance to governments in low-income countries: education, social insurance, and tax evasion. Through the lens of these topics, the basic questions of Public Economics, using theory and empirical evidence, are addressed.
ECON 141D.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors only.

ECON 142A.title: Industrial Organization I
ECON 142A.description: The theory of market structure. Imperfect markets, government policies, and industry performance.
ECON 142A.prereq_text: (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or STATS 120B or MATH 130B) and (ECON 100A and ECON 100B) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B).
ECON 142A.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 142CW.title: Industrial Organization III
ECON 142CW.description: Research in industrial organization. Imperfect competition, antitrust, and regulation.
ECON 142CW.prereq_text: (ECON 100A and ECON 100B) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ECON 142CW.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 144A.title: Urban Economics I
ECON 144A.description: Why cities exist, economics of urban land-use, housing demand and tenure choice, traffic congestion.
ECON 144A.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) and (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4). Recommended: ECON 100A.
ECON 144A.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 144B.title: Urban Economics II
ECON 144B.description: Housing policy analysis, urban public goods and services, crime, pollution, urban amenities.
ECON 144B.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) and (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4). Recommended: ECON 100A.
ECON 144B.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 145E.title: Economics of the Environment
ECON 145E.description: Surveys economic aspects of natural resources, pollution, population, and the environment. Examines the causes of pollution; analysis of public policies regarding these problems. Emphasis on microeconomic aspects of environmental problems.
ECON 145E.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 145FW.title: Economics of the Environment II
ECON 145FW.description: Applications of tools covered in ECON 145E to topics in environmental economics. Emphasis on independent research papers. Syllabus and classes include writing technique and use cutting-edge research papers as a base for developing effective reading, writing, and research skills.
ECON 145FW.prereq_text: (ECON 15A or STATS 120A or MATH 130A) and (ECON 15B or STATS 120B or MATH 130B) and (ECON 122A or ECON 123A) and (ECON 100A or ECON 105A) and (ECON 100B or ECON 105B) and (ECON 100C or ECON 105C). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ECON 145FW.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 145L.title: Economics of Law
ECON 145L.description: Examination of several economic concepts which are useful in understanding legal rules: externalities, the assignment of property rights, and Coase's theorem. Examples are drawn from the fields of pollution control, no-fault insurance, medical malpractice, and product liability.
ECON 145L.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 146A.title: Illegal Economics
ECON 146A.description: How illegal firms function in illegal markets, why individuals participate in these groups and markets, and what federal, state, and local governments do to disrupt organized illegal activity.
ECON 146A.restriction: Business Economics majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 146B.title: Economics of Criminal Justice
ECON 146B.description: Provides an introduction to the economics of crime literature.
ECON 146B.restriction: Business Economics majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 146D.title: Conflict and Economics
ECON 146D.description: Applies the tools of economics to study the causes and consequences of violent conflict (e.g., wars between nations, civil wars, and crime) and more refined forms of conflict (e.g., lobbying and litigation).
ECON 146D.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 147B.title: Economics of Strategy
ECON 147B.description: Uses tools of economics, game theory in particular, to develop an understanding of business decision-making. Deals with questions such as how the firm decides what kind of business to be in, how large should it be, and others.
ECON 147B.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 148.title: Business Decisions
ECON 148.description: Surveys normative and descriptive models of decision-making behavior, with an emphasis on organizational and policy contexts. Topics include rational choice theory, biases and heuristics, framing effects, and overconfidence. Management fads, panics, and herd behavior are also discussed.
ECON 148.prereq_text: (ANTHRO 10A and ANTHRO 10B and ANTHRO 10C) or (SOCIOL 10A and SOCIOL 10B and SOCIOL 10C) or (SOC SCI 10A and SOC SCI 10B and SOC SCI 10C) or (MATH 2A and MATH 2B and (STATS 7 or MGMT 7) or (STATS 120A and STATS 120B and STATS 120C) or (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or MATH 130B).
ECON 148.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 149.title: Special Topics in Economics of Public and Private Organizations
ECON 149.description: Studies in selected areas of Economics of Public and Private Organizations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ECON 149.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 151A.title: Labor Economics and Human Resources I
ECON 151A.description: Labor demand, labor supply, human capital, personnel economics, and other topics.
ECON 151A.prereq_text: (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or STATS 120B or MATH 130B) and (ECON 100A and ECON 100B) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B).
ECON 151A.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 151B.title: Labor Economics and Human Resources II
ECON 151B.description: Labor market discrimination, compensating wage differentials, immigration, and other topics.
ECON 151B.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 152A.title: Economic Anthropology
ECON 152A.description: Economic systems in comparative perspective: production, distribution, and consumption in market and non-market societies; agricultural development in the third world.
ECON 152A.prereq_text: One course in general science, anthropology, economics, geography, or sociology.
ECON 152A.restriction: Anthropology majors, Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors only.

ECON 153W.title: Political Institutions, Legal Systems, and Economic Development
ECON 153W.description: Studies a variety of empirical papers analyzing how institutions affect economic development. The topics include cross-country studies of institutions as well as narrower topics such as corruption, regulation of entry, political connections, and pork barrel politics.
ECON 153W.prereq_text: (ECON 100A or ECON 105A) and (ECON 100B or ECON 105B) and (ECON 100C or ECON 105C) and (ECON 122A or ECON 123A). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ECON 154.title: Voting and Political Manipulation
ECON 154.description: Introduction to social choice and cooperative games. Topics include majority rule, types of voting methods, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.
ECON 154.restriction: Business Economics majors, Political Science majors, International Studies majors, and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 155.title: Current Issues in Political Economy
ECON 155.description: Political economy seeks explanations that combine insights from both economics and politics. Topics include the interaction of government and markets, the causes of the Great Recession, and the sources of income and wealth inequality.
ECON 155.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) or (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4) or ECON 13 or INTL ST 13.

ECON 157.title: Economic Development
ECON 157.description: Considers the process of economic development across the globe and why some countries are rich and others poor. Discusses the major problems facing developing countries, such as population growth, education, capital formation, environmental protection, and international trade.
ECON 157.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) and (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4).
ECON 157.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 161A.title: Money and Banking
ECON 161A.description: Basic elements of money and banking: institutional features and economics of financial markets and, in particular, the U.S. banking system; determinants of interest rates; the Federal Reserve and its role in money supply; effects of money on output and inflation.
ECON 161A.prereq_text: (ECON 100A and ECON 100B) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B) and (ECON 100C or ECON 105C).
ECON 161A.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 161B.title: International Money
ECON 161B.description: Open economy macroeconomics and determination of exchange rates. Asset-market approach to the balance of payments. Internal and external balance in the economy. Macroeconomic policies under fixed and floating exchange rates. The international monetary system and institutions.
ECON 161B.prereq_text: (ECON 100A and ECON 100B) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B) and (ECON 100C or ECON 105C).
ECON 161B.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 161D.title: Advanced Money and Banking
ECON 161D.description: Studies business cycles in the United States during the last century. The first portion of the course reviews the theoretical models employed to study economic fluctuations and empirical methods used to measure fluctuations.
ECON 161D.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 162.title: Poverty, Growth, and Development
ECON 162.description: Examines India as a case study for each of the topics studied: growth experience of India along with its poverty eradication record, aspects of poverty, and the policies that have been undertaken to tackle poverty.
ECON 162.prereq_text: (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or STATS 120B) and (ECON 100A and ECON 100B and ECON 100C) or (ECON 105A and ECON 105B and ECON 105C).

ECON 163.title: Poverty and Inequality
ECON 163.description: Examines the measurement, causes, consequences, and correlates of poverty and inequality in the United States. Topics include the roles of public policy responses through income taxes, transfers, and direct labor-market interventions, family structure and neighborhoods.
ECON 163.prereq_text: (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or STATS 120B or MATH 130B) and (ECON 100A or ECON 105A).
ECON 163.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 164AW.title: The Industrial Revolution in Western Europe
ECON 164AW.description: How do economists explain the process of economic development during the past three centuries? Has the process of industrialization affected living standards? Focusing on these questions, students learn how to apply economic theory and quantitative methods.
ECON 164AW.prereq_text: ECON 100C or ECON 105C. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ECON 164AW.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 164C.title: American Economic History from Colonization to the Present
ECON 164C.description: Examines how the American economy evolved from colonization to the post-war era. Topics include relations with foreign countries, the emergence of manufacturing and big business, railroads, slavery, war, the Great Depression, the rise of fiscal and monetary policies.
ECON 164C.prereq_text: (ECON 20A or AP Economics Micro with a minimum score of 4) and (ECON 20B or AP Economics Macro with a minimum score of 4).

ECON 165.title: Economics of International Business
ECON 165.description: Students learn to understand and analyze the principal economic issues in the international business arena. Covers topics such as trade theory, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange market, and strategy of international business.
ECON 165.prereq_text: ECON 100C (may be taken concurrently) or ECON 105C (may be taken concurrently).

ECON 166.title: Development Economics
ECON 166.description: Uses theory and empirics to understand the economies of low- and middle-income countries. Explores the concept, determinants, and consequences of economic growth, drawing on historical and cross-country evidence. Topics include poverty, inequality, agriculture, demography, and strategies of risk management.
ECON 166.prereq_text: (ECON 122A or ECON 123A) and (ECON 100A or ECON 105A) and (ECON 100B or ECON 105B) and (ECON 100C or ECON 105C).
ECON 166.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 167.title: International Trade and Commercial Policy
ECON 167.description: Determination of trade flows and the relative prices. Gains from trade, the terms of trade, and income distribution. Imperfect competition and international trade. The effect of tariffs, export subsidies, and import quotas. The effects of free and restricted trade.
ECON 167.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 169.title: Special Topics in Development Economics
ECON 169.description: Studies in selected areas of Development Economics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
ECON 169.restriction: Economics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Business Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ECON 190.title: Senior Thesis
ECON 190.description: Students work with faculty to complete their honors thesis.

ECON 190BW.title: Economics Honors Colloquium II
ECON 190BW.description: Colloquium required for honors students in Economics, Quantitative Economics, and Business Economics. Introduces students to independent research and helps students plan a research program. Students complete their thesis.
ECON 190BW.prereq_text: ECON H190A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ECON H190A.title: Economics Honors Colloquium I
ECON H190A.description: Colloquium required for honors students in economics, quantitative economics, and business economics. Introduces students to independent research. Helps students plan a research program. Prepares students for thesis writing.
ECON H190A.prereq_text: ECON 122A or ECON 123A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ECON 200A.title: Graduate Colloquium for Economics I
ECON 200A.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors. Supplemented by class discussion of these presentations and other material on current research methodology.

ECON 200B.title: Graduate Colloquium for Economics II
ECON 200B.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors. Supplemented by class discussion of these presentations and other material on current research methodology.
ECON 200B.prereq_text: ECON 200A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 200C.title: Graduate Colloquium for Economics III
ECON 200C.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors. Supplemented by class discussion of these presentations and other material on current research methodology.
ECON 200C.prereq_text: ECON 200B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 203A.title: Mathematics for Economists
ECON 203A.description: Gives students the mathematical background required for graduate work in economics. Topics covered include multivariate calculus, differential equations, and linear algebra.

ECON 210A.title: Microeconomic Theory I
ECON 210A.description: Theoretical microeconomics. Emphasis on the meaning and empirical interpretation of theoretical models. Topics include theory of the firm, theory of the market, theory of the consumer, duality theory, application to econometrics, general equilibrium and welfare economics, uncertainty, game theory.

ECON 210B.title: Microeconomic Theory II
ECON 210B.description: Theoretical microeconomics. Emphasis on the meaning and empirical interpretation of theoretical models. Topics include theory of the firm, theory of the market, theory of the consumer, duality theory, application to econometrics, general equilibrium and welfare economics, uncertainty, game theory.
ECON 210B.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 210C.title: Microeconomic Theory III
ECON 210C.description: Theoretical microeconomics. Emphasis on the meaning and empirical interpretation of theoretical models. Topics include theory of the firm, theory of the market, theory of the consumer, duality theory, application to econometrics, general equilibrium and welfare economics, uncertainty, game theory.
ECON 210C.prereq_text: ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 210D.title: Macroeconomic Theory I
ECON 210D.description: Advanced macroeconomic theory including alternative macroeconomic models, microeconomic foundations of macroeconomics, investment and growth theory, inflation and unemployment, rational expectations and macroeconomic policy, wealth effects, crowding out and fiscal policy, money and interest, open economy models.

ECON 210E.title: Macroeconomic Theory II
ECON 210E.description: Advanced macroeconomic theory including alternative macroeconomic models, microeconomic foundations of macroeconomics, investment and growth theory, inflation and unemployment, rational expectations and macroeconomic policy, wealth effects, crowding out and fiscal policy, money and interest, open economy models.
ECON 210E.prereq_text: ECON 210D with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 210F.title: Macroeconomic Theory III
ECON 210F.description: Advanced macroeconomic theory including alternative macroeconomic models, microeconomic foundations of macroeconomics, investment and growth theory, inflation and unemployment, rational expectations and macroeconomic policy, wealth effects, crowding out and fiscal policy, money and interest, open economy models.
ECON 210F.prereq_text: ECON 210E with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 211L.title: Macroeconomics Theory II Lab
ECON 211L.description: Overview of stochastic processes; introduction to dynamic programming; two equilibrium concepts; Ricardian equivalence; real business cycle model; complete versus incomplete markets; asset pricing and the equity premium puzzle.

ECON 220A.title: Statistics and Econometrics I
ECON 220A.description: Takes up where ECON 202 leaves off. Continuing in the likelihood perspective, begins with Bayesian point estimation and then covers interval estimation and hypothesis testing from both frequentist and Bayesian perspectives.

ECON 220B.title: Statistics and Econometrics II
ECON 220B.description: Begins by relaxing the ideal conditions of the standard regression model. Potential topics include kernel density estimation, instrumental variables (IV), two stage least squares (2SLS), panel data models, and simulation-based Bayesian methods, including Gibbs sampling, and the bootstrap.
ECON 220B.prereq_text: ECON 220A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 220C.title: Statistics and Econometrics III
ECON 220C.description: Covers econometric time series, discrete choice and count models, sample selection, and duration models along with Bayesian and classical asymptotic methods.
ECON 220C.prereq_text: ECON 220B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 221A.title: Statistics and Econometrics Laboratory I
ECON 221A.description: Discussion of problems in statistics and econometrics, and their relationships to statistical and econometrics theory. Instruction in the use of computers for applied econometric work.

ECON 221B.title: Statistics and Econometrics Laboratory II
ECON 221B.description: Discussion of problems in statistics and econometrics, and their relationships to statistical and econometrics theory. Instruction in the use of computers for applied econometric work.

ECON 221C.title: Statistics and Econometrics Laboratory III
ECON 221C.description: Discussion of problems in statistics and econometrics, and their relationships to statistical and econometrics theory. Instruction in the use of computers for applied econometric work.

ECON 227A.title: Experimental Econ I
ECON 227A.description: An introduction to experimental social science. Students learn experimental methodology, design, and analysis, and be exposed to active research areas. Each student writes a proposal for their own experiment and presents the design in class.

ECON 227B.title: Experimental Econ II
ECON 227B.description: Focuses on implementing experimental projects in a laboratory environment. Subjects learn about human subjects protection, program experimental software for their own projects, and conduct live experiment sessions.

ECON 229.title: Special Topics in Econometrics
ECON 229.description: Studies in selected areas of Econometrics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ECON 232.title: Business Cycles in Historical Perspective
ECON 232.description: Investigates business cycles in the United States and worldwide during the last two centuries. Topics include causes and consequences of business fluctuations, monetary and fiscal policy, models of fluctuations, and empirical macroeconomics.
ECON 232.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210D with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210E with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210F with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 235.title: Health and Development in Historical Perspective
ECON 235.description: Investigates the evolution of population health over time and across the development process. Examines how the environment, nutrition, public health systems, and medical innovations have influenced health and demographic behavior. Also explores the interplay between health capital and economic growth.
ECON 235.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 220A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 220B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 239.title: Special Topics in Financial Economics
ECON 239.description: Studies in selected areas of Financial Economics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ECON 241A.title: Industrial Organization I
ECON 241A.description: Analysis of the structure and economic performance of markets, and the impact of public policy and their efficiency and equity. Effects of information structure. Oligopoly, cartels, mergers, vertical integration, patents, innovation, antitrust, and regulation.
ECON 241A.prereq_text: ECON 100B and ECON 203A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 241B.title: Industrial Organization II
ECON 241B.description: Analysis of the structure and economic performance of markets, and the impact of public policy and their efficiency and equity. Effects of information structure. Price flexibility and dispersion, auctions, search and industrial structure, intrafirm organization.
ECON 241B.prereq_text: ECON 241A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 100B and ECON 203A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 242.title: Development Economics
ECON 242.description: Uses theory and empirics to understand the economies of low- and middle-income countries. Explores the concept, determinants, and consequences of economic growth, drawing on historical and cross-country evidence. Topics include poverty, inequality, agriculture, demography, and strategies of risk management.
ECON 242.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 220A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 220B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 243A.title: Game Theory
ECON 243A.description: A formal introduction to non-cooperative game theory. Topics include properties of Nash Equilibrium and equilibrium refinements, games with imperfect information, and games with incomplete information.
ECON 243A.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 243B.title: Advanced Game Theory
ECON 243B.description: Provides advanced instruction in game theory. The topics covered will be (i) the theory of repeated games and (ii) evolutionary game theory. Applications include bargaining, collusion, reputation, social norms, and the evolution of preferences via natural selection and cultural transmission.
ECON 243B.prereq_text: ECON 243A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 245.title: Empirical Methods in Applied Microeconomics
ECON 245.description: Focuses on the empirical methods used in modern applied microeconomics. Teaches methods that can be applied to produce original research in applied fields using cross-sectional and panel data. Applications will be drawn heavily from labor, public, health and development economics.

ECON 249.title: Special Topics in Microeconomics
ECON 249.description: Studies in selected areas of Microeconomics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ECON 251A.title: Labor Economics I
ECON 251A.description: Analysis of the relationships between education and the labor market (human capital theory), between resources devoted to education and the return to education (the education production function) and between education and labor market inequality (the theory of skill-biased technical change).
ECON 251A.prereq_text: ECON 203A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 251B.title: Labor Economics II
ECON 251B.description: Analysis of core topics in labor economics, with an emphasis on empirical methods. Topics may include minimum wages, discrimination, gender, aging and retirement, labor market networks, personnel economics, and employment policy.
ECON 251B.prereq_text: ECON 203A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 255.title: Microeconomics and Public Policy
ECON 255.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of microeconomics that are required for applied policy analysis. Provides students with an intuitive understanding of the microeconomic approach, and familiarizes them with concepts used in applied public policy analysis.

ECON 259.title: Special Topics in Labor Economics
ECON 259.description: Studies in selected areas of Labor Economics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ECON 260B.title: Monetary Economics II
ECON 260B.description: Surveys recent issues on monetary policy in uncertain environments. Examines settings where both the policy makers and the private sector are uncertain of future outcomes or the underlying economic structure.

ECON 261A.title: International Trade I
ECON 261A.description: Covers theoretical models, empirical methods, and policy issues in international trade. Following the conventional treatment of the Richardian model, the Heckscher-Ohlin model and the specific factors model, new trade models which incorporate scale economics and imperfect competition will be discussed.
ECON 261A.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 261B.title: International Trade II
ECON 261B.description: Covers theoretical models, empirical methods, and policy issues in international trade. Following the conventional treatment of the Richardian model, the Heckscher-Ohlin model, and the specific factors model, new trade models which incorporate scale economics and imperfect competition are discussed.
ECON 261B.prereq_text: ECON 261A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 263A.title: Advanced Macroeconomics I
ECON 263A.description: Students build Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) macroeconomic models from microeconomic foundations. This approach emphasizes intertemporal optimization by firms and households and typically incorporates nominal rigidities such as sluggish price and/or wage adjustment.

ECON 269.title: Special Topics in Macroeconomics
ECON 269.description: Studies in selected areas of Macroeconomics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ECON 270A.title: Political Economy I
ECON 270A.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.

ECON 270B.title: Political Economy II
ECON 270B.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.
ECON 270B.prereq_text: ECON 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 270C.title: Political Economy III
ECON 270C.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.
ECON 270C.prereq_text: ECON 270B with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 271.title: Economics of Criminal Justice
ECON 271.description: Considers empirical research from the economics literature on various topics related to the criminal justice system, such as policing, bail reform, incarceration, or recidivism.

ECON 272A.title: Public Economics I
ECON 272A.description: Covers welfare economics, the theory of optimal taxation, tax incidence, and empirical methods in tax policy. Empirical topics include tax evasion, measurement of incidence, efficiency costs, and other policy issues.
ECON 272A.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 272B.title: Public Economics II
ECON 272B.description: Covers the theory of public goods and models of decentralized provision of such goods, including voluntary provision, voting, bureaucratic provision, and preference revelation mechanisms, as well as the Tiebout model. Also covers externalities, cost-benefit analysis, and intergovernmental competition.
ECON 272B.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 272C.title: Public Economics III
ECON 272C.description: Covers the rationale for and effects of government intervention in insurance markets and for redistribution. Includes theoretical and empirical analyses of cash and in-kind assistance programs, unemployment insurance, disability insurance, Social Security, and other programs.
ECON 272C.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 275.title: Economics of Government
ECON 275.description: Prepares students to analyze public policy questions with tools from economics. By the end, students should be able to identify important economic issues in public policy debates and consume and critique economic research on these topics.

ECON 279.title: Special Topics in Political Economy
ECON 279.description: Studies in selected areas of Political Economy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ECON 281A.title: Urban Economics I
ECON 281A.description: Economic reasons for the existence of cities, analysis of urban spatial structure, urban sprawl, Third World urbanization, hedonic price analysis, housing tenure choice.
ECON 281A.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 281B.title: Urban Economics II
ECON 281B.description: Housing in the portfolio, land-use controls, rent control, homelessness, neighborhood effects, urban quality-of-life measurement, and subcenters.
ECON 281B.prereq_text: ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 282B.title: Transportation Economics II
ECON 282B.description: Economics of the airline industry. Hub-and-spoke networks, the effects of competition on airfares, price dispersion, airline alliances, airport congestion, product unbundling.
ECON 282B.prereq_text: ECON 282A with a minimum grade of B-.

ECON 284.title: Health Economics
ECON 284.description: Introduction to graduate-level Health Economics. Research-oriented and focuses on the synthesis and critical examination of existing Economics research, as well as analyzing and producing research, with a focus on the U.S.
ECON 284.prereq_text: (ECON 210A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 210C with a minimum grade of B-) and (ECON 220A with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 220B with a minimum grade of B- and ECON 220C with a minimum grade of B-) or UPPP 215 with a minimum grade of B- and UPPP 240 with a minimum grade of B-.

ECPS 202.title: Cyber-Physical Systems Design
ECPS 202.description: Requirements and specification, models of computation, tools, design, merging cyber and physical, data-driven modeling for edge artificial intelligence systems, cyber-physical examples. Design process, specification, requirements, modeling, components, selection, interfaces, system structure, different levels, verification, testing.

ECPS 203.title: Embedded Systems Modeling and Design
ECPS 203.description: Embedded systems definition, system-level specification, models and languages. Concepts, requirements, examples. Embedded system models at different levels of abstraction. Test benches, design under test, IP components. Discrete event simulation, semantics, and algorithms.

ECPS 204.title: Embedded System Software
ECPS 204.description: Embedded system software requirements, concepts, and examples for applications in the cyber-physical domain. Embedded operating systems, real-time system software (RTOS), I/O software. Multithreading. System software for power and energy management, and middleware.

ECPS 205.title: Sensors, Actuators, and Sensor Networks
ECPS 205.description: Fundamental principles and applications of sensors, actuators. Smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices. Introduction to signal processing and sensor/actuator networks, deployment and architecture, wireless communication, multiple access control layer, data gathering, routing and querying, collaborating signal processing.

ECPS 207.title: Security and Privacy in Cyber-Physical Systems
ECPS 207.description: Embedded and cyber-physical systems security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, confidentiality, data integrity, authorization, access control, security protocols. Privacy awareness and mitigation. Side-channel attacks and defenses. Applications of public key and symmetric cryptography, digital certificates, credentials.

ECPS 208.title: Control Systems for Cyber-Physical Systems
ECPS 208.description: Dynamic models, from first principles or via identification. Concepts in control (stability, controllability, observability). Control design (continuous times) and digital implementation. Introduction to optimization and direct discrete time control. Multi-agent systems, their control and implementation related concepts.

ECPS 209.title: Cyber-Physical Systems Case Studies
ECPS 209.description: Covers CPS case studies in applications such as (but not limited to): automotive and transportation, manufacturing, power distribution grid, medical and healthcare, robotics, civil infrastructure, avionics.

ECPS 210.title: Cyber-Physical Systems Project
ECPS 210.description: Students are required to complete a project that deals with a specific emphasis of Cyber-Physical Systems, such as (but not limited to): automotive, transportation, manufacturing, power grid, medical healthcare, robotics, civil infrastructure, avionics.
ECPS 210.prereq_text: ECPS 202 with a minimum grade of B- or ECPS 203 with a minimum grade of B- or ECPS 216 with a minimum grade of B-.

ECPS 211.title: Machine Learning and Data Mining
ECPS 211.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and data-mining. Learning algorithms for classifications, regression, and clustering. Emphasis is on discriminative classification methods such as decision trees, rules, nearest neighbor, linear models, and naive Bayes.

ECPS 212.title: Entrepreneurship for Scientists and Engineers
ECPS 212.description: Real-world introduction to the theory and practice of entrepreneurship. Explores organizational, strategic, and financial challenges; start-up strategies; business-idea evaluation; and business-plan writing. Presentations by prestigious entrepreneurs and industry leaders.

ECPS 215.title: Foundations of Autonomous Systems
ECPS 215.description: Introduces the fundamentals of perception, planning, and control of autonomous systems. Students learn how to use Robotic Operating Systems (ROS), integrate data from various sensors while implementing algorithms for localization, planning, mapping, and control of autonomous vehicles.

ECPS 216.title: Internet of Things Systems and Software
ECPS 216.description: Internet of Things (IoT) concept, sensors and actuators, serial protocols, network and communication protocols and programming, IoT platforms, real-time performance, middleware architecture for IoT, edge and cloud support for IoT applications.

ECPS 234.title: Preparation for Capstone Design
ECPS 234.description: Provides students in the Master of Embedded and Cyber Physical Systems program with information, practical skills, and preparation for their capstone project. Students form capstone teams and participate in initial project matching with faculty and industry mentors.

ECPS 291.title: Internship
ECPS 291.description: Students go through practical training under an industry mentor in a technical field corresponding to their area of interest.

ECPS 294.title: MECPS Proseminar
ECPS 294.description: Information and practical skills for students in the MECPS program. Also covers professional development career planning.

ECPS 295.title: Special Topics in CPS
ECPS 295.description: Studies in selected areas of CPS. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ECPS 299.title: Individual Research
ECPS 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

EDUC 10.title: Educational Research Design
EDUC 10.description: Designed to help students become intelligent consumers of research and independent researchers, and provides an introduction to the basic principles of educational research. Topics include research questions, literature reviews, and qualitative and quantitative research designs.
EDUC 10.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 15.title: Statistics for Education Research
EDUC 15.description: Provides an introduction to the use of statistics in educational research. Focuses on testing and measurement, and provides basic tools to read, interpret, and draw conclusions from quantitative educational research.

and.not: AP STATISTICS score of 3 or greater

EDUC 15.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 25.title: Introduction to Education: Disciplinary Perspectives
EDUC 25.description: Provides insights into educational organizations and processes by developing understanding of concepts used by four different disciplines (economics, history, psychology, and sociology) to analyze key issues and phenomenon in the field of education that profoundly influence individual life course outcomes.
EDUC 25.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 30.title: 21st Century Literacies
EDUC 30.description: Provides an overview of literacies required for academic and career success in the 21st century. Issues addressed include reading, writing, academic language, research skills, media and technology skills, scientific literacy, critical thinking, communication, collaboration, and creativity.
EDUC 30.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 40.title: Theories of Development and Learning Applied to Education
EDUC 40.description: Provides an introductory examination of central theories of human development and learning in their application to contemporary educational settings.
EDUC 40.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 50.title: Origins, Purposes, and Central Issues in K-12 Education
EDUC 50.description: An introduction to the role of education in U.S. society and to central issues in K–12 education. Education is studied from four different perspectives: social, historical, philosophical, and political.
EDUC 50.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 52.title: Foundations of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism
EDUC 52.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of current issues in bilingual education and bilingualism. Topics include dimensions of bilingualism, the effects of bilingualism on children's linguistic and cognitive development, bilingual education programs, literacy, special needs, and assessment.

EDUC 55.title: Knowing and Learning in Mathematics and Science
EDUC 55.description: Multidisciplinary study of knowing and learning in secondary school mathematics and science. Topics include standards for knowing, scientific epistemologies, mental representations, problem solving, expert-novice studies, assessment, and domain-specific thinking, learning, and teaching. Applied analysis of learning through clinical interviews.

EDUC 70.title: Bilingual Minds and Brains
EDUC 70.description: Examines the variation in the languages that are spoken and the social contexts in which they are used may shape the way we communicate. Explore ways emerging science of bilingualism might be better communicated to the public.
EDUC 70.restriction: Education Sciences majors and Language Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 80.title: Interdisciplinary Topics in Education
EDUC 80.description: Analysis of issues in education from interdisciplinary perspectives. Topics covered vary with interests of instructor.
EDUC 80.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 100.title: Educational Strategies for Tutoring and Teacher Aiding
EDUC 100.description: Placement in a public elementary or secondary school to gain experience as a tutor or teacher aide. Emphasis on cognitive learning and the development of instructional strategies and resources which can be used in effective cross-age and cross-cultural experiences.
EDUC 100.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 101.title: Strategies for Tutoring and Teacher Aiding in a Bilingual Classroom
EDUC 101.description: Placement in a dual immersion school setting to gain experience as a bilingual (Spanish) tutor or teacher aide. Emphasis on cognitive learning and the development of instructional strategies and resources which can be used in effective cross-age and cross-cultural experiences.
EDUC 101.prereq_text: Must be able to communicate in Spanish.
EDUC 101.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 104D.title: The Arts and Human Development
EDUC 104D.description: Students use various arts disciplines (e.g. studio art, music, dance, drama, and media arts) to investigate how visual and performing arts support individual human development. Introduction to pedagogy for integrating the arts in K-12 settings. Materials Fee
EDUC 104D.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 104E.title: Multimedia and the Arts in the Multicultural Classroom
EDUC 104E.description: Multiculturalism and under-represented U.S. minorities and the visual and performing arts: perspectives in artistic perception, creative expression, historical and cultural context, aesthetic valuing, and media literacy in the interpretation and production of multimedia arts products and applications for K-12 classrooms.
EDUC 104E.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 106.title: Early Childhood Education Curriculum and Instruction
EDUC 106.description: Designed to provide an introductory survey of the nature, needs, and education of young children. Explores questions such as "What should we teach young children?" and "How should we teach?"
EDUC 106.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 107.title: Child Development in Education
EDUC 107.description: Explores the pathways of normally developing children's growth and change over time. In particular, focuses on how cognitive and social development impact and are driven by educational contexts.
EDUC 107.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 108.title: Adolescent Development and Education
EDUC 108.description: Explores the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social development of adolescents, with an emphasis on the practical implications of developmental theory and research findings for teachers and other professionals who work with adolescents in middle or high school contexts.
EDUC 108.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 109.title: Reading and Writing in Mathematics and Science
EDUC 109.description: Emphasis is placed on understanding the literacy processes (listening, speaking, viewing, thinking, reading, and writing) as they relate to middle and high school mathematics and science. Students integrate literacy-related strategies with curriculum-based goals supported in the California State Frameworks.

EDUC 120A.title: Introduction to Positive Psychology in Education
EDUC 120A.description: Positive psychology is a recent focus area within the field of psychology that explores what is positive, creative, and fulfilling in human behavior. It is the scientific study of well-being and flourishing.
EDUC 120A.restriction: Education Sciences majors, Psychological Science majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 120B.title: Applied Positive Psychology in Education
EDUC 120B.description: Covers select positive psychology topics, theories, and interventions at an advanced level. Students focus on developing an understanding of positive psychology evidence-based practices that can be applied in classrooms and schools to promote learning in an academic environment.
EDUC 120B.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 122A.title: Foundations of Elementary Mathematics Learning I
EDUC 122A.description: Provides understanding of fundamental mathematics necessary to teach for conceptual understanding and higher-level reasoning and problem solving. Conceptual understanding of place value, fractions, proportionality, geometry, algebra, functions, probability, statistics, and measurement. Instructional applications of these concepts in grades K-8 teaching.
EDUC 122A.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 122B.title: Foundations of Elementary Mathematics Learning II
EDUC 122B.description: Provides understanding of fundamental mathematics necessary to teach for conceptual understanding and higher-level reasoning and problem solving. Conceptual understanding of place value, fractions, proportionality, geometry, algebra, functions, probability, statistics, and measurement. Instructional applications of these concepts in grades K-8 teaching.
EDUC 122B.restriction: Education Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EDUC 122C.title: Foundations of Elementary Mathematics Learning III
EDUC 122C.description: Provides understanding of fundamental mathematics necessary to teach for conceptual understanding and higher-level reasoning and problem solving. Conceptual understanding of place value, fractions, proportionality, geometry, algebra, functions, probability, statistics, and measurement.
