EECS 170D.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

EECS 170E.title: Analog and Communications IC Design
EECS 170E.description: Advanced topics in design of analog and communications integrated circuits. Topics include: implementation of passive components in integrated circuits; overview of frequency response of amplifiers, bandwidth estimation techniques, high-frequency amplifier design; design of radio-frequency oscillators.
EECS 170E.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

EECS 170LA.title: Electronics I Laboratory
EECS 170LA.description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170A to perform experiments on semiconductor material properties, semiconductor device physics and operation principles, and transistor amplifiers to improve experimental skills and to enhance the understanding of lecture materials.
EECS 170LA.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors, Computer Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EECS 170LB.title: Electronics II Laboratory
EECS 170LB.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors and Computer Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

EECS 170LC.title: Electronics III Laboratory
EECS 170LC.description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170C to provide hands-on training in design of digital/analog circuits/subsystems. Materials Fee
EECS 170LC.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

EECS 174.title: Semiconductor Devices
EECS 174.description: Metal-semiconductor junctions, diodes, bipolar junction transistors, MOS structures, MOSFETs, CMOS technology, LEDs, and laser diodes.
EECS 174.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

EECS 176.title: Fundamentals of Solid-State Electronics and Materials
EECS 176.description: Physical properties of semiconductors and the roles materials play in device operation. Topics include: crystal structure, phonon vibrations, energy band, transport phenomenon, optical properties and quantum confinement effect essential to the understanding of electronic, optoelectronic and nanodevices.
EECS 176.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors, Electrical Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EECS 179.title: Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS)
EECS 179.description: Small-scale machines, small-scale phenomena, MEMS fabrication, MEMS CAD tools, MEMS devices and packaging, MEMS testing.
EECS 179.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EECS 180A.title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
EECS 180A.description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, and electromagnetic fields: solutions to problems in engineering applications; transmission lines, Maxwell's equations and phasors, plane wave propagation, reflection, and transmission.
EECS 180A.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors, Biomedical Engineering majors, and Materials Science Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EECS 180B.title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
EECS 180B.description: Time-varying electromagnetic fields, plane waves, polarization, guidance of waves like rectangular waveguides and microstrips, optical fibers resonant cavities, skin effects and losses, spherical waves, radiation and reception of waves, antenna basics.
EECS 180B.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

EECS 182.title: Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Analysis and Design
EECS 182.description: Design of microwave amplifiers including low-noise amplifiers, multiple stage amplifiers, power amplifiers, and introduction to broadband amplifiers. The goal is to provide the basic knowledge for the design of microwave amplifiers ranging from wireless system to radar system.
EECS 182.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

EECS 188.title: Optical Electronics
EECS 188.description: Photodiodes and optical detection, photometry and radiometry, geometric optics, lens theory, imaging system, EM wave propagation, optical waveguides and fibers, heterojunction structures, laser theory, semiconductor lasers, and optical transmission system.
EECS 188.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

EECS 195.title: Special Topics in Electrical and Computer Engineering
EECS 195.description: Studies special topics in selected areas of Electrical and Computer Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

EECS 197.title: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Internship
EECS 197.description: Students majoring in EECS may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.

EECS 198.title: Group Study
EECS 198.description: Group study of selected topics in Electrical and Computer Engineering.

EECS 199.title: Individual Study
EECS 199.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking Individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

EECS 199P.title: Individual Study
EECS 199P.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

EECS 202P.title: Techniques in Medical Imaging: X-ray, Nuclear, and NMR Imaging
EECS 202P.description: Ionizing radiation, planar and tomographic radiographic and nuclear imaging, magnetism, NMR, MRI imaging.

EECS 203A.title: Digital Image Processing
EECS 203A.description: Pixel-level digital image representation and elementary operations; Fourier and other unitary transforms; compression, enhancement, filtering, and restoration; laboratory experience is provided.

EECS 203P.title: Digital Image Processing
EECS 203P.description: Pixel-level digital image representation and elementary operations; Fourier and other unitary transforms; compression, enhancement, filtering, and restoration; laboratory experience is provided.

EECS 204P.title: Personalized Medical Devices
EECS 204P.description: Introduces students to fundamental aspects of medical devices and discusses therapeutic as well as diagnostic devices. Basic aspects of microfluidics and biology critical to personalized medical systems are studied. Typical FDA approval pathways for medical devices are presented.

EECS 211.title: Advanced System Software
EECS 211.description: Study of operating systems including interprocess communication, scheduling, resource management, concurrency, reliability, validation, protection and security, and distributed computing support. System software design languages and modeling analysis.

EECS 211P.title: Advanced System Software
EECS 211P.description: Study of operating systems including interprocess communication, scheduling, resource management, concurrency, reliability, validation, protection and security, and distributed computing support. System software design languages and modeling analysis.
EECS 211P.prereq_text: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of system software (e.g. EECS 111) and organization of digital computers (e.g. UCI EECS 112).

EECS 213.title: Computer Architecture
EECS 213.description: Problems in hardware, firmware (microprogram), and software. Computer architecture for resource sharing, real-time applications, parallelism, microprogramming, and fault tolerance. Various architectures based on cost/performance and current technology.

EECS 213P.title: Computer Architecture
EECS 213P.description: Problems in hardware, firmware (microprogram), and software. Computer architecture for resource sharing, real-time applications, parallelism, microprogramming, and fault tolerance. Various architectures based on cost/performance and current technology.
EECS 213P.prereq_text: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of organization of digital computers (e.g. EECS 112 and EECS 112L).

EECS 215.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
EECS 215.description: Computer algorithms from a practical standpoint. Algorithms for symbolic and numeric problems such as sorting, searching, graphs, and network flow. Analysis includes algorithm time and space complexity.

EECS 215P.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
EECS 215P.description: Computer algorithms from a practical standpoint. Algorithms for symbolic and numeric problems such as sorting, searching, graphs, and network flow. Analysis includes algorithm time and space complexity.

EECS 216.title: Advanced Application of Algorithms
EECS 216.description: Medium-sized group and individual programming project. Topics include specification requirements documentation, practical implementation of algorithms, and testing/verification of design.
EECS 216.prereq_text: Recommended: Undergraduate course work in engineering data structures and algorithms.

EECS 217.title: VLSI System Design
EECS 217.description: Overview of integrated fabrication, circuit simulation, basic device physics, device layout, timing; MOS logic design; layout generation, module generation, techniques for very large scale integrated circuit design.

EECS 217P.title: VLSI System Design
EECS 217P.description: Overview of integrated fabrication, circuit simulation, basic device physics, device layout, timing; MOS logic design; layout generation, module generation, techniques for very large scale integrated circuit design.
EECS 217P.prereq_text: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of organization of digital computers (e.g. EECS 112).

EECS 220P.title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing Architecture
EECS 220P.description: Study the latest DSP architectures for applications in communication (wired and wireless) and multimedia processing. Emphasis given to understanding the current design techniques and to evaluate the performance, power, and application domain of the latest DSP processors.
EECS 220P.prereq_text: EECS 213P with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 221.title: Topics in Computer Engineering
EECS 221.description: New research results in computer engineering.

EECS 222.title: Embedded System Modeling
EECS 222.description: Computational models for embedded systems. System-level specification and description languages. Concepts, requirements, examples. Embedded system models at different levels of abstraction. Modeling of test benches, design under test, IP components. Discrete event simulation, semantics, and algorithms. Formerly EECS 222A.

EECS 223P.title: Real-Time Computer Systems
EECS 223P.description: Time bases, clock synchronization, real-time communication protocols, specification of requirements, task scheduling. Validation of timelines, real-time configuration management.
EECS 223P.prereq_text: EECS 211P with a minimum grade of B- and EECS 213P with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 224.title: High-Performance Computing
EECS 224.description: Fundamentals of high-performance computing, covering both theory and practice. Topics include performance analysis and tuning, design of parallel and I/O efficient algorithms, basics of parallel machine architectures, and current/emerging programming models (shared memory, distributed memory, and accelerators).
EECS 224.prereq_text: EECS 215 with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 260 with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 226.title: Embedded System Software
EECS 226.description: Embedded system software concepts, requirements, examples, for engineering applications such as multi-media and automotive. Software generation methodology. Algorithmic specification, design constraints. Embedded operating systems. Static, dynamic, real-time scheduling. Input/output, interrupt handling. Code generation, compilation, instruction set simulation. Formerly EECS 222C.

EECS 227.title: Cyber-Physical System Design
EECS 227.description: Model-based design of cyber-physical systems including, e.g., plant, sensing, control, actuation, embedded hardware/software, communication, real-time analysis, various levels of simulation (MILS, SILS, HILS), tools and methodologies for automatic synthesis, and application from various interdisciplinary domains.

EECS 230.title: Energy Efficiency
EECS 230.description: Green energy sources for production, transmission, storage, and utilization of electricity, with a special focus on solar, wind, and nuclear energy production. Study of newly developed renewable sources of energy including capital cost, product cost, environmental issues, and technical feasibility.

EECS 230P.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
EECS 230P.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in programming and machine learning. The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to the field of machine learning and related techniques for students with a wide variety of engineering degrees.

EECS 231.title: Advanced System Security
EECS 231.description: Advanced study about system security. Topics include software vulnerabilities (buffer overflow), vulnerability discovery (fuzzing), network security, side-channel analysis (power analysis and micro-architecture attacks), machine-learning security, IoT security, and privacy (differential privacy).

EECS 232.title: Data Privacy
EECS 232.description: Presents data privacy in the digital age from multiple perspectives, including theoretical frameworks for privacy; tracking practices and privacy-enhancing technologies in various application domains; and data protection laws and policy.
EECS 232.prereq_text: Recommended: Students should have familiarity with networking (web/HTTP, DNS, mobile devices) (EECS 148 or equivalent), probability (EECS 55 or equivalent), and programming in python (EECS 12 or equivalent) at the undergraduate level.

EECS 235.title: Quantum Information and Architecture
EECS 235.description: Fundamentals of quantum mechanics and quantum information; learn the principles, advantages, and challenges of quantum computing and its architectures; acquire hands-on experience with basic quantum information techniques.
EECS 235.prereq_text: Knowledge in linear algebra and complex analysis.

EECS 240.title: Random Processes
EECS 240.description: Extensions of probability theory to random variables varying with time. General properties of stochastic processes. Convergence. Estimation, including nonlinear and linear minimum mean square error and maximum likelihood. Spectral density and linear filters. Poisson processes and discrete-time Markov chains.

EECS 240P.title: Random Processes
EECS 240P.description: Extensions of probability theory to random variables varying with time. General properties of stochastic processes. Convergence. Estimation, including nonlinear and linear minimum mean square error and maximum likelihood. Spectral density and linear filters. Poisson processes and discrete-time Markov chains.
EECS 240P.prereq_text: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering probability (e.g. EECS 55).

EECS 241A.title: Digital Communications I
EECS 241A.description: Concepts and applications of digital communication systems. Baseband digital transmission of binary, multiamplitude, and multidimensional signals. Introduction to and performance analysis of different modulation schemes.

EECS 241AP.title: Digital Communications I
EECS 241AP.description: Concepts and applications of digital communication systems. Baseband digital transmission of binary, multiamplitude, and multidimensional signals. Introduction to and performance analysis of different modulation schemes.

EECS 241B.title: Digital Communications II
EECS 241B.description: Concepts and applications of equalization, multi-carrier modulation, spread spectrum and CDMA. Digital communications through fading memory channels.
EECS 241B.prereq_text: EECS 241A with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 241BP.title: Digital Communications II
EECS 241BP.description: Concepts and applications of equalization, multi-carrier modulation, spread spectrum, and CDMA. Digital communications through fading memory channels.
EECS 241BP.prereq_text: EECS 241AP with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 242.title: Information Theory
EECS 242.description: Fundamental capabilities and limitations of information sources and information transmission systems. Analytical framework for modeling and evaluating communication systems: entropy, mutual information asymptotic equipartition property, entropy rates of a stochastic process, data compression, channel capacity, differential entropy, the Gaussian channel.
EECS 242.prereq_text: EECS 240 with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 244.title: Wireless Communications
EECS 244.description: Introduction to wireless communications systems. Wireless channel modeling. Single carries, spread spectrum, and multi-carrier wireless modulation schemes. Diversity techniques. Multiple-access schemes. Transceiver design and system level tradeoffs. Brief overview of GSM, CDMA, (IS-95) and 2.5, 3G cellular schemes.
EECS 244.prereq_text: EECS 241B with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 244P.title: Wireless Communications
EECS 244P.description: Introduction to wireless communications systems. Wireless channel modeling. Single carries, spread spectrum, and multi-carrier wireless modulation schemes. Diversity techniques. Multiple-access schemes. Transceiver design and system level tradeoffs. Brief overview of GSM, CDMA, (IS-95) and 2.5, 3G cellular schemes.
EECS 244P.prereq_text: EECS 241BP with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 247.title: Information Storage
EECS 247.description: Storage architecture, storage network and networking algorithms in data centers, principle of storage devices and non-volatile memory, data consistency, data availability and integrity, power management.

EECS 248A.title: Computer and Communication Networks
EECS 248A.description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.

EECS 250.title: Digital Signal Processing I
EECS 250.description: Fundamental principles of digital signal processing, sampling, decimation and interpolation, discrete Fourier transforms and FFT algorithms, transversal and recursive filters, discrete random processes, and finite-word effects in digital filters.

EECS 250P.title: Digital Signal Processing I
EECS 250P.description: Fundamental principles of digital signal processing, sampling, decimation and interpolation, discrete Fourier transforms and FFT algorithms, transversal and recursive filters, discrete random processes, and finite-word effects in digital filters.
EECS 250P.prereq_text: Recommended: Knowledge of digital signal processing (e.g. EECS 152A).

EECS 251A.title: Detection, Estimation, and Demodulation Theory
EECS 251A.description: Fundamentals of hypothesis testing and Bayes and Maximum Likelihood Estimation. ARMA and state variable models for random time series analysis. Wiener and Kalman filtering and prediction. Adaptive algorithms for identification and tracking of parameters of time-varying models.
EECS 251A.prereq_text: EECS 240 with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 253.title: Machine Learning for Signal Processing
EECS 253.description: Machine learning and computational neuroscience methods for signal processing. Theory and applications are described, as well as practical programming methods in Python using Keras and TensorFlow 2.
EECS 253.prereq_text: Recommended: EECS 125 or equivalent undergraduate-level introduction to machine learning and EECS 152A or equivalent undergraduate course in digital signal processing. Knowledge of introductory linear algebra and differential equations, elementary probability theory, and elementary Python programming.

EECS 254.title: Unsupervised Computational Neural Networks and Machine Learning
EECS 254.description: Unsupervised machine learning and computational neuroscience methods. Theory and applications are described, as well as practical programming methods in Python using Keras and TensorFlow 2.
EECS 254.prereq_text: Recommended: EECS 125 or equivalent undergraduate-level introduction to machine learning. Knowledge of introductory linear algebra and differential equations, elementary probability theory, and elementary Matlab programming.

EECS 260A.title: Linear Systems I
EECS 260A.description: State-space representation of continuous-time and discrete-time linear systems. Controllability, observability, stability. Realization of rational transfer functions.

EECS 261A.title: Linear Optimization Methods
EECS 261A.description: Formulation, solution, and analysis of linear programming and linear network flow problems. Simplex methods, dual ascent methods, interior point algorithms, and auction algorithms. Duality theory and sensitivity analysis. Shortest path, max-flow, assignment, and minimum cost flow problems.

EECS 263.title: Introduction to Non-Linear Optimization
EECS 263.description: Explores convex optimization problems that arise in scientific and engineering applications, presenting the basic theory, and concentrating on modeling aspects and results useful in applications. Covers the fundamentals of convex optimization and its applications to signal processing, control, machine learning.
EECS 263.restriction: Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy only.

EECS 267A.title: Industrial and Power Electronics
EECS 267A.description: Power switching devices, pulse width modulation (PWM) methods, switching converter topologies, control, and magnetics. Materials Fee

EECS 267B.title: Topics in Industrial and Power Electronics
EECS 267B.description: Practical design of switching converters, electromagnetic compatibility, thermal management, and/or control methods.
EECS 267B.prereq_text: EECS 267A with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 270A.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I
EECS 270A.description: Basic transistor configurations; differential pairs; active load/current sources; supply/temperature-independent biasing; op-amp gain and output stages; amplifier frequency response and stability compensation; nonidealities in op-amps; noise and dynamic range in analog circuits.

EECS 270AP.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I
EECS 270AP.description: Basic transistor configurations; differential pairs; active load/current sources; supply/temperature-independent biasing; op-amp gain and output stages; amplifier frequency response and stability compensation; nonidealities in op-amps; noise and dynamic range in analog circuits.
EECS 270AP.prereq_text: Recommended: Introductory knowledge of control systems (e.g. EECS 160A) and electronics (e.g. EECS 170C).

EECS 270B.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design II
EECS 270B.description: Advanced transistor modeling issues; discrete-time and continuous-time analog Integrated Circuit (IC) filters; phase-locked loops; design of ICs operating at radio frequencies; low-voltage/low-power design techniques; A/D and D/A converters; AGC circuits.
EECS 270B.prereq_text: EECS 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 270BP.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design II
EECS 270BP.description: Advanced transistor modeling issues; discrete-time and continuous-time analog Integrated Circuit (IC) filters; phase-locked loops; design of ICs operating at radio frequencies; low-voltage/low-power design techniques; A/D and D/A converters; AGC circuits.
EECS 270BP.prereq_text: EECS 270AP with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 270C.title: Design of Integrated Circuits for Broadband Applications
EECS 270C.description: Topics include: broadband standards and protocols; high-frequency circuit design techniques; PLL theory and design; design of transceivers; electrical/optical interfaces.
EECS 270C.prereq_text: EECS 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 270D.title: Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuits and Systems
EECS 270D.description: Fundamental topics in radio-frequency (RF) integrated circuits and systems including basic concepts in RF circuits and systems, RF receiver and transmitter architectures, and RF core building blocks such as low-noise amplifiers (LNAs), RF mixers, and power amplifiers.
EECS 270D.prereq_text: EECS 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 270E.title: MM-Wave and Terahertz Circuits
EECS 270E.description: Discussion of the new methodologies, circuits, and systems developed at mm-wave and terahertz frequency ranges due to the growing interest in high speed communication and high frequency signal generation.

EECS 272P.title: Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuit Design
EECS 272P.description: Topics include RF component modeling; matching network design; transmission line theory/modeling; Smith chart and S-parameters; noise modeling of active and passive components; high-frequency amplifier design; low-noise amplifier (LNA) design; mixer design; RF power amplifier.
EECS 272P.prereq_text: EECS 270AP with a minimum grade of B.

EECS 277A.title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices I
EECS 277A.description: Advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (CMOSFET), device scaling, device modeling and fabrication, equivalent circuits, and their applications for digital, analog, RF.

EECS 277B.title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices II
EECS 277B.description: Metal-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MESFET), heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT), microwave semiconductor devices, equivalent circuits, device modeling and fabrication, microwave amplifiers, transmitters, and receivers.

EECS 277C.title: Nanotechnology
EECS 277C.description: Fabrication and characterization techniques of electrical circuit elements at the nanometer scale. Quantized conductance, semiconductor quantum dots, single electron transistors, molecular wires, carbon nanotubes, self-assembly of nano-circuit elements, quantum methods of information processing.

EECS 278.title: Micro-System Design
EECS 278.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

EECS 279.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
EECS 279.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale. Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

EECS 280A.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
EECS 280A.description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.

EECS 280B.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics II
EECS 280B.description: Two- and three-dimensional boundary value problems, dielectric waveguides and other special waveguides, microwave networks and antenna arrays, electromagnetic properties of materials, and electromagnetic optics.
EECS 280B.prereq_text: EECS 280A with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 280P.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
EECS 280P.description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.
EECS 280P.prereq_text: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering electromagnetics (e.g. EECS 180A).

EECS 284.title: Wireless Communication Links and Antenna Design
EECS 284.description: Provides the fundamental understanding of the electromagnetic part of wireless communication links and their antennas, i.e., their key components. Contains hands-on component where students learn how to use the best CADs used in industry and academia.

EECS 284P.title: RF Antenna Design
EECS 284P.description: Advanced transmission line design, radiation of electromagnetic waves, dipole antennas, antenna arrays, advanced antenna designs, and practical design considerations in communications systems. Course is supplemented by RF design tools and modeling.
EECS 284P.prereq_text: EECS 280AP with a minimum grade of B-.

EECS 285A.title: Optical Communications
EECS 285A.description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.

EECS 285C.title: Nano Imaging
EECS 285C.description: Theory and practice of modern nanoscale imaging techniques and applications. Traces the development of microscopy from ancient times to modern day techniques used for visualizing the nano-world from atoms to molecules including hands-on experience in the laboratory.

EECS 285P.title: Optical Communications
EECS 285P.description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.
EECS 285P.prereq_text: Undergraduate-level Engineering Electromagnetics I (e.g. EECS E80A).

EECS 286.title: Fabrication of Biomedical and Wearable Microdevices
EECS 286.description: Covers preliminary details on prototyping and fabrication techniques for biomedical and wearable microdevices. Fabrication and behavior of modern biomed device materials such as hydrogel, PDMS, biopolymer, smart materials, and their uses are introduced.
EECS 286.prereq_text: Required: Knowledge of undergraduate-level basic physics.

EECS 287.title: Micro/Nano Biotechnology and Biosensing: Fundamentals, Designs, and Applications
EECS 287.description: Provides insight into the current topics in Micro/Nanoscience, Micro/Nanotechnology fundamentals, and their modern-day applications in life sciences. Focus is on Micro/Nanodevices; Sensors’ fundamentals; NanoBioSensors; Microfluidics; Micro/Nanofabrication, detection system-level characterization; performance determination; solid-state materials; and more.

EECS 289.title: Bioinstrumentation
EECS 289.description: Introduces instrumentation used in biomedical research, clinical medicine, and health monitoring. Interfacing of bioelectronics and biomedical sensing are taught with the most updated methods. The integration of bioinstrumentation with data science and cloud computing are introduced.

EECS 292.title: Preparation for M.S. Comprehensive Examination
EECS 292.description: Individual reading and preparation for the M.S. comprehensive examination.

EECS 293.title: Preparation for Ph.D. Preliminary Examination
EECS 293.description: Individual reading and preparation for the Ph.D. preliminary examination.

EECS 294.title: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Colloquium
EECS 294.description: Invited speakers discuss their latest research results in electrical engineering and computer science.

EECS 295.title: Seminars in Engineering
EECS 295.description: Scheduled each year by individual faculty in major field of interest.

EECS 295P.title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
EECS 295P.description: Studies in selected areas of Electrical Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

EECS 296.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
EECS 296.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the thesis required for the M.S. degree in Engineering.

EECS 297.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
EECS 297.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparing and completing the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree in Engineering.

EECS 298.title: Topics in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
EECS 298.description: Study of Electrical and Computer Engineering concepts.

EECS 299.title: Individual Research
EECS 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

EHS 70.title: Toxicology and Society
EHS 70.description: Introduces principles of toxicology and societal implications of toxic exposures. Focuses on mechanisms of action, dose-response relationships, exposure pathways, and risk assessment. Includes applications in food safety, occupational health, environmental toxicology, regulatory policy, and health equity.
EHS 70.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

EHS 201.title: Case Studies in Environmental Toxicology
EHS 201.description: Explores toxicology principles through case-based discussions. Topics include exposure routes, absorption, metabolism, and mechanisms of toxicity. Lectures with discussions are delivered by invited faculty experts.
EHS 201.prereq_text: EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-.

EHS 202.title: Principles of Environmental Toxicology
EHS 202.description: Explores molecular, biological, and structure-based toxicity of environmental toxicants. Topics include dose-response relationship, ADME, mechanisms of action, and its impact on the environment, wildlife, and human health. Covered through lectures, research papers, and discussion.

EHS 203.title: Occupational Epidemiology
EHS 203.description: The importance of work environment for workers’ health and productivity has increased with changing technology, work organization, demographics, and occupation/industry structures. This advanced occupational epidemiology course focuses on work environment as exposures, and workers’ health and productivity as outcomes.

EHS 204.title: Neurotoxicology
EHS 204.description: The effects of various harmful chemicals upon nervous system function. Emphasis given to the molecular events underlying neurological damage and to the relation of such processes to basic mechanisms of neurobiology.

EHS 206A.title: Target Organ Toxicology I
EHS 206A.description: Outlines vulnerability of selected organ systems to environmental and occupational chemicals. Reviews molecular aspects of toxicological damage. Topics include molecular toxicology and the following organ systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, dermal, and skeletal embryology.

EHS 206B.title: Target Organ Toxicology II
EHS 206B.description: Analyzes mechanistic responses in animals and humans to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation, focusing on organ system physiology. Topics specifically covered include reproductive, endocrine, developmental, kidney, liver, pancreas, vascular, immune toxicology, radiation, and chemical carcinogenesis.

EHS 207.title: Experimental Design and Interpretation of Toxicology Studies
EHS 207.description: Introduction to methods of structuring toxicology experiments and analyzing data, including experimental design, data distributions, sample sizes, hypothesis testing, linear regression, analysis of variance, multiple comparison testing, and non-parametric tests.

EHS 212.title: Inhalation Toxicology
EHS 212.description: Explores laboratory inhalation toxicology principles and practices. Covers aerosols, gases, respiratory tract structure/function, lung defenses, exposure techniques, experimental designs, animal models, and regulations/guidelines.

EHS 220.title: Industrial Toxicology
EHS 220.description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.
EHS 220.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 277B with a minimum grade of B- or EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-.

EHS 264.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
EHS 264.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EHS 264.prereq_text: ( MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR OHW MAJORS ONLY OR OKQ MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
EHS 264.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EHS 269.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
EHS 269.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

EHS 275.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
EHS 275.description: Learn general principles and basic mathematical methods for environmental modeling and human health risk assessment, including compartmental and advection-dispersion models for contaminants in air and water, uptake by plants and animals, exposure, assessment, dose-response modeling, risk management, and risk perception.

EHS 290.title: Independent Study in Environmental Toxicology
EHS 290.description: With consent from a faculty member who will supervise the program, a student may receive credit for individual study in some area of toxicology, culminating in the completion of a scholarly paper on the subject.

EHS 294.title: Health Psychology
EHS 294.description: Focus on theory and research in health psychology as applied to major acute, chronic, and occupational health problems. Adopting the biopsychosocial model of health, emphasis is on understanding and influencing how biology, behavior, and the environment influence health and illness.

EHS 297.title: Advanced Topics in Occupational Toxicology
EHS 297.description: Discussions with clinical and research faculty in environmental toxicology and occupational medicine on current toxicology problems in the workplace and critical review of current publications in the field.

EHS 298.title: Seminar in Environmental Health Sciences
EHS 298.description: Presentation and discussion of current research problems and issues by students, postdoctoral fellows, faculty, and guests, covering the broad research and policy areas of environmental health sciences.

EHS 299.title: Research Problems
EHS 299.description: Research work for the M.S. thesis or Ph.D. dissertation.

ENGLISH 8.title: Multicultural American Literature
ENGLISH 8.description: Writings from at least two historically underrepresented groups in California and the United States with particular attention to historical conditions of literary production. Considers in-depth how literary works relate to racial constructions, economic conditions, and/or social movements.

ENGLISH 9.title: Shakespeare
ENGLISH 9.description: Plays by William Shakespeare are used to explore the playwright’s poetic gifts, theatrical imagination, and inquiry into human relationships and the human condition.

ENGLISH 10.title: Topics in English and American Literature
ENGLISH 10.description: Explores the diversity of human expression manifested in selected works of literature. By engaging with substantial literary texts, students will think critically about how meaning is created and how experience is interpreted in literary language.

ENGLISH 11.title: Society, Law, and Literature
ENGLISH 11.description: Examines how works of literature represent and influence the relation between law and society. The primary readings will be works of literature, but selections of works of law, politics, and sociology may also be assigned.

ENGLISH 11C.title: Society, Law, and Literature
ENGLISH 11C.description: Linked with Writing 60. Explores how works of literature represent and influence the relation between law and society. The primary readings are works of literature, but selections of works of law, politics, and sociology may also be assigned.

ENGLISH 12.title: Young Adult Fiction
ENGLISH 12.description: Traces the history and development of young adult (YA) fiction, with particular attention to the development of interpretive approaches to YA fiction that take into account YA fiction as a cultural phenomenon.

ENGLISH 15.title: Introductory Seminar in English: Topics in Literary Studies
ENGLISH 15.description: Discussion-based seminar on a faculty-chosen topic that introduces majors and those considering a major in English to interpretive methodologies and critical frameworks that characterize the field of English studies.
ENGLISH 15.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ENGLISH 15.restriction: English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 16.title: The Craft of Poetry
ENGLISH 16.description: Reading of selected texts to explore the ways in which these modes formulate experience. Students write several short analytic papers. Requires creative writing.
ENGLISH 16.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ENGLISH 17.title: The Craft of Fiction
ENGLISH 17.description: Reading of selected texts to explore the ways in which these modes formulate experience. Students write several short analytic papers. Requires creative writing.
ENGLISH 17.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ENGLISH H80.title: Sanctuary: Medieval and Modern
ENGLISH H80.description: Principles and significance of the practice of legal sanctuary in medieval English history, literature, and religion. Development of modern use of churches and other safe spaces in the American Civil Rights movement, immigrant sanctuary movements, and international asylum.

ENGLISH H81.title: What is a Person?
ENGLISH H81.description: Contemporary debates about personhood in law, culture, and society. Beginning with the emergence of ideas of personhood in philosophy and theology, and culminating in the study of highly contested cases: slavery, abortion law, animal rights, corporate personhood, and artificial intelligence.

ENGLISH H83.title: What is a University?
ENGLISH H83.description: The history and present of the modern university, with special attention to the history of the UC system. Problems of social justice, racial equality, class mobility in the university as well as student life and universities in popular culture.

ENGLISH 100.title: Introduction to Literary Theory
ENGLISH 100.description: Using Plato and Aristotle as points of departure, addresses a range of perspectives and problems in literary theory. To be taken by English majors in the junior year.
ENGLISH 100.prereq_text: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8, ENGLISH 9, ENGLISH 10, ENGLISH 11, ENGLISH 12, ENGLISH 15, ENGLISH 16, ENGLISH 17, LIT JRN 20, LIT JRN 21.

ENGLISH 101W.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Critical Writing: Topics in Literary History
ENGLISH 101W.description: Each instructor identifies a topic within literary history; special attention is given to mastering the conventions of academic argument and expression. To be taken as early as possible in the junior year.
ENGLISH 101W.prereq_text: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8, ENGLISH 9, ENGLISH 10, ENGLISH 11, ENGLISH 12, ENGLISH 15, ENGLISH 16, ENGLISH 17; or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ENGLISH 101W.restriction: English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 102A.title: Topics in Medieval and Renaissance Literature
ENGLISH 102A.description: Studies of works representative of Medieval and Renaissance literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
ENGLISH 102A.prereq_text: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8, ENGLISH 9, ENGLISH 10, ENGLISH 11, ENGLISH 12, ENGLISH 15, ENGLISH 16, ENGLISH 17. Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list.
ENGLISH 102A.restriction: English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 102B.title: Topics in Restoration and 18th-Century Literature
ENGLISH 102B.description: Studies of works representative of Restoration and 18th-century literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
ENGLISH 102B.prereq_text: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8, ENGLISH 9, ENGLISH 10, ENGLISH 11, ENGLISH 12, ENGLISH 15, ENGLISH 16, ENGLISH 17. Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list.
ENGLISH 102B.restriction: English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 102C.title: Topics in Romantic and 19th-Century Literature
ENGLISH 102C.description: Studies of works representative of Romantic and 19th-century literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
ENGLISH 102C.prereq_text: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8, ENGLISH 9, ENGLISH 10, ENGLISH 11, ENGLISH 12, ENGLISH 15, ENGLISH 16, ENGLISH 17. Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list.
ENGLISH 102C.restriction: English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 102D.title: Topics in 20th-Century Literature
ENGLISH 102D.description: Studies of works representative of 20th-century literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
ENGLISH 102D.prereq_text: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8, ENGLISH 9, ENGLISH 10, ENGLISH 11, ENGLISH 12, ENGLISH 15, ENGLISH 16, ENGLISH 17. Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list.
ENGLISH 102D.restriction: English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 103.title: Topics in Literature, Theory, and Criticism
ENGLISH 103.description: A series of lectures on and discussions of announced topics in literary criticism, theory, history, genres, modes, major authors.
ENGLISH 103.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ENGLISH 105.title: Multicultural Topics in Literatures in English
ENGLISH 105.description: Focuses on ethnic or minority literatures, or treats issues related to race and cultural identity.
ENGLISH 105.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ENGLISH 106.title: Advanced Seminar: Topics in English Literature
ENGLISH 106.description: Capstone course. Provides intensive work on a topic within the area of literatures in English with particular attention to the theoretical, critical, or conceptual issues it raises, with the goal of producing a substantive research paper.
ENGLISH 106.prereq_text: (ENGLISH 101W or WRITING 101W) and (ENGLISH 100 and 102A) or (ENGLISH 100 and 102B) or (ENGLISH 100 and 102C) or (ENGLISH 100 and 102D) or (ENGLISH 102A and 102B) or (ENGLISH 102A and 102C) or (ENGLISH 102A and 102D) or (ENGLISH 102B and 102C) or (ENGLISH 102C and 102D) or (ENGLISH 103 and 102A) or (ENGLISH 103 and 102B) or (ENGLISH 103 and 102C) or (ENGLISH 103 and 102D) or (ENGLISH 105 and 102A) or (ENGLISH 105 and 102B) or (ENGLISH 105 and 102C) or (ENGLISH 105 and 102D) or (ENGLISH 100 and 103) or (ENGLISH 103 and 105) or (ENGLISH 100 and 105).
ENGLISH 106.restriction: Seniors and English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 107.title: English in Action
ENGLISH 107.description: Career exploration for English majors connecting writing, close reading, critical analysis, and communication skills to diverse career paths including marketing, publishing, non-profits, technical writing, education, digital media. Special attention given to mentorship, job search strategies, resume writing, and interview techniques.
ENGLISH 107.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ENGLISH 107.restriction: English majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGLISH 160.title: Topics in English Language Film and TV
ENGLISH 160.description: Focuses on the analysis of film and/or television traditions in the English-speaking world, from a historical, theoretical, or comparative perspective.
ENGLISH 160.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ENGLISH 198.title: Special Topics
ENGLISH 198.description: Directed group study of selected topics as arranged by instructor.

ENGLISH 199.title: Independent Study
ENGLISH 199.description: To be taken only when the materials to be studied lie outside the normal run of departmental offerings, and when the student will have no formal chance to pursue the subject. Research paper required.

ENGLISH 205.title: Master of English Seminar
ENGLISH 205.description: Studies in selected areas of literary history for Master of English students. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGLISH 206.title: Master of English Research and Writing Colloquium
ENGLISH 206.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGLISH 207.title: Master of English Thesis Practicum
ENGLISH 207.description: A yearlong undertaking of original research and writing, developed in close coordination with a faculty mentor. Accordingly, the precise contents and contours vary by advisor and by project.

ENGLISH 208.title: Master of English Thesis Workshop
ENGLISH 208.description: Students practice the scholarly genres that they will use throughout their career as an academic. The ultimate goal is to move toward a finished piece of writing: a masters thesis.

ENGLISH 210.title: Studies in Literary History
ENGLISH 210.description: Studies in selected areas of literary history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGLISH 255.title: Graduate Workshop in Academic Publishing
ENGLISH 255.description: Reading and critique of student-authored essays with the goal of producing a publishable essay. Instructor leads discussion, meets with students individually, and provides an introduction to appropriate venues for publication and the process of submission, peer review, and revision.

ENGLISH 290.title: Reading and Conference
ENGLISH 290.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGLISH 291.title: Guided Reading Course
ENGLISH 291.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGLISH 299.title: Dissertation Research
ENGLISH 299.description: A units-only course for students in the dissertation phase.

ENGLISH 398.title: Rhetoric/Teaching of Composition
ENGLISH 398.description: Readings, lectures, and internship designed to prepare graduate students to teach composition. Formal instruction in rhetoric and practical work in teaching methods and grading.

ENGLISH 399.title: University Teaching
ENGLISH 399.description: A units-only course for students appointed as teaching assistants or associates.

ENGR 1A.title: General Chemistry for Engineers
ENGR 1A.description: Emphasis on solid-state chemistry. Quantum theory, atomic structure, periodic trends, chemical bonding, molecular orbitals, electronic band structure, gases, liquids, intermolecular forces, unit cells, crystal lattices, phase transformations, and electrochemistry.
ENGR 1A.prereq_text: AP Chemistry with a minimum score of 3 or SAT Subject Chemistry with a minimum score of 600 or SAT Mathematics with a minimum score of 600 or ACT Mathematics with a minimum score of 27. A score of 85 or higher on the Engineering Chemistry Placement Exam (fee required) is also accepted.
ENGR 1A.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors, Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, Materials Science Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 7A.title: Introduction to Engineering I
ENGR 7A.description: Introduction to engineering disciplines and the design process. Students enrolled in the online lecture also attend a three-hour lab on campus. Materials Fee
ENGR 7A.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 7B.title: Introduction to Engineering II
ENGR 7B.description: Introduction to engineering disciplines and the design process. Students enrolled in the online lecture also attend a three-hour lab on campus. Materials Fee
ENGR 7B.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 30.title: Statics
ENGR 30.description: Addition and resolution of forces, distributed forces, equivalent system of forces centroids, first moments, moments and products on inertia, equilibrium of rigid bodies, trusses, beams, cables.
ENGR 30.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 54.title: Principles of Materials Science and Engineering
ENGR 54.description: Superconductors to biodegradable polymers. Structure and properties of materials, including metal, ceramics, polymers, semiconductors, composites, traditional materials. Atomic structure, bonding, defects, phase equilibria, mechanical properties, electrical, optical and magnetic properties. Introduction to materials processing and synthesis. Materials Fee
ENGR 54.prereq_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A or CHEM H2A) and PHYSICS 7C.
ENGR 54.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 80.title: Dynamics
ENGR 80.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.
ENGR 80.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, Materials Science and Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 92.title: Engineering and Computer Educational Laboratory
ENGR 92.description: Comprehensive academic support designed primarily for underrepresented or underprepared students in Engineering, ICS, or selected areas of the physical sciences. Typical program activities: tutoring, study skills, career planning, self-esteem enhancement, library research techniques.

ENGR 93.title: Public and Professional Service in Engineering
ENGR 93.description: Student participation in public and professional service activities related to engineering.

ENGR 98.title: Group Study
ENGR 98.description: Group study of selected topics in engineering.

ENGR 100.title: Special Topics in Fabrication Safety
ENGR 100.description: Hands on training in the safe use of item fabrication: metalworking, woodworking, electronics fabrication, composites, welding, adhesives, water disposal, and others. Safety certification will be granted from this course and is required for access to Engineering School fabrication facilities.
ENGR 100.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 113.title: Introduction to STEM Education Research
ENGR 113.description: Introduces students to education research and topics studied in STEM education. Enables students to develop research questions, participate in research projects, design and utilize research tools, and contribute to STEM education research products.
ENGR 113.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 150.title: Mechanics of Structures
ENGR 150.description: Introduction to mechanics of materials. Topics include stresses and strains, axial and torsional loading, bending, shear, combined loading, stress and strain transformation, failure theories, beam deflection, and buckling.
ENGR 150.prereq_text: (ENGRCEE 30 or ENGR 30 or ENGRMAE 30) and MATH 3A.
ENGR 150.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 165.title: Advanced Manufacturing
ENGR 165.description: Principles in manufacturing processes. All machining requires energy: mechanical (cutting and shaping), heat energy (laser cutting), photochemical (photolithography), chemical energy (electro chemical machining and chemical vapor deposition). These methods and their fundamentals are examined. Materials Fee
ENGR 165.restriction: Seniors and School of Engineering students only.

ENGR 180.title: Entrepreneurship for Scientists and Engineers
ENGR 180.description: Learn the theory and practice of entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship. Covers positioning an idea, establishing the value propositions and benefits case, going to market strategy, creating an execution plan, and raising funds. Concepts are applied to a real-world venture project.
ENGR 180.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGR 189.title: Senior Project - Topics Vary
ENGR 189.description: Multidisciplinary group senior project of theoretical or applied nature involving design.

ENGR 190W.title: Communications in the Professional World
ENGR 190W.description: Upper-division technical writing course including the development of presentation skills. Effective communication with a range of audiences. Recognition of ethical and professional responsibilities for engineers.
ENGR 190W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
ENGR 190W.restriction: School of Engineering students only. Graduating seniors with an application on file have first consideration.

ENGR 191.title: Curricular Practical Training
ENGR 191.description: Practical training under an industry mentor in a technical field corresponding to students' area of interest.

ENGR 195.title: Special Topics in Engineering
ENGR 195.description: Studies in selected areas of Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGR 196W.title: Engineering Thesis
ENGR 196W.description: Preparation of final presentation and paper describing individual research in Engineering completed in one or more quarters of individual study (i.e., ENGR 199).
ENGR 196W.prereq_text: Completion of at least 4 units of Individual Research in Engineering. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ENGR H196W.title: Honors Thesis
ENGR H196W.description: Preparation of final presentation and paper describing individual research in Engineering. For participants in the Campuswide Honors Program.
ENGR H196W.prereq_text: ENGR H199. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

ENGR 199.title: Individual Study
ENGR 199.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

ENGR 199P.title: Individual Study
ENGR 199P.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

ENGR H199.title: Individual Study for Honors Students
ENGR H199.description: Supervised research in Engineering for participants in the Campuswide Honors Program. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

ENGR 201P.title: Leadership I: Foundations and Innovation
ENGR 201P.description: Establishes a shared foundation in leadership, management, and innovation. Exposes students to a spectrum of leadership pathways, including intrapreneurship, product and engineering leadership, people and team management, and project and program execution.

ENGR 202P.title: Leadership II: Opportunity Design and Build
ENGR 202P.description: Prepares students to operate as product-focused engineering leaders responsible for translating ideas into executable, scalable products. Emphasizes how to define and prioritize product features, align engineering and business objectives, lead cross-functional collaboration.

ENGR 203P.title: Leadership III: Execution and Impact
ENGR 203P.description: Prepares students to operate as engineering managers and product leaders responsible for taking a product from final development through launch and market adoption. Simulates real-world product launch environments, where success depends on building the product and delivering business outcomes.

ENGR 205P.title: Technical Project Management
ENGR 205P.description: Project management is the most effective method of delivering products within cost, schedule, and resource constraints. Students gain a strong working knowledge of the basics of technical project management, particularly, managing scope, planning, budgeting, resourcing, and risk management.

ENGR 206P.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurial Thinking
ENGR 206P.description: Unlock innovation by learning the techniques, models, and tools to create unique products and solve complex problems. Uses real-world projects to provide hands-on experience from ideation to product go live to apply the course concepts.

ENGR 207P.title: People Management and Communication
ENGR 207P.description: Students gain knowledge on the strategies to effectively manage people. This includes improving recruitment and retention, training, managing conflicts, motivating people, giving feedback, and effective communication to manage each direct report.

ENGR 210P.title: Capstone Project
ENGR 210P.description: Students are required to complete a project that deals with a specific emphasis of their Master of Engineering concentration/specialization.

ENGR 211P.title: M.Eng Proseminar
ENGR 211P.description: Provides students in the Master of Engineering program with information and practical skills for success in the M.Eng program as well as for professional development career planning.

ENGR 230P.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
ENGR 230P.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in programming and machine learning. The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to the field of machine learning and related techniques for students with a wide variety of engineering degrees.

ENGR 231P.title: Robotics and Controls
ENGR 231P.description: Covers basic aspects of robotic and mechatronic design, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, finite state machines, and implementation of advanced feedback control laws.

ENGR 233P.title: Additive Manufacturing
ENGR 233P.description: Covers the key concepts of Additive Manufacturing (AM, aka 3D printing), including historical perspectives, the general AM process chain, an overview of available AM technologies, materials for AM, and design strategies for AM.

ENGR 234P.title: Advanced Manufacturing and Design
ENGR 234P.description: An in-depth knowledge of manufacturing processes with focus on the fundamentals of materials processing (heat flow, mass flow, fluid flow, etc.). Processing fundamentals that apply to the three main classes of engineering materials: metals, ceramics, and polymers.

ENGR 235P.title: Engineering Design and Simulation: Tools and Process
ENGR 235P.description: Practical techniques and use of industry tools that improve the engineering design process by simulating the performance of design options prior to the costly steps of prototyping and manufacturing are covered. Applicable to a wide variety of engineering disciplines.

ENGR 243P.title: Robotics and Controls
ENGR 243P.description: Covers basic aspects of robotic and mechatronic design, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, finite state machines, and implementation of advanced feedback control laws.

ENGR 244P.title: Personalized Medical Devices
ENGR 244P.description: Introduces students to fundamental aspects of medical devices and discusses therapeutic as well as diagnostic devices. Basic aspects of microfluidics and biology critical to personalized medical systems are studied. Typical FDA approval pathways for medical devices are presented.

ENGR 252P.title: Fundamentals of Microfabrication
ENGR 252P.description: Introduces engineering and science students to the science of miniaturization. Different options to make very small machines (micro and nano size) are reviewed, materials choices are discussed, scaling laws are analyzed, and many practical applications are listed.

ENGR 265.title: Advanced Manufacturing
ENGR 265.description: Principles in manufacturing processes. All machining requires energy: mechanical (cutting and shaping), heat energy (laser cutting), photochemical (photolithography), chemical energy (electro chemical machining and chemical vapor deposition). These methods and their fundamentals are examined. Materials Fee

ENGR 290.title: Developing Teaching Excellence
ENGR 290.description: Introduces the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) as it applies to Engineering Education. Focuses on how teaching practice can be guided by the research literature on teaching and learning.

ENGR 290P.title: M.Eng Internship
ENGR 290P.description: Students go through practical training under an industry mentor in a technical field corresponding to their area of interest.

ENGR 291.title: Internship
ENGR 291.description: Practical training under an industry mentor in a technical field corresponding to the student's area of interest.

ENGR 295P.title: Special Topics in Master of Engineering
ENGR 295P.description: Studies in selected areas of Master of Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGR 298P.title: M.Eng Individual Project
ENGR 298P.description: Supervised independent project for Master of Engineering students under the direction of the selected faculty member.

ENGR 299.title: Individual Research
ENGR 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty.

ENGRCEE 11.title: Methods II: Probability and Statistics
ENGRCEE 11.description: Modeling and analysis of engineering problems under uncertainty. Engineering applications of probability and statistical concepts and methods.
ENGRCEE 11.prereq_text: (ENGRCEE 20 or EECS 10 or EECS 12 or ENGRMAE 10 or I&C SCI 31) and MATH 3A.
ENGRCEE 11.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 15.title: Introduction to Energy Systems
ENGRCEE 15.description: Introduces technological, economic, environmental, social, and political aspects behind power systems' design, planning, operations, and maintenance. Changes to demand and supply for electricity, climate change risks to power systems, and equity dimensions.

ENGRCEE 20.title: Introduction to Computational Problem Solving
ENGRCEE 20.description: Introduction to computer programming within a numerical computing environment (MATLAB or similar) including types of data representation, graphical display of data, and development of modular programs with application to engineering analysis and problem solving.
ENGRCEE 20.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 21.title: Computational Problem Solving
ENGRCEE 21.description: Engineering analysis and problem solving using MATLAB (or similar), including matrix algebra, solving systems of linear and nonlinear equations, numerical integration of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and coupled ODEs, and analysis of numerical errors.
ENGRCEE 21.prereq_text: (ENGRCEE 20 or BME 60B) and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N).
ENGRCEE 21.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 30.title: Statics
ENGRCEE 30.description: Addition and resolution of forces, distributed forces, equivalent system of forces centroids, first moments, moments and products on inertia, equilibrium of rigid bodies, trusses, beams, cables.
ENGRCEE 30.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 40.title: Fundamentals of Economic Analysis for Scientists and Engineers
ENGRCEE 40.description: Introduction to microeconomics and cost benefit analysis. Integration of economic, social, and behavioral considerations into the engineering design process. Applications to contemporary problems via case studies.

ENGRCEE 50.title: Infrastructure Equity
ENGRCEE 50.description: The intersection of social justice with the built and natural environment through theories of equity and justice to analyze transportation, housing, water systems, energy service disparities in historically marginalized and underserved communities of color in California.

ENGRCEE 60.title: Contemporary and Emerging Environmental Challenges
ENGRCEE 60.description: Introduces contemporary and emerging environmental challenges, illustrates links between human behavior, environmental policy, and engineering practices, examines policy options in the context of current institutions, and introduces tools and frameworks to reach sound economic, social, and environmental solutions.

ENGRCEE 80.title: Dynamics
ENGRCEE 80.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.
ENGRCEE 80.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, Materials Science and Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 81A.title: Civil Engineering Practicum I
ENGRCEE 81A.description: Introduction to civil engineering through presentations on structural, environmental, water, and transportation systems. Introduction to graphics. Graphical visualization and communication using hand and computer sketching. Fundamentals of Computer Aided Design (CAD) using AutoCad. Laboratory sessions. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 81A.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 81B.title: Civil Engineering Practicum II
ENGRCEE 81B.description: Principles of surveying; fundamentals of Geographic Information Systems (GIS); introduction to the state-of-the-art and future areas of the profession, including applications of advanced technology and computers; Introduction to visualization and communication of design concepts; laboratory sessions. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 81B.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 110.title: Methods III: Modeling, Economics, and Management
ENGRCEE 110.description: Analysis, modeling, and management of civil engineering systems. Statistics and system performance studies, probabilistic models and simulation, basic economics and capital investments, project elements and organization, managerial concepts and network technique, project scheduling. Emphasis on real-world examples. Laboratory sessions.
ENGRCEE 110.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 111.title: Methods IV: Systems Analysis and Decision-Making
ENGRCEE 111.description: Analysis and optimization for decision-making in civil and infrastructural systems. Topics include linear programming formulations and solution algorithms, network models, and logistical models. Emphasis is on project-level and managerial decision-making and selection from alternative designs.
ENGRCEE 111.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 114.title: GIS for Civil and Environmental Engineering
ENGRCEE 114.description: GIS for CEE provides an introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their various applications in civil and environmental engineering. Topics include GIS data formats, data queries, spatial and attribute data, spatial data analysis, coordinate systems, and raster data analysis.

ENGRCEE 121.title: Transportation Systems I: Analysis and Design
ENGRCEE 121.description: Introduction to analysis and design of fundamental transportation system components, basic elements of geometric and pavement design, vehicle flow and elementary traffic, basic foundations of transportation planning and forecasting. Laboratory sessions.
ENGRCEE 121.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 122.title: Transportation Systems II: Operations and Control
ENGRCEE 122.description: Introduction to fundamentals of urban traffic engineering, including data collection, analysis, and design. Traffic engineering studies, traffic flow theory, traffic control devices, traffic signals, capacity and level of service analysis of freeways and urban streets. Laboratory sessions.
ENGRCEE 122.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 123.title: Transportation Systems III: Planning and Forecasting
ENGRCEE 123.description: Theoretical foundations of transportation planning, design, and analysis methods. Theory and application of aggregate and disaggregate models for land use development, trip generation, destination, mode, and route choice. Transportation network analysis. Planning, design, and evaluation of system alternatives.
ENGRCEE 123.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 124.title: Transportation Systems IV: Freeway Operations and Control
ENGRCEE 124.description: Fundamentals of traffic on urban freeways, including data collection analysis, and design. Traffic engineering studies, traffic flow theory, freeway traffic control devices, capacity, and level of service analysis of freeways and highways. Laboratory sessions.
ENGRCEE 124.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 125.title: Transportation and the Environment
ENGRCEE 125.description: Analysis of the impacts of motor vehicle transportation on the environment. Introduction to life cycle analysis applied to transportation. Basic economic tools for transportation externalities. Transportation planning, urban form, health, and the environment. Transportation sustainability.
ENGRCEE 125.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 127.title: Innovation in Transportation
ENGRCEE 127.description: Survey and critical assessment of the costs and benefits of recent and emerging innovations in passenger and freight transportation. Topics include: driverless vehicles, drones, shared micromobility, fare-free transit, congestion pricing, transportation electrification, transportation systems analysis.

ENGRCEE 130.title: Soil Mechanics
ENGRCEE 130.description: Mechanics of soils, composition and classification of soils, compaction, compressibility and consolidation, shear strength, seepage, bearing capacity, lateral earth pressure, retaining walls, piles.
ENGRCEE 130.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 130L.title: Soil Mechanics Laboratory
ENGRCEE 130L.description: Laboratory procedures of soil testing for engineering problems. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 130L.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 149.title: Introduction to Earthquake Engineering
ENGRCEE 149.description: Earthquake characteristics, ground motion, and fundamental structural response concepts. Seismic load determination including equivalent lateral force procedure, including vertical distribution and diaphragm forces. Seismic load combinations and load paths. Application of building code seismic requirements for steel, concrete, and timber.
ENGRCEE 149.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 11 and (ENGRCEE 20 or BME 60B) and ENGRCEE 151A.
ENGRCEE 149.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 150.title: Mechanics of Materials
ENGRCEE 150.description: Stresses and strains, strain-stress diagrams, axial deformations, torsion, bending and shear stresses in beams, shear force and bending moment diagrams, combined stresses, principal stresses, Mohr's circle, deflection of beams, columns.
ENGRCEE 150.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 30 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGRMAE 30 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGR 30 with a minimum grade of C-.
ENGRCEE 150.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 150L.title: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
ENGRCEE 150L.description: Experimental methods and fundamentals for mechanics of materials analysis. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 150L.prereq_text: (ENGRCEE 30 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGRMAE 30 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGR 30 with a minimum grade of C-) and ENGRCEE 150.
ENGRCEE 150L.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 151A.title: Structural Analysis
ENGRCEE 151A.description: Fundamentals of structural analysis and loading. Deformation of statically determinate and indeterminate structures. Influence lines. Structural systems.
ENGRCEE 151A.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 151B.title: Structural Timber Design
ENGRCEE 151B.description: Design of timber structures. Beams, columns, beam-columns, roof, and connections.
ENGRCEE 151B.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 151C.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
ENGRCEE 151C.description: Ultimate strength design. Design of reinforced concrete beam sections. Design for shear and deflection. Design of columns. Design of isolated and combined footings. Laboratory sessions. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 151C.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 152.title: Computer Methods in Structural Analysis and Design
