ENGRCEE 152.description: Matrix techniques for indeterminate framed structures. Computer implementation using the stiffness method. Software packages for design of reinforced concrete, steel, and/or timber structures.
ENGRCEE 152.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 155.title: Structural Steel Design
ENGRCEE 155.description: Design in steel of tension members, beams, columns, welded and bolted connections; eccentrically loaded and moment resistant joints; plate girders. Plastic design; load and resistance factor design. Composite construction; introduction to computer-aided design.
ENGRCEE 155.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 156.title: Foundation Design
ENGRCEE 156.description: Applications of soil mechanics principles to the analysis and design of shallow foundations, retaining walls, pile foundations, and braced cuts. Design criteria: bearing capacity, working loads and tolerable settlements, structural integrity of the foundation element. Damage from construction operations.
ENGRCEE 156.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 160.title: Environmental Processes
ENGRCEE 160.description: Introduction to environmental processes in air and water, mass balances, and transport phenomena. Fundamentals of water-quality engineering including water and wastewater treatment.
ENGRCEE 160.restriction: Civil Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 162.title: Introduction to Environmental Chemistry
ENGRCEE 162.description: Basic concepts from general, physical, and analytical chemistry as they relate to environmental engineering. Particular emphasis on the fundamentals of equilibrium and kinetics as they apply to acid-base chemistry, gas solubility, and redox reactions. Laboratory sessions. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 162.prereq_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A or CHEM H2A) and (CHEM 1B or CHEM H2B) and (CHEM 1LC or CHEM 1LE or CHEM H2LB or CHEM M2LB) and (CHEM 51A or CHEM H52A).
ENGRCEE 162.restriction: Chemical Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 163.title: Wastewater Treatment Process Design
ENGRCEE 163.description: Design of biological treatment processes. Topics include attached and suspended growth, aeration, anaerobic systems, process control, and economics. Design projects included. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 163.restriction: Civil Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 164.title: Carbon and Energy Footprint Analysis
ENGRCEE 164.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Mass- and energy-balance analysis applied to water and wastewater treatment systems. Case studies include analysis of water supply, treatment, reclamation, and reuse.
ENGRCEE 164.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 165.title: Unit Operations II in Environmental Engineering
ENGRCEE 165.description: Theory and dynamics of physical, chemical, and biological processes for water and wastewater treatment. Topics include: mixing; coagulation/flocculation; barrier and gravity separations; biological treatment: aerobic, anoxic, anaerobic; control strategies.
ENGRCEE 165.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 166.title: Microbial Processes for Bioremediation
ENGRCEE 166.description: Fundamental knowledge on microbiology, organic chemistry, biodegradability and persistence, reaction kinetics, and contaminant transport of water and soil remediation of organic contaminants under aerobic and anaerobic conditions. Overview of Environmental Law and Superfund. Design project of bioremediation for contaminated site.
ENGRCEE 166.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 167.title: Fundamentals of Sustainable Engineering
ENGRCEE 167.description: Introduces students to sustainability and its connection to civil and environmental engineering infrastructure. Course topics are divided into environmental, economic, and social sustainability and include life cycle assessment, life cycle costing, and robust quantitative methods that support decision-making.

ENGRCEE 168.title: Microorganisms and Climate Change
ENGRCEE 168.description: Climate change and impacts on microbial processes: greenhouse gas generation, biogeochemical cycles, permafrost thawing, ocean acidification, eutrophication, pathogen proliferation. Microorganism-based solutions that can mitigate climate change impacts (microbial greenhouse control, production of lower carbon and energy footprint goods, carbon sequestration).

ENGRCEE 169.title: Environmental Microbiology for Engineers
ENGRCEE 169.description: Fundamental and applied principles of microbiology. Structures and functions of microorganisms, the microbiology of water, wastewater and soil used in environmental engineering, and the impact of microorganisms on human and environmental health.
ENGRCEE 169.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 170.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
ENGRCEE 170.description: Thermodynamic and mechanical fluid properties; fluid statics; control volume and differential approaches for mass, momentum, and energy; dimensional analysis and similarity.
ENGRCEE 170.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 171.title: Water Resources Engineering
ENGRCEE 171.description: Principles governing the analysis and design of water resource systems including pressurized pipelines, pipe networks, channels, and ground water. Coverage of fluid mass, momentum and energy conservation, flow resistance, and related laboratory measurements in different systems. Materials Fee
ENGRCEE 171.restriction: Chemical Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 172.title: Groundwater Hydrology
ENGRCEE 172.description: Topics include conservation of fluid mass, storage properties of porous media, matrix compressibility, boundary conditions, flow nets, well hydraulics, groundwater chemistry, and solute transport. Design projects and computer applications included.
ENGRCEE 172.restriction: Civil Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 173.title: Watershed Modeling
ENGRCEE 173.description: Basic principles of hydrologic modeling are practiced. Concepts of watershed delineation, land use change impact, design studies, and GIS tools are discussed. Focus on the USACE (HEC) software tools (HEC-HMS, and HEC-RAS) along with their associated GIS interfaces.
ENGRCEE 173.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 175.title: Stochastic Hydrology
ENGRCEE 175.description: Statistical methods relevant for water resources engineering and hydrologic/ geophysical data analysis for decision making. Estimation of design events, analysis of time series and spatio-temporally correlated fields, and applications to flood frequency analysis, climate extremes and subsurface characterization.
ENGRCEE 175.restriction: Seniors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 176.title: Hydrology
ENGRCEE 176.description: Elements of the hydrologic cycle including precipitation, infiltration, evapotranspiration, ground water, and runoff. Unit Hydrograph theory and routing methods. Introduction to precipitation/runoff relationship and watershed modeling. Statistical methods and flood frequency analysis.
ENGRCEE 176.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 178.title: Fluid Mechanics of Open Channels
ENGRCEE 178.description: Fundamentals of fluid motion in open channels. Navier-Stokes equations and one-dimensional momentum and energy principles. Topics include rapidly varied flow, flow resistance and turbulence, gradually varied flow, unsteady flow, and computational methods for channel flow modeling.
ENGRCEE 178.prereq_text: (ENGRCEE 20 or BME 60B or ENGRMAE 10) and (ENGRCEE 170 or ENGRMAE 130A or CBE 120A).
ENGRCEE 178.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRCEE 181A.title: Senior Design Practicum I
ENGRCEE 181A.description: Team designs land development project including infrastructural, environmental, circulation aspects. Focus on traffic impact studies, design of roads, geometry, signals, geotechnical and hydrological analysis, design of structural elements, economic analysis. Oral/Written interim and final design reports. Laboratory sessions.
ENGRCEE 181A.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 81A and ENGRCEE 81B and ENGRCEE 110 and (ENGRCEE 121 or ENGRCEE 151C or ENGRCEE 162 or ENGRCEE 171). ENGRCEE 181A and ENGRCEE 181B and ENGRCEE 181C must be taken in the same academic year.
ENGRCEE 181A.restriction: Seniors, Civil Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors only.

ENGRCEE 181B.title: Senior Design Practicum II
ENGRCEE 181B.description: Team designs land development project including infrastructural, environmental, circulation aspects. Focus on traffic impact studies, design of roads, geometry, signals, geotechnical and hydrological analysis, design of structural elements, economic analysis. Oral/Written interim and final design reports. Laboratory sessions.
ENGRCEE 181B.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 181A. ENGRCEE 181A and ENGRCEE 181B and ENGRCEE 181C must be taken in the same academic year.
ENGRCEE 181B.restriction: Seniors, Civil Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors only.

ENGRCEE 181C.title: Senior Design Practicum III
ENGRCEE 181C.description: Team designs land development project including infrastructural, environmental, circulation aspects. Focus on traffic impact studies, design of roads, geometry, signals, geotechnical and hydrological analysis, design of structural elements, economic analysis. Oral/Written interim and final design reports. Laboratory sessions.
ENGRCEE 181C.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 181B. ENGRCEE 181A and ENGRCEE 181B and ENGRCEE 181C must be taken in the same academic year.
ENGRCEE 181C.restriction: Seniors, Civil Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors only.

ENGRCEE 195.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
ENGRCEE 195.description: Studies in selected areas of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGRCEE 197.title: Civil and Environmental Engineering Internship
ENGRCEE 197.description: Students majoring in CEE may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.

ENGRCEE 198.title: Group Study
ENGRCEE 198.description: Group study of selected topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering.

ENGRCEE 199.title: Individual Study
ENGRCEE 199.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

ENGRCEE 199P.title: Individual Study
ENGRCEE 199P.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

ENGRCEE 201P.title: Life Cycle Assessment Methods
ENGRCEE 201P.description: Introduction and application of life cycle assessment methods for characterizing resource consumption and environmental emissions of products and civil infrastructure systems. Life cycle inventory development, system boundaries and scoping, calculation of environmental impact indicators.

ENGRCEE 202P.title: Green Building Design
ENGRCEE 202P.description: Application of life cycle assessment methods to green and sustainable building design. Overview and application of building sustainability rating and certification systems using the LEED framework. Assessment and comparison of different building types.

ENGRCEE 203P.title: Organizational Pollutant Emissions Accounting
ENGRCEE 203P.description: Application of life cycle assessment methods to account for emissions from the supply chain of products and infrastructure systems. Calculation and proper interpretation of Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions categories and emissions footprint metrics.

ENGRCEE 204P.title: Fundamentals of Sustainable Engineering
ENGRCEE 204P.description: Introduction to sustainability and its connection to environmental engineering infrastructure: economic/social sustainability, lifecycle assessment/cost, water and waste management, empathy in engineering, quantitative approaches for social sustainability, and decision-making across sustainability metrics. Includes guest lectures and field trips.

ENGRCEE 205P.title: Wastewater Treatment Process Design
ENGRCEE 205P.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Topics include solids separation, biological treatment, aeration, sludge stabilization, process control, and economics. Design projects included.

ENGRCEE 206P.title: Biological Processes for Bioremediation
ENGRCEE 206P.description: Fundamental knowledge on microbiology, organic chemistry, biodegradability and persistence, reaction kinetics, and for development of water and soil remediation of organic contaminants under aerobic and anaerobic conditions. Overview of Environmental Law and Superfund.

ENGRCEE 207P.title: Introduction to Data Science Programming and Optimization
ENGRCEE 207P.description: Basics of object-oriented programming; data analysis using scientific programming packages; best programming practices; civil and environmental engineering analysis and design of linear systems; introduction to the analysis and design of non-linear systems in civil engineering.

ENGRCEE 208P.title: Data Analytics for Civil Engineers
ENGRCEE 208P.description: Quantitative research methods and statistical techniques for analyzing and viewing civil and environmental engineering data. Descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, linear and logical regression, clustering and introduction to machine learning.

ENGRCEE 209P.title: Applied Sustainability Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering Practice
ENGRCEE 209P.description: Case studies guiding project-based assignments for applying sustainability fundamentals, pollution and life-cycle cost analyses, and green building design principles to real-world problems in civil and environmental engineering.
ENGRCEE 209P.restriction: M.Engr. - Civil and Environmental Engineering majors only.

ENGRCEE 210P.title: Smart City Transport Systems
ENGRCEE 210P.description: Focuses on engineering methods and concepts associated with smart cities and applies these methods and concepts to analyze emerging and future transportation technologies, services, and systems.

ENGRCEE 211P.title: Sustainable Transportation
ENGRCEE 211P.description: Overview of the impacts of transportation on the environment, with an emphasis on air pollution from motor vehicles, but including broader impacts such as regional air quality, noise, human health, water and solid waste pollution, land use, and climate change.

ENGRCEE 212P.title: Transportation Policy and Technology
ENGRCEE 212P.description: The process of planning, designing, and managing the transportation system from the perspective of current and emerging transportation policies and technologies. Focus on technical and institutional perspectives on issues.

ENGRCEE 213P.title: Air Pollution Science and Control
ENGRCEE 213P.description: Concepts related to sources, dispersion, and effects of air pollutants. Topics include emission factors, emission inventory, air pollution, meteorology, air chemistry, air quality modeling, impact assessment, source and ambient monitoring, regional control strategies.

ENGRCEE 214.title: GIS for Civil and Environmental Engineering
ENGRCEE 214.description: GIS for CEE provides an introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their various applications in civil and environmental engineering. Topics include GIS data formats, data queries, spatial and attribute data, spatial data analysis, coordinate systems, raster data analysis.

ENGRCEE 215P.title: Environmental Permitting and Impact Reporting
ENGRCEE 215P.description: Regulatory frameworks, CEQA, NEPA. Environmental documents: Initial Studies, EIRs, EAs. Mitigation measures, legal challenges. Case studies, project-based exercises, industry guest lectures. Emphasis on practical applications, real-world environmental reviews, compliance, and permitting processes.

ENGRCEE 220A.title: Travel Demand Analysis I
ENGRCEE 220A.description: Fundamentals of transportation systems analysis. Theoretical aspects of travel demand. Travel behavior. Modeling of performance characteristics and costs of transportation modes. In-depth presentation of travel demand modeling techniques. Development of travel choice models including mode, route, and destination choice. Equilibrium.

ENGRCEE 220B.title: Travel Demand Analysis II
ENGRCEE 220B.description: Methods of discrete choice analysis and their applications in the modeling of transportation systems. Emphasis on the development of a sound understanding of theoretical aspects of discrete choice modeling that are useful in many applications in travel demand analysis.
ENGRCEE 220B.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 220A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 220C.title: Travel Demand Analysis III: Activity-based Approaches
ENGRCEE 220C.description: The methodological underpinnings of activity-based travel demand modeling. Presents methodologies within the context of a generalization of discrete choice modeling approaches, emphasizing the distinctions that separtate these two approaches and presenting appropriate mathematical and statistical tools to address these distinctions.
ENGRCEE 220C.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 220A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 221A.title: Transportation Systems Analysis I
ENGRCEE 221A.description: Introduction to mathematical methods and models to address logistics and urban transportation problems. Techniques include stochastic models, queueing theory, linear programming, and introductory non-linear optimization.

ENGRCEE 221B.title: Transportation Systems Analysis II
ENGRCEE 221B.description: Advanced mathematical methods and models to address logistics and urban transportation problems. Topics include network flows, advanced optimization techniques, network models, and heuristic algorithms.
ENGRCEE 221B.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 221A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 221C.title: Transportation Systems Analysis III: Stochastic Simulation for Design of Mobility and Logistics Services
ENGRCEE 221C.description: Fundamentals and applied methods for simulating stochastic and stochastic-dynamic transportation systems. Topics include uncertainty modeling of inputs, discrete-event simulation, programming simulation logic in Python, generating random variates, analyzing simulation outputs, experimental design, model verification and validation.

ENGRCEE 222.title: Transit Systems Planning
ENGRCEE 222.description: Planning methods for public transportation in urban areas. Technological and operating characteristics of vehicles, facilities, and systems. Short-range planning techniques: data collection and analysis, demand analysis, mode choice, operational strategies, financial analysis. Design of systems to improve performance.

ENGRCEE 223.title: Transportation Systems III: Planning and Forecasting
ENGRCEE 223.description: Theoretical foundations of transportation planning, design, and analysis methods. Theory and application of aggregate and disaggregate models for land use development, trip generation, destination, mode, and route choice. Transportation network analysis. Planning, design, and evaluation of system alternatives.

ENGRCEE 224A.title: Transportation Data Analysis I
ENGRCEE 224A.description: Statistical analysis of transportation data sources. Analysis of categorical and ordinal data. Regression and advanced multivariate analysis methods such as discriminant analysis, canonical correlation, and factor analysis. Sampling techniques, sample error and bias, survey instrument design.

ENGRCEE 226A.title: Traffic Flow Theory I
ENGRCEE 226A.description: Traffic measurement and fundamental speed-density-flow relationships. Kinematic models. Shock waves. Statistical-kinetic theory of traffic. Introductory car-following principles and stability. Gap acceptance. Platoon dispersion. Two-fluid model. Queueing process. Multi-regime and catastrophe models. Higher-order continuum models. Microscopic and macroscopic simulation.

ENGRCEE 226B.title: Traffic Flow Theory II
ENGRCEE 226B.description: Advanced mathematical analysis of vehicular flow. Detailed treatise on car-following models. Fourier and Laplace analysis of stability problems. Perturbation analysis. Derivation of macroscopic traffic flow relationships from microscopic considerations. Advanced hydrodynamic theory.
ENGRCEE 226B.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 226A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 227.title: Innovation in Transportation
ENGRCEE 227.description: Survey and critical assessment of the costs and benefits of recent and emerging innovations in passenger and freight transportation. Topics include: driverless vehicles, drones, shared micromobility, fare-free transit, congestion pricing, transportation electrification, transportation systems analysis.

ENGRCEE 228A.title: Urban Transportation Networks I
ENGRCEE 228A.description: Analytical approaches and algorithms to the formulation and solution of the equilibrium assignment problem for transportation networks. Emphasis on user equilibrium (UE) comparison with system optimal, mathematical programming formulation, supply functions, estimation. Estimating origin-destination matrices, network design problems.
ENGRCEE 228A.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 220A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 228B.title: Urban Transportation Networks II
ENGRCEE 228B.description: Advanced analysis, optimization, and modeling of transportation networks. Topics include advanced static and dynamic traffic assignment algorithms, linear and nonlinear multi-commodity network flow optimization, network simplex, and network control problems.
ENGRCEE 228B.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 221A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRCEE 228A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 229A.title: Traffic Systems Operations and Control I
ENGRCEE 229A.description: Introduction to operation, control, and analysis of arterial and freeway traffic systems. Control concepts, traffic stream principles, detectors, local controllers, system masters, traffic signal and ramp metering timing principles, traffic measurement technologies, traffic delay principles.

ENGRCEE 231.title: Foundation Engineering
ENGRCEE 231.description: Essentials for design and analysis of structural members that transmit superstructure loads to the ground. Topics include subsurface investigations, excavation, dewatering, bracing, footing, mat foundations, piles and pile foundations, caissons and cofferdams, other special foundations.

ENGRCEE 231P.title: Foundation Engineering
ENGRCEE 231P.description: Essentials for design and analysis of structural members that transmit superstructure loads to the ground. Topics include subsurface investigations, excavation, dewatering, bracing, footing, mat foundations, piles and pile foundations, caissons and cofferdams, other special foundations.

ENGRCEE 232.title: Geotech Earthquake Engineering
ENGRCEE 232.description: In-situ and laboratory determination of dynamic soil properties, liquefaction of soil, cyclic softening of clays, seismic compression and settlement analyses, ground improvement methods, seismic slope stability, introduction to soil structure interaction.

ENGRCEE 234P.title: Adv Structural Modeling with Commercial Software
ENGRCEE 234P.description: Nonlinear analysis fundamentals, pushover and time history analysis, material and component cyclic modeling and validation. Damping considerations, practical modeling challenges. Applied use of commercial software for nonlinear structural modeling.

ENGRCEE 235P.title: Applied Structural Seismic Design and Evaluation
ENGRCEE 235P.description: Contemporary and emerging structural design/assessment methods, performance-based seismic design, hazard analysis, engineering response assessment, prediction of collapse, damage and loss modeling. Project involving performance assessment of multistory buildings.
ENGRCEE 235P.restriction: M.Engr. - Civil and Environmental Engineering majors only.

ENGRCEE 236P.title: Practical Soil-Structure Interaction for Infrastructure
ENGRCEE 236P.description: Principles and applications of soil-structure interaction in foundation and structural design. Topics include seismic effects, numerical modeling, superstructure implications, and case studies. Hands-on use of industry software to simulate and evaluate real-world geo-structural systems.

ENGRCEE 237P.title: Building Information Modeling and Structural Design Management
ENGRCEE 237P.description: Understanding integration of Building Information Modeling (BIM) into structural design workflows. Focus on project coordination, collaboration with other contractors, and effective management of design data to streamline construction processes and ensure project success including plan reading and interpretation.

ENGRCEE 240.title: High Performance Materials
ENGRCEE 240.description: Part I: Linear and nonlinear fracture mechanics, methodology, real-world case studies; Part II: Composite material toughening, underlying micromechanics, materials engineering towards microstructure tailoring and new material design approaches; Part III: Emerging high-performance engineering materials for safety, energy and the environment.

ENGRCEE 242.title: Advanced Strength of Materials
ENGRCEE 242.description: Beams on elastic foundations. Combined axial and lateral loads. Curved beams. Unsymmetric bending. Shear center. Stresses and strains. Basic equations for theory of elasticity. Energy principles. Theory of torsion. Combined bending and torsion.

ENGRCEE 243.title: Mechanics of Composite Materials
ENGRCEE 243.description: Stress-strain relationship for orthotropic materials; invariant properties of an orthotropic lamina; biaxial strength theory for an orthotropic lamina; mechanics of materials approach to stiffness; elasticity approach to stiffness; classical lamination theory; strength of laminates; statistical theory of fatigue damage.

ENGRCEE 247.title: Structural Dynamics
ENGRCEE 247.description: Vibration of discrete and continuous mass elastic systems. Isolation and transmissability. Dynamic recording instruments. Introduction to nonlinear theory of vibration. Response of structures to earthquake, traffic, and wind loads. Response spectra concepts. Normal mode analysis. Numerical integration techniques.

ENGRCEE 247P.title: Structural Dynamics
ENGRCEE 247P.description: Dynamic equilibrium of structures. Response of a single degree of freedom system to dynamic excitation: free vibration, harmonic loads, pulses, and earthquakes. Response spectra. Response of multi-degree of freedom systems. Seismic behavior of buildings and the basis of seismic building.

ENGRCEE 249.title: Earthquake Engineering
ENGRCEE 249.description: Nature and mechanics of earthquakes. Seismic hazard analysis. Structural analysis methods for earthquake engineering. Determination of seismic demand forces and displacements. Nonlinear response, ductile systems, hysteretic behavior. Application of seismic design principles for buildings and bridges.

ENGRCEE 250.title: Finite Element Method in Structural Engineering
ENGRCEE 250.description: Finite element concepts in structural engineering including variational formulations, shape functions, elements assembly, convergence and computer programming. Stiffness of truss, beam, and frame members, two- and three-dimensional solids, plate and shell elements. Static, vibration, stability, and inelastic analysis.

ENGRCEE 250P.title: Finite Element Method in Structural Engineering
ENGRCEE 250P.description: Finite element concepts in structural engineering including mathematical/variational formulations, shape functions, elements assembly, convergence, and computer programming; stiffness of truss, beam, and frame members; and two- and three-dimensional solids.

ENGRCEE 251.title: Performance-Based Structural Engineering
ENGRCEE 251.description: Introduction and implementation of current approaches in performance-based assessment and design of building structures. Emphasis is on applied and evolving methods and tools for exercising performance-based engineering of building structures.
ENGRCEE 251.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 247 with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRCEE 249 with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 252.title: Multiscale Modeling of Materials and Structures
ENGRCEE 252.description: Introduction to modeling materials and structures across length and time scales. Emphasis is on fundamental concepts, numerical simulation techniques, and algorithms for exercising multiscale modeling from nano to meso and microscale.

ENGRCEE 253.title: Micromechanics
ENGRCEE 253.description: Micromechanics concepts in solid mechanics including eigenstrains, Eshelby equivalent inclusion theories, homogenization procedures, Mori-Tanaka method, self-consistent scheme, and effective mechanical behavior of composites.

ENGRCEE 254.title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Behavior and Design
ENGRCEE 254.description: Flexural strength of reinforced concrete elements. Flexural ductility of unconfined and confined members with axial loads. Shear and torsional behaviors. Strength of reinforced concrete ductile frames and shear walls. Reinforced concrete detailing.

ENGRCEE 254P.title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Behavior and Design
ENGRCEE 254P.description: Centers on advanced concepts in the design of reinforced concrete structures, encompassing areas such as two-way slabs, flat plates, slender columns, member ductility, special moment frames, shear walls, and incorporating sustainability considerations.
ENGRCEE 254P.prereq_text: Knowledge of reinforced concrete design and introduction to earthquake engineering.

ENGRCEE 255.title: Advanced Behavior and Design of Steel Structures
ENGRCEE 255.description: Advanced principles of structural steel design. Analysis and design of beam-column members, braced and unbraced frames for buildings, and plate girders. Review of seismic design provisions. Design of connections.

ENGRCEE 255P.title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
ENGRCEE 255P.description: Advanced principles of structural steel design with special coverage on the sustainability of structural steel as a building material. Technical coverage in the analysis and design of beam-column members, braced and unbraced frames for buildings, and plate girders.
ENGRCEE 255P.prereq_text: Knowledge of structural design engineering and seismic design provisions.

ENGRCEE 260.title: Desalination
ENGRCEE 260.description: Introduction of state of technology, costs and benefits, environmental issues, and implementation issues related to desalination. Emphasis on membrane processes and biofouling prevention.

ENGRCEE 262.title: Environmental Chemistry II
ENGRCEE 262.description: Advanced concepts from physical and organic chemistry as they relate to environmental engineering. Emphasis on equilibrium and kinetics as they apply to redox reactions, coordination, absorption, gas phase reactions, and ion exchange.

ENGRCEE 263.title: Advanced Biological Treatment Processes
ENGRCEE 263.description: Analysis of biological processes in natural and engineered systems. Biological treatment processes, both aerobic and anaerobic, with emphasis on suspended growth systems including design consideration. Containment degradation or control covered. Includes laboratory on molecular tools used in wastewater treatment.

ENGRCEE 264.title: Carbon and Energy Footprint Analysis
ENGRCEE 264.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Mass- and energy- balance analysis applied to water and wastewater treatment systems. Case studies include analysis of water supply, treatment, reclamation, and reuse.

ENGRCEE 264P.title: Carbon and Energy Footprint Analysis
ENGRCEE 264P.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Mass- and energy- balance analysis applied to water and wastewater treatment systems. Case studies include analysis of water supply, treatment, reclamation, and reuse.
ENGRCEE 264P.prereq_text: Undergraduate-level introduction to environmental processes, mass balances, and transport phenomena.

ENGRCEE 265.title: Unit Operations II in Environmental Engineering
ENGRCEE 265.description: Theory and dynamics of physical, chemical, and biological processes for water and wastewater treatment. Topics include mixing; coagulation/flocculation; barrier and gravity separations; biological treatment: aerobic, anoxic, anaerobic; control strategies.

ENGRCEE 266P.title: Biological Process Design
ENGRCEE 266P.description: Applied microbiology and engineering principles to understand and solve important environmental problems in water quality. Focus on biological processes within both engineered and natural systems, and utilizes fundamental stoichiometry, kinetics, and material balances to analyze and quantify microbial processes.

ENGRCEE 267.title: The Science and Engineering of Wildfires
ENGRCEE 267.description: Covers the fundamental science of wildfire behavior, scales, modeling techniques, and emerging engineering solutions to mitigate wildfire risks.

ENGRCEE 268.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics and Turbulence
ENGRCEE 268.description: Covers the nonlinear physics of turbulence flows with a focus on environmental applications.

ENGRCEE 269.title: Beach Dynamics
ENGRCEE 269.description: Coastal erosion in California, human and natural influences on southern California beaches, and present-day challenges. Littoral cells and sediment budgets. Water wave theory. Littoral sediment transport and shoreline change modeling. Shoreline stabilization using green and gray infrastructure.

ENGRCEE 269P.title: Beach Dynamics
ENGRCEE 269P.description: Provides an introduction to the processes that influence coastal erosion and morphological change and the broader factors that must be considered to implement projects such as project financing, coastal protection. Includes field trips to beaches in southern California.

ENGRCEE 270.title: Flood Risk and Modeling
ENGRCEE 270.description: Global and national trends in flooding and related impacts including disasters; flood risk management; theory and numerical methods for flood inundation modeling; flood risk communication strategies including flood hazard visualizations.

ENGRCEE 270P.title: Flood Risk and Modeling
ENGRCEE 270P.description: Introduction to flood risk management, including coverage of the consequences and causes of flooding, trends in flooding, how flood risk is managed, and modeling methods for supporting various aspects of flood management.

ENGRCEE 271.title: Flow in Unsaturated Porous Media
ENGRCEE 271.description: Fluid flow in the unsaturated zone (zone of aeration) of the subsurface. Soil-water physics, flow in regional groundwater systems, miscible displacement, mathematical modeling techniques.

ENGRCEE 272.title: Groundwater Hydrology
ENGRCEE 272.description: Topics include conservation of fluid mass, storage properties or porous media, matrix compressibility, boundary conditions, flow nets, well hydraulics, groundwater chemistry, and solute transport. Includes introduction to advanced topics in porous media. Design projects and computer applications included.

ENGRCEE 273.title: Watershed Modeling
ENGRCEE 273.description: Basic principles of hydrologic modeling are practiced. Concepts of watershed delineation, land use change impact, design studies, and GIS tools are discussed. Focus on the USACE (HEC) software tools (HEC-HMS and HEC-RAS) along with their associated GIS interfaces.

ENGRCEE 274.title: Climate Data Analysis
ENGRCEE 274.description: Trend analysis; statistical indices for diagnosing and detecting changes in extremes; nonstationary processes; extreme value analysis; multivariate extreme value methods; tail dependence estimation; uncertainties in observed and projected changes in climate extremes.

ENGRCEE 275.title: Stochastic Hydrology
ENGRCEE 275.description: Statistical methods relevant for water resources engineering and hydrologic/ geophysical data analysis for decision making. Estimation of design events, analysis of time series and spatio-temporally correlated fields, and applications to flood frequency analysis, climate extremes and subsurface characterization.

ENGRCEE 276.title: Hydrology
ENGRCEE 276.description: Elements of the hydrologic cycle including precipitation, infiltration, evapotranspiration, ground water, and runoff. Unit Hydrograph theory and routing methods. Introduction to precipitation/runoff relationship and watershed modeling. Statistical methods and flood frequency analysis. Discussion section covers advanced topics.

ENGRCEE 278.title: Environmental Biotechnology
ENGRCEE 278.description: Microbiology, chemistry, and engineering principles to design microbial bioremediation of organic and inorganic pollutants. Biological processes in engineered and natural systems, using stoichiometry, kinetics, and material balances to analyze and quantify microbial processes.

ENGRCEE 279.title: Environmental Transport Modeling
ENGRCEE 279.description: Computational modeling of multi-dimensional flow and scalar transport problems in surface and ground water. Topics include mathematical model formulation, numerical method selection, serial and parallel implementation, model verification and validation.

ENGRCEE 281.title: Structural Reliability
ENGRCEE 281.description: Applications of probability theory to reliability analysis of engineering structures. Theory of structural reliability. Estimation of static random loads. Reliability analysis of structural components and system. Monte Carlo simulation.

ENGRCEE 283.title: Mathematical Methods in Engineering Analysis
ENGRCEE 283.description: Matrices; vector calculus; eigenvalue problems; Fourier analysis; partial differential equations; special functions; numerical analysis; finite difference method.

ENGRCEE 289.title: Analysis of Hydrologic Systems
ENGRCEE 289.description: Application of systems theory in hydrologic, land surface, biogeochemical modeling. Design, identification, and calibration of conceptual models. Principles of dynamic systems, modeling approaches, theory of linear systems, mathematical concepts of differential calculus, theoretical concepts of parameter estimation and optimization theory.

ENGRCEE 290A.title: Machine, Model, and Statistical Learning I
ENGRCEE 290A.description: Introduction to machine, model, and statistical learning, featuring a series of topics on how to leverage data for model development (“learning”), model calibration (“training”), model evaluation (“verification”), and uncertainty quantification, illustrated using simple practice exercises and real-world case studies.
ENGRCEE 290A.prereq_text: Recommended: Foundational skills in Mathematics, Statistics, and MATLAB.

ENGRCEE 290B.title: Machine, Model, and Statistical Learning II
ENGRCEE 290B.description: Advanced mathematical concepts in machine, model, and statistical learning. Linear algebra, information, probability, and set theory. Topics include sensitivity analysis, forecast verification, model selection, model averaging, data assimilation (Kalman filter), and sequential Monte Carlo (particle filter).
ENGRCEE 290B.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 290A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 291.title: Hydrologic Remote Sensing
ENGRCEE 291.description: Introduction to principles of remote sensing and application in hydrology. Review of sensor systems, thermal and multispectral image processing, and image classification. Examples from remote sensing of hydrologic processes such as precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation are covered.
ENGRCEE 291.prereq_text: ENGRCEE 276 with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRCEE 292.title: Wavelets in Hydrology, Engineering, and Geoscience
ENGRCEE 292.description: Multiscale analysis of hydrologic, engineering, and earth system processes; energy decomposition in the time-frequency domain via wavelets; applications to fluid flows, climate and mechanical signals for feature extraction, trend analysis, coherent structures, and upscaling/downscaling.

ENGRCEE 293.title: River Networks and Earth Surface Processes
ENGRCEE 293.description: Analysis of drainage patterns in river networks and river deltas and relation to fluxes of water and sediment. Scaling laws of channel properties and simple models to estimate fluxes and response to upstream perturbations.

ENGRCEE 295.title: Seminars in Engineering
ENGRCEE 295.description: Seminars scheduled each year by individual faculty in major field of interest.

ENGRCEE 295P.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
ENGRCEE 295P.description: Studies in selected areas of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGRCEE 296.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
ENGRCEE 296.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation of the thesis required for the M.S. degree in Engineering.

ENGRCEE 297.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
ENGRCEE 297.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree in Engineering.

ENGRCEE 298.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
ENGRCEE 298.description: Presentation of advanced topics and special research areas in civil and environmental engineering.

ENGRCEE 299.title: Individual Research
ENGRCEE 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

ENGRMAE 10.title: Introduction to Engineering Computations
ENGRMAE 10.description: Introduction to the solution of engineering problems through the use of the computer. Elementary programming, numerical analysis, and data visualization with a high-level programming language such as MATLAB.
ENGRMAE 10.prereq_text: MATH 2A or MATH 5A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3.
ENGRMAE 10.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, Materials Science and Engineering majors, and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 30.title: Statics
ENGRMAE 30.description: Addition and resolution of forces, distributed forces, equivalent system of forces centroids, first moments, moments and products on inertia, equilibrium of rigid bodies, trusses, beams, cables.
ENGRMAE 30.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 52.title: Computer-Aided Design
ENGRMAE 52.description: Develops skills for the creation and use of CAD models and drawings in engineering design. Manufacturing techniques, tolerancing, kinematics, and basic simulation are also covered. Students build a functioning, physical prototype from a CAD design. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 52.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 60.title: Electric Circuits
ENGRMAE 60.description: Design and analysis of analog circuits based on lumped circuit elements with emphasis on the use of operational amplifiers. Sinusoidal and transient response. Constructional and laboratory testing of analog circuits, and introduction to data acquisition. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 60.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, and Materials Science Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 80.title: Dynamics
ENGRMAE 80.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.
ENGRMAE 80.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, Materials Science and Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 91.title: Introduction to Thermodynamics
ENGRMAE 91.description: Thermodynamic principles; open and closed systems representative of engineering problems. First and second law of thermodynamics with applications to engineering systems and design.
ENGRMAE 91.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, Materials Science and Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 93.title: Topics in Design Project
ENGRMAE 93.description: Early-stage design/hands-on experience for students, and allows them to participate alongside seniors in the design project.
ENGRMAE 93.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 106.title: Mechanical Systems Laboratory
ENGRMAE 106.description: Experiments in linear systems, including op-amp circuits, vibrations, and control systems. Emphasis on demonstrating that mathematical models can be useful tools for the analysis and design of electro-mechanical systems. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 106.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, Materials Science and Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 107.title: Fluid Thermal Science Laboratory
ENGRMAE 107.description: Fluid and thermal science laboratory. Experimental analysis of fluid flow, heat transfer, and thermodynamic systems. Probability, statistics, and uncertainty analysis. Report writing is emphasized and a design project is required. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 107.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 108.title: Aerospace Laboratory
ENGRMAE 108.description: Analytical and experimental investigation in aerodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer. Emphasis on study of flow over objects and lift and drag on airfoils. Introduction to basic diagnostic techniques. Report writing is emphasized.
ENGRMAE 108.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 110.title: Combustion and Fuel Cell Systems
ENGRMAE 110.description: Fundamentals of gaseous, liquid, and coal-fired combustion and fuel cell systems. Fuels, fuel-air mixing, aerodynamics, and combustion and fuel cell thermodynamics. Operating and design aspects of practical systems including engines, power generators, boilers, furnaces, and incinerators.
ENGRMAE 110.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 112.title: Propulsion
ENGRMAE 112.description: Application of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics to basic flow processes and cycle performance in chemical propulsion systems: gas turbines, ramjets, scramjets, and rockets. Introduction to electric and electromagnetic rocket thrusters, nuclear rockets, and solar sails.
ENGRMAE 112.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 113.title: Electric Propulsion
ENGRMAE 113.description: Space propulsion requirements and maneuvers, stressing those best suited to electric propulsion. An introduction to plasma physics. Electrothermal, electromagnetic, and electrostatis accelerators, with emphasis in technologies (ion engines, Hall thrusters, and colloidal thrusters) belonging to the latter family.
ENGRMAE 113.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 114.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
ENGRMAE 114.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions, and other characteristics.
ENGRMAE 114.restriction: Seniors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 115.title: Applied Engineering Thermodynamics
ENGRMAE 115.description: Application of thermodynamic principles to compressible and incompressible processes representative of practical engineering problems; power cycles, refrigeration cycles, multicomponent mixtures, air conditioning systems, combustion, and compressible flow. Design of a thermodynamic process.
ENGRMAE 115.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 117.title: Solar and Renewable Energy Systems
ENGRMAE 117.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of solar and other renewable energy systems including solar photo-voltaic, solar thermal, wind, and PEM fuel cell. Includes power generation and storage, and renewable fuels for transportation and stationary power generation.
ENGRMAE 117.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 118.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
ENGRMAE 118.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of sustainable energy systems including wind, solar photo-voltaic and thermal, hydroelectric, geothermal, oceanic, biomass combustion, advanced coal, and next generation nuclear. Includes power generation, storage, and transmission for stationary power generation.
ENGRMAE 118.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 119.title: Climate Solutions
ENGRMAE 119.description: Introduction to climate change science and impacts on the health of people and the planet with a focus on the multi-dimensional aspects of solutions to the climate crisis.

ENGRMAE 120.title: Heat and Mass Transfer
ENGRMAE 120.description: Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer. Conduction, heat and mass transfer by convection in laminar flow, radiation heat transfer, and combined modes of heat and mass transfer. Practical engineering applications.
ENGRMAE 120.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 130A.title: Fluid Dynamics I
ENGRMAE 130A.description: Fundamental concepts; fluid statics; kinematics; incompressible and compressible flows; Bernoulli's equation; control-volume analysis; conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; differential analysis; introduction to potential flow and viscous flow.
ENGRMAE 130A.prereq_text: PHYSICS 7C with a minimum grade of C- and MATH 2D with a minimum grade of C- and MATH 3D with a minimum grade of C- and (ENGRMAE 30 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGRCEE 30 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGR 30 with a minimum grade of C-).
ENGRMAE 130A.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 130B.title: Fluid Dynamics II
ENGRMAE 130B.description: Analysis of viscous flows: stress-strain rate, fully developed laminar and turbulent flows. Review of thermodynamics, sound speed, stagnation properties. One dimensional isentropic and non-isentropic compressible flows. Normal and oblique shock waves. Two-dimensional supersonic isentropic flow.
ENGRMAE 130B.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 130A and (ENGRMAE 80 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGRCEE 80 with a minimum grade of C- or ENGR 80 with a minimum grade of C-).
ENGRMAE 130B.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 130C.title: Fluid Dynamics III
ENGRMAE 130C.description: Advanced topics in viscous and compressible flows. Viscous boundary layers, basic concepts in turbulent flow, separated flows, thermal transport, two-dimensional supersonic flow, shock polars, supersonic airfoils, conical flows.
ENGRMAE 130C.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 135.title: Compressible Flow
ENGRMAE 135.description: Compressibility effects in fluid mechanics. One-dimensional flow with area variation, friction, heat transfer, and shocks. Design of gas supply systems. Two-dimensional flow with oblique shocks and isentropic waves. Supersonic airfoil theory and design, wind tunnel design. Basic diagnostics.
ENGRMAE 135.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 136.title: Aerodynamics
ENGRMAE 136.description: Advanced potential flow, including vorticity, circulation, and the Kutta-Joukowski theorem. Incompressible flow over 2D inviscid airfoils. Prandtl lifting-line theory for finite wings. Effects of viscosity and compressibility. Elements of supersonic aerodynamics. Source and vortex panel methods.
ENGRMAE 136.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 145.title: Theory of Machines and Mechanisms
ENGRMAE 145.description: Presents the basic mathematical theory of machines. Focuses on the principles of cam design, gearing and gear train analysis, and the kinematic and dynamic analysis of linkages, together with an introduction to robotics.
ENGRMAE 145.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 52 and (ENGRMAE 80 or ENGRCEE 80 or ENGR 80) and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N).
ENGRMAE 145.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 146.title: Astronautics
ENGRMAE 146.description: Motion in gravitational force fields, orbit transfers, rocketry, interplanetary trajectories, attitude dynamics and stabilization, navigation, reentry, the space environment.
ENGRMAE 146.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 147.title: Vibrations
ENGRMAE 147.description: Analysis of structural vibrations of mechanical systems. Modeling for lumped and distributed parameter systems. Topics include single and multi-degree of freedom systems, free and forced vibrations, Fourier series, convolution integral, mass/stiffness matrices, and normal modes with design project.
ENGRMAE 147.prereq_text: (ENGR 80 or ENGRCEE 80 or ENGRMAE 80) and MATH 2E and MATH 3D.
ENGRMAE 147.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 148.title: Mechanics of Smart Structures
ENGRMAE 148.description: Introduction to modeling, numerical simulation, design, and control of axial, torsional, and bending actuators. Fundamentals of shape-changing trusses, frames, and panels. Introduction to the behavior and modeling of smart materials such as shape memory alloys/polymers.

ENGRMAE 150.title: Mechanics of Structures
ENGRMAE 150.description: Introduction to mechanics of materials. Topics include stresses and strains, axial and torsional loading, bending, shear, combined loading, stress and strain transformation, failure theories, beam deflection, and buckling.
ENGRMAE 150.prereq_text: (ENGRCEE 30 or ENGR 30 or ENGRMAE 30) and MATH 3A.
ENGRMAE 150.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 150L.title: Mechanics of Structures Laboratory
ENGRMAE 150L.description: Experimental techniques for the measurement of mechanical properties of materials and structures. Methods for load, displacement, and strain measurements. Tension, bending, compression tests. Determination of strength. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 150L.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 151A.title: Mechanical Engineering Design I
ENGRMAE 151A.description: Teaching and implementation of all phases of the engineering design process that begins with identifying needs, setting requirements, concept generation, and preliminary design. Emphasis on detailed engineering analysis and documentation for a small-team, open-ended design project. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 151A.restriction: Seniors and Mechanical Engineering majors only.

ENGRMAE 151B.title: Mechanical Engineering Design II
ENGRMAE 151B.description: Manufacturing, diagnostics and quality, economics, ethics, and inclusivity. Continuation of the engineering design process with analysis and modeling, physical prototyping, testing, verification, and validation of solutions for the open-ended design project. Teamwork, project presentations, and documentation. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 151B.restriction: Seniors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 152.title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Engineering
ENGRMAE 152.description: Elements and principles of simulation in engineering design using industry software tools. Examples of finite-element method applications covered may include structural, thermal, dynamics, kinematics, fatigue, optimization and fluid flow problems.
ENGRMAE 152.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 153.title: Advanced BIOMEMS Manufacturing Techniques
ENGRMAE 153.description: Introduction to BIOMEMS. Advanced biotechnology/biomedicine equipment based on MEMS and NEMS. Fundamentals of MEMS/NEMS sensing techniques and the biological and physics principles involved and the preferred MEMS and NEMS manufacturing techniques.
ENGRMAE 153.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, and Biomedical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 155.title: Composite Materials and Structures
ENGRMAE 155.description: Micro and macro mechanical properties and failure mechanisms of lamina and laminates. Laminate theory, hygrothermal effects, failure analysis and design. Manufacturing methods, non-destructive evaluation, experimental characterization. Application of numerical modeling for analysis and design.
ENGRMAE 155.prereq_text: ENGR 54 and (ENGRMAE 150 or ENGRCEE 150 or ENGR 150).
ENGRMAE 155.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 156.title: Mechanical Behavior and Design Principles
ENGRMAE 156.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, yielding, necking, creep, and fracture of materials. Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize the properties of materials. Design parameters.
ENGRMAE 156.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 157.title: Lightweight Structures
ENGRMAE 157.description: Mass minimization under stiffness, strength, and buckling constraints. Finite Element method and application to trusses. Three-dimensional bending. Thin-wall, composite, and functionally graded beams. Plates and shells, design of laminated and functionally graded plates. Stress analysis of aircraft components.
ENGRMAE 157.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 158.title: Aircraft Performance
ENGRMAE 158.description: Flight theory applied to subsonic propeller and jet aircraft. Nature of aerodynamic forces, drag and lift of wing and fuselage, high-lift devices, level-flight performance, climb and glide performance, range, endurance, take-off and landing distances, static and dynamic stability and control.
ENGRMAE 158.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 159.title: Aircraft Design
ENGRMAE 159.description: Preliminary design of subsonic general aviation and transport aircraft with emphasis on layout, aerodynamic design, propulsion, and performance. Estimation of total weight and weight distribution, design of wings, fuselage, and tail, selection and location of engines, prediction of overall performance.
ENGRMAE 159.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 163.title: Aviation Systems and the Environment
ENGRMAE 163.description: Methods for analyzing aviation systems, flight and engine performance, and operations, and associated modern environmental challenges, including fuel burn, emissions, and noise are introduced. Analysis methods and technological and policy approaches for environmental impact mitigation examined.
ENGRMAE 163.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Aerospace Engineering majors only.

ENGRMAE 164.title: Air Pollution and Control
ENGRMAE 164.description: Sources, dispersion, and effects of air pollutants. Topics include emission factors, emission inventory, air pollution, meteorology, air chemistry, air quality modeling, impact assessment, source and ambient monitoring, regional control strategies.
ENGRMAE 164.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Chemical Engineering majors, and Environmental Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 170.title: Introduction to Control Systems
ENGRMAE 170.description: Feedback control systems. Modeling, stability, and systems specifications. Root locus, Nyquist, and Bode methods of analysis and design.
ENGRMAE 170.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors, Aerospace Engineering majors, Civil Engineering majors, and Materials Science and Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 171.title: Digital Control Systems
ENGRMAE 171.description: Methods for analysis and design of discrete-time control systems. Z-transforms, difference equations, discrete Fourier transforms. Sampling theorem and applications. Z-plane stability, frequency response. Digital controller design. Introduction to digital filters.
ENGRMAE 171.restriction: Civil Engineering majors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 172.title: Design of Computer-Controlled Robots
ENGRMAE 172.description: Students design a small robotic device and program it to exhibit sentient behaviors. The basic aspects of mechatronic design are covered, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, and microcomputer programming for the implementation of control paradigms. Materials Fee
ENGRMAE 172.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 175.title: Dynamics and Control of Aerospace Vehicles
ENGRMAE 175.description: Equations of motion, linearization, stability derivatives, and longitudinal and lateral modes of motion. Handling qualities, sensors and actuators, and effects of various feedbacks on stability and performance. Stability augmentation. Autopilot design.
ENGRMAE 175.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 181A.title: Racecar Engineering I
ENGRMAE 181A.description: Project-based learning course focused on the design, fabrication, and testing of vehicles for intercollegiate competition. Focuses on the system and subsystem engineering analysis, design drawings, and parts specification.

ENGRMAE 181B.title: Racecar Engineering II
ENGRMAE 181B.description: Project-based learning course focused on the design, fabrication, and testing of vehicles for intercollegiate competition. Focuses on subsystem prototype fabrication and verification, as well as system integration.

ENGRMAE 181C.title: Racecar Engineering III
ENGRMAE 181C.description: Project-based learning course focused on the design, fabrication, and testing of vehicles for intercollegiate competition. Focuses on system verification, driver training, competition team training, in-field maintenance, and design improvements for the following year.

ENGRMAE 182.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
ENGRMAE 182.description: Fundamental principles necessary to understand statistical learning methods. Introduction to the R programming language. Mathematical foundation for various machine learning algorithms. Computer implementation.

ENGRMAE 183.title: Computer-Aided Mechanism Design
ENGRMAE 183.description: Focuses on design of planar, spherical, and spatial mechanisms using computer algebra and graphics. Topics include exact and approximate analytical design techniques. Students are required to use existing software (or develop new algorithms) to design various mechanisms for new applications.
ENGRMAE 183.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 184.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Design
ENGRMAE 184.description: Review of statistics as applied to experimental research. Fundamentals and principles of statistical experimental design and analysis with emphasis on understanding and use of designed experiments, response surfaces, linear regression modeling, and process optimization.
ENGRMAE 184.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors and Aerospace Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 185.title: Numerical Analysis in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
ENGRMAE 185.description: Solution of mechanical and aerospace engineering equations by means of numerical methods. Errors in numerical analysis. Methods for solving systems of algebraic equations. Interpolation, integration and differentiation. Numerical solutions to differential equations. Introduction to Python and its scientific computing modules.
ENGRMAE 185.prereq_text: (ENGRMAE 10 or EECS 10 or EECS 12 or BME 60B) and MATH 3D and MATH 2E.

ENGRMAE 188.title: Engineering Design in Industry
ENGRMAE 188.description: Principles of engineering design in the context of an industrial application. Local manufacturing firms define an engineering design project to be completed in 10 weeks. Projects include initial brainstorming to final design, with a formal presentation
ENGRMAE 188.restriction: Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 189.title: Senior Project - Special Topics
ENGRMAE 189.description: Group or individual senior project of theoretical or applied nature involving design.
ENGRMAE 189.restriction: Seniors and Mechanical Engineering majors only.

ENGRMAE 193.title: Topics in MAE Design
ENGRMAE 193.description: Provides early-stage design/hands-on experience for upper-division students, and allows them to participate in senior design projects course ENGRMAE 189.
ENGRMAE 193.restriction: Aerospace Engineering majors and Mechanical Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 195.title: Seminars in Engineering
ENGRMAE 195.description: Seminars by individual faculty in major fields of interest. Materials fee.

ENGRMAE 197.title: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering Internship
ENGRMAE 197.description: Students majoring in MAE may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.

ENGRMAE 198.title: Group Study
ENGRMAE 198.description: Group study of selected topics in Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering.

ENGRMAE 199.title: Individual Study
ENGRMAE 199.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

ENGRMAE 200A.title: Engineering Analysis I
ENGRMAE 200A.description: Linear algebra, including vector spaces, matrices, linear systems of equations, least squares, and the eigenvalue problem. Ordinary differential equations, including analytical and numerical solution methods, stability, and phase portraits.

ENGRMAE 200B.title: Engineering Analysis II
ENGRMAE 200B.description: Review of ordinary differential equations, including Bessel and Legendre functions. Partial differential equations, including the diffusion equation, Laplace's equation, and the wave equation. Fourier series, Fourier and Laplace transforms and their applications.

ENGRMAE 202P.title: Professional Engineering Fundamentals
ENGRMAE 202P.description: The fundamentals of the core topics in mechanical and aerospace engineering are first reviewed and then integrated and applied in the context of engineered systems.

ENGRMAE 204P.title: Personalized Medical Devices
ENGRMAE 204P.description: Introduces students to fundamental aspects of medical devices and discusses therapeutic as well as diagnostic devices. Basic aspects of microfluidics and biology critical to personalized medical systems are studied. Typical FDA approval pathways for medical devices are presented.

ENGRMAE 205.title: Perturbation Methods in Engineering
ENGRMAE 205.description: Asymptotic Expansions of integrals. Regular and singular perturbations. Perturbation methods for ordinary and partial differential equations. Matched asymptotic expansions. Multiple-scale asymptotic expansion schemes. Not offered every year.
ENGRMAE 205.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 200A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 200B with a minimum grade of B-. Knowledge of linear differential equations.

ENGRMAE 205P.title: Model-Based Engineering: Systems and Design
ENGRMAE 205P.description: Engineering design, systems engineering, and product lifecycle management. Model-based approaches and modeling for the digital twin. Software tools and application to the design of a complete product from problem definition to production.

ENGRMAE 206.title: Nonlinear Optimization Methods
ENGRMAE 206.description: Numerical methods for constrained and unconstrained optimization. Necessary and sufficient conditions for optimimality. Conjugate gradient, variable metric algorithms. Gradient projection, penalty functions, and Lagrange methods. Not offered every year.
ENGRMAE 206.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 200A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 209P.title: Energy Efficiency in the Built Environment
ENGRMAE 209P.description: Energy and power for the built environment; building energy modeling; heat transfer and losses; heating and cooling cycles; control hardware and software; carbon neutrality, optimization.

ENGRMAE 210.title: Advanced Fundamentals of Combustion
ENGRMAE 210.description: Premixed, nonpremixed, and heterogenous reactions, with emphasis on kinetics, thermal ignition, turbulent flame propogation, detonations, explosions, flammability limits, diffusion flame, quenching, flame stabilization, and particle and spray combustion. Not offered every year.

ENGRMAE 213.title: Electric Propulsion
ENGRMAE 213.description: Space propulsion requirements and maneuvers, stressing those best suited to electric propulsion. An introduction to plasma physics. Electrothermal, electromagnetic and electrostatic accelerators, with emphasis in technologies (ion engines, Hall thrusters and colloidal thrusters) belonging to the latter family.

ENGRMAE 214A.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
ENGRMAE 214A.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions and other characteristics.

ENGRMAE 214B.title: Fuel Cell Systems and Degradation
ENGRMAE 214B.description: Fuel cell systems design; impacts of operating conditions; experimental and theoretical analysis methods for fuel cells systems; introduction to degradation mechanisms and mitigation techniques; provides broad insight into fuel-cell science, technology, system design and operation. Offered every other year.
ENGRMAE 214B.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 214A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 214P.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
ENGRMAE 214P.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions, and other characteristics.

ENGRMAE 215.title: Advanced Combustion Technology
ENGRMAE 215.description: Recap of combustion thermodynamics, equilibrium, chemistry concepts in the context of practical systems. Overview of renewable and non-renewable fuels and their implications for practical devices. Concepts associated with computation and experimental methods. Emphasis on pollutant formation and emissions.

ENGRMAE 216.title: Statistical Thermodynamics
ENGRMAE 216.description: Statistics of independent particles, development of quantum mechanical description of atoms and molecules, application of quantum mechanics, evaluation of thermodynamics properties for solids, liquids, and gases, statistical mechanics of dependent particles (ensembles).

ENGRMAE 217.title: Generalized Thermodynamics
ENGRMAE 217.description: Generalized thermodynamics develops the laws of continuum thermodynamics from a set of plausible and intuitive postulates. The postulates are motivated qualitatively by a statistical description of matter and are justified by a posterior success for the resulting theory.

ENGRMAE 218P.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
ENGRMAE 218P.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of sustainable energy systems including wind, solar photo-voltaic and thermal, hydroelectric, geothermal, oceanic, biomass combustion, advanced coal, and next generation nuclear. Includes power generation, storage, and transmission for stationary power generation.

ENGRMAE 219P.title: Solar and Renewable Energy Systems
ENGRMAE 219P.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of solar and other renewable energy systems including solar photo-voltaic, solar thermal, wind, and PEM fuel cell. Includes power generation and storage, and renewable fuels for transportation and stationary power generation.
ENGRMAE 219P.prereq_text: Required: Knowledge of applied engineering thermodynamics.

ENGRMAE 220.title: Conduction Heat Transfer
ENGRMAE 220.description: Steady state and transient conduction heat transfer in one- and multi-dimensional geometries. Analytical methods, exact and approximate. Numerical techniques are also included.

ENGRMAE 221.title: Convective Heat and Mass Transfer
ENGRMAE 221.description: Fundamental convective heat transfer for various cases, including flow conditions, flow phases, and boundary conditions. Analysis of heat convection by exact, approximate solutions, and similarity solutions. Boundary layer theory and equations.
ENGRMAE 221.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 230B with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 223A.title: Numerical Methods in Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transport (Laminar Flows) I
ENGRMAE 223A.description: Introduction to the discretization of various types of partial differential equations (parabolic, elliptic, hyperbolic). Finite-volume discretization for one- and two-dimensional flows. Use of a two-dimensional elliptic procedure to predict sample laminar flows.
ENGRMAE 223A.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 230A (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 224.title: Advanced Transport Phenomena
ENGRMAE 224.description: Fundamentals of transport phenomena. Covers the subjects of conservation equations, dimensionless numbers, fundamentals of diffusion, perturbation methods, ion transport, two-phase transport, and interfacial phenomena.

ENGRMAE 227.title: Thermal Resistance Analysis in Microdevices and Nanomaterials
ENGRMAE 227.description: Heat transfer and thermal resistance analysis relevant for microdevices and nanomaterials. Overview of recent progress in nanotechnology and materials science. Thermal modeling strategies for novel electronic devices and energy conversion systems.

ENGRMAE 228.title: Nanoscale Phase Change Transport Physics
ENGRMAE 228.description: Discusses a wide range of phase change processes (i.e., evaporation, boiling, condensation, and freezing) through the use of novel thermal metamaterials with the aim of enhancing phase change performances.

ENGRMAE 230A.title: Inviscid Incompressible Fluid Mechanics I
ENGRMAE 230A.description: Equations of motion. Vector notation. Flow kinematics. Potential flow and complex potential. Vorticity and circulation. Bernoulli's theorem. Crocco's theorem. Conformal, Joukowski, and Schwarz-Christoffel transformations.

ENGRMAE 230B.title: Viscous Incompressible Fluid Mechanics II
ENGRMAE 230B.description: Review of mass, momentum, energy equations. Stress tensor, constitutive relations. Laminar flows. Stokes and Oseen flows. Self-similarity. Boundary layer theory: thin-layer approximation, Falkner-Skan, Blasius solutions, integral methods. Jet, wake, cavity flows. Introduction to turbulence: instability, Reynolds averaging, mixing length.

ENGRMAE 230C.title: Compressible Fluid Dynamics
