ENGRMAE 230C.description: One-dimensional unsteady flow; Riemann invariants, acoustics, shock tube. Two-dimensional flow: shock polars, linear theory, similarity rules, method of characteristics. Three dimensional flow: slender-body theory. Effects of viscosity and conductivity: laminar boundary layer, Crocco-Busemann relations.
ENGRMAE 230C.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 230A with a minimum grade of B- or ENGRMAE 230B with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 230D.title: Theoretical Foundations of Fluid Mechanics
ENGRMAE 230D.description: Well-posed problems and boundary, initial, and interface conditions; strong and weak solutions. Similarity, perturbation theory and limit behavior, bifurcations. Dispersive and nondispersive wave propagation, acoustics, ship waves, internal gravity waves, water waves. Vortices: mutual interactions and stability. Jets, wakes, cavities.
ENGRMAE 230D.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 230A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 230B with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 230P.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
ENGRMAE 230P.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in programming and machine learning. The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to the field of machine learning and related techniques for students with a wide variety of engineering degrees.

ENGRMAE 231.title: Fundamentals of Turbulence
ENGRMAE 231.description: Phenomenon of turbulence. Reynolds equations. Dynamics of turbulence. Free turbulent shear flows. Wall-bounded turbulent shear flows. Turbulent transport of scalar quantities. Spectral dynamics. Mathematical models of turbulence.
ENGRMAE 231.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 230A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 230B with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 231P.title: Robotics and Controls
ENGRMAE 231P.description: Covers basic aspects of robotic and mechatronic design, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, finite state machines, and implementation of advanced feedback control laws.

ENGRMAE 233.title: Turbulent Free Shear Flows
ENGRMAE 233.description: Practical and theoretical aspects of turbulent free shear flows. Instability, global scaling laws, mixing, and noise generation in incompressible and compressible shear layers, jets, and wakes. Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, near- and far-field growth rates, effect of compressibility, aeroacoustics of jets.
ENGRMAE 233.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 200B with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 230A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 230B with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 235P.title: Engineering Design and Simulation: Tools and Process
ENGRMAE 235P.description: Practical techniques and use of industry tools that improve the engineering design process by simulating the performance of design options prior to the costly steps of prototyping and manufacturing are covered. Applicable to a wide variety of engineering disciplines.

ENGRMAE 236.title: Nonequilibrium Gas Dynamics
ENGRMAE 236.description: Molecular description of fluid flow. Boltzmann equation. Chapman-Enskog expansion for flows with translational nonequilibrium. Shock structure. Inviscid flows with chemical and vibrational nonequilibrium. Not offered every year.
ENGRMAE 236.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 230C with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 239.title: Dynamics of Unsteady Flows
ENGRMAE 239.description: Unsteady potential flow modeling (Kelvin's circulation theorem, unsteady Bernoulli's equation). Theodorsen's frequency response, Wagner's step response, and the Kussner sharp-edged gust. State Space approximations for Unsteady Loads. Vortex Lattice. Flutter.

ENGRMAE 240.title: Inertial Navigation
ENGRMAE 240.description: Provides a basic understanding of 1) theory, operation, and performance characteristics of a strapdown inertial navigation system (INS), (2) distinction between strap down and gimbaled INS, (3) Kalman filtering theory and its application to strap down INS aiding.

ENGRMAE 241.title: Dynamics
ENGRMAE 241.description: Kinematics and dynamics of three-dimensional motions. Lagrange's equations, Newton-Euler equations. Applications include robot systems and spinning satellites.

ENGRMAE 242.title: Robotics
ENGRMAE 242.description: Spatial rigid-body transformations. Forward and inverse kinematics. Jacobian of serial and parallel chains. Screw coordinates and transformations. Rate and static analyses using screw theory. Singularity analysis. Trajectory generation. Not offered every year.

ENGRMAE 245.title: Spatial Mechanism Design
ENGRMAE 245.description: Fundamental kinematic theory required for planar, spherical, and spatial mechanism design. The focus is on algebraic methods for the exact solution of constraint equations. Not offered every year.

ENGRMAE 247.title: Micro-System Design
ENGRMAE 247.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

ENGRMAE 247P.title: Micro-System Design
ENGRMAE 247P.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

ENGRMAE 249.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
ENGRMAE 249.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale. Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

ENGRMAE 249P.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
ENGRMAE 249P.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale. Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

ENGRMAE 250.title: Biorobotics
ENGRMAE 250.description: Sensors, actuators, and neural circuits for biological movement control from an engineering perspective. Current approaches to robotic and mechatronic devices that support and enhance human movement in health and following neurologic injuries like stroke and spinal cord injury.

ENGRMAE 251.title: Micro/Nano Robotics
ENGRMAE 251.description: Covers the emerging field of robotics at small scale (micro/nano robotics). Understanding different physical phenomena at small scales, the differences between nano and micro robotics, common fabrication, and different mechanisms of locomotion and environmental interaction.
ENGRMAE 251.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 252.title: Fundamentals of Microfabrication
ENGRMAE 252.description: Introduces Engineering and Science students to the science of miniaturization. Different options to make very small machines (micro and nano size) are reviewed, materials choices are discussed, scaling laws are analyzed, and many practical applications are listed.

ENGRMAE 252P.title: Fundamentals of Microfabrication
ENGRMAE 252P.description: Introduces engineering and science students to the science of miniaturization. Different options to make very small machines (micro and nano size) are reviewed, materials choices are discussed, scaling laws are analyzed, and many practical applications are listed.

ENGRMAE 254.title: Mechanics of Solids and Structures
ENGRMAE 254.description: Finite deformation kinematics; stress and strain measures; invariance in solid mechanics; objective rates; constitutive theory of elastic and inelastic solids; rate formulations; computational approaches; theories of plates and shells; applications to aerospace vehicles.

ENGRMAE 255.title: Composite Materials and Structures
ENGRMAE 255.description: Motivation for composite materials. Different classifications according to the nature of the matrix (PMC, MMC, CMC) and the reinforcement topology (fibers, whiskers, particulates). Mechanical properties. Failure mechanisms. Designing with composite materials. Advantages and limitations of homogenization techniques for numerical modeling.

ENGRMAE 256.title: Nano and Micro Mechanics
ENGRMAE 256.description: Nanoscale materials and the experimental and computational techniques used to measure their properties. Mechanical behavior is the main focus, but other material properties such as diffusion and electron transport are discussed.
ENGRMAE 256.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering majors only.

ENGRMAE 257.title: Materials Failure and Fracture
ENGRMAE 257.description: Introduces materials failure and fracture behaviors under mechanical, thermal, and environmental conditions. It aims to provide a solid foundation and basic understanding of classic fatigue and fracture problems, and their underlying physical mechanisms.
ENGRMAE 257.prereq_text: Recommended: A foundational knowledge of mechanical behavior and mechanics of materials, or completion of ENGRMAE 156.

ENGRMAE 258.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Continuum Theories
ENGRMAE 258.description: Presents a continuum, macroscopic view of deformation and failure of solids. Covers elasticity, plasticity, visco-elasticity, visco-plasticity, fracture and fatigue. Topics include discussions of physical behavior, mathematical formalism and measurement techniques.
ENGRMAE 258.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 254 with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 259.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Atomistic Theories
ENGRMAE 259.description: Presents atomistic mechanisms that control mechanical behavior of materials. Covers plasticity, dislocation theory, strengthening mechanisms, high-temperature diffusion and gain boundary sliding, shear localization, void formation, ductile rupture, brittle fracture and fatigue.

ENGRMAE 259P.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Atomistic Theories
ENGRMAE 259P.description: Presents atomistic mechanisms that control mechanical behavior of materials. Covers plasticity, dislocation theory, strengthening mechanisms, high-temperature diffusion and gain boundary sliding, shear localization, void formation, ductile rupture, brittle fracture, and fatigue.

ENGRMAE 260.title: Current Issues Related to Air Quality, Climate, and Energy
ENGRMAE 260.description: Current issues related to the atmosphere, climate, and air quality in the context of energy conversion and sustainability. Topics include transportation systems; building design; impacts on humans and ecosystems; modeling and meteorology; economics; and application to public policies.
ENGRMAE 260.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 261 with a minimum grade of B- or CHEM 245 with a minimum grade of B- or EARTHSS 240 with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 263.title: Aviation Systems and the Environment
ENGRMAE 263.description: Methods for analyzing aviation systems, flight and engine performance, operations, and associated modern environmental challenges, including fuel burn, emissions, and noise are introduced. Analysis methods and technological and policy approaches for environmental impact mitigation examined.

ENGRMAE 270A.title: Linear Systems I
ENGRMAE 270A.description: Input-output and state-space representations of continuous-time linear systems. State transition matrices, Controllability and observability. Irreducible realizations. State feedback and observer design.

ENGRMAE 270B.title: Linear Systems II
ENGRMAE 270B.description: Advanced topics in linear systems: bases, linear operator representations, and Jordan forms. Review of dynamical systems, and stability. Time-varying systems, discrete-time representations, and multi-input/multi-output systems. Introduction to continuous and discrete time linear regulator (LQR) problems. Not offered every year.
ENGRMAE 270B.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 271.title: Network Control
ENGRMAE 271.description: Provides foundations on graph-theoretic, probabilistic and analytic techniques that have proven instrumental for studying networked dynamical systems. Applications are presented in diverse areas of science and engineering that include the coordination of vehicles and distribution of energy and resources.

ENGRMAE 272.title: Robust Control Theory
ENGRMAE 272.description: Methods for control design of systems with uncertainty. Feedback stability and small gain theorem. Multivariable stability margins and multiplier theory. H-infinity-optimal control, linear matrix inequalities. Not offered every year.
ENGRMAE 272.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 270A with a minimum grade of B-.
ENGRMAE 272.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 274.title: Optimal Control
ENGRMAE 274.description: Principles and methods of optimal control. Topics include objectives and issues in controlling nonlinear systems; linear variational and adjoint equations; optimality conditions via variational calculus, maximum principle, and dynamic programming; solution methods; applications to control robots and aerospace vehicles.
ENGRMAE 274.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 200A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 275.title: Nonlinear Feedback Systems
ENGRMAE 275.description: Advanced tools for feedback control system analysis and synthesis. Norms, operators, Lp spaces, contraction mapping theorem, Lyapunov techniques along with their extensions. Circle criterion positivity and passivity. Applications to nonlinear control methods, such as sliding mode or adaptive techniques.
ENGRMAE 275.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 270B with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 276.title: Geometric Nonlinear Control
ENGRMAE 276.description: Using the mathematics of differential geometry, a number of the concepts and results of linear systems theory have been extended to nonlinear systems. Describes these extensions and illustrate their use in nonlinear system analysis and design. Not offered every year.
ENGRMAE 276.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 200A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 277.title: Learning Control Systems
ENGRMAE 277.description: Supervised learning for classification and regression: perceptrons, support vector machines, feed-forward neural networks, Gaussian processes. Generalization and model selection: cross-validation, regularization, and Bayesian methods. Unsupervised learning: clustering and dimensionality reduction. Learning control systems. Introduction to reinforcement learning.

ENGRMAE 278.title: Parameter and State Estimation
ENGRMAE 278.description: Bayesian and frequentist approaches to parameter and state estimation. Properties of estimators. Linear Gaussian systems and the Kalman Filter. Nonlinear state estimation, extended and unscented Kalman Filters. Introduction to Monte Carlo methods and particle filtering. Application to tracking and navigation.
ENGRMAE 278.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 200A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 270A with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 279.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Systems
ENGRMAE 279.description: Selected topics of current interest in mechanical systems. Topics include robotics, kinematics, control, dynamics, and geometric modeling.
ENGRMAE 279.prereq_text: ENGRMAE 270A with a minimum grade of B- and ENGRMAE 241 with a minimum grade of B-.

ENGRMAE 280.title: Design of Computer-Controlled Robots
ENGRMAE 280.description: The basic aspects of mechatronic design are covered, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, finite state machines, inertial measurement units, and implementation of advanced feedback control laws. Students work in groups to create their own mechatronic device. Materials Fee

ENGRMAE 282P.title: Model-Based Engineering: Systems and Design
ENGRMAE 282P.description: Engineering design, systems engineering, and product lifecycle management. Model-based approaches and modeling for the digital twin. Software tools and application to the design of a complete product from problem definition to production.

ENGRMAE 284.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Design
ENGRMAE 284.description: Fundamentals and principles of statistical experimental design and analysis. Emphasis addresses understanding and use of designed experiments, response surfaces, linear regression modeling, process optimization, and development of links between empirical and theoretical models.

ENGRMAE 285.title: Engineering Design Under Uncertainty
ENGRMAE 285.description: Introduces students to statistical and ML methods used in engineering design under uncertainty. Students learn how to probabilistically formulate a design problem, translate the formulations into a computer, and systematically find the solution.

ENGRMAE 286.title: Design for Human Movement
ENGRMAE 286.description: Introduces techniques for analysis and modeling of human locomotion, with a focus on lower-limb rehabilitating and robotic assistive devices. Discusses background and current research, with assignments covering independent reading, computer simulations, and a final project.

ENGRMAE 287P.title: Engineering Design and Simulation: Tools and Process
ENGRMAE 287P.description: Practical techniques and industry tools that improve engineering processes by simulating performance of design options prior to costly prototyping and manufacturing. Applicable to a variety of disciplines, simulation decreases the number of engineering issues that arise during design process.

ENGRMAE 291.title: Research Communication in Engineering
ENGRMAE 291.description: Guides students along research communication milestones by completion of a conference/journal publication, research proposal, MS thesis, or other significant publication. Peer review, response to reviewers, and a presentation are used to build skill and confidence.
ENGRMAE 291.restriction: School of Engineering students have the first consideration for enrollment.

ENGRMAE 294.title: Master of Science Thesis Project
ENGRMAE 294.description: Tutorial in which masters-level students taking the comprehensive examination option undertake a masters-level research project.

ENGRMAE 295.title: Special Topics in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
ENGRMAE 295.description: Special topics by individual faculty in major fields of interest.

ENGRMAE 295P.title: Special Topics in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
ENGRMAE 295P.description: Studies in selected areas of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

ENGRMAE 296.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
ENGRMAE 296.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the thesis required for the M.S. in Engineering.

ENGRMAE 297.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
ENGRMAE 297.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the dissertation required for the Ph.D. in Engineering.

ENGRMAE 298.title: Seminars in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
ENGRMAE 298.description: Presentation of advanced topics and reports of current research efforts in mechanical engineering. Required of all graduate students in mechanical engineering.

ENGRMAE 299.title: Individual Research
ENGRMAE 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

EPIDEM 199.title: Undergraduate Research in Epidemiology
EPIDEM 199.description: Provides disciplinary research participation. Original or existing research options provide undergraduates the opportunity for faculty/mentor interactions including access to appropriate facilities. Medical Epidemiology research areas: Cancer, Genetic/Molecular, Environmental, Occupational, Biostatistics, and Infectious Disease.

EPIDEM 200A.title: Epidemiologic Methods I
EPIDEM 200A.description: Introduces the scope of epidemiology, measures of disease occurrence and association in populations, public health surveillance, diagnostic testing and screening studies, and methods and best practices for collecting data.
EPIDEM 200A.prereq_text: ( ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY )

EPIDEM 200B.title: Epidemiologic Methods II
EPIDEM 200B.description: Design, conduct, and critical evaluation of randomized and observational study designs.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EPIDEM 200B.prereq_text: EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B.

EPIDEM 200C.title: Epidemiologic Methods III
EPIDEM 200C.description: Applies core epidemiologic concepts to the analysis, interpretation, and communication of epidemiologic data from different study designs.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EPIDEM 200C.prereq_text: EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B and EPIDEM 200B with a minimum grade of B.

EPIDEM 200D.title: Epidemiologic Methods IV
EPIDEM 200D.description: Introduces different causal inference and scientific reasoning frameworks, with an emphasis on study design and analysis using causal diagrams to identify and minimize potential biases in research questions.
EPIDEM 200D.prereq_text: EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B and EPIDEM 200B with a minimum grade of B and EPIDEM 200C with a minimum grade of B.

EPIDEM 200E.title: Epidemiologic Methods V
EPIDEM 200E.description: Introduces different approaches to formulating and appraising research questions accounting for study design and data analysis considerations with a focus on estimating causal effects from observational data.
EPIDEM 200E.prereq_text: EPIDEM 200D with a minimum grade of B.

EPIDEM 201.title: Cancer Epidemiology
EPIDEM 201.description: Concentrates on understanding how epidemiology plays a role in the search for cancer etiology, prevention, control, and treatment; gives an overview of cancer research with an appreciation of the multidisciplinary nature of the field.
EPIDEM 201.prereq_text: EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B- or PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B-.

EPIDEM 202.title: Genetic Epidemiology
EPIDEM 202.description: Genetic epidemiologic research principles, covering diverse study designs and methods. Integrates literature examples, lectures, demonstrations, and software applications for varied study designs, ranging from unrelated individuals to large extended kindreds. Includes in-class discussions, group projects, and exercises for concept reinforcement.
EPIDEM 202.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B-.

EPIDEM 204A.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods
EPIDEM 204A.description: Introduction to the basic statistical techniques commonly used in public health research. Topics include descriptive statistics, basic probability, inferential statistics (estimation, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing), and contingency tables. SAS software is introduced.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EPIDEM 204A.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
EPIDEM 204A.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EPIDEM 204B.title: Biostatistics II: Intermediate Statistical Methods
EPIDEM 204B.description: Explores advanced statistical analysis methods for biological and medical applications. Topics include linear, logistic, and generalized linear regression models like Poisson regression.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EPIDEM 204B.prereq_text: EPIDEM 204A with a minimum grade of B or PUBHLTH 204A with a minimum grade of B.
EPIDEM 204B.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EPIDEM 204C.title: Biostatistics III: Advanced Statistical Methods
EPIDEM 204C.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields. Introduces statistical methods for analyzing survival and longitudinal/clustered data, and techniques to resolve missing data.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EPIDEM 204C.prereq_text: EPIDEM 204B with a minimum grade of B or PUBHLTH 204B with a minimum grade of B.
EPIDEM 204C.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EPIDEM 204D.title: Biostatistics IV: Survival Analysis
EPIDEM 204D.description: Advanced statistical analysis for epidemiologic studies, focusing on time-to-event data. Modern approaches, covering survival analysis, missing data, and statistical power analysis. SAS procedures PHREG, LIFEREG, and LIFETEST for intricate dataset analysis. Emphasis on model selection and proper interpretation.
EPIDEM 204D.prereq_text: EPIDEM 204B with a minimum grade of B or STATS 202 with a minimum grade of B.

EPIDEM 205.title: Environmental Epidemiology
EPIDEM 205.description: Concentrates on epidemiological approaches to the assessment of community environmental hazards; issues involved in environmental exposure estimation; interdisciplinary approaches to environmental epidemiology, including the use of biomarkers of exposures and susceptibility; epidemiological studies within the context of risk assessment.
EPIDEM 205.prereq_text: EPIDEM 200 with a minimum grade of B- and EPIDEM 204 with a minimum grade of B-.

EPIDEM 207.title: Nutritional Epidemiology
EPIDEM 207.description: Human nutrition issues requiring epidemiologic principles and quantitative methods; historical and cultural dietary patterns; population dietary assessment; statistical approaches in nutrition research; public health and clinical topics including nutritional biochemistry and genomics, dietary guidelines, and food policy.
EPIDEM 207.prereq_text: (PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B- or EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B-) and (EPIDEM 204A with a minimum grade of B- or PUBHLTH 204A with a minimum grade of B-).

EPIDEM 215.title: Introduction to Statistical Genetics
EPIDEM 215.description: Provides students with knowledge of the basic principles, concepts, and methods used in statistical genetic research. Topics include principles of population genetics, and statistical methods for family- and population-based studies.
EPIDEM 215.prereq_text: Two quarters of upper-division or graduate training in statistical methods.

EPIDEM 220A.title: Data Management I
EPIDEM 220A.description: Learn SAS basics, Base SAS, DATA step essentials, and PROCs for data exploration and analysis. Topics include data reading, variable creation, sorting, merging, and common functions. Priority for MS/PhD Epidemiology, MPH Epidemiology/Biostatistics students concurrently enrolled.
EPIDEM 220A.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EPIDEM 220B.title: Data Management II
EPIDEM 220B.description: Develop practical R programming skills through a comprehensive introduction to data import, cleaning, and basic handling. Goals include creating simple statistical summaries, managing and visualizing data, and producing reproducible, professional reports. Emphasize foundational programming techniques and prepare students to perform

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EPIDEM 220B.prereq_text: EPIDEM 220A with a minimum grade of B and (EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B or PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B) and (EPIDEM 204A with a minimum grade of B or PUBHLTH 207A with a minimum grade of B or STATS 201 with a minimum grade of B).
EPIDEM 220B.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EPIDEM 232.title: Cardiovascular Disease Epidemiology and Prevention
EPIDEM 232.description: Insights into the descriptive epidemiology of cardiovascular disease, the worldwide cardiovascular disease epidemic, pivotal epidemiologic studies, assessment techniques for cardiovascular risk, and prevention and management strategies.

EPIDEM 244.title: Toxic Chemicals in Environment
EPIDEM 244.description: Industrial ecology of toxicants and their impacts on environmental quality and human health. Explores theoretical basis of toxicity thresholds and regulatory issues. Uses classic and contemporary research articles to understand the legacy of traditional toxicants, and to identify emerging threats.

EPIDEM 260.title: Machine Learning with R
EPIDEM 260.description: Hands-on course on machine learning for students who are familiar with R. Covers topics on Regression and Classification Trees (CART), Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, Dimension Reduction, and Clustering.
EPIDEM 260.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EPIDEM 264.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
EPIDEM 264.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

EPIDEM 264.prereq_text: ( MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
EPIDEM 264.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

EPIDEM 269.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
EPIDEM 269.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

EPIDEM 275.title: Special Topics in Epidemiology
EPIDEM 275.description: Presents various topics and the latest research in the broad field of epidemiology.

EPIDEM 280.title: Research Communication in Epidemiology
EPIDEM 280.description: Develop skills in literature review, critical appraisal of scientific research, and effective communications tailored specifically for the field of epidemiology. Communicate epidemiological concepts through various mediums, emphasizing both written and verbal communication.
EPIDEM 280.restriction: Epidemiology majors and MPH - Epidemiology majors only.

EPIDEM 282.title: Epidemiology Department Seminar
EPIDEM 282.description: A forum for the presentation of recent research to epidemiology students, faculty, and other interested parties. The atmosphere is informal, yet rigorous. Speakers range from graduate students through distinguished visitors from other institutions.

EPIDEM 296.title: M.S. Thesis Research and Writing
EPIDEM 296.description: Individual research and study necessary for a graduate student to prepare and complete the thesis required for the Master of Science (M.S.) degree.

EPIDEM 297.title: PhD Degree Dissertation Research & Writing
EPIDEM 297.description: Individual research and study necessary for a graduate student to prepare and complete the dissertation required for the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree.

EPIDEM 399.title: University Supervised Teaching
EPIDEM 399.description: Limited to students with active Teaching Assistant (T.A.) appointments.

EURO ST 9.title: Topics in Europe in the Middle Ages
EURO ST 9.description: Explores the literature, history, and thought of the European Middle Ages. Topics may include understandings of self and community, aristocratic power and courtly life, colonialism, crusading, religious beliefs and persecution, monasticism and reform, university culture, epic literature, and Arthurian romance.

EURO ST 10.title: Topics in Historical Foundations (1500-1800)
EURO ST 10.description: Offers an overview of the European experience from its social, political, and cultural foundations to modern European issues and institutions in a globalized world. Topics include social, political, and cultural history up to the French Revolution.

EURO ST S10.title: Historical Foundations: Europe and the Foundations of the Modern World
EURO ST S10.description: Encompasses a variety of perspectives in the social sciences and the humanities involving crucial developments coming out of Europe from roughly 1500 to 1800, (the Protestant Reformation through the French Revolution), that helped shape the modern (western) world.

EURO ST 11.title: Issues and Institutions in Modern Europe (1789-1945)
EURO ST 11.description: Offers an overview of modern European societies in social, political, and cultural terms. Topics include shifting geopolitical borders, social movements, and various forms of cultural expression (film, art, literature) as they intersect with and shape issues and events after 1800.

EURO ST S11.title: Europe's Futures: 1755-Present
EURO ST S11.description: Introduces students to competing approaches from humanities and social sciences to conceptualizing the future in politics, art, and literature. From the enlightenment to today, investigates the cultural and political context of moments when new ideas emerged to secure Europe's futures.

EURO ST 12.title: What is the Origin of Language?
EURO ST 12.description: Teaches symbol-based logic and universal grammar in human language as tools to investigate the origin of language. Does language originate with reason? Is language inherently universal or diverse? Does it begin as something literal or figurative?

EURO ST 13.title: Topics in Contemporary Europe (1945 – Today)
EURO ST 13.description: Offers a perspective on contemporary politics and social and cultural life of today’s Europe. Introduces students to literature, film, and social theory crises of the contemporary world as they emanated from World War II, such as nationalism and populism.

EURO ST 100A.title: Topics in European Literatures and Visual Cultures
EURO ST 100A.description: Explores developments in literature and/or the visual culture (art, film, media) within the broader context of Europe by comparing different traditions.

EURO ST 100B.title: Topics in European Identities: Race, Nation, Religion, Migration
EURO ST 100B.description: Introduces Europe not as a geographical location but as a site of constant evolution and change. Its “identity” has been negotiated and is being negotiated in the face of significant social, cultural, and political developments, also in a global context.

EURO ST 100C.title: Topics in European Thought, Culture, and Society
EURO ST 100C.description: Introduces multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in European society, culture, art, literature, philosophy, and politics.

EURO ST 101A.title: European Studies Core I - Early Europe (Pre-1789)
EURO ST 101A.description: Introduction to multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in European society, culture, art, literature, and politics; encourages students to explore intersections among disciplines. Possible themes: Concept of Europe in Renaissance, Self and Other: Europe and Islam, Hybrid Cultures in Medieval Europe.

EURO ST 101B.title: European Studies Core II: Modern Europe (Post-1789)
EURO ST 101B.description: Multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in modern European society, culture, art, literature, and politics, encouraging students to see points of intersection among disciplines. Possible themes: Subjects, Citizens, and Representation; Europe in the World; European Revolutions in Art and Society.

EURO ST 102.title: Topics in Early European History and Culture: Pre-1789
EURO ST 102.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts (art, literature, music, political theory) from the pre-1789 period in more than one European country.

EURO ST 103.title: Topics in Modern European History and Culture: Post-1789
EURO ST 103.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts (art, literature, music, political theory) from 1789 to present in more than one European country.

EURO ST 139W.title: Topics in European Culture and Society
EURO ST 139W.description: Students engage in rigorous, in-depth, interdisciplinary exploration of specific topics, periods, or themes, investigating and analyzing the intersection of history and culture in different periods and geographical locations in Europe.
EURO ST 139W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

EURO ST 150.title: Topics in European Culture and Society
EURO ST 150.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts from an interdisciplinary perspective (art, literature, music, political theory). The historical focus could be from the Middle Ages to the present.

EURO ST 190W.title: Senior Seminar in European Studies
EURO ST 190W.description: Capstone research seminar. Students engage in rigorous, in-depth, interdisciplinary exploration of specific topics, periods, or themes, investigating and analyzing the intersection of material and discursive culture in different historical periods and geographical locations.
EURO ST 190W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

EURO ST 199.title: Independent Study
EURO ST 199.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty advisor. Substantial written work required.

EURO ST 200A.title: Core Seminar I: Foundations of European Thought and Culture
EURO ST 200A.description: Provides a historical, geographical, and methodological overview of foundational texts and issues in European thought and culture. Covering several historical periods between the Middle Ages and the present, students will see how ideas and institutions change over time.

EURO ST 200B.title: Core Seminar II: Theorizing Periods and Movements in European Thought and Culture
EURO ST 200B.description: Periods and movements still form basic units for organizing European thought and theory, even as such categories are problematized. This course will allow for greater focus on a specific time period or constellation of issues around a period or movement.

EURO ST 200C.title: Core Seminar III: European Thought and Culture Beyond Europe
EURO ST 200C.description: Studies the intersection and afterlives of European thought and culture with and in non-European contexts, the way European thought and culture has been translated and transformed, taken up and challenged, in colonial, postcolonial, and other global situations.

EURO ST 201.title: Topics in European Studies
EURO ST 201.description: Seminars on various topics related to European Studies.

EURO ST 290.title: Reading and Conference
EURO ST 290.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

EURO ST 299.title: Independent Research
EURO ST 299.description: For students to do independent research with advisors on their master's thesis or master's examination reading lists.

FIN 203A.title: Financial Reporting for Management
FIN 203A.description: Financial reporting is concerned with the preparation and public dissemination of financial reports designed to reflect corporate performance and financial condition. Provides a base level of knowledge needed by corporate executives to understand and discuss corporate financial statements.

FIN 209B.title: Investments Management
FIN 209B.description: Introduction to how securities are traded and how their prices are determined. Discussion of different market organizations, including some recently developed online financial markets. Study of pricing models, including Capital Asset, factor models, and Arbitrage Pricing Theory.

FIN 210.title: Foundations of Finance
FIN 210.description: Examines foundations of finance. Teaches tools such as time value of money, capital budgeting techniques, cash flow analysis. Examines foundations of investment management and theory/empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, asset pricing models, factor models, option pricing theory.

FIN 211.title: Master of Finance ProSeminar
FIN 211.description: Provides students in the Merage School Master of Finance program with information and practical skills for success in the program and for business career planning.

FIN 231.title: Financial Statement Analysis
FIN 231.description: Develops skills to extract, analyze, and interpret financial statements for investment and credit decisions. Covers profitability, cash flow, and credit risk analysis, accounting quality assessment, and financial forecasting, integrating data analytics tools including GPT, SQL, and Tableau.
FIN 231.restriction: School of Business students and Master of Finance only.

FIN 240.title: Financial Research Methodology
FIN 240.description: Provides an introduction into the computational research methods necessary in modern finance, such as optimization, simulation methods, and finite difference and finite element methods. Some applications include quadratic programming for portfolio selection and option pricing.

FIN 241.title: Risk Management
FIN 241.description: Examines modern techniques for managing financial risks, including market, credit, liquidity, and operational risks. Covers measurement techniques for different financial risks and instruments. Discusses how risk measurement tools can be used for management of the risk/return profile of financial institutions.
FIN 241.prereq_text: FIN 249 with a minimum grade of B-.

FIN 242.title: Portfolio Management
FIN 242.description: Provides a working understanding of the themes and concepts of portfolio management. Covers several disciplines, such as investment valuation, investment decision-making, investing styles, asset allocation, monitoring and re-balancing portfolios, risk management strategies, performance evaluation, and attribution analysis.
FIN 242.prereq_text: ( BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR DIGITAL LEADERSHIP MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - FULLY EMPLYD MAJORS ONLY OR BIOTECHNOLOGY MGMT MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - EXECUTIVE MAJORS ONLY )
FIN 242.restriction: Biotechnology Management majors, School of Business students, Master of Finance, and Master in Management only.

FIN 243.title: Bonds and Fixed Income
FIN 243.description: Addresses concepts covering a broad spectrum of debt securities with emphasis on qualitative and quantitative analysis of fixed income securities in many areas, including corporate (credit) debt, MBS/ABS, structured debt, and credit derivatives.
FIN 243.restriction: Biotechnology Management majors, School of Business students, Master in Management, and Master of Finance only.

FIN 244.title: Multinational Finance
FIN 244.description: Examines the history of the world’s foreign exchange markets, the macroeconomics of foreign exchange, major parity conditions, hedging of currency exposure and international investment. Gives students a basic understanding of foreign exchange market.
FIN 244.restriction: Biotechnology Management majors, School of Business students, Master in Management, and Master of Finance only.

FIN 245.title: FinTech
FIN 245.description: Provides working knowledge of the role of IT-enabled innovation in financial markets to help students acquire an understanding of broad economic issues that are of wide applicability in many areas of FinTech. Both qualitative analysis and quantitative applications are explored.
FIN 245.restriction: Biotechnology Management majors, School of Business students, and Master in Management only.

FIN 246D.title: The Real Estate Development Process
FIN 246D.description: Nature and composition of development community and development process. Emphasis on role of conflicting interests, values and goals, and market uncertainty. Special attention paid to deal structuring and risk management. Lectures, guest lecturers, team projects evaluating actual development project.

FIN 246F.title: Seminar in Management of the Real Estate Enterprise
FIN 246F.description: Capstone seminar. Looks beyond “The Deal” to management of the real estate enterprise itself. Explores aspects of decision-making focused upon strategic objectives: goal setting, legal/tax structures, public vs. closely-held entities, corporate ethics, capital structure, managing growth, diversification, technology. Guest professionals.
FIN 246F.prereq_text: ( BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR DIGITAL LEADERSHIP MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - FULLY EMPLYD MAJORS ONLY OR BIOTECHNOLOGY MGMT MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - EXECUTIVE MAJORS ONLY )

FIN 246H.title: Real Estate Transactions
FIN 246H.description: For real estate professionals engaged in purchasing, selling, appraising, evaluating, analyzing and lending on, and developing real property with the basic tools needed to understand the primary elements of a commercial real estate transaction in California.

FIN 246I.title: Corporate Real Estate Management (CREM)
FIN 246I.description: Introduction to Corporate Real Estate Management (CREM) and its many facets. Appreciate the role of CREM, its impact on global society, and its importance to both the real estate community and corporations that it supports.

FIN 247.title: Cases in Corporate Financial Management
FIN 247.description: Case-based course in corporate finance. Introduces advanced analytical tools and techniques for value-based financial management in a broad range of corporate settings, including financial forecasting, mergers and acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, ownership and control, corporate restructuring, and financial distress.

FIN 249.title: Derivatives
FIN 249.description: Covers major derivative instruments that are widely used for hedging, including forward, futures, swaps and options, speculation, and arbitrage. Focuses on understanding the instruments, how to use and price them, basic risk management principles, and how to implement investment strategies.

FIN 250.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
FIN 250.description: Focuses on mastering mergers and acquisitions concepts and techniques that enable participants to practically apply them in related fields such as investment banking, consulting, and corporate development. Studies drivers of success in M&A with heavy attention on transactional review.
FIN 250.prereq_text: ( BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR DIGITAL LEADERSHIP MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - FULLY EMPLYD MAJORS ONLY OR BIOTECHNOLOGY MGMT MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - EXECUTIVE MAJORS ONLY )

FIN 252.title: Wealth Management
FIN 252.description: Provides overview of considerations needed to connect singular functional areas that comprise personal and business wealth management, including basic and advanced estate planning, investment management, tax management, life/liability and property/casualty insurance, medical and long‐term care coverage, retirement and philanthropy considerations.
FIN 252.restriction: Master Of Finance majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Business students only.

FIN 253.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
FIN 253.description: Overview of venture capital and private equity, which constitute the “alternative” asset class (as opposed to conventional investments). Many start-up and entrepreneurial firms require substantial capital, and venture capital and private equity organizations finance these high-risk but potentially high-reward companies.

FIN 255.title: Finance Internship
FIN 255.description: Provides students with opportunities to apply knowledge obtained from classroom theory through actual practical work experiences. Also provides knowledge of career opportunities, understanding of finance in business environments, and preparation for the finance profession.

FIN 256.title: Financial Innovation
FIN 256.description: Examines financial innovation across product, technology, and ESG domains. Explores innovation cycles, regulatory implications, and economic impact. Applies Clayton Christensen's Theory of Disruption to finance and investigates methods for quantifying innovation and managing associated risks.
FIN 256.restriction: School of Business students and Master of Finance only.

FIN 258.title: Fundamentals of Financial Analysis
FIN 258.description: Introduces foundational investment concepts aligned with the CFA Level I curriculum, covering ethics, financial statement analysis, equity and fixed income valuation, corporate issuers, alternatives, and portfolio management. Prepares students to apply professional standards in investment practice.

FIN 270.title: Application of Machine Learning in Finance
FIN 270.description: Explores Machine Learning applications in finance and business, covering supervised and unsupervised learning, CART, random forests, SVM, neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Emphasizes real-world implementation, model validation, ethics, and algorithmic bias.
FIN 270.restriction: School of Business students and Master of Finance only.

FIN 271.title: Programming and Data Analysis for Business
FIN 271.description: Introduces Python programming for finance and business, covering data cleaning, web scraping, robotic process automation, machine learning, and textual analysis. Builds transferable skills applicable across programming languages. No prior programming experience required.
FIN 271.restriction: School of Business students and Master of Finance only.

FIN 290.title: Special Topics in Finance
FIN 290.description: Studies in selected areas of finance. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
FIN 290.prereq_text: ( BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR DIGITAL LEADERSHIP MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - FULLY EMPLYD MAJORS ONLY OR BIOTECHNOLOGY MGMT MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - EXECUTIVE MAJORS ONLY )
FIN 290.restriction: Master Of Finance majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Business students only.

FIN 296.title: Master of Finance Capstone
FIN 296.description: Students work in teams on an applied finance project associated with their area of focus to demonstrate knowledge and expertise. The project can involve experiential learning, collaboration with a faculty member, or association with an internship.

FIN 299.title: Individual Study
FIN 299.description: Individual study under the direction of a select faculty member.

FLM&MDA 75.title: Media and Identities
FLM&MDA 75.description: Examines how media give expression to cultural and social identities, through onscreen representations and behind-the-scenes practices. Studies how media reflect and influence cultural politics.
FLM&MDA 75.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 76.title: Global Media
FLM&MDA 76.description: Examines global media, including different approaches to their study, focusing on how film, television, streaming, and digital media circulate across borders and shape cultural identities, industries, and power relations.
FLM&MDA 76.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA H80.title: Honors Seminar: Race Sport Media
FLM&MDA H80.description: Honors seminar examining the intersection of race, sports, and media in everyday U.S. popular culture (film, TV, advertising, gaming, social media) and political culture.

FLM&MDA 85.title: Introduction to Film and Visual Analysis
FLM&MDA 85.description: Introduces the language and techniques of visual and film analysis. Teaches students to analyze the moving image; emphasize framing, camera movement, and sound; and conveys how editing produces meaning, reproduces historical ideologies, fosters or disrupts narrative, and cues spectators. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 85.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 86.title: Introduction to Television Analysis
FLM&MDA 86.description: Introduces critical approaches to the study of television from a range of theoretical perspectives. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 86.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 87.title: Introduction to New Media and Digital Technologies
FLM&MDA 87.description: The study of digital media, computer-mediated communication, and Internet cultures, from historical and theoretical perspectives. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 87.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 101A.title: History of Film I: The Silent Era
FLM&MDA 101A.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from its invention to the adoption of synchronous sound. Includes early exhibition, developments in narrative and editing, the formation of the studio system, and avant-garde film movements. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 101A.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 101B.title: History of Film II: The Studio Era
FLM&MDA 101B.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from the 1930s through the 1960s. Includes the Hollywood studio system, propaganda films, Italian neorealism, post-war Japanese cinema, and the French New Wave. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 101B.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 101C.title: History of Film III: The Contemporary Era
FLM&MDA 101C.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from the late 1960s to the present. Includes New Hollywood and independent U.S. films, ethnic cinemas, postcolonial cinemas, East-Asian new waves, and digital filmmaking. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 101C.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 101D.title: History of Radio and Television
FLM&MDA 101D.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical development of radio and television. Includes rise of broadcasting, transition to cable, and emergence of streaming. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 101D.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 101E.title: History of Digital Media
FLM&MDA 101E.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical development of digital media. May include history of video games, computing, and social media. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 101E.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 110.title: Film and Media Theory
FLM&MDA 110.description: Survey of major directions in film and media theory. Various theories of mass culture, realism, auteurism, semiotics, feminism, cultural studies, and theories of other media, with an emphasis on developing the student’s ability to analyze and articulate a theoretical argument. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 110.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85 and FLM&MDA 86 and FLM&MDA 87 and (FLM&MDA 101A or FLM&MDA 101B or FLM&MDA 101C or FLM&MDA 101D or FLM&MDA 101E). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 111.title: Film and Media Theory and Practice
FLM&MDA 111.description: Seminar focusing on issues in film and media production and editing. Reading and exercises to understand aspects of film and media production (montage, sound, film movement, directing, and mise en scène), and how ideology works in tandem with style.
FLM&MDA 111.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85 and FLM&MDA 86 and FLM&MDA 87 and FLM&MDA 120A and (FLM&MDA 101A or FLM&MDA 101B or FLM&MDA 101C or FLM&MDA 101D or FLM&MDA 101E). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 112.title: Topics in Genre Study
FLM&MDA 112.description: Critical approaches to the serial productions we call "genre" films such as westerns, weepies, musicals, horror films, and others; televisual genres such as sitcoms, drama, comedy, news, docudrama, police; Internet categories such as chat-rooms, listservs, Web pages.
FLM&MDA 112.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 113.title: Topics in Narrative/Image
FLM&MDA 113.description: What relations do sound, image, and story assume in film, television, video, and Internet narratives? In what ways do these media interact with and borrow from each other and traditional story-telling media? How have the new media explored non-narrative strategies?
FLM&MDA 113.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 115.title: Topics in Authorship
FLM&MDA 115.description: Theoretical and analytical discussions of visual media authorship, focusing on case studies of directors, producers, scriptwriters, and film, video, and digital artists.
FLM&MDA 115.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 117A.title: Introduction to Screenwriting
FLM&MDA 117A.description: Introduction to the technique and format of the screenplay, with a particular focus on its three act structural elements: coverage, treatment, and 60 beat outline. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 117A.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 117B.title: Intermediate Screenwriting
FLM&MDA 117B.description: Exercises in the development of screenplays, with emphasis on formal and structural considerations of character development. Students work with the hero structure and other character development methodologies, such as method acting. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 117B.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 117A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 118A.title: Writing Television I
FLM&MDA 118A.description: Introduction to the technique and format of the television screenplay. Focuses on character, storytelling, structure, and scene development; culminating in a one-hour drama series treatment and first act of the pilot.
FLM&MDA 118A.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 86. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 118B.title: Writing Television II
FLM&MDA 118B.description: Intermediate-level screenwriting class exploring the one-hour television drama format. Students write and workshop an original pilot, continuing work started in 118A, and finish a complete draft of the pilot script.
FLM&MDA 118B.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 118A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 120A.title: Basic Production
FLM&MDA 120A.description: Introduction to the basic apparatus of video/film production. The elementary essentials of production, including the use of camera and lenses, lighting, editing, and sound. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 120A.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 120B.title: Intermediate Production
FLM&MDA 120B.description: Students work on individual and group projects, utilizing skills and insights introduced in Film and Media Studies 120A. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 120B.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 120A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 120C.title: Production Workshop
FLM&MDA 120C.description: As film and video are collaborative media, students form production groups and ultimately produce final 10-15-minute film/video projects. Materials Fee
FLM&MDA 120C.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 120B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 130.title: Multicultural Topics in the Media
FLM&MDA 130.description: Investigation of media representations of gender, race, and sexuality in the United States. Topics include media images of and by one or more minority groups in the United States, including African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicano/Latinos, Native Americans, gays, and lesbians.
FLM&MDA 130.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 139W.title: Writing on Film and Media
FLM&MDA 139W.description: Writing on cinema, television, and/or digital culture, emphasizing identification of reliable sources, close readings, addressing academic, professional, and/or popular audiences. Requires at least 4,000 words of assigned composition.
FLM&MDA 139W.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85 or FLM&MDA 86 or FLM&MDA 87. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
FLM&MDA 139W.restriction: Film and Media Studies majors only.

FLM&MDA 143.title: Critical Theory of Television
FLM&MDA 143.description: Introduction to critical, theoretical, and scholarly understandings and analyses of television, which offer in-depth analyses of television programming, audience reception practices, and industry strategies of address.
FLM&MDA 143.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 86. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 144.title: Studies in New Media
FLM&MDA 144.description: Advanced analysis of the technologies, texts, theories, and cultures of computers, video games, networks, or platforms.
FLM&MDA 144.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 87. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 145.title: Topics in Popular Culture and Media
FLM&MDA 145.description: Considers the forms, ideologies, consumption, and marketing of popular entertainment and technologies. May focus on cultural studies methods, transnational approaches, and synergy between media.
FLM&MDA 145.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 146.title: Topics in Sound Studies
FLM&MDA 146.description: Focuses on the production, theories, and meanings of sound recordings, music, and/or audio technologies. Topics may include the cultures of popular music and audio devices, music television, and theories of film sound.
FLM&MDA 146.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 151.title: Topics in Documentary and Experimental Film and Media
FLM&MDA 151.description: Examines nonfiction and/or experimental cinemas and media, such as documentary, the historical avant-garde, video art, and activist media. Students consider the specific aesthetics and ideologies of forms distinct from narrative feature films.
FLM&MDA 151.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 160.title: National/Regional Cinemas and Media
FLM&MDA 160.description: National schools, period styles, or cultural movements beyond U.S. cinema, as defined by national borders or by geographic regions, such as Latin America. May be approached from a comparative perspective.
FLM&MDA 160.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 161.title: Global/Transnational Cinemas and Media
FLM&MDA 161.description: Analyzes the multinational production, circulation, and reception of film and media texts beyond singular national borders or specific geographic regions. Topics may include transnational co-productions, exports, and diasporic reception.
FLM&MDA 161.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 162.title: Topics in US Cinema
FLM&MDA 162.description: Explores the modes of production and distribution, aesthetics, and contexts that have shaped cinema in the United States. Topics may include classical Hollywood, American independent cinema, or periods such as 1970s cinema.
FLM&MDA 162.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 185.title: Topics in Television and New Media
FLM&MDA 185.description: Advanced seminar focusing on special topics in television and new media. Past examples have included courses on media marketing and brand identity; television and sound; game theory; and other issues related to popular culture, broadcast media, and new media technologies.
FLM&MDA 185.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 86 or FLM&MDA 87. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 190.title: Special Topics in Film and Modern Media
FLM&MDA 190.description: Special issues concerned with film and media history, theory, and criticism.
FLM&MDA 190.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 191.title: Special Topics in Critical Practice
FLM&MDA 191.description: Integrates critical analysis, historical, and theoretical methods with creative projects to illuminate film and media production and industries. May include courses in adaptation, writing television, media activism, writing the short film, performance studies, and movie title sequences.
FLM&MDA 191.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 85. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 192.title: Special Topics in Advanced Film Production
FLM&MDA 192.description: Focuses on special topics in production. Culminates in final 6-10-minute group film projects. Topics include producing, acting, and/or directing in short films, experimental films, documentaries, television, and other media.
FLM&MDA 192.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 120A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 193.title: Special Topics in Advanced Screenwriting
FLM&MDA 193.description: Focuses on special topics in screenwriting. Topics include adaptation, alternative screenwriting, writing the first feature, act two construction, and rewriting.
FLM&MDA 193.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 117A or FLM&MDA 118A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 194.title: Special Topics in Interdisciplinary Studies
FLM&MDA 194.description: Interdisciplinary approaches to special issues concerned with film and media history, theory, and criticism.

FLM&MDA 197.title: Professional Internship
FLM&MDA 197.description: Professional internship in the film, broadcast, and/or digital media industries designed to provide students with closely supervised professional experience to enhance their understanding of media from industrial, historical, and critical perspectives. Journal and final report required.

FLM&MDA 198.title: Creative Project
FLM&MDA 198.description: Creative project in screenwriting, filmmaking, videomaking, or Web or internet design intended to provide advanced production and creative writing training beyond the Film and Media Studies 117A-B-C or 120A-B-C series. Final project required.
FLM&MDA 198.prereq_text: (FLM&MDA 85 and FLM&MDA 117A and FLM&MDA 117B and FLM&MDA 117C) or (FLM&MDA 120A and FLM&MDA 120B and FLM&MDA 120C). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Recommended: FLM&MDA 101A.

FLM&MDA 199.title: Directed Research
FLM&MDA 199.description: Directed reading and research under supervision of a faculty member in topic areas not covered by regular course offerings. Final research paper required.
FLM&MDA 199.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

FLM&MDA 285A.title: Film Studies: Theory and Methods
FLM&MDA 285A.description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in film studies.

FLM&MDA 285B.title: Television Studies: Theory and Methods
FLM&MDA 285B.description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in television studies.

FLM&MDA 285C.title: Digital Media and Game Studies: Theory and Methods
FLM&MDA 285C.description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in digital media and game studies.

FLM&MDA 286A.title: Film and Media Studies Historiography
FLM&MDA 286A.description: Approaches to film and media studies historiography.

FLM&MDA 286B.title: Media/Power/Culture
FLM&MDA 286B.description: Approaches to the study of power and culture in relation to film and media.

FLM&MDA 286C.title: Methods and Research Design
FLM&MDA 286C.description: Explores a range of research methods and trains students to design original research projects.

FLM&MDA 287.title: Practicum in Pedagogy
FLM&MDA 287.description: Students learn best practices for teaching film and media studies.

FLM&MDA 288A.title: Practicum in Professionalization I
FLM&MDA 288A.description: Students learn best practices for film and media studies professionalization.

FLM&MDA 288B.title: Practicum in Professionalization II
FLM&MDA 288B.description: Students learn best practices for film and media studies professionalization.

FLM&MDA 288C.title: Practicum in Professionalization III
FLM&MDA 288C.description: Students learn best practices for film and media studies professionalization.

FLM&MDA 291.title: Graduate Seminar in Film and Media Studies
FLM&MDA 291.description: Studies in selected areas of film and media studies. Topics vary each quarter.

FLM&MDA 292.title: Graduate Seminar in Film and Media Critical Practice
FLM&MDA 292.description: Integrates critical analysis, historical, and/or theoretical methods with creative projects. Topics vary each quarter.

FLM&MDA 295.title: Directed Reading
FLM&MDA 295.description: Directed reading on a specific topic agreed upon by student and instructor.

FLM&MDA 296.title: Reading for the Preliminary Examination
FLM&MDA 296.description: Directed reading in preparation for the preliminary exam.
FLM&MDA 296.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 285A and FLM&MDA 285B and FLM&MDA 285C and FLM&MDA 286A and FLM&MDA 286B and FLM&MDA 286C.

FLM&MDA 297.title: Prospectus Research
FLM&MDA 297.description: Research and writing of the dissertation prospectus.

FLM&MDA 298.title: Prospectus Writing Practicum
FLM&MDA 298.description: Offered spring quarter each year and taught in a workshop format. Assists students with the preparation and revision of the dissertation prospectus.
FLM&MDA 298.prereq_text: FLM&MDA 285A and FLM&MDA 285B and FLM&MDA 285C and FLM&MDA 286A and FLM&MDA 286B and FLM&MDA 286C.

FLM&MDA 299.title: Dissertation Research
FLM&MDA 299.description: Research and writing of the dissertation.

FRENCH 1A.title: Fundamentals of French
FRENCH 1A.description: First quarter of first-year French in a hybrid format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.

FRENCH 1AB.title: Intensive Fundamentals of French
FRENCH 1AB.description: Intensive first half of first-year French. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to read, write, and speak. Students develop an awareness of and sensibility to French and Francophone life and culture through reading, viewing, and discussion.

FRENCH 1ABSP.title: Accelerated Fundamentals of French for Spanish Speakers
FRENCH 1ABSP.description: First half of first-year French in an accelerated form and hybrid format designed for Spanish Speakers. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH 1ABSP.prereq_text: Two years of high school Spanish, one semester of college Spanish, or heritage speaker of Spanish.

FRENCH 1B.title: Fundamentals of French
FRENCH 1B.description: Second quarter of first-year French in a hybrid format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH 1B.prereq_text: FRENCH 1A with a minimum grade of C.

FRENCH 1BC.title: Intensive Fundamentals of French
FRENCH 1BC.description: Intensive second half of first-year French. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to read, write, and speak. Students develop an awareness of and sensibility to French and Francophone life and culture through reading, viewing, and discussion.
FRENCH 1BC.prereq_text: FRENCH 1AB with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1B with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into FRENCH 1BC is also accepted.

FRENCH 1BCSP.title: Accelerated Fundamentals of French for Spanish Speakers
FRENCH 1BCSP.description: Second half of first-year French in an accelerated form and hybrid format designed for Spanish Speakers. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH 1BCSP.prereq_text: FRENCH 1ABSP with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1AB with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S1AB with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1B with a minimum grade of C. Two years of high school Spanish, one semester of college Spanish, or heritage speaker of Spanish.

FRENCH 1C.title: Fundamentals of French
FRENCH 1C.description: Third quarter of first-year French in a hybrid format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH 1C.prereq_text: FRENCH 1B with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 3.

FRENCH S1AB.title: Intensive Fundamentals of French
FRENCH S1AB.description: First half of first-year French in an intensified form. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.

FRENCH S1BC.title: Intensive Fundamentals of French
FRENCH S1BC.description: Second half of first-year French in an intensified form. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH S1BC.prereq_text: FRENCH S1AB with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1B with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1AB with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1ABSP with a minimum grade of C.

FRENCH 2A.title: Intermediate French
FRENCH 2A.description: Second-year French in a hybrid format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH 2A.prereq_text: FRENCH 1C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S1BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1BCSP with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 3. Placement into FRENCH 2A is also accepted.
FRENCH 2A.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

FRENCH 2AB.title: Intensive Intermediate French
FRENCH 2AB.description: First half of Intermediate French in an intensified form and online format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak.
FRENCH 2AB.prereq_text: FRENCH 1C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S1BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1BCSP with a minimum grade of C. Prior high school or college French is recommended. Placement into FRENCH 2AB is also accepted.

FRENCH 2B.title: Intermediate French
FRENCH 2B.description: Second-year French in a hybrid format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH 2B.prereq_text: FRENCH 2A with a minimum grade of C.
FRENCH 2B.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

FRENCH 2BC.title: Intensive Intermediate French
FRENCH 2BC.description: Second half of Intermediate French in an intensified form and online format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak.
FRENCH 2BC.prereq_text: FRENCH S2AB with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2AB with a minimum grade of C. Prior high school or college French is recommended. Placement into FRENCH 2BC is also accepted.

FRENCH 2C.title: Intermediate French
FRENCH 2C.description: Second-year French in a hybrid format. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH 2C.prereq_text: FRENCH 2B with a minimum grade of C.
FRENCH 2C.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

FRENCH S2AB.title: Intermediate French
FRENCH S2AB.description: First half/second half of second-year French in an intensified form. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH S2AB.prereq_text: FRENCH 1C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 1BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into FRENCH S2AB is also accepted.

FRENCH S2BC.title: Intermediate French
FRENCH S2BC.description: First half/second half of second-year French in an intensified form. Students are taught to conceptualize in French as they learn to understand, read, write, and speak. Classes are conducted entirely in French.
FRENCH S2BC.prereq_text: FRENCH S2AB with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2B with a minimum grade of C.

FRENCH 10.title: French Peer Tutoring
FRENCH 10.description: Tutoring Program in which advanced French students provide assistance to students at a lower level. One hour of tutoring per week.

FRENCH 50.title: Topics in French Culture and the Modern World
FRENCH 50.description: Introductory course for non-majors. Focuses on France's role in the modern world and its cultural connections to Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, and the Americas. Taught in English.

FRENCH 102A.title: Grammar and Composition
FRENCH 102A.description: Review of grammar taught in FRENCH 2A-B-C. Students gain facility in writing French and increase reading comprehension. Short texts and films are introduced to generate substantive discussion, and multiple short writing exercises are assigned to solidify skills. Formerly FRENCH 60.
FRENCH 102A.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 102B.title: Topics in Issues in French and Francophone Culture
FRENCH 102B.description: Investigation of an issue of cultural significance in the francophone world through historical documents, literary works, and newspaper articles. Supplemented with films and/or other elements of popular culture. Multiple short writing assignments to solidify writing skills. Formerly FRENCH 61.
FRENCH 102B.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 102C.title: Translation
FRENCH 102C.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of translation from French to English and English to French. Many opportunities provided to improve skills in writing and comprehension. Formerly FRENCH 62.
FRENCH 102C.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 102D.title: Topics in the Work World in French
FRENCH 102D.description: A view into the world of work in French. Areas of study include international relations; French administration; and tensions between management and workers. Attention given to vocabulary and grammar of professional interactions in French. Formerly FRENCH 63.
FRENCH 102D.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 102E.title: Advanced French Language and Style
