FRENCH 102E.description: Intended for advanced students who wish to improve their expressive capabilities in French. Review of more nuanced grammar points. Emphasis placed on rhetoric, syntax, and precision. Advanced readings increase comprehension. Formerly FRENCH 64.
FRENCH 102E.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 102F.title: French for International Relations
FRENCH 102F.description: Explores the culture of international relations, diplomacy, and humanitarian organizations in France and the French-speaking world with an emphasis on oral communication usually through the completion of simulated professional tasks in a professional context.
FRENCH 102F.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C. Students enrolled in FRENCH 2B can request permission from the department to enroll in FRENCH 102F.

FRENCH 115.title: Topics in Medieval Literature and Culture
FRENCH 115.description: Examines the literature and culture of the Middle Ages with attention to the historical context of feudalism and the early development of the French language.
FRENCH 115.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C.

FRENCH 116.title: Topics in 16th-Century French Literature
FRENCH 116.description: Examines the diverse literature of the Renaissance and the Age of Exploration.
FRENCH 116.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 117.title: Topics in 17th-Century French Literature
FRENCH 117.description: Examines the age of drama and other vibrant forms in French literature of the period.
FRENCH 117.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 118.title: Topics in 18th-Century French Literature
FRENCH 118.description: Examines the literature and philosophy of the Enlightenment, the Ancient Régime, Classicism, and/or Revolution.
FRENCH 118.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 119.title: Topics in 19th-Century French Literature
FRENCH 119.description: Focuses on the literature of an era that experienced many modernist transformations.
FRENCH 119.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 120.title: Topics in 20th-Century French and Francophone Literature
FRENCH 120.description: A study of modern and contemporary literature and culture.
FRENCH 120.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 127.title: Topics in Francophone Literature and Culture
FRENCH 127.description: Literature and cultures of the francophone world.

FRENCH 139W.title: Literature and Society
FRENCH 139W.description: In English. Readings of masterpieces of French literature in their social, political, and historical contexts. Requires at least 4,000 words of assigned composition based on French works. Several essays required.
FRENCH 139W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
FRENCH 139W.restriction: French majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

FRENCH 140.title: Topics in French Literary Genre
FRENCH 140.description: Examines the development and transformation of a single genre, such as the poem or the novel.
FRENCH 140.prereq_text: FRENCH 2C with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH 2BC with a minimum grade of C or FRENCH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or French Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

FRENCH 150.title: Topics in French Literature and Culture
FRENCH 150.description: Study of a theme, movement, or problem crucial to understanding French Literature and Culture.

FRENCH 160.title: French Cinema
FRENCH 160.description: Study of a period, movement, or theme in French or Francophone cinema.

FRENCH 170.title: Topics in History and Literature
FRENCH 170.description: Examines the dialogue between historical events and literary texts.

FRENCH 171.title: Politics and Literature
FRENCH 171.description: Examines the role played by politics and ethics in French literature, film, and culture.

FRENCH 199.title: Topics in French
FRENCH 199.description: A project proposal is prepared by the student and approved by the faculty member who directs the project. Procedure must be completed by the end of the first week of classes.
FRENCH 199.restriction: Repeatability: once for M.A. candidates; twice for Ph.D. candidates.

FRENCH 299.title: Dissertation Research
FRENCH 299.description: For graduate students writing a dissertation with a faculty member in French.

FRENCH 399.title: University Teaching
FRENCH 399.description: For graduate students completing a course on foreign language pedagogy.

GDIM 25.title: Game Design Fundamentals
GDIM 25.description: Explore the fundamentals of game design through the design and play of simple analog game systems. Students explore the principles and usage of game design elements through hands-on projects emphasizing iteration and playtesting in a creative game design community.

GDIM 27.title: Intermediate Game Design
GDIM 27.description: More advanced study of game design principles and systems design through the study of complex problems and play experiences. Topics include economies, game balancing, level design, prototyping, stat design, playtesting, and design documentation.
GDIM 27.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second consideration for enrollment.

GDIM 31.title: Introduction to Programming for Games
GDIM 31.description: Learn the fundamentals of programming for games through hands-on exercises in programming languages like C#, Processing, Visual Studio, .NET, and the Unity engine. Students build several small game prototypes.
GDIM 31.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.

GDIM 32.title: Intermediate Programming for Games
GDIM 32.description: Students advance their skills with game programming, building on existing skills developed in Introduction to Programming for Games. Hands-on projects emphasize general procedural and problem-solving skills, as well as furthering knowledge of C# and the Unity3D/Unreal game engines.
GDIM 32.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors will have second consideration.

GDIM 33.title: Coding In Game Engines
GDIM 33.description: Introduces students to visual scripting tools in game engines in the context of game design, level, design, and experience design. Students gain fluency in one or more visual scripting languages.
GDIM 33.prereq_text: GDIM 31 with a minimum grade of C.
GDIM 33.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second consideration for enrollment.

GDIM 41.title: Games and Society
GDIM 41.description: The study and critical analysis of computer games as art objects, cultural artifacts, gateways to virtual worlds, educational aids, and tools for persuasion and social change. Emphasis on understanding games in their historical and cultural context.

GDIM 49.title: Special Topics in Games and Society
GDIM 49.description: Studies in selected areas of games and their relationship to society. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
GDIM 49.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.

GDIM 51.title: Visual Design Fundamentals
GDIM 51.description: The principles, tools, and techniques of visual design for playable media. How do shape, line, color, composition, typography, and time work together to communicate information, emotion, and meaning in interfaces, game worlds, and stories?
GDIM 51.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Informatics majors have second right of consideration. School of ICS majors have third right of consideration.

GDIM 53.title: Roleplaying and Improvisational Play
GDIM 53.description: How do practices of performance, role-playing, and improvisation overlap with contemporary practices of game design? Connecting these forms of play to their contemporary uses within role-playing games, virtual worlds, and playable media more broadly.
GDIM 53.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.

GDIM 55.title: Storytelling for Interactive Media
GDIM 55.description: The history, theory, and practice of interactive storytelling for games and other interactive media. Starting with the emergence of electronic literature and hypertext narratives, students encounter and experience a compressed history of this emergent form through play, analysis, and design.
GDIM 55.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Informatics majors have second right of consideration. School of ICS majors have third right of consideration.

GDIM 61.title: Introduction to Game Development
GDIM 61.description: Introduction to the design and development of games. Includes core concepts in software development, team management, leadership, and project management.
GDIM 61.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.

GDIM 127.title: Professional Studio/Practicum
GDIM 127.description: Professional skills are essential in today’s competitive job market. Covers interview techniques, resume building, professional networking, personal brand development, online portfolios, and presentation.
GDIM 127.restriction: Seniors and Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Informatics majors have second right of consideration. School of ICS majors have third right of consideration.

GDIM 129.title: Special Topics: Project in Advanced Game Design
GDIM 129.description: Studies in selected areas of advanced game design. Topics addressed vary each quarter. Students work alone or in teams to design and implement a unique game or interactive experience.
GDIM 129.prereq_text: GDIM 25 with a minimum grade of C.
GDIM 129.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second consideration for enrollment.

GDIM 131.title: Data Analytics for Interactive Media
GDIM 131.description: Survey of analysis methods for understanding player and user data, including playtesting, telemetry data collection and analysis, metrics visualization, and its application in development and business.
GDIM 131.prereq_text: STATS 6 with a minimum grade of C or STATS 7 with a minimum grade of C or STATS 67 with a minimum grade of C.
GDIM 131.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Informatics majors have second right of consideration. School of ICS majors have third right of consideration.

GDIM 139.title: Special Topics in Game Programming
GDIM 139.description: Studies in selected areas of game programming. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
GDIM 139.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second consideration for enrollment.

GDIM 149.title: Special Topics in Interactive Media Design
GDIM 149.description: Studies in selected areas of games and interactive media and design. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
GDIM 149.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second consideration for enrollment.

GDIM 161.title: Multiplayer Game Project
GDIM 161.description: Design and develop a multiplayer game using Unity or similar engine, with a focus on learning to work in a development team, writing design documents, working with platform features and limitations, developing engaging mechanics, playtesting, and post-mortems.
GDIM 161.prereq_text: GDIM 27 with a minimum grade of C and GDIM 33 with a minimum grade of C and GDIM 61 with a minimum grade of C.
GDIM 161.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second consideration for enrollment.

GDIM 163.title: Solo Game Project
GDIM 163.description: Students work on their own to design, develop, and playtest a small game from scratch, taking into consideration psychology, narrative, platform features and limitations, marketing, computer science capabilities, human-computer interface principles, industry trends, aesthetic judgment, and other factors.
GDIM 163.prereq_text: GDIM 27 with a minimum grade of C and GDIM 33 with a minimum grade of C and GDIM 51 and GDIM 61.
GDIM 163.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second consideration.

GDIM 165.title: Games Entrepreneurship
GDIM 165.description: As the audiences for games continue to diversify so have the channels for game publishing and monetization. Explore connections between the business and creative side of games in context like esports, education, indie game development, mobile apps, and AAA studios.
GDIM 165.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Informatics majors given second consideration. School of ICS majors given third consideration.

GDIM 167A.title: Capstone Game Project I
GDIM 167A.description: Students work in teams to design and implement a unique game or interactive experience. Emphasis on sound, art, and level design, building a community, production values, full utilization of hardware and software platform, and current industry trends.
GDIM 167A.prereq_text: GDIM 27 with a minimum grade of C or GDIM 61 with a minimum grade of C.
GDIM 167A.restriction: Seniors and Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second right of consideration.

GDIM 167B.title: Capstone Game Project II
GDIM 167B.description: Students continue work in teams to design and implement a unique game or interactive experience. Emphasis on sound, art, and level design, building a community, production values, full utilization of hardware and software platform, and current industry trends.
GDIM 167B.prereq_text: GDIM 167A with a minimum grade of C. In Progress grade for GDIM 167A also accepted.

GEN&SEX 20.title: Introduction to Queer Studies
GEN&SEX 20.description: Study of sexuality from the perspective of lesbian, gay, queer, transgender scholarship spanning humanities, social sciences, and arts.

GEN&SEX 50A.title: Gender and Feminism in Everyday Life
GEN&SEX 50A.description: What is gender? Why does studying it matter? Explores how feminism has understood not only gender as a category of social analysis, but how gender structures personal identities, family, citizenship, work and leisure, social policy, sexuality, and language.

GEN&SEX 50B.title: Gender and Power
GEN&SEX 50B.description: From workplace to home to schools to prisons, how are societal institutions and politics “gendered”? Examines power and inequalities around gender, race, class, and sexuality in national and transnational contexts.

GEN&SEX 50C.title: Gender and Popular Culture
GEN&SEX 50C.description: An investigation of gender, race, and sexuality in film, TV, video, music, and advertising, with attention to the ways that popular culture shapes understandings of technology, national identities, leisure and work, historical memory, international communication, and multicultural representation.

GEN&SEX 60A.title: Gender and Science
GEN&SEX 60A.description: Examines science from a variety of feminist viewpoints in order to explore how science influences everyday life. Special attention is given to the ways science shapes our understanding of gender, race, and sexuality.

GEN&SEX 60B.title: Gender and Law
GEN&SEX 60B.description: Introduction to the relationship between gender, race, sexuality, and the law. Critical thinking about how law defines citizenship, political representation, and democracy, focusing on the history of legal reform undertaken in the name of women as a social group.

GEN&SEX 60C.title: Gender and Religion
GEN&SEX 60C.description: Introduces the topic of religion in a feminist context by performing cross-cultural exploration of gender, authority, and faith in various traditions. Study includes (but is not limited to) writings of contemporary Jewish, Christian, and Muslim feminists.

GEN&SEX 100A.title: Feminism and Social Change
GEN&SEX 100A.description: Explores feminist modes of knowledge production in relation to histories and activist practices of various social movements. Examines the kinds of information, research, ideas, theories, and concepts that underlie feminist cultural analysis and social movement organizing.

GEN&SEX 100B.title: Feminist Theory
GEN&SEX 100B.description: Introduction to historical traditions in theory and various conceptual frameworks informing scholarship in gender studies, sexuality studies, and women's studies as a field of critical inquiry.

GEN&SEX 100C.title: Feminist Cultural Studies
GEN&SEX 100C.description: Investigation of the theories and methods that inform the feminist study of culture. Focuses on the interpretation of the visual arts and literature created by, and predominately for, women.

GEN&SEX 100D.title: Queer Knowledges
GEN&SEX 100D.description: Explores the emergence of historical elaboration of non-normative sexual identities, practices, and communities; focuses on medical, legal, literary, aesthetic, scientific, and religious notions about homosexuality and appropriations and subversions of these notions by queer people.

GEN&SEX 110A.title: Gender, State, and Nation
GEN&SEX 110A.description: Examination of gender and sexuality in relation to the production of identities created through participation in state and nation. Examines complexity of relationship between feminism and nationalism, feminism and the state.

GEN&SEX 110B.title: Money, Sex, and Power
GEN&SEX 110B.description: Examination of gender and sexuality in relation to the emergence of the modern world, modernity, and capitalism; commodification, circulation, and transnational exchanges relating to race, gender, class, sexuality, religion, and nationality.

GEN&SEX 110D.title: The Politics of Health and Medicine
GEN&SEX 110D.description: Focuses on cultural and political-economic analysis and representations of disease both within the U.S. and globally.

GEN&SEX 120A.title: Histories of Sexuality
GEN&SEX 120A.description: Examines the historical production of non-normative sexual and gender identities, bodies, practices, and communities. Explores how past formations inform and shape the present and future.

GEN&SEX 120B.title: Image Problems
GEN&SEX 120B.description: Examination of scholarly approaches to gender stereotypes and politics of representation as they present possibilities for critical analysis and produce problems and limitations; how powerful ideas of gender intersect with other forms of social differentiation such as race and class.

GEN&SEX 155.title: Topics in Gender and Sexuality Studies
GEN&SEX 155.description: Designed to provide students with an opportunity to conduct advanced work in Gender and Sexuality Studies.

GEN&SEX 157.title: Topics in Queer Studies
GEN&SEX 157.description: Explores issues in queer studies from one or more of the following perspectives: theoretical, historical, legal, economic, political, sociological, and representation in the arts.

GEN&SEX 165F.title: Gender and Technology
GEN&SEX 165F.description: Using a variety of disciplinary methods, examines how various technological processes and products produce culturally complex meanings associated with gender and technology.

GEN&SEX 167A.title: Militarism and Gender
GEN&SEX 167A.description: Examination of feminist approaches to militarism, war, and political violence; drawing on representations of women as both victims of and participants in military violence; effects of militarism on formations of gender; effects of military industrial complex on nationalism and identity.

GEN&SEX 170.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, Literature, and Language
GEN&SEX 170.description: Topics cover issues in language and literature which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 171.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and History
GEN&SEX 171.description: Topics cover issues in history which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 171A.title: Sex and Conquest in Latin America
GEN&SEX 171A.description: Competing ideas of masculinity and femininity, sexual violence, sexual identities, and gendered hierarchies informed how the Spanish engaged in military and religious domination of Mexican and Andean communities, as well as the forms of native resistance throughout colonial Latin America.

GEN&SEX 172.title: Gender and Ethnicity: Chicana/Latina Feminisms in the US
GEN&SEX 172.description: Focuses on the Latina Feminist Group and testimonios to examine the historical development of Chicana/Latinx feminist thought and practice. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship to survey the diversity of contemporary Chicana/Latinx feminisms through an intersectionality lens.

GEN&SEX 174.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and the Arts
GEN&SEX 174.description: Topics cover issues in the arts which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 175.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and the Media
GEN&SEX 175.description: Topics cover issues in the media which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 181.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and Cognitive Psychology
GEN&SEX 181.description: Topics cover issues in cognitive psychology which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 182.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism and Economics
GEN&SEX 182.description: Topics cover issues in economics which relate to women and gender or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 183.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and Sociology
GEN&SEX 183.description: Topics cover issues in sociology which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 184.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and Political Science
GEN&SEX 184.description: Topics cover issues in political science which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 185.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and Social Sciences
GEN&SEX 185.description: Topics cover issues in social sciences which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 187.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and Social Ecology
GEN&SEX 187.description: Topics cover issues in social ecology which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 188.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and Science
GEN&SEX 188.description: Topics cover issues in science which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 189.title: Topics in Gender, Feminism, and Interdisciplinary Studies
GEN&SEX 189.description: Topics cover issues in interdisciplinary studies which relate to women or gender, or which are taught from a feminist methodological perspective.

GEN&SEX 190.title: Topics in Sexualities Studies
GEN&SEX 190.description: Topics cover issues in the humanities, social sciences, sciences, and arts that relate to critical inquiry of sexualities.

GEN&SEX 197.title: Senior Seminar in Gender and Sexuality Studies
GEN&SEX 197.description: Students read advanced scholarship in Gender and Sexuality Studies and complete a major seminar paper.
GEN&SEX 197.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement.
GEN&SEX 197.restriction: Gender and Sexuality Studies majors only.

GEN&SEX 199.title: Independent Study
GEN&SEX 199.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty member. Substantial written work required. Includes independent study, involving 3-12 hours a week.

GEN&SEX 200A.title: Feminist Knowledge and Social Change
GEN&SEX 200A.description: Provides a broad and introductory overview of Women’s Studies and feminist knowledge, including key concepts, theoretical frameworks, disciplinary approaches and methods, and critical debates that have shaped the field.

GEN&SEX 200B.title: Problems in Feminist Research
GEN&SEX 200B.description: Colloquium on analytic approaches to interdisciplinary feminist research in Women’s Studies and exploration of how feminist knowledges are produced in different academic disciplines.

GEN&SEX 201.title: Special Topics in Feminist Studies
GEN&SEX 201.description: Seminars on various topics in feminist studies.

GEN&SEX 290.title: Directed Research
GEN&SEX 290.description: Directed graduate study/research in Gender and Sexuality Studies.

GERMAN 1A.title: Fundamentals of German
GERMAN 1A.description: Emphasizes the development of meaningful communicative skills in German for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and beginning study of German. With a learner-centered approach, the courses help students develop speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.

GERMAN 1B.title: Fundamentals of German
GERMAN 1B.description: Emphasizes the development of meaningful communicative skills in German for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and beginning study of German. With a learner-centered approach, students develop speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.
GERMAN 1B.prereq_text: GERMAN 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into GERMAN 1B is also accepted.

GERMAN 1BC.title: Intensive German Fundamentals
GERMAN 1BC.description: Second half of first-year German in a time-intensive form. Development of meaningful communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and beginning study of German. Learner-centered approach develops speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.
GERMAN 1BC.prereq_text: GERMAN 1AB with a minimum grade of C or GERMAN 1B with a minimum grade of C or GERMAN S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into GERMAN 1BC is also accepted.
GERMAN 1BC.restriction: GERMAN 1BC and GERMAN 1B and GERMAN 1C and GERMAN S1AB may not be taken for full credit.

GERMAN 1C.title: Fundamentals of German
GERMAN 1C.description: Emphasizes the development of meaningful communicative skills in German for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and beginning study of German. With a learner-centered approach, students develop speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.
GERMAN 1C.prereq_text: GERMAN 1B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into GERMAN 1C is also accepted.

GERMAN S1AB.title: Fundamentals of German
GERMAN S1AB.description: First half of first-year German in a time-intensive form. Development of meaningful communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and beginning study of German. Learner-centered approach develops speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.

GERMAN S1BC.title: Fundamentals of German
GERMAN S1BC.description: Second half of first-year German in a time-intensive form. Development of meaningful communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and beginning study of German. Learner-centered approach develops speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.
GERMAN S1BC.prereq_text: GERMAN 1AB with a minimum grade of C or GERMAN 1B with a minimum grade of C or GERMAN S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into GERMAN S1BC is also accepted.

GERMAN 2A.title: Intermediate German
GERMAN 2A.description: Emphasizes communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and intermediate study of German. With a learner-centered approach, helps students develop reading, writing, speaking, listening, grammatical, and cultural skills and knowledge. First-year grammar is reviewed and expanded.
GERMAN 2A.prereq_text: GERMAN 1BC with a minimum grade of C or GERMAN 1C with a minimum grade of C or GERMAN S1BC with a minimum grade of C or German Language and Culture with a minimum score of 3. Placement into GERMAN 2A is also accepted.
GERMAN 2A.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

GERMAN 2B.title: Intermediate German
GERMAN 2B.description: Emphasizes communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and intermediate study of German. With a learner-centered approach, helps students develop reading, writing, speaking, listening, grammatical, and cultural skills and knowledge. First-year grammar is reviewed and expanded.
GERMAN 2B.prereq_text: GERMAN 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into GERMAN 2B is also accepted.
GERMAN 2B.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

GERMAN 2C.title: Intermediate German
GERMAN 2C.description: Emphasizes communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with German speakers and intermediate study of German. With a learner-centered approach, helps students develop reading, writing, speaking, listening, grammatical, and cultural skills and knowledge. First-year grammar is reviewed and expanded.
GERMAN 2C.prereq_text: GERMAN 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into GERMAN 2C is also accepted.
GERMAN 2C.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

GERMAN 97.title: Fundamentals of German (with Emphasis on Reading)
GERMAN 97.description: Primarily for students interested in acquiring a solid reading knowledge of German. Facilitates comprehension and translation of texts in various disciplines. Does not serve as prerequisite for any higher-level German courses or fulfill any undergraduate foreign language requirement.

GERMAN 101.title: Topics in Introduction to German Literature and Culture
GERMAN 101.description: Sample interpretations of texts in their cultural and historical contexts. Introduction to critical language in German.
GERMAN 101.prereq_text: GERMAN 2C with a minimum grade of C or German Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

GERMAN 102.title: Topics in German Culture and Society
GERMAN 102.description: Interdisciplinary introduction to German culture from the perspective of its aesthetic, social, and political aspects. Methodological problems arising from an analysis of culture in its historical context.
GERMAN 102.prereq_text: GERMAN 2C with a minimum grade of C or German Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

GERMAN 103.title: Topics in German Film
GERMAN 103.description: Introduction to the history and interpretation of German film within its cultural and social contexts. Enhances German grammar knowledge and vocabulary and develops sophisticated speaking, writing, and reading skills.
GERMAN 103.prereq_text: GERMAN 2C with a minimum grade of C or German Language and Culture with a minimum score of 4.

GERMAN 115.title: Topics in Advanced German for Business and Economics
GERMAN 115.description: Explores the structure of the German economy and business practices while developing advanced verbal and written skills important for professional life in Germany. Taught in German.
GERMAN 115.prereq_text: GERMAN 101 (may be taken concurrently) or GERMAN 102 (may be taken concurrently) or GERMAN 103 (may be taken concurrently) or GERMAN 104 (may be taken concurrently) or GERMAN 105 (may be taken concurrently).

GERMAN 140W.title: Topics in Literary Theory and Criticism
GERMAN 140W.description: In English. Theoretical dimensions of literary criticism and the German philosophical tradition. Topics have included Marxism, Freudian thought, German Idealist aesthetics, Historicism, twentieth-century hermeneutics, Frankfurt School, and Rezeptionsaesthetik.
GERMAN 140W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

GERMAN 150.title: German Literature and Culture in Translation
GERMAN 150.description: In English. Major works in Germanic literature and culture in context.

GERMAN 160.title: German Cinema
GERMAN 160.description: Historical, theoretical, and comparative perspectives on German cinema.

GERMAN 160W.title: German Cinema
GERMAN 160W.description: Historical, theoretical, and comparative perspectives on German cinema.
GERMAN 160W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

GERMAN 170W.title: Topics in German Linguistics
GERMAN 170W.description: Explores linguistic, sociolinguistic, or ethnography-of-communication topics of German or other Germanic languages (Swedish, Icelandic, Yiddish, and others). Taught in English.
GERMAN 170W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

GERMAN 197.title: German Internship
GERMAN 197.description: In this internship course, students will engage in professional practice (e.g., Engineering, Business Administration, government) in a German setting and thereby increase their knowledge of German language and culture in a setting beyond the academic classroom.

GERMAN 290.title: Independent Study
GERMAN 290.description: Counted toward course requirements for the M.A. or Ph.D. A term paper or project is required.

GERMAN 298.title: Independent Directed Reading
GERMAN 298.description: For students preparing for doctoral examination.

GERMAN 299.title: Dissertation Research
GERMAN 299.description: For students who have been admitted to doctoral candidacy.

GLBLCLT 7.title: Social Media and Social Change
GLBLCLT 7.description: Explores social media’s role in activism, identity formation, and global movements. Students analyze digital campaigns, online rhetoric, and cultural impacts while integrating theoretical perspectives with real-world case studies to develop critical media literacy and digital engagement skills.

GLBLCLT 11.title: Digital Literacies
GLBLCLT 11.description: Examines digital literacy through the lens of the humanities, digital storytelling, and emerging technologies. Explores multimodal composition, digital ethics, and online engagement while analyzing and creating digital narratives to navigate contemporary media and information ecosystems critically.

GLBLCLT 103A.title: Global Cultures I
GLBLCLT 103A.description: Introduction to the processes by which economies, cultural practices, national entities, groups, individuals, and personal identities have undergone globalization. General background and methodological tools for understanding problems and processes of globalization.

GLBLCLT 103B.title: Global Cultures II
GLBLCLT 103B.description: Introduction to the processes by which economies, cultural practices, national entities, groups, individuals, and personal identities have undergone globalization. Explores how globalization has manifested itself in specific topics, periods, or societies.

GLBLCLT 105.title: Language Origins: Evolution, Genetics, and the Brain
GLBLCLT 105.description: Examines how human language(s) may have originated. Studies pertinent techniques (reconstruction) and addresses related questions, including is our language faculty inborn (i.e., genetically encoded)? Can brain imaging and population genetics research help to unlock this mystery of human evolution?

GLBLCLT 191.title: Senior Seminar:Topics in Global Cultures
GLBLCLT 191.description: Students explore a topic(s) concerning processes and/or problems of globalization from an interdisciplinary perspective and build on their critical and analytical skills when investigating cultural and other phenomena that cut across national borders. Research assignments, class presentations, final seminar paper.

GLBLCLT 199.title: Independent Study
GLBLCLT 199.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty advisor. Substantial written work required.

GLBL ME 60A.title: Humanities and Arts: Problems and Methods for Global Middle East Studies
GLBL ME 60A.description: Introduces students to the broad set of humanities and arts approaches to studying the Middle East as a global zone of cultural, political, and economic interaction.

GLBL ME 60B.title: Social Sciences: Problems and Methods for Global Middle East Studies
GLBL ME 60B.description: Introduces students to the broad set of social sciences approaches to studying the Middle East as a global zone of cultural, political, and economic interaction.

GLBL ME 60C.title: Social Ecology and Sciences: Problems and Methods for Global Middle East Studies
GLBL ME 60C.description: Introduces students to the broad set of approaches to studying the Middle East as a global zone of cultural, political, and economic interaction, focusing on the disciplines related to Social Ecology.

GLBL ME 100W.title: Research and Writing for Global Middle East Studies
GLBL ME 100W.description: Research and writing course for Global Middle East Studies majors. The primary focus is to refine the skills necessary for students to engage in independent research and writing in Global Middle East Studies.
GLBL ME 100W.prereq_text: GLBL ME 60A (may be taken concurrently) or GLBL ME 60B (may be taken concurrently) or GLBL ME 60C (may be taken concurrently). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
GLBL ME 100W.restriction: Global Middle East Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

GREEK 1A.title: Classical and Biblical Greek
GREEK 1A.description: Elements of Classical Greek grammar, syntax, and vocabulary.

GREEK 1B.title: Classical and Biblical Greek
GREEK 1B.description: Elements of Classical Greek grammar, syntax, and vocabulary.
GREEK 1B.prereq_text: GREEK 1A with a minimum grade of C.
GREEK 1B.restriction: GREEK 1B and GREEK S1AB and GREEK S1BC may not be taken for full credit.

GREEK 1C.title: Classical and Biblical Greek
GREEK 1C.prereq_text: GREEK 1B with a minimum grade of C.

GREEK 99.title: Special Studies in Greek
GREEK 99.description: Lower-division level independent research with Greek faculty.

GREEK 100.title: Topics in Attic Greek
GREEK 100.description: Selected readings in Attic Greek prose and poetry. Authors may include Xenophon, Lysias, Antiphon, Euripides, and others. Selections from prose and poetry will be read each quarter. Grammar and syntax review included.
GREEK 100.prereq_text: GREEK 1C with a minimum grade of C. Placement into GREEK 100 is also accepted.

GREEK 103.title: Seminar in Greek Prose
GREEK 103.description: Specialized and focused study of a particular Greek prose author or topic.

GREEK 104.title: Seminar in Greek Poetry
GREEK 104.description: Specialized and focused study of a particular topic or author of Greek poetry.

GREEK 198.title: Directed Group Study
GREEK 198.description: Special topics in Greek culture and civilization through directed reading and research.

HEBREW 1A.title: Fundamentals of Hebrew
HEBREW 1A.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Hebrew. May focus on Biblical Hebrew and/or modern Hebrew. Students learn the writing system and basics of grammar via latest pedagogical materials. Topics in Jewish culture are also included.
HEBREW 1A.prereq_text: Placement into HEBREW 1A is also accepted.

HEBREW 10A.title: Hebrew Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
HEBREW 10A.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. HEBREW 10A is for language mentors.

HEBREW 10B.title: Hebrew Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
HEBREW 10B.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. HEBREW 10B is for language mentors.

HISTORY 5.title: Truth, Lies, and History: The Uses of the Past
HISTORY 5.description: Focuses on how struggles over the meaning of historical events have shaped and continue to shape our understandings of the world. Through guest lectures from history faculty, students explore debates about the meaning of the past.

HISTORY 10.title: The Holocaust
HISTORY 10.description: Introduction to the history of European Jewish communities before the Holocaust; the origins of Nazi antisemitism; the implementation of the "Final Solution"; Jewish resistance to the Nazis; and attempts in film and literature to represent the Holocaust since 1945.

HISTORY 11.title: Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity Since WWII
HISTORY 11.description: Investigates instances of genocide since 1945 (including Cambodia, Bosnia, Rwanda, and others); explores the history behind these mass murders; considers why people kill, how victims survive, and questions whether international agreements are enough to prevent crimes against humanity.

HISTORY 12.title: Introductory Topics in History
HISTORY 12.description: Introduces methods and premises of historical study. Topics include introductions to cultural, political, economic, social, and religious history.

HISTORY 15A.title: Native American History
HISTORY 15A.description: Native American history in North America, emphasizing Indigenous perspectives and creative adaptations to changing historical circumstances. Topics may include sovereignty, settler colonialism, treaties, decolonization, Indigeneity; cultural, economic, religious, environmental practices and experiences; and intersections of U.S. and Native histories.

HISTORY 15B.title: The U.S. and Asia
HISTORY 15B.description: Explores the historical and contemporary transnational linkages between the U.S. and regions in Asia and their resultant flows of people, goods, and ideas. Attention given to the role of militarism and processes of globalization, and the histories of cultural contact/conflict.

HISTORY 15C.title: Asian American Histories
HISTORY 15C.description: Examines and compares diverse experiences of major Asian American groups since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics include origins of emigration; the formation and transformation of community; gender and family life; changing roles of Asian Americans in American society. Formerly ASIANAM 60A.

HISTORY 15D.title: History of Sexuality in the US
HISTORY 15D.description: Explores intertwined histories of sexuality, race, and gender in the US. By examining how different cultures and times viewed sexuality, race, and gender, it analyzes relationships between regulation of bodies/behaviors and construction of cultural, economic, and political norms.

HISTORY 15F.title: What to Eat? Immigrants and the Development of American Cuisines
HISTORY 15F.description: Relationship between immigration and changing American foodways; impact of several major culinary traditions of immigrants and racial minorities, such as African Americans, Asian Americans, Mexican Americans, Italian Americans, Irish Americans, and Jewish Americans, on America’s gastronomical and socioeconomic landscape.

HISTORY 15G.title: Racial Segregation in Modern U.S
HISTORY 15G.description: Explores the history of racial segregation in the United States from the late 19th century to the present.

HISTORY 16A.title: World Religions I
HISTORY 16A.description: An introduction to the history, doctrine, culture, and writing of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

HISTORY 16B.title: World Religions II
HISTORY 16B.description: An introduction to various religious traditions in selected areas of the world—including India and South Asia, East Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

HISTORY 16C.title: Religious Dialogue
HISTORY 16C.description: Lectures and discussion on controversial topics in religion: sexual morality; religious violence; science; treatment of women and girls; religious truth, American Constitutional matters; secularization; the future of religion, and other topics.

HISTORY 18A.title: Major Jewish Texts
HISTORY 18A.description: Introduction to the diversity of Jewish cultures from ancient to modern times. Surveys the Jewish experience in various societies and civilizations: ancient Mediterranean, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

HISTORY 21A.title: World: Innovations
HISTORY 21A.description: Treats major themes of world historical development through the mid-17th century, focusing on the Eurasian world, but with secondary emphasis on Africa and the Americas.

HISTORY 21B.title: World: Empires and Revolutions
HISTORY 21B.description: Examines three major transformations that made the world of 1870 dramatically different from that of 1650: e.g., the scientific revolution, industrialization, and the formation of modern states and nations.

HISTORY 21C.title: World: Nation, War, and Rights
HISTORY 21C.description: Considers several major currents of modern history: technological change and its social effects; changes in gender relations; totalitarianism; peasant revolutions and the crisis of colonization; international migration; and ecological problems.

HISTORY 36A.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Early Greece
HISTORY 36A.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from its origins in the Bronze Age to the mid-Archaic period. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, religion, and archaeological remains.

HISTORY 36B.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Late Archaic and Classical Greece
HISTORY 36B.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the Late Archaic period to the Classical period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

HISTORY 36C.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Fourth-Century and Hellenistic Greece
HISTORY 36C.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the fourth century BCE through to the Hellenistic period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

HISTORY 37A.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Origins to Roman Republic
HISTORY 37A.description: A survey of the development of Roman civilization from its eighth century BCE beginnings to the civil wars of the first century BCE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

HISTORY 37B.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Roman Empire
HISTORY 37B.description: A survey of Roman civilization from Augustus’s consolidation of power following the civil wars of the first century BCE to the crisis of the third century CE. Includes social history, literature, art, architecture, and religion.

HISTORY 37C.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: The Fall of Rome
HISTORY 37C.description: A survey of Roman civilization from the crisis of the third century CE to the so-called “fall of Rome” in 476 CE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

HISTORY 40A.title: Colonial America: New Worlds
HISTORY 40A.description: Important themes in the social, economic, political, and cultural development in North America that transformed part of the geographical space into the U.S. Topics include Native Americans, European colonization, African enslavement, borderlands, gender, economic stratification, the American Revolution, the Constitution.
HISTORY 40A.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

HISTORY 40B.title: Nineteenth-Century U.S.: Crisis and Expansion
HISTORY 40B.description: Explores the transformation of American society, economy, and politics during the 19th century. Topics include industrial revolution, slavery, antislavery, women's rights, reform movements, Civil War and Reconstruction, immigration and ethnicity, and cultural and social transformation.
HISTORY 40B.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

HISTORY 40C.title: Modern America: Culture and Power
HISTORY 40C.description: Important themes in U.S. history in the 20th and early 21st centuries. Topics include corporate capitalism, empire, immigration, race, gender, consumer society, World Wars, Progressiveness, New Deal, Great Society, civil rights, women's movements, Vietnam War, conservative politics, and economic stratification.
HISTORY 40C.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

HISTORY 60.title: The Making of Modern Science
HISTORY 60.description: Surveys the history of science and mathematics since the Scientific Revolution, examining central developments both chronologically and thematically, as well as investigating their significance for contemporary philosophical debates about the role and status of current scientific theories.

HISTORY 70A.title: Problems in History: Asia
HISTORY 70A.description: An introduction to the historical problems, the issues of interpretation, the primary sources, and the historical scholarship of the history of Asia, with an emphasis on developing skills in historical essay-writing.

HISTORY 70B.title: Problems in History: Europe
HISTORY 70B.description: An introduction to the historical problems, the issues of interpretation, the primary sources, and the historical scholarship of the history of Europe, with an emphasis on developing skills in historical essay-writing.

HISTORY 70C.title: Problems in History: United States
HISTORY 70C.description: An introduction to the historical problems, the issues of interpretation, the primary sources, and the historical scholarship of the history of the United States, with an emphasis on developing skills in historical essay-writing.

HISTORY 70D.title: Problems in History: Latin America
HISTORY 70D.description: An introduction to the historical problems, the issues of interpretation, the primary sources, and the historical scholarship of the history of Latin America, with an emphasis on developing skills in historical essay-writing.

HISTORY 70E.title: Problems in History: Middle East and Africa
HISTORY 70E.description: An introduction to the historical problems, the issues of interpretation, the primary sources, and the historical scholarship of the history of the Middle East and Africa, with an emphasis on developing skills in historical essay-writing.

HISTORY 70F.title: Problems in History: Transregional History
HISTORY 70F.description: An introduction to the historical problems, the issues of interpretation, the primary sources, and the historical scholarship of transregional history, with an emphasis on developing skills in historical essay-writing.

HISTORY 100W.title: Writing About History
HISTORY 100W.description: Specialized courses focusing on history writing and research skills. Each class reflects the instructor's intellectual interests and is conducted as a discussion group. Limited to 18 students. Several short writing assignments and one longer project meeting the upper-division writing requirement.
HISTORY 100W.prereq_text: HISTORY 5 or HISTORY 12 or HISTORY 15A or HISTORY 15C or HISTORY 15D or HISTORY 16A or HISTORY 16B or HISTORY 16C or HISTORY 18A or HISTORY 21A or HISTORY 21B or HISTORY 21C or HISTORY 40A or HISTORY 40B or HISTORY 40C or HISTORY 60 or HISTORY 70A or HISTORY 70B or HISTORY 70C or HISTORY 70D or HISTORY 70E or HISTORY 70F. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
HISTORY 100W.restriction: History majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

HISTORY 101A.title: Culture, Money, and Globalization
HISTORY 101A.description: Examines the fundamental dynamics of cultural production and consumption under conditions of globalization.

HISTORY 102B.title: Topics in Environmental History
HISTORY 102B.description: Explores the many historical interfaces between climate change, modes of production, and culture. Topics include the environmental history of warfare, imperialism, and famine in the nineteenth century and the history of environmental thought.

HISTORY 110D.title: Topics in Medieval Europe
HISTORY 110D.description: Theme-based approach to the main social, political, religious, and cultural developments in Europe between the 4th and 15th centuries. Topics include the Crusades, medieval towns, medieval visionaries, and the deadly sins.

HISTORY 112D.title: Topics in Early Modern Europe
HISTORY 112D.description: Theme-based approach to the main social, political, and cultural developments in Europe between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries. Topics included Renaissance humanism, Reformation and Counter-Reformation, scientific revolution, court culture and nation building, interactions with non-European peoples, cities and commerce.

HISTORY 114.title: Topics in Modern European History
HISTORY 114.description: Course content changes with instructor. Topics include the Inquisition; science and religion in modern Europe; sex and society in modern Europe; French revolutions; culture in interwar Europe; the Holocaust; the fall of communism in Eastern Europe.

HISTORY 120D.title: War and Empire: France and the World in the 20th Century
HISTORY 120D.description: Examines French experience of World War I, the defeat and occupation by Germany in World War II, the violent struggles that came with the loss of the French empire in the 1950s and 1960s, immigration, French responses to globalization.

HISTORY 123D.title: Topics in Spanish History
HISTORY 123D.description: Topics include Spain in the nineteenth century, the Spanish Civil War, and dictatorship and democracy in modern Spain.

HISTORY 126B.title: The Era of World War II: 1933-45
HISTORY 126B.description: The era of World War II and its political, social and economic history.

HISTORY 128C.title: Topics in the History of Women in Europe
HISTORY 128C.description: Studies in selected areas of history of European women. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 130C.title: Topics in the Jewish History
HISTORY 130C.description: Studies in selected areas of Jewish history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 130D.title: History of Antisemitism
HISTORY 130D.description: Survey of the history of antisemitism, ancient to modern. Topics include medieval religious anti-Judaism, persecution of Jews and Judaism during the Crusades and the Inquisition, the rise of modern racial antisemitism, Nazi antisemitism, and the persistence of antisemitism since 1945.

HISTORY 130F.title: Jews and Power
HISTORY 130F.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority?

HISTORY 131A.title: History of Zoroastrianism
HISTORY 131A.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

HISTORY 131B.title: Ancient Persia
HISTORY 131B.description: Survey of the history of Persia in antiquity.

HISTORY 131C.title: Medieval Persia
HISTORY 131C.description: A survey of Persian history in the context of Late Antique and Medieval Islamic history.

HISTORY 131D.title: Modern Iran
HISTORY 131D.description: The history of Iran from the end of the Safavid Empire in the eighteenth century to the present.

HISTORY 132B.title: The Emergence of the Modern Middle East
HISTORY 132B.description: Offers a survey of the history of the Middle East from the 19th century to the present time. Formerly History 133A.

HISTORY 132C.title: Women and Gender in the Middle East
HISTORY 132C.description: Focuses on women and gender in the Middle East from the pre-modern to the contemporary.

HISTORY 132D.title: Armenians and Armenia in Ancient to Early Modern World History
HISTORY 132D.description: A history of Armenia and Armenians from ethnogenesis to the early modern period at the end of the 1700s within a regional and global context. Takes into account interactions and encounters with the empires, and peoples that encompassed their orbit.

HISTORY 132E.title: Armenians and Armenia in Modern World History
HISTORY 132E.description: Covers the most important themes in the history of Armenians and Armenia in the 19th, 20th, and 21st centuries within a regional (i.e., Middle East and Caucasus) and global context.

HISTORY 132H.title: Topics in Middle Eastern History
HISTORY 132H.description: Topics include the cultural, political, intellectual, social, and/or economic histories of one or many regions of the Middle East.

HISTORY 134A.title: Africa: Societies and Cultures
HISTORY 134A.description: Introduction to the variety of cultures, political organizations, social structures, and artistic expressions created by Africans over a broad time span. Indigenous development of African societies in distinct regions of the continent. Issues, themes, processes for understanding history of Africa.

HISTORY 134C.title: Topics in the History of Africa
HISTORY 134C.description: Studies in selected areas of African history. Topics addressed vary each quarter

HISTORY 134D.title: Topics in South African History
HISTORY 134D.description: Introduction to important historical events and processes in Southern Africa. Focuses on particular themes and explores how those themes change over time. Topics include: changing ideas about race, the development of class structures, identity formation, the role of gender.

HISTORY 134E.title: History of the African Diaspora
HISTORY 134E.description: Examines the causes and consequences of the multiple diasporas of African peoples since the sixteenth century in the Atlantic world, especially the Americas and Europe.

HISTORY 135A.title: The Scientific Revolution
HISTORY 135A.description: An examination of early modern European science from 1500-1700. Includes primary readings from central figures (Copernicus, Harvey, Bacon, Descartes, et al.); themes include the impact of printing, humanism, patronage, technology, and discussion of the term "revolution" in this context.

HISTORY 135E.title: Topics in the History of Science and Technology
HISTORY 135E.description: Studies in selected areas of science and technological history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 135G.title: Language Origins: Evolution, Genetics, and the Brain
HISTORY 135G.description: Examines how human language(s) may have originated. Studies pertinent techniques (reconstruction) and addresses related questions, including is our language faculty inborn (i.e., genetically encoded)? Can brain imaging and population genetics research help to unlock this mystery of human evolution?

HISTORY 137.title: Surviving Epidemics
HISTORY 137.description: Analyzes diverse social and cultural responses to epidemics from mid-nineteenth century to the present, including incarceration, caregiving, and disability rights. Using interdisciplinary materials and collaborative activities, students interpret strategies and outcomes of Indigenous, racialized, and marginalized communities surviving great illness.
HISTORY 137.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

HISTORY 140.title: Topics in U.S. History
HISTORY 140.description: Studies in selected areas of U.S. history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 142A.title: California Dreaming: Conquest, Conflict, and Globalization in the Golden State
HISTORY 142A.description: California as a case study of national trends and as a unique setting: its specific problems and culture. Major themes include: colonization, immigration, race relations, agricultural development, industrialization, urbanization, working class movements, social conflict, and political reform.

HISTORY 142B.title: Topics in American Social and Economic History
HISTORY 142B.description: Studies in selected areas of American social and economic history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 144G.title: Topics in American Cultural and Intellectual History
HISTORY 144G.description: Studies in selected areas of American cultural and intellectual history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 147.title: Education and the American Dream: Historical Perspectives on Democracy and Education
HISTORY 147.description: Examines the relationship between public schooling and the promotion of democratic ideals in American society over the past two centuries.

HISTORY 148B.title: Topics in Multicultural U.S. History
HISTORY 148B.description: Examines the variety of cultural expressions through which the people who came to inhabit the United States historically signify their collective identities.

HISTORY 150.title: Topics in African American History
HISTORY 150.description: Studies in selected areas of African American history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 151B.title: Chicana/Chicano History: Twentieth Century
HISTORY 151B.description: Examines social history of the Southwest with emphasis on Mexican-origin people. Discusses major questions, theory and research methods pertinent to Chicana/Chicano history. Themes explored include: immigration, xenophobia, class struggle, leadership, generational cohorts, unionization, education, barrioization, ethnicity, patriarchy, sexuality.

HISTORY 151C.title: Latinas in the Twentieth Century U.S
HISTORY 151C.description: Latinas in the U.S. from 1900 to present, offering a diversity of their cultures, regional histories, sexualities, generations, and classes.

HISTORY 151D.title: Latina/Latino Pop: Latina/Latino Popular Culture
HISTORY 151D.description: With a focus on the politics of language and space/place, prepares students to critically analyze sites of Latina/Latino popular culture including: music, film, performance, sports, media, and varied subcultures.
HISTORY 151D.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies majors and History majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

HISTORY 152.title: Topics in Asian-American History
HISTORY 152.description: Introduction to important themes in the history of people of Asian ancestry in the United States from the nineteenth century to the present.

HISTORY 152A.title: Asian American Labor
HISTORY 152A.description: Explores history of Asian Americans and work from the nineteenth century to the present. Areas of study include migration, colonialism, family, social organization, and work culture.

HISTORY 154.title: American Urban History
HISTORY 154.description: A study of urban communities in the United States, from colonial times to the present. Traces the impact of industrialization and urbanization on social and cultural life, and investigates the significance of urban life for U.S. democratic culture.

HISTORY 160.title: Sex and Conquest in Latin America
HISTORY 160.description: Competing ideas of masculinity and femininity, sexual violence, sexual identities, and gendered hierarchies informed how the Spanish engaged in military and religious domination of Mexican and Andean communities, as well as the forms of native resistance throughout colonial Latin America.

HISTORY 163.title: World of Coffee
HISTORY 163.description: History of consumption and production of coffee over the centuries, and coffee's cultural, economic, social, political consequences. Coffee's social life as a drug, symbol of hospitality, religious rite, sociability and bourgeois lifestyle, commodity, source of livelihoods, imperial revenues, corporate profits.

HISTORY 164A.title: Caribbean History: Colonization to Emancipation
HISTORY 164A.description: Exploration of the history of the archipelago from pre-Columbian times to the end of slavery; examining the impact of European colonization, decimation of the indigenous populations, African slavery, resistance, and emancipation; the unity and diversity of experience in region.

HISTORY 164B.title: Caribbean History: Emancipation to Independence
HISTORY 164B.description: Post-emancipation and anti-colonial struggles ending with political independence for most of the region. Examines social, political, economic, cultural dimensions of post-emancipation period, including large-scale migration to Central America, the U.S., and Britain; the region's global cultural and political contribution.

HISTORY 165A.title: Revolution and Memory in Latin America
HISTORY 165A.description: Comparison of how Andeans resurrected the leaders of the Inca, a defeated indigenous empire, to contest the Spanish empire with how enslaved Africans, with their descendants and others, defeated Spanish colonial rule in what would become the Cuban nation.

HISTORY 166.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
HISTORY 166.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

HISTORY 166B.title: Revolution and Reaction in Cold War Latin America
HISTORY 166B.description: Explores Latin American experiences of revolutionary change and military dictatorship during the Cold War (1945-1990). Pays particular attention to the lives of women, peasants, workers, and the urban middle classes. Case studies include Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, Argentina, Nicaragua, and Mexico.

HISTORY 166C.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
HISTORY 166C.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

HISTORY 166D.title: Revolution in Latin America
HISTORY 166D.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada. Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

HISTORY 169.title: Topics in Latin American History
HISTORY 169.description: Studies in selected areas of Latin American history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 170A.title: Ancient India
HISTORY 170A.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan. Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

HISTORY 170B.title: Medieval India
HISTORY 170B.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

HISTORY 171D.title: Chinese History to 1800
HISTORY 171D.description: A survey of the history of China to 1800.

HISTORY 171E.title: Chinese History: 1800-1949
HISTORY 171E.description: An examination of Chinese society and thought from the late-eighteenth century to the 1949 revolution. Focuses on the role of intellectuals; popular culture; women in Chinese society; developments in commerce and urban life; rebellion; foreign imperialism.

HISTORY 171G.title: Topics in the History of China
HISTORY 171G.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of China.

HISTORY 172G.title: Topics in the History of Japan
HISTORY 172G.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual and religious history of Japan.

HISTORY 173G.title: Topics in the History of Korea
HISTORY 173G.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of Korea.

HISTORY 174G.title: Topics in the History of South Asia
HISTORY 174G.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of South Asia.

HISTORY 175G.title: Topics in the History of Southeast Asia
HISTORY 175G.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of Southeast Asia.

HISTORY 178.title: The Viet Nam War Seen Through Oral History
HISTORY 178.description: Offers an overview of the Viet Nam War; explores the art of doing oral history and the use of oral testimony in research and writing the history of war through conducting oral history interviews with individuals of the war generation.

HISTORY 180.title: Special Studies in Social History
HISTORY 180.description: Studies in selected areas of social history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 182.title: Special Studies in Intellectual-Cultural History
HISTORY 182.description: Studies in selected areas of intellectual-cultural history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 183.title: Special Studies in International History
HISTORY 183.description: Studies in selected areas of international history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 184.title: Special Studies in Comparative History
HISTORY 184.description: Studies in selected areas of comparative history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

HISTORY 190.title: Colloquium
HISTORY 190.description: Specialized courses dealing primarily with close reading and analysis of primary and secondary works; required reports and papers. Each colloquium reflects the instructor's intellectual interests and is conducted as a discussion group. Limited to 18 students.
HISTORY 190.restriction: History majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

HISTORY 193.title: Advanced Research Seminar I
HISTORY 193.description: The first course in a two-quarter advanced research sequence, this course allows upper-division history majors to undertake significant research and writing under close faculty supervision.
HISTORY 193.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

HISTORY 194.title: Advanced Research Seminar II
HISTORY 194.description: Second course in a two-quarter advanced research sequence. Allows upper division history majors to undertake significant research and writing under close faculty supervision.
HISTORY 194.prereq_text: HISTORY 193. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

HISTORY 197.title: Internships in Public History
HISTORY 197.description: Students will sharpen their abilities to research, critically interpret, and present history by “doing history” beyond the formal classroom. Internships, which introduce students to the field of “public history,” include working as archivists, oral historians, project advisers, and exhibit curators.

HISTORY 199.title: Independent Reading
HISTORY 199.description: Investigation of special topics through directed reading. Paper required.

HISTORY 200.title: History and Theory
HISTORY 200.description: Explores a variety of theoretical issues and methodological concerns that have sparked lively debate in the humanities and social sciences in past decades and which remain of urgent concern to 21st-century historical writing.

HISTORY 202A.title: First-Year Research Seminar
HISTORY 202A.description: Introduction to historical methodologies and preparation for the first-year research paper. Required of all first-year doctoral students and M.A. students.

HISTORY 202B.title: First-Year Research Seminar
HISTORY 202B.description: Research and writing of a paper demonstrating command of historical methods explored in HISTORY 202A. Required of all first-year Ph.D. students and M.A. students.
HISTORY 202B.prereq_text: HISTORY 202A with a minimum grade of B-.

HISTORY 204A.title: Second-Year Research Seminar
HISTORY 204A.description: Part one of a two-quarter sequence required of all Ph.D. students during the second year of the program; not required for M.A. students. Includes primary research and writing a research paper, often related to a future dissertation topic.

HISTORY 204B.title: Second-Year Research Seminar
HISTORY 204B.description: Part two of a two-quarter sequence required of all Ph.D. students. Taken during the second year of the Ph.D. program; not required for M.A. students. Includes primary research and writing a research paper, often related to a future dissertation topic.
HISTORY 204B.prereq_text: HISTORY 204A with a minimum grade of B-.

HISTORY 205.title: Approaches to History
HISTORY 205.description: Introduces graduate students to some of the most foundational ideas and debates that have shaped historiographical practice over the past half-century.

HISTORY 210A.title: History in the Professions: An Introduction to Doing History in Graduate School and Beyond
HISTORY 210A.description: Centers conversations and topics that illuminate the hidden curriculum of graduate school, explore the political economy of labor in the university, and provide students a foundational introduction to the historical profession.

HISTORY 210B.title: History in the Professions: An Introduction to Doing History in Graduate School and Beyond
HISTORY 210B.description: Centers conversations and topics that illuminate the hidden curriculum of graduate school, explore the political economy of labor in the university, and provide students a foundational introduction to the historical profession.

HISTORY 210C.title: History in the Professions: An Introduction to Doing History in Graduate School and Beyond
HISTORY 210C.description: Centers conversations and topics that illuminate the hidden curriculum of graduate school, explore the political economy of labor in the university, and provide students a foundational introduction to the historical profession.

HISTORY 230.title: Topics in European History
HISTORY 230.description: Studies in selected themes and time periods in European history. Topics and period vary.

HISTORY 240.title: Topics in World History
HISTORY 240.description: Studies in selected themes and time periods in world history. Topics and period vary.

HISTORY 250.title: Topics in Latin American History
HISTORY 250.description: Studies in selected themes and time periods in Latin American history. Topics and period vary.

HISTORY 260.title: Topics in American History
HISTORY 260.description: Studies in selected themes and time periods in U.S. history. Topics and period vary.

HISTORY 270.title: Topics in Middle Eastern History
HISTORY 270.description: Studies in selected themes and time periods in Middle Eastern history. Topics and period vary.

HISTORY 280.title: Topics in Asian History
HISTORY 280.description: Studies in selected themes and time periods in Asian history. Topics and period vary.

HISTORY 290.title: Special Topics
HISTORY 290.description: Lectures, readings, and discussion on subjects more limited in scope than those included in the year-long colloquium series.

HISTORY 291.title: Directed Reading
HISTORY 291.description: Reading courses focused on specialized topics.

HISTORY 297.title: History Internship
HISTORY 297.description: Limited to History graduate students with Department-approved internships.

HISTORY 298.title: Experimental Group Study
HISTORY 298.description: Open to four or more students.

HISTORY 299.title: Dissertation Research
HISTORY 299.description: Specifically designed for students researching and writing their dissertations.

HUMAN 1A.title: Humanities Core Lecture
HUMAN 1A.description: Through a range of cultural traditions and an interdisciplinary approach to works of literature, history, philosophy, and contemporary media, students are introduced to the humanities.
HUMAN 1A.prereq_text: ( ENTRY LEVEL WRITING OR ( PLACEMENT EXAM OR AUTHORIZATION (see SOC comments for authorization policy/instructions) ) ) AND LOWER DIVISION STANDING ONLY

HUMAN 1AES.title: Humanities Core Writing: Entry Level Writing
HUMAN 1AES.description: A small writing course for Entry Level Writing students exploring the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.
HUMAN 1AES.prereq_text: HUMAN 1A ( coreq ) AND LOWER DIVISION STANDING ONLY

HUMAN 1AS.title: Humanities Core Writing
HUMAN 1AS.description: A small writing course in which students explore the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.
HUMAN 1AS.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

HUMAN 1B.title: Humanities Core Lecture
HUMAN 1B.description: Through a range of cultural traditions and an interdisciplinary approach to works of literature, history, philosophy, and contemporary media, students are introduced to the humanities.

HUMAN 1BES.title: Humanities Core Writing: Entry Level Writing
HUMAN 1BES.description: A small writing course for Entry Level Writing students exploring the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.

HUMAN 1BS.title: Humanities Core Writing
HUMAN 1BS.description: A small writing course in which students explore the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.
HUMAN 1BS.prereq_text: HUMAN 1AS or HUMAN H1AS or HUMAN 1AES with a minimum grade of C. Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

HUMAN 1C.title: Humanities Core Lecture
HUMAN 1C.description: Through a range of cultural traditions and an interdisciplinary approach to works of literature, history, philosophy, and contemporary media, students are introduced to the humanities.

HUMAN 1CS.title: Humanities Core Writing
HUMAN 1CS.description: A small writing course in which students explore the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.
HUMAN 1CS.prereq_text: HUMAN 1AS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN H1AS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN 1BS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN H1BS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN 1BES with a minimum grade of C.

HUMAN H1AES.title: Humanities Core Writing: Honors Entry Level Writing
HUMAN H1AES.description: Entry Level Writing for Campuswide Honors students exploring the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.

HUMAN H1AS.title: Humanities Core Writing: Honors
