HUMAN H1AS.description: For Campuswide Honors students exploring the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.
HUMAN H1AS.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

HUMAN H1BS.title: Humanities Core Writing: Honors
HUMAN H1BS.description: For Campuswide Honors students exploring the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.
HUMAN H1BS.prereq_text: HUMAN 1AS or HUMAN H1AS or HUMAN 1AES with a minimum grade of C. Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

HUMAN H1CS.title: Humanities Core Writing: Honors
HUMAN H1CS.description: For Campuswide Honors students exploring the ideas presented in the companion lecture course and illustrated in the literary, historical, philosophical, and media works assigned.
HUMAN H1CS.prereq_text: HUMAN 1AS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN H1AS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN 1BS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN H1BS with a minimum grade of C- or HUMAN 1BES with a minimum grade of C.

HUMAN 10.title: Masterpieces of Literature
HUMAN 10.description: Students closely read major works of world literature that are significant (1) in their own right, (2) for a specific literary tradition, and (3) because of their reception in other cultural contexts. Literature written in English and English translation.

HUMAN 52.title: Foundations of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism
HUMAN 52.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of current issues in bilingual education and bilingualism. Topics include dimensions of bilingualism, the effects of bilingualism on children's linguistic and cognitive development, bilingual education programs, literacy, special needs, and assessment.

HUMAN H80.title: Exploring Memory
HUMAN H80.description: Questions about human memory are central to a wide range of disciplines. Students will explore how historians, sociologists, social psychologists, legal experts, and neuroscientists understand human memory and apply their findings to understand and shape their own societies.

HUMAN H81.title: The Vietnam War
HUMAN H81.description: Examines the origins, evolution, opposition against, conclusion, and legacy of the United States in the Vietnam War.

HUMAN H84.title: Traveling East/West
HUMAN H84.description: Traveling East/West presents a wide range of travel writings by Chinese, Indian, and Euro-American authors in which they contemplate the complexities of cross-cultural encounters and how knowledge about others and knowledge of ourselves are closely intertwined.

HUMAN 95.title: Professional Development
HUMAN 95.description: Introduces Humanities undergraduates to various field study and experiential learning opportunities in Humanities and at UCI. Includes internship and research exploration and preparation activities designed to equip students with the skills necessary for career readiness and professional development.

HUMAN H120.title: Honors Proseminar
HUMAN H120.description: Interdisciplinary Honors seminar organized each year around a single topic problem designed to compare and contrast modes of analysis in history, literary studies, and philosophy.
HUMAN H120.restriction: School of Humanities Honors students only.

HUMAN H140.title: Senior Honors Seminar
HUMAN H140.description: Directed by Humanities Honors Thesis Advisor and required of students in Humanities Honors program and Humanities majors in Campuswide Honors Program. Designed to facilitate exchange of ideas and research strategies among students and begin process of writing senior honors thesis.
HUMAN H140.restriction: Seniors only. School of Humanities Honors students only.

HUMAN H141.title: Senior Honors Thesis
HUMAN H141.description: Directed independent research required of participants in the Humanities Honors Program and Humanities majors in the Campuswide Honors Program.

HUMAN H142W.title: Senior Honors Colloquium
HUMAN H142W.description: Completion, presentation, and discussion of Senior Honors Theses.
HUMAN H142W.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium only. School of Humanities Honors students only.

HUMAN 176.title: Personal and Social Resilience in the Age of the Climate Crisis
HUMAN 176.description: In our rapidly changing world, many climate and other interrelated global crises are undermining human well-being. Students gain invaluable personal and social resilience skills (e.g., mindfulness), and implement collaborative high impact projects to navigate and build a meaningful future.

HUMAN 192A.title: Humanities Peer Mentee Seminar
HUMAN 192A.description: Seminar for first-year Humanities undergraduates admitted to the Peer Mentor Program to gain familiarity with campus resources, reflect on their educational goals and first-year experience, and explore the curriculum of a research university in a community-based setting.
HUMAN 192A.restriction: Freshmen and School of Humanities students only.

HUMAN 192B.title: Humanities Peer Mentor Seminar
HUMAN 192B.description: Mentor course for the Humanities Peer Mentor Program. Seminar for advanced Humanities majors to plan activities and lead discussion groups on mentoring, student development, and issues relevant to first-year Humanities majors.

HUMAN 195.title: Humanities Out There (H.O.T.) Practicum
HUMAN 195.description: H.O.T. sponsors tutoring opportunities in local schools and after-school sites for UCI students. Requirements include weekly one-hour training sessions at UCI; at least eight off-site tutoring sessions; and short writing assignments.

HUMAN 197.title: Topics in Humanities First-Generation Seminar
HUMAN 197.description: Special topics related to the support of first-generation undergraduates pursing a Humanities degree.
HUMAN 197.restriction: School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

HUMAN 198.title: Directed Group Study
HUMAN 198.description: Faculty-led studies on special topics in the Humanities.

HUMAN 260A.title: Critical Theory Workshop
HUMAN 260A.description: A year-long Critical Theory Workshop, conducted by a team of instructors, conceived as a reading group, and developed with the input of all participants, where significant texts are discussed and analyzed in class.

HUMAN 260B.title: Critical Theory Workshop
HUMAN 260B.description: A year-long Critical Theory Workshop, conducted by a team of instructors, conceived as a reading group, and developed with the input of all participants, where significant texts are discussed and analyzed in class.

HUMAN 260C.title: Critical Theory Workshop
HUMAN 260C.description: A year-long Critical Theory Workshop, conducted by a team of instructors, conceived as a reading group, and developed with the input of all participants, where significant texts are discussed and analyzed in class.

HUMAN 261.title: Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
HUMAN 261.description: A required writing-intensive seminar conducted by an instructor affiliated with the Race and Justice Studies emphasis. Students with manuscripts on relevant topics will read and critique peer manuscripts, and revise manuscripts toward completion of articles, dissertation chapters, and other publications.
HUMAN 261.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C260C with a minimum grade of B-.

HUMAN 264.title: Latin American Studies
HUMAN 264.description: Students discuss significant texts on Latin America from a range of disciplines in the humanities, social sciences, and the arts.

HUMAN 270.title: Advanced Critical Theory
HUMAN 270.description: Seminars on various topics in critical theory.
HUMAN 270.prereq_text: Students should have taken introductory courses before enrolling in these seminars.

HUMAN 298.title: Humanities Out There (H.O.T.) Practicum
HUMAN 298.description: Individual study with H.O.T. faculty supervisor.

HUMAN 398A.title: Foreign Language Teaching: Approaches and Methods
HUMAN 398A.description: Introduces approaches and methods of foreign language learning and teaching, and the theoretical models of second-language acquisition and teaching. Focus areas include lesson planning, teaching vocabulary, grammar, speaking, reading, writing, listening, culture, task-based teaching, uses of digital media.

HUMAN 398B.title: Foreign Language Teaching: Approaches and Methods
HUMAN 398B.description: Introduces approaches and methods of foreign language learning and teaching, and the theoretical models of second-language acquisition and teaching. Focus areas include lesson planning, teaching vocabulary, grammar, speaking, reading, writing, listening, culture, task-based teaching, uses of digital media.

HUMAN 399.title: University Teaching
HUMAN 399.description: Limited to Teaching Associates in Humanities Core course.

I&C SCI 3.title: Computing Technologies and Their Social Impact
I&C SCI 3.description: Examines current computing technologies and social implications at the individual, group, and societal level. Issues include privacy, trust, identity, reputation, governance, and malicious behavior, ethics, social justice, and culture and community.
I&C SCI 3.restriction: I&C SCI 3 may not be taken for credit after IN4MATX 161.

I&C SCI 4.title: Designing Computing Technology for People
I&C SCI 4.description: Introduces students to basic principles of human-centered computing and theories of human behavior that are relevant for the design of technology for people. Specific topics include usability, prototyping, heuristic evaluation, visual design, theory of perception, accessibility.
I&C SCI 4.restriction: I&C SCI 4 may not be taken for credit after IN4MATX 131.

I&C SCI 5.title: Global Disruption and Information Technology
I&C SCI 5.description: Explores how new forms of information technology may support transition to a sustainable civilization. Topics include design and implementation of IT systems, science of global change, online community building, and “green IT”. Activities involve reading, writing, discussion, and final project.

I&C SCI 6B.title: Boolean Logic and Discrete Structures
I&C SCI 6B.description: Relations and their properties; Boolean algebras, formal languages; finite automata.
I&C SCI 6B.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 6D.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
I&C SCI 6D.description: Covers essential tools from discrete mathematics used in computer science with an emphasis on the process of abstracting computational problems and analyzing them mathematically. Topics include mathematical induction, combinatorics, and recurrence relations.
I&C SCI 6D.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering majors have second consideration.

I&C SCI 6N.title: Computational Linear Algebra
I&C SCI 6N.description: Matrices and linear transformations, systems of linear equations, determinants, linear vector spaces, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, orthogonal matrices, diagonalization, and least squares. Topics taught primarily from an algorithmic perspective, including computational solutions, applications, and numerical error analysis.
I&C SCI 6N.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI H32 or AP Computer Science A with a minimum score of 3) and (MATH 2B or MATH 5B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4).
I&C SCI 6N.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 9.title: Introduction to Computation for Scientists and Engineers
I&C SCI 9.description: Introduces principles, techniques, and computational tools for quantitative approach to basic problem solving in physics and engineering. Project-based course that actively explores how programming techniques are used for solving STEM real-world problems.
I&C SCI 9.prereq_text: MATH 2A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 3.

I&C SCI 10.title: How Computers Work
I&C SCI 10.description: Introduction to digital computer and communication systems. Capabilities and limitations of information technology. Representing information in digital form. Overview of computer organization, internet, operating systems, software. Human-computer interaction and social impact.
I&C SCI 10.prereq_text: NO I&C SCI 105 AND NO IN4MATX 43 AND NO I&C SCI 51 AND NO I&C SCI 31 AND NO I&C SCI 32 AND NO I&C SCI H32

I&C SCI 11.title: The Internet and Public Policy
I&C SCI 11.description: How the Internet works. Current public policy issues concerning the Internet. Introductory economics. Communications law. Interactions between information technology, economics, and law. Case studies about Internet and communications policy.

I&C SCI 12.title: Artificial Intelligence and Society
I&C SCI 12.description: Investigates AI technologies and their impacts at individual, group, and societal levels. Topics include digital inclusion, bias, employment, governance, ethics, privacy, and cultural implications, emphasizing equitable opportunities and responsible AI development.

I&C SCI 20.title: Invitation to Computing
I&C SCI 20.description: Foundational principles of computer science for students with no computing background that are interested in a related career. Big ideas of computing explored, including programming through use of sequential, conditional, iterative logic. Good computational practices, problem solving, and organization discussed.

I&C SCI 31.title: Introduction to Programming
I&C SCI 31.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts and techniques for writing software in a high-level programming language. Covers the syntax and semantics of data types, expressions, exceptions, control structures, input/output, methods, classes, and pragmatics of programming.
I&C SCI 31.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 32.title: Programming with Software Libraries
I&C SCI 32.description: Construction of programs for problems and computing environments more varied than in I&C SCI 31. Using library modules for applications such as graphics, sound, GUI, database, Web, and network programming. Language features beyond those in I&C SCI 31 are introduced as needed.
I&C SCI 32.prereq_text: I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C.
I&C SCI 32.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI H32.title: Python Programming and Libraries (Accelerated)
I&C SCI H32.description: Introduces Python syntax and semantics for fundamental programming concepts. Constructing programs for varied problems and environments. Using library modules for applications such as graphics, sound, GUI, database, Web, and network programming. Accelerated course for students with previous programming background.
I&C SCI H32.prereq_text: AP Computer Science A with a minimum score of 3. Placement via a transfer course in computer programming or equivalent experience may also be accepted upon review.
I&C SCI H32.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 33.title: Intermediate Programming
I&C SCI 33.description: Intermediate-level language features and programming concepts for larger, more complex, higher-quality software. Functional programming, name spaces, modules, class protocols, inheritance, iterators, generators, operator overloading, reflection. Analysis of time and space efficiency.
I&C SCI 33.prereq_text: I&C SCI 32 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI H32 with a minimum grade of C.
I&C SCI 33.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 45C.title: Programming in C/C++ as a Second Language
I&C SCI 45C.description: An introduction to the lexical, syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic characteristics of the C/C++ languages for experienced programmers. Emphasis on object-oriented programming, using standard libraries, and programming with manual garbage collection.
I&C SCI 45C.prereq_text: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C or EECS 40 with a minimum grade of C.
I&C SCI 45C.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 45J.title: Programming in Java as a Second Language
I&C SCI 45J.description: An introduction to the lexical, syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic characteristics of the Java language for experienced programmers. Emphasis on object-oriented programming, using standard libraries, and programming with automatic garbage collection.
I&C SCI 45J.prereq_text: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C.
I&C SCI 45J.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 46.title: Data Structure Implementation and Analysis
I&C SCI 46.description: Focuses on implementation and mathematical analysis of fundamental data structures and algorithms. Covers storage allocation and memory management techniques.
I&C SCI 46.prereq_text: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C and I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C.
I&C SCI 46.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 51.title: Introductory Computer Organization
I&C SCI 51.description: Multilevel view, design, and operation of computer system components. Machine-level data and instruction representation. Instruction sets and addressing modes. Memory organization. Laboratory work using low-level programming languages.
I&C SCI 51.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 53.title: Principles in System Design
I&C SCI 53.description: Introduces basic principles of system software: operating systems, compilers, and networking. Exposure to the following topics through theoretical and practical programming experiences: linking and loading, process and memory management, concurrency and synchronization, network communication, programming for performance, etc.
I&C SCI 53.prereq_text: I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C and I&C SCI 51 with a minimum grade of C.
I&C SCI 53.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 60.title: Games and Society
I&C SCI 60.description: The study and critical analysis of computer games as art objects, cultural artifacts, gateways to virtual worlds, educational aids, and tools for persuasion and social change. Emphasis on understanding games in their historical and cultural context.
I&C SCI 60.restriction: Computer Game Science majors and Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.

I&C SCI 80.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
I&C SCI 80.description: Studies in selected areas of information and computer sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

I&C SCI 90.title: New Students Seminar
I&C SCI 90.description: Introduces students to the Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences. Focuses on advising students making the transition to UCI, community building, and mostly surveying the technical areas within departments in ICS, via talks by faculty on their research.
I&C SCI 90.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 139W.title: Critical Writing on Information Technology
I&C SCI 139W.description: Study and practice of critical writing and oral communication as it applies to information technology. Each student writes assignments of varying lengths, totaling at least 4,000 words.
I&C SCI 139W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
I&C SCI 139W.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 167.title: Multiplayer Game Systems
I&C SCI 167.description: Foundations and technologies that enable multiuser, networked, and persistent virtual environments. Emphasis on database design and management, network protocols, and concurrency control to accommodate large numbers of simultaneous users.
I&C SCI 167.restriction: Computer Game Science majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI 192.title: Industrial or Public Sector Field Study
I&C SCI 192.description: Students participate in an off-campus, supervised internship for a minimum of 60 hours. Students apply classroom knowledge through internship projects in the private sector or nonprofit agencies.
I&C SCI 192.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

I&C SCI H197.title: Honors Seminar
I&C SCI H197.description: An overview of computer science and selected recent trends in research. Students attend talks on current faculty research, with opportunities for discussion.
I&C SCI H197.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium only. School of Information and Computer Sciences Honors students only.

I&C SCI 398A.title: Teaching Assistant Training Seminar
I&C SCI 398A.description: Theories, methods, and resources for teaching computer science at the university level, particularly by teaching assistants. Classroom presentations, working with individuals, grading, motivating students. Participants will give and critique presentations and may be videotaped while teaching.

IN4MATX 80.title: Special Topics in Informatics
IN4MATX 80.description: Designed for informatics instructors to pilot new teaching materials and prototype new class. The format of the class is flexible based on the content to be offered in the future.
IN4MATX 80.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX H81.title: Ethics, Technology, and Design
IN4MATX H81.description: Provides a critical framework for how and why biases of many kinds are built into everyday digital tools. Reflections on ethics, technology, and design through case studies drawn from machine learning, CS education, engineering, social media, and criminal justice.

IN4MATX 131.title: Human Computer Interaction
IN4MATX 131.description: Basic principles of human-computer interaction (HCI). Introduces students to user interface design techniques, design guidelines, and usability testing. Students gain the ability to design and evaluate user interfaces and become familiar with some of the outstanding research problems in HCI.
IN4MATX 131.prereq_text: I&C SCI 10 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 32A with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI H32 with a minimum grade of C or GDIM 31 with a minimum grade of C or ENGR 10 with a minimum grade of C or ENGRMAE 10 with a minimum grade of C or EECS 10 with a minimum grade of C.
IN4MATX 131.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 132.title: Advanced Topics in Human-Computer Interaction
IN4MATX 132.description: Advanced material in the space of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) through application and practice. Introduces user research methods such as observation, interviewing, usability testing, design activities, and user analytics.
IN4MATX 132.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 133.title: User Interaction Software
IN4MATX 133.description: Introduction to human-computer interaction programming. Emphasis on current tools, standards, methodologies for implementing effective interaction designs. Widget toolkits, Web interface programming, geo-spatial and map interfaces, mobile phone interfaces.
IN4MATX 133.prereq_text: I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C.
IN4MATX 133.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 134.title: Advanced Topics in User Interface Software
IN4MATX 134.description: Advanced material in the space of human-computer interaction programming. Introduces core interface toolkit concepts including interface states, event handling, layout and positioning, and custom interactions. Materials Fee
IN4MATX 134.restriction: Informatics majors, Software Engineering majors, and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Information and Computer Sciences students only. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 143.title: Information Visualization
IN4MATX 143.description: Introduction to interactive visual interfaces for large datasets, and to principles of human visual perception and human computer interaction that inform their design. Various applications for data analysis and monitoring are discussed.
IN4MATX 143.prereq_text: (IN4MATX 131 with a minimum grade of C or SWE 43 with a minimum grade of C) and (I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI H32 with a minimum grade of C).
IN4MATX 143.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 148.title: Designing for the Internet of Things
IN4MATX 148.description: Introduction to design principles for Internet of Things applications. Prototyping, design, and evaluation of physical computing applications, smart environments, embedded systems, and future computing scenarios. Includes hands-on in-class laboratory exercises. Materials Fee
IN4MATX 148.prereq_text: I&C SCI 10 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI H32 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 32A with a minimum grade of C.
IN4MATX 148.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 151.title: Project Management
IN4MATX 151.description: Introduces theoretical and practical aspects of project management. Topics include organizational theory, group behavior, project management skills, case studies, personal and group productivity tools, management of distributed work, stakeholders, consultants, and knowledge management. Students do a project exercise.
IN4MATX 151.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 153.title: Design of Social and Interpersonal Technologies
IN4MATX 153.description: Considerations around the design of technologies beyond the individual. Topics may include social media, messaging and communication, feeds, algorithmic recommendations, privacy, and access.
IN4MATX 153.prereq_text: (IN4MATX 161 or SWE 43) and (I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI H32 with a minimum grade of C).
IN4MATX 153.restriction: Informatics majors, Software Engineering majors, and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

IN4MATX 161.title: Social Analysis of Computing
IN4MATX 161.description: Examines current computing technologies and their consequences at the individual, group, community, and societal level. Topics may include privacy, trust, identity, reputation, governance, ethics, social justice, and culture.
IN4MATX 161.prereq_text: I&C SCI 10 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 32A with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI H32 with a minimum grade of C or ENGR 10 with a minimum grade of C or EECS 10 with a minimum grade of C or ENGRMAE 10 with a minimum grade of C. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
IN4MATX 161.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 162.title: Information Systems in Organizations
IN4MATX 162.description: Introduction to role of information systems in organizations, components and structure of organizational information systems, and techniques used in information systems analysis, design, and implementation.
IN4MATX 162.prereq_text: I&C SCI 10 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 31 with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI H32 with a minimum grade of C or GDIM 31 with a minimum grade of C.
IN4MATX 162.restriction: Informatics majors and Software Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

IN4MATX 163.title: Project in Organization Analysis of Information Systems
IN4MATX 163.description: Students undertake a project in analyzing the use of information systems in organizations. Introduces research methods such as observation, interviewing, and document analysis. Students gain experience with techniques including jotting, writing field notes, qualitative coding, and memoing.
IN4MATX 163.restriction: Informatics majors, Software Engineering majors, and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

IN4MATX 164.title: Children's Learning and Media
IN4MATX 164.description: Examines how popular media may impact how young people learn, develop, and communicate by looking at research related to the impacts of a wide range of popular media including television, video games, digital environments, mobile devices, and other multimedia.
IN4MATX 164.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
IN4MATX 164.restriction: Education Sciences majors, Informatics majors, and Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

IN4MATX 171.title: Introduction to Health Informatics
IN4MATX 171.description: Broad overview of medical informatics for students with varied backgrounds. Electronic medical records, online resources, mobile technologies, patient safety, and computational design. Legal, ethical, and public policy issues. Health systems management. Evaluation and fieldwork for health systems.
IN4MATX 171.prereq_text: WRITING 60 with a minimum grade of C or WRITING 30 with a minimum grade of C or WRITING 31 with a minimum grade of C or HUMAN 1C with a minimum grade of C or HUMAN H1C with a minimum grade of C.
IN4MATX 171.restriction: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

IN4MATX 172.title: Project in Health Informatics
IN4MATX 172.description: Students undertake significant quarter-long projects related to health informatics. Topics may include field evaluations of health care technologies, prototypes, iterative design, and system implementations.

IN4MATX 173.title: Consumer Health Informatics
IN4MATX 173.description: Consumer health informatics is a subfield of health informatics aimed to empower healthcare consumers through a variety of consumer-facing technologies. Covers health behavior change, health literacy, social support, and the design, evaluation, and implementation of major technological applications.
IN4MATX 173.prereq_text: IN4MATX 171 with a minimum grade of C or PUBHLTH 105 with a minimum grade of C.
IN4MATX 173.restriction: Public Health majors, Health Informatics minors, and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 174.title: Health Data Analytics
IN4MATX 174.description: The increasing availability of electronic heath data provides an unprecedented opportunity to use data-driven approaches to improve human health. Equips students with essential skills in curating, managing, and analyzing health data, focusing on electronic health records.
IN4MATX 174.prereq_text: IN4MATX 171 with a minimum grade of C or PUBHLTH 105 with a minimum grade of C.
IN4MATX 174.restriction: Public Health majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 190.title: Special Topics in Informatics
IN4MATX 190.description: Studies in selected areas of informatics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

IN4MATX 191A.title: Senior Design Project
IN4MATX 191A.description: Group supervised project in which students analyze, specify, design, construct, evaluate, and adapt a significant information processing system. Topics include team management, professional ethics, and systems analysis.
IN4MATX 191A.prereq_text: SWE 113 and SWE 121 and IN4MATX 131 and IN4MATX 151.
IN4MATX 191A.restriction: Seniors, Software Engineering majors, and Informatics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

IN4MATX 191B.title: Senior Design Project
IN4MATX 191B.description: Group supervised project in which students analyze, specify, design, construct, evaluate, and adapt a significant information processing system. Topics include team management, professional ethics, and systems analysis.
IN4MATX 191B.prereq_text: IN4MATX 191A. In Progress (IP) grade for IN4MATX 191A is also accepted.

IN4MATX H198.title: Honors Research
IN4MATX H198.description: Directed independent research in Informatics for honors students.
IN4MATX H198.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
IN4MATX H198.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium only. School of Information and Computer Sciences Honors students only.

IN4MATX 199.title: Individual Study
IN4MATX 199.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

IN4MATX 201.title: Research Methodology for Informatics
IN4MATX 201.description: Introduction to strategies and idioms of research in Informatics. Includes examination of issues in scientific inquiry, qualitative and quantitative methods, and research design. Both classic texts and contemporary research literature are read and analyzed.

IN4MATX 203.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Information Systems
IN4MATX 203.description: Introduction to qualitative research methods used to study computerization and information systems, such as open-ended interviewing, participant observation, and ethnography. Studies of the methods in practice through examination of research literature.
IN4MATX 203.prereq_text: IN4MATX 261 with a minimum grade of B- or IN4MATX 251 with a minimum grade of B-.

IN4MATX 205.title: Quantitative Research Methods in Information Systems
IN4MATX 205.description: Quantitative research methods used to study computerization and information systems. Design of instruments, sampling, sample sizes, and data analysis. Validity and reliability. Longitudinal versus cross-sectional designs. Analysis of secondary data. Studies of the methods through examination of research literature.
IN4MATX 205.prereq_text: IN4MATX 251 with a minimum grade of B- or IN4MATX 261 with a minimum grade of B-. Basic knowledge of elementary statistics is also required.

IN4MATX 207S.title: Doctoral Seminar on Research and Writing
IN4MATX 207S.description: Doctoral seminar centered on original research and writing. Provides a chance for doctoral students at all levels to present original work, brainstorm ongoing issues, and learn to provide and receive critical feedback from peers.

IN4MATX 209S.title: Seminar in Informatics
IN4MATX 209S.description: Current research and research trends in informatics. Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress.

IN4MATX 231.title: User Interface Design and Evaluation
IN4MATX 231.description: Introduction to the design and evaluation of user interfaces, with an emphasis on methodology. Cognitive principles, design life cycle, on-line and off-line prototyping techniques. Toolkits and architectures for interactive systems. Evaluation techniques, including heuristic and laboratory methods.

IN4MATX 232.title: Research in Human-Centered Computing
IN4MATX 232.description: Introduction to contemporary topics in human-computer interaction, including methods, technologies, design, and evaluation. Emerging application domains and their challenges to traditional research methods. Advanced architectures and technologies. Critical issues.

IN4MATX 241.title: Introduction to Ubiquitous Computing
IN4MATX 241.description: The "disappearing computer" paradigm. Differences to the desktop computing model: applications, interaction in augmented environments, security, alternate media, small operating systems, sensors, and embedded systems design. Evaluation by project work and class participation.

IN4MATX 244.title: Introduction to Embedded and Ubiquitous Systems
IN4MATX 244.description: Embedded and ubiquitous system technologies including processors, DSP, memory, and software. System interfacing basics; communication strategies; sensors and actuators, mobile and wireless technology. Using pre-designed hardware and software components. Design case studies in wireless, multimedia, and/or networking domains.
IN4MATX 244.prereq_text: I&C SCI 51 and COMPSCI 152 and COMPSCI 161 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G or I&C SCI 6D). B.S. degree in Computer Science is also accepted.

IN4MATX 251.title: Computer-Supported Cooperative Work
IN4MATX 251.description: The role of information systems in supporting work in groups and organizations. Examines various technologies designed to support communication, information sharing, and coordination. Focuses on behavioral and social aspects of designing and using group support technologies.

IN4MATX 261.title: Social Analysis of Computing
IN4MATX 261.description: The social and economic impacts of computing and information technologies on groups, organizations, and society. Topics include computerization and changes in the character of work, social control and privacy, electronic communities, and risks of safety-critical systems to people.

IN4MATX 263.title: Computerization, Work, and Organizations
IN4MATX 263.description: Selected topics in the influence of computerization and information systems in transforming work and organizations. Theories of organization and organizational change. Processes by which diverse information technologies influence changes in work and organizations over short and long time periods.
IN4MATX 263.prereq_text: IN4MATX 251 with a minimum grade of B- or IN4MATX 261 with a minimum grade of B-.

IN4MATX 265.title: Theories of Information Society
IN4MATX 265.description: Social and economic conceptions of information technology. Macrosocial and economic conditions that foster changes in information technologies. Social construction of information and computer technology in professional worlds. Theories of information technology and large-scale social change.
IN4MATX 265.prereq_text: IN4MATX 251 with a minimum grade of B- or IN4MATX 261 with a minimum grade of B-.

IN4MATX 267.title: Digital Media and Society
IN4MATX 267.description: Selected topics in the technological and social aspects of online interactions, and policy including online games, social media, electronic activism, e-commerce, and digital libraries. Media-theoretic approaches to digital technology. Architectures, infrastructure considerations, and their consequences.

IN4MATX 273.title: Information Technology in Global Sustainability
IN4MATX 273.description: Explores the relationship between recent developments in information technology and the global transition to sustainability. Topics include the role of IT systems in the provision of human needs and wants (e.g., smart grids, food systems, and other IT-enabled infrastructure).

IN4MATX 280.title: Overview of Human-Computer Interaction and Design
IN4MATX 280.description: Introduction to human-computer interaction and user-centered design. The material is focused on laying the groundwork for understanding the history, importance, and methods of human-computer interaction and design.
IN4MATX 280.restriction: Master of Human Computer Interaction and Design only.

IN4MATX 281.title: User Needs Analysis
IN4MATX 281.description: Understanding the user's context, needs, and preferences. Topics include interviews and observations, modeling the context, flow, culture, space, and artifacts involved in an endeavor, ways of aggregating what is found, and presenting these findings to others.
IN4MATX 281.prereq_text: IN4MATX 280 with a minimum grade of B-.
IN4MATX 281.restriction: Master of Human Computer Interaction and Design only.

IN4MATX 282.title: Design and Prototyping
IN4MATX 282.description: Introduction to user-centered design and prototyping. Focused on practical methods for interaction design. Topics include the nature of design and the challenges to creating and evaluating good designs, as well specific skills for designing interactive systems.
IN4MATX 282.prereq_text: IN4MATX 280 with a minimum grade of B-.

IN4MATX 283.title: User Experience Evaluation
IN4MATX 283.description: Evaluating prototypes and completed systems. Topics include comparative analysis, laboratory experiments, heuristic evaluation, cognitive walkthroughs, surveys, clickstreams, and help-desk.
IN4MATX 283.prereq_text: IN4MATX 280 with a minimum grade of B-.
IN4MATX 283.restriction: Master of Human Computer Interaction and Design only.

IN4MATX 284.title: Advanced Design and Prototyping
IN4MATX 284.description: Develop and communicate interactive technology design prototypes. Moving concepts from brainstorming and paper prototypes to wireframe and limited functionality mock-ups.
IN4MATX 284.prereq_text: IN4MATX 282 with a minimum grade of B-.
IN4MATX 284.restriction: Master of Human Computer Interaction and Design only.

IN4MATX 285.title: Interactive Technology Studio
IN4MATX 285.description: Technologies and skills required for creating interactive technology prototypes and collaborating with experts in that practice. Covers principles and practices around web and mobile development, compatibility, software libraries, and architectures.
IN4MATX 285.prereq_text: IN4MATX 280 with a minimum grade of B-.
IN4MATX 285.restriction: Master of Human Computer Interaction and Design only.

IN4MATX 286.title: Innovations in HCI and Design
IN4MATX 286.description: Recent social and technological developments in human-computer interaction and design. Topics will vary as the field progresses but include novel input techniques, novel platforms, and innovations in theory and methods of design.
IN4MATX 286.prereq_text: IN4MATX 280 with a minimum grade of B-.

IN4MATX 287.title: Capstone Project in HCI and Design
IN4MATX 287.description: Group project that reinforces all concepts learned in this program, including knowing where user experience work is most appropriate and essential, and executing the appropriate steps.
IN4MATX 287.prereq_text: IN4MATX 283 with a minimum grade of B- and IN4MATX 284 with a minimum grade of B-.
IN4MATX 287.restriction: Human Computer Interaction and Design majors only.

IN4MATX 288.title: Capstone Project and Portfolio
IN4MATX 288.description: Completion of capstone projects and development of portfolios. Ideation, critique, development, and critique.
IN4MATX 288.prereq_text: IN4MATX 287 with a minimum grade of B-.

IN4MATX 289.title: Special Topics in Applying Human-Computer Interaction and Design in Industry
IN4MATX 289.description: Selected topics related to understanding and applying human-computer interaction and design concepts and practices within the User Experience industry. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
IN4MATX 289.restriction: Human Computer Interaction and Design majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

IN4MATX 290.title: Research Seminar
IN4MATX 290.description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.

IN4MATX 295.title: Special Topics in Informatics
IN4MATX 295.description: Studies in selected areas of informatics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

IN4MATX 298.title: Thesis Supervision
IN4MATX 298.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.

IN4MATX 299.title: Individual Study
IN4MATX 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

INNO 202.title: Leading People and Projects
INNO 202.description: Assists experienced and inexperienced entrepreneurs with some of the challenges of managing others, and helps them build their understanding and skills so they can become more successful managers of people.

INNO 203.title: Accounting for Entrepreneurs
INNO 203.description: Provides the building blocks of financial and managerial accounting that are essential to entrepreneurs. Covers financial ratios and statements, including forecasting financial statements, basic transaction analysis, and generally accepted accounting principles.

INNO 205.title: Marketing for Entrepreneurs
INNO 205.description: Develops familiarity with fundamental concepts, theories, and techniques in marketing, and acquaints students with the type of decisions made by marketing managers including customer targeting, product, pricing, placement, promotion, and research.

INNO 209.title: Managerial Finance and Venture Capital
INNO 209.description: Provides the building blocks of finance knowledge that are essential to entrepreneurs. Covers investment and financing decisions, including the time value of money, cash flow creation, cost of capital, and capital budgeting.

INNO 211.title: MIE ProSeminar
INNO 211.description: Prepares students for the New Venture Competition in spring quarter. Students form teams to create a startup, submit concept paper, pitch ideas, and attend workshops throughout the academic year.
INNO 211.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship only.

INNO 213.title: Building Prototypes with AI
INNO 213.description: Equips students with the ability to harness artificial intelligence, data analytics, and optimization tools to transform their business concepts into functional product prototypes.

INNO 214.title: Entrepreneurship
INNO 214.description: Student teams develop a business plan to launch a new venture. Drafts of sections of the plan are due throughout the course.
INNO 214.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship only.

INNO 215.title: Lean Startup
INNO 215.description: Exposes students to an entrepreneurial experience with the same pressures and demands of an early-stage startup to provide a real-world, hands-on learning experience in starting a company.
INNO 215.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship only.

INNO 216.title: User Experience Design For Entrepreneurs
INNO 216.description: Designed to teach students how to identify customer pain points, design interfaces, and evaluate usability through experiments. Students learn to conduct A/B tests, analyze results using statistical reasoning, and apply data.

INNO 275.title: Innovation Internship
INNO 275.description: Students apply innovative and creative knowledge obtained from classroom theory through work experiences. Provides knowledge of career opportunities, an understanding of the role innovation plays in business environments, and preparation to become an entrepreneur.
INNO 275.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship only.

INNO 290.title: Special Topics in Innovation and Entrepreneurship
INNO 290.description: Studies in selected areas of innovation and entrepreneurship. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

INNO 291A.title: Business Creation: Ideation
INNO 291A.description: Business Creation is the capstone element for the MIE program that integrates all curricular and co-curricular activities, leveraging course work, expert speakers, and workshops to improve the quality of your idea.
INNO 291A.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship only.

INNO 291B.title: Business Creation: Pitch Deck Preparation
INNO 291B.description: Capstone element for the MIE program that integrates all curricular and co-curricular activities, leveraging course work, expert speakers, and workshops to improve the quality of your idea.
INNO 291B.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship only.

INNO 292.title: Business Law for Entrepreneurs
INNO 292.description: Focuses on educating individuals starting, or investing in, a new business in the U.S. Provides an overview to common legal issues faced by entrepreneurs, such as business formation and structure, governance and employment contracts, and intellectual property and taxation.

INNO 294.title: Edge: Innovation in the New Digital Age
INNO 294.description: Explores the strategic and operational issues that business leaders face in adapting to the new business environment, what we call innovating, managing, and competing at the edge.
INNO 294.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship and Master in Management have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Business students only.

INNO 298.title: Merage Consulting Projects for Entrepreneurs
INNO 298.description: Provides students the opportunity to put into practice concepts, skills, and tools acquired in other parts of the MBA program. Seminars augment internship experiences with analyses of relevant administrative issues.
INNO 298.prereq_text: ( BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR DIGITAL LEADERSHIP MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - FULLY EMPLYD MAJORS ONLY OR BIOTECHNOLOGY MGMT MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - EXECUTIVE MAJORS ONLY )

INNO 299.title: Individual Study
INNO 299.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
INNO 299.restriction: Master Of Innovation and Entrepreneurship majors only.

INTL ST 1.title: Introduction to Global Studies
INTL ST 1.description: Ongoing historical processes that increase global integration, the social, economic, and political interdependence of different regions, cultures, and peoples. Topics include ancient empires, colonialism, nationalism, industrialization, modern imperialism and warfare, decolonization, global social movements, conflict, inequality, and global governance.
INTL ST 1.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 11.title: Global Cultures and Society
INTL ST 11.description: Offers a general overview of the rise of global interdependence in political, economic, demographic, and cultural terms. Considers what drove people from relative isolation into intensified intercourse with one another, and investigates the consequences of this shift.
INTL ST 11.restriction: Anthropology majors and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 12.title: Global Political Ideologies
INTL ST 12.description: An overview of the major political ideologies shaping the current world order and global conflict. Topics include liberalism, democracy, nationalism, capitalism, communism, socialism, fascism, neoliberalism, clash of civilizations, sectarian violence, populist nationalism, and de-globalization.
INTL ST 12.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 15.title: Global Political Economy
INTL ST 15.description: The global economy as an integrated system. The rise of world trade, capitalism, national economies, market cycles, competing economic ideologies, development, globalization, transnational labor, multinational corporations, and the role of UN, World Bank, WTO, and the IMF in global governance.
INTL ST 15.restriction: International Studies majors and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 16.title: Human Rights and Global Governance
INTL ST 16.description: Historical development of civil, political rights and the rise of human rights in international law. Explores role, and limitations, of the UN, ICJ, and ICC in global governance. Reconceptualizing democracy and political representation in a postnational 21st century.
INTL ST 16.restriction: International Studies majors and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 17.title: Global Environmental Issues
INTL ST 17.description: Examines problems such as global climate change, growing human populations, fisheries depletion, ocean acidification, biodiversity loss, deforestation, and food security. Introduces political, social, and economic factors contributing to environmental issues and their disproportional impacts on the world’s poor and minorities.
INTL ST 17.restriction: International Studies majors and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 100.title: Global Trials
INTL ST 100.description: Explores landmark legal trials that have impacted both domestic and world affairs.The trials provide a lens through which to explore society at the time, as well as shed light on the historical legacies of current social, political, and legal values.
INTL ST 100.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 101A.title: Global Social Movements
INTL ST 101A.description: The evolution of global social movements over past 250 years. Age of Revolutions in America, France, and Haiti; nationalism and labor; 1960s global decolonization; 21st century Latin American indigenous movements; Occupy Wall Street, Arab Spring, and social media's #metoo, #BlackLivesMatter.
INTL ST 101A.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 101B.title: Global Cities and Slums
INTL ST 101B.description: Cities as a window into contemporary challenges of the globalized world. Global cities such as Los Angeles, London, and Beijing compared with cities with slums in the global south such as Rio de Janeiro, Johannesburg, and Mumbai.
INTL ST 101B.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 102A.title: Global Refugees and Stateless People
INTL ST 102A.description: Examines the reason behind global refugee crises, and what it means to be a displaced migrant or stateless person in history and in contemporary society. Links case studies about refugees around the world.
INTL ST 102A.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 102B.title: Global Asias and Orientalism
INTL ST 102B.description: Examines how the modern world is divided between East and West in the age of globalization. Through the postcolonial framework of Orientalism, it considers a pluralistic idea of Asia and the current notion of the new world order as one.
INTL ST 102B.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 103A.title: Global Health
INTL ST 103A.description: Explores critical global health and planetary health studies, linking past trends to current research of health inequalities. Case studies include maternal-fetal mortality, environmental contamination, disaster preparedness, pharmaceutical development and access, and humanitarian aid interventions.
INTL ST 103A.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 104A.title: Global Trafficking
INTL ST 104A.description: Explores trafficking in different global contexts. Covers sex trafficking, labor trafficking, and organ trafficking. Tracks the use of the concept in policy, human rights, law, humanitarianism, and media. Provides a complex and nuanced understanding of the problem and its solutions.
INTL ST 104A.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 104BW.title: Global Gender and Sexuality
INTL ST 104BW.description: Develops critical insights into gender and sexuality as products of the world around us and as lived experiences across the globe. Topics include agency and resistance, intersectionality, feminisms, colonialism, heteronormativity, gender violence, masculinities, media and popular culture, globalization and migration.
INTL ST 104BW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
INTL ST 104BW.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 106A.title: Global Political Ecology
INTL ST 106A.description: Introduction to political ecology and critical analysis of the global scale and globalization. Topics include current and historical climate change, fossil fuels, international trade and investment, soil erosion and pollution, deforestation, waste, ocean ecology, water crisis, wars, revolutions, and refugees.
INTL ST 106A.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 106B.title: Global Food Environment
INTL ST 106B.description: Examines the global political ecology of food, focusing on the U.S., China, and Brazil. Topics include the history of agriculture, imperialism/neocolonialism, Malthusianism, migration, agro-industrialization, deforestation, GMOs, agrochemicals, soil and water contamination, land struggles, food security/safety/sovereignty, dietary habits, and climate change.
INTL ST 106B.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 112A.title: International Business
INTL ST 112A.description: Introduction to conducting business in the international arena, decision-making in the organization, and globalization of markets and production. Topics covered range from tax and finance to ethics, marketing, and more. Continuing corporate regulatory scandals discussed.

INTL ST 115.title: Global Poverty and Inequality in the 21st Century
INTL ST 115.description: Explores a multidisciplinary understanding of poverty and inequality in the 21st century and assesses impact of education, health, technology, and other interventions. Course offered online only.

INTL ST 122.title: Nuclear Environments
INTL ST 122.description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.

INTL ST 123.title: Global Borders
INTL ST 123.description: Engages with the theory and substance of global international borders, a relatively new, hotly contentious, and still unfolding global ordering system. Studies examples from the United States, Europe, Latin America, Asia, Africa, and Antarctica.
INTL ST 123.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 124A.title: Introduction to the Comparative Study of Legal Cultures
INTL ST 124A.description: Traces the anthropological and comparative cultural study of law from the nineteenth century to the present; briefly surveys the diversity of recorded legal cultures and critically examines key concepts which have been used to describe and classify them.
INTL ST 124A.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology - Urban and Regional Planning majors, and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 130.title: Transnational Gangs
INTL ST 130.description: Examines the internationalization of U.S. domestic street gangs. The relationship between California gangs Mara Salvatrucha and 18th Street and Mexico/Central American gangs is assessed. Specified topics include: mobilization, migration, territorialism, culture, organization, and use of technology.

INTL ST 137.title: Global Environmental Justice
INTL ST 137.description: Introduces Environmental Justice (EJ) framework as an alternative to mainstream approaches to socio-ecological issues, with special emphasis on communities confronting environmental racism. Examines EJ movements challenging pollution, climate change, disasters, deforestation, and unsafe working environments within a global context.
INTL ST 137.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 141B.title: Homeland Security
INTL ST 141B.description: Examines the 9/11 origins of the concept of homeland security; assess the evolution, structure, and operations of the Department of Homeland Security; critically examines the evolution of threat assessment to the U.S. and the utilization of risk management methodologies.

INTL ST 143A.title: Vietnam War
INTL ST 143A.description: Examines social structures and social changes in Vietnamese and U.S. societies through the study of the Vietnam War.

INTL ST 145A.title: International Law
INTL ST 145A.description: Examination of the origin, changing structure, application of international law, and the role of legal norms in regulating the behavior of states and maintaining international order.

INTL ST 146.title: Global Indigeneity
INTL ST 146.description: Situates the interdisciplinary fields of Native American and Indigenous Studies within a transnational context, focusing on the global dimensions of indigeneity informing local histories, politics, and experiences. Examines settler colonialism, sovereignty, and the enduring legacies of colonialism as global phenomena.
INTL ST 146.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 146W.title: Global Indigeneity
INTL ST 146W.description: Situates the interdisciplinary fields of Native American and Indigenous Studies within a transnational context, focusing on the global dimensions of indigeneity informing local histories, politics, and experiences. Examines settler colonialism, sovereignty, and the enduring legacies of colonialism as global phenomena.
INTL ST 146W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
INTL ST 146W.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 148W.title: Global Futures
INTL ST 148W.description: Develops critical insights into our collective future as it reflects different perspectives of the world. Topics include techno-orientalism, afro-futurism, feminist futures, indigenous cosmology, and environmental concerns.
INTL ST 148W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
INTL ST 148W.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 150.title: Racism and Global Apartheid
INTL ST 150.description: The concept of race has been used to draw a global color line dividing rich from poor, developed from developing, first from third worlds. Racism is used to justify slavery, colonialism, imperialism, eugenics, genocide, and extreme inequalities produced by globalization.
INTL ST 150.restriction: International Studies majors and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 152A.title: Non-Government Organization (NGO) Fundamentals
INTL ST 152A.description: Introduction to non-governmental organizations, including their role in U.S. society and the international community. Explores varying definitions of NGOs and the characteristics held in common by all NGOs.

INTL ST 153F.title: Militarism and Gender
INTL ST 153F.description: Examination of feminist approaches to militarism, war, and political violence; drawing on representations of women as both victims of and participants in military violence; effects of militarism on formations of gender; effects of military industrial complex on nationalism and identity.

INTL ST 154W.title: Ethics and Justice in International Affairs
INTL ST 154W.description: Analyzes choices regarding the use of force, resolving conflict, and promoting human rights and social justice. Special attention is given to the American experience as a principal case study of ethics and statecraft.
INTL ST 154W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
INTL ST 154W.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 155.title: Racial Capitalism
INTL ST 155.description: Explores the historical relationship between racism and capitalism. Social movements such as Black Lives Matter highlight the contemporary political economy of racial capitalism, and the relationship between domestic policing and international militarization as twin sides of global racial hegemony.
INTL ST 155.restriction: International Studies majors and International Studies minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 157C.title: Comparing European and US Societies
INTL ST 157C.description: Society, culture, institutions of U.S. and European countries. Fertility to football, guns to government, work to welfare, health to housework. Cross-national approaches for understanding the world and thinking critically about taken-for-granted practices. Policies the U.S. might borrow for social issues.

INTL ST 158B.title: Peoples of the Pacific
INTL ST 158B.description: The cultural history and recent developments among the Pacific peoples of Polynesia, Micronesia, Melanesia, New Guinea, and Australia.

INTL ST 158D.title: China in the Global Age
INTL ST 158D.description: Chinese society from 1949 to present. Social change in the context of political control and ideological considerations. Focus on the power structure, political decision processes, and ideological legitimation, and interplay with the Chinese community and its culture.

INTL ST 160.title: Global Childhoods
INTL ST 160.description: Explores the politics of childhood across global contexts. Children are portrayed as innocent victims needing help from governments and humanitarian organizations. How are children’s needs addressed and formulated? In turn, how do children navigate humanitarianism, schooling, and labor?
INTL ST 160.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 161A.title: Political Islam
INTL ST 161A.description: Political Islamd is a diverse phenomenon. While noticeable barriers exist to "Islamist democracy," it is the Islamists who will define the political future of much of the Muslim world. Reviews the experience of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, and Indonesia.

INTL ST 162B.title: Peoples and Cultures of Post-Soviet Eurasia
INTL ST 162B.description: Examines the cultures and political conflicts of the more than 130 indigenous ethnic groups in the European and Asian territories of the former U.S.S.R. Emphasis is on the theoretical issues of ethnicity, nationalism, and conflict management.

INTL ST 163.title: Global Inequalities
INTL ST 163.description: An examination of various forms of social, economic, and political inequality within and between nations. Different approaches to understanding inequality and the intersections of poverty, race, ethnicity, class, gender, nationality, health, and violence.
INTL ST 163.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 165.title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
INTL ST 165.description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

INTL ST 173.title: US-Mexico Borders
INTL ST 173.description: Analyzes the multiplicity of the US-Mexico border. From its inception to its contentious political present, the border is at once a historical, geo-political, and affective entity and space.
INTL ST 173.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 175A.title: U.S. War on Terrorism
INTL ST 175A.description: Analyzes the United States war on terrorism by focusing on terrorism, the U.S. wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and changes in police powers through the Patriot Act, as well as the political leadership which directs the war.

INTL ST 176C.title: Political Power in Contemporary China
INTL ST 176C.description: Analyzes the sources of political power in contemporary China, including historical legitimacy, political institutions, and Chinese Communist Party power. Identifies challenges to the CCP’s rule and rising socio-political issues such as mass protest, censorship, and the environment.
INTL ST 176C.restriction: Political Science majors and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 177C.title: Revolution in Latin America
INTL ST 177C.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada. Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

INTL ST 177D.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
INTL ST 177D.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

INTL ST 177E.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
INTL ST 177E.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

INTL ST 177G.title: Revolution and Reaction in Cold War Latin America
INTL ST 177G.description: Explores Latin American experiences of revolutionary change and military dictatorship during the Cold War (1945-1990). Pays particular attention to the lives of women, peasants, workers, and the urban middle classes. Case studies include Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, Argentina, Nicaragua, and Mexico.

INTL ST 177I.title: Ancient Civilization of Mexico and the Southwest
INTL ST 177I.description: The prehistory and cultural evolution of the civilization which originated in Mexico, including the Olmecs, Aztecs, Toltecs, Maya, and Zapotec, as well as the Pueblos of the Southwestern U.S. Topics include the origins of food production and of the state.

INTL ST 179.title: Special Topics: Geographic Focus in International Studies
INTL ST 179.description: Studies in selected areas of international studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

INTL ST H180.title: International Studies Honors Research Seminar
INTL ST H180.description: Assists students to prepare a thesis prospectus for the Honors Program in International Studies. Students choose a topic, learn writing and research methods, write a prospectus and orally present and defend it, and conduct a literature review.
INTL ST H180.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 183A.title: Global and International Studies Forum
INTL ST 183A.description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.

INTL ST 183CW.title: Seminar Conflict Resolution
INTL ST 183CW.description: Designed for seniors who are pursuing the International Studies major and/or minor. Provides a forum in which students will refine skills and theory in the study of cooperation and conflict, from local to global arenas. Students write research paper.
INTL ST 183CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
INTL ST 183CW.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

INTL ST 183E.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
INTL ST 183E.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

INTL ST 189.title: Special Topics: Global Focus in International Studies
INTL ST 189.description: Studies in selected areas of international studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

INTL ST H190.title: Honors Thesis
INTL ST H190.description: Students work with faculty to complete their honors thesis.

INTL ST 199.title: Individual Study
INTL ST 199.description: Students participate in planned research and study under written contract with a supervising UCI instructor. Students may enroll for only one individual study course each quarter.

INTL ST 201.title: What is Global Studies?
INTL ST 201.description: Introduces graduates to the field of global and international studies. Landmark studies outline the transition from globalization studies to contemporary global studies. Identify complex global issues, underlying processes of globalization, and the impacts they have on people around the world.

INTL ST 202.title: Foundations of European Social Thought
INTL ST 202.description: Provides graduate students with a broad overview of the major landmarks in the development of modern social thought. Introduces key philosophers and theorists Adam Smith, Marx, Durkheim, Weber, Freud, and Du Bois, focusing on the global dimensions of their work.

INTL ST 203.title: Globalizing Social Theory in the Age of Extremes
INTL ST 203.description: Examines important developments in social theory between 1914 and 1991. The overarching goal is to synthesize from these various approaches a critical and transdisciplinary theoretical framework to analyze complex global issues.

INTL ST 204.title: Theories of Globalization
INTL ST 204.description: Theories of globalization engage deep historical transformations, keeping the interrelated dynamics of economics, politics, and culture in focus. Theories examine transformations emanating at transnational and state levels, and from below in the form of social movements led by everyday people.

INTL ST 205.title: Theories from the Global South
INTL ST 205.description: Looking beyond the theoretical traditions of the Euro-American academy scholars can begin to engage important theoretical contributions from the Global South. Explores alternative standpoints and interventions challenging dominant narratives and calling into question taken-for-granted assumptions, categories, concepts, values, and perspectives.

INTL ST 206.title: Engaging Global Issues
INTL ST 206.description: Critical and interdisciplinary works on global issues serve as examples that graduates can use in their own research. Each week focuses on a different example of outstanding global research done by a scholar having an important impact on the field.

INTL ST 207.title: Research Design and Methods
INTL ST 207.description: Fundamentals of empirical research design, strategies for global research, sampling logics, reliability, validity, mixed methods, integrating qualitative and quantitative methods. Introduction to basic data collection methods and examples of more advanced methodological strategies. Research ethics and the IRB review process.

INTL ST 208.title: Grant Writing
INTL ST 208.description: Focuses on production, critique, and revision of student research proposals. A practical seminar designed to improve student proposals, help students through the application processes, and increase students' chances of obtaining support for their research.

INTL ST 210A.title: Proseminar in Global Studies I
INTL ST 210A.description: Year-long intensive introduction to graduate students to a range of topics pertinent to the field of Global Studies. The guest speakers and topics addressed vary each quarter.

INTL ST 210B.title: Proseminar in Global Studies II
INTL ST 210B.description: Year-long intensive introduction to graduate students to a range of topics pertinent to the field of Global Studies. The guest speakers and topics addressed vary each quarter.

INTL ST 210C.title: Proseminar in Global Studies III
INTL ST 210C.description: Year-long intensive introduction to graduate students to a range of topics pertinent to the field of Global Studies. The guest speakers and topics addressed vary each quarter.

INTL ST 215.title: Global Perspectives on Gender and Sexuality
INTL ST 215.description: Selected readings introduce students to topics such as queer globalization, global sexual economy, Indigenous feminism, gender regimes, heteronationalism, the straight state, heteropatriarchy, feminist science and environmentalism, and global masculinities.

INTL ST 220.title: Global Indigeneity
INTL ST 220.description: Examines issues impacting Indigenous peoples in local, national, and global contexts, including the cultural, political, and legal status of Indigeneity and geopolitical struggles over Indigenous territories, challenges such as climate change to Indigenous lifeways, and contemporary struggles for survivance.

INTL ST 225.title: Racial Capitalism
INTL ST 225.description: Explores the concept of “racial capitalism” that has been mobilized by contemporary radical movements from Black Lives Matter and the prison abolition movement, to movements for climate justice. How does race, class, gender, and sexuality feature in capitalism today?

INTL ST 230.title: Postcolonial, Anticolonial, and Decolonial Theories
INTL ST 230.description: Examines postcolonial, anticolonial, and decolonial theories through recent works that explore different issues, histories, and literatures around the world.

INTL ST 259.title: Special Topics in Global Studies
INTL ST 259.description: Studies in selected areas of global studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

INTL ST 260.title: Directed Reading and Research
INTL ST 260.description: Readings focused on specialized topics in consultation with, and with the consent of, a faculty member. Students are expected to produce a paper based on the readings.

INTL ST 290.title: Dissertation Research
INTL ST 290.description: Dissertation research with Global and International Studies faculty.

INTL ST 299.title: Independent Study
INTL ST 299.description: Independent research with Global and International Studies faculty.

IRAN 231A.title: History of Zoroastrianism
IRAN 231A.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

IRAN 231B.title: Ancient Persia
IRAN 231B.description: Survey of the history of Persia in antiquity.

IRAN 231C.title: Medieval Persia
IRAN 231C.description: A survey of Persian history in the context of Late Antique and Medieval Islamic history.

IRAN 255A.title: Ancient India
