MATH 13.description: Introduction to formal definition and rigorous proof writing in mathematics. Topics include basic logic, set theory, equivalence relations, and various proof techniques such as direct, induction, contradiction, contrapositive, and exhaustion.
MATH 13.prereq_text: MATH 2A or MATH 5A or I&C SCI 6D or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 3.
MATH 13.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 13X.title: Skills for Success in Abstract Math
MATH 13X.description: Group activities designed to practice fundamental concepts used in abstract mathematics. Logic and reasoning; functions; sets. Proof techniques. Most coursework is done in class in collaboration with peers.
MATH 13X.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 99.title: New Math Major Seminar for First-Year and Transfer Students
MATH 99.description: A series of presentations and activities to help first-year and transfer students transition to the UCI mathematics majors. Presentations are given by faculty, current students, and school staff to ensure that students make the most of the math major.
MATH 99.restriction: New math majors only, including transfer students majoring in math.

MATH 105A.title: Numerical Analysis I
MATH 105A.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of numerical computation with an emphasis on solving equations. Solving transcendental equations; linear systems, Gaussian elimination, QR factorization, iterative methods, eigenvalue computation, power method.
MATH 105A.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 105B.title: Numerical Analysis II
MATH 105B.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of numerical computation with an emphasis on topics from calculus and approximation theory. Lagrange interpolation; Gaussian quadrature; Fourier series and transforms; Methods from data science including least squares and L1 regression.
MATH 105B.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 105LA.title: Numerical Analysis Laboratory
MATH 105LA.description: Provides practical experience to complement the theory developed in MATH 105A.
MATH 105LA.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 105LB.title: Numerical Analysis Laboratory
MATH 105LB.description: Provides practical experience to complement the theory developed in MATH 105B.
MATH 105LB.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 107.title: Numerical Differential Equations
MATH 107.description: Theory and applications of numerical methods to initial and boundary-value problems for ordinary and partial differential equations.
MATH 107.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 107L.title: Numerical Differential Equations Laboratory
MATH 107L.description: Provides practical experience to complement the theory developed in MATH 107.
MATH 107L.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 110A.title: Optimization I
MATH 110A.description: Introduction to optimization, linear search method, trust region method, Newton method, linear programming, linear, and non-linear least square methods.
MATH 110A.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 110B.title: Optimization II
MATH 110B.description: The simplex method, interior point method, penalty barrier method, primal dual method, augmented Lagrangian method, and stochastic gradient method.
MATH 110B.prereq_text: MATH 110A with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 110B.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 112A.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Applications I
MATH 112A.description: Introduction to ordinary and partial differential equations and their applications in engineering and science. Basic methods for classical PDEs (potential, heat, and wave equations). Classification of PDEs, separation of variables and series expansions, special functions, eigenvalue problems.
MATH 112A.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 112B.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Applications II
MATH 112B.description: Introduction to partial differential equations and their applications in engineering and science. Basic methods for classical PDEs (potential, heat, and wave equations). Green functions and integral representations, method of characteristics.
MATH 112B.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 112C.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Applications III
MATH 112C.description: Nonhomogeneous problems and Green's functions, Sturm-Liouville theory, general Fourier expansions, applications of partial differential equations in different areas of science.
MATH 112C.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 113A.title: Mathematical Modeling in Biology I
MATH 113A.description: Discrete mathematical and statistical models; difference equations, population dynamics, Markov chains, and statistical models in biology.
MATH 113A.prereq_text: MATH 2B or MATH 5B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4.
MATH 113A.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 113B.title: Mathematical Modeling in Biology II
MATH 113B.description: Linear algebra; differential equations models; dynamical systems; stability; hysteresis; phase plane analysis; applications to cell biology, viral dynamics, and infectious diseases.
MATH 113B.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 115.title: Mathematical Modeling
MATH 115.description: Mathematical modeling and analysis of phenomena that arise in engineering physical sciences, biology, economics, or social sciences.

MATH 117.title: Dynamical Systems
MATH 117.description: Introduction to the modern theory of dynamical systems including contraction mapping principle, fractals and chaos, conservative systems, Kepler problem, billiard models, expanding maps, Smale's horseshoe, topological entropy.
MATH 117.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 118.title: The Theory of Differential Equations
MATH 118.description: Existence and uniqueness of solutions, continuous dependence of solutions on initial conditions and parameters, Lyapunov and asymptotic stability, Floquet theory, nonlinear systems, and bifurcations.
MATH 118.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 120A.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra: Groups
MATH 120A.description: Axioms for group theory; permutation groups, matrix groups. Isomorphisms, homomorphisms, quotient groups. Advanced topics as time permits. Special emphasis on doing proofs.
MATH 120A.prereq_text: MATH 3A and MATH 13 with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 120A.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 120B.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra: Rings and Fields
MATH 120B.description: Basic properties of rings; ideals, quotient rings; polynomial and matrix rings. Elements of field theory.
MATH 120B.prereq_text: MATH 120A with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 120B.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 120C.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra: Galois Theory
MATH 120C.description: Galois Theory: proof of the impossibility of certain ruler-and-compass constructions (squaring the circle, trisecting angles); nonexistence of analogues to the "quadratic formula" for polynomial equations of degree 5 or higher.
MATH 120C.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 121A.title: Linear Algebra I
MATH 121A.description: Introduction to modern abstract linear algebra. Special emphasis on students doing proofs. Vector spaces, linear independence, bases, dimension. Linear transformations and their matrix representations. Theory of determinants.
MATH 121A.prereq_text: MATH 3A and MATH 13 with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 121A.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 121B.title: Linear Algebra II
MATH 121B.description: Introduction to modern abstract linear algebra. Special emphasis on students doing proofs. Inner products; similarity of matrices; singular value decomposition. Other topics as time permits.
MATH 121B.prereq_text: MATH 121A with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 121B.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 130A.title: Probability I
MATH 130A.description: Combinatorial probability, conditional probabilities, independence, discrete and continuous random variables, expectation and variance, common probability distributions.
MATH 130A.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors, Mathematics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 130B.title: Probability II
MATH 130B.description: Joint distributions, sums of independent random variables, conditional distributions and conditional expectation, covariances, moment generating functions, limit theorems.
MATH 130B.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors, Mathematics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 130C.title: Stochastic Processes
MATH 130C.description: Markov chains, Brownian motion, Gaussian processes, applications to option pricing and Markov chain Monte Carlo methods.
MATH 130C.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors, Mathematics majors, and Quantitative Economics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 134A.title: Fixed Income
MATH 134A.description: Overview of interest theory, time value of money, annuities/cash flows with payments that are not contingent, loans, sinking funds, bonds, general cash flow and portfolios, immunization, duration and convexity, swaps.
MATH 134A.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 134B.title: Mathematics of Financial Derivatives
MATH 134B.description: General derivatives; call/put options; hedging and investment strategies; spreads and collars; risk management; forwards and futures; bonds.
MATH 134B.prereq_text: MATH 130A with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 134B.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 134C.title: Mathematical Models for Finance
MATH 134C.description: General properties of options: option contracts (call and put options, European, American and exotic options); binomial option pricing model, Black-Scholes option pricing model; risk-neutral pricing formula using Monte-Carlo simulation; option greeks and risk management; interest rate derivatives, Markowitz portfolio theory.
MATH 134C.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 140A.title: Elementary Analysis I
MATH 140A.description: Introduction to real analysis, including convergence of sequence, infinite series, differentiation and integration, and sequences of functions. Students are expected to do proofs.
MATH 140A.prereq_text: MATH 2D and MATH 3A and MATH 13 with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 140A.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 140B.title: Elementary Analysis II
MATH 140B.description: Introduction to real analysis including convergence of sequences, infinite series, differentiation and integration, and sequences of functions. Students are expected to do proofs.
MATH 140B.prereq_text: MATH 140A with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 140B.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 140C.title: Analysis in Several Variables
MATH 140C.description: Rigorous treatment of multivariable differential calculus. Jacobians, Inverse and Implicit Function theorems.
MATH 140C.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH H140A.title: Honors Introduction to Graduate Analysis I
MATH H140A.description: Construction of the real number system, topology of the real line, concepts of continuity, differential and integral calculus, sequences and series of functions, equicontinuity, metric spaces, multivariable differential and integral calculus, implicit functions, curves and surfaces.
MATH H140A.prereq_text: MATH 2E with a minimum grade of A and MATH 3A and MATH 13 with a minimum grade of A and MATH 121A with a minimum grade of A and MATH 140A with a minimum grade of A.

MATH H140B.title: Honors Introduction to Graduate Analysis II
MATH H140B.description: Construction of the real number system, topology of the real line, concepts of continuity, differential and integral calculus, sequences and series of functions, equicontinuity, metric spaces, multivariable differential and integral calculus, implicit functions, curves and surfaces.
MATH H140B.prereq_text: MATH H140A with a minimum grade of C-.

MATH H140C.title: Honors Introduction to Graduate Analysis III
MATH H140C.description: Construction of the real number system; topology of the real line; concepts of continuity, differential, and integral calculus; sequences and series of functions, equicontinuity, metric spaces, multivariable differential, and integral calculus; implicit functions, curves and surfaces.
MATH H140C.prereq_text: MATH H140B with a minimum grade of C-.

MATH 141.title: Introduction to Topology
MATH 141.description: The elements of naive set theory and the basic properties of metric spaces. Introduction to topological properties.
MATH 141.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 147.title: Complex Analysis
MATH 147.description: Rigorous treatment of basic complex analysis: analytic functions, Cauchy integral theory and its consequences, power series, residue calculus, harmonic functions, conformal mapping. Students are expected to do proofs.
MATH 147.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 150.title: Introduction to Mathematical Logic
MATH 150.description: First order logic through the Completeness Theorem for predicate logic.
MATH 150.prereq_text: MATH 13 with a minimum grade of C- or (I&C SCI 6B with a minimum grade of C- and I&C SCI 6D with a minimum grade of C-).
MATH 150.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 161.title: Modern Geometry
MATH 161.description: Euclidean Geometry; Hilbert's Axioms; Absolute Geometry; Hyperbolic Geometry; the Poincare Models; and Geometric Transformations.
MATH 161.prereq_text: MATH 13 with a minimum grade of C- or (I&C SCI 6B with a minimum grade of C- and I&C SCI 6D with a minimum grade of C-).
MATH 161.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 162A.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry I
MATH 162A.description: Applications of advanced calculus and linear algebra to the geometry of curves and surfaces in space.
MATH 162A.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 162B.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry II
MATH 162B.description: Applications of advanced calculus and linear algebra to the geometry of curves and surfaces in space.
MATH 162B.prereq_text: MATH 162A with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 162B.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 173A.title: Introduction to Cryptology I
MATH 173A.description: Introduction to some of the mathematics used in the making and breaking of codes, with applications to classical ciphers and public key systems. Includes topics from number theory, probability, and abstract algebra.
MATH 173A.prereq_text: (MATH 2B or MATH 5B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and (MATH 3A and MATH 13) or (I&C SCI 6B and I&C SCI 6D).
MATH 173A.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 173B.title: Introduction to Cryptology II
MATH 173B.description: Introduction to some of the mathematics used in the making and breaking of codes, with applications to classical ciphers and public key systems. The mathematics covered includes topics from number theory, probability, and abstract algebra.
MATH 173B.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 175.title: Combinatorics
MATH 175.description: Introduction to combinatorics including basic counting principles, permutations, combinations, binomial coefficients, inclusion-exclusion, derangements, ordinary and exponential generating functions, recurrence relations, Catalan numbers, Stirling numbers, and partition numbers.
MATH 175.prereq_text: (MATH 2B or MATH 5B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and MATH 13 with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 175.restriction: Applied and Computational Mathematics majors and Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 176.title: Mathematics of Finance
MATH 176.description: After reviewing tools from probability, statistics, and elementary differential and partial differential equations, concepts such as hedging, arbitrage, Puts, Calls, the design of portfolios, the derivation and solution of the Blac-Scholes, and other equations are discussed.
MATH 176.restriction: Business Economics majors, Economics majors, Mathematics majors, Quantitative Economics majors, and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 178.title: Mathematical Machine Learning
MATH 178.description: Theoretical introduction to Mathematical Machine Learning. Mathematical foundations and coding implementations using Python libraries such as scikit-learn and Keras. Supervised and unsupervised learning; regression and classification; loss functions; overfitting and the bias-complexity tradeoff. Prominent algorithms in machine learning.

MATH 180A.title: Number Theory I
MATH 180A.description: Introduction to number theory and applications. Divisibility, prime numbers, factorization. Arithmetic functions. Congruences. Quadratic residue. Diophantine equations. Introduction to cryptography.
MATH 180A.prereq_text: MATH 3A and MATH 13 with a minimum grade of C-.
MATH 180A.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 180B.title: Number Theory II
MATH 180B.description: Introduction to number theory and applications. Analytic number theory, character sums, finite fields, discrete logarithm, computational complexity. Introduction to coding theory. Other topics as time permits.
MATH 180B.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 184.title: Topics in the History of Mathematics
MATH 184.description: Topics include mathematics in ancient times; the development of modern analysis; the evolution of geometric ideas. Students are assigned individual topics for term papers.
MATH 184.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 184L.title: History of Mathematics Lesson Lab
MATH 184L.description: Aspiring math teachers research, design, present, and peer review middle school or high school math lessons that draw from history of mathematics topics.

MATH 192.title: Studies in the Learning and Teaching of Secondary Mathematics
MATH 192.description: Focus is on historic and current mathematical concepts related to student learning and effective math pedagogy, with fieldwork in grades 6-14.

MATH 194.title: Problem Solving Seminar
MATH 194.description: Develops ability in analytical thinking and problem solving, using problems of the type found in the Mathematics Olympiad and the Putnam Mathematical Competition. Students taking the course in fall will prepare for and take the Putnam examination in December.

MATH 195W.title: Mathematical Writing
MATH 195W.description: Techniques of mathematical writing and communication. Covers effectively writing mathematical papers, creating effective presentations, and communicating mathematics in a variety of media. Focuses on utilizing LaTeX for typesetting mathematics.
MATH 195W.prereq_text: MATH 120A with a minimum grade of C- or MATH 121A with a minimum grade of C- or MATH 140A with a minimum grade of C-. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
MATH 195W.restriction: Mathematics majors and Applied and Computational Mathematics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MATH 199A.title: Special Studies in Mathematics
MATH 199A.description: Supervised reading. For outstanding undergraduate Mathematics majors in supervised but independent reading or research of mathematical topics.

MATH 199B.title: Special Studies in Mathematics
MATH 199B.description: Supervised reading. For outstanding undergraduate Mathematics majors in supervised but independent reading or research of mathematical topics.

MATH 199C.title: Special Studies in Mathematics
MATH 199C.description: Supervised reading. For outstanding undergraduate Mathematics majors in supervised but independent reading or research of mathematical topics.

MATH 205A.title: Introduction to Graduate Analysis
MATH 205A.description: Construction of the real number system, topology of the real line, concepts of continuity, differential and integral calculus, sequences and series of functions, equicontinuity, metric spaces, multivariable differential and integral calculus, implicit functions, curves and surfaces.
MATH 205A.prereq_text: Recommended: MATH 2E and MATH 3A and MATH 13, or equivalent.
MATH 205A.restriction: Mathematics majors, Doctor of Philosophy, and Master of Science only.

MATH 205B.title: Introduction to Graduate Analysis
MATH 205B.description: Construction of the real number system, topology of the real line, concepts of continuity, differential and integral calculus, sequences and series of functions, equicontinuity, metric spaces, multivariable differential and integral calculus, implicit functions, curves and surfaces.

MATH 205B.restriction: Mathematics majors, Doctor of Philosophy, and Master of Science only.

MATH 205C.title: Introduction to Graduate Analysis
MATH 205C.description: Construction of the real number system, topology of the real line, concepts of continuity, differential and integral calculus, sequences and series of functions, equicontinuity, metric spaces, multivariable differential and integral calculus, implicit functions, curves and surfaces.

MATH 210A.title: Real Analysis
MATH 210A.description: Measure theory, Lebesgue integral, signed measures, Radon-Nikodym theorem, functions of bounded variation and absolutely continuous functions, classical Banach spaces, Lp spaces, integration on locally compact spaces and the Riesz-Markov theorem, measure and outer measure, product measure spaces.

MATH 210B.title: Real Analysis

MATH 218A.title: Introduction to Manifolds and Geometry
MATH 218A.description: General topology and fundamental groups, covering space; Stokes theorem on manifolds, selected topics on abstract manifold theory.
MATH 218A.prereq_text: Recommended: MATH 140C and MATH 121B, or equivalent.

MATH 218B.title: Introduction to Manifolds and Geometry
MATH 218B.description: General topology and fundamental groups, covering space; Stokes theorem on manifolds, selected topics on abstract manifold theory.

MATH 220A.title: Analytic Function Theory
MATH 220A.description: Standard theorems about analytic functions. Harmonic functions. Normal families. Conformal mapping.

MATH 220B.title: Analytic Function Theory
MATH 220B.description: Standard theorems about analytic functions. Harmonic functions. Normal families. Conformal mapping.

MATH 220C.title: Analytic Function Theory
MATH 220C.description: Standard theorems about analytic functions. Harmonic functions. Normal families. Conformal mapping.

MATH 222A.title: Topics in Several Complex Variables and Complex Geometry
MATH 222A.description: Several Complex variables, d-bar problems, mappings, Kaehler geometry, de Rham and Dolbeault Theorems, Chern Classes, Hodge Theorems, Calabi conjecture, Kahler-Einstein geometry, Monge-Ampere.

MATH 222C.description: Several Complex variables, d-bar problems, mappings, Kaehler geometry, Le Rham and Dolbeault Theorems, Chern Classes, Hodge Theorems, Calabi conjecture, Kahler-Einstein geometry, Monge-Ampere.

MATH 225A.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing
MATH 225A.description: Introduction to fundamentals of numerical analysis from an advanced viewpoint. Error analysis, approximation of functions, nonlinear equations.
MATH 225A.prereq_text: Recommended: MATH 3D and MATH 105B and MATH 140A and MATH 121A and MATH 112A, or equivalent.

MATH 225B.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing
MATH 225B.description: Introduction to fundamentals of numerical analysis from an advanced viewpoint. Numerical linear algebra, numerical solutions of differential equations; stability.

MATH 225C.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing
MATH 225C.description: Introduction to fundamentals of numerical analysis from an advanced viewpoint. Numerical linear algebra, numerical solutions of differential equations; stability.
MATH 225C.prereq_text: Recommended: MATH 3D and MATH 105B and MATH 140A and MATH 121A and MATH 112A, or equivalent.

MATH 226A.title: Computational Differential Equations
MATH 226A.description: Finite difference and finite element methods. Quick treatment of functional and nonlinear analysis background: weak solution, Lp spaces, Sobolev spaces. Approximation theory. Fourier and Petrov-Galerkin methods; mesh generation. Elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic cases in 226A-B-C, respectively.
MATH 226A.prereq_text: Recommended: MATH 3D and MATH 112A and (MATH 140B or MATH 105B), or equivalent.

MATH 226B.title: Computational Differential Equations
MATH 226B.description: Finite difference and finite element methods. Quick treatment of functional and nonlinear analysis background: weak solution, Lp spaces, Sobolev spaces. Approximation theory. MATH 227A.title: Mathematical and Computational Biology
MATH 227A.description: Analytical and numerical methods for dynamical systems, temporal-spatial dynamics, steady state, stability, stochasticity. Application to life sciences: genetics, tissue growth and patterning, cancers, ion channels gating, signaling networks, morphogen gradients. Analytical methods.

MATH 299C.prereq_text: MATH 299B with a minimum grade of B-.

MED HUM 1.title: Health, Wellness, and Conception of the Body
MED HUM 1.description: Asks what is health and who gets to have it? What is considered a “healthy” or “sick” body? We analyze historical and contemporary experiences of illness, medicine, and caregiving, including how patients represent their bodies and healing.

MED HUM 3.title: Art and Medicine
MED HUM 3.description: Analyzes the relationship between medicine and the visual arts from the late medieval to modern periods, covering topics such as anatomy, optical medical technologies, gender and race in medicine, and popular representations of disease and doctors.

MED HUM 137.title: Surviving Epidemics
MED HUM 137.description: Analyzes diverse social and cultural responses to epidemics from mid-nineteenth century to the present, including incarceration, caregiving, and disability rights. Using interdisciplinary materials and collaborative activities, students interpret strategies and outcomes of Indigenous, racialized, and marginalized communities surviving great illness.
MED HUM 137.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

MED HUM 195.title: Capstone Seminar: The Clinical Moral Laboratory
MED HUM 195.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of the clinical encounter, and the importance of meaning making in these “moral laboratories.” Students enter the clinical space as participant observers, and reflect on how the clinical site informs and challenges reading practices.
MED HUM 195.prereq_text: MED HUM 1 or MED HUM 3 or GEN&SEX 60A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

MED HUM 200.title: Critical Perspectives in Medical Humanities
MED HUM 200.description: Analyzes social and cultural understandings of the body, health, illness, medicine, and disease. Themes include critical histories of the body; non-compliant subjects interacting with medicine; racial-sexual hierarchies of health; and theories and expressions of pain and suffering.

MGMT 1.title: Introduction to Business and Management
MGMT 1.description: Rigorous overview of major business functions and management topics. Addresses the global and fast-changing environment in which modern business enterprises operate as well as the challenges posed by concerns about sustainable growth, ethics, and social responsibility.
MGMT 1.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 4A.title: Basic Economics for Managers I
MGMT 4A.description: Microeconomic principles for managers. Useful applications of basic economic principles to situations in business as well as in various professions.

and.not: AP ECONOMICS:MICRO score of 4 or greater

MGMT 4A.prereq_text: NO AP ECONOMICS:MICRO score of 4 or greater AND NO ECON 20A
MGMT 4A.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4A may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20A.

MGMT 4B.title: Basic Economics for Managers II
MGMT 4B.description: Macroeconomic principles for managers. Useful applications of basic economic principles to situations in business as well as in various professions.

and.not: AP ECONOMICS:MACRO score of 4 or greater

MGMT 4B.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4B may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20B.

MGMT 7.title: Statistics for Business Decision Making
MGMT 7.description: Basics of data analysis and the fundamental notion of statistical inference emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Classical estimation and hypotheses testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, nonparametric methods, and statistical probability.

and.not: AP STATISTICS score of 3 or greater

MGMT 7.prereq_text: NO STATS 7 AND NO STATS 8 AND NO ECON 15A AND NO ECON 15B AND NO AP STATISTICS score of 3 or greater
MGMT 7.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 30A.title: Principles of Accounting I
MGMT 30A.description: First in a two-course introductory series. Emphasis on financial accounting concepts and practices essential to the administration of business enterprises; including recording and valuation of financial transactions, and preparation, analysis, and interpretation of financial statements.
MGMT 30A.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 30B.title: Principles of Accounting II
MGMT 30B.description: Second in a two-course introductory series. Emphasis is on the introduction of managerial accounting concepts and techniques as tools to aid management in carrying out the primary internal functions of planning, control, and decision-making.
MGMT 30B.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 90.title: Special Topics in Management
MGMT 90.description: Studies in selected areas of management. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
MGMT 90.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 101.title: Management Science
MGMT 101.description: Concepts and methods of management science, which applies mathematical modeling and analysis to management problems. Topics include linear and integer programming, project scheduling, inventory management, queuing analysis, decision analysis, and simulation.
MGMT 101.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 102.title: Managing Organizational Behavior
MGMT 102.description: Basic theory and concepts which provide the manager with tools for understanding behavior of people in organizations. Areas such as individual, group, and organizational determinants of attitudes, turnover, and job performance.
MGMT 102.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 105.title: Introduction to Marketing
MGMT 105.description: Basic marketing concepts; discussion of the role marketing plays in modern society. Topics include industrial and consumer marketing, promotion, distribution, and pricing theory.
MGMT 105.prereq_text: ( BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR BUSINESS INFO MGMT MAJORS ONLY )
MGMT 105.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 107.title: Introduction to Management Information Systems
MGMT 107.description: Information Technology (IT) continues to drive rapid productivity growth and structural changes in the economy. Topics include what IT is, and how companies can use IT to improve business processes, enhance customer services, and gain competitive advantage over rivals.
MGMT 107.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 109.title: Introduction to Managerial Finance
MGMT 109.description: Basics of financial administration. Capital budgeting, cost of capital, cash budgeting, working capital management, and long-term sources of funds. Provides a basic understanding of issues and techniques involved in financial decision making.
MGMT 109.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 110.title: Strategic Management
MGMT 110.description: Addresses management of the entire business. Role of the general manager in organizations, industry analysis, core competencies, growth through vertical integration, innovation, acquisition and diversification, globalization, strategy implementation, and the ethical and moral responsibility of a manager.
MGMT 110.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 113.title: New Ventures: A Course in Entrepreneurship
MGMT 113.description: Introduction to the survival and growth of new ventures. Methods include analysis of live cases, guest speakers, discussion, and field projects with contemporary new ventures to learn about new venture management and surviving the liabilities of newness.
MGMT 113.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 114.title: Intro to Consulting
MGMT 114.description: Introduces business consulting fundamentals through case studies, frameworks, and team projects. Students develop client engagement strategies, problem-solving methods, AI applications, and presentation skills to address real-world challenges across diverse industries.
MGMT 114.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 115.title: Lean Startup
MGMT 115.description: Based on the well-known Lean Launchpad course currently used by a growing segment of the startup world. Students work in teams to ideate, develop a Business Model Canvas, and gather customer/market feedback.
MGMT 115.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 120.title: Managing Organizational Change
MGMT 120.description: Focuses on the implementation of change. Identifies the features of successful changes in organizations of varying sizes and configurations, with an emphasis on the reasons why individuals resist or embrace change.
MGMT 120.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 121.title: Human Resources Analytics
MGMT 121.description: Using hands-on projects, case discussions, and video demonstrations, students learn how to use HR analytics to make strategic decisions. These skills benefit students who plan to enter management, consulting, or HR Analytics. No prior analytical training is necessary.
MGMT 121.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 122.title: Beyond Networking: Mastering the Hidden Dynamics of Connection
MGMT 122.description: Explores how relationships and network structures critically impact career and life success. Students learn to analyze network patterns, assess their own connections, measure social networks, and understand trust's vital role, discovering why networks are invaluable assets.
MGMT 122.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Business students only.

MGMT 123.title: Creativity and Leadership in Entrepreneurial Organizations
MGMT 123.description: Uses activities, experiments, readings, and reflections to develop the skills, self-awareness, and confidence to be more creative. Then uses examples, case studies, and a group project to put creativity into practice—i.e., to innovate—to solve worthwhile problems.
MGMT 123.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 124.title: Human Resources Management
MGMT 124.description: Theory and practice of managing human resources. Students identify and analyze HR dilemmas, apply labor law, and design systems and processes to develop the human resources needed to help organizations achieve their goals.
MGMT 124.restriction: Business Information Management majors and Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 125.title: Negotiations
MGMT 125.description: Assists students in developing an understanding of different theoretical perspectives and develop their skills in negotiating. Exploration of feelings and beliefs about negotiation, negotiation skills, and putting theory into action by practicing new negotiation skills.
MGMT 125.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 126.title: Foundations of Teams
MGMT 126.description: Social and psychological processes that detract from effective teamwork and collaboration. Tools to understand how to be a better team member are introduced. Provides the foundation for students to become effective team leaders and to manage difficult team situations.
MGMT 126.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 127.title: Business Ethics
MGMT 127.description: Comprehensive introduction to ethical considerations in business with a focus on awareness to the complexity of ethical decision-making and how to make choices from a standpoint of ethical consciousness.
MGMT 127.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 128.title: International Management
MGMT 128.description: Impact of different cultures and political/economic systems on assumptions, expectations, and organizational practices relevant to conducting business in different national settings. Understanding of the challenges of cross-national management and resources utilized to work and conduct business outside the United States.
MGMT 128.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 129.title: Leadership
MGMT 129.description: Case analyses, free-form discussion, and written assignments designed to develop critical thinking skills, as well as knowledge of approaches to differing leadership challenges. Experiential exercises encourage students to develop their ability to innovate, foster collaboration, manage conflict, and value diversity.
MGMT 129.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 131A.title: Intermediate Accounting I
MGMT 131A.description: First course in a series of two intermediate-level courses in financial accounting theory and practice. Concepts include the measurement, valuation, and reporting of current and long-term assets, current liabilities, and revenue recognition issues.
MGMT 131A.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 131B.title: Intermediate Accounting II
MGMT 131B.description: Second course in a series of two intermediate-level courses in financial accounting theory and practice. Concepts include the measurement, valuation, and reporting of long-term liabilities and contingencies, accounting for stockholders' equity, and the Statement of Cash Flows.
MGMT 131B.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 131C.title: Intermediate Accounting III
MGMT 131C.description: Third in a three-part series (A, B, and C). Focuses on developing knowledge related to investments, debt/equity issues, accounting for income taxes, pensions, leases, and revenue recognition
MGMT 131C.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 132A.title: Individual Taxation
MGMT 132A.description: Fundamentals of federal income taxation pertaining to individuals. Topics include income, deductions, credits, property transactions, and the impact of taxes on business and investment decisions.
MGMT 132A.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 133.title: Corporate and Partnership Taxation
MGMT 133.description: Fundamentals of federal income taxation pertaining to partnerships and corporations, including subchapter S corporations. Emphasis on the tax issues associated with formation, operation, and termination of these entities.
MGMT 133.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 134.title: Data Analytics in Accounting
MGMT 134.description: Provides students with an understanding of data types and sources and how to apply and leverage analytical techniques in making financial and managerial accounting decisions. Business and ethical issues surrounding the collection and use of Big Data are also discussed.

MGMT 137.title: Advanced Accounting
MGMT 137.description: Covers advanced concepts in accounting theory and practice. Topics include business combinations, consolidated financial statements, foreign exchange transactions, international, and governmental/nonprofit accounting standards.
MGMT 137.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 138.title: Auditing
MGMT 138.description: An introduction to auditing practice with emphasis on the verification of financial statements and related information. Topics include professional ethics, assessment of audit risk, study and evaluation of internal control, gathering and evaluating audit evidence, and audit reporting.
MGMT 138.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 141.title: Investments
MGMT 141.description: Foundations of investment management. Theory and empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, asset pricing models, factor models, and option pricing theory. Students are expected to combine market research results and electronic information sources to create optimal investment strategies.
MGMT 141.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 142.title: Financial Data Analysis and Python Applications
MGMT 142.description: Introduces fundamental methods for financial data analysis and their real-world applications using Python. Integrating statistical concepts, programming, and finance theory, students apply visualization, regression, simulation, and portfolio modeling to investment analysis, trading strategies, performance evaluation, and practical projects.
MGMT 142.restriction: Business Information Management majors and Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 143.title: Bonds and Fixed Income
MGMT 143.description: Provides coverage of topics in fixed income securities. Examines bond pricing and yield calculation, duration and convexity, term structure of interest rates, treasure bond market and corporate debt market. Helps students understand and manage risks of fixed income securities.
MGMT 143.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 144.title: Multinational Finance
MGMT 144.description: Focuses on financial issues facing multinational corporations, the most important of which is the management of foreign exchange risk. Introduction to investments and financing decisions in international capital markets.
MGMT 144.prereq_text: MGMT 109 and (ECON 20A or MGMT 4A) and (ECON 20B or MGMT 4B).
MGMT 144.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 145.title: FinTech
MGMT 145.description: Provides working knowledge of economic mechanisms in areas of FinTech. Identifying and analyzing important issues through a balance of qualitative analysis and quantitative applications. Topics covered include Bitcoin, Blockchain, Crowdfunding, peer-to-peer lending, robo-advisor, and their economic and social impacts.
MGMT 145.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 146A.title: Introduction to the Real Estate Process
MGMT 146A.description: Introductory survey course providing a working knowledge of the real estate market, both residential and commercial. Topics include real estate economics, appraisal, feasibility, investment, tax considerations, financing, and development. Lectures and cases, with supplemental presentations by real estate professionals.
MGMT 146A.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 147.title: Cases in Corporate Financial Management
MGMT 147.description: Case study course designed to confront students with real-world corporate finance problems and provide an active learning experience. Introduces advanced analytical tools/techniques and provides an integrated framework for value-based financial management in a broad range of corporate settings.
MGMT 147.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 148.title: Financial Institutions
MGMT 148.description: Explores different types of financial institutions, their role in the economy, how they are managed, as well as their regulation. Topics include commercial banking, the Fed and monetary policy, risk management, financial regulation, insurance, and investment companies.
MGMT 148.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 149.title: Derivatives
MGMT 149.description: Introduction to financial derivatives. Covers forward contracts, futures, swaps, and options. Applications of these instruments, including pricing and risk management, are emphasized.
MGMT 149.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 150.title: Consumer Behavior
MGMT 150.description: Application of the behavioral sciences to understanding buyer behavior. Topics include perception, memory, affect, learning, persuasion, motivation, behavioral decision theory, social and culture influences, and managerial implications.
MGMT 150.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 151.title: Marketing Research
MGMT 151.description: Research to aid managerial decisions for products and services; problem formulation, research design, data collection, sampling, statistical analyses, managerial recommendations, and implementation in several real-world settings.
MGMT 151.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 153.title: Sales Management
MGMT 153.description: Designed for students interested in learning about sales force management and personal selling by firms engaged in business-to-business and consumer goods/services marketing. Covers advantages of personal selling, how to perform sales calls, challenges of sales managers, roles of buying centers.
MGMT 153.restriction: Business Information Management majors and Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 154.title: Global Marketing
MGMT 154.description: Students are exposed to the challenges and opportunities facing marketers in the international marketplace. Special attention is given to the management of cultural differences in product development, distribution systems, pricing, and promotion.
MGMT 154.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 155.title: Brand Management
MGMT 155.description: Introduction to issues in planning, implementing, and evaluating brand strategies, relevant theories, models, and tools for the making of brand decisions; application of these principles.
MGMT 155.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 156.title: Pricing Strategy
MGMT 156.description: Provides a framework for designing and analyzing pricing strategies. Emphasizes role of pricing in the marketing-mix decisions and broader marketing strategy of a firm. Incorporates study of various economic, psychological, competitive, and organizational foundations that enter into effective pricing decisions.
MGMT 156.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 158.title: Digital Media Marketing Strategy
MGMT 158.description: Entails developing digital marketing strategy across numerous digital marketing platforms; understanding digital native consumers and newer consumer behaviors on the internet, trends in delivering value in the digital age, and how to analyze digital marketing performance.
MGMT 158.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 159.title: Analysis of Marketing Data
MGMT 159.description: Provides opportunity to learn and apply analytical skills to marketing datasets to unveil hidden patterns and truths, to measure and quantify the performance differences between different initiatives, and to inform decision-making in an increasingly digital world.
MGMT 159.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 160.title: Global Impact Leadership
MGMT 160.description: Seeks to address critical issues and reviews how leaders and stakeholders deal with those issues; including the concept of sustainability, “the ability to endure,” and climate change. Addresses “sustainable development.” Explores critical views; pro-business views, skepticism and global warming denial.
MGMT 160.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 161.title: Global Digital Economy
MGMT 161.description: Provides a better understanding of how the digital world is changing the global economic environment and the skills needed to critically assess how it is affecting macroeconomic trends, fluctuations, and the regulatory environment, emphasizing current events and global perspective.
MGMT 161.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 162.title: Managing a Virtual Workforce
MGMT 162.description: Explores strategies for managing virtual teams in global contexts, emphasizing communication, trust, cultural diversity, and technology. Students apply theory through collaborative projects, developing skills for leadership and productivity in digitally driven, geographically dispersed work environments.
MGMT 162.restriction: Business Information Management majors and Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 165.title: U.S. Healthcare Systems
MGMT 165.description: Providers, suppliers, payers, consumers, and the unique market dynamics among these players. Structure, organization, and financing of health care. The health care industry's relationship to the overall economy will be explored.
MGMT 165.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 166.title: Business of Medicine
MGMT 166.description: In order to improve the quality and efficiency of health care delivery one must understand the design and management of health care operations. Opportunities for innovation and changes needed to design a simple, accessible, fair, and effective health care system.
MGMT 166.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 171.title: Social Media
MGMT 171.description: Covers theoretical aspects and business applications of social media tools including blogs, wikis, social networking platforms, immersive environments, and other social computing technologies. Also covers business value of social-media-enabled processes.
MGMT 171.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 172.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
MGMT 172.description: Challenges and teaches students how to handle data that come in a variety of forms and sizes. Guides students through the whole data management process, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis.
MGMT 172.prereq_text: Recommended: Previous experience with programming languages (preferably Python).
MGMT 172.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 173.title: Business Intelligence for Analytical Decisions
MGMT 173.description: BI from both managerial and technical perspectives. Learn to apply a variety of data mining techniques to learn business intelligence embedded in data, and apply that intelligence to run your business more efficiently. These techniques are useful in different areas.
MGMT 173.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 174.title: Business Data Management
MGMT 174.description: Query, manipulate, and understand data and learn about leading edge applications for databases. Database fundamentals including entity relationship design, creating database tables, normalization, and data querying. Contemporary applications of database using case studies. Applications include data warehousing, data mining.
MGMT 174.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 176.title: Digital Strategies
MGMT 176.description: Covers business strategies for firms that make technology products. Insights are applicable not only to industries that make information and technology goods but also to industries that leverage digitization and network effects for their products.
MGMT 176.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 178.title: Management of Information Technology
MGMT 178.description: Strategic use and impact of information technology (IT) in organizations. Covers what IT is, and how it works, business value of IT, and IT strategies that organizations can employ to create value.
MGMT 178.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 182.title: Supply Chain Management
MGMT 182.description: Flows of materials and information among all of the firms that contribute to a product or service. Forecasting, demand management, logistical networks, inventory management, supplier contracting, sourcing, information technology, flexibility, globalization, and performance management.
MGMT 182.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 184.title: Business Process Management
MGMT 184.description: Learn core business functions, processes, and data requirements to support complex interrelationships between procurement, sales, and logistics. Hands-on experience with enterprise resource planning, sales and operations planning, material requirements planning, master scheduling, and aggregate planning.
MGMT 184.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 189.title: Operations Management
MGMT 189.description: Managing the productive resources, from which raw materials as inputs are being transformed into useful outputs of final products and services. Explanation of issues pertaining to both manufacturing and services-oriented systems.
MGMT 189.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 190.title: Special Topics in Management
MGMT 190.description: Studies in selected areas of management. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
MGMT 190.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 191W.title: Business Communication
MGMT 191W.description: Provides students with a solid foundation in business communication. Emphasis is placed on improving students' written and oral communication skills to help them succeed in (1) upper-division Business Administration courses, (2) graduate school, and (3) work and career activities.
MGMT 191W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

MGMT 192.title: Business Law
MGMT 192.description: A study of the legal environment of business. Topics include contracts, agency, partnerships, corporations, and other basic principles of law as they relate to business transactions.
MGMT 192.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 194.title: Financial Statement Analysis
MGMT 194.description: Study of financial statements and their related footnotes; tools and procedures common to financial statement analysis; relationships among business transactions, environmental forces (political, economic, social), and reported financial statement information; how financial statement information can help solve certain business problems.
MGMT 194.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 195.title: Experiential Development of a Global Business Perspective
MGMT 195.description: Opportunity for students to consider historical and modern global businesses, governmental, and non-profit operations in Switzerland. Effectively provides live case studies for analysis of global interrelatedness. Materials Fee
MGMT 195.restriction: Business Administration majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 196.title: Decision Analysis
MGMT 196.description: Use of decision analysis digital technologies for multiple objective decisions under certainty; decision-making under risk using decision trees; fitting probability distributions to judgments or data; and Monte Carlo simulation, applied to business, government, not-for-profit, and personal decisions.
MGMT 196.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 197.title: Predictive Analytics
MGMT 197.description: Addresses prediction and classification problems in the management context via statistical learning. Provides an overview of modern methodologies in forecasting and data mining including multiple regression, decision trees, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor, support vector machines, and neural nets.
MGMT 197.restriction: Business Administration majors and Business Information Management majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MGMT 198A.title: Administrative Internship
MGMT 198A.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.

MGMT 198B.title: Administrative Internship
MGMT 198B.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.

MGMT 198C.title: Administrative Internship
MGMT 198C.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.

MGMT 199.title: Independent Study
MGMT 199.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.

MGMT EP 200.title: Thinking Strategically in the Digital Age for Executives
MGMT EP 200.description: Focuses on the strategic and organizational challenges that a rapidly changing environment poses to the firm’s management and frames them according to Merage’s strategic emphasis on analytical decision making, innovation, and information technology.

MGMT EP 201A.title: Business Analytics: Decision-Making for Executives
MGMT EP 201A.description: Methods of statistical inference, emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Topics include classical estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, decision analysis, and forecasting.

MGMT EP 202.title: Organizational Leadership for Executives
MGMT EP 202.description: Develops a better understanding of individual and group behavior in and across organizations, and the frameworks by which to analyze and understand behavior in complex organizations. Enhances the skills required to manage collaboration and lead. Every other weekend course.

MGMT EP 203A.title: Financial Reporting Policies for Executives
MGMT EP 203A.description: Involves the development, analysis, and interpretation of financial accounting information for external reporting purposes. Emphasis on measurement and valuation issues in decision-making problems and cases. Every other weekend course format.

MGMT EP 203B.title: Managerial Accounting for Executives
MGMT EP 203B.description: Involves developing and using internal financial and non-financial information to help organizations make planning, budgeting, control, operating, and performance evaluation decisions. Every other weekend course format.
MGMT EP 203B.prereq_text: MGMT EP 203A with a minimum grade of B-.
MGMT EP 203B.restriction: School of Business students and Master of Business Administration only.

MGMT EP 204A.title: Microeconomics for Executives in the Digital Age
MGMT EP 204A.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions of consumers and firms. Topics include demand and supply analysis, production and cost theory, perfect competition, monopoly, market failures, and introductory game theory. Every other weekend course format.

MGMT EP 205.title: Marketing Leadership
MGMT EP 205.description: Introduction to marketing. Topics include developing familiarity with fundamental marketing concepts, theories, and techniques; acquainting students with the type of decisions made by executives, including customer targeting, product, pricing, place, promotion, and research. Every other weekend course format.

MGMT EP 207.title: AI for Executives: Technology, Analytics, and Organizations
MGMT EP 207.description: Focuses on how information technology is used to create value in organizations through product, process, and strategy innovation. Aims to help managers understand the strategic role of key information technologies in managing organizations. Every other weekend course format.

MGMT EP 208.title: Operational Excellence: Processes, Strategy, and Analytics
MGMT EP 208.description: Introduction to strategic and tactical issues in production and operations management. A blend of quantitative and qualitative considerations. Topics include product planning, process design, capacity management, production planning, inventory control, just-in-time manufacturing, and quality management. Every other weekend course format.

MGMT EP 209A.title: Managerial Finance for Executives
MGMT EP 209A.description: Introduces students to financial theory and concepts. Topics include time value of money, valuation of stocks and bonds, capital budgeting, portfolio theory, and capital structure choice. Every other weekend course format.
MGMT EP 209A.prereq_text: MGMT EP 201A with a minimum grade of B- and MGMT EP 203A with a minimum grade of B- and MGMT EP 204A with a minimum grade of B-.

MGMT EP 210.title: Strategy for Executives: Foundations and Dynamics
MGMT EP 210.description: Provides conceptual frameworks and techniques to analyze and develop firm strategies. Through case analysis/discussion, helps improve strategic thinking by developing frameworks by which to assess, evaluate, and respond to different business situations. Every other weekend course format.

MGMT FE 204A.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions, the determinants and consequences of market structure and market failure. MGMT FE 207.title: AI for Managers: Technology, Analytics, and Organizations
MGMT FE 207.description: Focuses on the technological and managerial issues surrounding the development and use of IT in organizations.
