MUSIC 147.description: Specialized topics in electronic music, computer-aided music, and other aspects of music technology.

MUSIC 148.title: Studies in Ethnomusicology
MUSIC 148.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 149.title: Studies in Music History
MUSIC 149.description: Specialized topics in musical genres; culture and social issues; performance practices; and interrelated arts.
MUSIC 149.prereq_text: MUSIC 39A and MUSIC 39B. Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement.
MUSIC 149.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 150.title: Composition
MUSIC 150.description: Exercises and projects for diverse instrumental-vocal combinations; contemporary techniques and problems. Participation in the improvisation ensemble and working with electronic media.
MUSIC 150.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 151.title: Computer Music Composition
MUSIC 151.description: Exercises in the composition of music uniquely possible by computer, including digital signal processing, computer control of synthesizers and processors, and algorithmic composition. Demonstrations and musical analyses in class; considerable studio work outside class.

MUSIC 153.title: Counterpoint
MUSIC 153.description: Studies in contrapuntal practices of various style periods such as the 16th, 18th, and 20th centuries.
MUSIC 153.prereq_text: MUSIC 16B with a minimum grade of C-.
MUSIC 153.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 155.title: Analysis
MUSIC 155.description: Methods of formal analysis applicable to all Western musical styles: additive, continuous, transformational, and hierarchic forms; rhythm, texture, and sonority as form and process.
MUSIC 155.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 156A.title: Song Literature
MUSIC 156A.description: A survey of song literature. Designed as an overview of the song repertoire, German Lieder.
MUSIC 156A.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 156B.title: Song Literature
MUSIC 156B.description: A survey of song literature. Designed as an overview of the song repertoire, French mélodie.
MUSIC 156B.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 157.title: Advanced Study in Composition
MUSIC 157.prereq_text: MUSIC 150 with a minimum grade of C-.
MUSIC 157.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 158A.title: Diction
MUSIC 158A.description: In-depth study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), including its transcription and pronunciation, and its application for singers. Introduction to IPA and Italian diction.
MUSIC 158A.restriction: Music - Performance majors and Music majors only.

MUSIC 158B.title: Diction
MUSIC 158B.description: In-depth study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), including its transcription and pronunciation, and its application for singers. German diction.
MUSIC 158B.restriction: Music - Performance majors and Music majors only.

MUSIC 158C.title: Diction
MUSIC 158C.description: In-depth study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), including its transcription and pronunciation, and its application for singers. French Diction.
MUSIC 158C.restriction: Music - Performance majors and Music majors only.

MUSIC 160.title: University Orchestra
MUSIC 160.description: Study and performance of standard orchestral repertory and works by contemporary composers. Membership is open to all qualified students by audition only.

MUSIC 161.title: Wind Ensemble
MUSIC 161.description: Study and performance of works written for varying combinations of wind and percussion instruments. Membership is open to all qualified students by audition only.

MUSIC 162.title: University Chorus
MUSIC 162.description: Make-up of the ensembles varies and may include University Chorus, Chamber Choir, Madrigal Singers, Women's Chorus, and Reading Choir. Membership is open to all students.

MUSIC 162P.title: University Chorus: Accompanying
MUSIC 162P.description: Keyboard accompanying for one of the UCI choral organizations, with individual coaching in sight reading, score reading, and other accompanying skills.

MUSIC 164.title: Opera Workshop
MUSIC 164.description: Preparation and performance of operatic repertoire, including arias, scenes, and fully staged operas, and/or stage training and role analysis.
MUSIC 164.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 164P.title: Opera Workshop: Accompanying
MUSIC 164P.description: Training in techniques and operatic repertory for keyboard players.

MUSIC 166P.title: String Accompaniment
MUSIC 166P.description: Chamber ensemble experience with the solo string repertory for keyboard, participation in the weekly string master class, performance in public recitals.

MUSIC 170.title: Guitar, Lute, and Other Plucked Instruments for Music Performance Majors
MUSIC 170.description: Private weekly lessons and a weekly master class/workshop for the discussion of solo repertory and performance practice, including special topics such as historical notational systems, traditional American guitar styles, and demonstrations of period plucked instruments. Materials Fee

MUSIC 171.title: Chamber Singers
MUSIC 171.description: A select ensemble specializing in vocal chamber music from all periods. Frequent performances on and off campus. Membership is open to all singers by audition. Materials Fee

MUSIC 176.title: Chamber Ensembles
MUSIC 176.description: Make-up of the ensembles varies and may include various Classical ensembles, Latin Jazz Ensemble, Small Jazz Combos, Percussion Ensemble, and Guitar Ensemble. Membership is open to all qualified students by audition only.
MUSIC 176.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MUSIC 178.title: Jazz Orchestra
MUSIC 178.description: Rehearsal and performance of literature written for large jazz ensemble with emphasis on methods and materials. Laboratory setting for new arrangers and/or composers of modern jazz pieces.

MUSIC 181.title: Improvisation
MUSIC 181.description: Improvisation has been central to all music traditions. Course explores real-time music-making in a variety of non-notated contexts. Different improvisational styles are presented, including jazz, Asian improvisation, and experimental modern music. Emphasis on actual classroom performance.
MUSIC 181.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 182.title: Advanced Jazz Combo
MUSIC 182.description: Small-group jazz ensemble and improvisational workshop. Range of music covered encompasses the full traditional jazz from improvised ragtime up through the most current avant-garde musical techniques.

MUSIC 183A.title: Jazz Composition I
MUSIC 183A.description: Performance and lecture course for writing and performing original jazz compositions. Emphasis is placed on composing as a way to create new improvisational frameworks. Cyclical forms, modal compositions, blues-oriented compositions, and ballad writing.

MUSIC 183B.title: Jazz Composition II
MUSIC 183B.description: Performance and lecture course for writing and performing original jazz compositions. Emphasis is placed on composing as a way to create new improvisational frameworks. Non-functional harmony, contemporary forms, free-bop, and current trends.

MUSIC 183C.title: Jazz Composition III
MUSIC 183C.description: Performance and lecture course for writing and performing original jazz compositions. Emphasis is placed on composing as a way to create new improvisational frameworks. Study of modern tonal-center compositions, intervallic compositions, and alternate rhythms.
MUSIC 183C.prereq_text: MUSIC 78 and MUSIC 132 and MUSIC 183A and MUSIC 183B.

MUSIC 186.title: Integrated Composition, Improvisation, and Technology Workshop
MUSIC 186.description: A practice-based course in which students create original musical works through composition, improvisation, and/or technology, both individually and collaboratively.
MUSIC 186.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

MUSIC 189.title: Accompanying for Plucked Strings: Continuo and Changes
MUSIC 189.description: Students apply theory to their instruments as they learn the basics of pre-1800 continuo playing and post-1900 jazz charts. Includes discussions of appropriate repertory, treatment of harmonic progressions, and finer points of style and technique.
MUSIC 189.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 191.title: Tutorial in Music
MUSIC 191.description: Supplemental instruction related to student's area of study. Taken only when the materials studied lie outside regular departmental offerings, and when the student has no formal chance to pursue the subject.

MUSIC 193.title: Conducting
MUSIC 193.description: Introduces students to the basic techniques employed in the practice of conducting and includes score study and development of leadership skills.
MUSIC 193.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 195A.title: Senior Thesis
MUSIC 195A.description: With consultation in regularly scheduled meetings, students identify and study relevant texts and materials and prepare a prospectus for an original thesis.
MUSIC 195A.prereq_text: Senior standing in the Honors Program in Music and Culture.
MUSIC 195A.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 195B.title: Senior Thesis
MUSIC 195B.description: Students submit an outline and preliminary drafts of section of their thesis to the instructor, on a schedule supervised by the instructor. The final version will address the instructor's comments and criticisms.
MUSIC 195B.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 197.title: Word and Music
MUSIC 197.description: Performance class for advanced singers and pianists with emphasis on collaborative approach to vocal literature.
MUSIC 197.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 199.title: Independent Study
MUSIC 199.description: Student-devised research/composition project, with faculty guidance, resulting in a formal paper/project. Taken only when materials studied lie outside regular departmental offerings or when students have no formal chance to pursue the subject.
MUSIC 199.prereq_text: Undergraduate or graduate advisor approval required.
MUSIC 199.restriction: Music majors and Music - Performance majors only.

MUSIC 200.title: Bibliography and Research
MUSIC 200.description: Required of all entering students. A systematic introduction to the bibliographical tools both in the general field of music and in the student's areas of specialization.

MUSIC 202.title: Proseminar in Musicology
MUSIC 202.description: Introduces significant issues and recent developments in musicology and music criticism, including exposure to the controversies that have brought change and reflection to the discipline.
MUSIC 202.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 203.title: Music Thesis
MUSIC 203.description: Intensive work dedicated to researching and writing a Master's thesis under the supervision of a faculty advisor.
MUSIC 203.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 204.title: Proseminar in Music Theory and Analysis
MUSIC 204.description: Introduction to music theories, analytic approaches, and methodologies as applied to repertories drawn from Western art and popular music.
MUSIC 204.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 209.title: Seminar in Creative Practices
MUSIC 209.description: Core first-year seminar required for graduate students in the Integrated Composition, Improvisation, and Technology emphasis of the M.A. and Ph.D. programs. Composition and presentation of original student works, lecture, and discussion.

MUSIC 210.title: Choral Conducting
MUSIC 210.description: Intensive private instruction and study of the various choral literatures.

MUSIC 211.title: Performance
MUSIC 211.description: Contents vary according to the student's major instrument. Intensive private instruction and study of the various literatures.

MUSIC 212.title: Composition
MUSIC 212.description: Intensive work in composition geared to each student's level of competence.

MUSIC 215A.title: Computer Music Composition and Production
MUSIC 215A.description: Study of the composition and production of music made uniquely possible by the computer, including usage of prevalent digital music technology, techniques of digital signal processing, and computer control of synthesizers and audio processors.

MUSIC 222.title: Seminar in Musicology
MUSIC 222.description: Focuses on current scholarship in musicology and related fields with a strong critical content. Addresses topics relative to their historical and stylistic periods. Recent topics have included Stravinsky, Holy Women, Mahler, Historiography, Issues in Performance Practice, and Brahms’s Chamber Music.
MUSIC 222.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 224.title: Seminar in Music Theory and Analysis
MUSIC 224.description: Typical topics include Schenkerian theory and analysis, contemporary form theory, and advanced techniques in the analysis of late 19th-century and contemporary music (e.g., transformational theory, Neo-Riemannian, and scale network theory).
MUSIC 224.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 231.title: Improvisation
MUSIC 231.description: Introduces the practice and history of improvisation in diverse fields of Western music since 1950. Performance projects and group critiques, weekly reading and listening assignments, participation in a class concert, and a research paper.

MUSIC 235.title: Critical Studies in Music
MUSIC 235.description: A critical examination of music traditions, institutions, and aesthetics, employing new scholarship in music and new critical studies in other disciplines.
MUSIC 235.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 236.title: Theoretical ICIT Seminar
MUSIC 236.description: Seminar studying new genres and topics that integrate composition, improvisation, new technologies, and non-classical cultures.

MUSIC 237.title: Practical ICIT Seminar
MUSIC 237.description: Study of new practices and techniques that integrate composition, improvisation, new technologies, and non-classical cultures.

MUSIC 239.title: Thesis Colloquium
MUSIC 239.description: ICIT students present their thesis work-in-progress for discussion and criticism. Faculty and visiting artists/scholars also present their current work.

MUSIC 240.title: Graduate Projects
MUSIC 240.description: Substantial projects in performance, conducting, or composition (other than those specifically required for the degree), accompanied by a summary paper.

MUSIC 242A.title: First-Year Research and Writing Seminar I
MUSIC 242A.description: Guided reading for one quarter on a broad subject selected by the instructor, followed by one quarter in which the student undertakes independent research on the selected topic, leading to a substantial term paper.
MUSIC 242A.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 242B.title: First-Year Research and Writing Seminar II
MUSIC 242B.description: Guided reading for one quarter on a broad subject selected by the instructor, followed by one quarter in which the student undertakes independent research on the selected topic, leading to a substantial term paper.
MUSIC 242B.prereq_text: MUSIC 200 with a minimum grade of B and MUSIC 242A with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 243A.title: Second-Year Research and Writing Tutorial I
MUSIC 243A.description: In this two-quarter sequence, students gain expertise in a first area of research concentration by undertaking directed reading on a topic of their choice and then writing a paper of near-publishable length and quality on that topic.
MUSIC 243A.prereq_text: MUSIC 242B with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 243B.title: Second-Year Research and Writing Tutorial II
MUSIC 243B.description: In this two-quarter sequence, students gain expertise in a first area of research concentration by undertaking directed reading on a topic of their choice and then writing a paper of near-publishable length and quality on that topic.
MUSIC 243B.prereq_text: MUSIC 243A with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 244.title: Readings for the Qualifying Examination
MUSIC 244.description: Directed reading in preparation for the Qualifying Examination.
MUSIC 244.prereq_text: MUSIC 243B with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 245.title: Prospectus Research
MUSIC 245.description: Research and writing of the Dissertation Prospectus.
MUSIC 245.prereq_text: MUSIC 244 with a minimum grade of B.

MUSIC 250.title: Directed Research
MUSIC 250.description: Preparation for qualifying exams in ICIT or an individual research project, resulting in a substantial paper or comparable documentation of the research results.

MUSIC 276.title: Contemporary Ensemble
MUSIC 276.description: Chamber ensemble for the performance of contemporary music, including newly composed and improvised forms.

MUSIC 290.title: Dissertation Research
MUSIC 290.description: Research and writing of a Ph.D. dissertation.

MUSIC 299.title: Independent Study
MUSIC 299.description: Student-devised research/composition project, with faculty guidance, resulting in a formal paper/project. Taken only when materials studied lie outside regular departmental offerings or when students have no formal chance to pursue the subject.

NET SYS 201.title: Computer and Communication Networks
NET SYS 201.description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.

NET SYS 202.title: Networking Laboratory
NET SYS 202.description: A laboratory-based introduction to basic networking concepts such as addressing, sub-netting, bridging, ARP, and routing. Network simulation and design. Structured around weekly readings and laboratory assignments.

NET SYS 210.title: Advanced Networks
NET SYS 210.description: Design principles of networked systems, advanced routing and congestion control algorithms, network algorithms, network measurement, management, security, Internet economics, and emerging networks.
NET SYS 210.prereq_text: NET SYS 201 with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 232 with a minimum grade of B- or EECS 248A with a minimum grade of B-.

NET SYS 230.title: Wireless and Mobile Networking
NET SYS 230.description: Introduction to wireless networking. The focus is on layers 2 and 3 of the OSI reference model, design, performance analysis, and protocols. Topics covered include: an introduction to wireless networking, digital cellular, next generation cellular, wireless LANs, and mobile IP.

NET SYS 240.title: Network and Distributed Systems Security
NET SYS 240.description: Modern computer and networks security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Group communication and multicast security techniques. Covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.

NET SYS 260.title: Middleware for Networked and Distributed Systems
NET SYS 260.description: Discusses concepts, techniques, and issues in developing distributed systems middleware that provides high performance and Quality of Service for emerging applications. Also covers existing standards (e.g., CORBA, DCOM, Jini, Espeak) and their relative advantages and shortcomings.
NET SYS 260.prereq_text: An undergraduate-level course in operating systems and networks.

NET SYS 295.title: Networked Systems Seminar
NET SYS 295.description: Current research in networked systems. Includes talks by UCI faculty, visiting researchers, and Networked Systems graduate students.

NEURBIO 200A.title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
NEURBIO 200A.description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.

NEURBIO 200B.title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
NEURBIO 200B.description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
NEURBIO 200B.prereq_text: NEURBIO 200A with a minimum grade of B-.

NEURBIO 200C.title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
NEURBIO 200C.description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
NEURBIO 200C.prereq_text: NEURBIO 200B with a minimum grade of B-.

NEURBIO 201A.title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
NEURBIO 201A.description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.

NEURBIO 201B.title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
NEURBIO 201B.description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
NEURBIO 201B.prereq_text: NEURBIO 201A with a minimum grade of B-.

NEURBIO 201C.title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
NEURBIO 201C.description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
NEURBIO 201C.prereq_text: NEURBIO 201B with a minimum grade of B-.

NEURBIO 202A.title: Foundations of Neuroscience
NEURBIO 202A.description: Intended to expose students to critical reading and analysis of the primary neuroscience literature. Instructors from departments associated with the Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program participate and discuss topics of current interest.

NEURBIO 202B.title: Foundations of Neuroscience
NEURBIO 202B.description: Intended to expose students to critical reading and analysis of the primary neuroscience literature. Instructors from departments associated with the Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program participate and discuss topics of current interest.
NEURBIO 202B.prereq_text: NEURBIO 202A with a minimum grade of B-.

NEURBIO 206.title: Molecular Neuroscience
NEURBIO 206.description: Surveys molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in neuronal function, including control of gene expression, post-transcriptional and post-translational processing, RNA and protein targeting, cell death mechanisms, and molecular genetic basis of neurological disorders. Overview of the molecular aspects of developmental neurobiology.

NEURBIO 207.title: Cellular Neuroscience
NEURBIO 207.description: Neurophysiological and neurochemical mechanisms of electrical and chemical signaling in neurons. Topics include generation of resting- and action-potentials, voltage- and ligand-gated ion channels, second messenger systems, and synaptic transmission and integration.

NEURBIO 208.title: Systems Neuroscience
NEURBIO 208.description: Study of the mammalian nervous system at the systems level. Anatomy and physiology of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.

NEURBIO 209.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
NEURBIO 209.description: Overview of fundamental conceptual and experimental issues in the neurobiology of learning and memory. The approach is a cross-level integration of research in molecular-genetic, cellular, circuit, systems, and behavioral analyses.

NEURBIO 217.title: Foundations in Neuroimmunology II
NEURBIO 217.description: The immune system supports normal brain development as well as controls central nervous system (CNS) infection, and neurodegenerative and neurological diseases. Assesses how the immune system contributes to both host defense and disease.
NEURBIO 217.prereq_text: Undergraduate- or graduate-level immunology experience is required.

NEURBIO 220.title: Neural Coding, Computation, and Dynamics
NEURBIO 220.description: Theoretical principles and biological mechanisms underlying how brains acquire, assimilate, store, and retrieve information, compute adaptive responses to external inputs, and how knowledge is extracted from experience to generate an internal model of the world.
NEURBIO 220.prereq_text: At least one upper-division course in the field of Neuroscience or one upper-division course in Cognitive Science or Machine Learning.

NEURBIO 227.title: Bioinformatics and Systems Biology
NEURBIO 227.description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics, genomic approaches, and Linux and R program in order to analyze RNA-sequencing data.

NEURBIO 230.title: Epigenetics in Health and Disease
NEURBIO 230.description: Focuses on the role of chromatin/nuclear structure organization (histone and DNA modification, chromatin remodeling, higher order chromatin structure and nuclear organization) on gene regulation, DNA replication and repair, relevant to development, metabolism, learning and memory, and human disease.
NEURBIO 230.prereq_text: MOL BIO 203 with a minimum grade of B- or MOL BIO 204 with a minimum grade of B- or NEURBIO 206 with a minimum grade of B-.

NEURBIO 233.title: Neurobiology of Drug Addiction
NEURBIO 233.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of topics in the addiction field, including drug pharmacology, models/approaches to investigate addiction, brain circuits, genetics, epigenetics, and the cellular and molecular biology of drug addiction.

NEURBIO 236.title: Cortex: Structure, Function, and Plasticity
NEURBIO 236.description: Structured to include lectures and presentation of papers about cortex with emphasis on sensory-motor cortex. Both historical and current perspectives on cortical structure-function relationship are critically evaluated.

NEURBIO 237.title: Neurobiology of Aging and Alzheimer's Disease
NEURBIO 237.description: Outlines changes occurring in aging and Alzheimer’s disease, and clinical manifestations of those changes. Emphasis on genetic and lifestyle risk factors, molecular mechanisms that are basis for detrimental and protective responses, diagnosis, and developing therapies for aging and Alzheimer's disease.
NEURBIO 237.prereq_text: NEURBIO 209 with a minimum grade of B-.

NEURBIO 239.title: Functional Imaging of the Nervous System
NEURBIO 239.description: Overview of technical and applied aspects of imaging techniques available for studying the nervous system. The areas emphasized are cellular and subcellular imaging of neural function, systems-level imaging of brain function, and imaging of the human brain.

NEURBIO 240.title: Advanced Analysis of Learning and Memory
NEURBIO 240.description: Advanced analysis of contemporary research concerning the nature and neurobiological bases of learning and memory. Special emphasis is given to time-dependent processes involved in memory storage.

NEURBIO 247.title: Programming for Neuroscience Research
NEURBIO 247.description: A neuroscience-specific introduction to programming and data analysis using either MATLAB or Scientific PYTHON. Students will learn general programming skills and effective use of programming for data management, statistical analysis, and image analysis.

NEURBIO 257.title: Statistics and Experimental Design
NEURBIO 257.description: Introduction to common methods for statistical analysis used in neurobiology. Topics covered include t-tests, ANOVAs, correlations and regressions, general linear model, power analysis, and non-parametric tests.

NEURBIO 260.title: Auditory Neuroscience
NEURBIO 260.description: Multidisciplinary overview of brain mechanisms of hearing. Emphasizes breadth of auditory function and research: single neurons to psychoacoustics, the chochlea to the cortex, and basic science to clinic.

NEURBIO 290.title: Colloquium in Neurobiology and Behavior
NEURBIO 290.description: Presentation of contemporary research problems in neurobiology and behavior and related areas by invited speakers.

NEURBIO 291.title: Neuroscience Journal Club
NEURBIO 291.description: Covers emerging topics in addiction neuroscience research in a journal club format. Students discuss recent articles and may present an article of their choosing. Students gain skills in critical thinking and scientific communication.

NEURBIO 292.title: Scientific Proposals for Neuroscience Trainees
NEURBIO 292.description: Students learn how to effectively communicate scientific ideas and results. Activities include learning how to effectively write a scientific proposal, how to perform a coherent, persuasive slide presentation, and how to give meaningful, constructive review critiques.

NUR SCI 50.title: Nutrition Across the Lifespan
NUR SCI 50.description: Focuses on the relationship between diet and health, and how the human body responds to different diets and food components. Emphasizes how diet interacts with activity and the impact of exercise or sedentary lifestyle on health.
NUR SCI 50.restriction: Nursing Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

NUR SCI 90.title: Introduction to Pain Medicine
NUR SCI 90.description: Gives students introductory knowledge in pain medicine.

NUR SCI 92.title: Compassion in Health Care
NUR SCI 92.description: An overview of the importance of compassion in health care, providing examples from a variety of health care professions through lectures and discussion.

NUR SCI 101.title: Introduction to Nursing Informatics
NUR SCI 101.description: Covers topics relevant to evidence-based practice; nursing informatics as a specialty; electronic health records and clinical informatics; clinical decision support and decision analysis; using informatics to promote community/population health; telenursing and remote access telehealth; and ethical issues in nursing informatics.

NUR SCI 108W.title: Frameworks for Professional Nursing Practice
NUR SCI 108W.description: Conceptual frameworks for professional practice. Scope of professional nursing, jurisprudence and ethics, professional interpersonal relationships, and health care delivery systems in the context of the social, political, and economic environments. Socialization of the student for professional roles in nursing.
NUR SCI 108W.prereq_text: BIO SCI D170 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120L with a minimum grade of C and BIO SCI M115 with a minimum grade of C. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

NUR SCI 109A.title: Physical Assessment
NUR SCI 109A.description: Development of skills in communication, interviewing, functional and physical health assessment across the life-span, the art and science of human care, and clinical judgment. Provides in-depth introductory review/synthesis of physical assessment skills and knowledge covering the life-span. Materials Fee
NUR SCI 109A.prereq_text: BIO SCI M115 with a minimum grade of C and BIO SCI D170 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120L with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 109B.title: Nursing Skills
NUR SCI 109B.description: Provides an in-depth introductory review and synthesis of physical assessment skills covering the lifespan, application of the nursing process, nursing interventions, nursing evaluations, patient care management, and the development of critical thinking in nursing practice.
NUR SCI 109B.prereq_text: NUR SCI 109A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 108W with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 119 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 116.title: Human Growth and Development through the Lifespan
NUR SCI 116.description: Examines theories and concepts of typical human development throughout the life cycle, from the time of conception through adulthood, and familiarizes students with the many forces that shape individual development, including family, society, and culture.
NUR SCI 116.prereq_text: COGS 7A with a minimum grade of C or PSCI 9 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 117.title: Applied Pharmacology
NUR SCI 117.description: Presents principles of pharmacology applied to interventions in pathophysiologic states across the life span. Discussion of the major drug groups with implications for monitoring, drug administration, toxicity, and patient education are included.
NUR SCI 117.prereq_text: NUR SCI 108W with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 109A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 119 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 119.title: Pathophysiology
NUR SCI 119.description: Presents content on pathologic alterations in physiologic processes in cells, tissues, organs, and systems across the life span. Emphasis on critical thinking, application of concepts to clinical practice, and related research.
NUR SCI 119.prereq_text: BIO SCI M115 with a minimum grade of C and BIO SCI D170 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120L with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 121A.title: Medical Surgical Nursing I
NUR SCI 121A.description: Introduction to medical surgical nursing application focused on the older adult population. Students assess, interpret, and provide priority nursing interventions with an emphasis the unique factors influencing nursing management of older adults.
NUR SCI 121A.prereq_text: NUR SCI 108W with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 109A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 119 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 121B.title: Medical Surgical Nursing II
NUR SCI 121B.description: Examines nursing assessment and advanced nursing management for acute and chronic health problems within the inpatient hospital setting. Emphasizes assessment, health history, diagnostic reasoning and nursing prioritization of care in medically complicated patients.
NUR SCI 121B.prereq_text: NUR SCI 109B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 117 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121A with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 125.title: Research Methods and Applications in Health Care
NUR SCI 125.description: Foundational concepts of research in health care. Emphasizes critical evaluation and interpretation of research for application in practice.
NUR SCI 125.prereq_text: STATS 7 with a minimum grade of C or STATS 8 with a minimum grade of C or SOCIOL 10A with a minimum grade of C or SOC SCI 10A with a minimum grade of C or COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C. Satisfactory completion of Lower-Division Writing requirement is recommended.

NUR SCI 128.title: Human Behavior and Mental Health Care
NUR SCI 128.description: Biopsychosocial and cultural influences on promotion and restoration of mental health in adults and adolescents. Assessment, classification, and care of clients with mental health problems and/or substance abuse. Concurrent practicum in adult/adolescent inpatient psychiatric units and outpatient mental health clinics.
NUR SCI 128.prereq_text: NUR SCI 109B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 117 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121A with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 133.title: Complementary and Integrative Health
NUR SCI 133.description: Complementary and integrative healthcare emphasized a holistic, patient-focused approach to healthcare and wellness. Key research is critically evaluated and applications for improving patient care emphasized. Knowledge and skills are developed through lectures, guest speakers, and discussion.

NUR SCI 144.title: Personal and Social Resilience in the Age of the Climate Crisis
NUR SCI 144.description: In our rapidly changing world, many climate and other interrelated global crises are undermining human well-being. Students gain invaluable personal and social resilience skills (e.g., mindfulness), and implement collaborative high impact projects to navigate and build a meaningful future.

NUR SCI 171.title: Community-Based Health Care
NUR SCI 171.description: Epidemiology, primary health care promotion, and disease prevention applied to nursing care of individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes sociocultural, political, economic, and environmental influences. Concepts and methods of assessing populations and communities incorporated in concurrent practicum.
NUR SCI 171.prereq_text: NUR SCI 174 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 176 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 179AW with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 172.title: Pediatrics: Care of Children and Families
NUR SCI 172.description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of infants, children, and adolescents with acute, chronic and/or life-threatening conditions. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.
NUR SCI 172.prereq_text: NUR SCI 101 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 116 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 128 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 173.title: Maternity and Women’s Health Care
NUR SCI 173.description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of women’s wellness across the lifespan, the childbirth process, and newborn care. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.
NUR SCI 173.prereq_text: NUR SCI 101 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 116 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 128 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 174.title: Critical and Specialty Health Care
NUR SCI 174.description: Delivery of patient-centered care for individuals with life-threatening alterations in health status utilizing technology and pharmacology for life support. Concurrent practicum in critical care units emphasizes collaboration, team work, and quality improvement in safe care delivery.
NUR SCI 174.prereq_text: NUR SCI 172 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 173 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 175.title: Clinical Preceptorship
NUR SCI 175.description: Focuses on in-depth clinical nursing practice and preparation for transition to independent practice. Students are mentored by a preceptor who is an expert clinician in the clinical area and guided through critical thinking and clinical decision-making exercises.
NUR SCI 175.prereq_text: NUR SCI 174 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 176 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 179AW with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 176.title: Leadership and Management in Health Care
NUR SCI 176.description: Principles, concepts, and theories related to organizations, management, leadership, decision-making, and group process applied to the delivery of health care. The professional nurse using evidenced-based practice, collaboration, and informatics is incorporated in concurrent practicum emphasizing safe patient care delivery.
NUR SCI 176.prereq_text: NUR SCI 172 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 173 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 179AW.title: Scholarly Concentration I
NUR SCI 179AW.description: Focuses on analysis and use of evidence to improve nursing practice. Emphasis is to develop critical analysis skills synthesizing a body of research evidence for clinical issues on a formal, collaborative written paper.
NUR SCI 179AW.prereq_text: NUR SCI 172 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 173 with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 179B.title: Scholarly Concentration II
NUR SCI 179B.description: Continuation of evidence-based research and application for nursing practice. Emphasis is to develop a collaborative quality improvement project with clinical nurses applying the evidence to improve nursing practice.
NUR SCI 179B.prereq_text: NUR SCI 174 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 176 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 179AW with a minimum grade of C.

NUR SCI 199.title: Independent Study in Nursing Science
NUR SCI 199.description: Original research with Nursing Science faculty.

NUR SCI 200.title: Research Methods and Evaluation for Evidence-Based Practice
NUR SCI 200.description: Equips students with the essential knowledge and skills to understand, apply, and synthesize clinical research, relevant to nursing and health promotion.

NUR SCI 201.title: Introduction to Nursing Informatics
NUR SCI 201.description: Covers topics relevant to evidence-based practice, nursing informatics as a specialty, electronic health records and clinical informatics, clinical decision support and decision analysis, using informatics to promote community/population health, telenursing and remote access telehealth, and ethical issues in nursing informatics.

NUR SCI 202.title: Compassion, Communication, and Care of Underserved Populations
NUR SCI 202.description: Addresses the root causes of health disparities experienced by underserved at-risk populations (e.g., the homeless, people of color, victims of violence) using a historical, sociocultural, behavioral, and personal lens.

NUR SCI 208.title: Frameworks for Professional Nursing Practice
NUR SCI 208.description: Focuses on the scope and standards of professional nursing practice. Topics address the professional, political, and economic contexts of nursing practice, with an emphasis on jurisprudence and ethics, professional interpersonal relationships, and nursing’s role in the care delivery system.

NUR SCI 209A.title: Physical Assessment
NUR SCI 209A.description: Focuses on the development of skills in therapeutic communication, interviewing, functional assessment across the lifespan, the art and science of human care, and clinical judgment. Materials Fee
NUR SCI 209A.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 209B.title: Nursing Skills
NUR SCI 209B.description: Focuses on the development of skills in therapeutic communication, interviewing, functional assessment across the lifespan, the art and science of human care, and clinical judgment.
NUR SCI 209B.prereq_text: NUR SCI 202 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 208 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 209A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 219 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 209B.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 211.title: Ph.D. Seminar: Nursing and Interdisciplinary Research to Improve Human Health
NUR SCI 211.description: Students learn from interdisciplinary scientists about aspects of applied health-related research. Students are introduced to new paradigms, theories, approaches, and analytical methods in health-related research. Ph.D. Nursing Science students and Ph.D. students in other disciplines are encouraged.

NUR SCI 212.title: Philosophy, Science, and Nursing: Comparisons and Critiques
NUR SCI 212.description: Development of philosophy and science in relation to nursing science, scholarship, and practice; emphasis on inquiry, scientific reasoning, and contemporary philosophical thought; historical and contemporary influences on nursing science theory development; evaluation/analysis of interdisciplinary theory and application to nursing research.

NUR SCI 213.title: Measurement of Health-Related Behavior
NUR SCI 213.description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of psychometric principles, analyses, and emerging concepts like Intensive Longitudinal Methods to measure behavior in natural contexts using newer technologies (e.g., smartphones, wearable sensors, and Internet of Things). Students from different disciplines are encouraged.

NUR SCI 215.title: Health Promotion/Disease Prevention
NUR SCI 215.description: Incorporates principles of health promotion and disease prevention to provide culturally sensitive, evidence-based care for individuals, families, and communities. Focuses on critically analyzing and integrating current prevention guidelines to develop individualized plans of care and provide holistic and integrative education.

NUR SCI 216.title: Critical Thinking Through Writing Critique
NUR SCI 216.description: Aims to stimulate critical thinking by using existing scientific literature to work out the structure of their arguments, evaluate their logical clarity, identify unquestioned assumptions, and link all this to the rigor/appropriateness of any inferences made.

NUR SCI 217.title: Applied Pharmacology
NUR SCI 217.description: Principles of pharmacology applied to intervention in pathophysiologic states across the life span. Discussion of the major drug groups with implications for monitoring, drug administration, toxicity, and patient education included. Physical, psychological, social, and cultural factors affecting drug administration.
NUR SCI 217.prereq_text: NUR SCI 202 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 208 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 209A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 219 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 217.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 219.title: Pathophysiology
NUR SCI 219.description: Focuses on pathologic alterations in physiologic processes in cells, tissues, organs, and systems across the life span. Emphasis is placed on critical thinking, application of concepts to clinical practice, and related research.
NUR SCI 219.prereq_text: NUR SCI 209A ( coreq ) AND NUR SCI 208 ( coreq ) AND NUR SCI 202 ( coreq )
NUR SCI 219.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 221A.title: Medical Surgical Nursing 1
NUR SCI 221A.description: Focuses on the introduction of medical surgical nursing application with a focus on the older adult population. Emphasis is placed on identifying and synthesizing the unique set of factors influencing nursing management of individual older adults.
NUR SCI 221A.prereq_text: NUR SCI 202 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 208 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 209A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 219 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 221A.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 221B.title: Medical Surgical Nursing 2
NUR SCI 221B.description: Examines nursing assessment and advanced nursing management for acute and chronic health problems within the inpatient hospital setting. Theory content emphasizes assessment, health history, diagnostic reasoning, and nursing prioritization of care in medically complicated patients.
NUR SCI 221B.prereq_text: NUR SCI 209B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 217 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221A with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 221B.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 222A.title: Seminar in Clinical Translational Science
NUR SCI 222A.description: Discussion of clinical translational science methods in the context of nursing science research. Emphasis placed on interdisciplinary and community participatory research approaches.
NUR SCI 222A.prereq_text: Consent of the instructor is required.

NUR SCI 223A.title: Biostatistics for Health Sciences I
NUR SCI 223A.description: Helps students to develop skills necessary for applying statistical principles and practices in health research. This is achieved through in-depth review of existing research articles and hands-on statistical programming exercises.

NUR SCI 223B.title: Biostatistics for Health Sciences II
NUR SCI 223B.description: Introduces advanced methods of statistical analysis and research design used in health research. These include linear, logistic, Poisson regression, and a brief introduction to regression models for correlated data.
NUR SCI 223B.prereq_text: NUR SCI 223A with a minimum grade of B-.

NUR SCI 224.title: Research Designs in Nursing Science
NUR SCI 224.description: Provides an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research designs, methods, and analyses in nursing science. Evaluation of measurement and population issues, data management, ethics, analytical approaches, mixed methods work, and translational potential in the context of research.

NUR SCI 225B.title: Advanced Pharmacology II
NUR SCI 225B.description: Principles of pharmacology that serve as a foundation for the pharmacotherapeutic management of patients evaluated and treated by advanced practice nurses. Emphasis includes the application of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles.
NUR SCI 225B.prereq_text: NUR SCI 225A with a minimum grade of B.

NUR SCI 226.title: Theoretical and Conceptual Frameworks
NUR SCI 226.description: Explores the history, roles, and uses of theory in nursing and health scholarship. Students examine, analyze, and utilize the components of theory, theory construction, concept analysis, and theory evaluation.

NUR SCI 227A.title: Grant Writing I
NUR SCI 227A.description: Introduction to the principles and methods of proposal writing used in preparing grant proposals. Provides content on the process for good proposal development, key elements and sections of proposal, necessary information to include in grant proposal and development of budget.
NUR SCI 227A.prereq_text: NUR SCI 212 with a minimum grade of B- and NUR SCI 226 with a minimum grade of B-.

NUR SCI 227B.title: Grant Writing II
NUR SCI 227B.description: Provides a continuation of skill building in preparing a grant proposal, with emphasis on developing the educational training plan, budget and budget justification, the IRB and ethics component, and letters of support for a career-development grant.

NUR SCI 228.title: Human Behavior and Mental Health Care
NUR SCI 228.description: Focuses on nursing management of individuals across the lifespan with alterations in mental health. Mental health promotion and crisis intervention, chemical dependency, acute and chronic care for psychiatric conditions, rehabilitation, and recovery are addressed.
NUR SCI 228.prereq_text: NUR SCI 209B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 217 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221A with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 228.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 229.title: Pain: Symptoms, Science, and Treatment
NUR SCI 229.description: Covers theory, assessment, experience, and management of pain.

NUR SCI 230.title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment
NUR SCI 230.description: Application of theoretical concepts related to comprehensive health assessment of patients across the lifespan. Analysis, synthesis, and application of comprehensive health assessment data.

NUR SCI 230L.title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment Laboratory
NUR SCI 230L.description: Clinical laboratory course for the application of concepts related to comprehensive health assessment of patients across the lifespan.

NUR SCI 233.title: Appraisal and Translation of Evidence for Practice
NUR SCI 233.description: Provides advanced concepts on research methods and measurement strategies that are applicable to support the advanced practice nurse to access, evaluate, and utilize data from various sources including research, quality improvement initiatives, and information technology origins to achieve improvements.
NUR SCI 233.prereq_text: Consent of the instructor is required.

NUR SCI 234.title: Health Politics and Policy
NUR SCI 234.description: Participants analyze, apply, and evaluate current health policy-related literature, engage in the process of health policy development within professional, regulatory, or administrative environments, and develop an evidence-based health policy proposal across the spectrum of health care systems.

NUR SCI 235.title: DNP Scholarly Project I: Conceptualization and Planning
NUR SCI 235.description: Students gain the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to develop an evidence-based project plan and proposal. Structured didactic content and application of the Student's DNP Scholarly Project. First of four DNP Scholarly Project courses.

NUR SCI 236.title: Social Determinants of Health and Health Equity
NUR SCI 236.description: The four components of the Clinical Prevention and Population Health Framework: evidence-based practice, clinical preventive service and health promotion, health systems and policy, and population health and community aspects of practice with emphasis on ethical care delivery.

NUR SCI 237.title: DNP Intersession
NUR SCI 237.description: Provides DNP students an opportunity to present and receive faculty and peer feedback on their DNP project plan. Recommendations related to practical data collection and information gathering approaches and data analysis are also emphasized.

NUR SCI 238.title: Foundations of Health Systems and Health Economics
NUR SCI 238.description: Foundational understanding of how healthcare is financed in the U.S. Explores economic theories and policies, various types of healthcare organizations, and healthcare delivery systems. Healthcare finance is discussed at national and practice levels.

NUR SCI 239.title: The Science of Change, Quality Improvement, and Program Evaluation
NUR SCI 239.description: Intro to science of quality improvement and program evaluation. Focus on info system technology and its application in quality improvement. Focus placed on the role of the advanced practice nurse leader in developing and leading clinical quality and safety initiatives.

NUR SCI 240.title: DNP Scholarly Project II: Proposal
NUR SCI 240.description: Developing a full proposal that reflects synthesis of the student's knowledge from prior coursework and work in an area of interest or expertise under the direction of a faculty mentor. Second of four DNP Scholarly Project course sequence.

NUR SCI 241.title: DNP Scholarly Project III: Implementation and Evaluation
NUR SCI 241.description: Continued development of knowledge, skills, and abilities to implement the chosen DNP proposal. Students receive direction from a faculty mentor and peer feedback as they become engaged in the microsystem where they are implementing their DNP Scholarly Project.

NUR SCI 242.title: DNP Scholarly Project IV: Implications
NUR SCI 242.description: Selection and implementation of evidence-based interventions supported through informatics and technological advances and measurement of outcomes in a selected practicum site as applicable. Includes reflection and mapping of the DNP Scholarly Project with DNP Essentials as published.

NUR SCI 243.title: DNP Epilogue
NUR SCI 243.description: DNP students develop DNP competency through the presentation of their project and development of a professional manuscript. Individual direction from the DNP Project Team and peer feedback are provided throughout the course.

NUR SCI 244.title: A Systems Approach to Health and Well-Being
NUR SCI 244.description: Focuses on using a systems approach to promote individual and population wellness. The key topics include complex/dynamic system, analytic tools to measure dynamic/ interrelated processes, critical analysis of literature that utilizes the systems approach to promote holistic well-being.

NUR SCI 245.title: Primary Care Adult/Gerontology Acute Common Conditions
NUR SCI 245.description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting patients and families across the lifespan. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutics are integrated. Concepts of quality health care, resource management, and shared-decision making are emphasized.
NUR SCI 245.prereq_text: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B.

NUR SCI 246.title: Qualitative Research Designs in Nursing Science
NUR SCI 246.description: Seminar in qualitative research philosophies, methods, and analysis in nursing science clinical research. Consideration of population access and sampling, ethics, data management, analytical approaches, and translational potential.

NUR SCI 247.title: Quantitative Research Designs in Nursing Science
NUR SCI 247.description: Seminar in experimental and survey research designs, methods, and analysis in nursing science clinical research. Consideration of measurement issues, mixed methods models, population access and sampling, data management, analytical approaches, and translational potential.
NUR SCI 247.prereq_text: NUR SCI 212 with a minimum grade of B-.

NUR SCI 248.title: Curricular Design for the Health Professions
NUR SCI 248.description: Introduces students to the theoretical foundations, essential components, and accreditation standards for curriculum development at the program level. Outcome competencies are addressed as they apply to the development and evaluation of an educational program to meet society’s diverse healthcare needs.

NUR SCI 249.title: Transformational Leadership in Education for the Health Professions
NUR SCI 249.description: Students are introduced to the role of the nurse educator as change agent, leader, and scholar and are provided experience in planning learner-centered learning activities that are engaging and effective in achieving desired student performance.

NUR SCI 250.title: Primary Care Women's Health
NUR SCI 250.description: Primary health care needs of women including adolescent, adult, and aging adults. Emphasizes assessment, diagnosis, prevention, management, and education of common gynecologic and family planning health care needs.
NUR SCI 250.prereq_text: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 250.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 251.title: Nursing Informatics
NUR SCI 251.description: Provides an overview of nursing informatics topics for practice.

NUR SCI 252.title: Applied Data Science for Clinical Research
NUR SCI 252.description: Provides hands-on training in applied data science for clinical research.

NUR SCI 255.title: Primary Care Obstetrics
NUR SCI 255.description: Assessment and management of women during pregnancy. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology and therapeutics are integrated. Includes assessment, differential diagnosis, management, patient/family education, and counseling related to normal pregnancy care.
NUR SCI 255.prereq_text: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 255.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 260A.title: Primary Care Adult/Gerontology Chronic Conditions
NUR SCI 260A.description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting adult and geriatric patients and their families. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutic are integrated.
NUR SCI 260A.prereq_text: NUR SCI 245 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 260A.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 261.title: Advanced Qualitative and Mixed Methods Research Design
NUR SCI 261.description: Discussion and application course on design and implementation of qualitative, mixed methods research. Emphasis on data analysis and management skills, interpretation of findings, reflexivity and ethical considerations in field work, and the development of publishable products for dissemination.
NUR SCI 261.prereq_text: Enrollment in a UCI Ph.D. program and at least one introduction qualitative course.

NUR SCI 270.title: Primary Care Pediatrics
NUR SCI 270.description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting pediatric patients and their families. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutics are integrated.
NUR SCI 270.prereq_text: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 270.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 271.title: Community-Based Health Care
NUR SCI 271.description: Epidemiology, primary health care promotion, and disease prevention applied to nursing care of individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes sociocultural, political, economic, and environmental influences. Concepts and methods of assessing populations and communities incorporated in concurrent practicum.
NUR SCI 271.prereq_text: NUR SCI 215 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 274 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 276 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 271.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 272.title: Pediatrics: Care of Children and Families
NUR SCI 272.description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of infants, children, and adolescents with acute, chronic, and emergency illnesses with an emphasis on social, cultural, and developmental influences.
NUR SCI 272.prereq_text: NUR SCI 201 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 228 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 272.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 273.title: Maternity and Women’s Health Care
NUR SCI 273.description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of women’s wellness across the lifespan, the childbirth process, and newborn care. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.
NUR SCI 273.prereq_text: NUR SCI 201 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 228 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 273.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 274.title: Critical and Specialty Health Care
NUR SCI 274.description: Focuses on the delivery of patient-centered care and collaborative management of individuals with actual or potential life-threatening alterations in health status. Practicum in critical care units emphasizes teamwork, collaboration, informatics, evidence-based practice, safety, and quality improvement in safe care delivery.
NUR SCI 274.prereq_text: NUR SCI 200 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 272 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 273 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 274.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 275.title: Clinical Preceptorship
NUR SCI 275.description: Hybrid clinical course facilitated by nursing faculty and clinicians focusing on in-depth clinical nursing practice and preparation for transition to independent practice. Topics covering NCLEX preparation, BRN application, and professional transition activities are discussed.
NUR SCI 275.prereq_text: NUR SCI 215 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 274 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 276 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 275.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 276.title: Leadership and Management in Health Care
NUR SCI 276.description: Focuses on the role of the professional nurse as leader and manager of a health team. Principles, concepts, and theories related to organizations, management, leadership, change, decision-making, and group process are applied to the delivery of health care.
NUR SCI 276.prereq_text: NUR SCI 200 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 272 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 273 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 276.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 277.title: Implementation Science
NUR SCI 277.description: Focuses on dissemination and implementation (D&I) science. Emphasizes the types of questions D&I research seeks to answer, commonly used models and frameworks, methods employed, and outcomes examined.

NUR SCI 279A.title: Frameworks for the Advanced Practice Registered Nursing Role: Nurse Practitioner
NUR SCI 279A.description: Orientation to the scope and standards of advanced practice registered nursing pertinent to the APRN role. Principles of jurisprudence, ethics, and advocacy will be introduced along with conceptual frameworks for advanced nursing practice.

NUR SCI 282.title: Compassionate Care with Underserved Populations
NUR SCI 282.description: Addresses theory/research on health risk factors (e.g., psychiatric illness, sociocultural and economic characteristics) that impact patient health and well-being across the lifespan. Emphasis is on cultural awareness, lifestyle modification, community resources, and communication/coping strategies to promote well-being.

NUR SCI 283.title: Primary Care Procedures
NUR SCI 283.description: Introduces the theoretical basis for common procedures performed in primary care clinical practice. Focus includes EKG interpretation, x-ray interpretation, minor surgery, and orthopaedic procedures.
NUR SCI 283.prereq_text: NUR SCI 245 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 283.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 284.title: Scholarly Concentration
NUR SCI 284.description: Focuses on analysis and use of research to provide the evidence-base nursing practice in an area of interest. Students critique, synthesize, and analyze a body of clinical and behavioral research evidence.
NUR SCI 284.prereq_text: NUR SCI 200 with a minimum grade of C.
NUR SCI 284.restriction: Community and Population Health majors only.

NUR SCI 285.title: DNP APRN Practicum I
NUR SCI 285.description: Clinical application of theory and research related to the advanced assessment and health promotion of patients across the lifespan.
NUR SCI 285.prereq_text: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B and (NUR SCI 230L with a minimum grade of B or NUR SCI 231L with a minimum grade of B).

NUR SCI 287.title: DNP APRN Practicum III
NUR SCI 287.description: Clinical application of theory and research through clinical experiences in selected primary care settings designed to provide students with competencies in the assessment, diagnosis, management, and education/counseling in selected populations.
NUR SCI 287.prereq_text: NUR SCI 286 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 287.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 288.title: DNP APRN Practicum IV
NUR SCI 288.description: Continued clinical application of theory and research through clinical experiences in selected primary care settings designed to provide students with competencies in the assessment, diagnosis, management, and education/counseling in selected populations.
NUR SCI 288.prereq_text: NUR SCI 287 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 288.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 289.title: DNP APRN Practicum V
NUR SCI 289.description: Culminating clinical experience serves as a transition from the student role to that of the advanced practice nurse.
NUR SCI 289.prereq_text: NUR SCI 288 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 289.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 290.title: DNP APRN Practicum VI
NUR SCI 290.description: Through continued clinical experience, students demonstrate increased responsibility and accountability for performance as an advanced practice nurse and clinical scholar, synthesizing knowledge of pathophysiology and disease management, evidence-based guidelines, anticipatory guidance, models of provider-patient communication, and provision of educational resources.
NUR SCI 290.prereq_text: NUR SCI 289 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 290.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 291.title: DNP Practicum I
NUR SCI 291.description: Implementation and evaluation of an evidence-based, DNP project in an area of advanced practice in partnership with a selected agency or organization that solves a practice problem or improves population health, educational, or performance outcomes.

NUR SCI 292.title: DNP Practicum II
NUR SCI 292.description: Implementation and evaluation of an evidence-based, DNP project in an area of advanced practice in partnership with a selected agency or organization that solves a practice problem or improves population health, educational, or performance outcomes.
NUR SCI 292.prereq_text: NUR SCI 291 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 292.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 293.title: DNP Practicum III
NUR SCI 293.description: Implementation and evaluation of an evidence-based, DNP project in an area of advanced practice in partnership with a selected agency or organization that solves a practice problem or improves population health, educational, or performance outcomes.
NUR SCI 293.prereq_text: NUR SCI 292 with a minimum grade of B.
NUR SCI 293.restriction: Consent of instructor required to enroll.

NUR SCI 296.title: Doctoral Dissertation Reading and Writing
NUR SCI 296.description: Dissertation research with Nursing Sciences faculty.

NUR SCI 298.title: Directed Studies in Nursing Science
NUR SCI 298.description: Directed study with Nursing Science faculty.

NUR SCI 299.title: Independent Study in Nursing Science
NUR SCI 299.description: Independent research with Nursing Science faculty.

PATH 200A.title: Research in Experimental Pathology
PATH 200A.description: Independent research for the Ph.D. program within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in Experimental Pathology.

PATH 200B.title: Research in Experimental Pathology
PATH 200B.description: Independent research for the Ph.D. program within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in Experimental Pathology.

PATH 200C.title: Research in Experimental Pathology
PATH 200C.description: Independent research for the Ph.D. program within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in Experimental Pathology.

PATH 200R.title: Research in Experimental Pathology for First-Year Students
PATH 200R.description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in Experimental Pathology for first-year Ph.D. students.

PATH 203A.title: Advanced Studies in Experimental Pathology
PATH 203A.description: A tutorial course for Ph.D. students in Experimental Pathology entailing attendance at Departmental seminars and critical reading of the scientific literature.

PATH 203B.title: Advanced Studies in Experimental Pathology
PATH 203B.description: A tutorial course for Ph.D. students in Experimental Pathology entailing attendance at Departmental seminars and critical reading of the scientific literature.

PATH 203C.title: Advanced Studies in Experimental Pathology
PATH 203C.description: A tutorial course for Ph.D. students in Experimental Pathology entailing attendance at Departmental seminars and critical reading of the scientific literature.

PATH 204A.title: Experimental Pathology Research Seminar
PATH 204A.description: Seminar series for graduate students in Experimental Pathology. Students attend seminars and, beginning in their third year of graduate study, present one formal seminar on their graduate research.

PATH 204B.title: Experimental Pathology Research Seminar
PATH 204B.description: Seminar series for graduate students in Experimental Pathology. Students attend seminars and, beginning in their third year of graduate study, present one formal seminar on their graduate research.

PATH 204C.title: Experimental Pathology Research Seminar
PATH 204C.description: Seminar series for graduate students in Experimental Pathology. Students attend seminars and, beginning in their third year of graduate study, present one formal seminar on their graduate research.

PATH 221.title: Immunopathogenic Mechanisms of Disease
PATH 221.description: Examination of the mechanisms underlying disease states mediated by immune dysregulation including mechanisms of immune evasion by cancer, diseases mediated by cytokine dysregulation, role of the microbiome of the GI tract and of other disease sites, and adoptive T-cell (CAR-T-cells).
PATH 221.restriction: Campus Honors Collegium students and juniors and seniors may audit.

PATH 225.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Human Disease
PATH 225.description: Provides an overview of the molecular mechanisms of human diseases, including neurologic, hematologic, neoplastic, and infectious diseases. Students gain an understanding of these mechanisms, as well as models of human diseases.

PATH 227.title: Experimental Pathology Journal Club
PATH 227.description: Graduate-level course, which is open to all years, will involve the reading and discussion of papers, preferably written by the invited seminar speaker. Discussions will cover advanced topics in experimental pathology as related to an understanding of human disease.

PATH 240.title: Neuropathology
PATH 240.description: Covers genetic and molecular mechanisms of neurological diseases. A grounding in neuroanatomy and prior or simultaneous enrollment in Anatomy 210A or the equivalent is strongly recommended. Resident physicians and clinical fellows can audit the course.

PATH 291.title: M.D. and Ph.D. Fundamentals
PATH 291.description: For MSTP students during their first or second year of graduate school. The goals are to help early graduate-phase MSTPs to get off to faster starts in their dissertations and better leverage their dual-degree training during their physician-scientist journeys.

PATH 292A.title: Scientific Communication
PATH 292A.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

PATH 292B.title: Scientific Communication
PATH 292B.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

PATH 292C.title: Scientific Communication
PATH 292C.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

PATH 298.title: Independent Study
PATH 298.description: Provided for Medical Science Training Program students to synthesize the basic science information learned during the basic science years of medical school and learn how to apply that knowledge toward graduate research directed at understanding the basis of human disease.

PATH 299.title: Dissertation in Experimental Pathology
PATH 299.description: Provided for the preparation and completion of the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree.

PED GEN 200A.title: Introduction to Medical Genetics and Genomics
PED GEN 200A.description: Covers current concepts regarding mitosis, meiosis, the cell cycle, and chromosome ultrastructure and function. Clinical disorders caused by chromosomal aneuploidy, duplication, and deletion, and principles of Mendelian, chromosomal, and multifactorial and nontraditional inheritance are presented and illustrated.

PED GEN 200B.title: Genetic Screening, Prenatal Development, and Human Teratology
PED GEN 200B.description: Principles and techniques of prenatal, neonatal, and carrier screening. Infertility, pregnancy, and delivery. Normal and abnormal prenatal growth and development. Reproductive and fetal effects of drugs, radiation, infections, and other environmental factors.
PED GEN 200B.prereq_text: PED GEN 200A with a minimum grade of B-.

PED GEN 200C.title: Human Genetic Disorders
PED GEN 200C.description: Inheritance, diagnosis, natural history, management, and counseling considerations for commonly encountered genetic diseases, birth defects, and dysmorphic syndromes.
PED GEN 200C.prereq_text: PED GEN 200B with a minimum grade of B-.

PED GEN 200D.title: Disorders due to Inborn Errors of Metabolism
PED GEN 200D.description: Aspects of biochemistry and metabolism are reviewed with special emphasis on genetic abnormalities which lead to inborn errors of metabolism. Diagnostic procedures, heterozygote detection, treatment, counseling issues, and prenatal diagnosis are reviewed.
PED GEN 200D.prereq_text: PED GEN 200A with a minimum grade of B-.

PED GEN 200E.title: Molecular Genetics, Gene Mapping, and Genetic Linkage
PED GEN 200E.description: Derivation of different types of DNA probes and DNA libraries, restriction endonuclease polymorphisms, assignment of genes to chromosomes, and genetic linkage. Emphasis on the use of recombinant DNA technologies and genetic analysis for diagnosis of human genetic disease.
PED GEN 200E.prereq_text: PED GEN 200A with a minimum grade of B- and PED GEN 200D with a minimum grade of B-.

PED GEN 200F.title: Quantitative Genetics
PED GEN 200F.description: Quantitative aspects of human genetics, including population studies, segregation analysis, linkage, mapping, and genetic risk determination.
PED GEN 200F.prereq_text: PED GEN 200A (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B-.

PED GEN 200G.title: Hereditary Cancer Counseling
PED GEN 200G.description: Issues in genetic counseling for cancer. Cancer biology; genetic mechanisms and environmental influences in carcinogenesis; tumor pathology; cancer gene mapping; epidemiology. Features natural history, diagnosis, prevention, surveillance, and management of heredity cancers. Psychosocial, ethical, legal aspects of cancer risk assessment.
PED GEN 200G.prereq_text: PED GEN 200B with a minimum grade of B-.

PED GEN 200H.title: Genetic Counseling Research Design
PED GEN 200H.description: Quantitative and qualitative methods for genetic counseling research. Reference management; statistics: sample size, power, and data analysis; reliability and validity; surveys, questionnaires, interviews, focus groups; quality of life and genetic epidemiology research; designing a research protocol; IRB issues; grant writing.

PED GEN 200L.title: Laboratory Fundamentals in Genetic Counseling
PED GEN 200L.description: Practical aspects of genetic testing including cytogenetic and molecular nomenclature and testing technologies, analysis of genetic test reports, roles of laboratory counselors, strategies for working with laboratories, fundamentals of billing/reimbursement for genetic testing, variant interpretation, genomic sequencing, and direct-to-consumer testing.

PED GEN 200M.title: Embryology for Medical Genetics
PED GEN 200M.description: Introduction to normal and abnormal prenatal growth and development of the major systems of the body from an embryological point of view. Intended for first-year genetic counseling students in preparation for clinical rotations.

PED GEN 201A.title: Introduction to Genetic Counseling
PED GEN 201A.description: Through directed readings, observing patient evaluations, role-playing, and conducting intake interviews, students are introduced to the process of diagnosis, management, and counseling for genetic disease. Psychosocial issues, interviewing techniques, pedigree construction, clinical photography, and various other skills are addressed.

PED GEN 201B.title: Clinical Rotation I
PED GEN 201B.description: Provides extensive supervised experience in history taking, interviewing, and psychosocial assessment in the clinical genetics setting. Students independently perform telephone, office, and home-visit intake interviews, participate in counseling, and present cases at patient management conferences.

PED GEN 201C.title: Clinical Rotation II
PED GEN 201C.description: Provides further supervised experience in genetic counseling, case management, clinic administration and organization, and the use of community resources. Emphasis is on sharpening counseling skills and on developing a professional identity and code of ethics.

PED GEN 202A.title: Counseling in Human Genetics: Theory and Methods
PED GEN 202A.description: Theoretical approaches, counseling models and methods, and bio-psychosocial assessment strategies are examined in the context of genetic counseling. Contract-setting, working alliance, the use of self and evaluation methods. Beginning counseling and peer supervision skills are practiced in class.

PED GEN 202B.title: Community Resources
PED GEN 202B.description: Lectures, guest speakers, and community visits acquaint genetic counselors with public and private health care and funding agencies, parent support and advocacy groups, and other resources to assist individuals and families confronted with genetic disorders, developmental disabilities, and birth defects.

PED GEN 202C.title: Ethical Issues in Human Genetics
PED GEN 202C.description: Explores major social, legal, and ethical issues in genetic counseling including those arising in genetic screening, prenatal diagnosis, informed consent, privacy and confidentiality, rights of the disabled, new genetic and reproductive technologies, treatment, and access to services.

PED GEN 203A.title: Counseling in Human Genetics: Putting Thought to Practice
