PED GEN 203A.description: Builds upon the skills learned in previous courses emphasizing advanced counseling methods such as listening, empathy, and collaboration. The counselor's own self-awareness, ethical behaviors, and limits are explored. Individual, team, and group exercises are performed.
PED GEN 203A.prereq_text: PED GEN 202A with a minimum grade of B-.

PED GEN 204.title: Professional Skills Development
PED GEN 204.description: Hones and augments existing competencies in genetic counseling through ongoing clinical experiences. Develops skills using computers for genetics applications, provision of community and professional education, and clinic administration. Further experience in genetics laboratories or specialty clinics may be elected.

PED GEN 295.title: Master's Thesis and Research Writing
PED GEN 295.description: Under the supervision of one or more faculty members, the student designs and conducts a research project or completes a case report. A problem in the cytogenetics, biochemical, clinical, psychosocial, or behavioral areas of medical genetics may be investigated.

PERSIAN 1A.title: Fundamentals in Persian
PERSIAN 1A.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Persian. Students learn the modern writing system and grammar of Persian. Facilitates basic reading, writing, and speaking skills and fosters college-level literacy in Persian culture.
PERSIAN 1A.restriction: PERSIAN 1A and PERSIAN S1AB may not be taken for full credit.

PERSIAN 1B.title: Fundamentals in Persian
PERSIAN 1B.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Persian. Students learn the modern writing system and grammar of Persian. Facilitates basic reading, writing, and speaking skills and fosters college-level literacy in Persian culture.
PERSIAN 1B.prereq_text: PERSIAN 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into PERSIAN 1B is also accepted.
PERSIAN 1B.restriction: PERSIAN 1B and PERSIAN S1AB and PERSIAN S1BC may not be taken for full credit.

PERSIAN 1C.title: Fundamentals in Persian
PERSIAN 1C.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Persian. Students learn the modern writing system and grammar of Persian. Facilitates basic reading, writing, and speaking skills and fosters college-level literacy in Persian culture.
PERSIAN 1C.prereq_text: PERSIAN 1B with a minimum grade of C or PERSIAN S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into PERSIAN 1C is also accepted.
PERSIAN 1C.restriction: PERSIAN 1C and PERSIAN S1BC may not be taken for full credit.

PERSIAN 2A.title: Intermediate Persian
PERSIAN 2A.description: Designed for students to advance their Persian language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Student will advance their understanding of grammar and syntax. Facilitates intermediate-level reading, writing, and speaking skills. Fosters college-level cultural literacy.
PERSIAN 2A.prereq_text: PERSIAN 1C with a minimum grade of C or PERSIAN S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into PERSIAN 2A is also accepted.
PERSIAN 2A.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PERSIAN 2B.title: Intermediate Persian
PERSIAN 2B.description: Designed for students to advance their Persian language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Students will advance their understanding of grammar and syntax. Facilitates intermediate-level reading, writing, and speaking skills. Fosters college-level cultural literacy.
PERSIAN 2B.prereq_text: PERSIAN 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into PERSIAN 2B is also accepted.
PERSIAN 2B.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PERSIAN 2C.title: Intermediate Persian
PERSIAN 2C.description: Designed for students to advance their Persian language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Students will advance their understanding of grammar and syntax. Facilitates intermediate-level reading, writing, and speaking skills. Fosters college-level cultural literacy.
PERSIAN 2C.prereq_text: PERSIAN 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into PERSIAN 2C is also accepted.
PERSIAN 2C.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PERSIAN 10A.title: Persian Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
PERSIAN 10A.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. PERSIAN 10A is for language mentors.

PERSIAN 10B.title: Persian Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
PERSIAN 10B.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. PERSIAN 10B is for language mentees.

PERSIAN 150.title: Topics in Advanced Persian Culture
PERSIAN 150.description: In-depth examination of major works in premodern and modern Persian literature and/or the arts, with specific emphasis upon historical and cultural context and relevant societal issues and trends. Course is conducted in English.

PERSIAN 165A.title: Modern Iran: Cinema and the City
PERSIAN 165A.description: Exploring modern Iran through film, literature, photography, travel writing, and philosophy and social science texts that introduce students to important concepts in post-colonial studies, social thought, war culture, religion, and media as experienced through the paradigm of a non-Western modernity.

PHARM 270.title: Applied Pharmacology
PHARM 270.description: Introduction to pharmacological techniques and current research problems; includes laboratory demonstrations and research seminars.

PHARM 271.title: Principles of Pharmacology
PHARM 271.description: Principles of pharmacology: pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, pharmacogenetics, drug interactions, and toxicity.

PHARM 272.title: Receptors and Drug Targets
PHARM 272.description: Molecular basis of drug-receptor interaction. Receptor properties including gene and protein structure, signaling mechanisms, trafficking and physiological effects: G-protein linked receptors, ligand-gated ion channels, receptor tyrosine kinases, nuclear receptors, and ligand regulated transcription factors.

PHARM 274.title: Research Techniques in Pharmacology
PHARM 274.description: Experimental techniques and model systems used in pharmacological research. Receptor analysis, bioassay, molecular biology, in vitro pharmacology, biochemical pharmacology, imaging, electrophysiology, in vivo pharmacology, disease models.

PHARM 276.title: Experimental Design and Data Analysis
PHARM 276.description: Experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, and power calculations.

PHARM 277.title: Ethics in Scientific Research
PHARM 277.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, and handling of misconduct.

PHARM 278.title: Concepts in Drug Discovery
PHARM 278.description: Critical steps involved in discovery and optimization of a new drug. Target selection, relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activities, screening methods, strategies to identify lead compounds, and preclinical characterization necessary for development of the drug for clinical trials.

PHARM 279A.title: Special Topics in Pharmacology I
PHARM 279A.description: Topics of current interest in pharmacology; discussion of recent research publications.

PHARM 279B.title: Special Topics in Pharmacology II
PHARM 279B.description: Topics of current interest in pharmacology; discussion of recent research publications.

PHARM 280.title: Master's Project in Pharmacology
PHARM 280.description: Capstone research paper on topic of interest in pharmacology.

PHARM 281.title: Neuropharmacology
PHARM 281.description: Autonomic and central nervous system pharmacology, including major drug classes and therapeutic uses. Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and peripheral nervous system, including neurotransmitter synthesis, inactivation, and receptor action.

PHARM 282.title: Behavioral Pharmacology
PHARM 282.description: Pharmacology of integrative function and behavior. Drug treatment of pain. Mechanisms of reward, addiction, and drugs of abuse.

PHARM 283.title: Cardiovascular Pharmacology
PHARM 283.description: Basic understanding of drugs used in the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular disease. Mechanisms of action, clinical and adverse effects.

PHARM 284.title: Endocrine, Respiratory, and Gastrointestinal Pharmacology
PHARM 284.description: Basic understanding of drugs used in endocrine, respiratory, and gastrointestinal conditions, including hormone replacement, contraceptives, and drugs for diabetes, asthma, obesity, ulcer, and gastric reflux. Mechanisms of drug action, clinical and adverse effects.

PHILOS 1.title: Introduction to Philosophy
PHILOS 1.description: A selection of philosophical problems, concepts, and methods, e.g., free will, cause and substance, personal identity, the nature of philosophy itself.

PHILOS 2.title: Puzzles and Paradoxes
PHILOS 2.description: Introduction to the formal tools needed to comprehend and evaluate philosophical arguments and theoretical reasoning in general.

PHILOS 3.title: Technology and Society
PHILOS 3.description: A study of the nature of technology, its relation to human values, the philosophical assumptions in its development, and the philosophical implications of technology.

PHILOS 4.title: Introduction to Ethics
PHILOS 4.description: Selected topics from the history of ethics, e.g., the nature of the good life and the moral justification of conduct.

PHILOS 5.title: Contemporary Moral Problems
PHILOS 5.description: Selected moral issues of current interest, e.g., abortion, sexual morality, euthanasia, capital punishment, reverse discrimination, civil disobedience, or violence.

PHILOS 10.title: History of Ancient Philosophy
PHILOS 10.description: Examination of the central philosophical themes developed by the pre-Socratics, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, the Stoics, the Epicureans, and the Skeptics.

PHILOS 12.title: History of Modern Philosophy
PHILOS 12.description: A study of major developments in western philosophy from Descartes to Kant with readings from Descartes, Leibniz, Locke, Berkeley, Hume, and Kant.

PHILOS 13.title: History of Contemporary Philosophy
PHILOS 13.description: A study of recent philosophical developments in Anglo-American and Continental philosophy with readings from such figures as Russell, Moore, Wittgenstein, Quine, Heidegger, and Sartre.

PHILOS 21.title: Philosophy and Religion
PHILOS 21.description: Examines the intersection of religion and philosophy from a standpoint that does not presuppose previous academic study of either. Both Western and Eastern traditions and perspectives may be explored.

PHILOS 22.title: Introduction to Law and Society
PHILOS 22.description: What constitutes a legal system? What does it mean for a society to have a system as a part of the social fabric? Examines the social status of law and its use as a tool for fashioning society.

PHILOS 29.title: Critical Reasoning
PHILOS 29.description: Introduction to analysis and reasoning. The concepts of argument, premise, and conclusion, validity and invalidity, consistency and inconsistency. Identifying and assessing premises and inferences. Deductive versus inductive reasoning, and introduction to the probability calculus. Evaluating definitions. Informal fallacies.

PHILOS 30.title: Introduction to Symbolic Logic
PHILOS 30.description: An introduction to the symbolism and methods of the logic of statements, including evaluation of arguments by truth tables, the techniques of natural deduction, and semantic tableaux.

PHILOS 31.title: Introduction to Inductive Logic
PHILOS 31.description: Philosophical questions concerning the foundations of scientific inference, e.g., the traditional problem of induction, the Goodman paradox, the concept of cause, Mill's method of inductive reasoning, probability calculus, different interpretations of probability, and their interaction in inductive reasoning.

PHILOS 40.title: Special Topics in Philosophy
PHILOS 40.description: Lectures on selected topics at the lower-division level.

PHILOS 41.title: The Nature of Scientific Inquiry
PHILOS 41.description: Investigates the nature, scope, and status of scientific knowledge and the methods used to acquire it. Uses concrete historical examples from a variety of scientific fields to identify distinctive features of the scientific enterprise and explore their significance.

PHILOS 50.title: Business Ethics
PHILOS 50.description: Exploration of business and corporate operations from a philosophical lens. Philosophical analysis of profits, the production process and products themselves, and the business environment. Discussion of business decision-making drawn on the work of experts, case studies, and current events.

PHILOS 51.title: Science in the Public Sphere
PHILOS 51.description: Investigates the role of science in a democratic society. Discusses the scope and limits of scientific knowledge in the context of arguments for the special status of science in political decision-making. Uses concrete historical examples from a variety of fields.

PHILOS 60.title: Reason and Rhetoric
PHILOS 60.description: Examination of techniques for empathetic listening, role reversal, classical and modern persuasion methods. Development of critical thinking and argumentation skills, emphasizing active engagement in controversial debates. Practice in analyzing claims, identifying assumptions, and understanding biases in public discourse and humanities.

PHILOS 91.title: Sex, Race, and Science
PHILOS 91.description: Discusses the origins of biological sex, dynamics of sexual selection, sex differences in humans, and the construction of gender in human societies. Seeks to understand the role social values play in the creation of science.

PHILOS 100W.title: Writing Philosophy
PHILOS 100W.description: Discussion of those aspects of writing of special importance in philosophy, e.g., philosophical terminology, techniques for evaluating arguments, philosophical definitions and theories. At least 4,000 words of assigned composition based on philosophical readings.
PHILOS 100W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PHILOS 101.title: Introduction to Metaphysics
PHILOS 101.description: A study of one or more of the problems of "first philosophy," e.g., substance, free will, causation, abstract entities, identity.

PHILOS 102W.title: Introduction to the Theory of Knowledge
PHILOS 102W.description: A study of one or more of the basic issues in epistemology, e.g., the role of perception in the acquisition of knowledge, the nature of evidence, the distinction between belief and knowledge, and the nature of truth and certainty.
PHILOS 102W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PHILOS 103.title: Introduction to Moral Philosophy
PHILOS 103.description: A study of one or more of the problems of contemporary moral philosophy, e.g., the nature of justice, liberalism versus conservatism, happiness and its relation to virtue and right conduct, the objectivity of moral standards.

PHILOS 104.title: Introduction to Logic
PHILOS 104.description: Introduction to sentence logic, including truth tables and natural deduction; and to predicate logic, including semantics and natural deduction.

PHILOS 105A.title: Introduction to Set Theory and Mathematical Reasoning
PHILOS 105A.description: An introduction to the basic working vocabulary of mathematical reasoning and proof. Topics include sets, Boolean operations, ordered n-tuples, relations, functions, induction, and their applications to mathematical philosophy.

PHILOS 105B.title: Metalogic
PHILOS 105B.description: Introduction to formal syntax (proof theory) and semantics (model theory) for first-order logic, including the deduction, completeness, compactness, and Löewenheim-Skolem theorems.

PHILOS 105C.title: Undecidability and Incompleteness
PHILOS 105C.description: Introduction to the formal theory of effective processes, including recursive functions, Turing machines, Church's thesis, and proofs of Göedel's incompleteness theorem for arithmetic, and Church's undecidability theorem for first-order logic.

PHILOS 106.title: Topics in Logic
PHILOS 106.description: Selected topics in mathematical or philosophical logic.
PHILOS 106.prereq_text: (LPS 105A or PHILOS 105A or LSCI 145A) and (LPS 105B or PHILOS 105B or LSCI 145B) and (LPS 105C or PHILOS 105C or LSCI 145C).

PHILOS 108.title: Topics in Induction, Probability, and Decision Theory
PHILOS 108.description: Selected topics in induction, probability, and decision theory.

PHILOS 110.title: Topics in Ancient Philosophy
PHILOS 110.description: Selected topics from the writings of Plato and Aristotle, e.g., Aristotle's criticisms of Plato's metaphysics, ethics, or politics.

PHILOS 113.title: Topics in Modern Philosophy
PHILOS 113.description: Focuses on the works of central philosophical figures of modern Philosophy (e.g., Descartes, Leibniz, Hobbes, Locke, Hume, Kant) or on the treatment of one or more central philosophical problems by a number of these figures.

PHILOS 114.title: Topics in Nineteenth-Century Philosophy
PHILOS 114.description: Studies of some of the major figures after Kant (e.g., Hegel, Nietzsche, Marx, Kierkegaard), especially in German idealism and social thought.

PHILOS 115.title: Topics in History of Analytic Philosophy
PHILOS 115.description: Review of central theories or figures in the history of analytic philosophy. Emphasis on writings of Frege, Russell, Schlick, Carnap, and Quine. Topics include the nature of meaning and truth, the synthetic/analytic distinction, and scientific knowledge.

PHILOS 117.title: Topics in Asian Philosophy
PHILOS 117.description: Selected topics in the philosophies of Asia, e.g. Jainism, Buddhism, Yoga, Vedanta, Confucianism, Taoism, and Shinto.

PHILOS 120.title: Topics in Metaphysics
PHILOS 120.description: Examines central philosophical questions concerning our own fundamental nature and that of the world around us (e.g., causation and necessity, determination, free will, personal identity, the mind-body problem).

PHILOS 121.title: Topics in the Theory of Knowledge
PHILOS 121.description: One or more topics in the theory of knowledge, e.g., the nature of rational justification, of perceptual knowledge, of a priori knowledge.

PHILOS 121A.title: Medical Epistemology
PHILOS 121A.description: Analysis of epistemological issues concerning medical research and health care. Topics may include medical evidence, transmission of medical knowledge, medical expertise, the epistemology of medical disagreement, classification of illnesses, well-being, philosophy of pain, and medical decision making.

PHILOS 122.title: Topics in Philosophy of Mind
PHILOS 122.description: Selected topics involving the concept of mind, e.g., the relation between mind and body, the self, personal identity, consciousness, the unconscious.

PHILOS 123.title: Topics in Philosophy of Religion
PHILOS 123.description: Critical examination of concepts involved in the theological literature, e.g., the nature and existence of God, miracles, the problem of evil, divine command theories in ethics.

PHILOS 124.title: Topics in Feminist Epistemology
PHILOS 124.description: Investigates the nature of knowledge from a feminist standpoint. Emphasizes the relevance of the knower’s gender and social situatedness in knowledge practices against a traditional account of knowledge as a detached activity of an independent, neutral subject.

PHILOS 131A.title: Applied Ethics
PHILOS 131A.description: Topics may include capital punishment, world hunger, obligations to future generations, environmental ethics, animal rights, economic justice, sexual morality, affirmative action, racism and sexism, or legalization of drugs.

PHILOS 131C.title: Medical Ethics
PHILOS 131C.description: Analysis of moral issues concerning health care. Topics may include just allocation of scarce medical resources, the doctor/patient relationship, genetic engineering, surrogate motherhood, abortion, euthanasia, or social policy concerning AIDS.

PHILOS 133.title: Topics in Philosophy of Law
PHILOS 133.description: Selected topics concerning legal systems and the concept of law, e.g., the nature and purpose of law, the nature of authority, the relationship between law and morality, law and political-economic systems.

PHILOS 134.title: Topics in Philosophy of Gender and Race
PHILOS 134.description: Controversies about race and racism, and sex and sexism, continue to play an important role in the public domain. Explores philosophical questions relating to gender and race.

PHILOS 135A.title: The Scientific Revolution
PHILOS 135A.description: An examination of early modern European science from 1500-1700. Includes primary readings from central figures (Copernicus, Harvey, Bacon, Descartes, et al.); themes include the impact of printing, humanism, patronage, technology, and discussion of the term "revolution" in this context.

PHILOS 140.title: Topics in Philosophy of Science
PHILOS 140.description: Selected topics in contemporary philosophy of science, e.g., the status of theoretical entities, the confirmation of theories, the nature of scientific explanation.

PHILOS 141B.title: Geometry and Spacetime
PHILOS 141B.description: An examination of the foundations of the special theory of relativity, with emphasis on the geometry of Minkowski spacetime, and its relation to both Euclidean and non-Euclidean (hyperbolic) plane geometries.

PHILOS 141D.title: Probability and Determinism
PHILOS 141D.description: An examination of a cluster of interrelated issues concerning probability, determinism, logic, and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

PHILOS 143.title: Topics in Philosophy of Psychology
PHILOS 143.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of psychology, e.g., the nature of psychological explanation, reductionism, issues in cognitive, behavioral, and neuroscience.
PHILOS 143.restriction: Philosophy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHILOS 144.title: Topics in Philosophy of Social Science
PHILOS 144.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of the social sciences, e.g.: Is their goal to understand behavior or to predict and control it? Are they normative and the natural sciences not? Do they incorporate philosophical doctrines about language and mind?

PHILOS 145.title: Topics in Philosophy of Language
PHILOS 145.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of language, e.g., the nature of meaning, mechanisms of reference, speech acts.

PHILOS 147.title: Topics in Philosophy of Mathematics
PHILOS 147.description: Selected historical and contemporary topics in the philosophy of mathematics, e.g., mathematical truth and ontology, mathematical knowledge, the nature and role of proof, the workings of mathematics in application.

PHILOS 150.title: Phenomenology
PHILOS 150.description: A study of the foundations of phenomenology in Husserl and its background in Bolzano, Frege, Brentano, Meinong, Kant, and Descartes.

PHILOS 162.title: Social Ontology
PHILOS 162.description: Examines how things in one’s social environment exist. Such things are compared and contrasted to others in what might be regarded as the given, natural environment. Topics discussed include natural kinds; artifacts; essentialism; constructivism; intentionality; agency.

PHILOS 163.title: Social Epistemology
PHILOS 163.description: Social epistemology is specifically concerned with questions concerning knowledge and justification that arise in a social context. Topics discussed include testimony, experts, disagreement, group knowledge, feminist epistemology, legal epistemology, and epistemology of education.

PHILOS 164.title: Well-Being
PHILOS 164.description: Examines what it is that makes a life good (or bad) for the person who lives it. Topics include hedonism, desire-satisfaction theories of well-being (as well as other such theories), the notion of harm, the possibility of posthumous harm.

PHILOS 165.title: Philosophy of Action
PHILOS 165.description: Philosophy of action is specifically concerned with questions concerning the nature of acting, and related phenomena such as intending, willing, trying, and trusting. It deals both with individual and group action and their moral and epistemological underpinnings.

PHILOS 166.title: Philosophy of Education
PHILOS 166.description: Exploration of the philosophical and historical underpinnings of education. Examination of educational theories and influential educational figures, comparison of critical thinking development with intellectual character cultivations, and analysis of philosophies of education through works by Rousseau, Locke, and others.

PHILOS 167.title: Intellectual Virtue
PHILOS 167.description: Examination of intellectual virtues of humility, intellectual tenacity, intellectual courage, and integrity via historical foundations, classical traditions, and relevance to contemporary topics of epistemology.

PHILOS 190.title: Special Topics in Philosophy
PHILOS 190.description: Lectures on selected topics to be given by regular faculty and visiting faculty.

PHILOS 199.title: Directed Special Studies
PHILOS 199.description: Independent study on a research topic supervised by a faculty member.

PHILOS 199H.title: Honors Directed Special Studies
PHILOS 199H.description: Independent study on a research topic supervised by a faculty member, with the objective of preparing the Department of Philosophy honors paper.

PHILOS 200.title: Special Topics in Philosophy
PHILOS 200.description: Seminars on selected topics to be given by regular faculty and visiting faculty.

PHILOS 201.title: First-Year Seminar
PHILOS 201.description: An examination of some standard works in the history of philosophy, value theory, metaphysics, or epistemology; required of all first-year Philosophy graduate students in the School of Humanities.
PHILOS 201.restriction: Philosophy majors and Logic and Philosophy Of Science majors only.

PHILOS 205A.title: Introduction to Set Theory and Mathematical Reasoning
PHILOS 205A.description: An introduction to the basic working vocabulary of mathematical reasoning and proof. Topics include sets, Boolean operations, ordered n-tuples, relations, functions, induction, and their applications to mathematical philosophy.

PHILOS 205B.title: Metalogic
PHILOS 205B.description: Formal syntax (proof theory) and semantics (model theory) for first-order logic, including the deduction, completeness, compactness, and Loewenheim-Skolem theorems.
PHILOS 205B.prereq_text: PHILOS 205A with a minimum grade of B- or LPS 205A with a minimum grade of B-.

PHILOS 205C.title: Undecidability and Incompleteness
PHILOS 205C.description: Formal theory of effective processes, including recursive function, Turing machines, Church's thesis, proofs of Goedel's incompleteness theorem for arithmetics, and Church's undecidability for first-order logic.
PHILOS 205C.prereq_text: PHILOS 205B with a minimum grade of B- or LPS 205B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHILOS 206.title: Topics in Logic
PHILOS 206.description: Studies in selected areas of logic. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 210.title: Topics in Ancient Philosophy
PHILOS 210.description: Studies in selected areas of ancient philosophy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 212.title: Topics in Renaissance Philosophy
PHILOS 212.description: Studies in selected areas of renaissance philosophy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 213.title: Topics in Modern Philosophy
PHILOS 213.description: Studies in selected areas of modern philosophy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 215.title: Topics in Analytic Philosophy
PHILOS 215.description: Studies in selected areas of analytic philosophy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 218.title: Topics in Contemporary Philosophy
PHILOS 218.description: Studies in selected areas of contemporary philosophy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 220.title: Topics in Metaphysics
PHILOS 220.description: Studies in selected areas of metaphysics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 221.title: Topics in Epistemology
PHILOS 221.description: Studies in selected areas of epistemology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 221A.title: Medical Epistemology
PHILOS 221A.description: Analysis of epistemological issues concerning medical research and healthcare. Topics may include medical evidence, transmission of medical knowledge in the doctor-patient interaction, medical expertise, epistemology of medical disagreement, classification of illness, well-being, philosophy of pain, or medical decision making.

PHILOS 222.title: Topics in Mind and Action
PHILOS 222.description: Studies in selected areas of mind and action. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 230.title: Topics in Ethics
PHILOS 230.description: Studies in selected areas of ethics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 232.title: Topics in Political and Social Philosophy
PHILOS 232.description: Studies in selected areas of political and social philosophy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 240.title: Topics in Philosophy of Science
PHILOS 240.description: Studies in selected areas of philosophy of science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 241.title: Topics in Philosophy of Physics
PHILOS 241.description: Studies in selected areas of philosophy of physics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 242.title: Topics in Philosophy of Biology
PHILOS 242.description: Studies in selected areas of philosophy of biology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 243.title: Topics in Philosophy of Psychology
PHILOS 243.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of psychology, e.g., the nature of psychological explanation, reductionism, issues in cognitive, behavioral, and neuroscience.

PHILOS 244.title: Topics in Philosophy of Social Science
PHILOS 244.description: Studies in selected areas of philosophy and social science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 244A.title: PPE Proseminar I
PHILOS 244A.description: Introduces tools and concepts useful for working in the intersection of philosophy, political science, and economics. These are drawn from probability theory, decision theory, and the psychology of belief, knowledge, and rational choice.

PHILOS 244B.title: PPE Proseminar II
PHILOS 244B.description: Introduces some of the main theoretical topics at the intersection of philosophy, political science, and economics. PPE II covers (1) Rational Choice based game theory, (2) Evolutionary Game Theory, and (3) Voting and Social Choice.

PHILOS 245.title: Topics in Philosophy of Language
PHILOS 245.description: Studies in selected areas of philosophy of language. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 246.title: Topics in Philosophy of Logic
PHILOS 246.description: Studies in selected areas of philosophy of logic. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHILOS 247.title: Topics in Philosophy of Mathematics
PHILOS 247.description: Studies in selected areas of philosophy of mathematics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHMD 200A.title: Interprofessional Clinical Foundations I
PHMD 200A.description: The first course in a four-part series that covers interprofessional patient communication, medical interviewing, physical examination, and health promotion. Direct instruction in professionalism, diversity, social determinants of health, kindness, mindfulness, well-being, epidemiology, and biostatistics.
PHMD 200A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 200B.title: Interprofessional Clinical Foundations II
PHMD 200B.description: The second course in four-part series that covers interprofessional communication, medical interviewing, physical examination, and health promotion. Direct instruction in professionalism, diversity, social determinants of health, kindness, mindfulness, well-being, epidemiology, and biostatistics.
PHMD 200B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 200C.title: Interprofessional Clinical Foundations III
PHMD 200C.description: The third course in a four-part series that covers interprofessional communication, medical interviewing, physical examination, and health promotion. Direct instruction in professionalism, diversity, social determinants of health, kindness, mindfulness, well-being, epidemiology, and biostatistics.
PHMD 200C.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 200D.title: Interprofessional Clinical Foundations IV
PHMD 200D.description: The fourth course in a four-part series that covers interprofessional communication, medical interviewing, physical examination, and health promotion. Direct instruction in professionalism, diversity, social determinants of health, kindness, mindfulness, well-being, epidemiology, and biostatistics.
PHMD 200D.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 201A.title: Principles of Pharmacy Practice I
PHMD 201A.description: The first of a four-part series that covers the function and role of the health care team, Pharmacist Patient Care Process, immunization certification, communication and documentation, informatics, patient safety, interviewing, active listening, management/leadership, careers, resiliency, and student wellness.
PHMD 201A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 201B.title: Principles of Pharmacy Practice II
PHMD 201B.description: The second of a four-part series that covers the function and roles of the health care team, Pharmacist Patient Care Process, immunization certification, communication and documentation, informatics, patient safety, interviewing, active listening, management/leadership, careers, resiliency, and student wellness.
PHMD 201B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 201C.title: Principles of Pharmacy Practice III
PHMD 201C.description: The third of a four-part series that covers the function and role of the health care team, Pharmacist Patient Care Process, immunization certification, communication and documentation, informatics, patient safety, interviewing, active listening, management/leadership, careers, resiliency, and student wellness.
PHMD 201C.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 201D.title: Principles of Pharmacy Practice IV
PHMD 201D.description: The fourth of a four-part series that covers the function and role of the health care team, Pharmacist Patient Care Process, immunization certification, communication and documentation, informatics, patient safety, interviewing, active listening, management/leadership, careers, resiliency, and student wellness.
PHMD 201D.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 202A.title: Self Care I: Conventional and Complementary
PHMD 202A.description: Educates pharmacy students about healthy lifestyle choices, the importance of mental and physical health, and self-care. Provides students with methods and techniques for dealing with the stressors of a professional educational environment and life challenges.
PHMD 202A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 202B.title: Self Care II: Conventional and Complementary
PHMD 202B.description: The study of nonprescription products, complementary/alternative medicine, and non-pharmacological interventions for select self-treatable medical conditions commonly encountered by the pharmacist. Emphasis on the pharmacist's consultant role in product selection and non-pharmacological recommendations.
PHMD 202B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 202C.title: Self Care III: Conventional and Complementary
PHMD 202C.description: Relates to patients' ability to care for themselves with emphasis on the pharmacist's consultant role and continues to explore self-treatable medical conditions commonly encountered by pharmacists, including non-pharmacologic interventions, nonprescription medications, and complementary/alternative products to treat them.
PHMD 202C.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203A.title: Pharmacotherapy Principles to Practice I: Cardiology and Respiratory
PHMD 203A.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers the cardiovascular and respiratory system.
PHMD 203A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203B.title: Pharmacotherapy Principles to Practice II: Gastrointestinal and Nutrition
PHMD 203B.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers the gastrointestinal system and nutrition topics.
PHMD 203B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203C.title: Pharmacotherapy - Principles to Practice III: Renal and Immunology
PHMD 203C.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers the renal and immune systems.
PHMD 203C.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203D.title: Pharmacotherapy - Principles to Practice IV: Endocrine System
PHMD 203D.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers the endocrine system.
PHMD 203D.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203E.title: Pharmacotherapy - Principles to Practice V: Infectious Disease
PHMD 203E.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers infectious disorders.
PHMD 203E.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203F.title: Pharmacotherapy - Principles to Practice VI: Central Nervous System
PHMD 203F.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers the central nervous system.
PHMD 203F.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203G.title: Pharmacotherapy - Principles to Practice VII: Hematology and Oncologic Disorders
PHMD 203G.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers hematology and oncologic disorders.
PHMD 203G.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 203H.title: Pharmacotherapy - Principles to Practice VIII: Special Populations and Special Topics
PHMD 203H.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers special populations, ophthalmology, and special topics.
PHMD 203H.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 204A.title: Information Analytics and Numeracy I: Biostatistics
PHMD 204A.description: Exposure to basic statistics and techniques that are commonly found in the medical and pharmacy literature, covering descriptive and inferential statistics. Students learn to choose the most appropriate statistical parametric and non-parametric tests and interpret findings from the literature.
PHMD 204A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 204B.title: Information Analytics and Numeracy II: Drug Information, Research Methods, and Literature Analysis
PHMD 204B.description: Addresses development of knowledge, skills, and attitudes required for biomedical inquiry and discovery, including methods for data retrieval, analysis, interpretation, and synthesis.
PHMD 204B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 204C.title: Information Analytics and Numeracy III: Epidemiology
PHMD 204C.description: Covers distribution of disease and health in groups of people and the factors that influence the distribution, including evaluation of therapeutic and diagnostic treatments and delivery of health care services.
PHMD 204C.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 205A.title: Molecular Basis of Health and Disease I: Microbiology and Immunology
PHMD 205A.description: Principles of medical microbiology, immunology, virology, and parasitology. Introduction to classification, morphology, and physiology of microorganisms, particularly those that cause human pathology - bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans, parasite, and worms - and the body's immune response.
PHMD 205A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 205B.title: Molecular Basis of Health and Disease II: Microbiology and Immunology
PHMD 205B.description: Principles of medical microbiology, immunology, virology, and parasitology. Introduction to classification, morphology, and physiology of microorganisms, particularly those that cause human pathology - bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans, parasite, and worms - and the body's immune response.
PHMD 205B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 205C.title: Molecular Basis of Health and Disease III: Clinical Chemistry
PHMD 205C.description: Emphasis on normal human physiology and pathology as it related to clinical chemistry and assessment of disease states with the context of the Pharmacist Patient Care Process. Alterations of clinical chemistry results due to drug therapy are covered.
PHMD 205C.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 209.title: Concepts in Pharmacology
PHMD 209.description: Provides an overview of the core concepts of pharmacology, including pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics. Drug mechanism of action is addressed.
PHMD 209.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 210.title: Principles of Pharmacology
PHMD 210.description: Provides an overview of the basic principles of pharmacology, covering pharmacodynamics - effects of drugs on the body - and pharmacokinetics - the process by which a drug is absorbed, distributed, metabolized, and excreted by the body.
PHMD 210.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 211.title: Principles of Public Health
PHMD 211.description: Covers the framework, principles, and core responsibilities of public health research and practice from multidisciplinary perspectives. It also provides the necessary foundation for further studies using crosscutting approaches essential for public health practice.
PHMD 211.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 212.title: Principles of Pharmacogenomics
PHMD 212.description: Walks students through the basics of genetics and genomics. Particular emphasis is placed on the use of genetics or genetic testing to assist in patient treatment regimens and evaluation of disease.
PHMD 212.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 213.title: Pharmaceutical Biochemistry
PHMD 213.description: Topics include the biological, chemical and cellular roles of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, hormones, enzymes and vitamins. In addition, the chemical and cellular basis of digestion, intermediary metabolism, biological oxidation and metabolic antagonism are discussed.
PHMD 213.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 214.title: Pharmacy Law and Ethics
PHMD 214.description: An introduction to California and federal legal requirements that impact pharmacy practice, emphasizing the legal and ethical principles applied by pharmacists in their decision-making. Explores approaches for resolving ethical dilemmas in patient care.
PHMD 214.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 215.title: Health Policy and Pharmacoeconomics
PHMD 215.description: Introduces students to the organization, financing, and delivery of health care services in the U.S. The relationship of providers, patients, payers, etc., are analyzed. Management and research principles utilized to manage drug therapy are introduced.
PHMD 215.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 216.title: Clinical Toxicology
PHMD 216.description: Fundamentals of pharmacology and mechanisms of action are reinforced and applied to learn the clinical effects of acute/chronic exposure derived from environmental, dietary, occupational and pharmaceutical sources. Students focus on information literacy skills and clinical management of poisonings.
PHMD 216.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 220.title: Medical Physiology with Anatomic Correlates
PHMD 220.description: Concepts of physiology and mechanisms of body function at various levels of organization from cellular to organ systems. Emphasis on quantitative understanding of various body processes. Human anatomy is integrated with physiological concepts. Anatomic-physiologic relationships facilitated through virtual labs.
PHMD 220.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 230.title: Cannabis Pharmacology and Therapeutics
PHMD 230.description: Provide knowledge about the cannabis plant and the derivative constituents. Introduce the scientific basis for development of cannabis-derived medicinal drug products. Provide evidence-based information to navigate the mass of cannabis information and counsel patients in its use and safety.

PHMD 231.title: Anti-Aging Pharmacology
PHMD 231.description: Addresses why we age and what we can do about it. Introduces the five models of aging. Covers the major pathways of aging and drugs that have been demonstrated to extend lifespan in model systems.
PHMD 231.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 232.title: Pharmacotherapy Principle to Practice: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation and Cellular Therapy
PHMD 232.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease in patients receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and cellular therapies.
PHMD 232.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 240.title: Mental Health, Medications, and the Media
PHMD 240.description: Examines the portrayal of psychiatric disease states and psychoactive drugs through the lens of the media. Critically evaluate documentaries, movies, and television series that portray topics such as drug misuse, psychedelic use, and disease states.
PHMD 240.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 241.title: Travel Health
PHMD 241.description: Learn to provide effective pre-travel itinerary-based assessment, planning, and consultation related to vaccine-preventable diseases, prevention of other infectious and non-infectious travel-related diseases, and self-treatable conditions not requiring a diagnosis. Topics include yellow fever, malaria, altitude sickness, and emerging tropical diseases.
PHMD 241.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 242.title: Advanced Cardiology Pharmacotherapy
PHMD 242.description: Focuses on cardiology specialty topics such as arrhythmias, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock, sudden cardiac arrest, advanced cardiovascular life support, and the pharmacist's role in Code Blue situations, medical devices for hemodynamic monitoring and cardiac support, and heart transplantation.
PHMD 242.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 250A.title: Managed Care Pharmacy I
PHMD 250A.description: Introduction to the principles and practice of managed care pharmacy, including collection and synthesis of clinical data, assessment of economic data, and decision-making for a Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee.
PHMD 250A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 260.title: Leadership and Management
PHMD 260.description: Provide an introduction to various leadership roles in the field of pharmacy, as well as management techniques to engage and inspire team building, cultivate a productive work environment, and develop future leaders in the industry.

PHMD 261.title: Health Coaching and Wellness for Pharmacists
PHMD 261.description: Trains student pharmacists to use health coaching techniques to care for those with different clinical conditions and goals. Reviews adult learning theories and skills, such as motivational interviewing, as they apply to health coaching. Reviews elements of clinician wellness.
PHMD 261.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 262.title: Overcoming Healthcare Disparities in Pharmacy Practice
PHMD 262.description: Providing an understanding of the causes for healthcare disparities and then proposing pharmacy practice-based solutions for overcoming them. Engaging with community partners and healthcare professionals for real-world experiences.
PHMD 262.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 270.title: Introduction to Drug Development and Evaluation
PHMD 270.description: Introduces drug development fundamentals, including drug discovery, clinical trials, and regulatory approval. It covers the FDA's role in drug safety, formulation optimization, and introduces Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling for predicting drug behavior and enhancing trial efficiency.

PHMD 274A.title: Pharmaceutics I
PHMD 274A.description: The first in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics and interconnections with the Pharmacist Patient Care Process.
PHMD 274A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 274B.title: Pharmaceutics II
PHMD 274B.description: The second course in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics, and interconnections with the pharmacist patient care process. Topics include drug substances, dosage forms, and therapeutic effects. Includes laboratory.
PHMD 274B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 274C.title: Pharmaceutics III
PHMD 274C.description: The final course in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics,and interconnections with the Pharmacist Patient Care Process.
PHMD 274C.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 277.title: Medicinal Chemistry
PHMD 277.description: Walks students through medicinal chemistry, broadly defined. Students utilize the knowledge gained in organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, physical chemistry, pharmacology and physiology in an integrated fashion as applied to modern medicinal chemistry. Continuation of Medicinal Chemistry I.
PHMD 277.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 280A.title: Scholarly Project I
PHMD 280A.description: Provides students an opportunity to develop independent thinking, with particular focus on maturing analytical skills. Students are encouraged to develop an independent project, with a mentor, to study pharmacy-related aspects of multiple areas. First phase identifies project focus.
PHMD 280A.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 280B.title: Scholarly Project II
PHMD 280B.description: Provides students an opportunity to develop independent thinking, with particular focus on maturing analytical skills. Students develop an independent project, with a mentor, to study pharmacy-related aspects of multiple areas. Phase 2 focuses on final evaluation of project.
PHMD 280B.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 281.title: Clinical Trial Design
PHMD 281.description: Provide the basic principles for design of randomized clinical trials; provide a foundation in clinical trial phases and design; and recognize key stakeholders in clinical trials.

PHMD 282.title: Pharmacists Impact through Roles in the Pharmaceutical Industry – Trends and Needs
PHMD 282.description: Examines pharmacists’ evolving roles in the pharmaceutical industry, addressing perceptions and impact through industry-focused perspectives and examples from Research and Development, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, and Managed Care to highlight cross-functional collaboration and influence on patient outcomes.

PHMD 290.title: Doctor of Pharmacy Epilogue
PHMD 290.description: Reinforces and assesses student pharmacist’s performance on cumulative learning outcomes; pre-APPE and APPE knowledge, skills, and attitudes; entrustable professional activities; team- and practice-readiness; and to demonstrate that student pharmacists are achieving outcomes required by the ACPE.
PHMD 290.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 298.title: Research Seminar
PHMD 298.description: Designed to engage students and expose them to seminar speakers that come to discuss research or case studies in pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy.
PHMD 298.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHMD 299.title: Independent Research
PHMD 299.description: Supervised investigation and study of topics relevant to the practice of pharmacy not covered in other courses. Intended to facilitate a small number of students performing a deeper dive into topics of particular interest to them.

PHRMSCI 1.title: New Student Seminar
PHRMSCI 1.description: Weekly meetings consisting of presentations by faculty, professional staff, and Peer Academic Advisors provide information about the Pharmaceutical Sciences major, campus resources, learning skills, and special programs and opportunities.
PHRMSCI 1.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors only. New students only.

PHRMSCI 3.title: Professional Development and Careers in the Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI 3.description: Pharmaceutical Science majors select a career track and prepare for graduate program applications and careers in industry.

PHRMSCI 42.title: Life 101
PHRMSCI 42.description: Covers the latest scientific work on the impact of nutrition, exercise, and lifestyle choices on mental and physical health. Motivates students to make positive changes by fostering personal growth.

PHRMSCI 66.title: Gateway to Drugs
PHRMSCI 66.description: Introduces students to human physiology, how drugs work, and where they come from, common health issues and the drugs used to treat them, and well-known recreational drugs.

PHRMSCI 76.title: Ethical Conduct of Research
PHRMSCI 76.description: Covers the ethical responsibilities of biomedical scientists. Topics include, as discussions and case studies, the high standards of science, the responsible conduct of research, animal experimentation, and clinical trials as they relate to the pharmaceutical sciences.

PHRMSCI H80.title: Drugs and Society
PHRMSCI H80.description: Where drugs come from, how drugs work, how and why people abuse drugs, the costs of drug abuse on society, which drugs are commonly abused, and how drug abuse can be prevented and treated. Course intended for non-science majors.
PHRMSCI H80.prereq_text: Recommended: High school chemistry and biology.

PHRMSCI 90.title: The Art of Public Speaking
PHRMSCI 90.description: Teaches effective preparation and delivery of public speeches and slide presentations. Included are storytelling, informative, commemorative, and persuasive speeches, and scientific presentation. Evaluating speeches and strategies to reduce speaker apprehension is also covered.
PHRMSCI 90.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI H90.title: The Idiom and Practice of the Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI H90.description: Explores pharmaceutical sciences: the discovery, development, and safe use of medicines. Students study the drug development process from concept to product, examining interdisciplinary approaches combining biology, chemistry, physics, and engineering for human health.
PHRMSCI H90.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PHRMSCI 120.title: Human Physiology
PHRMSCI 120.description: Surveys the function of the human body. All major organ systems are discussed. Designed to prepare students for healthcare careers, such as nursing, pharmacy, and medicine, and for research careers which require basic knowledge of how the human body functions.
PHRMSCI 120.restriction: Nursing Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 120L.title: Human Physiology Lab
PHRMSCI 120L.description: Complements PHRMSCI 120. Computer-based lab simulations are used to study the function of the human body. Class meets in person for review sessions and exams.
PHRMSCI 120L.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors and Nursing Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 121.title: Human Anatomy with Pathological Correlates
PHRMSCI 121.description: Covers the forms of, and relationships between, the many anatomical components of the human body, including discussion of several pathological conditions of the body as they relate to anatomy.
PHRMSCI 121.prereq_text: BIO SCI 97 and BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99. Recommended: Organic Chemistry series is highly encouraged.
PHRMSCI 121.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 122.title: Medical Microbiology
PHRMSCI 122.description: Introduces students to microbiology, emphasizing microorganisms that are medically important and drive human disease and mortality.
PHRMSCI 122.prereq_text: BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51C and BIO SCI E109.
PHRMSCI 122.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 122L.title: Medical Microbiology Laboratory
PHRMSCI 122L.description: An introduction to the structure, metabolism, cultivation, isolation, classification, and identification of the major groups of bacteria. Additional focus on identification of infection and use of antibiotics in diseased patients.

PHRMSCI 142.title: Healthspan Sciences
PHRMSCI 142.description: Covers the complex and multi-factorial process of aging and increases the understanding of factors that contribute to enhanced lifespan, including basic principles of health and wellness and scientifically proven interventions, both pharmacological and non-pharmacological.
PHRMSCI 142.prereq_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and PHRMSCI 120.

PHRMSCI 155.title: Neuropsychopharmacology
PHRMSCI 155.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the nervous system. Fundamental knowledge for understanding the cellular and molecular actions of drugs and their mechanisms of action on synaptic transmission. Applied neuropsychopharmacology including major drug classes and therapeutic uses.

PHRMSCI 163.title: Pharmacogenomics and Epigenetics
PHRMSCI 163.description: Survey of the genetic and epigenetic basis of inter-subject variability in response to drugs. Covers drug efficacy, safety, and need for their optimization in pharmacotherapy. Emphasizes genetic mechanisms of polymorphisms in the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of representative therapeutic drugs.

PHRMSCI 170A.title: Molecular Pharmacology I
PHRMSCI 170A.description: Surveys the basis of drug-receptor action at the molecular and cellular levels. Structure-function of drug targets emphasizing enzymes, ion channels, and membrane transport proteins.
PHRMSCI 170A.prereq_text: (CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C) and (PHRMSCI 120 or BIO SCI E109).
PHRMSCI 170A.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 170B.title: Molecular Pharmacology II
PHRMSCI 170B.description: Survey of central nervous system drug mechanisms of action. Drug classes covered include anxiolytics, antidepressants, antipsychotics, hypnotics, muscle relaxants, recreational drugs, antibiotics, antihistamines, immunosuppressants, and cancer chemotherapeutics.

PHRMSCI 171.title: Physical Biochemistry
PHRMSCI 171.description: Thermodynamics and kinetic fundamentals as applied to problems relevant to pharmaceutical sciences such as receptor/enzyme-ligand interactions. Fundamentals of biophysical methods used in the pharmaceutical sciences including structure determination and biomolecular spectroscopy.
PHRMSCI 171.prereq_text: (PHYSICS 3C or PHYSICS 7E) and (CHEM 1C or CHEM H2C) and BIO SCI 99.
PHRMSCI 171.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 172.title: Special Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI 172.description: In-depth survey of special research topics intertwined with discussions of careers and graduate school opportunities in pharmaceutical sciences. Helps Pharmaceutical Sciences students select electives appropriate to their future goals.

PHRMSCI 173.title: Pharmacotherapy
PHRMSCI 173.description: An exploration of the clinical application of medications to selected disease states. Focus is on an understanding of underlying principles of pharmacology and how this knowledge can be applied to treatment of diseases.

PHRMSCI 174.title: Biologics
PHRMSCI 174.description: Introduces concepts in macromolecular drug design, production, and formulation. Topics include popular and emerging modalities (e.g., monoclonal antibodies, cellular therapies), clinical trial design, and regulatory affairs.
PHRMSCI 174.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 174L.title: Cellular Pharmacology Lab
PHRMSCI 174L.description: Introduction to tissue culture and cellular analysis technologies. Techniques include microplate cell-based assays of reporter gene expression and cytotoxicity, real-time tissue culture, fluorescence imaging microscopy, and flow cytometry. Materials Fee

PHRMSCI 175.title: Drug Discovery Computing Techniques
PHRMSCI 175.description: Techniques used in computer-aided drug discovery, including theory behind these techniques and practical applications. Topics include scientific computing; python; classical force fields and simulations; visualization and movie-making; quantum mechanics in drug discovery; molecular dynamics; solvation models; and several others.
PHRMSCI 175.prereq_text: CSE 41 or I&C SCI 31. CSE 42 or I&C SCI 32 is recommended.

PHRMSCI 177.title: Medicinal Chemistry
PHRMSCI 177.description: Surveys drug target classes; lead identification and optimization; pharmacokinetics; discovery strategies including natural product chemistry, encoded combinatorial libraries, molecular modeling, and high-throughput screening; case studies in antiviral, antibacterial, and anticancer drug discovery and development.
PHRMSCI 177.prereq_text: CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C and (BIO SCI 98 or CHEM 128). Recommended: BIO SCI 99.
PHRMSCI 177.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 177L.title: Medicinal Chemistry Laboratory
PHRMSCI 177L.description: Introduction to high-throughput experimentation for identifying bioactive compounds. Techniques include microplate assay setup, IC50 determination, quantitative assay development, library screening, and structure-activity analysis. Materials Fee
PHRMSCI 177L.prereq_text: CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C and (BIO SCI 98 or CHEM 128).
PHRMSCI 177L.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHRMSCI 179.title: Emerging Technologies in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Medicine
PHRMSCI 179.description: Introduces emerging, ground-breaking technologies in biomedical research and medicine, including pharmacogenomics, genome editing, and stem cell and engineered T cell therapies. Explores these novel technologies with both their underlying theories and forward-thinking applications.

PHRMSCI 197.title: Professional Internship
PHRMSCI 197.description: Provides students with opportunity to develop leadership and professional skills necessary for competitive placement in their chosen industry. Students gain new and field-specific skills outside the classroom environment while participating in a supervised internship for a total of 100 hours.

PHRMSCI 198.title: Independent Study in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI 198.description: Students interested in independent study should arrange with a faculty member to sponsor and supervise such work. A time commitment of three hours per week per unit is expected. A written report is required at the end of each quarter.

PHRMSCI 199.title: Undergraduate Research
PHRMSCI 199.description: Original research in the laboratory of Pharmaceutical Sciences faculty. Attendance at regular research group meetings is also generally expected, and a quarterly written report is required. Strongly recommended for students considering research careers and/or graduate degree programs.

PHRMSCI H199.title: Honors Research in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI H199.description: Undergraduate honors research in Pharmaceutical Sciences. A student time commitment of 10-15 hours per week is required.

PHRMSCI 223.title: Biological Macromolecules
PHRMSCI 223.description: Introduction to nucleic acid and protein structure, dynamics, and function. Topics include analytical methods, molecular evolution, folding, and catalysis.

PHRMSCI 241.title: Advanced Topics in Pharmacology
PHRMSCI 241.description: Application of pharmacological principles in disease therapy. Advanced pharmacological mechanisms and in-depth study of drug action. Discussion of several major drug classes/therapeutic strategies: molecular mechanisms of action, physiological consequences of administration, and clinical use.

PHRMSCI 242.title: Healthspan Sciences
PHRMSCI 242.description: Covers the complex and multi-factorial process of aging and increases the understanding of factors that contribute to enhanced lifespan, including basic principles of health and wellness and scientifically proven interventions, both pharmacological and non-pharmacological.
PHRMSCI 242.prereq_text: Recommended: Undergraduate courses in biochemistry, molecular biology, and basic physiology.

PHRMSCI 250A.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI 250A.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of pharmaceutical sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
PHRMSCI 250A.restriction: Mathematical and Computational Biology majors only.

PHRMSCI 250B.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI 250B.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of pharmaceutical sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
PHRMSCI 250B.prereq_text: PHRMSCI 250A with a minimum grade of B-.
PHRMSCI 250B.restriction: Mathematical and Computational Biology majors only.

PHRMSCI 250C.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI 250C.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of pharmaceutical sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
PHRMSCI 250C.prereq_text: PHRMSCI 250B with a minimum grade of B-.
PHRMSCI 250C.restriction: Mathematical and Computational Biology majors only.

PHRMSCI 251.title: Experimental Pharmacology
PHRMSCI 251.description: Introduction to the concepts and techniques used in pharmacological science. Molecular biology, quantitative and biochemical pharmacology, fluorescent probes, behavior, genetics, animal handling, anatomical and receptor binding analysis, methods for ion channel study, the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination of drugs.

PHRMSCI 254.title: Introduction to Pharmacology
PHRMSCI 254.description: Ligand-gated ion channels, G protein-coupled receptors, receptor tyrosine kinases, ligand-regulated transcription factors, their signaling mechanisms, trafficking, macromolecular complexes, and physiological responses.

PHRMSCI 255.title: Neuropharmacology
PHRMSCI 255.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and periphery. Molecular biology, signal transduction, transmitter synthesis, and inactivation of major neurotransmitter systems. Drugs that act on these major neurotransmitters.

PHRMSCI 256.title: Experimental Design for Pharmacologists
PHRMSCI 256.description: Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, experimental design, power, and the use of statistical computer software.
PHRMSCI 256.prereq_text: PHARM 251 with a minimum grade of B-.

PHRMSCI 257.title: Ethics in Research
PHRMSCI 257.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, handling of misconduct.
PHRMSCI 257.prereq_text: PHARM 299 with a minimum grade of B-.

PHRMSCI 263.title: Pharmacogenomics and Epigenetics
PHRMSCI 263.description: Survey of the genetic and epigenetic basis of inter-subject variability in response to drugs. Covers drug efficacy, safety, and the need for their optimization in pharmacotherapy.Emphasizes genetic mechanisms of polymorphisms in the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of representative therapeutic drugs.

PHRMSCI 272.title: Special Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHRMSCI 272.description: Current topics in pharmaceutical sciences not covered elsewhere, emphasizing emerging fields and specialized research areas. Content varies annually; multiple sections may address distinct themes.

PHRMSCI 275.title: Drug Discovery Computing Techniques
PHRMSCI 275.description: Computer-aided drug discovery methods, including scientific computing, Python-based workflows, molecular modeling, classical force fields, molecular dynamics, solvation models, quantum mechanics, visualization, and simulation-based applications in drug design.

PHRMSCI 277.title: Medicinal Chemistry
PHRMSCI 277.description: Drug target classes; lead identification and optimization; pharmacokinetics; discovery strategies including natural product chemistry, encoded combinatorial libraries, molecular modeling, and high-throughput screening; case studies in antiviral, antibacterial, and anticancer drug discovery and development; advanced readings and presentations required.

PHRMSCI 279.title: Emerging Technologies in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Medicine
PHRMSCI 279.description: Emerging technologies in biomedical research and medicine, including pharmacogenomics, genome editing, and stem cell and engineered T cell therapies; underlying theoretical frameworks and forward-looking applications; advanced readings and presentations required.

PHRMSCI 298.title: Research Seminar
PHRMSCI 298.description: Presentation and discussion of current problems and methods in teaching and research in pharmaceutical sciences.

PHRMSCI 299.title: Graduate Research
PHRMSCI 299.description: Supervised original research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

PHY SCI 5.title: California Teach 1: Introduction to Science and Mathematics Teaching
PHY SCI 5.description: First in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies. Includes supervised field experience in a K-12 classroom.
PHY SCI 5.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students, School of Physical Sciences students, School of Engineering students, and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHY SCI 9.title: Introduction to Computation for Scientists and Engineers
PHY SCI 9.description: Introduces principles, techniques, and computational tools for quantitative approach to basic problem solving in physics and engineering. Project-based course that actively explores how programming techniques are used for solving STEM real-world problems.
PHY SCI 9.prereq_text: MATH 2A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 3.

PHY SCI 80.title: Skills Development
PHY SCI 80.description: Undergraduates identify, cultivate, and practice relevant soft skills applicable to careers in mathematics and science. The focus is on career readiness, how to market oneself to future employers, and what to expect from the professional world.
PHY SCI 80.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
PHY SCI 80.restriction: School of Physical Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHY SCI 105.title: California Teach 2: Middle School Science and Mathematics Teaching
PHY SCI 105.description: Second in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies for grades 6-8. Includes supervised field experience in a middle school classroom.
PHY SCI 105.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students, School of Physical Sciences students, School of Engineering students, and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHY SCI 139W.title: Technical Writing and Communication Skills
PHY SCI 139W.description: Workshop in writing technical reports, journal articles, proposals. Oral presentations. Communicating with the public. May not be used in satisfaction of any School or departmental requirement.
PHY SCI 139W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
PHY SCI 139W.restriction: School of Physical Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHY SCI 220.title: Science Communication Skills
PHY SCI 220.description: Development of effective communication skills, oral and written presentations. Topics range from the art of creating keynote slides to strategically crafting a personal story, culminating in a live presentation to an invited audience.

PHYSICS 2.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods for Physics
PHYSICS 2.description: Provides the applied mathematics and problem solving/presentation skills necessary for success in an introductory physics sequence. Focuses on practical exercises in problem solving. Covers kinematics in one and two dimensions in detail. Additional topics include vectors, differentiation, and integration.
PHYSICS 2.prereq_text: MATH 2A or MATH 5A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3.
PHYSICS 2.restriction: PHYSICS 2 may not be taken for credit if taken after PHYSICS 7C.

PHYSICS 3A.title: Basic Physics I
PHYSICS 3A.description: Introductory physics with applications to life sciences. Vectors; motion, force, and energy.
PHYSICS 3A.prereq_text: MATH 2A or MATH 5A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 3.
PHYSICS 3A.restriction: PHYSICS 3A may not be taken for credit if taken after PHYSICS 7C.

PHYSICS 3B.title: Basic Physics II
PHYSICS 3B.description: Introductory physics with applications to life sciences. Energy and thermodynamics; waves and sound; optics.
PHYSICS 3B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 3A or AP Physics C: Mechanics with a minimum score of 5.

PHYSICS 3C.title: Basic Physics III
PHYSICS 3C.description: Introductory physics with applications to life sciences. Electricity and magnetism; electromagnetic waves; modern physics.
PHYSICS 3C.prereq_text: PHYSICS 3A or AP Physics C: Mechanics with a minimum score of 5. A score of 4 or higher on the AP Calculus BC exam

PHYSICS 3LB.title: Basic Physics Laboratory
PHYSICS 3LB.description: Practical applications of electronics and classical physics to biology. Goals include skill to use oscilloscope and other basic instrumentation. Materials Fee
PHYSICS 3LB.prereq_text: PHYSICS 3A or AP Physics C: Mechanics with a minimum score of 5.

PHYSICS 3LC.title: Basic Physics Laboratory
PHYSICS 3LC.description: Practical applications of physics to medical imaging. Topics include optics, radioactivity, and acoustics. Materials Fee
PHYSICS 3LC.prereq_text: PHYSICS 3A or AP80 with a minimum score of 5.

PHYSICS 7C.title: Classical Physics
PHYSICS 7C.description: Topics include force, energy, momentum, rotation, and gravity.
PHYSICS 7C.prereq_text: Recommended: PHYS 2 or (MATH 2D and (CHEM 1C or CHEM H2C or CHEM M3C) or CHEM M2C) or AP Physics C: Mechanics or AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism or SAT Mathematics or ACT Mathematics or passing score on self-assessment test. PHYS 2 with a grade of C or better. AP Physics C: Mechanics with a minimum score of 4. AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism with a minimum score of 4. SAT Mathematics with a minimum score of 650. ACT Mathematics with a minimum score of 27. Students are recommended to take a self-assessment test provided by the UCI Department of Physics and Astronomy.
