If the student can fairly easily answer at least 75 percent of the questions with a calculator, but no other help, then the student is ready to take Physics 7C and should enroll in it if they have completed one year of high school physics and are Math 2B ready (or have credit for Math 2B).
PHYSICS 7C.restriction: Some offerings restricted to Physics Majors.

PHYSICS 7D.title: Classical Physics
PHYSICS 7D.prereq_text: PHYSICS 7C and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4).
PHYSICS 7D.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 7E.title: Classical Physics
PHYSICS 7E.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 7LC.title: Classical Physics Laboratory
PHYSICS 7LC.description: Experiments related to lecture topics in Physics 7C. Materials Fee
PHYSICS 7LC.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 7LD.title: Classical Physics Laboratory
PHYSICS 7LD.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 14.title: Energy and the Environment
PHYSICS 14.description: The physics of society’s energy production and consumption, and of their influences on the environment. Topics include fossil and renewable energy resources; nuclear power; prospects for a hydrogen economy; efficient and environmentally benign transportation; efficient home and commercial energy usage.
PHYSICS 14.restriction: No School of Physical Sciences students.

PHYSICS 15.title: Physics of Music
PHYSICS 15.description: Introduces basic physical principles underlying generation and properties of music, including basic properties of sound waves, musical scales and temperament, musical instruments, and acoustics of music halls. No mathematics background required, but high school algebra is recommended.

PHYSICS 18.title: How Things Work
PHYSICS 18.description: Survey of the physical basis of modern technology, with an emphasis on electronics and materials. Topics include power generation and distribution, communication (radio, TV, telephone, computers, tape recorders, CD players), imaging (optics, x-rays, MRI), and modern materials (alloys, semiconductors, superconductors).

PHYSICS 19.title: Great Ideas of Physics
PHYSICS 19.description: Introduces non-science majors to physics, examining important breakthroughs and controversies. Potential topics: Einstein's Relativity; Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle; black holes; extra-dimensions; antimatter. Case studies illustrate the essential nature of scientific review and independent confirmation of results. No mathematics background required.

PHYSICS 20A.title: Introduction to Astronomy
PHYSICS 20A.description: History of astronomy. Underlying physics. Objects in the solar system and how they are studied. Properties of stars: their formation, structure, and evolution. Pulsars and black holes. Galaxies and quasars.

PHYSICS 20B.title: Cosmology: Humanity's Place in the Universe
PHYSICS 20B.description: An overview of the origin, evolution, and ultimate fate of the Universe. Galaxies and dark matter. The Big Bang and dark energy. Ancient world models.

PHYSICS 20D.title: Space Science
PHYSICS 20D.description: Space exploration. Human missions to the moon, Mars, and beyond. Space stations, observatories, and deep-space probes. Robots and drones on distant worlds. Propulsion mechanisms, rockets, space flight, and the dangers of solar radiation.

PHYSICS 20E.title: Life in the Universe
PHYSICS 20E.description: An overview of the scientific quest to discover life elsewhere in the universe. Topics include the origin of life on Earth, Mars, extra-solar planets, interstellar travel, and extra-terrestrial intelligence.

PHYSICS 21.title: Special Topics in Physics
PHYSICS 21.description: Topics addressed vary each quarter. Past topics have included physics and music, Newton, planetary science. Lectures on areas of special interest in physics used to introduce students to scientific method, fundamental laws of science, qualitative and quantitative analysis of data.

PHYSICS 50.title: Introductory Mathematical Physics
PHYSICS 50.description: Introduction to math methods for upper-division physics. Taylor and Fourier series; complex algebra; ordinary differential equations; matrices, tensors and vector spaces; eigensystems; orthogonal coordinates; vector calculus and fields. Symbolic computation with Mathematica is incorporated through-out.
PHYSICS 50.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 51A.title: Modern Physics
PHYSICS 51A.description: Wave-particle duality; quantum mechanics; special relativity; statistical mechanics.

PHYSICS 52A.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Physics
PHYSICS 52A.description: Optics: lenses, mirrors, polarization, lasers, optical fibers, interference, spectra. Materials Fee
PHYSICS 52A.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 52B.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Physics
PHYSICS 52B.description: Circuits: oscilloscope, meters, DC and AC circuits. Materials Fee
PHYSICS 52B.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 52C.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Physics
PHYSICS 52C.description: Data analysis: random and systematic errors, curve fitting; nuclear counting; quantum experiments. Error analysis: random and systematic errors, curve fitting, nuclear counting, and quantum experiments. Materials Fee
PHYSICS 52C.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 53.title: Introduction to Programming and Numerical Analysis
PHYSICS 53.description: Introduction to structured programming; in-depth training in python. Elementary numerical methods applied to physics problems.
PHYSICS 53.restriction: Physics majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PHYSICS 60.title: Thermal Physics
PHYSICS 60.description: Introduction to thermodynamics and systems of many particles. Topics include first and second laws of thermodynamics, ideal gas laws, kinetic theory, heat engines and refrigerators, thermodynamic potentials, phase transitions, dilute solutions, chemical equilibrium, and basic statistical distributions.

PHYSICS 61A.title: Modern Physics for Majors
PHYSICS 61A.description: Special relativity; Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle and wave-particle duality; the Schrödinger equation.

PHYSICS 61B.title: Modern Physics for Majors
PHYSICS 61B.description: Hydrogen atom; spin and angular momentum; multi-electron atoms and the periodic table; introductions to nuclear physics, particle physics, and cosmology.

PHYSICS 61C.title: Introduction to Astrophysics
PHYSICS 61C.description: Introduction to fundamental topics in astrophysics, including stellar structure and evolution; stellar remnants; detection and characterization of exoplanets; physics of interstellar gas and star-forming regions.

PHYSICS H80.title: Impact of World War I on Science
PHYSICS H80.description: Introduction to science in 1914 and WWI. Participants in groups of two or three will pick a preferred science; find out what happened to it during and after the war; write reports and present what they learned.

PHYSICS H90.title: The Idiom and Practice of Science
PHYSICS H90.description: A series of fundamental and applied scientific problems of social relevance. Possible topics include Newton's Law, calculus, earthquake physics, and radiation.

PHYSICS 99.title: Current Topics in Physics
PHYSICS 99.description: Designed to introduce undergraduate students to current topics in physics. Focus is discussion of selected readings on current research issues.

PHYSICS 100.title: Computational Methods
PHYSICS 100.description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.

PHYSICS 106W.title: Advanced Data Acquisition, Analysis, and Scientific Writing
PHYSICS 106W.description: Introduces modern practical laboratory techniques for developing data interface devices, acquiring and analyzing data, and writing up results in manuscript format. Experiments include interfacing with instruments through software and hardware development, PID controller, Fourier analysis, and lock-in amplifier.
PHYSICS 106W.prereq_text: PHYSICS 52B and PHYSICS 194. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PHYSICS 111A.title: Classical Mechanics
PHYSICS 111A.description: One-dimensional motion and oscillations; three-dimensional motion, non-inertial coordinates, conservation laws, and Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics; rigid body motion and relativity.

PHYSICS 111B.title: Classical Mechanics
PHYSICS 111B.description: One-dimensional motion and oscillations; three-dimensional motion, non-inertial coordinates, conservation laws, and Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics; rigid body motion and relativity.

PHYSICS 112A.title: Electromagnetic Theory
PHYSICS 112A.description: Electric, magnetic, and gravitational fields and potentials; electrodynamics; mechanical and electromagnetic waves and radiation.

PHYSICS 112B.title: Electromagnetic Theory
PHYSICS 112B.description: Electric, magnetic, and gravitational fields and potentials; electrodynamics; mechanical and electromagnetic waves and radiation.

PHYSICS 113A.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYSICS 113A.description: The wave function and its interpretation; time independent and time dependent Schrödinger equation; Hilbert space and the uncertainty principle; systems in one to three dimensions; the hydrogen atom, angular momentum and spin.

PHYSICS 113B.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYSICS 113B.description: Identical particles in quantum systems; atoms and the periodic table; theories of solids; time-independent perturbation theory; fine structure of hydrogen, the Zeeman effect and hyperfine structure; the variational principle; the WKB approximation and tunneling.

PHYSICS 113C.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYSICS 113C.description: Symmetries and conservation laws in quantum mechanics; degeneracy; quantum dynamics and selection rules; scattering theory; time-dependent perturbation theory; emission and absorption of radiation; Fermi's golden rule; selected contemporary topics.

PHYSICS 115A.title: Statistical Physics
PHYSICS 115A.description: Microscopic theory of temperature, heat, and entropy; kinetic theory; multicomponent systems; quantum statistics.
PHYSICS 115A.prereq_text: PHYSICS 50 and (PHYSICS 60 or CHEM 1C or ENGRMAE 91).

PHYSICS 116.title: Relativity and Black Holes
PHYSICS 116.description: Introduces students to both special and general relativity; includes the formalism of four-vectors, equivalence principle, curved space-time, and modern issues with black holes.

PHYSICS 120.title: Electronics for Scientists
PHYSICS 120.description: Applications of modern semiconductor devices to physical instrumentation. Characteristics of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, analog and digital circuits. Materials Fee

PHYSICS 121W.title: Advanced Laboratory
PHYSICS 121W.description: Experiments in atomic, condensed matter, quantum, nuclear, particle, and plasma physics. Introduction to instrumentation, computational methods for data analysis, and a first experience in the research laboratory.
PHYSICS 121W.prereq_text: (PHYSICS 51B or PHYSICS 61B or PHYSICS 61C) and (PHYSICS 52C or PHYSICS 193) and (PHYSICS 194 or EDUC 143BW). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PHYSICS 125A.title: Mathematical Physics
PHYSICS 125A.description: Complex variables; Legendre and Bessel functions; complete sets of orthogonal functions; partial differential equations; integral equations; calculus of variations; coordinate transformations; special functions and series.

PHYSICS 125B.title: Mathematical Physics
PHYSICS 125B.description: Complex variables; Legendre and Bessel functions; complete sets of orthogonal functions; partial differential equations; integral equations; calculus of variations; coordinate transformations; special functions and series.

PHYSICS 133.title: Introduction to Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 133.description: Phenomena of solids and their interpretation in terms of quantum theory.

PHYSICS 134A.title: Physical and Geometrical Optics
PHYSICS 134A.description: Focuses on the practical aspects of optics and optical engineering, starting at the fundamentals. Topics include geometrical optics, ray tracing, polarization optics, interferometers, and diffractive optics.

PHYSICS 135.title: Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 135.description: Basic concepts, orbits, kinetic and fluid equations, Coulomb collisions, fluctuations, scattering, radiation.

PHYSICS 136.title: Introduction to Particle Physics
PHYSICS 136.description: Experimental techniques and theoretical concepts of high-energy phenomena: accelerators and detectors; classification of particles and interactions; particle properties; symmetries and mass multiplets; production and decay mechanisms.

PHYSICS 137.title: Introduction to Cosmology
PHYSICS 137.description: Solution of the differential equations governing the expansion of the Universe. Observational determinations of the parameters governing the expansion. Big Bang inflation, primordial nucleosynthesis, and cosmic microwave background. Dark matter, dark energy, and large-scale structure of the Universe.

PHYSICS 138.title: Astrophysics of Galaxies
PHYSICS 138.description: Introduction to the solar neighborhood, Milky Way, and other galaxies. Interstellar medium. Star formation. Stellar populations. Evolution of spiral, elliptical, and irregular galaxies. Supermassive black holes, quasars, and active galaxies. Galaxies as probes of the expansion rate of the Universe.

PHYSICS 139.title: Observational Astrophysics
PHYSICS 139.description: Telescopes and astronomical observations, imaging with CCD detectors and image processing techniques. Photometry and spectroscopy of stars, galaxies, and quasars. Advanced imaging techniques such as deconvolution, adaptive optics, and interferometry.
PHYSICS 139.prereq_text: PHYSICS 52C and (PHYSICS 53 or I&C SCI 45C or EECS 12) and PHYSICS 61C.

PHYSICS 140.title: Discoveries and Inventions of Modern Physics
PHYSICS 140.description: Introduction to phenomenology and applications of modern physics intended to complement the traditional physics curriculum, with topics from atomic physics, condensed matter, particle physics, and astrophysics such as NMR, lasers, superconductivity, semiconducting devices, quantum computing, Big Bang, etc.
PHYSICS 140.prereq_text: MATH 2E and PHYSICS 7C and PHYSICS 7D and PHYSICS 7E and PHYSICS 60 and (PHYSICS 51A or PHYSICS 61A) and PHYSICS 112A.

PHYSICS 143A.title: Lasers 1 - Oscillators and Amplifiers
PHYSICS 143A.description: Semiclassical and quantum-mechanical development of electro-magnetic interactions with matter. Atomic rate equations and amplification of light via stimulated emission in gases, solids, liquids, and plasmas. Optical components and resonators that enable production of coherent radiation from laser oscillators.

PHYSICS 143B.title: Lasers 2 - Beams and Pulses
PHYSICS 143B.description: Hermite-gaussian and Laguerre-gaussian laser beam solutions of the paraxial wave equation, characterization of laser beams, laser resonator design, ABCD matrix formalism for laser beam and laser pulse propagation, methods for ultra-short duration laser pulse formation, manipulation, amplification, and measurement.

PHYSICS 144.title: Stellar Astrophysics
PHYSICS 144.description: Stars: their structure and evolution; physical state of the interior; the Hertzprung- Russell diagram, stellar classification, and physical principles responsible for the classification; star formation; nuclear burning; giant and dwarf stars; neutron stars and black holes.
PHYSICS 144.prereq_text: (PHYSICS 51A or PHYSICS 61A) and PHYSICS 111A and PHYSICS 112A.

PHYSICS 145.title: High-Energy Astrophysics
PHYSICS 145.description: Production of radiation by high-energy particles, white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. Evolution of galactic nuclei, radio galaxies, quasars, and pulsars. Cosmic rays and the cosmic background radiation.
PHYSICS 145.prereq_text: (PHYSICS 51A or PHYSICS 61A) and PHYSICS 111A and PHYSICS 112A.

PHYSICS 146A.title: Biophysics of Molecules and Molecular Machines
PHYSICS 146A.description: Physical concepts and experimental and computational techniques used to study the structure and function of biological molecules and molecular machines with examples from enzyme action, protein folding, molecular motors, photobiology, chemotaxis, and vision.

PHYSICS 146B.title: Biophysics of Molecules and Molecular Machines
PHYSICS 146B.description: Physical concepts and experimental and computational techniques used to study the structure and function of biological molecules and molecular machines with examples from enzyme action, protein folding, molecular motors, photobiology, chemotaxis, and vision.

PHYSICS 150.title: Special Topics in Physics and Astronomy
PHYSICS 150.description: Current topics in physics. Includes topics from nano-science, biological sciences, astrophysics, and the common use of estimation across subdisciplines within physics.

PHYSICS 191.title: Field Experience in Physics Education
PHYSICS 191.description: Students develop and perform physics assemblies at neighboring public schools.

PHYSICS 192.title: Tutoring in Physics
PHYSICS 192.description: Formalizes the already existing free tutoring for the lower-division physics courses that is provided by the Society of Physics Students (SPS). Includes instructions on tutoring techniques.
PHYSICS 192.restriction: Society of Physics Students (SPS) tutoring program students only.

PHYSICS 193.title: Research Methods
PHYSICS 193.description: Explores tools of inquiry for developing and implementing science research projects. Students undertake independent projects requiring data collection, analysis, and modeling, and the organization and presentation of results. Additional topics include ethical issues and role of scientific literature.

PHYSICS 194.title: Research Communication for Physics Majors
PHYSICS 194.description: Students learn the fundamentals of communicating about research. Topics include preparing abstracts, proposals, and literature reviews. Provides preparation for presentation of independent research projects in PHYSICS 121 and PHYSICS 196.
PHYSICS 194.prereq_text: PHYSICS 61A or PHYSICS 51A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PHYSICS 195.title: Undergraduate Research
PHYSICS 195.description: Independent research under the guidance of a Physics faculty member.

PHYSICS 196A.title: Thesis in Physics I
PHYSICS 196A.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.

PHYSICS 196B.title: Thesis in Physics II
PHYSICS 196B.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.

PHYSICS 196C.title: Thesis in Physics III
PHYSICS 196C.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.

PHYSICS H196A.title: Honors Thesis in Physics I
PHYSICS H196A.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.
PHYSICS H196A.restriction: Physics majors and Campuswide Honors Collegium only. Physics Honors students only.

PHYSICS H196B.title: Honors Thesis in Physics II
PHYSICS H196B.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.
PHYSICS H196B.restriction: Physics majors and Campuswide Honors Collegium only. Physics Honors students only.

PHYSICS H196C.title: Honors Thesis in Physics III
PHYSICS H196C.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.
PHYSICS H196C.restriction: Physics majors and Campuswide Honors Collegium only. Physics Honors students only.

PHYSICS 199.title: Readings on Special Topics
PHYSICS 199.description: Readings in selected areas of Physics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PHYSICS 206.title: Advanced Data Acquisition and Analysis
PHYSICS 206.description: Introduces students to a variety of practical laboratory techniques, including lock-in, boxcar, coincidence counting, noise filtering, PID control, properties of common transducers, computer interfacing to instruments, vacuum technology, laboratory safety, basic mechanical design, and shop skills. Materials Fee

PHYSICS 207.title: Applied Physical Chemistry
PHYSICS 207.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts in molecular structure and reactivity: theory of bonding, valence and molecular orbitals; structure and reactivity in inorganic chemistry; elements in molecular group theory; nomenclature in organic chemistry; and survey of macromolecules.

PHYSICS 208.title: Math Methods
PHYSICS 208.description: Applications of mathematics to physical and chemical problems. Calculus of special functions, complex variables and vectors; linear vector spaces and eigenvalue problems. Differential equations.

PHYSICS 211.title: Classical Mechanics
PHYSICS 211.description: Variational principles, Lagrange's equations; applications to two body problems, small oscillation theory, and other phenomena. Hamilton's equations. Hamilton-Jacobi theory. Canonical transformations.

PHYSICS 212A.title: Mathematical Physics
PHYSICS 212A.description: Complex variables and integration; ordinary and partial differential equations; the eigenvalue problem.

PHYSICS 213A.title: Electromagnetic Theory
PHYSICS 213A.description: Electrostatics; magnetostatics; relativity; classical electron theory; fields in vacuum and matter; retardation; radiation and absorption; dispersion; propagation of light; diffraction; geometric optics; theories of the electric and magnetic properties of materials; scattering.

PHYSICS 213B.title: Electromagnetic Theory
PHYSICS 213B.description: Electrostatics; magnetostatics; relativity; classical electron theory; fields in vacuum and matter; retardation; radiation and absorption; dispersion; propagation of light; diffraction; geometric optics; theories of the electric and magnetic properties of materials; scattering.
PHYSICS 213B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 213A with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 214A.title: Statistical Physics
PHYSICS 214A.description: Maxwell-Boltzmann, Bose-Einstein, Fermi-Dirac statistics; ideal and imperfect gases; thermodynamic properties of solids; transport theory.

PHYSICS 214C.title: Many Body Theory
PHYSICS 214C.description: Application of field theory methods, perturbative and non-perturbative, to many particle systems; second quantization, Feynman diagrams, linear response theory, and functional integral methods applied to the ground state and at finite temperature.
PHYSICS 214C.prereq_text: PHYSICS 214A with a minimum grade of B- and PHYSICS 215A with a minimum grade of B- and PHYSICS 215B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 215A.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYSICS 215A.description: Foundations; Dirac notation; basic operators and their eigenstates; perturbation theory; spin.

PHYSICS 215B.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYSICS 215B.description: Atomic physics; scattering theory, formal collision theory; semi-classical radiation theory; many body systems.
PHYSICS 215B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 215A with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 220.title: Electronics for Scientists
PHYSICS 220.description: Applications of modern semiconductor devices to physical instrumentation. Characteristics of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, analog and digital circuits.

PHYSICS 222.title: Continuum Mechanics
PHYSICS 222.description: Introduction to the continuum limit and stress and strain tensors. Hydrodynamics of perfect fluids; two-dimensional problems, motion of incompressible viscous fluids, Navier Stokes equations. Basic elasticity theory. Description of viscoelastic materials. Introduction to nonlinear behavior instabilities.

PHYSICS 223.title: Machine Learning and Statistics
PHYSICS 223.description: Theory and practice of machine learning and statistics for physics and astronomy. Topics include: clustering, dimensionality reduction, Bayesian statistics, Markovchains, variational inference, supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks and modern deep learning architectures. Familiarity with python numerical programing assumed.

PHYSICS 228.title: Electromagnetism
PHYSICS 228.description: Maxwell’s equations, electrodynamics, electromagnetic waves and radiation, wave propagation in media, interference and quantum optics, coherent and incoherent radiation, with practical applications in interferometry, lasers, waveguides, and optical instrumentation.

PHYSICS 229A.title: Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences
PHYSICS 229A.description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.

PHYSICS 230A.title: Biophysics of Molecules and Molecular Machines
PHYSICS 230A.description: Physical concepts and experimental and computational techniques used to study the structure and function of biological molecules and molecular machines with examples from enzyme action, protein folding, molecular motors, photobiology, chemotaxis, and vision.

PHYSICS 230B.title: Biophysics of Molecules and Molecular Machines
PHYSICS 230B.description: Physical concepts and experimental and computational techniques used to study the structure and function of biological molecules and molecular machines with examples from enzyme action, protein folding, molecular motors, photobiology, chemotaxis, and vision.

PHYSICS 234A.title: Elementary Particle Physics
PHYSICS 234A.description: Overview of Standard Model theory and phenomenology. Electromagnetic, strong and weak forces, quark model, interactions with matter, particle detectors and accelerators.
PHYSICS 234A.prereq_text: PHYSICS 215B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 234B.title: Advanced Elementary Particle Physics
PHYSICS 234B.description: SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) model of strong, weak, and electromagnetic interactions. K-meson system and CP violation, neutrino masses and mixing, grand-unified theories, supersymmetry, introduction to cosmology and its connection to particle physics.
PHYSICS 234B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 234A with a minimum grade of B- and PHYSICS 235A with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 235A.title: Quantum Field Theory
PHYSICS 235A.description: Canonical quantization, scalar field theory, Feynman diagrams, tree-level quantum electrodynamics.
PHYSICS 235A.prereq_text: PHYSICS 215B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 235B.title: Advanced Quantum Field Theory
PHYSICS 235B.description: Pathintegral techniques, loop diagrams, regularization and renormalization, anomalies.
PHYSICS 235B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 235A with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 235C.title: Modern Topics in Advanced Quantum Field Theory
PHYSICS 235C.description: Quantum field theory: spinor-helicity techniques, topological objects, and symmetry breakdown.
PHYSICS 235C.prereq_text: PHYSICS 235B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 238A.title: Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 238A.description: Bonding in solids; crystal symmetry and group theory, elastic properties of crystals; lattice vibrations, interaction of radiation with matter; cohesion of solids; the electron gas; electron energy bands in solids; ferromagnetism; transport theory; semiconductors and superconductors; many-body perturbation theory.
PHYSICS 238A.prereq_text: (PHYSICS 214A with a minimum grade of B- or CHEM 232A with a minimum grade of B-) and (PHYSICS 215B with a minimum grade of B- or CHEM 231B with a minimum grade of B-).

PHYSICS 238B.title: Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 238B.description: Bonding in solids; crystal symmetry and group theory, elastic properties of crystals; lattice vibrations, interaction of radiation with matter; cohesion of solids; the electron gas; electron energy bands in solids; ferromagnetism; transport theory; semiconductors and superconductors; many-body perturbation theory.
PHYSICS 238B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 238A with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 238C.title: Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 238C.description: Bonding in solids; crystal symmetry and group theory, elastic properties of crystals; lattice vibrations, interaction of radiation with matter; cohesion of solids; the electron gas; electron energy bands in solids; ferromagnetism; transport theory; semiconductors and superconductors; many-body perturbation theory.
PHYSICS 238C.prereq_text: PHYSICS 238B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 239A.title: Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 239A.description: Basic concepts, orbits, kinetic and fluid equations, Coulomb collisions, fluctuations, scattering, radiation.

PHYSICS 239B.title: Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 239B.description: Magnetic confinement, MHD equilibrium and stability, collisional transport.
PHYSICS 239B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 239A with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 239C.title: Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 239C.description: Linear waves and instabilities, uniform un-magnetized and magnetized plasmas, non-uniform plasmas.
PHYSICS 239C.prereq_text: PHYSICS 239B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 240A.title: Galactic Astrophysics
PHYSICS 240A.description: The morphology, kinematics, and evolution of our Milky Way and other galaxies. Topics include stellar formation and stellar evolution, end states of stars (supernovae, neutron stars), the distribution of stars, interstellar gas and mass in galaxies. The Local Group.

PHYSICS 240B.title: Cosmology
PHYSICS 240B.description: An introduction to modern cosmology set within the context of general relativity. Topics include the expansion history of the Universe, inflation, the cosmic microwave background, density fluctuations, structure formation, dark matter, dark energy, and gravitational lensing.

PHYSICS 240C.title: Radiative Processes in Astrophysics
PHYSICS 240C.description: Exploration of radiation mechanisms (electron scattering, synchrotron emission, collisional excitation, and more) and radiative transfer through matter including absorption and emission. Includes such observational astrophysics topics as spectroscopic study of atoms and nuclei, X-rays, and cosmic rays.

PHYSICS 241A.title: Solar System and Extrasolar Planets
PHYSICS 241A.description: Formation, evolution, and habitability of planetary systems. Observational and theoretical study of the origin and evolution of the Solar System, present day dynamical state of the Solar System (asteroids, Kuiper Belt Objects, Oort cloud), planetary atmospheres, processes governing planetary climate.

PHYSICS 241B.title: Stellar Astrophysics
PHYSICS 241B.description: Physics of stellar interiors and equations of stellar structure. Stellar atmospheres and absorption processes. Introduction to stellar winds. Thermonuclear reactions, nucleosynthesis, and solar neutrinos. Binary stars and mass accretion. White dwarfs, supernovae, neutron stars, and black holes.
PHYSICS 241B.prereq_text: PHYSICS 242 with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 241C.title: Extragalactic Astrophysics
PHYSICS 241C.description: The physics and phenomenology of galaxies; star formation, interstellar medium, and intergalactic medium. Galaxy structure and dynamics. Galaxy evolution, stellar populations, and scaling relations; the relationship between galaxy properties and environment. Galaxy clusters and active galactic nuclei.
PHYSICS 241C.prereq_text: PHYSICS 242 with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 241D.title: Early Universe Physics
PHYSICS 241D.description: Includes a thorough quantum treatment of the generation of perturbations during inflation and various topics related to kinetic theory in an expanding Universe. Other topics include the astrophysics and cosmology of weakly interacting particles.
PHYSICS 241D.prereq_text: PHYSICS 240B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 242.title: Astro Fundamentals
PHYSICS 242.description: Introduction to topics in astrophysics including measurement of stellar properties, stellar structure and evolution, stellar remnants and supernovae, the interstellar medium, exoplanets, gravitational lensing, galactic structure, extragalactic distance measurements, and the expanding universe.

PHYSICS 243A.title: Lasers 1 - Oscillators and Amplifiers
PHYSICS 243A.description: Semiclassical and quantum-mechanical development of electro-magnetic interactions with matter. Atomic rate equations and amplification of light via stimulated emission in gases, solids, liquids, and plasmas. Optical components and resonators that enable production of coherent radiation from laser oscillators.

PHYSICS 243B.title: Lasers 2 - Beams and Pulses
PHYSICS 243B.description: Hermite-gaussian and Laguerre-gaussian laser beam solutions of the paraxial wave equation, characterization of laser beams, laser resonator design, ABCD matrix formalism for laser beam and laser pulse propagation, methods for ultra-short duration laser pulse formation, manipulation, amplification, and measurement.

PHYSICS 246.title: Special Topics in Astrophysics
PHYSICS 246.description: Outlines and emphasizes a subarea of astrophysics that is undergoing rapid development.

PHYSICS 247.title: Special Topics in Particle Physics
PHYSICS 247.description: Current topics in particle non-accelerator-based research fields.

PHYSICS 248.title: Special Topics in Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 248.description: Outlines and emphasizes a subarea of condensed matter physics that is undergoing rapid development.

PHYSICS 249.title: Special Topics in Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 249.description: Outlines and emphasizes a subarea of plasma physics that is undergoing rapid development.
PHYSICS 249.prereq_text: PHYSICS 239A with a minimum grade of B- and PHYSICS 239B with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSICS 250.title: Physics and Astronomy Communications Skills
PHYSICS 250.description: Fundamentals of effectively communicating research through written and oral platforms. Topics include writing compelling proposals and journal articles for peer review, and the development of engaging oral presentations of science results and significance to a wide range of audiences.

PHYSICS 255.title: General Relativity
PHYSICS 255.description: An introduction to Einstein’s theory of gravitation. Tensor analysis, Einstein’s field equations, astronomical tests of Einstein’s theory, gravitational waves.

PHYSICS 260A.title: Seminar in Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 260A.description: Seminar designed to acquaint students with recent advances in solid state physics. Lecturers from the Department of Physics and Astronomy (both faculty and graduate students), other UCI departments, and other institutions.

PHYSICS 260B.title: Seminar in Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 260B.description: Seminar designed to acquaint students with recent advances in solid state physics. Lecturers from the Department of Physics and Astronomy (both faculty and graduate students), other UCI departments, and other institutions.

PHYSICS 260C.title: Seminar in Condensed Matter Physics
PHYSICS 260C.description: Seminar designed to acquaint students with recent advances in solid state physics. Lecturers from the Department of Physics and Astronomy (both faculty and graduate students), other UCI departments, and other institutions.

PHYSICS 261A.title: Topics in Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 261A.description: Advanced topics in plasma physics: wave propagation, nonlinear effects, kinetic theory and turbulence, stability problems, transport coefficients, containment, and diagnostics. Applications to controlled fusion and astrophysics.

PHYSICS 261B.title: Topics in Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 261B.description: Advanced topics in plasma physics: wave propagation, nonlinear effects, kinetic theory and turbulence, stability problems, transport coefficients, containment, and diagnostics. Applications to controlled fusion and astrophysics.

PHYSICS 261C.title: Topics in Plasma Physics
PHYSICS 261C.description: Advanced topics in plasma physics: wave propagation, nonlinear effects, kinetic theory and turbulence, stability problems, transport coefficients, containment, and diagnostics. Applications to controlled fusion and astrophysics.

PHYSICS 263A.title: Seminar in Particle Physics
PHYSICS 263A.description: Discussion of advanced topics and reports of current research results in theoretical and experimental particle physics and cosmic rays.

PHYSICS 263B.title: Seminar in Particle Physics
PHYSICS 263B.description: Discussion of advanced topics and reports of current research results in theoretical and experimental particle physics and cosmic rays.

PHYSICS 263C.title: Seminar in Particle Physics
PHYSICS 263C.description: Discussion of advanced topics and reports of current research results in theoretical and experimental particle physics and cosmic rays.

PHYSICS 265A.title: Seminar in Astrophysics
PHYSICS 265A.description: Acquaints students with current research in astrophysics. Lecturers from the Department of Physics and Astronomy and from other institutions.

PHYSICS 265B.title: Seminar in Astrophysics
PHYSICS 265B.description: Acquaints students with current research in astrophysics. Lecturers from the Department of Physics and Astronomy and from other institutions.

PHYSICS 265C.title: Seminar in Astrophysics
PHYSICS 265C.description: Acquaints students with current research in astrophysics. Lecturers from the Department of Physics and Astronomy and from other institutions.

PHYSICS 266.title: Current Topics in Chemical, Applied, and Materials Physics
PHYSICS 266.description: The subjects covered vary from year to year. Connection between fundamental principles and implementations in practice in science, industry, and technology.

PHYSICS 268.title: Seminar in Systems Microbiology Research
PHYSICS 268.description: A research and journal club seminar that covers topics on bacteria and phage using approaches and principles from biology, engineering, and physics.

PHYSICS 269.title: Seminar in Teaching Physics
PHYSICS 269.description: Techniques for effective teaching. Covers active listening and student engagement, problem-solving skills, peer instruction and collaborative learning, and evaluation. Required of all new Teaching Assistants.

PHYSICS 273.title: Technical Communication Skills
PHYSICS 273.description: Development of effective communication skills, oral and written presentations, through examples and practice.

PHYSICS 291.title: Research Seminar
PHYSICS 291.description: Detailed discussion of research problems of current interest in the Department. Format, content, and frequency of the course are variable.

PHYSICS 295.title: Experimental Research
PHYSICS 295.description: With the approval of a faculty member, a student may pursue a research program in experimental physics. Typical areas include astrophysics, condensed matter physics, elementary particle physics, and plasma physics.
PHYSICS 295.restriction: School of Physical Sciences students only.

PHYSICS 296.title: Theoretical Research
PHYSICS 296.description: With approval of a faculty member, a student may pursue a research program in theoretical physics. Typical areas include astrophysics, condensed matter physics, elementary particle physics, and plasma physics.
PHYSICS 296.restriction: School of Physical Sciences students only.

PHYSICS 298.title: Physics Colloquium
PHYSICS 298.description: Seminar held each week, in which a current research topic is explored. Frequently, off-campus researchers are invited to present the seminar, and on occasion a faculty member or researcher from the Department will speak.
PHYSICS 298.restriction: School of Physical Sciences students only.

PHYSICS 299.title: Topics in Reading
PHYSICS 299.description: With special consent from a faculty member who will agree to supervise the program, a student may receive course credit for individual study of some area of physics.

PHYSICS 395.title: Laboratory Teaching
PHYSICS 395.description: Required of and limited to teaching assistants of undergraduate laboratory courses. Designed to teach the necessary skills required of teaching assistants for these courses.

PHYSICS 399.title: University Teaching
PHYSICS 399.description: Required of and limited to Teaching Assistants.

PHYSIO 200.title: Research in Physiology and Biophysics
PHYSIO 200.description: Individual research directed toward doctoral dissertation and supervised by a particular professor.

PHYSIO 200R.title: Research in Physiology and Biophysics for First-Year Students
PHYSIO 200R.description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Physiology and Biophysics for first-year Ph.D. students.

PHYSIO 208.title: Approaches in Circuit Neuroscience
PHYSIO 208.description: Introduces modern methods in circuit neuroscience and how they are used to explore questions relating to the neurological basis of animal behavior. Emphasis is on rodent models but other model systems are incorporated where relevant.

PHYSIO 215A.title: Integrative Immunology I
PHYSIO 215A.description: Provides an introduction to immunology, but focuses on providing in-depth analysis of selected topics within the broader field of immunology, including relevant research techniques, while improving critical thinking skills.

PHYSIO 215B.title: Integrative Immunology II
PHYSIO 215B.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology. Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
PHYSIO 215B.prereq_text: PHYSIO 215 with a minimum grade of B+.

PHYSIO 227.title: Immunology Journal Club
PHYSIO 227.description: Advanced topics in immunology as related to an understanding of human disease.

PHYSIO 232.title: The Physiology of Ion Channels
PHYSIO 232.description: Discusses how ion channels work (molecular/structural biophysics) and what ion channels do in diverse cell types (cell physiology). Also discusses the role of ion channels in disease, mechanisms of drug targeting ion channels, and techniques used in ion channel research.

PHYSIO 237.title: Muscle Journal Club and Research in Progress
PHYSIO 237.description: Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of current research and advancements in the field of skeletal muscle biology and disease.
PHYSIO 237.restriction: School of Medicine students, Master of Science, and Doctor of Philosophy only.

PHYSIO 252.title: Introduction to Proteomics
PHYSIO 252.description: Introduces students to concepts and methods of proteomics including protein identification, expression proteomics, and protein-protein interactions.

PHYSIO 272.title: Eye: Health and Disease
PHYSIO 272.description: Introduces the anatomic and physiological basis of vertebrate vision and disease states in which the structure and function of the eye is disrupted with emphasis on current and developing research areas.

PHYSIO 273.title: Practical Structural Biology: How to Use High-Resolution Structures to Guide Research
PHYSIO 273.description: Geared toward students who want to gain a better understanding of how to use the vast quantity of structural biology information available in publicly accessible databases to help guide their research.
PHYSIO 273.prereq_text: BIOCHEM 210A with a minimum grade of B- or BIO SCI 98 or BIO SCI M114 or BIO SCI M133 or MOL BIO 211 with a minimum grade of B- or MOL BIO 204 with a minimum grade of B-.

PHYSIO 290.title: Topics in Physiology
PHYSIO 290.description: Contemporary research problems in physiology. Students review research articles in current literature and present ideas contained therein, focusing on groundbreaking discoveries and methodologies. Students present results of their own research and attend presentations given by other students and departmental researchers.

PHYSIO 292A.title: Scientific Communication
PHYSIO 292A.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

PHYSIO 292B.title: Scientific Communication
PHYSIO 292B.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

PHYSIO 292C.title: Scientific Communication
PHYSIO 292C.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

PHYSIO 299.title: Dissertation in Physiology and Biophysics
PHYSIO 299.description: Preparation and completion of the dissertation required for the Ph.D.

POL SCI 11A.title: Introduction to Political Science: Political Analysis
POL SCI 11A.description: Presents various modes of understanding politics. Emphasis on basic approaches to political analysis, their uses in constructing theories, and their application to particular national political systems.

POL SCI 21A.title: Introduction to American Government
POL SCI 21A.description: Introduction to American political processes and institutions. Topics include elections, political participation, parties, interest groups, the Presidency, Congress, the bureaucracy, and the judiciary.

POL SCI 31A.title: Introduction to Political Theory
POL SCI 31A.description: Types of questions: What is politics? What are the theoretical and philosophical bases for different types of political arrangements? How do these perspectives get translated into reality? Among others, the works of Rousseau, Locke, Mill, and Marx are read.

POL SCI 32A.title: Dilemmas of Diversity
POL SCI 32A.description: Focuses on racial, ethnic, and gender diversity, multiculturalism, and their impact on our social and political ideals. Traces the sources of ideas about difference, equality, and toleration, and examines tensions that occur when forms of identity conflict with one another.

POL SCI 41A.title: Introduction to International Relations
POL SCI 41A.description: Analysis of political relations between and among nations with emphasis on explanations of conflict and cooperation. The role of ideologies and their relation to international problems are also examined.
POL SCI 41A.restriction: Political Science majors and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 51A.title: Introduction to Politics Around the World
POL SCI 51A.description: Introduces comparative politics. Compares political systems in a variety of countries. Includes elections, parties, parliaments, presidents, protest movements, and other aspects of national politics. Addresses how to make meaningful comparisons across countries.

POL SCI 61A.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnicity in Political Science
POL SCI 61A.description: Examines major theories that attempt to explain the roles of race and ethnicity in U.S. politics.

POL SCI 71A.title: Introduction to Law
POL SCI 71A.description: An introduction to the study of judicial politics. Questions include: what is law?; what is a court?; who are the judges? Analysis of a wide range of judicial decisions illustrates the political importance of courts in the U.S. and elsewhere.

POL SCI 111.title: Public Policy and Evaluation
POL SCI 111.description: Covers qualitative and quantitative research methods relevant for the evaluation of educational programs. Students have the opportunity to plan, execute, and write-up a small evaluation project.
POL SCI 111.prereq_text: EDUC 15 or SOCECOL 13 or STATS 7 or ANTHRO 10B or COGS 10B or SOC SCI 10B or SOCIOL 10B.
POL SCI 111.restriction: Education Sciences majors and Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 120.title: Public Opinion
POL SCI 120.description: Theories concerning sources of public opinion, processes by which it is altered, organization of citizens’ belief systems, and role of public opinion in government policy. Students analyze survey data as a research project.
POL SCI 120.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 121A.title: The American Presidency
POL SCI 121A.description: Presents a comprehensive survey of the American presidency and considers the question of political power.
POL SCI 121A.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 121C.title: U.S. Elections and Voting Behavior
POL SCI 121C.description: Examines how voters evaluate political parties, candidates, and issues in electoral campaigns to reach their decisions. Numerous controversies concerning the degree of issue voting, sophistication of candidate evaluations, and the decline of political parties are discussed.
POL SCI 121C.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 121D.title: Gender and Politics
POL SCI 121D.description: Examines the role of gender in American politics. We begin by considering women and men as citizens and voters. How do women and men differ in their political opinions and behavior?

POL SCI 121F.title: Presidents Since World War II
POL SCI 121F.description: Reviews the actions and character of presidents from Harry Truman through Bill Clinton. Each week a different president is examined from a variety of perspectives. Students are expected to write a substantial original research paper.
POL SCI 121F.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 121G.title: American Public Policy
POL SCI 121G.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

POL SCI 121HW.title: Writing for the President of the United States
POL SCI 121HW.description: Imagines how White House staffers can help presidents with clear, focused, and effective writing. Through a variety of formats, students study, hone, and practice writing skills that will prove useful in and out of the White House.
POL SCI 121HW.prereq_text: POL SCI 21A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

POL SCI 121J.title: John F. Kennedy and Lyndon B. Johnson
POL SCI 121J.description: Investigates the politics of the 60s through the lens of the presidents who defined them: John F. Kennedy (JFK) and Lyndon B. Johnson (LBJ). Studies each president’s campaign and election, options and actions, successes and failures.
POL SCI 121J.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 124A.title: The Politics of Protest
POL SCI 124A.description: Examines the Civil Rights, Black Power, and women’s movements in relationship to the Asian American movement. Uses social movement theories to illuminate the cases, and the cases to critique and revise the theories.

POL SCI 124B.title: Latinos in U.S. Politics
POL SCI 124B.description: Comparing the political issues facing Latino groups by examining their migration histories, voting behavior, nonelectoral participation, and policy issues. Latino issues are examined on the national, state, and local levels, including formal representation, immigration, affirmative action, and language policy.

POL SCI 124D.title: Black Political Thought
POL SCI 124D.description: Due to Black people’s existence on margins of Western society, Black political thought necessarily opens up new possibilities beyond the political present and towards a free future. Surveys texts that re-imagine the state beyond its current formation.

POL SCI 124E.title: African American Politics
POL SCI 124E.description: Examines politics of African Americans in order to gain a broader perspective of the American political process. Major developments in African American politics (including the civil rights movement, Black presidential bids), continuing problem of racism, responsiveness of key governing institutions.

POL SCI 125A.title: The United States Congress
POL SCI 125A.description: Does the Congress do a good job of representing the American citizenry? Is it the most appropriate mechanism for the creation, resolution, and implementation of public policy?
POL SCI 125A.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 126C.title: U.S. Immigration Policy
POL SCI 126C.description: Examines selected immigration policy debates since the nineteenth century, rationale and consequences of immigration law since 1965, problems of administration, implementation and enforcement, impact of immigration policy on foreign relations, and contemporary debate regarding the future of U.S. policy.

POL SCI 126F.title: Politics of Animal Rights
POL SCI 126F.description: Examines animal rights/welfare movement’s efforts to transform moral, practical, and legal standing of nonhuman animals in contemporary U.S. Explores intersection of racism, sexism, and speciesism informed by theories of race and ethnicity, including Asian American Studies.
POL SCI 126F.restriction: Political Science majors and Asian American Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 126G.title: Sex, Drugs, and Rock and Roll: The Politics of Prohibition
POL SCI 126G.description: Why and how does the U.S. government prohibit, regulate, or try to control sex, drugs, and rock and roll? Reveals the motivations and politically strategic decisions that underpin these governmental efforts.

POL SCI 127A.title: Mass Media and Politics
POL SCI 127A.description: Examines the ways in which news and popular media constitute a major American institution by influencing public attitudes and government outcomes. Discusses the main functions of media, and how they are shaped by the particular medium.
POL SCI 127A.prereq_text: ( MATH 2A OR AP CALCULUS AB ( min score = 4 ) OR AP CALCULUS BC ( min score = 4 ) ) AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ( min score = 4 ) ) AND ECON 100A AND ECON 100B

POL SCI 128BW.title: Political Ideologies: The Way We View Our World
POL SCI 128BW.description: Politics has become divisive and ideological. But ideologies are poorly understood and have become mere labels for identifying friends and enemies. Course analyzes the nature of ideology, focusing on liberalism, conservatism, fascism, socialism, and contemporary "liberation" ideologies.
POL SCI 128BW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

POL SCI 128C.title: Political Psychology
POL SCI 128C.description: Examination of how psychological theory and research may be used to better understand political thought and behavior. Drawing on theories of learning, cognition, and personality, discusses such topics as the formation of political attitudes, and the process of political decision-making.

POL SCI 129.title: Special Topics in American Politics and Society
POL SCI 129.description: Studies in selected areas of American politics and society. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
POL SCI 129.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 130A.title: Game Theory and Politics I
POL SCI 130A.description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.
POL SCI 130A.restriction: Social Policy and Public Service majors, Political Science majors, International Studies majors, and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 131C.title: Modern Political Theory
POL SCI 131C.description: Examines major thinkers and intellectual movements in the political thought of the 17th and 18th centuries.
POL SCI 131C.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 131F.title: Modern Political Theory
POL SCI 131F.description: Examines major thinkers and intellectual movements in the political thought of the 20th century.

POL SCI 134F.title: Social and Political Theory
POL SCI 134F.description: Focus is on recent major work in social and political theory. An in-depth analysis of a relatively small body of writing. Authors discussed include Jurgen Habermas, Anthony Giddens, and Richard Rorty.
POL SCI 134F.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 135B.title: Just War Revisited
POL SCI 135B.description: Examines the evolution of the doctrine of the just war across the history of Western political thought, the importance of changes in the doctrine and whether it applies today; examines international relations case studies to determine today's relevancy.

POL SCI 136BW.title: Cannibals and Conquistadores: The Philosophy of the Other
POL SCI 136BW.description: Examines critically the notion of the "other" by looking at the philosophical challenges difference poses in the context of the European discovery of the New World. Seeks to understand the naissance of the concept of human rights and tolerance.
POL SCI 136BW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

POL SCI 138AW.title: Moral of the Story: Introduction to Ethics
POL SCI 138AW.description: Focuses on how we learn about ethics from stories, in the form of fables, bedtime stories, religious stories, soap operas, television, and movies as adults. Students bring in stories that informed their own ethical development.
POL SCI 138AW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

POL SCI 138CW.title: Ethics of Difference
POL SCI 138CW.description: Examines differences traditionally judged politically salient—race, ethnicity, religion, gender. Personal interviews with an elderly person encourage students to understand the social construction of difference and to reexamine their own attitudes by putting themselves in the place of another.
POL SCI 138CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
POL SCI 138CW.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 138DW.title: The Moral Life During War
POL SCI 138DW.description: Can people keep their humanity during war? What does the term humanity signify when simply surviving requires faith, courage, and desperation? When facing wartime brutality, must we abrogate morality? What does it mean to compose a moral life during war?
POL SCI 138DW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
POL SCI 138DW.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 139.title: Special Topics in Political Theory and Methods
POL SCI 139.description: Studies in selected areas of political theory and methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
POL SCI 139.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 141.title: International Security
POL SCI 141.description: Introduces students to debates in the subfields of security studies, peace and conflict studies within the field of International Relations. Topics explored range from causes of war, civil wars, nuclear deterrence, human security, peacekeeping, peace processes to peace-building.

POL SCI 141B.title: International Political Economy
POL SCI 141B.description: Examination of problems in global political-economic relations through competing conceptual lenses or grand theories: mercantilism, liberalism, and Marxism. Surveys North-North and North-South issues relating power and wealth.

POL SCI 141C.title: International Political Economy of East Asia
POL SCI 141C.description: Integration of theoretical perspectives in international political economy with the study of economic development in East Asia, with special emphasis on regional integration.

POL SCI 141E.title: US Foreign Policy Toward Asia
POL SCI 141E.description: U.S. policy toward the countries of East Asia: bilateral and regional security relationships, U.S. economic relations with the major Asian countries, the development of regional institutions, and human rights.

POL SCI 142B.title: The International Relations of East Asia
POL SCI 142B.description: Surveys various aspects of relations between the nations of East Asia. Topics include the historical development of the region; current political and security relations, including the impact of the American military presence.
POL SCI 142B.restriction: Political Science majors and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 142D.title: U.S. Foreign Policy I: Globalism and Cold War
POL SCI 142D.description: Looks at changing international perspectives, policy responses, and military strategies of presidential administrations from Truman to Reagan. In assessing the motives and objectives of U.S. foreign policy leaders during the “Cold War” era, the concept of “national interest” is examined.
POL SCI 142D.restriction: Political Science majors and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 142J.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
POL SCI 142J.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

POL SCI 143D.title: East Asian Security
POL SCI 143D.description: Provides an overview of issues in East Asian security including U.S.-China relations, economic interdependence, global supply chains, South China Sea, environmental cooperation, COVID-19, and others. Includes Oxford-style debates.

POL SCI 143G.title: Homeland Security
POL SCI 143G.description: Examines the 9/11 origins of the concept of homeland security; assess the evolution, structure, and operations of the Department of Homeland Security; critically examines the evolution of threat assessment to the U.S. and the utilization of risk management methodologies.

POL SCI 147CW.title: International Humanitarianism
POL SCI 147CW.description: Examines, analyzes, and evaluates the humanitarian phenomenon, the actors involved in it (including states, international organizations (IOs), and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs)), the rise of a body of international humanitarian law, and the problems and debates associated with international humanitarianism today.
POL SCI 147CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

POL SCI 147D.title: International Organizations
POL SCI 147D.description: Active learning course that examines origins, decision-making processes, activities, and evolution of leading international organizations (e.g. U.N., NATO, EU, AU, WTO, World Bank, IMF). Activities include drafting reforms, applying theory, assessing dysfunctions, and participating in U.N. negotiation simulations.

POL SCI 147E.title: Critical Investigations into Humanitarianism in Africa
POL SCI 147E.description: Explores the complex phenomenon of aid to Africa (emergency and development aid), and the representational, cultural, historical, and other reasons why some participants and many observers critique it. Students occasionally engage with peers and faculty in African institutions.

POL SCI 148B.title: War, Peace, and Gender
POL SCI 148B.description: Focuses on the diverse ways that gender affects human security, civil wars, peacekeeping, peace processes, and post-conflict peacebuilding, among other topics in the field of peace and conflict.

POL SCI 149.title: Special Topics in International Relations
POL SCI 149.description: Studies in selected areas of international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
POL SCI 149.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 151B.title: Political Power in Contemporary China
POL SCI 151B.description: Analyzes the sources of political power in contemporary China, including historical legitimacy, political institutions, and Chinese Communist Party power. Identifies challenges to the CCP’s rule and rising socio-political issues such as mass protest, censorship, and the environment.
POL SCI 151B.restriction: Political Science majors and International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 151H.title: Voting and Political Manipulation
POL SCI 151H.description: Introduction to social choice and cooperative games. Topics include majority rule, types of voting methods, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.
POL SCI 151H.restriction: Business Economics majors, Political Science majors, International Studies majors, and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 152B.title: Gender and Power
POL SCI 152B.description: Examines the intersection of gender and development, focusing on gender influences and shapes experiences within political, economic, and social institutions. Explores why gender disparities persist in various sectors and investigates the role of gender in development outcomes.

POL SCI 152C.title: Politics of Decolonization
POL SCI 152C.description: The politics of colonization and decolonization are explored with examples from around the world. We begin looking at global political history as well as specific histories of colonial subjects in the Americas, including the United States; Africa; Asia; Europe; Mideast.

POL SCI 152D.title: Politics of Global Development
POL SCI 152D.description: Examines how politics shapes global development. Evaluates how social, political, and economic institutions influence development prospects. The guiding question is: What political factors help explain patterns of development – pertaining to health, education, prosperity, and security?

POL SCI 152F.title: Politics of Genetics
POL SCI 152F.description: The politics of identity, especially the politics of genetic identity are explored. Begins with a discussion of the politics of identity including especially racial and ethnic identity. How do these identities matter for politics, if at all?

POL SCI 152JW.title: Political Economy of Development
POL SCI 152JW.description: Why are some countries rich and some countries poor? In Political Economy of Development, students assess and evaluate competing hypotheses on what drives social, economic, and political development around the world.

POL SCI 152K.title: Immigration Politics
POL SCI 152K.description: Examines immigration politics in advanced democracies, analyzing trends and policy from the postwar period through to today. Topics include citizenship, immigrant integration, asylum, the far-right, and a rotating focus on contemporary issues, e.g., terrorism, birthright citizenship.

POL SCI 153G.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
POL SCI 153G.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

POL SCI 154F.title: Peoples and Cultures of Post-Soviet Eurasia
POL SCI 154F.description: Examines the cultures and political conflicts of the more than 130 indigenous ethnic groups in the European and Asian territories of the former U.S.S.R. Emphasis is on the theoretical issues of ethnicity, nationalism, and conflict management.

POL SCI 154G.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
POL SCI 154G.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

POL SCI 154H.title: Arab Uprisings
POL SCI 154H.description: Examines political mobilization against authoritarian rule in individual Arab countries, explaining specific outcome in each. Addresses the movement’s second wind nearly a decade later, which affected a new subset of Arab countries.
POL SCI 154H.restriction: Formerly offered under SOC SCI 189 / INTL ST 179 / POL SCI 149.

POL SCI 154J.title: Jews and Power
POL SCI 154J.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority?

POL SCI 154K.title: Antisemitism
POL SCI 154K.description: Covers the key concepts, sources, and dynamics of historical and contemporary antisemitism. Topics covered include the politics of anti-Jewish hatred, conspiracy theories, and the Holocaust.

POL SCI 154KW.title: US Government in Comparative Perspective
POL SCI 154KW.description: Introduction to the United States in comparative perspective, covering general features of the United States and other countries, such as institutional design and policy choices. Addresses the debates about American exceptionalism and American decline.
POL SCI 154KW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
POL SCI 154KW.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 155A.title: Failed States
POL SCI 155A.description: What is a “failed” state? How is it measured? Covers the theories, processes, and outcomes of state fragility and failure from both comparative politics and international relations perspective.

POL SCI 155B.title: Making Government Work
POL SCI 155B.description: Government, whether democratic or not, is expected to provide public goods and services to its citizens. With a limited budget but potentially unlimited needs and wants from its citizens, how best should government decide which goods and services to provide.

POL SCI 155C.title: Organizations
POL SCI 155C.description: How bureaucracies, formal organizations, and voluntary associations work, how/why they grow, and where they are going. History and structure of organizational rationality; dynamics of organized groups; behavior in organizations; limits of bureaucratization and attempts to overcome these limits through decentralization.
POL SCI 155C.restriction: Political Science majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 156B.title: Political Violence
POL SCI 156B.description: Designed to provide the student with advanced knowledge of main theoretical issues surrounding violence in politics. Although violence is virtually everywhere in political life, focuses especially on the causes and consequences of genocide and war.

POL SCI 156D.title: Protests, Movements, and Revolutions
POL SCI 156D.description: A survey of models of collective action drawn from sociology, economics, psychology, and political science. Focus on areas such as social movements, strikes, crowd psychology, cults, fads, fashions, public opinion, and symbolic and mythical elements in collective culture.
POL SCI 156D.prereq_text: SOCIOL 1 or POL SCI 11A or ECON 1.
POL SCI 156D.restriction: Political Science majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 157B.title: International Divided Cities
POL SCI 157B.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

POL SCI 158D.title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
POL SCI 158D.description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

POL SCI 159.title: Special Topics in Comparative Politics
POL SCI 159.description: Studies in selected areas of comparative politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
POL SCI 159.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 171AW.title: Law and Society
POL SCI 171AW.description: Law and its various roles in society. The nature and meaning of law; legality and power in the American system; law as a mechanism for social change; the role of law in dispute processing, social control, compliance with judicial decisions.
POL SCI 171AW.prereq_text: POL SCI 71A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
POL SCI 171AW.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 172A.title: International Law
POL SCI 172A.description: Examination of the origin, changing structure, application of international law, and the role of legal norms in regulating the behavior of states and maintaining international order.

POL SCI 173A.title: Law and Race
POL SCI 173A.description: American political culture is principled upon the self-evident truth that all people are created equal, held equal before the law, and that human rights are inalienable and inviolable. Surveying American legal history and addresses whether it is actually practiced.

POL SCI 174A.title: Civil Liberties
POL SCI 174A.description: Political analysis of selected Supreme Court cases involving claims under the Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment. Topics include: race, sex, and other forms of discrimination; criminal justice; privacy; freedom of speech and related claims.
POL SCI 174A.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 174B.title: Justice
POL SCI 174B.description: Explores questions related to the endlessly complex concept of justice. Studies various theories of justice (utilitarian, libertarian, Kantian, egalitarian), elements of justice (rights, freedom, equality, virtue, fairness), institutions of justice (state) and frameworks of justice.

POL SCI 174C.title: U.S. Supreme Court
POL SCI 174C.description: Overview and analysis of the role played by the U.S. Supreme Court in the American political system. Judicial review, appointment of justices, judicial activism and judicial restraint, process of case selection, court deliberation, land decision-making, impact of Supreme Court decisions.
POL SCI 174C.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 174CW.title: U.S. Supreme Court
POL SCI 174CW.description: Overview and analysis of the role played by the U.S. Supreme Court in the American political system. Judicial review, appointment of justices, judicial activism and judicial restraint, process of case selection, court deliberation, land decision-making, impact of Supreme Court decisions.
POL SCI 174CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
POL SCI 174CW.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI 175A.title: Art of Trial Law
POL SCI 175A.description: A hands-on introduction to trial advocacy and the Rules of Evidence, modeled after traditional law school evidence courses but focused on practical application. Using a fictional case, students break down the components of a trial.

POL SCI 179.title: Special Topics in Public Law
POL SCI 179.description: Studies in selected areas of public law. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
POL SCI 179.restriction: Political Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

POL SCI H180D.title: Honors Seminar in Political Science
POL SCI H180D.description: Course for students enrolled in the Honors Program in Political Science.
POL SCI H180D.prereq_text: Only open to students in the Political Science Honors Program.

POL SCI H182A.title: Honors Thesis Workshop
POL SCI H182A.description: A weekly seminar/workshop to facilitate the exchange of ideas and research strategies among students and to review their progress in writing the thesis.
POL SCI H182A.restriction: Open only to students in the Political Science Senior Thesis program.

POL SCI 190.title: Senior Thesis
POL SCI 190.description: Thesis research with Political Science faculty.

POL SCI 190W.title: Senior Thesis
POL SCI 190W.description: Thesis research with Political Science faculty.
POL SCI 190W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

POL SCI 198.title: Directed Group Study
POL SCI 198.description: Directed group study with Political Science faculty.

POL SCI 199.title: Independent Study
POL SCI 199.description: Independent study or research with a Political Science faculty member.

POL SCI 200.title: Research Design
POL SCI 200.description: Introduces the fundamentals of research design. The central goal is to train students to conduct and evaluate research design for qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-method work. Topics range from case selection to disciplinary standards of replication and transparency.

POL SCI 210.title: Colloquium
POL SCI 210.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations. This workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and discussions regarding research with departmental faculty.

POL SCI 211A.title: Introduction to Statistics for Political Science I
POL SCI 211A.description: Serves as the foundational introduction to quantitative methods for political science research. Prioritizes developing a deep understanding of statistical concepts, enabling students to intuitively grasp what statistical output means and how to apply it.

POL SCI 211B.title: Introduction to Statistics for Political Science II
POL SCI 211B.description: Provides an overview of fundamental notions and recent advancements in quantitative social science, with focus on how data- driven approaches can be used to better understand the political world and test theories of politics and political behavior.
POL SCI 211B.prereq_text: POL SCI 211A with a minimum grade of B.

POL SCI 211C.title: Introduction to Statistics for Political Science III
POL SCI 211C.description: Builds on POL SCI 211B, focusing on more advanced statistical techniques essential for research in political science. It aims to deepen understanding of theoretical underpinnings of statistical models and equip students with practical skills to apply methods.
POL SCI 211C.prereq_text: POL SCI 211B with a minimum grade of B.

POL SCI 212.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
POL SCI 212.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

POL SCI 212B.title: Ethics Workshop
