POL SCI 212B.description: Students find an important question in ethics, search literature to assess topic's importance, post question to be researched, propose method of analysis and type of data, analyze data, and note how their works contribute to knowledge in the field.

POL SCI 219.title: Special Topics in Politics and Society
POL SCI 219.description: Current research in politics and society.

POL SCI 220.title: American Politics Field Seminar
POL SCI 220.description: Introduces students to some of the major works, questions, and debates that have defined the subfield in American political behavior and political institutions.

POL SCI 221A.title: Public Policy
POL SCI 221A.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst. Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.

POL SCI 229.title: Special Topics in American Politics
POL SCI 229.description: Current research in American Politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

POL SCI 230A.title: Theory Field Seminar: Political Epistemology
POL SCI 230A.description: Focuses on fundamental issues of knowledge in the study of politics, especially interconnections and tensions between politics and knowledge. Counts as the Field Seminar in Political Theory.

POL SCI 230B.title: Theory Field Seminar: Theories of Textual Interpretation
POL SCI 230B.description: Examination of different theories of textual interpretation, including Straussian, hermeneutical, poststructuralist, feminist, postcolonial, and critical race theories. Key questions include: How does one go about the task of interpreting texts? What makes one interpretation better or more insightful than another?

POL SCI 239.title: Special Topics in Political Theory
POL SCI 239.description: Current research in political theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

POL SCI 240.title: International Relations Field Seminar
POL SCI 240.description: Overview of the major theories guiding research and scholarship in international relations. Focus on major conceptual approaches (realism, neoliberalism, marxism) and levels of analysis (systemic, state, and subnational), as well as on methodological/epistemological debates engulfing the field.

POL SCI 241E.title: Research Design in International Relations
POL SCI 241E.description: Surveys research design primarily through substantive readings in international relations. The purpose is to familiarize students with choices/dilemmas relevant to IR-specific research. Students at various stages in the graduate program and with different methodological orientations are welcome.

POL SCI 242.title: International Political Economy
POL SCI 242.description: Politics of cross-border flows of money, goods, and services, with an emphasis on how ideas, institutions, interests, and structures shape the global distribution of resources in ways that can variously challenge or reinforce power dynamics and inequality.

POL SCI 249.title: Special Topics in International Relations
POL SCI 249.description: Current research in international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

POL SCI 250.title: Comparative Politics Field Seminar
POL SCI 250.description: Introduces students to the political science subfield of comparative politics. Readings draw from leading theoretical approaches, including structural, institutional, rational choice, and cultural perspectives, and covers a range of substantive topics, like the state, regimes, identity, and representation.

POL SCI 252.title: Introduction to Voting Theory
POL SCI 252.description: Introduction to voting models. Substantive topics include majority rule, voting methods and their properties, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

POL SCI 254A.title: Introduction to Game Theory
POL SCI 254A.description: Introduction to non-cooperative games. The prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, sequential games, subgame perfection. Applications include collective action, agenda-setter models, spatial competition of political parties, models of revolution and arms race.

POL SCI 259.title: Special Topics in Comparative Politics
POL SCI 259.description: Current research in comparative politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

POL SCI 290.title: Dissertation Research
POL SCI 290.description: Dissertation research with Political Science faculty.

POL SCI 299.title: Independent Study
POL SCI 299.description: Independent research with Political Science faculty.

PORTUG 243.title: Studies in Luso-Brazilian Literature and Culture
PORTUG 243.description: Critical analysis of selected literary works from Portugal and/or Brazil. Contextualizes the works within their historical and literary specificity, and discusses pertinent theoretical issues raised by them. Taught in Portuguese.

PSY 9.title: Introduction to Psychology
PSY 9.description: Introduction to field of psychology, addressing the application of scientific methods to the study of human development, learning, memory, problem solving, perception, biological mechanisms, emotions and motivation, personality, psychopathology, and effects of diverse social and cultural contexts on human behavior.
PSY 9.prereq_text: NO COGS 7A AND NO COGS 9A AND NO COGS 9B AND NO PSCI 11A AND NO PSCI 11B AND NO PSCI 11C AND NO COGS 9C
PSY 9.restriction: No Cognitive Sciences majors, No Psychology majors, and No Psychological Science majors.

PSY 21.title: Psychology Foundations 1
PSY 21.description: Covers several important areas of psychology: brain and behavior, sensation and perception, consciousness learning, memory, thinking, language, cognitive development, and social development.
PSY 21.prereq_text: NO COGS 9A AND NO PSCI 11A AND NO PSCI 11B
PSY 21.restriction: Psychology majors and Psychological Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 22.title: Psychology Foundations 2
PSY 22.description: Introduces central areas of psychology, including research methods, motivation and emotion, health and well-being, social psychology, personality psychology, abnormal psychology, therapies, and industrial/organizational psychology.
PSY 22.restriction: Psychology majors and Psychological Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 100.title: Special Topics in Social Behavior
PSY 100.description: Course content varies with interest of instructor.
PSY 100.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 101D.title: Life Span Developmental Psychology
PSY 101D.description: Addresses the major issues, concepts, and methods of life span developmental psychology. The fundamental theories, distinctive methods, and the physical, perceptual, cognitive, social, motivational, and emotional development for each developmental phase of the life course are considered.
PSY 101D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 11B or COGS 7A or COGS 9B or PSY 22.
PSY 101D.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 102C.title: Abnormal Psychology
PSY 102C.description: Survey of disorders organized by the diagnostic categories of the American Psychiatric Association. Interdisciplinary orientation combines environmental, psychological, and organic perspectives on etiology and treatment.
PSY 102C.prereq_text: Recommended: (PSY 9 or PSY 11C or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22) and SOCECOL 10.
PSY 102C.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 103H.title: Health Psychology
PSY 103H.description: Theory and research are considered as they contribute to an understanding of the role of psychological processes in health and illness. The distinction between prevention and treatment of illness is established, and a variety of psychosocial interventions are elaborated.
PSY 103H.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 11C or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 103H.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 104S.title: Social Animal: An Introduction to Social Psychology
PSY 104S.description: Theories and research exploring social behavior and social influences on behavior. Topics include methods of social research, attitude formation and change, social perception, the social self, stereotypes and prejudice, conformity, obedience, altruism, aggression, interpersonal relationships and love, and group behavior.
PSY 104S.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 11C or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 104S.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 110D.title: Infant Development
PSY 110D.description: Study of human development from conception through the first two years of life, covering processes and events in the domains of physical, social, and cognitive development.
PSY 110D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 11B or COGS 7A or COGS 9B or PSY 21.
PSY 110D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 111D.title: Child Development
PSY 111D.description: Examines social, emotional, and intellectual growth and development between the ages of 2 and 12 years.
PSY 111D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 11B or COGS 7A or COGS 9B or PSY 21.
PSY 111D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 111W.title: Advanced Research Methods
PSY 111W.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
PSY 111W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PSY 112D.title: Adolescent Development
PSY 112D.description: Examines current research on the biological, social, and cultural contexts of adolescent development. Topics include the impacts of puberty, adolescents' decision-making competencies, changes in family and peer relationships, identity development, and psychosocial problems such as depression and problem behavior.
PSY 112D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 9B or COGS 7A or PSY 21.
PSY 112D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 114D.title: Psychology of Aging
PSY 114D.description: Students learn to 1) identify the characteristics, strengths, and difficulties associated with aging; 2) differentiate normal aging from problems and diseases associated with decline; and 3) apply biological, psychological, and sociocultural theories to aging and geriatric care.
PSY 114D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 115D.title: Cognitive Development
PSY 115D.description: Examines theories on nature of cognitive development. Discusses behaviorist theories on role of the environment including those of Vygotsky and Piaget, and recent evidence from cognitive psychologists stressing the importance of knowledge and skills within specific domains.
PSY 115D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9B or PSY 21.
PSY 115D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 116D.title: Human Development and Cross-Cultural Perspectives
PSY 116D.description: Human development in diverse cultures (e.g., Asian, American, and African). Special emphasis on East-West contrasts and when East meets West (i.e., Asian-American experiences). Topics include parenting, family relations, language and cognition, schooling and academic achievement, and morality.
PSY 116D.prereq_text: Recommended: (PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9B or PSY 22) and SOCECOL 10.
PSY 116D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 118D.title: Human Sexuality
PSY 118D.description: A broad survey of human sexuality encompassing genetic factors, physiological and anatomical development, customary and atypical forms of behavior, reproductive processes, and cultural determinants.
PSY 118D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9B or PSY 21.
PSY 118D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 121D.title: Work and Family
PSY 121D.description: Effects of employment and unemployment on mental health and marital quality; effects of work on parenting and child development; corporate and social policies for "families that work"; young adults' decision-making about work and family.
PSY 121D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 121D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 122D.title: Psychology of Success
PSY 122D.description: What does success mean to you, and what factors contribute to it? Framed by these questions, explore success in college and beyond as a window into exciting topics and theories across several subdisciplines of psychology.
PSY 122D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 123D.title: In Search of the Perfect School
PSY 123D.description: Explores how to define and create a “perfect” school. Guided by these overarching questions, students are introduced to theory and research in both psychology and education, focusing on the application of developmental and educational psychology.
PSY 123D.restriction: Psychology majors, Psychological Science majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 126D.title: Development of Motivation Across the Lifespan
PSY 126D.description: Introduces major concepts in life-span development of motivation and self-regulation, and discusses exemplar empirical findings pertaining to these concepts during the various phases of life. Students participate in discussion, present findings from research articles, and write a paper.
PSY 126D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors only.

PSY 127D.title: Attachment Relationships
PSY 127D.description: Students learn about the development of attachment-related needs throughout development, as well as the links between attachment and emotion, psychopathology and treatment. Lectures emphasize classic as well as cutting-edge research and are supplemented by primary source readings.
PSY 127D.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9A or COGS 9B or PSY 21.
PSY 127D.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 136H.title: Behavioral Medicine
PSY 136H.description: Examines biobehavioral aspects of health and illness, focusing on how stress contributes to or exacerbates disease processes. Background information on psychosomatic medicine and stress models and detailed examination of specific organ systems emphasizing the reactivity of these systems to stress.
PSY 136H.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 136H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 137H.title: Human Stress
PSY 137H.description: Stress as a multidisciplinary topic. Biological, psychological, and sociological approaches to adaptation-related disorders. Effects of acute and chronic stress on emotions, physiology, and behavior. Methods of stress assessment, stress reduction, and intervention.
PSY 137H.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 137H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 138H.title: Child Health Psychology
PSY 138H.description: Exploration of psychological antecedents, concomitants, and consequences of medical illnesses in children. Children's beliefs about health, illness, and medication; the role of stress; coronary-prone behavior; therapeutic adherence and physician-patient interaction; coping with chronic illness; effects of child's illness on family.
PSY 138H.prereq_text: Recommended: (PSY 9 or COGS 9C or COGS 7A or PSY 22) and SOCECOL 10.
PSY 138H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 139H.title: Clinical Sport Psychology
PSY 139H.description: An interdisciplinary introduction to clinical sport psychology, that includes, among other things, an introduction to psychopathology in sport; plus the use of psychological skills training, including anxiety reduction techniques, visualization, self-efficacy, coping skills, concentration, and goal-setting in sports.
PSY 139H.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 139H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 140H.title: The Hardiness Approach to Stress Management
PSY 140H.description: New development within psychology involving a combination of motivations and skills that extensive research has shown enhances performance, conduct, morale, stamina, and health. Combines study of hardiness research with strategies for improvement of personal hardiness through a series of exercises.
PSY 140H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 141H.title: Clinical Health Psychology
PSY 141H.description: Behavioral role in etiology, treatment, and prevention of certain diseases. Behavioral intervention including biofeedback, stress-, pain-management, health habit counseling, and other skills to assist patients make cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes needed to cope with disease or achieve better health.
PSY 141H.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 141H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Public Health Policy majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 143H.title: The Science and Practice of Wellness and Resilience
PSY 143H.description: Wellness is a common, but elusive goal. Covers the history, theory, psychology, and behavioral science behind skills for wellness and resilience. Provides opportunities to practice the strategies to help further understanding of the behavioral nature of each of the areas.
PSY 143H.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 143H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors only.

PSY 144H.title: Health and Social Relationships
PSY 144H.description: Theoretical and empirical arguments for an association between health and social relationships are highlighted. The complexities of this association based on relationship type and context, attachment, gender, culture, sexuality, age, and other factors are also highlighted.
PSY 144H.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 150C.title: Clinical Psychology
PSY 150C.description: Overview of theories, assessment techniques, research methodologies, and intervention approaches in clinical psychology. Psychodynamic, behavioral, humanistic, and cognitive perspectives are examined along with ethical and professional issues.
PSY 150C.prereq_text: Recommended: (PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22) and PSY 102C.
PSY 150C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 152C.title: Clinical Child Psychology
PSY 152C.description: Examines research and theory concerning childhood psychopathology behavior disorders. Diagnosis and assessment, early identification of high-risk children, fears and phobias, antisocial behavior, childhood psychoses, autism, depression, attention deficit/hyperactivity disorders, and ethical and policy implications of identifying children who are different.
PSY 152C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 152C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 153C.title: Developmental Psychopathology
PSY 153C.description: Research and theory of origins, course, and outcomes of disordered behavior. Continuity and change in patterns of behavior; environmental challenges and buffers; stress/competence in children; vulnerable/invincible children; children of mentally ill parents; families at risk; childhood antecedents of adult disorders.
PSY 153C.prereq_text: Recommended: (PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22) and SOCECOL 10.
PSY 153C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 154C.title: Cognitive Behavior Therapy
PSY 154C.description: Presentation of principles and procedures of therapeutic interventions based on cognitive-behavior methods. Cognitive factors in learning, emotional arousal, psychological disorder, and psychotherapy reviewed. Introduces the application of cognitive behavioral methods to problems of depression, anxiety, anger, pain, and impulsivity.
PSY 154C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or (COGS 9A and COGS 9C) or (PSY 21 and 22).
PSY 154C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 155C.title: Child Therapies
PSY 155C.description: Examines research methodologies, empirical data, and implications of diverse intervention strategies. Primary topics include psychotherapy process and outcome, family therapies, behavioral intervention, cognitive behavior modification, pediatric psychopharmacology, and ethical and social policy implications of intervening in other people's lives.
PSY 155C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PSY 155C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 156C.title: Forensic Psychology: Advanced Seminar
PSY 156C.description: Focuses on the psychology of criminal offending, particularly violent behavior. Examines violence, sexual offending, and mental disorder related to crime with regard to clinical assessment and treatment; mental health services within forensic institutions.
PSY 156C.prereq_text: (PSY 9 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C) and PSY 102C and (PSY 161C or CRM/LAW C160). Interview required
PSY 156C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 159C.title: Clinical Neuropsychology
PSY 159C.description: Introduces key concepts and case studies in clinical neuropsychology. Instruction focuses on neuropsychological concepts underlying brain-behavior relationships and their assessment in clinical case examples; and psychological science as relates to brain injuries/diseases impacting higher mental functions (e.g., memory).
PSY 159C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors only.

PSY 160C.title: Clinical Neuroscience
PSY 160C.description: An introduction to the neuroclinical bases of human behavior, including neuropsychological approaches to mental disorders. Also includes case formulations, research articles, therapeutic approaches, and other discussions related to select psychopathology and other neurobehavioral topics.
PSY 160C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or PSY 21 or COGS 9A or BIO SCI 99.
PSY 160C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, Social Ecology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 161C.title: Forensic Psychology
PSY 161C.description: Forensic psychology is the interface between clinical psychology and the law. Emphasizes clinically relevant legal topics (insanity defense; competency to stand trial) and includes critical thinking about issues that arise when psychologists are involved in legal proceedings.
PSY 161C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 21 or PSY 22.
PSY 161C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 162C.title: Psychodynamic Studies
PSY 162C.description: Introduction to contemporary psychodynamic studies. Emphasis on clinical concepts associated with psychodynamic psychotherapy, including unconscious determinants of behavior, typical defenses, life experiences, and techniques. Exploration of links between psychodynamic-oriented psychotherapy and other disciplines (e.g., psychology, music, medicine, neuroscience, film).
PSY 162C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C.
PSY 162C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 163C.title: Human Neuropsychology
PSY 163C.description: A survey of human brain disorders using a clinical case study approach to illustrate fundamental issues in studying brain and behavior. Topics include sensory deficits, attentional neglect, amnesia, cortical organization, clinical psychopathology, and more.
PSY 163C.prereq_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or COGS 9A.
PSY 163C.restriction: Cognitive Sciences majors, Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and School of Biological Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 164C.title: Addiction
PSY 164C.description: Designed for those with an interest in the nature and treatment of addiction. Focuses on the etiology and treatment of addiction, but does not prepare students to treat substance abuse disorders.
PSY 164C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 21 and PSY 22 and PSY 102C.
PSY 164C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 166C.title: Pets and Human Behavior
PSY 166C.description: Introduction to evolution, evidence, narratives, and clinical benefits of ethical human-animal interactions and resulting relationships to support positive health and well-being in humans. Focus is on mutually-beneficial bonds between people and animals, including cats and dogs, and other identified animals.
PSY 166C.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or PSY 22
PSY 166C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 167C.title: Biological Psychology
PSY 167C.description: Introduces the principal theories, concepts, phenomena, and methods of biological psychology, the study of the effects of biological systems and processes on the behavior of individuals which integrates knowledge from neuroscience, cellular biology, psychology, and development.
PSY 167C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 168C.title: Personality Disorders
PSY 168C.description: The history of personality disorder classification; defining characteristics of each disorder; the causes, courses, and outcomes of personality disorders; and information regarding assessment, prevention, and treatments of these disorders.
PSY 168C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, Social Ecology majors, and Cognitive Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 169C.title: Psychosis
PSY 169C.description: Describes the origins, development, assessment, neurological correlates, and treatment of psychosis spectrum disorders. Emphasis is placed on early onset, early identification, and early psychosocial interventions of the disorders.
PSY 169C.prereq_text: Recommended: COGS 9C or PSY 22, and PSY 102C
PSY 169C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 171S.title: Environmental Psychology
PSY 171S.description: Impact of the physical environment on individual and group behavior. Three basic concerns examined: (a) environmental determinants of behavior at the individual and interpersonal level; (b) social planning and urban design; (c) methodological approaches to the study of environmental issues.
PSY 171S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 173S.title: Social Relationships
PSY 173S.description: Examines major issues, concepts, and methods in the scientific study of social relationships. Topics include relationship formation and dissolution, friendships and love relationships, loneliness, bereavement, societal influences on close relationships, significance of close relationships for health and well-being.
PSY 173S.prereq_text: Recommended: SOCECOL 10 and (PSY 9 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C).
PSY 173S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 174S.title: Error and Bias in Social Judgement
PSY 174S.description: Examines how people encode, reason about, and remember social information and explores how biases and shortcomings in social perception, judgment, and memory are central to understanding both effective social functioning and many forms of maladaptive behavior and social conflict.
PSY 174S.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C.
PSY 174S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 176S.title: Motivation
PSY 176S.description: History, major theories, methods, and applications of motivational psychology, with emphasis on European approaches. Origins of the field in personality, learning, cognition, and activation research. Recent innovations in motivational and volitional self-recognition. Current approaches, major debates, empirical research programs.
PSY 176S.prereq_text: Recommended: (PSY 9 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C) and PSY 101D and PSY 104S.
PSY 176S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 178S.title: Violence in Society
PSY 178S.description: Current theory and research on aggression; anger and violence as problems in individual and social functioning. Process and functions of anger examined with regard to normal behavior and psychopathology. The determinants, prevalence, and implications of violence in society are analyzed.
PSY 178S.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9C.
PSY 178S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 179S.title: Cultural Psychology
PSY 179S.description: An examination of culture's influence on human minds. Topics include culture's impact on perception, cognition, motivation, emotion, moral reasoning, communication, and health. Addresses cultural psychology's methods, history, and place within psychology and related fields.
PSY 179S.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or PSY 21 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9B or COGS 9C.
PSY 179S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 180S.title: Psychology of Judgment and Decision Making
PSY 180S.description: Principles of judgment and rational decision making, and psychological underpinnings of how people often deviate from these principles are discussed.
PSY 180S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 181S.title: Psychology of Social Inequality
PSY 181S.description: Reviews contemporary research on the social psychology of inequality. Specifically, examines the origins of inequality and how social class, ethnic/racial, gender, and other group differences are created, perceived, and upheld.
PSY 181S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 182S.title: Psychology for a Better Society
PSY 182S.description: Covers how basic concepts from behavioral research in social psychology can shape policy formulation and implementation. Central themes include human judgment and decision-making, and how motives as well as situational forces can affect people’s choices and behavior.
PSY 182S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 183S.title: Social Epidemiology
PSY 183S.description: Overviews evidence linking environmental factors to mental and physical disorders including such variables as socioeconomic status, income inequality, work stress, job loss, social capital, location, and other demographic characteristics. Measurement and research design issues of both individual and aggregate levels.
PSY 183S.prereq_text: Recommended: (COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22) and SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13.
PSY 183S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Public Health Policy majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 184S.title: Positive Psychology
PSY 184S.description: The field of positive psychology focuses on what is right and positive about people and institutions. Introduces findings associated with human strengths and positive emotions, and provides clinical and personal applications and implications.
PSY 184S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 185S.title: Industrial-Organizational Psychology
PSY 185S.description: Examines the application of social psychology to organizational settings. Topics include motivation of workers, group decision-making, leadership styles, career management, and organizational development.
PSY 185S.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 21 or PSY 22 or COGS 7A or COGS 9A or COGS 9B or COGS 9C.
PSY 185S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 186S.title: Chicano/Latino Families
PSY 186S.description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

PSY 188S.title: Evolutionary Psychology
PSY 188S.description: Understanding our evolutionary origins is critical to truly understanding the complexities of human psychology. Explores how Darwinian principles, applied to both genes and culture, can help us understand not just how the mind works, but why.
PSY 188S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 189S.title: The Science and Practice of Compassion
PSY 189S.description: Explores the latest scientific research on compassion and its correlates, and considers practical strategies for increasing compassion in everyday life. Students discover how cutting-edge research is yielding insights into kindness, empathy, altruism, and compassion.
PSY 189S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 190.title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
PSY 190.description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.
PSY 190.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 192P.title: Latinas and Chronic Illness: Cultural and Psychological Perspectives
PSY 192P.description: Explores chronic illness in Latina communities through a qualitative lens, focusing on cultural values, healthcare access, and systemic barriers. Students design and conduct a group-based study to better understand lived experiences and health inequities.
PSY 192P.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 192Q.title: Chicano/Latino Social Psychology
PSY 192Q.description: Examines theories, research, and major issues of relevance to understanding social psychological processes in Chicano/Latino populations. Topics include social development, cultural orientations, gender and sexuality, close relationships, happiness and well-being, stereotyping, prejudice and discrimination, and mental and physical health.
PSY 192Q.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
PSY 192Q.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Chicano/Latino Studies majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 192R.title: Latina Reproductive Health
PSY 192R.description: Gives an overview of active areas of research on the psychological, social, and cultural factors that influence Latina reproductive health. Critically examines selected topics in reproductive health not merely as biological processes, but as psychological events.

PSY 192S.title: Health and the Latino Paradox
PSY 192S.description: Examines research and theories concerning the physical and mental health of U.S. Latino populations. Contemporary accounts, health care implications, and new directions for understanding sources of risks and resilience for health in Latino populations are evaluated and discussed.
PSY 192S.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
PSY 192S.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Chicano/Latino Studies majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors only.

PSY 192T.title: Cognition and Learning in Educational Settings
PSY 192T.description: Exploration of historical foundations of cognitive psychology and cognitive development, cognitive neuroscience in education, complex cognition, individual differences, and cognitive foundations of learning.
PSY 192T.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Education Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 192U.title: Psychology of Learning, Abilities, and Intelligence
PSY 192U.description: Overview of classic positions on the mind, human abilities, and intelligence, especially as related to academic achievement. Contrasting views: psychometric versus information processing; experimental versus correlational research.
PSY 192U.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Education Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 192V.title: Language and Literacy
PSY 192V.description: Addresses the linguistic principles and processes that underlie oral and written language proficiency. Emphasis is on how to use phonology, morphology, orthography, semantics, syntax, and pragmatics to support literacy and oral language development for K-12 students.
PSY 192V.restriction: Language Science majors, Psychological Science majors, Education Sciences majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 192X.title: Introduction to Positive Psychology in Education
PSY 192X.description: Positive psychology is a recent focus area within the field of psychology that explores what is positive, creative, and fulfilling in human behavior. It is the scientific study of well-being and flourishing.
PSY 192X.restriction: Education Sciences majors, Psychological Science majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 193B.title: Juvenile Delinquency
PSY 193B.description: Patterns of delinquent behavior, theories that explain behavior, current research aimed at enhancing exploratory power. Attempts to prevent and control delinquency are put in historical perspective. Development of the current juvenile justice system and evolution of modern juvenile law.
PSY 193B.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology - Urban and Regional Planning majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 193C.title: Social Control of Delinquency
PSY 193C.description: Assumes familiarity with theories of delinquency, the juvenile justice system, and elements of juvenile law. Explores socio-historical origins and evolution of juvenile justice, current research and policy on delinquency prevention and treatment, and future directions of law, policy, and practice.
PSY 193C.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 193E.title: Psychology and the Law
PSY 193E.description: Psychological assumptions of the American legal system and mental health aspects of provision of criminal justice services. Civil commitment, insanity defense, competence to stand trial, jury selection, eyewitness identification. Use of police, courts, correctional institutions in prevention of behavior disorder.
PSY 193E.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology - Urban and Regional Planning majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 193F.title: Family Law
PSY 193F.description: Examines legal issues surrounding marriage, cohabitation, divorce, child custody and support, adoption, and the rights of parents and children in the family context. The findings of social science research are used to illuminate the legal issues.
PSY 193F.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 193G.title: Eyewitness Testimony
PSY 193G.description: Faulty eyewitness testimony is a major cause of wrongful convictions. Covers the fast-growing topic of eyewitness testimony and memory for real-world events, both how psychologists study eyewitness capacity, and how the legal system has dealt with eyewitness issues.
PSY 193G.restriction: Seniors, Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY 196.title: Research Seminar in Psychology
PSY 196.description: Special topics research seminar. Content varies with interest of instructor. Capstone seminar for students who have conducted research with, or have a background in, the research topics of the Psychology faculty member offering this seminar in a given quarter.

PSY C200.title: Evidence-Based Treatments
PSY C200.description: Presents empirically-supported treatment approaches and professional strategies for the practice of them. Covers cognitive-behavior therapy, acceptance and commitment therapy, dialectical behavior therapy, mindfulness meditation, exposure and response prevention, parent-child interaction therapy and their application to various clinical disorders.

PSY P200.title: Introduction to Legal and Forensic Psychology
PSY P200.description: Familiarizes students with the interrelated fields of psychology, law, and forensic studies. Emphasizes clinically relevant legal topics (insanity defense; competency to stand trial) and includes critical thinking about issues that arise when psychologists are involved in legal proceedings.
PSY P200.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY C201.title: Clinical Assessment and Interviewing
PSY C201.description: Prepares students to conduct clinical interviews, which are the building blocks for psychotherapy and clinical research. Develops basic skills of interviewing and covers how to conduct the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 Disorders and how to make differential diagnoses.

PSY P201.title: Research Methods in Psychology
PSY P201.description: In-depth examination of the conceptualization of research problems and linkages between theory and the design of appropriate strategies for empirical research in psychological science. Topics include experimental and quasi-experimental designs, reliability and validity of measurement and non-experimental procedures.
PSY P201.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors only.

PSY C202.title: Cognitive and Neuropsychological Assessment
PSY C202.description: Provides empirical background and introductory skills for students to begin supervised cognitive and neuropsychological assessment practice in a professional, ethical, competent, culturally sensitive manner. Administration, scoring, and interpreting standardized cognitive assessment measures and neuropsychological assessment measures. Neuropsychological disorders and anomalies.

PSY P202.title: Data Analysis and Statistics
PSY P202.description: Statistical techniques to facilitate inferences in psychological research, including fundamentals of statistical inference and methods for analyzing data.
PSY P202.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY C203.title: Professional Issues and Ethics in Clinical Psychology
PSY C203.description: Examines professional guidelines and ethical principles in clinical psychology research, assessment, and treatment, with an emphasis on the American Psychological Association Code of Ethics for Psychologists. Helps students develop awareness of ethical issues arising in clinical research and practice.

PSY C204.title: Practicum in Clinical Psychology
PSY C204.description: Clinical work at on-campus or off-campus clinical practice sites, such as hospitals and clinics, supervised by a licensed clinical psychologist, in addition to the students’ faculty advisor.

PSY P204.title: Adolescence
PSY P204.description: Considers pubertal and cognitive changes and their social consequences; the family, peer group, school, and cultural contexts in which adolescence is embedded; and selected psychosocial issues including autonomy, identity, health, and well-being.

PSY C205.title: History and Systems
PSY C205.description: Surveys ideas of major figures in the history of psychology, from pre-Socratic Greek philosophers to psychologists active prior to the middle of the 20th century. Provides an appreciation of the forces (intellectual, cultural, scientific) that have shaped modern psychology.

PSY P206.title: Big Data Analytics for the Social Sciences II
PSY P206.description: A practical lecture and lab course for learning how to engage with big data in various forms and use data science techniques (e.g., data reduction, NLP) to analyze and visualize data for research purposes.
PSY P206.prereq_text: SOCECOL 264A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCECOL 264B with a minimum grade of B- and PSY P203 with a minimum grade of B-.
PSY P206.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors only.

PSY C208.title: Family and Systems Therapy
PSY C208.description: Presents family/systems therapy as a treatment modality, emphasizing the interdependence of theory, practice, and research. Examines various therapeutic models (e.g., structural, strategic, multi-generational, cognitive-behavioral, attachment, and narrative approaches) and evidence relevant to effectiveness and hypothesized mechanisms of change.

PSY P208.title: Research Methods
PSY P208.description: In-depth examination of issues relevant to designing and evaluating research in psychological science. Topics address casual inference, ethical issues surrounding the responsible conduct of research, experimental and quasi-experimental designs, reliability and validity of measurement, and non-experimental procedures.
PSY P208.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY C209.title: Clinical Psychology Research Designs and Methods
PSY C209.description: Reviews major issues in conducting scientific research and important methodological issues in psychological clinical science.

PSY P209A.title: Applied Psychological Research
PSY P209A.description: Focuses on scientific and professional issues in the field of psychology. Topics include communication skills; intervention approaches; collaboration, consultation, and referral; and ethical issues associated with at-risk populations research.

PSY P210.title: The New Statistics and Open Science
PSY P210.description: Introduces the fundamentals of research design and methodology from the perspective of the new statistics and open science. With this introduction, students should be better able to design and conduct their own research.
PSY P210.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors only.

PSY P214.title: Seminar in Social Psychology
PSY P214.description: Presents an overview of selected theoretical and empirical topics in social psychology including social influence and conformity, altruism and aggression, persuasion and attitude change, self and social perception, and social cognition.

PSY C215.title: Evidence-Based Psychological Treatments II
PSY C215.description: Examines theory, research, and application in family, couple, and child therapy using culturally and developmentally sensitive principles. Students are exposed to theoretical frameworks guiding approaches to the treatment of the family system using readings, lectures, and activities.
PSY C215.prereq_text: PSY C200 with a minimum grade of B-.

PSY P215.title: Psychology and Law
PSY P215.description: An interdisciplinary approach to research in psychology, law, and/or criminology. Examines how psychology is applied to the civil and criminal justice systems, how case law shapes this application, and how legal decisions affect the direction of psychological research.
PSY P215.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY C216.title: Adult Psychopathology
PSY C216.description: Explores the antecedents, characteristics, course, outcomes, and options for the prevention or management of various forms of psychopathology and behavior disorder. Focuses on psychological and biobehavioral mechanisms that influence the development, expression, and amelioration of maladaption.

PSY C217.title: Psychological Assessment
PSY C217.description: Familiarizes students with psychological assessments in intelligence, clinical diagnosis, personality, and neuropsychological functioning. Exposure to administering, scoring, and interpreting assessments. Special focus on psychometrics (e.g., reliability and validity), test construction, and ethical responsibilities.

PSY P217.title: Life-Span Development
PSY P217.description: Introduces the major concepts of life-span development and discusses those with regard to some key topics of developmental psychology. For example, change and continuity, evolutionary and inherited nature, culture, society, and family-based nurture, and their dynamic interaction.

PSY P218.title: Infancy
PSY P218.description: Covers development from conception through the second year. Focus is on research and theory concerning infants' physical, social, cognitive, perceptual, emotional, and language development. Also covers transition to parenthood and family context of infant development.

PSY P219.title: Forensic Neuropsychology
PSY P219.description: Introduces key concepts in clinical neuropsychology as applied in legal/forensic settings. Instruction focuses on neuropsychological concepts underlying brain-behavior relationships and their assessment in forensic case examples; and ethical/legal issues in brain injuries/diseases impacting higher mental functions (e.g., memory).
PSY P219.restriction: Legal and Forensic Psychology majors only.

PSY P220.title: Developmental Psychology: Theories and History
PSY P220.description: Examines key concepts, theories, and the historical and philosophical roots of research in human life span development. Focuses on biological and environmental causation, universalism and cultural relativism, continuity and change.

PSY P222.title: Forensic Assessment
PSY P222.description: Explores the various ways in which clinical psychology is relevant to the law, and how forensic psychologists can meaningfully contribute to the adjudicatory process. Examines legal, scientific, and ethical issues that arise when psychologists are involved in legal proceedings.
PSY P222.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P223.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
PSY P223.description: Examines human behavior in diverse cultures (e.g., Asian, American, and African). Cultural diversity within the U.S. and acculturation of various ethnic groups is also discussed. Topics include theories, methods, parenting, family relations, language, cognition, personality, morality, and health.

PSY P224.title: Children and the Law
PSY P224.description: Examines how psychology research and practice can inform several areas of law and social policy affecting children, adolescents, and families. Topics include education, mental health, reproductive rights, and delinquency.
PSY P224.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P225.title: Forensic Geropsychology
PSY P225.description: Introduces key concepts in Geropsychology as it is applied in forensic settings. Topics covered include basic concepts in Geropsychology, as well as the role of cognitive disorders and dementia, elder abuse, guardianship, diversity, and other older adult issues.
PSY P225.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P226.title: Emotion in Psychology
PSY P226.description: Covers original and recent theories of emotions and how they guide current research. Specific topics include neuroantomical structure of emotion, life-span emotional development, and health and emotion.

PSY P227.title: Sexual Deviance and the Law
PSY P227.description: Focuses on sex crimes with legal debate, including age of consent, sex work, and registration as a sexual offender. Also investigates how psychological theory and research can be applied to legal issues related to sex crimes.
PSY P227.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P228.title: Psychosis and the Law
PSY P228.description: Examines the intersection of serious mental health concerns relation to psychosis and the law. Students use critical thinking skills to facilitate consideration of the myriad of factors that bring people with psychosis to interact with the justice system.
PSY P228.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P229.title: Addiction and the Law
PSY P229.description: Analysis of the intersection of addiction and the legal system, including historical, theoretical, practical, and policy dimensions. Provides students with insights into treatment and prevention strategies as well as policy and legal considerations.
PSY P229.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P231.title: Professional Issues in Psychology
PSY P231.description: Examines a variety of issues related to the professional socialization and development of graduate students in psychology. Topics include the publication process, sources of research funding, alternative employment options, competitiveness on the job market, and the academic career route.

PSY P232.title: Trauma and Resilience
PSY P232.description: Psychological impact of trauma; biopsychosocial factors affecting development of traumatic stress, treatment, and preventive interventions for traumatic stress; define and measure resilience; moral injury and post traumatic growth; ethics of studying trauma.

PSY C233.title: Neuropsychophysiology of Self- and Emotion-Regulation
PSY C233.description: Intended to survey the evidence for a common set of neural structures that underlies self-regulation (e.g., emotion regulation) with the goal of assessing the relevance for health and disease.

PSY P234.title: Childhood
PSY P234.description: Provides graduate students with an overview of traditional and emerging theories, models, and research designed to understand children's development in the domains of cognitive, social, and emotional functioning.

PSY P235.title: Social Health Psychology
PSY P235.description: Enables students to critically evaluate research related to social health psychology. Offers a deeper understanding of the potential physiological mechanisms underpinning the impact of social psychological factors on health and well-being.
PSY P235.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors only.

PSY P236.title: Inequality and Privilege
PSY P236.description: Using a social-psychological perspective, examines the origins of inequality and how social class, ethnic/racial, gender, and other group differences are created, perceived, and upheld. Covers current issues in the area of inequality and intergroup relations.

PSY P237.title: Cooperation and Helping
PSY P237.description: Consists of topics in contemporary psychology which focus on core processes that enable prosocial action, cooperation, and helping. Students identify proximal forces at four levels of analysis: intrapsychic, dyadic, group, and sociocultural factors that influence cooperation and helping.

PSY P239.title: Moral Psychology
PSY P239.description: Provides a selective overview of both classic work and new trends in the study of morality and moral reasoning in contemporary psychological science, with a particular emphasis on topics of relevance to social psychology.

PSY P240.title: Child and Adolescent Testimony
PSY P240.description: Reviews classic and emerging research on children's and adolescents' memory, suggestibility, and disclosure processes. Highlights theoretical and practical implications of the research when children and adolescents are victims of or witnesses to crime.

PSY P242.title: Legal Reasoning and Jurisprudence
PSY P242.description: Overview of the law and legal process as well as the history and assumptions underlying modern legal reasoning. Issues related to procedure and evidence as well as key jurisprudential perspectives are discussed.
PSY P242.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P247.title: EEG Methods
PSY P247.description: Provides an in-depth training of the electroencephalogram (EEG) methodology with a specific focus on the event-related potential technique. Emphasis is on learning how to use this methodology and how to analyze data, with a focus on emotional stimuli.

PSY P249.title: Advanced Social Psychology
PSY P249.description: Conveys an appreciation of the flavors of contemporary social psychology, an understanding of empirical approaches to problems in this area, and a sense of the array of theoretical orientations in the field.

PSY P250.title: Emotion, Reasoning, and Memory
PSY P250.description: Examines research and theory on emotion from the perspective of cognitive psychology. Topics include the effects of emotions on attention, memory, and problem solving; the relations between emotional and cognitive development; flash-bulb memories of intense emotional experiences; eyewitness testimony.

PSY P251.title: Clinical Interviewing and Treatment in a Forensic Setting
PSY P251.description: Students receive an introduction to clinical interviewing, learn details of strategic, solution-focused therapy, and think critically about issues that come at the interaction of psychology and the law. Students are not "license-eligible" at end of this course.
PSY P251.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P253.title: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology Capstone
PSY P253.description: Focuses on macro-level writing topics such as developing a meaningful research question, conducting a thorough review of relevant literature, and presenting a clear and convincing research-based argument.

PSY P254.title: Mental Health and the Law
PSY P254.description: Explores the history of criminalization of persons with mental illness. Topics include challenges and needs of persons with mental illness; civil and outpatient commitment; law enforcement responses to persons with mental illness; and mentally ill offenders in jails and prisons.
PSY P254.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P255.title: Violence, Anger, and Psychopathology
PSY P255.description: Overviews the prevalence of violence as a criminal and public health problem. Topics include violence within families and intimate partner relationships, traumatic origins of violence, the development of a violence-prone personality, the association of anger and violence with psychopathology.
PSY P255.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P256.title: Family and the Law
PSY P256.description: Examines sociological and legal perspectives on the relationship between family life and law, with a focus on three distinct but sometimes interconnected domains: the child welfare system, the criminal justice system, and the immigration system.
PSY P256.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P257.title: Growing up Digital
PSY P257.description: Draws theory and research from across multiple fields including psychology, education, computer science, sociology, and medicine to examine the role that digital technology plays in the lives of young people.
PSY P257.restriction: Master of Legal and Forensic Psychology only.

PSY P258.title: Health Psychology
PSY P258.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of emerging fields of health psychology and behavioral medicine. Topics: role of stress in development/treatment of medical problems; sociocognitive determinants of health and illness; interpersonal health transactions; behavioral approaches to medical problems such as diabetes, obesity, hypertension.

PSY P259.title: Psychological Assessment
PSY P259.description: Introduces students to the science and practice of psychological assessment. Explores historical and theoretical foundations of psychological testing, key psychometric principles, and applications of assessment. Students learn how to evaluate, select, and ethically use psychological tests.

PSY P261.title: Intensive Longitudinal Data Analysis
PSY P261.description: Fundamentals of Intensive Longitudinal Study designs, gain first-hand experience collecting ILD using web and/or mobile-based platforms, and learn how to manage, analyze, and disseminate findings from these studies.
PSY P261.prereq_text: SOCECOL 264A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCECOL 264B with a minimum grade of B-.

PSY P263.title: Eyewitness Testimony
PSY P263.description: Examines the evidence that shows that faulty eyewitness memory is the major cause of wrongful convictions. Explores what the legal system thinks of eyewitness testimony and how the legal system has dealt with eyewitness issues.

PSY P264.title: Intensive Writing Workshop
PSY P264.description: Offers an intensive writing workshop for graduate students with instruction targeting academic writing, peer review, and publishing. Also covers techniques for translating research to a broader audience in the form of opinion, position, and policy papers.
PSY P264.restriction: Psychological Science majors and Psychology majors only.

PSY P265.title: Memory and the Law
PSY P265.description: Examines the controversial topic of repressed memory, or perception and memory of real-world events.

PSY P266.title: Psychology and the Law
PSY P266.description: Overview of how psychology is applied to the civil and criminal justice systems, how case law shapes this application, and how legal decisions affect the direction of psychological research. Interdisciplinary approach to research in psychology, law, and/or criminology.

PSY P268.title: Coping with Stressful Life Events
PSY P268.description: Explores how individuals cope with serious life crises (e.g., illness, bereavement), life transitions, and daily stressors. Considers how such events impact on people's cognitions, emotions, and health, and the role of others in the coping process.

PSY P269.title: Ethics in Psychological Assessment
PSY P269.description: Examines ethical and professional issues in psych assessment. Through discussion, vignette analysis, and critical reflection, students build competencies in ethical reasoning and responsible psychological practice.

PSY P270.title: Psychology of Pedagogy
PSY P270.description: Graduate-level introduction to the psychology of pedagogy grounds college teaching and learning in the theory and research of our discipline, which is uniquely positioned to inform it in an innovative, impactful, and inclusive way.
PSY P270.restriction: Psychology majors and Clinical Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PSY P271.title: Evolutionary Psychology
PSY P271.description: Covers theories and empirical research concerning the evolutionary origins of human behaviors and their variations. An interdisciplinary course emphasizing both evolutionary psychology (e.g., mating strategies, kinship, and parenting) and molecular evolution (i.e., evolution of genes for various behaviors).

PSY P275.title: Special Topics in Psychology
PSY P275.description: Topics covered vary with interests of instructor.

PSY P276.title: Systematic Review and Meta Analysis
PSY P276.description: The process of synthesizing results from a number of studies that address a common research question is often referred to as meta-analysis. Explores the meta-analysis process from the coding of retrieved studies to the final research synthesis.

PSY 277.title: Implementation Science
PSY 277.description: Focuses on dissemination and implementation (D&I) science. Emphasizes the types of questions D&I research seeks to answer, commonly used models and frameworks, methods employed, and outcomes examined.

PSY P278.title: Psychological Assessment Practicum
PSY P278.description: Provides supervised practical training in psychological and/or neuropsychological assessment. Emphasis is placed on ethical standards, cultural responsiveness, and preparation for registration as a Psychological Testing Technician through the California Board of Psychology.

PSY P280B.title: Interdisciplinary Salivary Bioscience Lab
PSY P280B.description: Laboratory sequel to the P280A seminar. Provides laboratory-based hands-on experience integrating salivary analytes into developmental, social, behavioral, and health sciences that also includes supervised training on sample processing.
PSY P280B.prereq_text: PSY P280A (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B.

PSY P283H.title: Psychoneuroimmunology
PSY P283H.description: Introduces students to the field of psychoneuroimmunology and helps them develop the conceptual and methodological skills necessary for designing and interpreting research on the bidirectional relationship between the immune system and psychological processes.

PSY P284.title: Health and Emotion
PSY P284.description: Overview of research focused on understanding how emotional processes influence physical health. Provides students with a deeper understanding of how emotions play into the health of others as well.

PSY P286.title: Motivation
PSY P286.description: Introduces major concepts of motivational psychology, theory, and history. Application of motivational concepts to phenomena from social psychology and affective science. Development of own research proposal in a motivational framework and/or conceptualizing or expanding an ongoing or planned research project.

PSY P287.title: Stereotyping and Person Perception
PSY P287.description: Investigates the processes and implications of stereotyping, prejudice, and person perception broadly. Questions such as: Where do our stereotypes and prejudices come from? What are the psychological mechanisms underlying them?

PSY P290.title: Research in Developmental Psychology
PSY P290.description: Introduces graduate students to research conducted by individual faculty members in the area of developmental psychology. This is accomplished by having students involve themselves in the conceptualization, strategy, and implementation of the faculty member's research.

PSY P291.title: Research in Health Psychology
PSY P291.description: Introduces graduate students to research conducted by individual faculty members in the area of health psychology. This is accomplished by having students involve themselves in the conceptualization, strategy, and implementation of the faculty member's research.

PSY P292.title: Research in Psychopathology and Behavior Disorder
PSY P292.description: Introduces graduate students to research conducted by individual faculty members in the area of psychopathology and behavior disorder. This is accomplished by having students involve themselves in the conceptualization, strategy, and implementation of the faculty member's research.

PSY P293.title: Research in Social and Personality Psychology
PSY P293.description: Introduces graduate students to research conducted by individual faculty members in the area of social and personality psychology. This is accomplished by having students involve themselves in the conceptualization, strategy, and implementation of the faculty member's research.

PSY P294A.title: Research Directions in Psychology I
PSY P294A.description: Introduces students to the current research of faculty, graduate students, and visitors to the Department of Psychology. Includes examination of contemporary research issues and controversies, as well as issues related to students' development as professionals.

PSY P294B.title: Research Directions in Psychology II
PSY P294B.description: Introduces students to the current research of faculty, graduate students, and visitors to the Department of Psychology. Includes examination of contemporary research issues and controversies, as well as issues related to students' development as professionals.

PSY P294C.title: Research Directions in Psychology III
PSY P294C.description: Introduces students to the current research of faculty, graduate students, and visitors to the Department of Psychology. Includes examination of contemporary research issues and controversies, as well as issues related to students' development as professionals.

PSY P295.title: Research in Psychology and Law
PSY P295.description: Introduces graduate students to research conducted by individual faculty members in the area of psychology and law. This is accomplished by having students involve themselves in the conceptualization, strategy, and implementation of the faculty member's research.

PSY P296.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
PSY P296.description: Dissertation research with Psychological Science faculty.

PSY P298.title: Directed Studies in Psychological Science
PSY P298.description: Directed study with Psychological Science faculty.

PUBHLTH 1.title: Principles of Public Health
PUBHLTH 1.description: Discover key principles of public health and health determinants in communities. Explores the ecological model, analyzing interconnections among natural and social determinants influencing health outcomes. Topics include epidemiology, environmental health, and health policy.
PUBHLTH 1.restriction: Nursing Science majors, Public Health Policy majors, and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 2.title: Case Studies in Public Health Practice
PUBHLTH 2.description: Explores public health through diverse case studies illustrating foundational principles and ongoing evolution. Topics include epidemiological investigations, health policy analysis, community interventions, and global health challenges.
PUBHLTH 2.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 5.title: Foundations of One Health
PUBHLTH 5.description: Introduces One Health principles to address challenges at the intersection of human, animal, and ecosystem health. Focuses on integration in public health, global health, and planetary health practices. Covers competency-based approaches and problem-solving strategies.
PUBHLTH 5.restriction: Public Health Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 7A.title: Public Health Statistics I
PUBHLTH 7A.description: First of two courses in statistics. Introduces fundamental statistics for health science students, emphasizing quantitative reasoning from a public health perspective. Topics include probability, data analysis, and statistical inference.
PUBHLTH 7A.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 7B.title: Public Health Statistics II
PUBHLTH 7B.description: Second of two courses in statistics. Focus on regression, probability, and significance testing from a public health perspective. Prepares students to interpret scientific publications and conduct basic statistical analyses.
PUBHLTH 7B.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 7A or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3.
PUBHLTH 7B.restriction: Public Health majors, Public Health Policy majors, and Public Health Sciences majors only.

PUBHLTH 10.title: Special Topics in Public Health
PUBHLTH 10.description: Introduction to emerging topics in public health. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PUBHLTH 30.title: Introduction to Urban Environmental Health
PUBHLTH 30.description: Explores urban health disparities, focusing on social determinants and environmental impacts. Examines global urban health challenges, disease burdens, and historical legacies of contamination. Introduces interventions and policies to mitigate urban health inequalities and enhance public health in diverse urban settings.
PUBHLTH 30.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 60.title: Environmental Quality and Health
PUBHLTH 60.description: Explores the interplay of pollution and human health: population, epidemiology, toxicology, zoonotic diseases, water and air quality, climate change, waste management, contaminants (metals, pesticides, organics, radioactivity), and environmental justice. Delves into risk assessment and public health policy implications.
PUBHLTH 60.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 70.title: Toxicology and Society
PUBHLTH 70.description: Introduces principles of toxicology and societal implications of toxic exposures. Focuses on mechanisms of action, dose-response relationships, exposure pathways, and risk assessment. Includes applications in food safety, occupational health, environmental toxicology, regulatory policy, and health equity.
PUBHLTH 70.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 80.title: AIDS Fundamentals
PUBHLTH 80.description: Considers the biological and sociological bases of the AIDS epidemic. Topics include the history of AIDS, current medical knowledge, transmission, risk reduction, and how the community can respond.

PUBHLTH 90.title: Natural Disasters
PUBHLTH 90.description: Examine natural disasters and their impacts on humans. Topics include volcanoes, earthquakes, severe weather, fires, floods, landslides, coastal processes, and risk assessment. Use WebGIS for hazard data and risk analysis in California.
PUBHLTH 90.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 91.title: Disparities in Health Care
PUBHLTH 91.description: Students become agents of social change for equitable health care delivery. Focus on cultural competency, awareness, communication skills, and disparities. Explore clinical, public service, and research opportunities. Engage with guest lecturers to cultivate and empower diverse communities.

PUBHLTH 100.title: Special Topics in Public Health
PUBHLTH 100.description: Studies in selected areas of public health. Topics addressed vary each quarter. Course may be offered online when topic is Public Health in the Corporate World.

PUBHLTH 101.title: Introduction to Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 101.description: The distribution of disease and injury across time, space, and populations. Covers basic concepts and methods of descriptive epidemiology including the natural history of disease, data, and indices of health.
PUBHLTH 101.prereq_text: STATS 7 or STATS 8 or PUBHLTH 7A or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3.
PUBHLTH 101.restriction: Public Health Sciences majors and Public Health Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 102.title: Social Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 102.description: Overviews evidence linking environmental factors to mental and physical disorders including such variables as socioeconomic status, income inequality, work stress, job loss, social capital, location, and other demographic characteristics. Measurement and research design issues of both individual and aggregate levels.
PUBHLTH 102.prereq_text: Recommended: (COGS 7A or COGS 9C or PSY 22) and SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13.
PUBHLTH 102.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Public Health Policy majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 105.title: Introduction to Health Informatics
PUBHLTH 105.description: Broad overview of medical informatics for students with varied backgrounds. Electronic medical records, online resources, mobile technologies, patient safety, and computational design. Legal, ethical, and public policy issues. Health systems management. Evaluation and fieldwork for health systems.
PUBHLTH 105.prereq_text: WRITING 60 with a minimum grade of C or WRITING 30 with a minimum grade of C or WRITING 31 with a minimum grade of C or HUMAN 1C with a minimum grade of C or HUMAN H1C with a minimum grade of C.
PUBHLTH 105.restriction: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PUBHLTH 106.title: Project in Health Informatics
PUBHLTH 106.description: Students undertake significant quarter-long projects related to health informatics. Topics may include field evaluations of health care technologies, prototypes, iterative design, and system implementations.
