PUBHLTH 107.title: Epidemiology of Drug Use and Misuse
PUBHLTH 107.description: Applies epidemiologic concepts to the use and misuse of licit/illicit substances. Emphasizes descriptive aspects of drug use and determinants of progressing from experimental use to misuse. Assesses subgroups of abusers, risk factors, trends, and surveillance techniques for estimating drug prevalence.
PUBHLTH 107.restriction: Public Health Sciences majors and Public Health Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 109.title: Consumer Health Informatics
PUBHLTH 109.description: Consumer health informatics is a subfield of health informatics aimed to empower healthcare consumers through a variety of consumer-facing technologies. Covers health behavior change, health literacy, social support, and the design, evaluation, and implementation of major technological applications.
PUBHLTH 109.prereq_text: IN4MATX 171 with a minimum grade of C or PUBHLTH 105 with a minimum grade of C.
PUBHLTH 109.restriction: Public Health majors, Health Informatics minors, and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 110.title: Health Data Analytics
PUBHLTH 110.description: The increasing availability of electronic heath data provides an unprecedented opportunity to use data-driven approaches to improve human health. Equips students with essential skills in curating, managing, and analyzing health data, focusing on electronic health records.
PUBHLTH 110.prereq_text: IN4MATX 171 with a minimum grade of C or PUBHLTH 105 with a minimum grade of C.
PUBHLTH 110.restriction: Public Health majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 112.title: Obesity Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 112.description: Exploration of the epidemiological evidence of obesity nationally and globally including the etiology of the obesity epidemic, various measurements of obesity, associated comorbidities, prognosis, treatment approaches, and prevention strategies. Emphasize preventing obesity at both individual and societal levels.

PUBHLTH 115.title: Community, Social Justice, and Health Equity Research for Action
PUBHLTH 115.description: Focuses on community as a unit of identity, community, well-being, and social justice perspectives and initiatives to promote community health. Addresses community change and improvements in community well-being, with a focus on health equity research for action.
PUBHLTH 115.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 1 or PUBHLTH 2 or CHC/LAT 61 or CHC/LAT 62 or CHC/LAT 63.

PUBHLTH 119.title: Special Topics in Epidemiology and Genetics
PUBHLTH 119.description: Studies in selected areas of epidemiology and genetics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PUBHLTH 120.title: Nutrition and Global Health
PUBHLTH 120.description: Global issues related to nutrition and public health. Evaluation of nutritional risk factors associated with the development of chronic diseases and the role of nutritional medicine in prevention. Topics include food safety, communicable diseases, supplements, and regulatory issues.
PUBHLTH 120.restriction: Public Health Sciences majors and Public Health Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 122.title: Health Policy
PUBHLTH 122.description: Considers social and economic aspects of health and disease in the United States. What are the proper roles of the individual, community, and government in improving health and health care? International comparisons will be made wherever possible.
PUBHLTH 122.prereq_text: ( SCHOOL OF PUBHLTH ONLY OR URBAN STUDIES MAJORS ONLY OR SOCIAL ECOLOGY MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 122.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Public Health Policy majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 125.title: Foundations of Community Health
PUBHLTH 125.description: A social ecological framework for understanding community health is presented. Measures of individual and community health are compared, and the influence of personal and environmental factors on individual, group, and population health is examined. Community health promotion strategies are discussed.
PUBHLTH 125.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Public Health Policy majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 126.title: Public Health Law: Fundamentals in Action
PUBHLTH 126.description: Addresses the relationship of U.S. public health law to health systems at the individual and population levels. Examines legislative and judicial concepts and how they are applied to disease prevention strategies, health services, management, and policy.

PUBHLTH 127.title: Public Health Programs for the Corporate World
PUBHLTH 127.description: International perspective on workplace health promotion. Strategies for developing programs to improve employee health and to decrease risks of chronic degenerative diseases. Case studies include assessment of employee health, program design, implementation, and evaluation. Emphasis on disease prevention.

PUBHLTH 129.title: Public Health Administration
PUBHLTH 129.description: Examines historical aspects of public health administration including policies, procedures, trends, and development of organizations. Addresses information and skills necessary to succeed in public health leadership roles. Discusses strategic planning, collaborations, and ethical considerations for successful management in public health.
PUBHLTH 129.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 132.title: American Public Policy
PUBHLTH 132.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

PUBHLTH 135.title: Medical Sociology
PUBHLTH 135.description: Current problems in U.S. health-care system and proposals for reform. Examines financial barriers to access; problem of patient dumping; underinsurance; prenatal and perinatal care; child services; preventative care and needs of the elderly; minorities; low-income people; undocumented.
PUBHLTH 135.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 138.title: Tobacco Control Policy
PUBHLTH 138.description: Explore tobacco control's interdisciplinary facets: history, policy, advocacy, and public health science. Analyze industry tactics, litigation, and impact of tobacco control policies. Discuss parallels with emerging industries. Culminates in a group project on tobacco's stakeholders.
PUBHLTH 138.restriction: Public Health majors, Public Health Policy majors, and Public Health Sciences majors only.

PUBHLTH 139.title: Special Topics in Health Policy and Administration
PUBHLTH 139.description: Studies in selected areas of health policy and administration. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
PUBHLTH 139.restriction: Public Health Sciences majors and Public Health Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 141.title: Clinical Health Psychology
PUBHLTH 141.description: Behavioral role in etiology, treatment, and prevention of certain diseases. Behavioral intervention including biofeedback, stress-, pain-management, health habit counseling, and other skills to assist patients make cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes needed to cope with disease or achieve better health.
PUBHLTH 141.prereq_text: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 9C or PSY 22.
PUBHLTH 141.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Psychology majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Public Health Policy majors, and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 144.title: Health Behavior Theory
PUBHLTH 144.description: Introduction to foundational theories for health behavior change. Explores individual, interpersonal, and community-level theories applied to health interventions. Understand societal challenges and preventable behavioral causes of diseases.
PUBHLTH 144.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 146.title: Health Promotion Programs
PUBHLTH 146.description: Explores social ecological perspectives and the role of behavior change theories in health promotion planning. Introduces systematic planning for the development of an intervention program. Emphasizes the cornerstone of planning, implementing, and evaluating a health promotion program.
PUBHLTH 146.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 147.title: Drug Abuse and its Prevention
PUBHLTH 147.description: Theoretical and practical underpinnings of drug abuse and its prevention at the individual and population levels. Students practice developing drug abuse prevention schemes for specific populations. Recent developments in pharmacological and biobehavioral theories of drug dependence are explored.
PUBHLTH 147.restriction: Public Health Sciences majors and Public Health Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 148.title: Public Health Communication
PUBHLTH 148.description: Theoretical foundations and practical use of communication sciences in public health, covering effective techniques such as audience segmentation, tailored messaging, and multi-model communication for behavior change campaigns across various settings. Includes crisis communication strategies.
PUBHLTH 148.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 152.title: Happiness, Wellbeing, and Health
PUBHLTH 152.description: Explores positive and protective psychological, social, and behavioral factors that influence physical, mental/emotional, and social wellbeing.

PUBHLTH 153.title: Public Health Nutrition
PUBHLTH 153.description: Nutrition from individual to population levels. Socioecological factors in dietary patterns and food choices. Disparities in food access and health outcomes. Evidence-based interventions for behaviors, perceptions, and built environment through clinical, epidemiological, and policy approaches.
PUBHLTH 153.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 158.title: Sociology of Mental Health
PUBHLTH 158.description: Examines the social causes, consequences, and patterns of mental health and illness. Students learn a sociological perspective on mental health, mental illness or disorder, and medicine/health care, ranging from social definitions, roles, and interactions to societal stratification and international patterns.
PUBHLTH 158.restriction: Public Health majors and Sociology majors only.

PUBHLTH 159.title: Special Topics in Social and Behavioral Health Science
PUBHLTH 159.description: Studies in selected areas of social and behavioral health sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PUBHLTH 161.title: Environmental Geology
PUBHLTH 161.description: Explores geologic principles applied to environmental and health issues. Topics include earth systems, earth materials, water pollution, natural hazards, waste disposal, climate change, and geology's impact on human health in UCI and Orange County.
PUBHLTH 161.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 163.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
PUBHLTH 163.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention and human well-being. Topics include air and water quality, food safety, built environment, radiation exposure, climate change, environmental justice, children's health, and policy interventions for public health improvement.
PUBHLTH 163.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 168.title: Nuclear Environments
PUBHLTH 168.description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.

PUBHLTH 170.title: Introduction to Global Health
PUBHLTH 170.description: Provides a foundational interdisciplinary understanding of global health issues and their importance to societal goals, including poverty reduction, sustainable development, and international contexts of wellness and covers major communicable and non-communicable diseases and demographic patterns of disease burden.

PUBHLTH 171.title: Human Exposure to Environmental Contaminants
PUBHLTH 171.description: Explores origins of environmental health awareness. Covers exposure assessment theory, variability, risk assessment integration, and societal implications. Discusses notable environmental contaminants impacting human health.

PUBHLTH 172.title: Climate Change and Disaster Management
PUBHLTH 172.description: Examines the social, economic, environmental, and health impacts of anthropogenic climate change through engaged learning that integrates practice and theory.

PUBHLTH 173.title: Health and Global Environmental Change
PUBHLTH 173.description: Examines global environmental and climate change's impact on human health. Explores metabolic pandemics, infectious diseases, and underlying health conditions. Fosters interdisciplinary collaboration among environmental health, public health, medicine, and policy sciences.
PUBHLTH 173.prereq_text: One upper-division course in environmental science, public health, environmental policy, and/or environmental management.
PUBHLTH 173.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 174.title: Global Health Ethics
PUBHLTH 174.description: Provides a foundation for understanding and application of key issues in global health ethics. Emphasizes competencies needed to practice global health during outbreaks, pandemics, emergencies and disasters, which raise several ethical issues for health professionals, first-responders, researchers, and government agencies.

PUBHLTH 176.title: War and Public Health
PUBHLTH 176.description: Analyzes war's impact on public health through the Social Ecological Framework, including effects on healthcare systems, infectious disease spread, and mental health. Emphasizes recent global conflicts, and U.S. military involvement overseas.

PUBHLTH 177.title: Global Health Policy and Diplomacy
PUBHLTH 177.description: Fundamental principles and consequences of global health policy and diplomacy, including governance structure, functions, analysis, advocacy, and outcomes. Emphasizes practical application of multilateral policies for global health security and responses to transnational threats such as pandemics, climate, pollution, and migration.

PUBHLTH 179.title: Special Topics in Environmental and Global Health Science
PUBHLTH 179.description: Studies in selected areas of environmental and global health sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PUBHLTH 180.title: Epidemiology of Infectious Disease
PUBHLTH 180.description: Explores the distribution of infectious disease and disease risks among human populations. Covers concepts and methods of infectious disease epidemiology, including case studies of important infectious diseases such as COVID-19, HIV, and malaria.

PUBHLTH 181.title: Infectious Disease Dynamics
PUBHLTH 181.description: Learn how the immune system interacts with infectious diseases, in particular with viral infections. An introduction to basic virology and immunology, it concentrates on the way in which the immune system is critical to the prevention of infections.

PUBHLTH 182.title: Evolutionary and Ecological Principles in Medicine
PUBHLTH 182.description: Explore the dynamics of populations on an ecological, epidemiological, and medical level. Considers the dynamics of competition, predation, and parasitism; the spread and control of infectious diseases; and the in vivo dynamics of viral infections and the immune system.

PUBHLTH 189.title: Special Topics in Infectious Diseases
PUBHLTH 189.description: Studies in selected areas of infectious diseases. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
PUBHLTH 189.restriction: Public Health Sciences majors and Public Health Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 190.title: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
PUBHLTH 190.description: Extensive use of GIS software. Lecture topics cover mapping basics, projections, and geocoding. Practical tutorials and lab sessions for hands-on practice with public health data. Assessments focus on synthesizing GIS tools for problem-solving.

PUBHLTH 191B.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
PUBHLTH 191B.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

PUBHLTH 191C.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
PUBHLTH 191C.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

PUBHLTH H192A.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis I
PUBHLTH H192A.description: Advanced research opportunity for Public Health Honors. Students conduct research projects with faculty, attend lectures, and engage in timeline creation. Requirements include upper-division coursework, GPA criteria, and a faculty-approved thesis project.
PUBHLTH H192A.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 199 ( coreq ) AND SCHOOL OF PUBHLTH ONLY
PUBHLTH H192A.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors only.

PUBHLTH H192B.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis II
PUBHLTH H192B.description: Students initiate and complete data collection for the honors thesis. In addition, students begin data analysis and summarize results at a class symposium at the end of the quarter. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
PUBHLTH H192B.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors only.

PUBHLTH H192C.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis III
PUBHLTH H192C.description: Students write their honors research project (PUBHLTH H192A-PUBHLTH H192B) and prepare an oral report to be presented at a class symposium at the end of the quarter. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
PUBHLTH H192C.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors only.

PUBHLTH 194A.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory I
PUBHLTH 194A.description: Provides training for students with an interest in clinical and translational research in the health care setting. Cultivates skills for study design, research literature review, ethics, responsible conduct of research, and cultural competence while emphasizing professionalism and personal responsibility.
PUBHLTH 194A.prereq_text: BIO SCI 99 and BIO SCI 194S and CHEM 1C and CHEM 1LC and CHEM 1LD. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

PUBHLTH 195P.title: Public Health Practicum
PUBHLTH 195P.description: Explore public health practice through internships at community agencies, non-profits, or labs. Analyze connections between academia and public health. Evaluate mission and operations, explore personal values and skills, and articulate role in public health.
PUBHLTH 195P.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors only.

PUBHLTH 195W.title: Writing for Public Health Practice
PUBHLTH 195W.description: Develop communication skills via writing projects addressing real-world issues. Analyze experiences, connect work to studies, and grasp professional paradigms. Gain practical insights and fulfill upper-division writing requirements. Apply, assess, and communicate public health concepts effectively.
PUBHLTH 195W.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 2. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
PUBHLTH 195W.restriction: Public Health Policy majors and Public Health Sciences majors only.

PUBHLTH 196A.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory I - Community-Based Research and Evaluation
PUBHLTH 196A.description: Provides training for students with an interest in clinical and translational research in a community-based setting. Cultivates skills for study design, research literature review, ethics, responsible conduct of research, and cultural competence while emphasizing professionalism and personal responsibility.

PUBHLTH 197.title: Field Studies in Public Health
PUBHLTH 197.description: Join faculty on field studies or work at field agencies post-practicum. Gain hands-on experience in real-world settings. Ideal for practical application of theoretical knowledge in diverse environments.

PUBHLTH 198.title: Directed Studies
PUBHLTH 198.description: Engage in faculty-guided research activities individually or in small groups. Explore diverse topics, develop critical thinking, and enhance research skills. Ideal for hands-on learning and academic growth.

PUBHLTH 199.title: Undergraduate Research
PUBHLTH 199.description: Engage in original research with public health faculty. Attend research group meetings and submit quarterly reports. Ideal for students pursuing research careers or advanced degrees.

PUBHLTH 200.title: Foundations of Public Health
PUBHLTH 200.description: Explores public health research and practices fundamentals from a multidisciplinary view. Gain core skills for crosscutting approaches essential in public health.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 200.prereq_text: ( HLTH, SCTY, BHVR MAJORS ONLY OR PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 200.restriction: Public Health majors, College of Health Sciences students, School of Population and Public Health students, and Master of Public Health only.

PUBHLTH 204A.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods
PUBHLTH 204A.description: Introduction to the basic statistical techniques commonly used in public health research. Topics include descriptive statistics, basic probability, inferential statistics (estimation, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing), and contingency tables. SAS software is introduced.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 204A.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 204A.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 204B.title: Biostatistics II: Intermediate Statistical Methods
PUBHLTH 204B.description: Explores advanced statistical analysis methods for biological and medical applications. Topics include linear, logistic, and generalized linear regression models like Poisson regression.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 204B.prereq_text: EPIDEM 204A with a minimum grade of B or PUBHLTH 204A with a minimum grade of B.
PUBHLTH 204B.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 204C.title: Biostatistics III: Advanced Statistical Methods
PUBHLTH 204C.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields. Introduces statistical methods for analyzing survival and longitudinal/clustered data, and techniques to resolve missing data.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 204C.prereq_text: EPIDEM 204B with a minimum grade of B or PUBHLTH 204B with a minimum grade of B.
PUBHLTH 204C.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 206A.title: Principles of Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 206A.description: Fundamental principles of epidemiology, biostatistics, and epidemiological research. Topics include research methods of measuring health problems in populations, disease control and prevention in populations, how epidemiology contributes to knowledge of disease etiology, and biostatistical analysis and interpretation of epidemiologic data.

PUBHLTH 206B.title: Intermediate Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 206B.description: Explores conceptual aspects of epidemiology, focusing on strengths and limitations of observational designs. Learn to identify, quantify, and correct bias (e.g. selection, confounding), and evaluate causal identical conditions. Gain skills to evaluate study designs systematically.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 206B.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B.
PUBHLTH 206B.restriction: Epidemiology majors, College of Health Sciences students, School of Population and Public Health students, and Master of Public Health only.

PUBHLTH 207A.title: Probability and Statistics in Public Health
PUBHLTH 207A.description: An introduction to probability and statistical methods, using examples in public health. Topics include descriptive statistics, laws of probability, discrete and continuous probability distributions, estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and power calculations for one- and two-sample comparisons.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 207A.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B.
PUBHLTH 207A.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students and Master of Public Health only.

PUBHLTH 207B.title: Analysis of Public Health Data Using Statistical Software
PUBHLTH 207B.description: Overview of common statistical methods in public health and how to implement them. Topics include linear regression, ANOVA, the Kruskal-Wallis test, logistic regression, missing data and censoring, Kaplan-Meier survival curves, log-rank tests, and Cox regression.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 207B.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 207A with a minimum grade of B.
PUBHLTH 207B.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students and Master of Public Health only.

PUBHLTH 208.title: Advances in Social Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 208.description: Introduces major themes in social epidemiology, adopting a topical approach. Weekly topics include theories, debates, methods, policy implications, and empirical examples of specific social factors. Students apply principles to their own health interests.
PUBHLTH 208.prereq_text: ( MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 208.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 209.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
PUBHLTH 209.description: Introduces basic demographic methods used in social science and public health research. Topics include sources and limitations of demographic data; components of population growth; measures of nuptiality, fertility, mortality, and population mobility projection methods; and demographic models.

PUBHLTH 210.title: Theory-Driven Secondary Data Analysis
PUBHLTH 210.description: Learn how to develop and test theoretically-driven research questions in secondary data sources. Logic of theory building and testing, how to conduct statistical analyses on testable research questions, and interpret results. There is also a lab component.
PUBHLTH 210.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 213.title: Epidemiology in Global Health
PUBHLTH 213.description: Examines epidemiology and global health. Topics include global health concepts, research in resource-poor settings, climate change's impact on health, and interventions in low-income settings. Emphasizes literature review, health determinants, and interdisciplinary approaches with a practical focus.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 213.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 213.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 216.title: Cancer Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 216.description: Concentrates on understanding how epidemiology plays a role in the search for cancer etiology, prevention, control, and treatment; gives an overview of cancer research with an appreciation of the multidisciplinary nature of the field.
PUBHLTH 216.prereq_text: EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B- or PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B-.

PUBHLTH 222A.title: Health Policy and Management
PUBHLTH 222A.description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 222A.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )

PUBHLTH 222B.title: Health Care Delivery and Financing
PUBHLTH 222B.description: Advances health policy comprehension. Explores healthcare delivery, spending, organizations, quality, insurance programs, payment mechanisms, reforms, and innovation. Special emphasis on incentives for payers, providers, and patients, influencing healthcare decisions.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 222B.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 222A with a minimum grade of B-.
PUBHLTH 222B.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 223.title: Risk Communication
PUBHLTH 223.description: Examines theory and research related to the communication of scientific information in risk communication contexts, risk perceptions, and behavior as related to decision-making under risk.

PUBHLTH 225.title: Health Politics and Policy
PUBHLTH 225.description: Explore health policy according to the World Health Organization, focusing on decisions, plans, and actions for societal health goals. Understand political institutions, stakeholders, and interest groups influencing policy. Develop policy analysis skills and advocacy strategies through an interdisciplinary approach.
PUBHLTH 225.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 222A (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B-.
PUBHLTH 225.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 228.title: Health Economics
PUBHLTH 228.description: An overview of health economics with a focus on U.S. healthcare and health management. Explore economic aspects such as evaluation, medical care demand, insurance, productivity, and markets for healthcare professionals. Delve into microeconomic theory, government regulation, and health reform.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 228.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 228.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 230.title: Public Health Science Seminar
PUBHLTH 230.description: Presents a curated series on contemporary topics and emerging research in public health, with a focus on global health and biobehavioral sciences. Through presentations by faculty and invited scholars, students engage with current debates, methods, and interdisciplinary perspectives.
PUBHLTH 230.restriction: Global Health majors, Biobehavioral Mechanisms Of Health majors, Disease Prevention majors, and Public Health majors only.

PUBHLTH 242.title: Theories of Health Communication
PUBHLTH 242.description: Evaluates health communication theory and strategies for diverse settings (healthcare, community, social media). Emphasizes audience segmentation, personalized tailoring, and subgroup targeting in case studies. Explores multimodal communication's role in persuasive messaging.

PUBHLTH 243.title: Biobehavioral Mechanisms of Health and Disease
PUBHLTH 243.description: Explore measurement of biobehavioral mechanisms underlying health and disease. Topics include assessment of stress physiology, inflammation, immune functioning, and gut microbiome using biomarkers, heart rate variability (HRV), microbiome sequencing, and ecological momentary assessment (EMA).
PUBHLTH 243.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 244.title: Health Behavior Theory
PUBHLTH 244.description: Explores theories of health behavior change, moving from individual to broader contexts, with a focus on applying theory to create population-based theory-driven models delineating behavioral determinants of public health problems.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 244.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR HLTH, SCTY, BHVR MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 244.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 245.title: Health Promotion Planning
PUBHLTH 245.description: Explores strategic planning for public health interventions, emphasizing social and behavioral health science. Develops intervention plans targeting specific health issues and populations.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 245.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 245.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 246.title: Social Research Methods
PUBHLTH 246.description: An interactive graduate seminar covering topics related to the research process and study design. Begins with conceptualizing research questions, hypotheses, and then turns to topics in measurement and concludes with experimental, quasi-experimental, and observational study designs.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 246.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 246.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 247.title: Program Evaluation
PUBHLTH 247.description: Interactive course develops program evaluation plans. Students create plans for health programs in partnership with community organizations. Activities include lectures, discussions, readings, critiques, presentations, and final evaluation plan submission.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 247.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR HLTH, SCTY, BHVR MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 247.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 248.title: Fundamentals of Maternal and Child Health - Programs, Problems, and Policy
PUBHLTH 248.description: Explores Maternal and Child Health (MCH) through public health and neurobiological perspectives. Study key factors influencing global development. Examine historical foundations, conceptual frameworks, and current issues such as COVID-19's impact. Analyze programs and legislation addressing MCH disparities.

PUBHLTH 250.title: Health Status and Care Disparities
PUBHLTH 250.description: Expert health care providers present viewpoints and interdisciplinary strategies for addressing sociocultural, economic, gender, age, and other disparities in population health status and care provision.
PUBHLTH 250.prereq_text: ( MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY )

PUBHLTH 251.title: Models of Practice and Intervention at the Community Level
PUBHLTH 251.description: Examines and critiques current models, frameworks, theories for understanding social and behavioral factors that are central to community health, and to the development, implementation, evaluation of interventions that encompass behavioral change at the group, organization, community, societal, policy, or multilevel.
PUBHLTH 251.prereq_text: CHC/LAT 200A with a minimum grade of B- or PUBHLTH 246 with a minimum grade of B-.

PUBHLTH 253.title: Introduction to Community Health and Health Equity
PUBHLTH 253.description: Explores community health roles, applications, and impacts in public health practice. Introduces community organizing, health advocacy, interventions, and strategies for addressing health inequities.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 253.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 253.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 255.title: Structural Racism and Health
PUBHLTH 255.description: Provides a basis for understanding how health inequities result from structural forms of racism in various forms—from residential segregation and environmental injustice to social and economic policies—to impact health fundamentally. Reviews evidence, measurement, analysis, and mitigation strategies.

PUBHLTH 258.title: Professional Development Seminar
PUBHLTH 258.description: Introduces expectations about scholarship and cultivate confidence to be competitive on academic job market; workshops on career development; effective approaches to presenting and critiquing research; orient students to resources, supports, and tools.
PUBHLTH 258.restriction: Health, Society, and Behavior majors and School of Population and Public Health students have the first consideration for enrollment.

PUBHLTH 264.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
PUBHLTH 264.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 264.prereq_text: ( MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 264.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 269.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
PUBHLTH 269.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

PUBHLTH 272.title: Health Psychology
PUBHLTH 272.description: Focus on theory and research in health psychology as applied to major acute, chronic, and occupational health problems. Adopting the biopsychosocial model of health, emphasis is on understanding and influencing how biology, behavior, and the environment influence health and illness.

PUBHLTH 275.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
PUBHLTH 275.description: Learn general principles and basic mathematical methods for environmental modeling and human health risk assessment, including compartmental and advection-dispersion models for contaminants in air and water, uptake by plants and animals, exposure, assessment, dose-response modeling, risk management, and risk perception.

PUBHLTH 276.title: War and Public Health
PUBHLTH 276.description: Explores war's impact on public health, including healthcare infrastructures, disease outbreaks, mental, environmental, and behavioral health, within the Social Ecological Framework. Emphasizes recent global conflicts, and U.S. military involvement overseas.

PUBHLTH 277A.title: Target Organ Toxicology I
PUBHLTH 277A.description: Outlines vulnerability of selected organ systems to environmental and occupational chemicals. Reviews molecular aspects of toxicological damage. Topics include molecular toxicology and the following organ systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, dermal, and skeletal embryology.

PUBHLTH 277B.title: Target Organ Toxicology II
PUBHLTH 277B.description: Analyzes mechanistic responses in animals and humans to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation, focusing on organ system physiology. Topics specifically covered include reproductive, endocrine, developmental, kidney, liver, pancreas, vascular, immune toxicology, radiation, and chemical carcinogenesis.
PUBHLTH 277B.prereq_text: ( PUBHLTH 277A ( min grade = B- ) OR EHS 206A ( min grade = B- ) )

PUBHLTH 278.title: Industrial Toxicology
PUBHLTH 278.description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.
PUBHLTH 278.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 277B with a minimum grade of B- or EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-.

PUBHLTH 279.title: Special Topics in Environmental & Occupational Health
PUBHLTH 279.description: Current research in environmental and occupational health. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.

PUBHLTH 280.title: Global Burden of Disease
PUBHLTH 280.description: Introduces composite measures of disease burden, including Disability Adjusted Life Years and their use in prioritizing disease burden at local, regional, and global levels. Focuses on WHO's landmark assessments and introduces DISMOD software for specific analyses.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 280.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 280.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 281.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 281.description: Covers concepts and methods of infectious disease epidemiology and case studies of various infectious diseases. Includes surveillance, outbreak investigation, emerging pathogens, ecological and molecular epidemiology.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 281.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 281.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 282.title: Climate Change and Global Health
PUBHLTH 282.description: Explore major topics in climate change and global health, analyzing micro- and macro-level impacts. Covers infectious and non-communicable diseases, demographic aspects, and interventions. Gain the ability to propose public health solutions for climate-related health challenges.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 282.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 282.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 283.title: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
PUBHLTH 283.description: Engage extensively with GIS software, combining lectures and hands-on tutorials. Cover mapping basics, projections, geocoding, and toolbars. Apply GIS to public health data for practical understanding of its applications.
PUBHLTH 283.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 206 with a minimum grade of B-.

PUBHLTH 286.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems and Spatial Epidemiology
PUBHLTH 286.description: Explore GIS software extensively, with lectures followed by hands-on tutorials. Topics include rasters, groundwater modeling, spatial statistics, and R programming. Analyze spatial epidemiology using public health data, with weekly assignments and a class project.
PUBHLTH 286.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 283 with a minimum grade of B-.

PUBHLTH 287.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Public Health
PUBHLTH 287.description: Introduction to qualitative research methods. Covers epistemology, the range of qualitative data, developing research questions appropriate for qualitative data analysis, fieldwork, data collection, analysis, and report writing. Students engage in fieldwork.

PUBHLTH 289.title: Special Topics in Global Health and Disease Prevention
PUBHLTH 289.description: Current research in global health and disease prevention. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.

PUBHLTH 290.title: Special Topics in Public Health
PUBHLTH 290.description: Studies in selected areas of public health. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

PUBHLTH 291B.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
PUBHLTH 291B.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 291B.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 291B.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 291C.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
PUBHLTH 291C.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 291C.prereq_text: ( PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR MASTER PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 291C.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 292.title: Ethics and Responsible Conduct of Research in Public Health
PUBHLTH 292.description: Ethical dimensions of public health research, practice, and policy: ethical principles and frameworks, moral challenges in public health, research ethics, oversight of public health research, structural racism and health inequities, ethical issues in cross-cultural research, research misconduct, whistleblowing.

PUBHLTH 293.title: Foundations of Clinical and Translational Science
PUBHLTH 293.description: Introduction to clinical research design, implementation, and translational science from lab to community. Foundation of clinical research design, approaches to accelerate therapeutic discoveries into healthcare practices, comparison of necessities and impediments to clinical research with transformative potential of translational science.

PUBHLTH 294.title: Research Communication in Public Health
PUBHLTH 294.description: Skills for academic writing: focus on peer-reviewed journal articles, writing strategies, effective dissemination to academic/non-academic audiences, and career-related topics for graduate students in health-related fields.

or.other: MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY

PUBHLTH 294.prereq_text: ( EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR DISEASE PREVENTION MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - EPIDEMIOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - HLTH SYS POL MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - BIOSTATISTICS MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - GLOBAL HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR BIOBEHAVIORAL MCHNSM MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - COMMUNITY HLTH MAJORS ONLY OR MPH - ENVIRON HEALTH MAJORS ONLY OR PUBLIC HEALTH MAJORS ONLY )
PUBHLTH 294.restriction: School of Population and Public Health students only.

PUBHLTH 295A.title: Graduate Practicum and Culminating Experience in Public Health I
PUBHLTH 295A.description: Supervised applied public health field practice with competency based work plan development; integration of foundational and concentration competencies; professional reflection; integrative learning experience proposal development.
PUBHLTH 295A.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 200 with a minimum grade of B and PUBHLTH 222A with a minimum grade of B and PUBHLTH 253 with a minimum grade of B and PUBHLTH 264 with a minimum grade of B and (PUBHLTH 206A with a minimum grade of B or EPIDEM 200A with a minimum grade of B).

PUBHLTH 295B.title: Graduate Practicum and Culminating Experience in Public Health II
PUBHLTH 295B.description: Completion of supervised public health field artifacts; integrative learning experience synthesis of foundational and concentration competencies; professional poster presentation; applied communication of practice-based public health work.
PUBHLTH 295B.prereq_text: PUBHLTH 295A with a minimum grade of B.

PUBHLTH 296.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
PUBHLTH 296.description: Dissertation research with Public Health faculty.

PUBHLTH 297.title: Research Design and Proposal Writing
PUBHLTH 297.description: Evaluate strengths of research findings based on methods used by researchers to develop research proposals. Components such as collaborative agreements, guidelines for proposal writing, budgeting, peer-review process, and transitioning from proposal to research project implementation are addressed.
PUBHLTH 297.restriction: Public Health majors, College of Health Sciences students, School of Population and Public Health students, and Doctor of Philosophy only.

PUBHLTH 298.title: Directed Studies in Public Health
PUBHLTH 298.description: Directed study with Public Health faculty.

PUBHLTH 299.title: Independent Study in Public Health
PUBHLTH 299.description: Independent research with Public Health faculty.

REL STD 5A.title: World Religions I
REL STD 5A.description: An introduction to the history, doctrine, culture, and writing of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

REL STD 5B.title: World Religions II
REL STD 5B.description: An introduction to various religious traditions in selected areas of the world—including India and South Asia, East Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

REL STD 5C.title: Religious Dialogue
REL STD 5C.description: Lectures and discussion on controversial topics in religion: sexual morality; religious violence; science; treatment of women and girls; religious truth, American Constitutional matters; secularization; the future of religion, and other topics.

REL STD 17.title: An Economic Approach to Religion
REL STD 17.description: Introduction to how basic economic concepts such as demand, supply, consumption, production, competition, free-riding, innovation, regulation, and rent-seeking can be applied to understand observed religious behavior.

REL STD 21.title: Philosophy and Religion
REL STD 21.description: Examines the intersection of religion and philosophy from a standpoint that does not presuppose previous academic study of either. Both Western and Eastern traditions and perspectives may be explored.

REL STD 60.title: Global Themes in Sikh Studies
REL STD 60.description: Serves as an introduction to Sikhism and the field of Sikh Studies. Examines the development of the religious tradition and the formation of the scholarly field of Sikh Studies in the contemporary Western university.

REL STD 61.title: Gender and Religion
REL STD 61.description: Introduces the topic of religion in a feminist context by performing cross-cultural exploration of gender, authority, and faith in various traditions. Study includes (but is not limited to) writings of contemporary Jewish, Christian, and Muslim feminists.

REL STD 100.title: Topics in the Study of Religion
REL STD 100.description: The intersection of religious belief and practices with selected subjects of continuing interest.

REL STD 103.title: Topics in the Philosophy of Religion
REL STD 103.description: Critical examination of philosophical concepts in religious scripture and theology, e.g., the nature and existence of God, miracles, the problem of evil, and divine command theories in ethics. May include any religious tradition.

REL STD 110W.title: Religion Research Lab: Applied Theories and Methods
REL STD 110W.description: A survey and investigation of the major thinkers, theories, and methodologies in the study of religions. Designed to develop the student's ability to analyze and articulate theoretical arguments in writing; includes a paper on relevant Religious Studies topics.
REL STD 110W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
REL STD 110W.restriction: Religious Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

REL STD 115.title: Religion and World Politics
REL STD 115.description: Examines the relationship between religion and world politics historically and today, focusing on connections with peace/war, democracy, human rights, secularism(s), and globalization. Covers major debates, scholarship, concepts, and theories through class exercises, exams, and essays.
REL STD 115.prereq_text: POL SCI 41A or INTL ST 11 or INTL ST 12 or REL STD 5A or REL STD 5B or REL STD 5C.

REL STD 120.title: Topics in Asian Religious Traditions
REL STD 120.description: Studies involving (but not limited to) Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Jainism, Sikhism, Daoism, Shinto or Shamanism, including both elite and doctrinal aspects and forms of more popular religiosity.

REL STD 122.title: Ancient India
REL STD 122.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan. Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

REL STD 123.title: Medieval India
REL STD 123.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

REL STD 124.title: Topics in Modern Indian Religion
REL STD 124.description: Topics in religions of the Indian subcontinent including, but not confined to, Hinduism, Jainism, Sikhism, Islam, and Buddhism from the founding of the Mughal Empire in 1526 to the creation of the several modern states of the Indian subcontinent.

REL STD 125.title: Jain History, Culture, and Ethics
REL STD 125.description: Introduces history, texts, philosophy, culture, and ethical practices of the Jain tradition as it developed in India and now exists globally, including in Orange County.

REL STD 126.title: Topics in Jain Studies
REL STD 126.description: Studies involving aspects of the Jain tradition in relation to philosophy, ethics, culture, ritual, art, or diaspora, and/or analyses of environment, gender, or in relation to other Indian traditions.

REL STD 130.title: Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Religious Traditions
REL STD 130.description: Character and evolution of Egyptian, Jewish, Zoroastrian, Muslim, and other religious communities of the region from their formative periods to the present era.

REL STD 130D.title: History of Antisemitism
REL STD 130D.description: Survey of the history of antisemitism, ancient to modern. Topics include medieval religious anti-Judaism, persecution of Jews and Judaism during the Crusades and the Inquisition, the rise of modern racial antisemitism, Nazi antisemitism, and the persistence of antisemitism since 1945.

REL STD 130F.title: Jews and Power
REL STD 130F.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority?

REL STD 131A.title: History of Zoroastrianism
REL STD 131A.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

REL STD 140.title: Early Western Religious Traditions
REL STD 140.description: Religious perspectives of the Mediterranean and European regions from the earliest times to approximately 1500 C.E.

REL STD 150.title: Religion in the Americas
REL STD 150.description: Religious belief and social context in North and South America from the earliest human societies to the present.

REL STD 155.title: Topics in Race and Religion
REL STD 155.description: Critical analysis of race and religion as expressed through (1) various structures of socio-political ordering, metaphysics, language, class, colorism, power, biology, nationalism, and culture, and (2) various expressions of moral philosophy, ethics, music, literature, arts, rituals, liberation, and revolution.

REL STD 158.title: Topics in Indigenous Religions
REL STD 158.description: A study of Indigenous Religions. Focus may be local, regional, or global. Primary texts may come from a variety of disciplines, with varying attention to similarities and differences to colonial religious conceptions.

REL STD 165.title: Topics in Religion and Science
REL STD 165.description: Examinations of the dynamic interplay between religion and science, including historical conflicts, contemporary dialogues, and ethical implications. Classes analyze how these two realms shape our understanding of the universe, humanity, and morality.

REL STD 170.title: Topics in Comparative Studies in Religion
REL STD 170.description: Literary, historical, or philosophical comparison of selected religious and quasi-religious traditions, their beliefs and practices.

REL STD 175.title: Medical Ethics
REL STD 175.description: Analysis of moral issues concerning health care. Topics may include just allocation of scarce medical resources, the doctor/patient relationship, genetic engineering, surrogate motherhood, abortion, euthanasia, or social policy concerning AIDS.

REL STD 199.title: Independent Study
REL STD 199.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty member. Substantial written work required.

REL STD 225.title: Jain History, Culture, and Ethics
REL STD 225.description: Introduces history, texts, philosophy, culture, and ethical practices of the Jain Tradition as it developed in India and now exists globally, including in Orange County.

REL STD 226.title: Topics in Jain Studies
REL STD 226.description: Studies involving aspects of the Jain tradition in relation to philosophy, ethics, culture, ritual, art, or diaspora, and/or analyses of environment, gender, or in relation to other Indian traditions.

REL STD 255.title: Topics in Race and Religion
REL STD 255.description: Critical analysis of race and religion as expressed through (1) various structures of socio-political ordering, metaphysics, language, class, colorism, power, biology, nationalism, and culture, and (2) various expressions of moral philosophy, ethics, music, literature, arts, rituals, liberation, and revolution.

REL STD 265.title: Topics in Religion and Science
REL STD 265.description: Examinations of the dynamic interplay between religion and science, including historical conflicts, contemporary dialogues, and ethical implications. Classes analyze how these two realms shape our understanding of the universe, humanity, and morality.

ROTC 10L.title: Military Science-Basic Leadership Laboratory
ROTC 10L.description: Provides hands-on and practical military science material covered in the corresponding military science courses.

ROTC 11.title: Military Science - Personal Development
ROTC 11.description: Focuses on life skills such as physical fitness, nutrition, and time management while providing an introduction to military knowledge, customs, and skills.

ROTC 12.title: Military Science - Leadership I
ROTC 12.description: Focuses on the fundamentals of leadership, Army leadership values, ethics, coaching, and mentoring techniques.

ROTC 13.title: Applied Leadership in Small Unit Operations
ROTC 13.description: Focuses on leadership at the tactical level and includes instruction in fundamental military skills such as map reading, land navigation, squad and platoon operations, and resource planning techniques.

ROTC 21.title: Leadership and Ethics
ROTC 21.description: Explores the dimensions of creative and innovative tactical leadership strategies and styles by examining team dynamics and two historical leadership theories that form the basis of the Army leadership requirements model.

ROTC 22.title: Team Leadership II
ROTC 22.description: Explores team dynamics and two historical leadership theories that form the basis of the Army leadership requirements model.

ROTC 23.title: Tactical Leadership II
ROTC 23.description: Examines the challenges of leading tactical teams in the OE. Highlights dimensions of terrain analysis, patrolling, and operation orders.

ROTC 100L.title: Military Science-Advanced Leadership Laboratory
ROTC 100L.description: Provides hands-on and practical exercises for the military science material covered in the corresponding military science courses as well as leader training through practical application of the Leadership Development Program.

ROTC 131.title: Adaptive Team Leadership I
ROTC 131.description: Challenges cadets to study, practice, and evaluate adaptive leadership skills as they are presented with challenging scenarios related to squad tactical operations. Cadets receive systematic and specified feedback on their leadership attributes and core leader competencies.
ROTC 131.prereq_text: ROTC 11 and ROTC 12 and ROTC 13 and ROTC 21 and ROTC 22 and ROTC 23.
ROTC 131.restriction: For students with a service obligation to the U.S. Army.

ROTC 132.title: Adaptive Team Leadership II
ROTC 132.description: Provides cadets systematic and specific feedback on their leadership attributes and core leader competencies. Based on such feedback, as well as their own self-evaluations, cadets continue to develop their leadership and critical thinking abilities.
ROTC 132.prereq_text: ROTC 11 and ROTC 12 and ROTC 13 and ROTC 21 and ROTC 22 and ROTC 23.
ROTC 132.restriction: For students with a service obligation to the U.S. Army.

ROTC 133.title: Tactical Leadership III
ROTC 133.description: Uses increasingly intense situational leadership challenges to build cadet awareness and skills in leading small units. Skills in decision-making, persuading, and motivating team members when "under fire" are explored, evaluated, and developed.
ROTC 133.prereq_text: ROTC 11 and ROTC 12 and ROTC 13 and ROTC 21 and ROTC 22 and ROTC 23.
ROTC 133.restriction: For students with a service obligation to the U.S. Army.

ROTC 141.title: Leadership III
ROTC 141.description: Transitions the focus of student learning from being trained, mentored, and evaluated as a cadet to learning how to train, mentor, and evaluate cadets. Cadets begin to learn the duties and responsibilities of an Army staff officer.
ROTC 141.restriction: For students with a service obligation to the U.S. Army.

ROTC 142.title: Developmental Leadership II
ROTC 142.description: Requires students to continue to train, mentor, and evaluate underclass cadets. Cadets learn to safely conduct training by understanding and employing the Composite Risk Management Process and the Comprehensive Soldier Fitness (CSF) program.
ROTC 142.prereq_text: ROTC 131 and ROTC 132 and ROTC 133 and ROTC 141.
ROTC 142.restriction: For students with a service obligation to the U.S. Army.

ROTC 143.title: Officership
ROTC 143.description: Explores the dynamics of leading in the complex situations of current military operations in the OE. Cadets examine differences in customs and courtesies, military law, principles of war, and rules of engagement in the face of international terrorism.
ROTC 143.prereq_text: ROTC 131 and ROTC 132 and ROTC 133 and ROTC 141 and ROTC 142.
ROTC 143.restriction: For students with a service obligation to the U.S. Army.

ROTC 151.title: Military History
ROTC 151.description: Develops an understanding of the role military officers have played in the defense of our country and the advancement of its military.

ROTC 197.title: Military Science Independent Studies
ROTC 197.description: Replaces any of the 12 core ROTC courses for students that are unable to attend the scheduled class time due to class conflicts or other extenuating circumstances. This course curriculum will mirror the course it is replacing.

RUSSIAN 1A.title: Fundamentals of Russian
RUSSIAN 1A.description: Focuses on reading, comprehension, basic composition, and conversation skills, and gives the student an initial exposure to the Russian cultural scene.

RUSSIAN 1AB.title: Intensive Russian Fundamentals
RUSSIAN 1AB.description: First half of first‐year Russian in a time‐intensive form. Development of meaningful communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with Russian speakers and beginning study of Russian. Learner‐centered approach develops speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.

RUSSIAN 1B.title: Fundamentals of Russian
RUSSIAN 1B.description: Focuses on reading, comprehension, basic composition, and conversation skills, and gives the student an initial exposure to the Russian cultural scene.
RUSSIAN 1B.prereq_text: RUSSIAN 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 1B is also accepted.

RUSSIAN 1BC.title: Intensive Russian Fundamentals
RUSSIAN 1BC.description: Second half of first‐year Russian in a time‐intensive form. Development of meaningful communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with Russian speakers and beginning study of Russian. Learner‐centered approach develops speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.
RUSSIAN 1BC.prereq_text: RUSSIAN 1AB with a minimum grade of C or RUSSIAN 1B with a minimum grade of C.

RUSSIAN 1C.title: Fundamentals of Russian
RUSSIAN 1C.description: Focuses on reading, comprehension, basic composition, and conversation skills, and gives the student an initial exposure to the Russian cultural scene.
RUSSIAN 1C.prereq_text: RUSSIAN 1AB with a minimum grade of C or RUSSIAN 1B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 1C is also accepted.

RUSSIAN 2A.title: Intermediate Russian
RUSSIAN 2A.description: Students read simple passages from contemporary Russian literary texts and newspapers. Development of oral skills and exposure to Russian culture continue.
RUSSIAN 2A.prereq_text: RUSSIAN 1BC with a minimum grade of C or RUSSIAN 1C with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 2A is also accepted.
RUSSIAN 2A.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

RUSSIAN 2B.title: Intermediate Russian
RUSSIAN 2B.description: Students read simple passages from contemporary Russian literary texts and newspapers. Development of oral skills and exposure to Russian culture continue.
RUSSIAN 2B.prereq_text: RUSSIAN 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 2B is also accepted.
RUSSIAN 2B.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

RUSSIAN 2C.title: Intermediate Russian
RUSSIAN 2C.description: Students read simple passages from contemporary Russian literary texts and newspapers. Development of oral skills and exposure to Russian culture continue.
RUSSIAN 2C.prereq_text: RUSSIAN 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 2C is also accepted.
RUSSIAN 2C.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

RUSSIAN 50.title: Topics in Russian Culture
RUSSIAN 50.description: Study of varied topics in Russian culture, area studies, and society, both in the present and in historical perspective.

RUSSIAN 139W.title: Writing About Russian Literature
RUSSIAN 139W.description: Requires at least 4,000 words of assigned composition based upon readings in Russian literature (in English translation), culture, and society. Several essays required.
RUSSIAN 139W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

RUSSIAN 150.title: Topics in Russian Literature
RUSSIAN 150.description: Examines major themes in Russian literature, film, and other media from the eighteenth to twenty-first centuries. Taught in English.

RUSSIAN 190.title: Topics in Russian Language Through Film
RUSSIAN 190.description: Uses Russian films of the late 20th century to enhance students' language skills and deepen their cultural knowledge. Work involves intensive conversation, reading and listening comprehension, and the acquisition of written skills and grammatical accuracy. Conducted primarily in Russian.

RUSSIAN 199.title: Independent Study
RUSSIAN 199.description: Independent study under direct faculty supervision.

SOC SCI 1A.title: Principles in the Social Sciences
SOC SCI 1A.description: Introduction to various disciplines within the social sciences. Provides an interdisciplinary perspective on understanding human behavior and social institutions, including interpersonal, economic, and cultural activities.

SOC SCI H1D.title: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOC SCI H1D.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

SOC SCI H1E.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOC SCI H1E.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

SOC SCI H1F.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOC SCI H1F.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
SOC SCI H1F.prereq_text: SOC SCI H1E or SOCECOL H20A.

SOC SCI H1G.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOC SCI H1G.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
SOC SCI H1G.prereq_text: SOC SCI H1F or SOCECOL H20B.

SOC SCI 2A.title: Introduction to Social Science Analysis
SOC SCI 2A.description: Introduction to social science research and analytical models. Theory construction and use of research methods in an interdisciplinary context. Discussion of the application of social science research to public policy. Computer laboratories develop creative thinking, graphing, and data presentation skills.
SOC SCI 2A.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 3A.title: Computer-Based Research in the Social Sciences
SOC SCI 3A.description: Focuses on the data manipulation, data visualization, and information searching techniques. Hands-on experience in hypothesis testing, mapping, graphics, and data arrays.
SOC SCI 3A.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 4A.title: Introduction to Global Studies
SOC SCI 4A.description: Ongoing historical processes that increase global integration, the social, economic, and political interdependence of different regions, cultures, and peoples. Topics include ancient empires, colonialism, nationalism, industrialization, modern imperialism and warfare, decolonization, global social movements, conflict, inequality, and global governance.
SOC SCI 4A.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 5A.title: Introduction to Human Geography
SOC SCI 5A.description: Human behavior in a geographical context. Spatial patterns and organization of the cultural, social, and economic activities of man as imposed on and influenced by the earth's physical setting.

SOC SCI 5B.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
SOC SCI 5B.description: An introduction to the physical world we live in. Distribution and dynamics of the earth's air, water, and solid crust. Concepts and principles from climatology and geology. Selected examples from North America and beyond.

SOC SCI 5D.title: US and World Geography
SOC SCI 5D.description: Survey of general geographical principles and facts on a world scale, as well as introduction to the broad regional and resource geography of the U.S., emphasizing in particular the interactions of physical and cultural factors.

SOC SCI 10A.title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences I
SOC SCI 10A.description: Introduction to the variety of statistical applications in the social sciences. Descriptive statistics. Measures of central tendency and dispersion. Percentile ranks. Standardization and normal approximation. Basic probability theory focuses on application to statistical inference and binomial distribution. Laboratory required.
SOC SCI 10A.restriction: Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment. SOC SCI 10A may not be taken for credit if taken after or concurrently with ECON 15A.

SOC SCI 10B.title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences II
SOC SCI 10B.description: Introduction to statistical inference, sampling distribution, standard error. Hypothesis tests for proportions and means. Inferential techniques for nominal variables including chi-square, study measures of strengths, significance of relationships between variables, assumptions, data requirements, and types of error in significance tests.
SOC SCI 10B.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 10C.title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences III
SOC SCI 10C.description: Focus on correlation, regression, and control for effects of variables. One-way and two-way factorial analysis of variance. A priori and a posteriori comparisons. Introduction to repeated measures design and non-parametric statistics. Discuss use of statistics in newspapers and popular magazines.
SOC SCI 10C.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 12.title: Global Political Ideologies
SOC SCI 12.description: An overview of the major political ideologies shaping the current world order and global conflict. Topics include liberalism, democracy, nationalism, capitalism, communism, socialism, fascism, neoliberalism, clash of civilizations, sectarian violence, populist nationalism, and de-globalization.
