SOC SCI 12.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 15.title: Global Political Economy
SOC SCI 15.description: The global economy as an integrated system. The rise of world trade, capitalism, national economies, market cycles, competing economic ideologies, development, globalization, transnational labor, multinational corporations, and the role of UN, World Bank, WTO, and the IMF in global governance.
SOC SCI 15.restriction: International Studies majors and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 16.title: Human Rights and Global Governance
SOC SCI 16.description: Historical development of civil, political rights and the rise of human rights in international law. Explores role, and limitations, of the UN, ICJ, and ICC in global governance. Reconceptualizing democracy and political representation in a postnational 21st century.
SOC SCI 16.restriction: International Studies majors and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 17.title: Global Environmental Issues
SOC SCI 17.description: Examines problems such as global climate change, growing human populations, fisheries depletion, ocean acidification, biodiversity loss, deforestation, and food security. Introduces political, social, and economic factors contributing to environmental issues and their disproportional impacts on the world’s poor and minorities.
SOC SCI 17.restriction: International Studies majors and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 19.title: AI Literacy
SOC SCI 19.description: Introduction to the basics of contemporary artificial intelligence. Distinction between symbolic and neural AIs. Generative AI, prediction engines, recommendation systems, machine perception. Near-term ethical issues, medium-term economic implications, long-term risk, and safety.
SOC SCI 19.prereq_text: NO LPS 19 AND NO REPEATS ALLOWED

SOC SCI 40.title: Social Policy and Public Service
SOC SCI 40.description: An introduction to the basic theories and principles of public policy. Students examine various influences on the development of public policy and the principle actors in the process, and learn to identify tools and techniques employed in policy making.

SOC SCI 66.title: Introduction to Gangs
SOC SCI 66.description: Introduces students to street gang subculture and explores risk factors associated with gang membership. Students develop a working definition for street gang and understand the difference between social and legal definitions. Also explores the connection between prison and street gangs.

SOC SCI 70C.title: Comparing Cultures
SOC SCI 70C.description: Introduces students to the scope of cross-cultural comparisons by analyzing the theories, methodologies, and facts utilized by anthropologists, sociologists, social psychologists, political scientists, and historians in comparing cultures.

SOC SCI 78A.title: Asian American Histories
SOC SCI 78A.description: Examines and compares diverse experiences of major Asian American groups since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics include origins of emigration; the formation and transformation of community; gender and family life; changing roles of Asian Americans in American society. Formerly ASIANAM 60A.

SOC SCI 78B.title: Asian American Communities
SOC SCI 78B.description: Examines the renewal of Asian immigration following World War II. Explores contemporary Asian American populations and communities in the U.S., and the impact of contemporary Asian immigration on the U.S. political economy and social order.

SOC SCI 78C.title: Asian Americans and Race
SOC SCI 78C.description: Analyzes the Asian American experience in comparative perspective, which includes comparisons of different ethnic and racial groups, and across gender and class. Possible topics include labor, economy, politics, migration, nation, popular culture, gender, family, sexuality, and multiraciality.

SOC SCI 89.title: Special Topics in Social Sciences
SOC SCI 89.description: Studies in selected areas of Social Sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOC SCI 102A.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems in Social Sciences
SOC SCI 102A.description: Hands-on laboratory course introduces students to the fundamentals of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) technology using social science applications. Students learn to organize, manipulate, and display spatial data leading to the design of their own GIS research project.
SOC SCI 102A.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 102B.title: Intermediate Geographic Information Systems in Social Sciences
SOC SCI 102B.description: Expands Geographic Information Systems (GIS) skills to more advanced theories and concepts in the spatial analysis of social science issues and particularly to analyzing and interpreting spatial data. Students develop and complete a GIS research project of their own choosing.
SOC SCI 102B.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 103A.title: Game Theory and Politics I
SOC SCI 103A.description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.
SOC SCI 103A.restriction: Social Policy and Public Service majors, Political Science majors, International Studies majors, and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 115D.title: International Business
SOC SCI 115D.description: Introduction to conducting business in the international arena, decision-making in the organization, and globalization of markets and production. Topics covered range from tax and finance to ethics, marketing, and more. Continuing corporate regulatory scandals discussed.

SOC SCI 119.title: Special Topics in Geography
SOC SCI 119.description: Studies in selected areas of geography. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOC SCI 120.title: Transnational Gangs
SOC SCI 120.description: Examines the internationalization of U.S. domestic street gangs. The relationship between California gangs Mara Salvatrucha and 18th Street and Mexico/Central American gangs is assessed. Specified topics include: mobilization, migration, territorialism, culture, organization, and use of technology.

SOC SCI 121T.title: Voting and Political Manipulation
SOC SCI 121T.description: Introduction to social choice and cooperative games. Topics include majority rule, types of voting methods, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.
SOC SCI 121T.restriction: Business Economics majors, Political Science majors, International Studies majors, and Social Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 132.title: Veterans in History and Society
SOC SCI 132.description: Explores key concepts, issues, and trends in the interdisciplinary field of veterans studies. Students gain a deep understanding of the ways that social scientists and historians have analyzed the identities, experiences, and worldviews of U.S. military veterans.

SOC SCI 133.title: Veterans’ Transitions
SOC SCI 133.description: Provides veteran and non-veteran students with a comprehensive and academically rigorous overview of the ways and means through which diverse communities of veterans have made and continue to make the complex and multi-faceted transition from active military.

SOC SCI 134W.title: Veterans’ Voices
SOC SCI 134W.description: Uses the medium of academic writing to develop a broad understanding and appreciation for the wide range of worldviews, priorities, and values embodied in the creative production and activism of diverse U.S. military veterans.

SOC SCI 147CW.title: International Humanitarianism
SOC SCI 147CW.description: Examines, analyzes, and evaluates the humanitarian phenomenon, the actors involved in it (including states, international organizations (IOs), and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs)), the rise of a body of international humanitarian law, and the problems and debates associated with international humanitarianism today.
SOC SCI 147CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOC SCI 152A.title: Non-Government Organization (NGO) Fundamentals
SOC SCI 152A.description: Introduction to non-governmental organizations, including their role in U.S. society and the international community. Explores varying definitions of NGOs and the characteristics held in common by all NGOs.

SOC SCI 152C.title: American Public Policy
SOC SCI 152C.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

SOC SCI 160.title: Leadership Through Mentorship
SOC SCI 160.description: A mentor driven forum, features lectures and discussions by professional leaders highlighting effective leadership styles, narratives, and accomplishments. Students learn different leadership methods and gain insight to their own professional aspirations.
SOC SCI 160.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only. Must be admitted to the LEADHER Mentoring Program to enroll. Undergraduate students only.

SOC SCI 163A.title: Race in the City: Past, Present, and Future
SOC SCI 163A.description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

SOC SCI 164.title: Chicane/Latine Education
SOC SCI 164.description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latine low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

SOC SCI 164B.title: Domestic Gangs
SOC SCI 164B.description: Examines the history and development of California street gangs and the role of historical events in that development. Students will be able to contrast and compare gang cohort behaviors between some of the major gangs in California.
SOC SCI 164B.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 164C.title: Prison Gangs
SOC SCI 164C.description: Examines the growth and spread of prison gangs throughout the country. Relationships between prison and street gangs, and possible relationships with foreign drug trafficking organizations studied. Violence examined as the standard to establish dominance in and out of prison.
SOC SCI 164C.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 164D.title: Juvenile Gangs
SOC SCI 164D.description: Examines risk factors that can be used to predict gang membership. Compares generational with non-generational gangs and develops a working sociological definition that can be used to identify street gangs. Myths about juveniles, street gangs.
SOC SCI 164D.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 165.title: Chicano/Latino Families
SOC SCI 165.description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

SOC SCI 168B.title: Immigration and Inequality
SOC SCI 168B.description: Explores immigration, ethnicity, and inequality as interconnected social forces. International migration, propelled by global inequalities, plays a central role in the formation of multinational societies, shapes inter-group relations and patterns of ethnic inequality, and transforms the immigrants themselves.

SOC SCI 170A.title: Research Methods in the Social Sciences
SOC SCI 170A.description: Examines how interdisciplinary social science research questions are formulated and studies several research methods including: experimental method, quasi-experimental methods, survey research, field research, evaluation research, and meta-analysis. Parametric and non-parametric statistical methods are illustrated using the SPSS program.
SOC SCI 170A.prereq_text: SOC SCI 1A and SOC SCI 2A and SOC SCI 3A and (SOC SCI 10A or STATS 7).
SOC SCI 170A.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 172AW.title: American Culture
SOC SCI 172AW.description: A survey of the historical development of dominant American culture and society; emphasis on a close reading of key cultural texts, with weekly text as a model of writing, examining its use of language and rhetoric.
SOC SCI 172AW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOC SCI 172AW.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 173N.title: Revolution in Latin America
SOC SCI 173N.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada. Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

SOC SCI 177B.title: Asian American Women
SOC SCI 177B.description: Examines the representations and experiences of Asian American women from diverse perspectives. Explores the commonalities and differences among various groups of Asian American women, with particular focus on history, culture, values, and family roles.

SOC SCI 178C.title: Korean American Studies
SOC SCI 178C.description: Explores the factors that have distinctly shaped the Korean American experience, including patterns of racial domination, the profile of immigrant flow, immigrant roles in the urban political economy, politics in Korea, and the role of the church.

SOC SCI 178D.title: Vietnamese American Studies
SOC SCI 178D.description: Studies the resettlement of Vietnamese in the United States following their exodus from Southeast Asia. Topics include the Vietnam War, the 1975 evacuation, boat and land refugees, the shaping of Vietnamese communities, and Vietnamese American literature.

SOC SCI 178E.title: Japanese American Studies
SOC SCI 178E.description: Studies the settlement of Japanese in Hawaii and the continental United States since the late 19th century. Topics include sugar plantations, development of rural Japanese America, World War II internment, post-War community development, and persistence of Japanese American identity.

SOC SCI 178F.title: South Asian American Studies
SOC SCI 178F.description: Examines and compares the experiences of South Asian immigrants in the U.S. over time. Looks at the economic, political, and social positions of the immigrants, with special emphasis on religious changes and the changes in the second and later generations.
SOC SCI 178F.restriction: Asian American Studies majors and Social Policy and Public Service majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 178H.title: Southeast Asian American Studies
SOC SCI 178H.description: Analyzes experiences of refugees and immigrants from Southeast Asia, which may include those from Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, and the Philippines. Examines political and economic factors for their exodus and how they reconstruct their identities, histories, and communities.

SOC SCI 178K.title: Filipina/Filipino American Studies
SOC SCI 178K.description: Explores the experience of Filipina/Filipino Americans from the era of Spanish colonization of the Philippines to present-day community formations in the United States, with special emphasis on the 20th century. Topics include colonialism, nation, migration, gender, and culture.

SOC SCI 179.title: Special Topics in Asian American Studies
SOC SCI 179.description: Studies in selected areas of Asian American Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOC SCI 180A.title: Summer Program in Research and Leadership A
SOC SCI 180A.description: Builds understanding of computational research methods and project design using diverse information sources. Focuses on social science statistics, including exploratory and descriptive analysis, chi-square, correlation, regression, and multiple regression techniques for applied research interpretation and practice.
SOC SCI 180A.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only. Students must apply and be admitted to enroll.

SOC SCI 180B.title: Summer Program in Research and Leadership B
SOC SCI 180B.description: Introduces theories and methods for quantitative and qualitative research in social sciences and humanities. Students develop research interests, design original proposals, apply methods like ethnography and statistics, conduct ethical fieldwork, and connect theory, methodology, and critical analysis.
SOC SCI 180B.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only. Students must apply and be admitted to enroll.

SOC SCI 180C.title: Summer Program in Research and Leadership C
SOC SCI 180C.description: Explores the transformative potential of graduate education. Students engage with texts, guest speakers, and workshops on mentorship, work-life balance, and graduate preparation while developing personal statements, relationships, and professional pathways across academia, public service, law, and consulting.
SOC SCI 180C.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only. Students must apply and be admitted to enroll.

SOC SCI 181A.title: Ethical Leadership
SOC SCI 181A.description: Explores historical and contemporary theories of ethical and unethical leadership. Examines models of "good leadership" such as cardinal and monastic virtues; and models of "bad leadership," such as Machiavelli's Prince. Explores the philosophies, styles, and accomplishments of leaders.
SOC SCI 181A.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 183A.title: Global and International Studies Forum
SOC SCI 183A.description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.

SOC SCI 183CW.title: Seminar Conflict Resolution
SOC SCI 183CW.description: Designed for seniors who are pursuing the International Studies major and/or minor. Provides a forum in which students will refine skills and theory in the study of cooperation and conflict, from local to global arenas. Students write research paper.
SOC SCI 183CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOC SCI 183CW.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 183E.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
SOC SCI 183E.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

SOC SCI 184A.title: Sage Leader Research I
SOC SCI 184A.description: Participants in the SAGE Scholars Program learn to define leadership concepts, discover various leadership styles, and develop strong leadership and communication skills resulting in strengthened ability to contribute to and interact with UCI and the Orange County community.

SOC SCI 184B.title: Sage Leader Research II
SOC SCI 184B.description: Provides a survey of contemporary topics and challenges in the fields of management and leadership. Case studies and text by leading authors are used to analyze key leadership issues in twenty-first century, with particular emphasis on current events.

SOC SCI 184GW.title: Media Writing
SOC SCI 184GW.description: Designed to teach reporting and news writing basics. Students learn how to gather and organize information, ask effective questions, develop story ideas, research facts, and write stories on deadline.
SOC SCI 184GW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOC SCI 184GW.restriction: International Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI 185W.title: People in Society
SOC SCI 185W.description: Through readings about people in distinctly different societies throughout history, students learn concepts that cross the boundaries of the social science disciplines. Such themes as democracy, elitism, power, social class, and gender are the basis for discussion and writing.
SOC SCI 185W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOC SCI 185W.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only.

SOC SCI 187.title: Twenty-First-Century Graduate Education
SOC SCI 187.description: Graduate and professional education in twenty-first century United States. Examines strategies for admission to postbaccalaureate programs and success in graduate study culture. Introduction to processes including planning and preparation, school selection, entrance examination preparation, submission of applications, writing personal statements.

SOC SCI 188A.title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
SOC SCI 188A.description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

SOC SCI 188B.title: Arab Uprisings
SOC SCI 188B.description: Examines political mobilization against authoritarian rule in individual Arab countries, explaining specific outcome in each. Addresses the movement’s second wind nearly a decade later, which affected a new subset of Arab countries.
SOC SCI 188B.restriction: Formerly offered under SOC SCI 189 / INTL ST 179 / POL SCI 149.

SOC SCI 188K.title: Political Islam
SOC SCI 188K.description: Political Islamd is a diverse phenomenon. While noticeable barriers exist to "Islamist democracy," it is the Islamists who will define the political future of much of the Muslim world. Reviews the experience of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, and Indonesia.

SOC SCI 189.title: Special Topics in Social Sciences
SOC SCI 189.description: Studies in selected areas of social sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
SOC SCI 189.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOC SCI H190A.title: Honors Research Workshop
SOC SCI H190A.description: Student develops a 10–15-page prospectus of research for the honors thesis which includes: the research question, literature review, methods of investigation, and bibliography. Student selects a faculty mentor who will supervise thesis research and writing in winter and spring.
SOC SCI H190A.restriction: Social Science majors and Social Policy and Public Service majors only.

SOC SCI H190B.title: Honors Thesis Research
SOC SCI H190B.description: The student initiates and completes data collection for the honors thesis. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
SOC SCI H190B.prereq_text: SOC SCI H190A or SPPS H190A.

SOC SCI H190C.title: Honors Thesis
SOC SCI H190C.description: The student completes, with the approval of the faculty mentor, an honors thesis containing: statement of the problem, literature review, research hypotheses, methods of investigation, results, discussion, and bibliography.
SOC SCI H190C.prereq_text: SOC SCI H190B or SPPS H190B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOC SCI 193A.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
SOC SCI 193A.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
SOC SCI 193A.prereq_text: SOC SCI 70C or SOCIOL 63. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOC SCI 193A.restriction: Social Policy and Public Service majors only.

SOC SCI 193B.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
SOC SCI 193B.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.

SOC SCI 193CW.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
SOC SCI 193CW.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and under-served communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.

SOC SCI 194A.title: Public Service Internship
SOC SCI 194A.description: Introduces the role of etiquette and leadership in the professional environment. With a two-unit (50 hours) or four-unit (100 hours) credit option, students intern at a nonprofit agency exploring their roles as community leaders and improving their professional skills.
SOC SCI 194A.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOC SCI 194A.restriction: Social Policy and Public Service majors only.

SOC SCI 194C.title: Management and Leadership Practicum-Social Science
SOC SCI 194C.description: Social Sciences Academic Resource Center (SSARC) Resource Mangers (RMs) report directly to the Director and Associate Director, serving as frontline resource consultants, assisting visitors with resume development, graduate and professional school planning, internship placement, and professional development.

SOC SCI 195A.title: Educational Policy Field Studies
SOC SCI 195A.description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.

SOC SCI 195B.title: Educational Policy Field Studies
SOC SCI 195B.description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.

SOC SCI 195C.title: Educational Policy Field Studies
SOC SCI 195C.description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.

SOC SCI 197.title: Professional Internship
SOC SCI 197.description: Students apply classroom knowledge through research projects in nonprofit agencies (local, state, and government) and the private sector. They pose solutions to agency-posed questions. Students gain field experience through 50 hours (for 2 units) or 100 (for 4 units).
SOC SCI 197.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOC SCI 197.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only.

SOC SCI 198.title: Directed Group Study
SOC SCI 198.description: Directed study with Social Science faculty.

SOC SCI 199.title: Individual Study
SOC SCI 199.description: Opportunities to do research and learn new skills outside the normal classroom environment. Students participate in planned research and study activities under a written contract with a supervising UCI instructor. Students may enroll for only one 199 each quarter.

SOC SCI 253K.title: Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
SOC SCI 253K.description: A required writing-intensive seminar conducted by an instructor affiliated with the Race and Justice Studies emphasis. Students with manuscripts on relevant topics will read and critique peer manuscripts, and revise manuscripts toward completion of articles, dissertation chapters, and other publications.
SOC SCI 253K.prereq_text: CRM/LAW C260C with a minimum grade of B-.

SOC SCI 254A.title: Transnational Migration
SOC SCI 254A.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

SOC SCI 290.title: Dissertation Research
SOC SCI 290.description: Dissertation research with Social Science faculty.

SOC SCI 299.title: Independent Study
SOC SCI 299.description: Independent research with Social Science faculty.

SOCECOL 1.title: Introduction to Social Ecology
SOCECOL 1.description: Introduction to the ecological paradigm through a consideration of the classic and recent works in human, cultural, and social ecology. Emphasis on the use of the ecological paradigm as an aid in analyzing societal problems and prescribing for their amelioration.

SOCECOL 10.title: Research Design
SOCECOL 10.description: An introduction to the logic behind and methods of designing and conducting research studies in Social Ecology. Topics include how to measure variables of interest, identifying causal relationships, sampling, survey research methods, experiments, quasi-experimental designs, and ethics in research.
SOCECOL 10.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors and School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 13.title: Statistical Analysis in Social Ecology
SOCECOL 13.description: Introduction to the techniques of statistical analysis in Social Ecology. Topics include probability, statistical inference, significance testing, univariate descriptive statistics, and multivariate analysis from an interdisciplinary perspective.

and.not: AP STATISTICS score of 3 or greater

SOCECOL 13.prereq_text: NO AP STATISTICS score of 3 or greater AND NO STATS 7 AND NO STATS 8 AND NO STATS 67 AND NO PSYCH 10A AND NO SOCIOL 10A AND NO POL SCI 10A AND NO SOC SCI 10A AND NO COGS 10A
SOCECOL 13.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors and School of Social Ecology students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCECOL H20A.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOCECOL H20A.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

SOCECOL H20B.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOCECOL H20B.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
SOCECOL H20B.prereq_text: SOC SCI H1E or SOCECOL H20A.

SOCECOL H20C.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOCECOL H20C.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
SOCECOL H20C.prereq_text: SOC SCI H1F or SOCECOL H20B.

SOCECOL H20D.title: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
SOCECOL H20D.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

SOCECOL 74A.title: Moral Development and Just Communities
SOCECOL 74A.description: A three-quarter sequence exploring interpersonal, personal, and social issues based on principles of fairness and justice. Both the living environment of a University residence hall and selected institutions of society are analyzed in terms of moral development theory.

SOCECOL 74B.title: Moral Development and Just Communities
SOCECOL 74B.description: A three-quarter sequence exploring interpersonal, personal, and social issues based on principles of fairness and justice. Both the living environment of a University residence hall and selected institutions of society are analyzed in terms of moral development theory.

SOCECOL 74C.title: Moral Development and Just Communities
SOCECOL 74C.description: A three-quarter sequence exploring interpersonal, personal, and social issues based on principles of fairness and justice. Both the living environment of a University residence hall and selected institutions of society are analyzed in terms of moral development theory.

SOCECOL 100.title: Special Topics in Social Ecology
SOCECOL 100.description: Special topics courses are offered from time to time. In general they will focus on a topic from interdisciplinary perspectives. Course content varies with the interest of the instructor.
SOCECOL 100.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 104W.title: Community Archiving in Social Ecology
SOCECOL 104W.description: Students are trained in community archiving, oral history, and ethnography in order to produce material for submission to a student-initiated Social Ecology community archive housed in the UC Irvine Special Collections section of the UC Irvine libraries.
SOCECOL 104W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Minimum cumulative GPA above 2.0. Authorization for field study.
SOCECOL 104W.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 106W.title: Building, Analyzing, and Sustaining a Digital Media Archive
SOCECOL 106W.description: Students are trained in contributing to and managing a digital media archive. Provided an opportunity to use resources in the archive to develop policy proposals to solve real-world problems at the intersection of crime, law, and society.
SOCECOL 106W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Minimum cumulative GPA above 2.0. Authorization for field study.
SOCECOL 106W.restriction: School of Social Ecology students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCECOL 111W.title: Advanced Research Methods
SOCECOL 111W.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
SOCECOL 111W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOCECOL 118.title: Domestic Violence
SOCECOL 118.description: General perspectives about domestic violence and theoretical accounts about what causes such behavior.
SOCECOL 118.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCECOL 119.title: Violence in Intimate Relationships
SOCECOL 119.description: Responses to various forms of domestic violence, such as intimate partner violence and child abuse. Covers barriers to reporting to the police, and prosecutors and courts. Human services, such as safety planning for victims, treatment programs, and restorative justice approaches.
SOCECOL 119.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors and Social Ecology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCECOL E127.title: Nuclear Environments
SOCECOL E127.description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.
SOCECOL E127.prereq_text: NO INTL ST 122 AND NO PUBHLTH 168

SOCECOL 183A.title: Global and International Studies Forum
SOCECOL 183A.description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.

SOCECOL 186A.title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability I
SOCECOL 186A.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare bibliography.
SOCECOL 186A.restriction: Seniors and Global Sustainability minors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCECOL 186B.title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability II
SOCECOL 186B.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare research proposal.
SOCECOL 186B.prereq_text: BIO SCI 191A or SOCECOL 186A or EARTHSS 190A.

SOCECOL 186CW.title: Writing/Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability III
SOCECOL 186CW.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum also is required. Seminar utilized to analyze Forum presentations and to prepare senior research paper. Prepare/write research paper under direction of faculty member.
SOCECOL 186CW.prereq_text: BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B. BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOCECOL 189.title: Advanced Seminar in the Science and Practice of Compassion
SOCECOL 189.description: For students who are accepted into the Global Service Scholars Program. Provides advanced training in empathy and compassion, and prepares students for their summer international field experience.

SOCECOL 190.title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
SOCECOL 190.description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.
SOCECOL 190.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCECOL H190A.title: Honors Research
SOCECOL H190A.description: Independent work on an individual research project in addition to participation in a mini proseminar in which faculty discuss their ongoing research. Students prepare a written proposal for a research project.
SOCECOL H190A.restriction: Seniors only. School of Social Ecology Honors students only.

SOCECOL H190B.title: Honors Research
SOCECOL H190B.description: Independent work on an individual research project in a addition to participation in a mini proseminar in which faculty discuss their ongoing research. Students prepare a written proposal for a research project.
SOCECOL H190B.restriction: Seniors only. School of Social Ecology Honors students only.

SOCECOL H190W.title: Honors Research
SOCECOL H190W.description: Students write up their honors research project (H190A-B) and prepare an oral report which is presented at the honors seminar.
SOCECOL H190W.prereq_text: SOCECOL H190B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCECOL H190W.restriction: Seniors only. School of Social Ecology Honors students only.

SOCECOL 194W.title: Naturalistic Field Research
SOCECOL 194W.description: Introduction to alternative models of experiential learning and to various methods of observation, assessment, and evaluation. Introduction to the nature of organizations and ethical issues that emerge from research and intervention in natural settings.
SOCECOL 194W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCECOL 194W.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 195.title: Field Study
SOCECOL 195.description: Community engagement to facilitate civic education through field research experience, social intervention, and professionalization. Small group instruction, discussion, writing, and presentations synthesizing students’ experiences in the field with theory, paradigms, and ideas learned about in their course work.
SOCECOL 195.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 195A.title: Advanced Field Study
SOCECOL 195A.description: While completing 8 hours of field work per week, students become acquainted with the goals and activities of their placement and work closely with the placement supervisor and AFS instructor to identify the scope of a community project.
SOCECOL 195A.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10. Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required.
SOCECOL 195A.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 195B.title: Advanced Field Study
SOCECOL 195B.description: While completing 8 hours of field work per week, students implement their research project through data collection and observations which allow them to reflect on, apply, and synthesize their academic training through observations and experiences at the placement.
SOCECOL 195B.prereq_text: SOCECOL 195A. Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required.
SOCECOL 195B.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 195CW.title: Advanced Field Study
SOCECOL 195CW.description: While completing 8 hours per week of field work, students write and finalize their AFS Client Project in consultation with the placement and the FS instructor, and make a final written and oral presentation to the placement and invited guests.
SOCECOL 195CW.prereq_text: SOCECOL 195B. Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCECOL 195CW.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.

SOCECOL 195W.title: Field Study Writing Seminar
SOCECOL 195W.description: Community engagement to promote civic education through field research experience, and the opportunity to study social issues and the environments where they occur. Develop discipline-specific writing and communication skills, methodology, and integrate information from multiple sources.
SOCECOL 195W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10. Cumulative UC GPA of 2.0. Authorization is required. Successful completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCECOL 195W.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology and Social Behavior majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors only.

SOCECOL 198.title: Directed Studies
SOCECOL 198.description: Directed study with Social Ecology faculty.

SOCECOL 199.title: Special Studies
SOCECOL 199.description: Special Studies with Social Ecology faculty.

SOCECOL 264A.title: Data Analysis
SOCECOL 264A.description: Provides an appreciation and understanding of statistics necessary to conduct applied research. Topics include approaches to and presentation of data, robust statistics, standardization techniques, multivariate regression, and analysis of variance.

SOCECOL 264B.title: Data Analysis
SOCECOL 264B.description: Provides an appreciation and understanding of statistics necessary to conduct applied research. Topics include approaches to and presentation of data, robust statistics, standardization techniques, multivariate regression, and analysis of variance.
SOCECOL 264B.prereq_text: SOCECOL 264A with a minimum grade of B-.

SOCECOL 266D.title: Analysis of Survival Data
SOCECOL 266D.description: Provides an introduction to survival analysis methods for the analysis of change in discrete dependent variables. Focuses on data collection strategies for obtaining longitudinal data and continuous-time hazards models. Communicates the variety and power of multivariate hazard models.

SOCECOL 272A.title: Structural Equation Modeling I
SOCECOL 272A.description: The general structural equation model is developed including path models, recursive and nonrecursive structural models, multiple indicator models, and confirmatory factor models. Use of LISREL and other software for estimating model parameters is covered.
SOCECOL 272A.prereq_text: SOCECOL 264A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCECOL 264B with a minimum grade of B-.

SOCECOL 272B.title: Structural Equation Modeling II: Longitudinal and Advanced Topics
SOCECOL 272B.description: Provides hands-on experience with longitudinal and advanced structural equation models and is of interest to students from a range of disciplines. Topics covered include confirmatory factor, latent growth curve, general growth mixture, and multi-level modeling.
SOCECOL 272B.prereq_text: SOCECOL 272A with a minimum grade of B-.

SOCECOL 275.title: Special Topics in Social Ecology
SOCECOL 275.description: Topics covered vary with interests of the instructor.

SOCECOL 295.title: Masters Thesis Research & Writing
SOCECOL 295.description: Independent research with Social Ecology faculty.

SOCECOL 296.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research & Writing
SOCECOL 296.description: Dissertation research with Social Ecology faculty.

SOCECOL 298.title: Directed Studies
SOCECOL 298.description: Directed study with Social Ecology faculty.

SOCECOL 299.title: Independent Study
SOCECOL 299.description: Independent study with Social Ecology faculty.

SOCIOL 1.title: Introduction to Sociology
SOCIOL 1.description: Considers major sociological concepts, theories, and research findings illuminating processes of interpersonal interaction, social differentiation and stratification, integration and conflict, and change, with attention to variation in class, race/ethnic, gender, multicultural, and cross-national perspectives and experiences.

SOCIOL 2.title: Globalization
SOCIOL 2.description: Examines globalization and international issues from the perspective of sociology and related fields. Issues include economic globalization and global inequality, international environmental problems, international politics, trends in global culture, and global conflict.

SOCIOL 3.title: Social Problems
SOCIOL 3.description: Focuses on how institutional and organizational features of societies generate problems for people. Particular attention directed at a set of problems related to political and economic inequality: poverty, racism, sexism, urban and population problems, the environment, the criminal justice system.

SOCIOL 10A.title: Probability and Statistics
SOCIOL 10A.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.
SOCIOL 10A.prereq_text: NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = F OR BETTER
SOCIOL 10A.restriction: Anthropology majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 10B.title: Probability and Statistics
SOCIOL 10B.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.
SOCIOL 10B.restriction: Anthropology majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 10C.title: Probability and Statistics
SOCIOL 10C.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.
SOCIOL 10C.restriction: Anthropology majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 19.title: Special Topics: Methods
SOCIOL 19.description: Studies in selected areas of methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 29.title: Special Topics: Theory
SOCIOL 29.description: Studies in selected areas of theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 31.title: Self-Identity and Society
SOCIOL 31.description: Studies sociological contributions to theory and research in social psychology, with focus on the social influences on personality, attitudes, beliefs, and behavior; socialization, human groups, and social interaction.

SOCIOL 39.title: Special Topics: Social Psychology
SOCIOL 39.description: Studies in selected areas of social psychology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 41.title: Small Group Dynamics
SOCIOL 41.description: Deals with models for understanding behavior in small groups, including coalition formation, socialization, group norms and decision rules, leadership, conformity, group structure, and communication processes.
SOCIOL 41.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 43.title: City and Community
SOCIOL 43.description: Examines nature, causes, and consequences of urbanization along with changing scale and complexity, demographic/ecological city growth patterns, quality of life in urban areas, processes of decision-making, and bearing of sociological investigation on public policy concerns in contemporary urban society.

SOCIOL 44.title: Births, Deaths, and Migration
SOCIOL 44.description: Introduction to the analysis of human population including fertility, mortality dispersion, sex distribution. Attention is focused on the effects of these variables on, e.g., over-population, social disorganization, and the stability of social institutions.

SOCIOL 51.title: Asian American Family & Community
SOCIOL 51.description: Briefly examines the history of different Asian American groups and provides an in-depth analysis of issues related to family composition, mate selection, changing gender roles, and intergenerational conflict.

SOCIOL 52.title: Disability in Society
SOCIOL 52.description: Explores issues around disability in society, including the central place that ableism plays in contemporary societies and the implications of categorizing certain bodies as disabled for social inequality.

SOCIOL 56.title: Religion and Society
SOCIOL 56.description: A critical and personal examination of the varieties of religious and spiritual experiences human beings are undergoing in contemporary society. The role of conscious understanding and unconscious conditioning regarding religion and spirituality.
SOCIOL 56.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 59.title: Special Topics: Social Institutions and Culture
SOCIOL 59.description: Studies in selected areas of social institutions and culture. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 62.title: Families and Intimate Relations
SOCIOL 62.description: Sociological theories/research on marriage, kinship, intimacy, and divorce. Emphasis on comparing family patterns in different social classes, ethnic groups, and societies, and on relating family life to the economy and other social institutions. Topics include gender roles, child-rearing, historical change.

SOCIOL 63.title: Race and Ethnicity
SOCIOL 63.description: Focuses on racial and ethnic relations in the United States and compares them with those found in other societies. Analyzes the conditions that favor either cooperation and integration or rivalry, tension, and conflict. Appraises strategies for reducing and resolving conflicts.

SOCIOL 64.title: Sociology of Sexuality
SOCIOL 64.description: Provides an introduction to and overview of the sociology of sex and sexuality. Considers the social meanings of sex and sexuality, the social contexts of sex and sexuality, and the social regulations of sex and sexuality.

SOCIOL 68.title: Gender and Race Inequality in the Workplace
SOCIOL 68.description: Analysis of current state and trends in major inequality measures including the wage gap, occupational segregation, and access to managerial positions. Theories that purport to explain such differences, and the related empirical evidence, are also covered.

SOCIOL 68A.title: Ethnic and Immigrant America
SOCIOL 68A.description: Focusing on Asian, Latino, and Black immigrant groups, examines the second generation's experience of straddling two cultures and growing up American. Covers topics such as assimilation, bilingualism, race relations, education, bicultural conflicts, interracial marriage, and multiracial identities.

SOCIOL 69.title: Special Topics: Age, Gender, Race, and Ethnicity
SOCIOL 69.description: Studies in selected areas of age, gender, race, and ethnicity. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 79.title: Special Topics: Societies and Social Inequality
SOCIOL 79.description: Studies in selected areas of societies and social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 110.title: Research Methods
SOCIOL 110.description: Methods of data collection and analysis used by sociologists. Experimental methods, surveys, and interviews, field research and participant observation, demographic methods, historical and comparative approaches.
SOCIOL 110.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 119.title: Special Topics: Methods
SOCIOL 119.description: Studies in selected areas of methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
SOCIOL 119.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 120.title: Sociological Theory
SOCIOL 120.description: What a theory of society is and is not. Historical and contemporary models, perspectives, and schools.
SOCIOL 120.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 134.title: Game Theory and Politics I
SOCIOL 134.description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.
SOCIOL 134.restriction: Social Policy and Public Service majors, Political Science majors, International Studies majors, and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 135.title: Social Psychology of Networks
SOCIOL 135.description: Review of network methods used in small group and organizational research. Discussion of social psychological literature relevant to the network of study of cognitive social structure, exchange/communication, identity negotiation, and social control. Case study of network datasets exemplifies research issues.
SOCIOL 135.restriction: Psychology majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 138.title: Business Decisions
SOCIOL 138.description: Surveys normative and descriptive models of decision-making behavior, with an emphasis on organizational and policy contexts. Topics include rational choice theory, biases and heuristics, framing effects, and overconfidence. Management fads, panics, and herd behavior are also discussed.
SOCIOL 138.prereq_text: (ANTHRO 10A and ANTHRO 10B and ANTHRO 10C) or (SOCIOL 10A and SOCIOL 10B and SOCIOL 10C) or (SOC SCI 10A and SOC SCI 10B and SOC SCI 10C) or (MATH 2A and MATH 2B and (STATS 7 or MGMT 7) or (STATS 120A and STATS 120B and STATS 120C) or (ECON 15 or ECON 15B or MATH 130B).
SOCIOL 138.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 141.title: Organizations
SOCIOL 141.description: How bureaucracies, formal organizations, and voluntary associations work, how/why they grow, and where they are going. History and structure of organizational rationality; dynamics of organized groups; behavior in organizations; limits of bureaucratization and attempts to overcome these limits through decentralization.
SOCIOL 141.restriction: Political Science majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 142.title: White-Collar Crime
SOCIOL 142.description: Examines criminal activity in business and corporate enterprise, organizations, and the professions. Theories regarding the causes and control of white-collar and corporate crime are covered as well as the numerous definitions of these terms.
SOCIOL 142.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology majors, and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 143.title: Social Networks and Social Support
SOCIOL 143.description: Examines the manner in which behaviors/attitudes of individuals are affected by their network ties to others. How are peoples' opportunities and well-being increased/decreased by their social networks? May include studies in mental/physical health, job seeking, separation and loss, and aging.
SOCIOL 143.restriction: Public Health majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 144.title: Politics, Power, and Society
SOCIOL 144.description: Includes an examination of the major theoretical approaches to political sociology, and the application of these ideas to the politics of advanced capitalist societies. Also considers stability and change in power structures.
SOCIOL 144.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 148.title: PrisonPandemic: Understanding Incarcerated People’s Pandemic Experiences
SOCIOL 148.description: Focuses on experiences shared by people incarcerated during the COVID-19 pandemic and helps students learn skills for interacting with archival materials and actively engaging with the sociohistorical context and modern critiques of the U.S. carceral system.
SOCIOL 148.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 149.title: Special Topics: Structures
SOCIOL 149.description: Studies in selected areas of structures. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
SOCIOL 149.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 150.title: Sociological Lens on Religion
SOCIOL 150.description: Examines the effects of religious beliefs, belonging, and institutions on social dynamics, including class, gender, and racial stratification, politics, and social movements. Additional topics: the sociological significance of conversion, commitment, and secularization/sacralization.
SOCIOL 150.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 151.title: Social Inequalities and Health
SOCIOL 151.description: Introduces ways in which social inequalities produce health disparities. Begins with general perspectives on social causation of health, and then considers how particular individual attributes (e.g., gender, SES, race/ethnicity, nativity) and social contexts (e.g., neighborhoods) can get “under the skin.”

SOCIOL 152W.title: Global Peace
SOCIOL 152W.description: Why do countries fight wars? Will world peace ever be possible? Focuses on social structures that might lead to global peace, with an emphasis on the role of culture and narrative in bringing peace locally, nationally, and globally.
SOCIOL 152W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCIOL 152W.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 154.title: Medical Sociology
SOCIOL 154.description: Current problems in U.S. health-care system and proposals for reform. Examines financial barriers to access; problem of patient dumping; underinsurance; prenatal and perinatal care; child services; preventative care and needs of the elderly; minorities; low-income people; undocumented.
SOCIOL 154.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 155B.title: Baseball and Society
SOCIOL 155B.description: An examination of baseball's role in American social life over the last 150 years. Issues of fraternal organizations, national development, capitalism, rationalization, race and ethnicity, gender, economic organization, labor relations, and politics are discussed.
SOCIOL 155B.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 155BW.title: Baseball and Society
SOCIOL 155BW.description: An examination of baseball's role in American social life over the last 150 years. Issues of fraternal organizations, national development, capitalism, rationalization, race and ethnicity, gender, economic organization, labor relations, and politics are discussed.
SOCIOL 155BW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCIOL 155BW.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 156.title: Deviance
SOCIOL 156.description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.
SOCIOL 156.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Social Ecology majors, Sociology majors, and Psychology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 157A.title: Sociology of Education
SOCIOL 157A.description: Focuses on education’s role in creating and redressing inequality, and in shaping how we understand our place in society. Education from cross-national and historical perspectives, and education as a vehicle for examining and solving social problems.

SOCIOL 157AW.title: Sociology of Education
SOCIOL 157AW.description: Focuses on education’s role in creating and redressing inequality, and in shaping how we understand our place in society. Education from cross-national and historical perspectives, and education as a vehicle for examining and solving social problems.

SOCIOL 157C.title: Comparing European and US Societies
SOCIOL 157C.description: Society, culture, institutions of U.S. and European countries. Fertility to football, guns to government, work to welfare, health to housework. Cross-national approaches for understanding the world and thinking critically about taken-for-granted practices. Policies the U.S. might borrow for social issues.

SOCIOL 158.title: Sociology of Mental Health
SOCIOL 158.description: Examines the social causes, consequences, and patterns of mental health and illness. Students learn a sociological perspective on mental health, mental illness or disorder, and medicine/health care, ranging from social definitions, roles, and interactions to societal stratification and international patterns.
SOCIOL 158.restriction: Public Health majors and Sociology majors only.

SOCIOL 158C.title: Money, Work, and Social Life
SOCIOL 158C.description: Sociological perspective on issues related to money and work. Consumption practices and lifestyles, jobs and organizations, issues of money in intimate relations, marriage, and households, illegal work, discrimination, economic globalization are discussed.
SOCIOL 158C.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 158CW.title: Money, Work, and Social Life
SOCIOL 158CW.description: Sociological perspective on issues related to money and work. Consumption practices and lifestyles, jobs and organizations, issues of money in intimate relations, marriage, and households, illegal work, discrimination, economic globalization are discussed.
SOCIOL 158CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCIOL 158CW.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 159.title: Special Topics: Social Institutions and Culture
SOCIOL 159.description: Studies in selected areas of social institutions and culture. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
SOCIOL 159.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 161.title: Sociology of Sex and Gender
SOCIOL 161.description: Explores complex processes contributing to social construction of gender and sexuality in the U.S. with focus on intersection of gender, race, ethnicity, sexuality, and class; evaluates how men and women are differentially constituted in family, education, work, politics, media, language.

SOCIOL 161W.title: Sociology of Sex and Gender
SOCIOL 161W.description: Explores complex processes contributing to social construction of gender and sexuality in the U.S. with focus on intersection of gender, race, ethnicity, sexuality, and class; evaluates how men and women are differentially constituted in family, education, work, politics, media, language.
SOCIOL 161W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOCIOL 163.title: Gender and Ethnicity: Chicana/Latina Feminisms in the US
SOCIOL 163.description: Focuses on the Latina Feminist Group and testimonios to examine the historical development of Chicana/Latinx feminist thought and practice. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship to survey the diversity of contemporary Chicana/Latinx feminisms through an intersectionality lens.

SOCIOL 163W.title: Credit, Debt, and Inequality
SOCIOL 163W.description: Examines the influence social background has on net worth. Engages sociological texts to understand the causes and consequences of credit and debt for inequality in the U.S.
SOCIOL 163W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCIOL 163W.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 164.title: Sociology of Aging
SOCIOL 164.description: Introduction to sociology of age, aging, and the aged. Problems posed by aging population. Life course transitions and how social organizations influence the life course. Addresses work, health, and family in later life.
SOCIOL 164.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 166.title: Immigration and Inequality
SOCIOL 166.description: Explores immigration, ethnicity, and inequality as interconnected social forces. International migration, propelled by global inequalities, plays a central role in the formation of multinational societies, shapes inter-group relations and patterns of ethnic inequality, and transforms the immigrants themselves.

SOCIOL 167A.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
SOCIOL 167A.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.
SOCIOL 167A.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 167AW.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
SOCIOL 167AW.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.
SOCIOL 167AW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCIOL 167AW.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 168W.title: Neighborhood Inequality and Residential Segregation
SOCIOL 168W.description: Examine how legacies of residential segregation continue to permeate areas of U.S. social life. Engage sociological texts alongside related current events that describe, explain, and predict the causes and consequences of residential segregation for enduring racial inequality in the U.S.
SOCIOL 168W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCIOL 168W.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 169.title: Special Topics in Age, Gender, Race, and Ethnicity
SOCIOL 169.description: Studies in selected areas of age, gender, race, and ethnicity. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
SOCIOL 169.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 170A.title: Vietnam War
SOCIOL 170A.description: Examines social structures and social changes in Vietnamese and U.S. societies through the study of the Vietnam War.

SOCIOL 170B.title: U.S. War on Terrorism
SOCIOL 170B.description: Analyzes the United States war on terrorism by focusing on terrorism, the U.S. wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and changes in police powers through the Patriot Act, as well as the political leadership which directs the war.

SOCIOL 171.title: Environment and Society
SOCIOL 171.description: Examines society's changing relationship to the natural world. Delineates different models of "nature" and then explores their institutional roots, the social responses they have generated, and their implications for social inequality.
SOCIOL 171.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 172A.title: Chicane/Latine Education
SOCIOL 172A.description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latine low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

SOCIOL 173.title: Social Inequality
SOCIOL 173.description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.
SOCIOL 173.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 173A.title: Sociology of Poverty
SOCIOL 173A.description: Examines the promise of social mobility and the roots of poverty in the United States with a focus on race, class, and gender.

SOCIOL 173W.title: Social Inequality
SOCIOL 173W.description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.
SOCIOL 173W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOCIOL 174.title: Protests, Movements, and Revolutions
SOCIOL 174.description: A survey of models of collective action drawn from sociology, economics, psychology, and political science. Focus on areas such as social movements, strikes, crowd psychology, cults, fads, fashions, public opinion, and symbolic and mythical elements in collective culture.
SOCIOL 174.prereq_text: SOCIOL 1 or POL SCI 11A or ECON 1.
SOCIOL 174.restriction: Political Science majors and Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 175B.title: China in the Global Age
SOCIOL 175B.description: Chinese society from 1949 to present. Social change in the context of political control and ideological considerations. Focus on the power structure, political decision processes, and ideological legitimation, and interplay with the Chinese community and its culture.

SOCIOL 176.title: International Divided Cities
SOCIOL 176.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

SOCIOL 177.title: Immigration and Social Policy
SOCIOL 177.description: Explains how people decide to migrate and how they are incorporated into a host society (both historically and currently), examines the effects of immigration on the U.S., analyzes how the framing of immigration shapes the discourse about the issue.
SOCIOL 177.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 177C.title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
SOCIOL 177C.description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

SOCIOL 178CW.title: Sociology of Human Rights
SOCIOL 178CW.description: Focuses on human rights – the idea that everyone has fundamental rights by virtue of being a human person – as a sociological phenomenon.
SOCIOL 178CW.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SOCIOL 178CW.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 179.title: Special Topics: Societies and Social Inequality
SOCIOL 179.description: Studies in selected areas of societies and social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
SOCIOL 179.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 180A.title: Sociology Majors Seminar
SOCIOL 180A.description: Students learn sociology by doing it. A modest-sized research project is planned and implemented by each student.

SOCIOL 180AW.title: Sociology Majors Seminar
SOCIOL 180AW.description: Students learn sociology by doing it. A modest-sized research project is planned and implemented by each student.
SOCIOL 180AW.prereq_text: SOCIOL 110. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOCIOL 188BW.title: Honors Research and Thesis
SOCIOL 188BW.description: Focuses on the design and implementation of individual research projects undertaken by senior Sociology majors. Writing projects consist of a proposal and paper on some empirical research.
SOCIOL 188BW.prereq_text: SOCIOL H188A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SOCIOL H188A.title: Honors Research and Thesis
SOCIOL H188A.description: Focuses on the design and implementation of individual research projects undertaken by senior Sociology majors. Writing projects consist of a proposal and paper on some empirical research.

SOCIOL 189.title: Special Topics: Honors Sequence
SOCIOL 189.description: Independent honors research with Social Sciences faculty.
SOCIOL 189.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 202A.title: Proseminar I in Sociology
SOCIOL 202A.description: Introduces first-year graduate students in Sociology to the current research interests of Sociology faculty, as well as to other aspects of graduate life at UCI and to the profession of sociology more generally.

SOCIOL 202B.title: Proseminar II in Sociology
SOCIOL 202B.description: Focus is on second-year research projects, design, development, data gathering, analysis, and preparing oral and written presentations of the results. Students learn analytic and writing skills, gain experience with research processes, and become socialized about professional standards, customs, and institutions.

SOCIOL 210A.title: Classical Social Theory
SOCIOL 210A.description: Examines the development of classical sociological theory through the writings of Karl Marx, Emile Durkheim, Max Weber, Georg Simmel, and George Herbert Mead.

SOCIOL 210B.title: Contemporary Social Theory
SOCIOL 210B.description: Familiarizes students with 20th-century developments in social thought that have influenced sociological research, suggesting "what is living and what is dead" in the "classics" and offering an overview of the main outlines of recent sociological theorizing.

SOCIOL 212.title: Network Theory
SOCIOL 212.description: An introduction to theoretical work in the field of social networks. Topics include baseline models, homphily, and propinquity, exchange and power, balance theory, diffusion and social influence, equivalence, and cohesion. Deductive use of theory to make novel predictions is emphasized.

SOCIOL 219.title: Special Topics: Theory
SOCIOL 219.description: Studies in selected areas of theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 220A.title: Research Design
SOCIOL 220A.description: Data collection, organization, and analysis in ethnographic or quasi-experimental settings, including interviewing, participant observations, behavior observations, and questionnaires. Research design issues include sampling, longitudinal research, and comparative research. Emphasis on the integration of qualitative and quantitative data.

SOCIOL 221A.title: Graduate Statistics I
SOCIOL 221A.description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.

SOCIOL 221B.title: Graduate Statistics II
SOCIOL 221B.description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.
SOCIOL 221B.prereq_text: SOCIOL 221A with a minimum grade of B-.

SOCIOL 221C.title: Graduate Statistics III
SOCIOL 221C.description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.
SOCIOL 221C.prereq_text: SOCIOL 221A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCIOL 221B with a minimum grade of B-.

SOCIOL 222A.title: Comparative and Historical Sociological Methods
SOCIOL 222A.description: Topics include the logic of comparative and historical analysis techniques and the examination of exemplar works in representative problem areas.

SOCIOL 223.title: Analyzing Qualitative Data
SOCIOL 223.description: Focuses on analyzing interview and field note data to write argument-driven academic papers.
SOCIOL 223.prereq_text: (SOCIOL 227A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCIOL 227B with a minimum grade of B-) or SOCIOL 224 with a minimum grade of B-. Required: At least 10-15 interview transcripts or field notes that correspond to at least 10-15 hours of ethnographic observation.
SOCIOL 223.restriction: Sociology majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

SOCIOL 224.title: Interview Methods
SOCIOL 224.description: Hands-on introduction to the use of interviews in social scientific research. Topics include when to use interviews and/or focus groups; how to design an interview-based study, how to conduct interviews, analyze interview data, and write up and publish interview-based results.

SOCIOL 226A.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
SOCIOL 226A.description: Introduces basic demographic methods used in social science and public health research. Topics include sources and limitations of demographic data; components of population growth; measures of nuptiality, fertility, mortality, and population mobility projection methods; and demographic models.

SOCIOL 227A.title: Seminar Ethnographic & Qualitative Field Methods
SOCIOL 227A.description: Comprehensive and critical discussion of the traditions of qualitative fieldwork; detailed examination of the collection, coding, analysis, and presentation of ethnographic/qualitative field data; and close mentoring of student projects culminating in an original research paper.

SOCIOL 227B.title: Seminar Ethnographic & Qualitative Field Methods
