SOCIOL 227B.description: Comprehensive and critical discussion of the traditions of qualitative fieldwork; detailed examination of the collection, coding, analysis, and presentation of ethnographic/qualitative field data; and close mentoring of student projects culminating in an original research paper.
SOCIOL 227B.prereq_text: SOCIOL 227A with a minimum grade of B-.

SOCIOL 229.title: Special Topics: Methods
SOCIOL 229.description: Studies in selected areas of methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 230A.title: Race and Ethnicity
SOCIOL 230A.description: An examination of central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity through a critical analysis and discussion of the principal theoretical perspectives and paradigms that have framed much of the scholarship in the area.

SOCIOL 231.title: Administrative Data Research
SOCIOL 231.description: Provides a supportive environment for students using administrative data in research projects across a wide range of fields, including, but not limited to, public health, education, economics, psychology, political science, and sociology.

SOCIOL 233A.title: Race and Ethnicity Perspectives
SOCIOL 233A.description: Discusses current research on race and ethnicity in the social sciences that incorporates critical race perspectives with an emphasis on explanations of social inequality.

SOCIOL 234.title: Ethnic America
SOCIOL 234.description: Examines critically the meaning and measurement of ethnicity, race, and nation in sociological theory and research. Theories of ethnicity are explored, along with empirical studies of the construction of ethnic and pan-ethnic identities in historical and contemporary contexts.

SOCIOL 235.title: Poverty and Development
SOCIOL 235.description: Examines competing conceptualizations, methods of measurement, and poverty alleviation strategies widely used in developing countries. Focuses on poverty conceptualized as economic deprivation, well-being, vulnerability, and social exclusion.

SOCIOL 237.title: Educational Inequality
SOCIOL 237.description: Focuses on macro-level explanations of inequality of schooling, particularly in the U.S. context. Explores traditional models, such as conflict, functionalism, status-attainment, cultural reproduction, and newer synthetic accounts. Emphasis on higher education access and the intersection of education and work.

SOCIOL 239.title: Special Topics: Social Inequality
SOCIOL 239.description: Studies in selected areas of social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 240A.title: Social Movements
SOCIOL 240A.description: A survey of the field of Social Movements, oriented around critical themes in the major theoretical traditions and contemporary exemplars.

SOCIOL 241A.title: Political Sociology
SOCIOL 241A.description: Begins with an examination of the three major orientations to the State (Pluralist, Elitist, and Class). Next considers current topics in political sociology including the Welfare State, the New Deal, political behavior, social movements, participation, and democracy.

SOCIOL 242.title: Sociology of Culture
SOCIOL 242.description: Major perspectives in the sociology of culture. Topics include the role of cultural dynamics in the reproduction of inequality, collective action, political and organizational decision making, emotional experience, and the social impacts of new technologies.

SOCIOL 249.title: Special Topics: Political Sociology and Social Movements
SOCIOL 249.description: Studies in selected areas of political sociology and social movements. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 252A.title: Global Urbanization
SOCIOL 252A.description: Examines the spread of cities worldwide in the 20th century. What are the political and economic causes of this process? What are the social-cultural, political, and economic effects? How is contemporary urbanization linked to global restructuring of other kinds?

SOCIOL 259.title: Special Topics: Global Studies and Comparative Development
SOCIOL 259.description: Studies in selected areas of global studies and comparative development. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 262A.title: Population
SOCIOL 262A.description: Introduces the interrelationships between population and social organization. Considers measurement and explanation of historical and contemporary trends in birth rates, death rates, migration, and marriage and divorce. Case material is drawn primarily from the U.S. and other industrialized nations.

SOCIOL 264.title: Immigrant America
SOCIOL 264.description: The study of the causes and consequences of international migration has become one of the most vital fields of sociological theory and research. Examines principal theoretical perspectives and empirical research on contemporary immigration flows and the processes of incorporation.

SOCIOL 265.title: DASA Research Design
SOCIOL 265.description: Data collection, organization, and analysis in population studies and demography. Research design issues include sampling, longitudinal research, and comparative research.

SOCIOL 268.title: Crimmigration
SOCIOL 268.description: Examines the criminalization of immigration, with an emphasis on U.S. enforcement procedures and outcomes. Analyzes the devolution of federal immigration law to local authorities, the rise in immigrant detention and deportation, and the militarization of the U.S.-Mexico border.

SOCIOL 269.title: Special Topics: Social Demography
SOCIOL 269.description: Studies in selected areas of social demography. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 279.title: Special Topics: Social Organizations and Institutions
SOCIOL 279.description: Studies in selected areas of social organizations and institutions. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SOCIOL 280.title: Analysis of Social Network Data
SOCIOL 280.description: Overview and application of methods for analyzing social network data. Topics include: data structures, visualization, graph theory, centrality, subgroups, positions, blockmodels, local properties, and statistical models. Social network analysis software is used to analyze a range of examples.

SOCIOL 281.title: Introduction to Social Networks
SOCIOL 281.description: Provides a broad overview of the history, concepts, and applications of social networks. Students have the opportunity to delve deeply into applications of the network approach in their individual areas of interest.

SOCIOL 289.title: Special Topics
SOCIOL 289.description: Studies in selected areas of Social Sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SPANISH 1A.title: Fundamentals of Spanish
SPANISH 1A.description: First quarter of Fundaments of Spanish that helps students develop basic reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.

SPANISH 1B.title: Fundamentals of Spanish
SPANISH 1B.description: Second quarter of Fundaments of Spanish that helps students develop basic reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.
SPANISH 1B.prereq_text: SPANISH 1A with a minimum grade of C-. Placement into SPANISH 1B is also accepted.

SPANISH 1C.title: Fundamentals of Spanish
SPANISH 1C.description: Third quarter of Fundaments of Spanish that helps students develop basic reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.
SPANISH 1C.prereq_text: SPANISH 1B with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S1AB with a minimum grade of B. Placement into SPANISH 1C is also accepted.

SPANISH S1AB.title: Fundamentals of Spanish
SPANISH S1AB.description: First half of first-year Spanish in an intensified form. Communicative approach with emphasis on conversational skills.

SPANISH S1BC.title: Fundamentals of Spanish
SPANISH S1BC.description: Second half of first-year Spanish in an intensified form. Communicative approach with emphasis on conversational skills.
SPANISH S1BC.prereq_text: SPANISH S1AB with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH 1A with a minimum grade of B or SPANISH 1B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into SPANISH 1B or SPANISH 1C is also accepted.

SPANISH 2A.title: Intermediate Spanish
SPANISH 2A.description: First quarter of Intermediate Spanish that helps students further develop their reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish and a cultural understanding of the Spanish-speaking world. Delivered in a hybrid format.
SPANISH 2A.prereq_text: SPANISH 1C with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S1BC with a minimum grade of C-. Placement into SPANISH 2A is also accepted.
SPANISH 2A.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SPANISH 2B.title: Intermediate Spanish
SPANISH 2B.description: Second quarter of Intermediate Spanish that helps students further develop their reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish and a cultural understanding of the Spanish-speaking world. Delivered in a hybrid format.
SPANISH 2B.prereq_text: SPANISH 2A with a minimum grade of C-. Placement into SPANISH 2B is also accepted.
SPANISH 2B.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SPANISH 2C.title: Intermediate Spanish
SPANISH 2C.description: Third quarter of Intermediate Spanish that helps students further develop their reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish and a cultural understanding of the Spanish-speaking world. Delivered in a hybrid format.
SPANISH 2C.prereq_text: SPANISH 2AB with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH 2B with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S2AB with a minimum grade of B. Placement into SPANISH 2C is also accepted.
SPANISH 2C.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SPANISH S2AB.title: Intermediate Spanish
SPANISH S2AB.description: First half of second-year Spanish in an intensified form. Conversation, reading, and composition skills are developed using texts of literary and social interest. Emphasis on grammar review.
SPANISH S2AB.prereq_text: SPANISH 1C with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into SPANISH 2A is also accepted.

SPANISH S2BC.title: Intermediate Spanish
SPANISH S2BC.description: Second half of second-year Spanish in an intensified form. Conversation, reading, and composition skills are developed using texts of literary and social interest. Emphasis on grammar review.
SPANISH S2BC.prereq_text: SPANISH 2B with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH S2AB with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH 2A with a minimum grade of B. Placement into SPANISH 2B or SPANISH 2C is also accepted.

SPANISH 3.title: US Latino Communities
SPANISH 3.description: Focuses on intermediate to advanced grammar and composition. Emphasis is placed on key elements of grammar, which constitutes about 70 percent of the curriculum, and composition writing, which constitutes the remaining 30 percent.
SPANISH 3.prereq_text: SPANISH 2C with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or AP Spanish Language Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 3 is also accepted.

SPANISH 3H.title: Heritage Spanish: Latinidades en California
SPANISH 3H.description: Designed for students who grew up speaking Spanish in their homes and who need additional practice writing in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.
SPANISH 3H.prereq_text: AP Spanish Language Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 3H.

SPANISH 50.title: Topics in Latin America, U.S. Latino, and Iberian Cultures
SPANISH 50.description: Introduction to the culture of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds (Europe, Latin America, U.S., Africa). May focus on any time period. Taught in English.

SPANISH 60E.title: Mexico and Central America: A Survey
SPANISH 60E.description: Panoramic view of Mexico and Central America examining key texts throughout history. Shows the richness of the culture, and an appraisal of various forms of representation, including images, chronicles, novels, essays, poems, and a film. Taught in English.

SPANISH 61.title: The Culture of the Visual Image in Latin America
SPANISH 61.description: A survey of visual forms of expression which have endured through more than five centuries of pre-colonial, colonial, and independent Latin America. Forms to be treated in the class include painting, monuments, sculpture, urban planning, graffiti, comics, and photography.

SPANISH 62.title: Latinx, Multilingualism, and Social Justice
SPANISH 62.description: Explores the role of multilingualism (Spanish, indigenous languages, Latino English) in Latinx social justice movements in the United States with an emphasis on California. Course is taught in English.

SPANISH 97.title: Fundamentals of Spanish (with Emphasis on Reading)
SPANISH 97.description: Designed for students interested in acquiring a solid reading knowledge of Spanish, and to facilitate the understanding and translating of Spanish texts covering a variety of disciplines. Does not fulfill any undergraduate foreign language requirement. Taught in English.
SPANISH 97.prereq_text: Does not serve as prerequisite for any higher-level Spanish courses.

SPANISH 101A.title: Introduction to Iberian Literature and Culture
SPANISH 101A.description: Introduction to the major authors and movements of Iberian literature and culture from the Middle Ages to the present.
SPANISH 101A.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 101B.title: Introductory Studies to Latin American Literature and Culture
SPANISH 101B.description: A historical overview of Latin American literature and culture mainly focused on canonical texts. Topics include colonialism and postcolonialism, the nation, indigenismo, gender, and literary movements. Also introduces literary analysis, research methods, and cultural critique.
SPANISH 101B.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 105.title: Spanish Communication
SPANISH 105.description: Designed to help students develop Spanish oral skills by exposing them to different verbal Spanish language registers. Special emphasis placed on abilities essential to professional or academic careers. Intended for Spanish majors as an important component of their overall education.
SPANISH 105.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 107.title: Advanced Spanish Grammar
SPANISH 107.description: Designed for students who have demonstrated a substantial level of proficiency in their studies of the Spanish language. Takes thorough approach to advanced grammatical problems, in order to assist students in their mastery of the elements of the Spanish language.
SPANISH 107.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 108.title: Topics in Spanish for the Professions
SPANISH 108.description: Taught in Spanish to promote linguistic competencies, intercultural awareness, and understanding of local Latino communities’ needs. Provides resources to carry out professional tasks and build meaningful community-based relationships in the health, legal, and business fields.
SPANISH 108.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 110A.title: Topics in Peninsular Literature and Cultures
SPANISH 110A.description: Topics in Peninsular literature and cultures.
SPANISH 110A.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 110C.title: U.S. Latino Literature and Cultures
SPANISH 110C.description: Focuses on aspects of literature, art, cultural production, and history of the multifaceted Latino cultures that have developed within the United States. Focuses on one group, such as Caribbean Americans, Chicanos, Central Americans, or a comparative perspective of several groups.

SPANISH 113A.title: Spanish Phonetics
SPANISH 113A.description: Introduction to fundamental notions of Spanish phonetics. Particular attention paid to problems of pronunciation that arise in native and non-native speakers of Spanish due to interference between Spanish and English. Phonology (the system that underlies phonetics) and Spanish dialectology included.
SPANISH 113A.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 113B.title: Introduction to Spanish Linguistics
SPANISH 113B.description: Introduces students to the scientific study of the Spanish language with a focus on its sound system, word components, word order as well as second language acquisition and language variation. Class is delivered in a hybrid format.
SPANISH 113B.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 119.title: Textual Analysis and Interpretation
SPANISH 119.description: Focus on analysis and interpretation of literary texts. Emphasis on narrative, poetry, theater/performance, and visual media. Introduces students to major currents in theoretical thought, such as cultural studies, postmodernism, and others. Oral presentations and short essays required. Taught in Spanish.
SPANISH 119.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 121.title: Topics in Golden Age Literature and Culture
SPANISH 121.description: Golden Age Literature in Spain, including the Renaissance and Baroque periods. Works of poetry, narrative, and theater. Historical and cultural background.
SPANISH 121.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 123.title: Topics in 20th and 21st Century Spanish Literature and Culture
SPANISH 123.description: 20th century Spanish authors. Works of poetry, narrative, or theater. Historical context of the period and principles of literary theory.
SPANISH 123.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 130C.title: Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture of the 20th Century
SPANISH 130C.description: Topics in Latin American literature and culture of the 20th century.
SPANISH 130C.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 140.title: Topics in Chicano Literature and Culture
SPANISH 140.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter. Taught in English.

SPANISH 150.title: Topics in Literature in Translation
SPANISH 150.description: Study of texts by modern and contemporary Peninsular, Latin American, and/or U.S. Latino writers in translation. Taught in English. Not applicable toward Spanish major or minor requirements.

SPANISH 160.title: Topics in Luso-Hispanic Film Studies
SPANISH 160.description: Study of Peninsular, Latin-American, and/or U.S. Latino film. Taught in English or Spanish.
SPANISH 160.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 185.title: Topics in Peninsular Literature and Culture
SPANISH 185.description: Selection of representative topics in Spanish and/or Portuguese literature and culture.
SPANISH 185.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 186.title: Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture
SPANISH 186.description: Selection of representative topics in the history of Latin American literature and culture.
SPANISH 186.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 187.title: Selected Topics in Spanish Linguistics
SPANISH 187.prereq_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.

SPANISH 190.title: Colloquium
SPANISH 190.description: Specialized, discussion-based course dealing primarily with a research topic that reflects the instructor's current intellectual interests. Required oral presentation(s) and final research paper. Limited to 15 students.

SPANISH 220.title: Topics in Twentieth Century
SPANISH 220.description: Topics in twentieth-century Spanish literature and culture.

SPANISH 239A.title: Topics in Literary Theory I
SPANISH 239A.description: Traces the development of Western literary critical principles from Aristotle to the twentieth century through selected readings of key figures in intellectual history (Aristotle, St. Augustine, Descartes, Kant, Hegel, Marx, Nietzsche, William James, Freud).

SPANISH 239C.title: Special Topics in Theory
SPANISH 239C.description: Focus on issues related to critical theory, theory of literature, cultural criticism and visual arts as they pertain specifically to Latin America, Spain, Portugal, and Brazil. Topics vary. Examples: Latin American cultural studies; theory, film, and media in post-war Spain.

SPANISH 260A.title: Professionalization Seminar
SPANISH 260A.description: Addresses the transition from graduate student to professional with a Ph.D. in Spanish. Covers formative stages in the progress of graduate students towards their degrees, as well as help with the preparation for a successful professional career.

SPANISH 260B.title: Professionalization Seminar
SPANISH 260B.description: Addresses the transition from graduate student to professional with a Ph.D. in Spanish. Covers formative stages in the progress of graduate students towards their degrees, as well as helps with the preparation for a successful professional career.

SPANISH 260C.title: Professionalization Seminar
SPANISH 260C.description: Addresses the transition from graduate student to professional with a Ph.D. in Spanish. Covers formative stages in the progress of graduate students towards their degrees, as well as helps with the preparation for a successful professional career.

SPANISH 265.title: World Language Teaching Methodologies: Theory and Practice
SPANISH 265.description: Graduate seminar introducing theory and world language teaching, with a focus on Spanish, grounding instructional techniques in Instructed Second Language Acquisition. Emphasizes reflective, evidence-based language teaching pedagogy, communicative and task-based language teaching, and professional development.

SPANISH 265A.title: Spanish Teaching Methodology I
SPANISH 265A.description: Required for graduate students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese who will teach in the Spanish Language Program. Prepares graduate students to develop effective teaching practices that promote learning Spanish as a second language.

SPANISH 265B.title: Spanish Teaching Methodology II
SPANISH 265B.description: Required for graduate students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese who will teach in the Spanish Language Program. Prepares graduate students to develop effective teaching practices that promote learning Spanish as a second language.

SPANISH 270.title: Creative Writing Workshop in Spanish/English
SPANISH 270.description: Discussion of theory and practice of creative writing. Focus on critical analysis of participant's work in progress. Texts may be written in Spanish and/or English and may be written in poetry or prose format.

SPPS 40.title: Social Policy and Public Service
SPPS 40.description: An introduction to the basic theories and principles of public policy. Students examine various influences on the development of public policy and the principle actors in the process, and learn to identify tools and techniques employed in policy making.

SPPS 70A.title: Race and Ethnicity
SPPS 70A.description: Focuses on racial and ethnic relations in the United States and compares them with those found in other societies. Analyzes the conditions that favor either cooperation and integration or rivalry, tension, and conflict. Appraises strategies for reducing and resolving conflicts.

SPPS 102.title: Critical Investigations into Humanitarianism in Africa
SPPS 102.description: Explores the complex phenomenon of aid to Africa (emergency and development aid), and the representational, cultural, historical, and other reasons why some participants and many observers critique it. Students occasionally engage with peers and faculty in African institutions.

SPPS H190A.title: Honors Research Workshop
SPPS H190A.description: Student develops a 10–15-page prospectus of research for the honors thesis which includes: the research question, literature review, methods of investigation, and bibliography. Student selects a faculty mentor who will supervise thesis research and writing in winter and spring.
SPPS H190A.restriction: Social Science majors and Social Policy and Public Service majors only.

SPPS H190B.title: Honors Thesis Research
SPPS H190B.description: The student initiates and completes data collection for the honors thesis. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
SPPS H190B.prereq_text: SOC SCI H190A or SPPS H190A.

SPPS H190C.title: Honors Thesis
SPPS H190C.description: The student completes, with the approval of the faculty mentor, an honors thesis containing: statement of the problem, literature review, research hypotheses, methods of investigation, results, discussion, and bibliography.
SPPS H190C.prereq_text: SOC SCI H190B or SPPS H190B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

SPPS 193A.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
SPPS 193A.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
SPPS 193A.prereq_text: SOC SCI 70C or SOCIOL 63. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
SPPS 193A.restriction: Social Policy and Public Service majors only.

SPPS 193B.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
SPPS 193B.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.

SPPS 193CW.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
SPPS 193CW.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and under-served communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.

STATS 5.title: Seminar in Data Science
STATS 5.description: An introduction to the field of Data Science; intended for entering freshman and transfers.
STATS 5.restriction: Information and Computer Science majors only.

STATS 6.title: Introduction to Data Science
STATS 6.description: Introduces the full data cycle. Topics include data collection and retrieval, data cleaning, exploratory analysis and visualization, introduction to statistical modeling, inference, and communicating findings. Applications include real data from a wide-range of fields with emphasis on understanding reproducible practices.

STATS 7.title: Basic Statistics
STATS 7.description: Introduces basic inferential statistics including confidence intervals and hypothesis testing on means and proportions, t-distribution, Chi Square, regression and correlation. F-distribution and nonparametric statistics included if time permits.

and.not: AP STATISTICS score of 3 or greater

STATS 7.prereq_text: NO STATS 8 AND NO SOCECOL 13 AND NO MGMT 7 AND NO AP STATISTICS score of 3 or greater AND NO PUBHLTH 7A

STATS 8.title: Introduction to Biological Statistics
STATS 8.description: Introductory statistical techniques used to collect and analyze experimental and observational data from health sciences and biology. Includes exploration of data, probability and sampling distributions, basic statistical inference for means and proportions, linear regression, and analysis of variance.
STATS 8.prereq_text: NO STATS 7 AND NO SOCECOL 13 AND NO MGMT 7 AND NO PUBHLTH 7A

STATS 67.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Computer Science
STATS 67.description: Introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics with discussion of applications to computer science.
STATS 67.prereq_text: MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4.
STATS 67.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. STATS 67 may not be taken for credit concurrently with or after STATS 120B.

STATS 68.title: Statistical Computing and Exploratory Data Analysis
STATS 68.description: Introduces key concepts in statistical computing. Techniques such as exploratory data analysis, data visualization, simulation, and optimization methods, are presented in the context of data analysis within a statistical computing environment.
STATS 68.prereq_text: (STATS 7 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3) and (I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI H32).

STATS 110.title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis I
STATS 110.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from experiments and surveys. Methods covered include two-sample procedures, analysis of variance, simple and multiple linear regression.
STATS 110.prereq_text: STATS 7 or STATS 8 or STATS 67 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3 or (STATS 120A and STATS 120B and STATS 120C).
STATS 110.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students only.

STATS 111.title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis II
STATS 111.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys or experiments. Emphasizes application and understanding of methods for categorical data including contingency tables, logistic and Poisson regression, loglinear models.

STATS 112.title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis III
STATS 112.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing longitudinal data from experiments and cohort studies. Topics covered include survival methods for censored time-to-event data, linear mixed models, non-linear mixed effects models, and generalized estimating equations.

STATS 115.title: Introduction to Bayesian Data Analysis
STATS 115.description: Basic Bayesian concepts and methods with emphasis on data analysis. Prior and posterior probability distributions, modeling, and Markov Chain Monte Carlo techniques are presented in the context of data analysis within a statistical computing environment.

STATS 120A.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics I
STATS 120A.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Axiomatic definition of probability, random variables, probability distributions, expectation.
STATS 120A.prereq_text: (MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 4 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 4 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3) and (MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and (MATH 2D or MATH 4).
STATS 120A.restriction: Data Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics majors have second consideration for enrollment.

STATS 120B.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics II
STATS 120B.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Point and interval estimation, frequentist hypothesis testing, Bayesian inference, limit theorems, simulation, and the bootstrap.
STATS 120B.restriction: Data Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics majors have second consideration.

STATS 120C.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics III
STATS 120C.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Power and sample size calculation, Neyman-Pearson lemma, (generalized) likelihood ratio test, one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA, simple linear regression and its statistical inference and diagnosis, and multiple linear regression.
STATS 120C.restriction: Data Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics majors have second consideration.

STATS 140.title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
STATS 140.description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, and factor analysis.

STATS 170A.title: Project in Data Science I
STATS 170A.description: Problem definition and analysis, data representation, algorithm selection, solution validation, and results presentation. Students do team projects and lectures cover analysis alternatives, project planning, and data analysis issues. First quarter emphasizes approach selection, project planning, and experimental design.
STATS 170A.prereq_text: STATS 68 and SWE 43 and COMPSCI 122A and COMPSCI 178 and I&C SCI 46 and STATS 111.
STATS 170A.restriction: Seniors and Data Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

STATS 170B.title: Project in Data Science II
STATS 170B.description: Problem definition and analysis, data representation, algorithm selection, solution validation, and results presentation. Students do team projects and lectures cover analysis alternatives, project planning, and data analysis issues. Second quarter emphasizes project execution and analysis, and presentation of results.
STATS 170B.prereq_text: STATS 170A and STATS 112. In Progress (IP) grade for STATS 170A is also accepted.
STATS 170B.restriction: Seniors and Data Science majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

STATS H198.title: Honors Research
STATS H198.description: Directed independent research in Statistics for ICS honors and Campuswide Honors Collegium students.

STATS 199.title: Individual Study
STATS 199.description: Individual research or investigations under the direction of an individual faculty member.

STATS 200A.title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory
STATS 200A.description: Basics of probability theory, random variables and basic transformations, univariate distributions—discrete and continuous, multivariate distributions.
STATS 200A.prereq_text: STATS 120C with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 200B.title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory
STATS 200B.description: Random samples, transformations, limit laws, normal distribution theory, introduction to stochastic processes, data reduction, point estimation (maximum likelihood).
STATS 200B.prereq_text: STATS 200A with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 200C.title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory
STATS 200C.description: Interval estimation, hypothesis testing, decision theory and Bayesian inference, basic linear model theory.
STATS 200C.prereq_text: STATS 200B with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 201.title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis I
STATS 201.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from experiments and surveys. Methods covered include two-sample procedures, analysis of variance, simple and multiple linear regression.
STATS 201.restriction: STATS 201 cannot be taken for credit after taking STATS 210.

STATS 202.title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis II
STATS 202.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys or experiments. Emphasizes application and understanding of methods for categorical data including contingency tables, logistic and Poisson regression, loglinear models.
STATS 202.prereq_text: STATS 201 with a minimum grade of B- or STATS 210 with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 203.title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis III
STATS 203.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing longitudinal data from experiments and cohort studies. Topics covered include survival methods for censored time-to-event data, linear mixed models, non-linear mixed effects models, and generalized estimating equations.
STATS 203.prereq_text: STATS 202 with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 205.title: Introduction to Bayesian Data Analysis
STATS 205.description: Basic Bayesian concepts and methods with emphasis on data analysis. Special emphasis on specification of prior distributions. Development for one-two samples and on to binary, Poisson and linear regression. Analyses performed using free OpenBugs software.

STATS 205P.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
STATS 205P.description: Covers basic Bayesian concepts and methods with emphasis on data analysis. Special emphasis on specification of prior distributions. Development of methods and theory for one and two samples, binary, Poisson, and linear regression.
STATS 205P.prereq_text: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 210P with a minimum grade of B.

STATS 210.title: Statistical Methods I: Linear Models
STATS 210.description: Statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys and experiments. Topics include randomization and model-based inference, two-sample methods, analysis of variance, linear regression and model diagnostics.
STATS 210.prereq_text: Knowledge of basic statistics, calculus, linear algebra.

STATS 210A.title: Statistical Methods I: Linear Models
STATS 210A.description: Statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys and experiments. Topics include randomization and model-based inference, two-sample methods, analysis of variance, linear regression, and model diagnostics.
STATS 210A.prereq_text: Knowledge of basic statistics (at the level of STATS 7), calculus, and linear algebra.

STATS 210B.title: Statistical Methods II: Categorical Data
STATS 210B.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing discrete and non-normal outcomes. Emphasizes the development and application of methods for categorical data, including contingency tables, logistic and Poisson regression, loglinear models.
STATS 210B.prereq_text: STATS 210 with a minimum grade of B-. May not be taken for graduate credit by Ph.D. students in Statistics.

STATS 210C.title: Statistical Methods III: Longitudinal Data
STATS 210C.description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing longitudinal outcomes. Emphasizes the development and application of regression methods for correlated and censored outcomes. Methods for continuous and discrete correlated outcomes, as well as censored outcomes, are covered.
STATS 210C.prereq_text: STATS 210B with a minimum grade of B-. May not be taken for graduate credit by Ph.D. students in Statistics.

STATS 211.title: Statistical Methods II: Generalized Linear Models
STATS 211.description: Development of the theory and application of generalized linear models. Topics include likelihood estimation and asymptotic distributional theory for exponential families, quasi-likelihood and mixed model development. Emphasizes methodological development and application to real scientific problems.
STATS 211.prereq_text: STATS 210 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 212.title: Statistical Methods III: Methods for Correlated Data
STATS 212.description: Development and application of statistical methods for analyzing corrected data. Topics covered include repeated measures ANOVA, linear mixed models, non-linear mixed effects models, and generalized estimating equations. Emphasizes both theoretical development and application of the presented methodology.
STATS 212.prereq_text: STATS 211 with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 220A.title: Advanced Probability and Statistics Topics
STATS 220A.description: Advanced topics in probability and statistical inference including measure theoretic probability, large sample theory, decision theory, resampling and Monte Carlo methods, nonparametric methods.
STATS 220A.prereq_text: STATS 200C with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 220B.title: Advanced Probability and Statistics Topics
STATS 220B.description: Advanced topics in probability and statistical inference, including measure theoretic probability, large sample theory, decision theory, resampling and Monte Carlo methods, nonparametric methods.
STATS 220B.prereq_text: STATS 220A with a minimum grade of B- and MATH 140B.

STATS 225.title: Bayesian Statistical Analysis
STATS 225.description: Introduction to the Bayesian approach to statistical inference. Topics include univariate and multivariate models, choice of prior distributions, hierarchical models, computation including Markov chain Monte Carlo, model checking, and model selection.
STATS 225.prereq_text: STATS 205 with a minimum grade of B- and STATS 230 with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 230.title: Statistical Computing Methods
STATS 230.description: Numerical computations and algorithms with applications in statistics. Topics include optimization methods including the EM algorithm, random number generation and simulation, Markov chain simulation tools, and numerical integration.
STATS 230.prereq_text: Two quarters of upper-division or graduate training in probability and statistics.

STATS 240.title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
STATS 240.description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, and factor analysis.

STATS 240P.title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
STATS 240P.description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and dimension reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, factor analysis.
STATS 240P.prereq_text: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B- and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 245P.title: Time Series Analysis
STATS 245P.description: Statistical models for time series. Topics include linear models for trends; stationary time-series; non-stationary time series; forecasting and Kalman filtering; time-series smoothing; seasonal models; ARCH, GARCH and stochastic volatility models; multivariate time series; vector autoregressive models; spectral analysis; case studies.
STATS 245P.prereq_text: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B- and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 262P.title: Theory and Practice of Sample Survey
STATS 262P.description: Basic techniques and statistical methods for designing surveys and analyzing collected survey data. Topics include simple random sampling, ratio and regression estimates, stratified sampling, cluster sampling, sampling with unequal probabilities, multistage sampling, and methods to handle nonresponse.
STATS 262P.prereq_text: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B.

STATS 265.title: Causal Inference
STATS 265.description: Various approaches to causal inference focusing on the Rubin causal model and propensity-score methods. Topics include randomized experiments, observational studies, non-compliance, ignorable and non-ignorable treatment assignment, instrumental variables, and sensitivity analysis. Applications from economics, politics, education, and medicine.
STATS 265.prereq_text: STATS 200C with a minimum grade of B- and STATS 210 with a minimum grade of B-.

STATS 270.title: Stochastic Processes
STATS 270.description: Introduction to the theory and application of stochastic processes. Topics include Markov chains, continuous-time Markov processes, Poisson processes, and Brownian motion. Applications include Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and financial modeling (for example, option pricing).

STATS 270P.title: Stochastic Processes
STATS 270P.description: Introduction to the theory and application of stochastic processes. Topics include Poisson processes, Markov chains, continuous-time Markov processes, and Brownian motion. Applications include Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and financial modeling (e.g. option pricing).
STATS 270P.prereq_text: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B.

STATS 275.title: Statistical Consulting
STATS 275.description: Training in collaborative research and practical application of statistics. Emphasis on effective communication as it relates to identifying scientific objectives, formulating a statistical analysis plan, choice of statistical methods, and interpretation of results and their limitations to non-statisticians.
STATS 275.prereq_text: STATS 203 with a minimum grade of B or STATS 212 with a minimum grade of B or STATS 210C with a minimum grade of B.

STATS 280.title: Seminar in Statistics
STATS 280.description: Periodic seminar series covering topics of current research in statistics and its application.

STATS 281A.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics I
STATS 281A.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Axiomatic definition of probability, random variables, probability distributions, expectation.

STATS 281B.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics II
STATS 281B.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Point estimation, interval estimating, and testing hypotheses, Bayesian approaches to inference.

STATS 281C.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics III
STATS 281C.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Contingency table analysis, linear regression, analysis of variance, model checking.

STATS 295.title: Special Topics in Statistics
STATS 295.description: Studies in selected areas of statistics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

STATS 298.title: Thesis Supervision
STATS 298.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.

STATS 299.title: Individual Study
STATS 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

SWE 43.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
SWE 43.description: Concepts, methods, and current practice of software engineering. Large-scale software production, software life cycle models, principles, and techniques for each stage of development.
SWE 43.prereq_text: I&C SCI 32 or I&C SCI H32 or I&C SCI 32A.
SWE 43.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 113.title: Requirements Analysis and Engineering
SWE 113.description: Equips students to develop techniques of software-intensive systems through successful requirements analysis techniques and requirements engineering. Students learn systematic process of developing requirements through cooperative problem analysis, representation, and validation.
SWE 113.prereq_text: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C and SWE 43 with a minimum grade of C.
SWE 113.restriction: Informatics majors, Software Engineering majors, Business Information Management majors, and Game Design and Interactive Media majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Information and Computer Sciences students only. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

SWE 115.title: Software Testing, Analysis, and Quality Assurance
SWE 115.description: Preparation for developing high-quality software through successful veriﬁcation and validation techniques. Fundamental principles of software testing, implementing software testing practices, ensuring the thoroughness of testing to gain conﬁdence in the correctness of the software.
SWE 115.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C) and SWE 43 with a minimum grade of C.
SWE 115.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 117.title: Project in Software System Design
SWE 117.description: Specification, design, construction, testing, and documentation of a complete software system. Special emphasis on the need for and use of teamwork, careful planning, and other techniques for working with large systems.
SWE 117.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 119.title: Engineering Artificial Intelligence Software
SWE 119.description: Design, deploy, and manage software incorporating AI components in real-world production environments. Topics include types of models, in-house vs. third-party models, retrieval augmented generation, fine-tuning, prompt engineering, model testing, and reliability.
SWE 119.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C) and (STATS 7 or STATS 67).
SWE 119.restriction: Informatics majors and Software Engineering majors have the first consideration for enrollment. School of Information and Computer Sciences students only. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.

SWE 121.title: Software Design: Applications
SWE 121.description: Introduction to application design: designing the overall functionality of a software application. Topics include general design theory, software design theory, and software architecture. Includes practice in designing and case studies of existing designs.
SWE 121.prereq_text: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C or GDIM 33 with a minimum grade of C.
SWE 121.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 122.title: Software Design: Structure and Implementation
SWE 122.description: Introduction to implementation design: designing the internals of a software application. Topics include design aesthetics, design implementation, design recovery, design patterns, and component reuse. Includes practice in designing and case studies of existing designs.
SWE 122.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 124.title: Internet Applications Engineering
SWE 124.description: Concepts in Internet applications engineering with emphasis on the Web. Peer-to-Peer and Interoperability. Topics include HTTP and REST, Remote Procedure/Method Calls, Web Services, data representations, content distribution networks, identity management, relevant W3C/IETF standards, and relevant new large-scale computing styles.
SWE 124.restriction: Computer Science and Engineering majors and School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 141.title: Information Retrieval
SWE 141.description: An introduction to information retrieval including indexing, retrieval, classifying, and clustering text and multimedia documents.
SWE 141.prereq_text: (I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C) and (STATS 7 or STATS 67 or MGMT 7 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3).
SWE 141.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 211.title: Software Engineering
SWE 211.description: Study of the concepts, methods, and tools for the analysis, design, construction, and measurement of complex software-intensive systems. Underlying principles emphasized. State-of-the-art software engineering and promising research areas covered, including project management.

SWE 212.title: Analysis of Programming Languages
SWE 212.description: Concepts in modern programming languages, their interaction, and the relationship between programming languages and methods for large-scale, extensible software development. Empirical analysis of programming language usage.

SWE 214.title: Program Analysis
SWE 214.description: Covers principles and concepts of automated program analysis. Topics include program representations; intra-procedural data-flow analysis; call-graph construction; pointer analysis; alias analysis; inter-procedural analysis; inter-procedural finite distributive subset problems; inter-procedural distributive environment problems; symbolic execution; and program-analysis applications.
SWE 214.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment.

SWE 215.title: Dynamic Analysis, Testing, and Debugging
SWE 215.description: Studies techniques for developing confidence in software from traditional testing techniques to state-of-the-art dynamic analysis and debugging techniques. Emphasis is on assisting developer comprehension of runtime behavior.

SWE 221.title: Software Architecture
SWE 221.description: Study of the concepts, representation techniques, development methods, and tools for architecture-centric software engineering. Topics include domain-specific software architectures, architectural styles, architecture description languages, software connectors, and dynamism in architectures.

SWE 225.title: Information Retrieval, Filtering, and Classification
SWE 225.description: Algorithms for the storage, retrieval, filtering, and classification of textual and multimedia data. The vector space model, Boolean and probabilistic queries, and relevance feedback. Latent semantic indexing; collaborative filtering; and relationship to machine learning methods.
SWE 225.prereq_text: COMPSCI 161 and COMPSCI 171 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G).

SWE 233.title: Intelligent User Interfaces
SWE 233.description: Explores example software systems and their underlying concepts that leverage computing to empower and augment human individuals in their activities. Topics span the fields of user interface design, human-computer interaction, software engineering, and cognitive computing.

SWE 234.title: Human Aspects of Software Engineering
SWE 234.description: Selected topics about the cooperative and human aspects of software engineering from the perspective that software engineering is inherently an endeavor involving human stakeholders. Topics may include but are not limited to collaboration, trust, creativity, well-being, productivity, and software tools.
SWE 234.restriction: School of Information and Computer Sciences students have the first consideration for enrollment. No Master of Software Engineering students.

SWE 240P.title: Data Structures
SWE 240P.description: Exploration of well-known data structures to represent computational problems. Topics include linked lists, graphs, binary trees, stacks, queues, heaps, and hash tables, among others.

SWE 241P.title: Algorithms
SWE 241P.description: Exploration of strategies to tackle computational problems whose solutions include well-known algorithms. Topics include sorting, searching, and indexing, among others.

SWE 242P.title: Network Programming
SWE 242P.description: Exploration of networking principles and concepts for the development of distributed software. Topics include programming against well-known network protocols, ports and sockets, and network APIs.

SWE 243P.title: Database Programming
SWE 243P.description: Exploration of software development with substantial reliance on a database for storage and retrieval of data. Topics include relational databases, structured query language, relational database management systems, APIs and libraries for database programming, among others.

SWE 244P.title: Concurrent Programming
SWE 244P.description: Exploration of concepts and mechanisms for the development of concurrent software. Topics include threads, locks, race conditions, and deadlocks, among others.

SWE 245P.title: GUI Programming
SWE 245P.description: Exploration of interactive software with substantial graphical user interface elements. Topics include libraries and frameworks for GUI programming, layout design and alternatives, event-driven programming, among others.

SWE 246P.title: Mobile Programming
SWE 246P.description: Exploration of contemporary libraries and frameworks for construction of mobile applications. Topics include emulators, mobile development standards and patterns, energy consumption issues, screen layout, among others.

SWE 247P.title: Applied Information Retrieval
SWE 247P.description: Exploration of principles and concepts for textual information retrieval. Topics include tokenization, inverted indexes, scored retrieval, and precision and recall.

SWE 248P.title: Neural Network Programming
SWE 248P.description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and processes for training and using deep neural networks for classification problems. Topics include tensors and tensor operations, gradient-based optimization, feature engineering and learning, and workflow of learning systems.

SWE 249P.title: Applied Data Analytics
SWE 249P.description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and processes used in supervised and unsupervised learning for classification and clustering, from a software engineering perspective. Topics include K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, K-Means, and model assessment.

SWE 250P.title: Web Programming
SWE 250P.description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and popular frameworks for developing full-stack web applications. Students develop simple applications using multiple development stacks, and deploy them on the cloud.

SWE 251P.title: Introduction to Large Language Models
SWE 251P.description: Introduces LLMs for software engineering, covering transformers, prompt/context engineering, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Students gain hands-on experience interacting with models using APIs and open-source models while laying the foundation for advanced study in SWE 270P.

SWE 261P.title: Software Testing and Debugging
SWE 261P.description: Designed to teach students how to ensure high-quality software by means of testing, debugging, and other quality assurance activities. Students learn a combination of both theoretical and practical skills, including hands-on experience with modern tools and approaches.

SWE 262P.title: Advanced Programming Techniques
SWE 262P.description: Teaches students the various ways software can be decomposed and then how to put the parts back together. Students are exposed to a variety of different programming styles and composition mechanisms.
SWE 262P.restriction: Master Of Software Engineering majors and Master of Software Engineering only.

SWE 263P.title: User Experience and Interaction
SWE 263P.description: Provides an introduction to the basic principles of human-computer interaction (HCI) and the pragmatic aspects of usability engineering. Topics include the fundamentals of interaction, user experience, design for usability, and evaluation of products for their usability.

SWE 264P.title: Distributed Software Architecture
SWE 264P.description: Study of software system architectures and architectural styles for large-scale distributed applications, and contemporary technologies and standards for their construction. Topics include client-server, peer-to-peer, publish-subscribe, REST, cloud computing, content distribution networks, scalability, latency, caching, and security, among others.

SWE 265P.title: Reverse Engineering and Modeling
SWE 265P.description: Introduces theories, concepts, representations, techniques, and case studies in understanding large-scale, complex software systems. Topics include static and dynamic modeling notations, manual and (semi-)automated reverse engineering techniques, APIs, patterns, and styles. A significant, hands-on project is included.

SWE 266P.title: Software Security and Dependability
SWE 266P.description: Principles and concepts for the design and construction of secure software. Topics include common types of software security vulnerabilities, methods for detecting vulnerabilities, design and process methodologies to improve security of software, and techniques for assessing security properties of software.

SWE 267P.title: Cloud and Security Foundations
SWE 267P.description: Cloud and security foundations provides students fundamental design and security principles about cloud computing and information security. Topics include cloud concepts and architectures; cloud security; data protection and privacy compliance and governance; and security by design, amongst other topics.

SWE 270P.title: Engineering Artificial Intelligence Software
SWE 270P.description: Design, deploy, and manage software incorporating AI components in real-world production environments. Topics include learning about different types of models, in-house vs. third-party models, retrieval augmented generation, fine-tuning, prompt engineering, model testing, and reliability.
SWE 270P.restriction: Master Of Software Engineering majors and Master of Software Engineering only.

SWE 275P.title: Curricular Practical Training
SWE 275P.description: Mandatory internship in which students individually work at an outside organization to gain experience with the challenges involved in the practice of software engineering.

SWE 276P.title: Capstone Project in Software Engineering
SWE 276P.description: Quarter-long software-intensive project focusing on the design and implementation of a novel software system. Students are expected to bring to bear the concepts acquired during the program.

SWE 277P.title: Capstone Project in Software Engineering II
SWE 277P.description: Focuses on designing and implementing a novel software system. Students work on their project while emphasizing communication skills in business and technical settings. Students practice presenting project ideas, developing portfolios.
SWE 277P.restriction: Master Of Software Engineering majors and Master of Software Engineering only.

SWE 290.title: Research Seminar
SWE 290.description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.

SWE 290P.title: Advisement
SWE 290P.description: Mandatory weekly meetings with a faculty advisor.

SWE 295.title: Special Topics in Software Engineering
SWE 295.description: Studies in selected areas of software engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

SWE 298.title: Thesis Supervision
SWE 298.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.

SWE 299.title: Individual Study
SWE 299.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

SWE 299P.title: Independent Study
SWE 299P.description: Supervised individual practical project in Software Engineering.

UCDC 170.title: Washington DC Internship
UCDC 170.description: Supervised internship (20-40 hours per week) in Washington DC government, nonprofit, or private institution consistent with student's interest.
UCDC 170.prereq_text: Selected for Washington DC Center Program.

UCDC 180.title: Washington-Themed Seminar
UCDC 180.description: UCDC core course (multiple topics offered each quarter). Enhances students' experiential learning and imparts knowledge and skills to help them transition into public service/private sector positions. One core course per quarter mandatory for all participants in Washington DC Center Program.
UCDC 180.prereq_text: Must be selected for Washington DC Center Program.

UCDC 190.title: Washington DC Elective
UCDC 190.description: Studies in selected areas related to the UC Washington, DC Center Program (UCDC). All courses taught in Washington, DC. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
UCDC 190.prereq_text: Selected for Washington DC Center Program.

UNI AFF 1A.title: Student Participation
UNI AFF 1A.description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.
UNI AFF 1A.prereq_text: Project must be approved by a Student Affairs Department head and the instructor.

UNI AFF 1B.title: Student Participation
UNI AFF 1B.description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.

UNI AFF 1C.title: Student Participation
UNI AFF 1C.description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.

UNI STU 1.title: Freshman Experience
UNI STU 1.description: An introduction to the freshman experience provides an overview of the University's aims and resources and exploration of developmental theories and skills necessary for academic success. Attention is also paid to questions of personal development and major choice. Materials Fee

UNI STU 3.title: Mini-Seminars
UNI STU 3.description: Designed primarily for freshmen as introduction to scholarly inquiry. Each section is taught by a faculty member from one of the academic disciplines and presents interesting and challenging topics representing the instructor's interest. Students participate in discussions, presentations, and projects.

UNI STU 7.title: UTeach: Student-Taught Seminar
UNI STU 7.description: Student-taught seminar courses on selected topics. Topics vary each year according to the interest of the students teaching the classes.

UNI STU 10.title: Introduction to Civic and Community Engagement and Community Research
UNI STU 10.description: Provides a foundation for understanding the role of public scholarship, civic engagement, and social action, and the relationship between service learning and engaged citizenship. Introduces key theoretical and research methodologies on the traditions and innovations of civic and community engagement.

UNI STU 18.title: Student Leadership Institute for Climate Resilience
UNI STU 18.description: An overview of some of the major challenges and opportunities we face in building community climate resilience, as well as tools for action.

UNI STU 19.title: Introduction to Free Speech and Academic Freedom
UNI STU 19.description: An introduction to the principles of free speech and academic freedom with a focus on the public university context. Attention is paid to the historical evolution of the central concepts as well as real-world case studies.

UNI STU 20A.title: Intercollegiate Athletics Seminar
UNI STU 20A.description: Designed to provide first-year student-athletes a thorough overview of university life and to help ease their transition into higher education. Ensures that students are successful throughout their time at UC Irvine by developing

UNI STU 20D.title: Intercollegiate Athletics Seminar
UNI STU 20D.description: Designed to provide first-year student-athletes a thorough overview of university life and to help ease their transition into higher education. Ensures that students are successful throughout their time at UC Irvine.

UNI STU 21A.title: Critical Thinking, Ethics, and Just Communities I
UNI STU 21A.description: Part of a three-course series; focuses on expanding critical thinking, developing personal ethics, understanding diversity, equity, and inclusion in on-campus residential communities.

UNI STU 21B.title: Critical Thinking, Ethics, and Just Communities II
UNI STU 21B.description: Part of a three-course series; focuses on expanding critical thinking, developing personal ethics, understanding diversity, equity, and inclusion in on-campus residential communities.

UNI STU 21C.title: Thinking, Ethics, and Just Communities III
UNI STU 21C.description: Part of a three-course series; focuses on expanding critical thinking, developing personal ethics, understanding diversity, equity, and inclusion in on-campus residential communities.

UNI STU 22.title: Introduction to Startups
UNI STU 22.description: Entrepreneurship intro course that merges academic rigor with real-world business insights, offering skill-based training in ideation, networking, leadership, team building, finance, and startup founding.

UNI STU 23A.title: Introduction to Research
UNI STU 23A.description: Assists incoming first years (freshmen and transfer students) in their understanding of research opportunities at UCI and how to get involved with faculty-mentored labs and creative projects; covers the necessary knowledge, skills, and resources regarding how to conduct research.

UNI STU 23B.title: Thrive in Research
UNI STU 23B.description: Second of a two-part series designed to assist incoming first years (freshmen and transfer students) in their understanding of research and research opportunities at UCI. Students learn how to get involved with faculty-mentored labs and creative projects.

UNI STU H30A.title: Critical Analysis of Health Science Literature
UNI STU H30A.description: Focuses on evaluation of scientific literature. Aspects of scientific inquiry include scientific method, scientific research design, statistical analysis, and publication processes. Addresses why scientific inquiry cannot be separated from sociocultural influences and concerns. Examples drawn from research on health-related issues.

UNI STU H30B.title: Environmental Issues Affecting the Sustainability of Societies I
UNI STU H30B.description: Focuses on several environmental challenges facing the world today, and explores the problem, possible solutions, and their scientific, technical, and social constraints. Models for systems, their assumptions, predictive uncertainty, and interpretation, play a large role.
UNI STU H30B.prereq_text: UNI STU H30A with a minimum grade of C.

UNI STU H30C.title: Environmental Issues Affecting the Sustainability of Societies II
UNI STU H30C.description: Focuses on how we can use Earth’s resources, e.g., food and water, in a more sustainable way, exploring their scientific, technical, and social constraints.
UNI STU H30C.prereq_text: UNI STU H30B with a minimum grade of C.

UNI STU H30D.title: Social Science Perspectives on the Sustainability of Societies
UNI STU H30D.description: Introduces the perspectives of social science using examples from different countries to explore how social issues regarding sustainability are influenced by a society’s changing economic and political institutions, and how economic, political, and other social choices affect their sustainability.
UNI STU H30D.prereq_text: EARTHSS H30C with a minimum grade of C.

UNI STU H30E.title: Cities: Focal Point for Sustainability Problems and Solutions I
UNI STU H30E.description: Explores the nature of cities, focusing on the challenges facing cities today, their possible solutions, and the technical and social constraints on those solutions.

UNI STU H30F.title: Cities: Focal Point for Sustainability Problems and Solutions II
UNI STU H30F.description: Explores the nature of cities, focusing on the challenges facing cities today, their possible solutions, and the technical and social constraints on those solutions.

UNI STU 43.title: Topics in Illuminations
UNI STU 43.description: This course connects students to Illuminations, the Chancellor’s Arts and Culture Initiative. Students will attend five Illuminations-sponsored events and engage in brief preparatory and reflective activities in response to these events.

UNI STU 45.title: Graduate School Opportunities and Preparation
UNI STU 45.description: Explores the opportunities associated with graduate school by considering a wide range of disciplines and career paths. Reviews professional and academic paths in graduate school and the ways to prepare for a chosen path.

UNI STU H80.title: Neurodivergent
UNI STU H80.description: Examines the evolution of the diagnosis of autism through history. Deep inquiry of the neuroscience, etiology, and genetics of neurodivergent individuals as well as a review of the validity of the varied treatments will inform critical thinking.

UNI STU 83.title: Pathways to University Success
UNI STU 83.description: Helps first-year students transition to UC Irvine and promotes a successful University experience. Students learn about academic resources and programs that support acclimation to the campus and enhance academic development through lectures, discussions, and a range of co-curricular activities.

UNI STU 84.title: Bridges to University Success
UNI STU 84.description: Helps first-year students transition to UC Irvine and promotes a successful University experience. Students learn about academic resources/programs that support acclimation to the campus and enhance academic development through lectures, writing laboratories, discussions, and a range of co-curricular activities.

UNI STU 85A.title: Leading from Within
UNI STU 85A.description: Students examine characteristics and behaviors of effective leaders. Study the history and theoretical framework for understanding effective leadership. In addition, examine their own leadership strengths and weaknesses and become familiar with the theory behind and use of comprehensive self-assessment tools.

UNI STU 85B.title: Leading Others
UNI STU 85B.description: Students examine best practices within a team environment. They learn goal setting, diagnosing performance problems, designing solutions, and recognizing relevant differences in culture, priorities, and values within a team through lectures, writing, discussions, and practical activities.

UNI STU 85C.title: Leading Change
UNI STU 85C.description: Focused on a global viewpoint, students learn the theoretical framework behind innovation and change management. Develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges, design strategies to bring an expansive vision into fruition, and learn to communicate a vision and strategies.

UNI STU 86.title: Leadership and Aikido
UNI STU 86.description: Covers practical applications of theories of leadership, communication, and self-efficacy through lessons in Aikido, personal reflection, and current articles. Focuses on skills that support academic and professional success.

UNI STU 87.title: Navigating Your UCI Journey: Foundations for Success
UNI STU 87.description: Provides all incoming students with a core experience focused on building a solid foundation for academic success. Recognizes students' different backgrounds and is designed around modules that support academic success.

UNI STU 93.title: Strategies for Success
UNI STU 93.description: Develops students' study skills for general education requirement courses through instruction, small group activities, and application assignments. Topics include goal setting, note taking, examination preparation, memory and concentration, and learning best practices.

UNI STU 100.title: Doing Research in the Community
UNI STU 100.description: Critically reimagines the research endeavor and its participants/outcomes. Grapples with methods, values, and relationships involved in research. Explores alternative conceptions of research; focus is community-based. Students work in teams on real-world community research projects with faculty mentors and community partners.

UNI STU H101.title: Special Topics in Campuswide Honors Education
UNI STU H101.description: Topics in honors education vary depending on the interest of the instructor.
UNI STU H101.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement is recommended.

UNI STU 110.title: Philanthropy in the Community
UNI STU 110.description: Introduces the role of community engagement, social action and philanthropy. Examines theories and practices of philanthropy, and strategies for social change. Involves hand-on engagement with philanthropy in the form of students making decisions about the distribution of a real fund.

UNI STU 170.title: Advanced Internship in Undergraduate Education
UNI STU 170.description: Advanced interns have a year's internship experience and return to contribute to Undergraduate Education programs in a leadership position. Students work three-five hours per week in a DUE office to coordinate or lead less-experienced interns and/or events.
UNI STU 170.prereq_text: UNI AFF 1A and UNI AFF 1B and UNI AFF 1C.

UNI STU 174.title: Peer Tutoring Methods and Applications
UNI STU 174.description: Overview and readings in research-based principles of learning for all undergraduate tutors. Tutors receive instruction, practice, and evaluation in effective communication strategies, learning development, cultural competencies, and 1:1 facilitation. Taken concurrently when serving as a tutor in any department.

UNI STU 175.title: Methods and Application in Small Group Instruction
UNI STU 175.description: Explores various theories and methods of learning and development and their practical application in small group settings. Peer tutors receive instruction in the design, implementation, and evaluation of an effective learning environment for undergraduate students.
UNI STU 175.restriction: Learning and Academic Resource Center employed tutors only.

UNI STU 176.title: Pedagogy of Small Group Facilitation - LAs
UNI STU 176.description: Overview and readings in evidence-based instruction for undergraduate learning assistants. LAs receive instruction, training, and feedback on effective small group facilitation and active learning. To be taken while serving as a learning assistant in a course.

UNI STU H176A.title: Campuswide Honors Thesis Seminar
UNI STU H176A.description: Supports the honors thesis research activities of Campuswide Honors Collegium students. Students set research goals, discuss, and develop their research interests.

UNI STU H176C.title: Campuswide Honors Thesis Seminar
UNI STU H176C.description: Supports the honors thesis research activities of Campuswide Honors Collegium students. Students work with each other to improve both written and spoken presentations of their results.

UNI STU 177.title: Mentored Learning Assistant Field Work
UNI STU 177.description: Oversight of trained learning assistants by the course instructor, including training in the discipline and responsibilities associated with supporting active group work. Instructor mentors LAs in how assisting small groups supports their career goals.
