UNI STU 190.title: Teaching Seminar: Theory and Practice
UNI STU 190.description: For students selected to be discussion leaders for University Studies 1. Models of teaching, developmental theory applied to college freshmen, curriculum development. Practice of teaching techniques and group management skills.

UNI STU 192.title: Group Project for Discussion Leaders
UNI STU 192.description: For discussion leaders for University Studies 1. Weekly discussion group training for leading effective groups in addition to evaluations of weekly discussion sections and completion of a special project on issues of freshman development. Materials Fee

UNI STU 193.title: Internship
UNI STU 193.description: Enables students from all majors to receive credit for an approved internship on or off-campus. Internship sites may be public or private, for profit or non-profit agencies, organizations, companies, or corporations offering paid or unpaid learning experiences.

UNI STU 196.title: Directed Studies in Undergraduate Education
UNI STU 196.description: Students do directed study (research, readings, etc.) on a topic related to Undergraduate Education under the supervision of one of the faculty who serve as Deans or Faculty Directors in the Division of Undergraduate Education.

UNI STU 197A.title: UTeach Special Study
UNI STU 197A.description: Students accepted to teach a UTeach course in spring quarter enroll in Special or Independent Study with their faculty mentor during the preceding fall quarter to develop their detailed course syllabus.

UNI STU 197B.title: UTeach: Teaching Theory and Practice
UNI STU 197B.description: Students accepted to teach a UTeach course in spring quarter enroll during the winter to develop their teaching skills in preparation for teaching the following quarter.

UNI STU 197C.title: UTeach: Teaching Practicum
UNI STU 197C.description: Students selected to teach in the UTeach Program teach their courses and meet weekly in a seminar to continue to develop and enhance their teaching skills.

UNI STU 197D.title: Study Abroad Experiential Learning
UNI STU 197D.description: Study abroad on an approved program. Complete critical reflection (written paper, blog, etc.) submitted no later than the end of the quarter following the completion of the study abroad program. Enroll while studying abroad or the quarter immediately following return.

UNI STU 197E.title: Reflections While Abroad
UNI STU 197E.description: For students while they are studying abroad; maximizing learning outcomes by critically reflecting on learning experiences while abroad. Topics include cultural observations, professional issues, cultural competence, etc. Participants are located in different countries around the world.

UNI STU 197F.title: Internship Plus
UNI STU 197F.description: Provides training and development of career readiness competencies in parallel with a student’s internship experience. Internship sites may be public or private, for profit or non-profit agencies, organizations, companies, or corporations offering paid or unpaid learning experiences.

UNI STU 231.title: NIH Fellowship Writing Skills
UNI STU 231.description: Designed for graduate students in biomedical science departments who are preparing to write applications for NRSA (F30/F31) fellowships from the NIH. It involves a mixture of lectures, panel discussions, and peer review of writing samples.

UNI STU 297.title: California Community College Internship
UNI STU 297.description: The California Community College Internship offers graduate students the opportunity to learn about faculty life, governance, and teaching at local community colleges. Structures fieldwork for students to participate in and reflect on the educational mission of community colleges.
UNI STU 297.restriction: MFA or Doctoral students who have advanced to candidacy.

UNI STU 390A.title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
UNI STU 390A.description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.

UNI STU 390B.title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
UNI STU 390B.description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.
UNI STU 390B.prereq_text: UNI STU 390A with a minimum grade of B-.

UNI STU 390C.title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
UNI STU 390C.description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.
UNI STU 390C.prereq_text: UNI STU 390B with a minimum grade of B-.

UNI STU 390X.title: Developing Teaching Excellence
UNI STU 390X.description: An introduction to evidence-based instructional design and methods, specifically for higher education courses. Students practice, observe, and design instruction based on pedagogical literature. Meets most of the requirements for the Certificate in Teaching Excellence Program.

UPPP 4.title: Introduction to Urban Studies
UPPP 4.description: Introduces the substantive areas, concepts, and tools in the field of urban studies. Acquaints students with physical, environmental, social, economic, and political dimensions of cities. Examines the challenges facing cities, including poverty, sustainability, development, globalization, and others.
UPPP 4.restriction: Urban Studies majors, Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors, and School of Social Ecology students have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 5.title: Introduction to Urban Planning and Policy
UPPP 5.description: Introduces students to the basic issues in urban planning and public policy.

UPPP 8.title: Introduction to Environmental Analysis and Design
UPPP 8.description: Overview of general concepts, theoretical principles, and analytical techniques for investigating environmental systems. Integrates tools from natural and social sciences to analyze contemporary environmental challenges such as pollution, resource acquisition, facility and ecosystem design, impact assessments, formulation of environmental policy.

prereq.not: AP ENVIRONMENTAL SCI score of 4 or greater

UPPP 8.prereq_text: NO AP ENVIRONMENTAL SCI score of 4 or greater

UPPP 40.title: Cities, Communities, and Urban Problems
UPPP 40.description: Overview of theoretical, substantive, and policy issues in urban sociology. History of urbanization, the school of human ecology, and recent trends regarding urbanism. Time is devoted to understanding the causes and possible solutions to urban problems.

UPPP 41.title: Introduction to Labor Studies
UPPP 41.description: Introduces students to various aspects of labor and employment relations in the U.S., including the perspective of working people and their collective labor organizations. Analyzes changes in employment trends and the changing nature of work.

UPPP 42.title: The Green New Deal
UPPP 42.description: Introduces students to the basic motivations and history behind policies collectively known as “The Green New Deal.” Students learn about large-scale models for equitable growth and sustainability and the politics of implementing them in the U.S. and internationally.

UPPP 50.title: The Power of Music and Social Change
UPPP 50.description: Introduces students to the emerging science of music and its remarkable power in shaping our lives, from individual flourishing and social change to higher education, careers, and connections with nature.

UPPP 100.title: Special Topics in Urban Studies
UPPP 100.description: Course content varies with interest of the instructor.
UPPP 100.prereq_text: ( URBAN STUDIES MAJORS ONLY OR SOCIAL ECOLOGY MAJORS ONLY )
UPPP 100.restriction: Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 101.title: History of Cities
UPPP 101.description: Surveys the global and historical co-evolution of cities and social institutions, including religion, the economy, governance, the arts, technology, and family life.

UPPP 102.title: Urban Inequality
UPPP 102.description: Examines structural inequality and the influence that urbanization has in affecting race, ethnic, and class relations. Explores how race/ethnicity, class, urban space, housing, economic development, public education, and land policy intersect in cities, both historically and today.
UPPP 102.prereq_text: ( URBAN STUDIES MAJORS ONLY OR SOCIAL ECOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR PUB HEALTH POLICY MAJORS ONLY )
UPPP 102.restriction: Public Health Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 103.title: Comparative Approaches to Urban Regions
UPPP 103.description: An introduction to comparative urbanization in developing countries. Introduces students to the geography, history, and theories of urbanization, and then reviews urban planning, public policy, and governance.
UPPP 103.prereq_text: ( URBAN STUDIES MAJORS ONLY OR SOCIAL ECOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR PUB HEALTH POLICY MAJORS ONLY )
UPPP 103.restriction: Public Health Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors only.

UPPP 104.title: Race in the City: Past, Present, and Future
UPPP 104.description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.
UPPP 104.prereq_text: NO CHC/LAT 162 AND NO SOC SCI 163A

UPPP 107.title: Urban and Regional Planning
UPPP 107.description: Important substantive areas, concepts, tools in the field of urban and regional planning. Topics include: forces that have historically guided and are currently guiding U.S. urbanization; land use, economic development, housing and community development, environmental planning; legal, environmental, governmental contexts.
UPPP 107.restriction: Earth System Science majors, Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 108.title: Cities and Transportation
UPPP 108.description: The relationship between urban areas and transportation systems. Economic analysis of cities, transportation and urban form, highway congestion, environmental impacts of transportation, public transit, land use and transportation, and political influences on transportation planning.
UPPP 108.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 109.title: Housing and Urban Development Policy
UPPP 109.description: Surveys public policy issues and develops analytic techniques in the areas of housing and urban development. Examines a range of policy topics including housing assistance to low- and moderate-income families, housing finance system, incentives for economic development, and neighborhood preservation.
UPPP 109.prereq_text: Recommended: Previous course work in economics.
UPPP 109.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 110.title: Urban Economic Development Policy
UPPP 110.description: Theoretical and practical perspectives on local economic development policy. Integrates economic, planning, and political perspectives. Overview of economic role of cities and metropolitan areas. Specific development issues include: link between taxes, regulation, job growth; redevelopment planning; evaluation economic development policy.
UPPP 110.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 111.title: Climate Solutions
UPPP 111.description: Introduction to climate change science and impacts on the health of people and the planet with a focus on the multi-dimensional aspects of solutions to the climate crisis.

UPPP 112.title: Foundations of Community Health
UPPP 112.description: A social ecological framework for understanding community health is presented. Measures of individual and community health are compared, and the influence of personal and environmental factors on individual, group, and population health is examined. Community health promotion strategies are discussed.
UPPP 112.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Public Health Policy majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 113.title: Poverty and Change in Developing Countries
UPPP 113.description: Focuses on poverty in developing countries. Analyzes the magnitude and changing nature of poverty in the global south. Critically examines poverty conceptualized in terms of economic deprivation, well-being, and social exclusion.
UPPP 113.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 114W.title: Advanced Research Methods
UPPP 114W.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
UPPP 114W.prereq_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

UPPP 115.title: Global Poverty and Inequality in the 21st Century
UPPP 115.description: Explores a multidisciplinary understanding of poverty and inequality in the 21st century and assesses impact of education, health, technology, and other interventions. Course offered online only.

UPPP 116.title: Cities and Climate Change
UPPP 116.description: Students examine the intersection between climate change and social justice while developing skills necessary for local climate action, such as inventorying emissions, assessing vulnerability, and evaluating the costs, benefits, and equity implications of mitigation and adaptation strategies.

UPPP 117.title: Environmental Justice
UPPP 117.description: Engages students to critically analyze and evaluate environmental problems, environmental responses, and planning and policy debates regarding "environmental justice" - essentially the race, class, and equity implications of environmental problems and policies.
UPPP 117.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 118.title: Gentrification
UPPP 118.description: Gentrification is a complex process that changes the makeup of neighborhoods and fuels political and policy conflicts. Students are provided with tools to understand the process and conceive of policies to ensure more inclusive and equitable cities.

UPPP 119.title: Human Trafficking: Prevention, Protection, Prosecution, Policy, and Partnership
UPPP 119.description: Equips students with a deeper understanding of human trafficking, and explores their role in ending the fastest-growing criminal industry worldwide: the exploitation of human beings through the use of force, fraud, or coercion.
UPPP 119.restriction: School of Social Ecology students have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 120.title: Introduction to GIS for Planning and Policy
UPPP 120.description: Provides hands-on experience creating, visualizing, and interpreting spatial data, with a focus on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications for urban planning and public policy.
UPPP 120.restriction: Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors, Environmental Science and Policy majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 125.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
UPPP 125.description: Provides hands-on experience using geoprocessing to analyze spatial data and using maps to visualize and communicate findings, with a focus on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications for urban planning and public policy.
UPPP 125.prereq_text: UPPP 120 with a minimum grade of C-.
UPPP 125.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 127.title: Spatial Analysis Project
UPPP 127.description: As the capstone in the Geographic Information Systems (GIS) degree specialization, students are guided through the process of applying their GIS skills to designing and conducting an original spatial research project, focusing on research design and research methods.
UPPP 127.prereq_text: UPPP 120 with a minimum grade of C- and UPPP 125 with a minimum grade of C-.
UPPP 127.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors only.

UPPP 129.title: American Public Policy
UPPP 129.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.
UPPP 129.prereq_text: NO PUBHLTH 132 AND NO SOC SCI 152C AND NO POL SCI 121G

UPPP 131.title: Environmental Sustainability I
UPPP 131.description: Provides an introduction to sustainability from different points of view; historical, scientific, political, ethical, and economic.
UPPP 131.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 132.title: Energy Justice and Just Transitions
UPPP 132.description: Investigates how sustainability can be implemented in a variety of contexts including water, energy, non-renewable resources, biodiversity, and urban policy, and also how it could be measured.
UPPP 132.restriction: Earth System Science majors, Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 133.title: Environmental Law and Policy
UPPP 133.description: Environmental law as a combination of traditional legal principles and newly created statutes, rules, and decisions applied to environmental protection. Investigates roles of courts, legislature, executive branch and administrative agencies, and private citizens attempting to regulate environmental quality.
UPPP 133.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society majors, Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors only.

UPPP 135.title: Urban Data Science
UPPP 135.description: Introduces computational tools, data literacy, spatial analysis methods, and introductory statistics for understanding cities and metropolitan regions.

UPPP 140.title: Global Metropolis
UPPP 140.description: Explores global perspectives on urban phenomena like poverty and housing, postcolonial and global-South urbanization, citizenship, race, violence, inequality, and our shared climate future.

UPPP 142.title: Environmental Hazards in an Urbanizing World
UPPP 142.description: Development patterns, including urbanization, can contribute to environmental hazard severity. Humans can plan, mitigate, and prepare to reduce costly hazard losses. Students learn about environmental hazards and human response to these threats.

UPPP 145.title: Environmental Governance
UPPP 145.description: How should the environment be managed and who should be responsible? What is effective environmental management, and for whom? These questions are answered by exploring traditional and emerging theoretical frameworks and applying them to real world environmental challenges.
UPPP 145.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 146.title: Principles of Economics for Planning and Policy
UPPP 146.description: Provides an introduction into economics for planning and policy students.
UPPP 146.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 155.title: Urban Design Principles
UPPP 155.description: Introduction to principles of urban design and its applications. Study of contemporary and traditional theories of urban design formulated to improve physical characteristics of built environment to facilitate an enhanced quality of life. A variety of case studies are discussed.
UPPP 155.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 166.title: Urban Politics and Policy
UPPP 166.description: Examines why and how urban policies are enacted and carried out in contemporary U.S. cities and regions. Topics include evolution and organization of city governments and policymaking over the past century; who directs public policy and controls how cities develop.

UPPP 167.title: Public Policy and Governance
UPPP 167.description: Exposes students to best practices that assure effective planning and implementation of policies and programs in government, business, and nonprofit sectors. Includes guest lecturers who are proven leaders in four principal institutions of community: business, education, government, and non-profit.
UPPP 167.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 170.title: Health Policy
UPPP 170.description: Considers social and economic aspects of health and disease in the United States. What are the proper roles of the individual, community, and government in improving health and health care? International comparisons will be made wherever possible.
UPPP 170.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy majors, Public Health Policy majors, Public Health Sciences majors, Social Ecology majors, Urban Studies majors, and Urban Studies, Planning, and Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 172.title: Latino Metropolis
UPPP 172.description: Explores the processes of Latino urbanization in the United States and the spatialization of Latino identities, particularly in the context of Southern California with selected comparisons drawing from other cities.

UPPP 178.title: International Divided Cities
UPPP 178.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.
UPPP 178.prereq_text: NO POL SCI 157B AND NO SOCIOL 176

UPPP 190.title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
UPPP 190.description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.
UPPP 190.restriction: Psychological Science majors, Criminology, Law and Society majors, Psychology majors, Social Ecology majors, and Urban Studies majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 202.title: History and Theory of Urban Planning
UPPP 202.description: Introduces students to the historical bases, fundamental perspectives, and current challenges of urban and regional planning. Critical historical episodes and personalities in planning and their influences on contemporary planning practice and thought are explored.
UPPP 202.restriction: Master of Urban and Regional Planning only.

UPPP 203.title: Theoretical Foundations of Planning
UPPP 203.description: Intellectual excursion into central themes in policy and planning, including philosophy of the market, institutionalization of space, hypostatizations of policy, constructions of communities, logics of spatial analysis. Objective is engagement of the professional in thoughtful reflections on practice and institutions.

UPPP 204.title: Plan Development and Communication
UPPP 204.description: Graphic representation and communication of physical place characteristics, design and physical planning ideas, and concepts using a variety of graphic techniques of free hand drawing, sketching, orthographic representations, scale drawings, 3D representations, maps, photo-documentation, and various media.
UPPP 204.restriction: Urban and Regional Planning majors only.

UPPP 206.title: Microeconomic Analysis for Urban Planning
UPPP 206.description: Provides students with a working knowledge of basic microeconomic concepts. Emphasizes applications related to urban planning and policy analysis. Topics covered include demand analysis, firm behavior, market structure, public goods, externalities, and the role of economics in land markets.

UPPP 207.title: Land-Use Law
UPPP 207.description: Investigates legal and institutional frameworks for development control. Review of constitutional issues implicated in land-use regulation. Traces development control historically and analyzes contemporary approaches to land-use control which reflect environmental and economic development concerns.

UPPP 209.title: Qualitative Research Methods: Overview
UPPP 209.description: Introduction to fundamentals of “qualitative” research and non-positivistic inquiry. Formulation of research questions, selection of method, data collection techniques, and analysis (briefly). Overview of selected methods from ethnography, naturalistic field research, phenomenology, ethnoarchaeology, critical approaches, and others.

UPPP 210.title: Practice Experience
UPPP 210.description: Provides Master of Urban and Regional Planning students an opportunity to link classroom knowledge with real planning situations through a 10-week unpaid practice experience.
UPPP 210.restriction: Urban and Regional Planning majors only.

UPPP 212.title: Transportation Planning and Policy
UPPP 212.description: Introduces current topics in transportation planning. Includes an analysis of the economic role of transportation in urban areas, land-use impacts of transportation projects, traffic congestion, air quality, alternatives to the automobile, and other transportation topics.

UPPP 213.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
UPPP 213.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

UPPP 214.title: Quantitative Analysis for Planners
UPPP 214.description: Introduces students to the basic statistical concepts used to address issues of public concern. Prepares students to perform, interpret, and evaluate quantitative data analyses commonly used in professional studies.

UPPP 215.title: Analytical Methods for Planning
UPPP 215.description: Emphasizes the development of analytical techniques proven useful in the fields of management and administration. Topics include multiple regression, cost-benefit analysis and discounting, decision trees, and other techniques useful for the purposes of community analysis and planning.

UPPP 216.title: Statistics and Methods for Public Policy
UPPP 216.description: Introductory course with focus on gaining a sound understanding of what constitutes credible evidence in support of policy arguments and management decisions.

UPPP 219.title: Information and Public Policy
UPPP 219.description: Evaluates strengths and weaknesses of qualitative and quantitative methods and the data used in making public policy claims. Looks at the bases of certain widely accepted measures of poverty, growth, environmental quality, and the like.
UPPP 219.restriction: Public Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 220.title: Qualitative Methods: Fieldwork and Data Collection
UPPP 220.description: Covers fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research. Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview. Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.

UPPP 221.title: Public Policy
UPPP 221.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst. Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.
UPPP 221.prereq_text: NO CRM/LAW C255 AND NO POL SCI 221A

UPPP 224.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
UPPP 224.description: Reviews and critiques literature on discussion topics including: the nature and effectiveness of environmental movements and policies; the role of science and technology; the use of economic incentives in policy; decentralization of decision making; and creating arenas for public involvement.

UPPP 225.title: Qualitative Methods for Public Policy
UPPP 225.description: Fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research. Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview. Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.

UPPP 227.title: Economics of Government
UPPP 227.description: Prepares students to analyze public policy questions with tools from economics. By the end, students should be able to identify important economic issues in public policy debates and consume and critique economic research on these topics.

UPPP 228.title: Demographics for Planning and Policy
UPPP 228.description: Provides planning and policy practitioners with a condensed, nonspecialist orientation to the sources, applications, and interpretation of population statistics, and conveys the steps used in constructing local-area population forecasts and projections.

UPPP 232.title: Water Policy and Planning
UPPP 232.description: Examines major issues in global water management including privatization, emerging water quality challenges, water system planning, affordability, conservation strategies, and flood resilience. Emphasizes integrated understanding of economics, governance, environmental health, technology, and development.

UPPP 235.title: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Problem Solving in Planning
UPPP 235.description: Explores the application of geographic information systems (GIS) in urban planning. Steps through a GIS-based planning procedure that balances housing, jobs, tax base, utilities, transportation, and the natural environment.

UPPP 237.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
UPPP 237.description: Application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to the field of urban and regional planning. Emphasizes current issues that occur in actual implementation settings. Lecture/discussion followed by laboratory demonstrating the area of GIS discussed. Offers "hands-on" student usage of GIS software.

UPPP 239.title: Urban Design Theories and Applications
UPPP 239.description: Introduction to contemporary and traditional theories of urban design and their applications. Organized around one question: How might planning and design of built environment contribute to making a good city? National and international case studies are introduced.

UPPP 240.title: Microeconomics and Public Policy
UPPP 240.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of microeconomics that are required for applied policy analysis. Provides students with an intuitive understanding of the microeconomic approach, and familiarizes them with concepts used in applied public policy analysis.

UPPP 243.title: Health Policy and Management
UPPP 243.description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.
UPPP 243.restriction: Urban and Regional Planning majors, School of Population and Public Health students, and Master of Public Policy have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 244.title: Land-Use Policy
UPPP 244.description: Examination of the role of public policy in guiding growth and development in urban and suburban environments. Description of a wide-ranging set of growth policies, the rationales underlying their use, controversies and legal constraints, and evaluation of their effectiveness.

UPPP 246.title: Housing Policy
UPPP 246.description: Examines theories and practices of housing policy and the relationship of housing to larger neighborhood, community, and regional development issues. Considers the roles of private for-profit and not-for-profit developers, lenders, and all levels of government in the provision of housing.
UPPP 246.prereq_text: Familiarity with basic statistics is required.

UPPP 251.title: Poverty and Development
UPPP 251.description: Examines competing conceptualizations, methods of measurement, and poverty alleviation strategies widely used in developing countries. Focuses on poverty conceptualized as economic deprivation, well-being, vulnerability, and social exclusion.

UPPP 252.title: Issues in Environmental Law and Policy
UPPP 252.description: Treatment of legal and policy strategies for promoting environmental protection and deterring environmental degradation within the context of other societal objectives. Topical approach with a focus on problems of special interest to criminologists and to environmental policy specialists.

UPPP 253.title: Foundations of Public Administration
UPPP 253.description: Introduction to the complex and interdisciplinary field of public administration. Topics include theories of public organizations, the role of bureaucracy in the political process, leadership and accountability, and the changing nature of public administration.

UPPP 254.title: Program Management and Evaluations
UPPP 254.description: Introduces students to the principles and practice of program evaluation and management. Emphasis is on both the theoretical foundations and practical applications in a variety of decision-making contexts within the public and nonprofit sectors.

UPPP 255.title: Public Budgeting and Financial Management
UPPP 255.description: The practice and problems of modern fiscal management in government, including budgetary procedures, major expenditure and revenue sources, and public financing methods.

UPPP 256.title: Sustainable Public Administration
UPPP 256.description: Overview of administrative structures that guide effective responses to complex environmental management challenges. Explores important questions regarding who makes environmental decisions, the processes behind those decisions, and the influence of political and economic power on environmental management.

UPPP 257.title: Designing and Consuming Research
UPPP 257.description: In-depth examination of issues relevant to designing and evaluating research in public administration. Topics address ethical issues surrounding the responsible conduct of research, experimental, quasi-experimental, and case study designs, and reliability and validity of measurement.

UPPP 258.title: Ethics and Leadership
UPPP 258.description: The importance of ethical leadership and the many challenges to behaving ethically that leaders face in the public, private and non-profit sectors. Topics include diverse ethical theories and principles, theories of effective leadership, and approaches to fostering ethical behavior.

UPPP 260.title: Policy and Ethics
UPPP 260.description: Examines the challenge of identifying ethical principles that can guide us in formulating and assessing public policy, the public policy process from an ethical perspective, and the ethics of the individual engaged in the public policy arena.

UPPP 266.title: Economic Democracy
UPPP 266.description: Explores a wide range of radical democratic and egalitarian visions (including but not limited to the Marxist tradition) for a more sane, just, and sustainable future.

UPPP 271.title: Public Finance for Urban Planning
UPPP 271.description: Introduction to public project financing, including overviews of major expenditure and revenue sources, budgeting processes, and the relationship between budgeting and planning. Practical skills covered include public financing methods, relevant mathematical analytic techniques, and grant writing.

UPPP 272.title: Site Development
UPPP 272.description: Basics of site plan review (e.g., site/plot plans, floor plans, elevations) to ensure compliance with the zoning code, comparison of ministerial vs. discretionary review processes, Intersection of California Environmental Quality Act with review processes, understanding reporting requirements.

UPPP 273.title: Global Urbanization
UPPP 273.description: Examines the spread of cities worldwide in the 20th century. What are the political and economic causes of this process? What are the social-cultural, political, and economic effects? How is contemporary urbanization linked to global restructuring of other kinds?

UPPP 274A.title: MPP Capstone Research Project and Briefing
UPPP 274A.description: Focuses on an issue by emphasizing all aspects of the policy process, including problem definition, mobilizing support, design, implementation, management, and entrepreneurship. Two quarters in length. Students work in teams and present their product to faculty, students, and policymakers.
UPPP 274A.restriction: Master of Public Policy only. Must be taken at the end of the second year in the program.

UPPP 274B.title: MPP Capstone Research Project and Briefing
UPPP 274B.description: Focuses on an issue by emphasizing all aspects of the policy process, including problem definition, mobilizing support, design, implementation, management, and entrepreneurship. Two quarters in length. Students work in teams and present their product to faculty, students, and policymakers.
UPPP 274B.restriction: Master of Public Policy only. Must be taken at the end of the second year in the program.

UPPP 275.title: Special Topics in Urban Planning
UPPP 275.description: Special topics in urban and regional planning are offered from time to time, but not on a regular basis. Course content varies with interest of the instructor.

UPPP 276.title: Planning for Sustainable Cities
UPPP 276.description: Measurement, implementation, and evaluation of urban sustainability practices.

UPPP 277.title: Site Planning and Design
UPPP 277.description: Enhance understanding of planning documents, including site plans, sections, design guidelines that are part of the everyday practice of most planners. Students gain opportunities to create a physical end product that can be added to a professional portfolio.

UPPP 279.title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
UPPP 279.description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

UPPP 280.title: Transportation Practice
UPPP 280.description: Broad survey of transportation policy issues that are confronting transportation planners, engineers, policymakers, and citizens.

UPPP 281.title: Theoretical Approaches in Planning and Policy
UPPP 281.description: Provides students with an overview of how theory is employed in urban planning and public policy research. Distinguishes between macro, meso and micro theories, including critical approaches. Cuts across disciplinary and topical boundaries. Ph.D. level course.

UPPP 282.title: Urban Design Studio for Planners: An Introduction
UPPP 282.description: Introductory urban design for planners. Organized around a variety of assignments to encourage learning by design in a studio setting. Students work on design projects and drawing assignments to learn practical aspects of urban design.

UPPP 283.title: Collaborative Governance and Public Management
UPPP 283.description: Introduction to inclusive management. To make effective use of public resources, public managers are inventing ways of managing that alter relationships within organizations, between organizations, between sectors, and with the public. Requires rethinking fundamentals such as leadership and motivation.
UPPP 283.restriction: Public Policy majors have the first consideration for enrollment.

UPPP 284.title: Environmental Theory and Topics
UPPP 284.description: Provides an overview of various theoretical approaches to the study of natural and built environments. Cuts across disciplinary boundaries. Canonical studies of the environment and sustainability are examined. Ph.D. level course.

UPPP 285.title: Urban Theory and Topics
UPPP 285.description: An advanced course for Ph.D. students looking to study canonical and contemporary urban theory that is both interdisciplinary and global.

UPPP 292.title: Professional Report
UPPP 292.description: Workshop designed to assist M.U.R.P. students in conducting their professional reports. Students select topics, design projects, conduct professional investigations, and write up reports.

UPPP 293.title: Planning Career Development
UPPP 293.description: Introduces students to the career options for urban planners. Provides opportunities to meet with professional planners practicing in a variety of settings (public, private, non-profit) and introduces students to professional norms, roles, and career paths.
UPPP 293.restriction: Master of Urban and Regional Planning only.

UPPP 294A.title: Urban Planning Practicum I
UPPP 294A.description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.

UPPP 294B.title: Urban Planning Practicum II
UPPP 294B.description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.
UPPP 294B.prereq_text: PP&D 294A with a minimum grade of B-.

UPPP 296.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
UPPP 296.description: Dissertation research with Urban Planning and Public Policy faculty.

UPPP 297.title: Research Design
UPPP 297.description: Provides training in research design and methods. Students learn how to evaluate the strength of research findings based on the methods used by a researcher and learn to use lessons from the course to develop a research proposal.

VIETMSE 1A.title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
VIETMSE 1A.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.
VIETMSE 1A.prereq_text: ( PLACEMENT EXAM OR AUTHORIZATION (see SOC comments for authorization policy/instructions) )

VIETMSE 1B.title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
VIETMSE 1B.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.
VIETMSE 1B.prereq_text: VIETMSE 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 1B is also accepted.

VIETMSE 1C.title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
VIETMSE 1C.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.
VIETMSE 1C.prereq_text: VIETMSE 1B with a minimum grade of C or VIETMSE S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 1C is also accepted.

VIETMSE 2A.title: Intermediate Vietnamese
VIETMSE 2A.description: Designed for students to advance their Vietnamese language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Designed to develop writing and reading skills and communicative skills in authentic situations. Students are introduced to aspects of Vietnamese culture relating to lesson topics.
VIETMSE 2A.prereq_text: VIETMSE 1C with a minimum grade of C and VIETMSE S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 2A is also accepted.
VIETMSE 2A.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

VIETMSE 2B.title: Intermediate Vietnamese
VIETMSE 2B.description: Designed for students to advance their Vietnamese language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Designed to develop writing and reading skills and communicative skills in authentic situations. Students are introduced to aspects of Vietnamese culture relating to lesson topics.
VIETMSE 2B.prereq_text: VIETMSE 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 2B is also accepted.
VIETMSE 2B.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

VIETMSE 2C.title: Intermediate Vietnamese
VIETMSE 2C.description: Designed for students to advance their Vietnamese language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Designed to develop writing and reading skills and communicative skills in authentic situations. Students are introduced to aspects of Vietnamese culture relating to lesson topics.
VIETMSE 2C.prereq_text: VIETMSE 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 2C is also accepted.
VIETMSE 2C.restriction: International Studies majors and School of Humanities students have the first consideration for enrollment.

VIETMSE 10A.title: Vietnamese Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
VIETMSE 10A.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. VIETMSE 10A is for language mentors.

VIETMSE 10B.title: Vietnamese Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
VIETMSE 10B.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. VIETMSE 10B is for language mentees.

VIETMSE 50.title: Topics in Vietnamese Culture
VIETMSE 50.description: Vietnamese culture and society in modern and historical contexts through the study of literary works, film, and other media. Philosophy and religious practices may also be examined. Course is taught in English.

VIS STD 290A.title: Art History:Theories and Methods
VIS STD 290A.description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in Art History.

VIS STD 290B.title: Theoretical and Historiographical Research Methods
VIS STD 290B.description: Provides students training in constructing and developing a research project integrating theoretical and historiographical methodologies.

VIS STD 290C.title: Visual Studies: Theories and Methods
VIS STD 290C.description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in Visual Studies.

VIS STD 295.title: Graduate Seminar in Visual Studies
VIS STD 295.description: Studies in selected areas of Visual Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

VIS STD 296.title: Directed Reading
VIS STD 296.description: Directed reading on a specific topic agreed upon by student and instructor.

VIS STD 297.title: Writing Practicum
VIS STD 297.description: Offered winter quarter each year and taught in a workshop format. Assists students with the preparation and revision of the dissertation prospectus so that they may advance to candidacy.
VIS STD 297.prereq_text: VIS STD 290A and VIS STD 290B and VIS STD 290C.

VIS STD 298A.title: Reading for the Preliminary Examination
VIS STD 298A.description: Directed reading in preparation for the preliminary examination. Formerly Visual Studies 298.

VIS STD 298B.title: Prospectus Research
VIS STD 298B.description: Research and writing of the dissertation prospectus.

VIS STD 299.title: Dissertation Research
VIS STD 299.description: Research and writing of the dissertation.

WRITING 30.title: The Art of Writing: Poetry
WRITING 30.description: Beginners' workshop in the writing of poetry, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.
WRITING 30.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

WRITING 31.title: The Art of Writing: Prose Fiction
WRITING 31.description: Beginners' workshop in fiction writing, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.
WRITING 31.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

WRITING 40.title: Introduction to Writing and Rhetoric
WRITING 40.description: Introduction to the principles of rhetoric through readings and writing assignments across a range of genres, including fiction, non-fiction, journalism and academic essays. Rigorous instruction in composition and style, including organization, paragraph development, sentence-level mechanics.
WRITING 40.prereq_text: AC ENG 20C with a minimum grade of C- and AC ENG 22A. Placement via the UC Irvine Writing Placement Process.

WRITING 40A.title: Introduction to Writing and Rhetoric with Lab
WRITING 40A.description: Introduces the principles of rhetoric through readings and writing assignments across a range of genres. Rigorous instruction in composition and style. Designed for students seeking additional English language support.
WRITING 40A.prereq_text: AC ENG 20C with a minimum grade of C- and AC ENG 22A. Placement via the UC Irvine Writing Placement Process.

WRITING 45.title: Intensive Writing
WRITING 45.description: Critical reading and analysis conducted through literary, academic, journalistic, and fictional genres with additional instruction in paragraph development and sentence-level mechanics. Students analyze and apply rhetorical principles in a range of writing assignments.
WRITING 45.prereq_text: AC ENG 20C with a minimum grade of C- and AC ENG 22A. Placement via the UC Irvine Writing Placement Process.

WRITING 50.title: Critical Reading and Rhetoric
WRITING 50.description: Critical reading and analysis conducted through literary, academic, journalistic, and fictional genres. Students analyze and apply rhetorical principles in a range of writing assignments. Letter Grade with P/NP Option.
WRITING 50.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

WRITING 60.title: Argument and Research
WRITING 60.description: Intensive instruction in research methods, argumentation, and rhetorical invention. Readings selected from current nonfiction and materials located by students from the University library’s holdings, to include databases across a range of disciplines.
WRITING 60.prereq_text: WRITING 45 with a minimum grade of C or WRITING 50 with a minimum grade of C- or AP English Language and Composition with a minimum score of 4 or AP English Literature and Composition with a minimum score of 4.

WRITING 90.title: Intermediate Poetry Writing
WRITING 90.description: Intermediate workshop in the writing of poetry, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.

WRITING 91.title: Intermediate Fiction Writing
WRITING 91.description: Intermediate workshop in the writing of fiction, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.

WRITING 101W.title: Undergraduate Seminar: Applications in Literary Theory and Criticism for Creative Writing
WRITING 101W.description: Readings in literature, with discussions and written rhetorical responses on their making.
WRITING 101W.prereq_text: (WRITING 30 or WRITING 31) and (WRITING 90 or WRITING 91) and (WRITING 30 or WRITING 31 or WRITING 90 or WRITING 91 or ENGLISH 16 or ENGLISH 17). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

WRITING 110.title: Short Story Writing
WRITING 110.description: Three-hour workshop in short fiction; discussion of student writing and of relevant literary texts.

WRITING 111.title: Poetry Writing
WRITING 111.description: Three-hour advanced poetry writing workshop; discussion of student writing and of relevant literary texts.

WRITING 113.title: Novel Writing
WRITING 113.description: Three-hour advanced workshop in fiction writing; discussion of student writing and of relevant literary texts.

WRITING 139W.title: Advanced Expository Writing
WRITING 139W.description: Study of rhetoric, disciplinary genres, and modes of knowledge production; practice in writing effective prose. Essays of varying lengths, totaling at least 4,000 words.
WRITING 139W.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

WRITING 197.title: Writing Internship
WRITING 197.description: Internships focused on writing. In consultation with a faculty advisor, students create a course from response essays, research essays, and assessment project data. Internships may include editing and publication projects, supervised teaching and tutoring assignments, community literacy projects.
WRITING 197.prereq_text: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement.

WRITING 250A.title: Graduate Writers' Workshop (Fiction)
WRITING 250A.description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.

WRITING 250B.title: Graduate Writers' Workshop (Fiction)
WRITING 250B.description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.

WRITING 250C.title: Graduate Writers' Workshop (Poetry)
WRITING 250C.description: Graduate poetry workshop open to students enrolled in the M.F.A. Programs in Writing.

WRITING 251A.title: Writing in Conference (Fiction)
WRITING 251A.description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.

WRITING 251B.title: Writing in Conference (Fiction)
WRITING 251B.description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.

WRITING 251C.title: Writing in Conference (Poetry)
WRITING 251C.description: Graduate poetry workshop open to students enrolled in the M.F.A. Programs in Writing.
